Na ukkuṭikāyāti ettha ukkuṭikā vuccati paṇhiyo ukkhipitvā aggapādehi vā aggapāde ukkhipitvā paṇhehiyeva vā bhūmiṃ phusantassa gamanaṃ. Karaṇavacanaṃ panettha vuttalakkhaṇameva. Na oguṇṭhitenāti sasīsaṃ pārutena. Na pallatthikāyāti na dussapallatthikāya. Ettha āyogapallatthikāpi dussapallatthikā eva. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajjāti there bhikkhū atiallīyitvā na nisīditabbaṃ. Na saṅghāṭiṃ ottharitvāti na saṅghāṭiṃ attharitvā nisīditabbaṃ.

"Not with the robe lifted" means not by lifting it up. Here, the instrumental case indicates the characteristic of being in such a state, meaning having the robe lifted on one side or both. From the city-post inwards, one should not go in this manner. However, when sitting, even when taking out a water-strainer, it should be taken out without lifting up the robe. "Not with loud laughter" means not laughing loudly. Here, the instrumental case follows the same explanation as above. "Not swaying the body" means without moving the body, holding the body firmly, making it motionless, with an upright body and a balanced posture. "Not swinging the arms" means without moving the arms, holding the arms firmly, making them motionless. "Not shaking the head" means without moving the head, holding the head firmly, keeping it motionless and upright. "Not with arms akimbo": 'arms akimbo' means placing the hands on the hips, making a pillar-like posture. "Not in a crouching manner": here, 'crouching' refers to walking with the heels raised and touching the ground only with the front of the feet, or raising the front of the feet and walking only on the heels. The instrumental case here has the same meaning as previously explained. "Not with the head covered" means not with the head wrapped up. "Not with the robe hitched up" means not with the lower robe hitched up. Here, even a waistband counts as hitching up the lower robe. "Not encroaching on the senior monks" means one should not sit too close to the senior monks. "Not spreading out the outer robe" means one should not sit having spread out the outer robe.

Sakkaccanti [V 2.0012] satiṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā. Pattasaññīti patte saññaṃ katvā. Samasūpako nāma yattha bhattassa catutthabhāgappamāṇo sūpo hoti. Samatitthikanti samapuṇṇaṃ samabharitaṃ. Thūpīkataṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassāti ettha thūpīkato nāma pattassa antomukhavaṭṭilekhaṃ atikkamitvā kato, patte pakkhitto bharito pūritoti attho. Evaṃ kataṃ aggahetvā antomukhavaṭṭilekhāsamappamāṇo gahetabbo. “Yaṃ kañci yāguṃ vā bhattaṃ vā phalāphalaṃ vā āmisajātikaṃ samatitthikameva gahetabbaṃ, tañca kho adhiṭṭhānupagena [M 2.0016] pattena, itarena pana thūpīkatampi vaṭṭati. Yāmakālikasattāhakālikayāvajīvikāni pana adhiṭṭhānupagapatte thūpīkatānipi vaṭṭanti. Yaṃ pana dvīsu pattesu bhattaṃ gahetvā ekasmiṃ pūretvā vihāraṃ pesetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ. Yaṃ patte pakkhipiyamānaṃ pūvaucchukhaṇḍaphalāphalādi heṭṭhā orohati, taṃ thūpīkataṃ nāma na hoti. Pūvavaṭaṃsakaṃ ṭhapetvā piṇḍapātaṃ denti, thūpīkatameva hoti. Pupphavaṭaṃsakatakkolakaṭukaphalādivaṭaṃsake pana ṭhapetvā dinnaṃ thūpīkataṃ na hoti. Bhattassa upari thālakaṃ vā pattaṃ vā ṭhapetvā pūretvā gaṇhāti, thūpīkataṃ nāma na hoti. Kurundiyampi vuttaṃ “thālake vā patte vā pakkhipitvā taṃ pattamatthake ṭhapetvā denti, pāṭekkabhājanaṃ vaṭṭati. Idha anāpattiyaṃ gilāno na āgato, tasmā gilānassapi thūpīkataṃ na vaṭṭati, sabbattha pana paṭiggahetumeva na vaṭṭati, paṭiggahitaṃ pana bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti.

`Sakkaccaṃ` means with mindfulness established. `Pattasaññī` means having awareness of the bowl. `Sama-sūpaka` means where the curry is about a quarter portion of the rice. `Sama-titthika` means evenly filled to the brim. If one receives almsfood heaped up, it is an offense of wrong conduct. Here, 'heaped up' (`thūpīkata`) means that which is made to exceed the inner rim of the bowl; the meaning is placed in the bowl, filled, and overflowing. Such food should not be accepted; it should be accepted only up to the level of the inner rim. 'Whatever gruel, rice, fruits, or any edible items should be taken only level to the brim, and that too with a determined bowl. With another bowl, however, even heaped-up food is permissible. But for tonics allowable for a day, for seven days, or for life, even heaped-up food is permissible in a determined bowl. However, it is allowable to take food in two bowls, fill one completely, and send it to the monastery,' as stated in the Mahāpaccarī. Whatever, when placed in the bowl, sinks to the bottom—such as cakes, sugarcane pieces, or fruits—is not considered heaped up. If almsfood is given by placing a cake as a base, it is considered heaped up. But if flowers, aromatics, bitter fruits, or similar items are placed as a base and then given, it is not considered heaped up. If one receives food by having a plate or bowl placed on top of the food and filled, it is not considered heaped up. In the Kurundī, it is also said: 'If they place food in a plate or bowl and, having placed that on top of the almsbowl, give it, a separate container is permissible. Here, in the section on no offense, the sick person is not mentioned; therefore, even for the sick, heaped-up food is not permissible. In all cases, it is not allowable to receive it; however, having received it, it is allowable to eat.'

“Sakkacca”nti ca “pattasaññī”ti ca ubhayaṃ vuttanayameva. Sapadānanti tattha tattha odhiṃ akatvā anupaṭipāṭiyā. Samasūpake vattabbaṃ vuttameva. Thūpakatoti matthakato, vemajjhatoti attho. Na sūpaṃ vā byañjanaṃ vātiādi pākaṭameva. Viññattiyaṃ vattabbaṃ natthi. Ujjhānasaññīsikkhāpadepi gilāno na muñcati. Nātimahanto kabaḷoti mayūraṇḍaṃ atimahantaṃ, kukkuṭaṇḍaṃ atikhuddakaṃ, tesaṃ vemajjhappamāṇo. Parimaṇḍalaṃ ālopoti nātidīgho ālopo. Anāhaṭeti anāharite, mukhadvāraṃ asampāpiteti attho. Sabbo hatthoti ettha hatthasaddo tadekadesesu aṅgulīsu daṭṭhabbo “hatthamuddo”tiādīsu viya samudāye pavattavohārassa avayave pavattanato. Ekaṅgulimpi mukhe pakkhipituṃ na vaṭṭati. Na sakabaḷenāti ettha dhammaṃ kathento harītakaṃ vā laṭṭhimadhukaṃ vā [M 2.0017] mukhe pakkhipitvā katheti, yattakena vacanaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hoti, tattake mukhamhi sante kathetuṃ vaṭṭati.

'Carefully' (`sakkaccaṃ`) and 'aware of the bowl' (`pattasaññī`) both follow the method previously explained. `Sapadānaṃ` means not making a boundary here and there, but proceeding in sequence. Regarding 'equal in curry' (`samasūpake`), what has been said already applies. `Thūpakato` means from the top of the heap. 'Not the soup or the relish,' and so forth, is clear enough. There is nothing to be said about 'requesting' (`viññattiyaṃ`). Even in the training rule on looking resentfully (`ujjhānasaññīsikkhāpade`), a sick person is not exempt. 'A mouthful not too large' (`nātimahanto kabaḷo`) means a peacock’s egg is too large, a chicken’s egg is too small—the middle size between them. 'A round morsel' (`parimaṇḍalaṃ ālopo`) means the morsel is not too elongated. `Anāhaṭe` means before it is brought; the meaning is before it has reached the entrance of the mouth. 'The whole hand' (`sabbo hattho`): here the word 'hand' (`hattha`) should be understood as referring to its parts, the fingers, as in expressions like 'hand-gesture' (`hattha-muddo`), where a term for the whole is used for a part. Not even a single finger may be put into the mouth. 'Not with a mouthful' (`na sakabaḷena`): here, when teaching the Dhamma, one may put a myrobalan or a stick of licorice in the mouth and speak. It is permissible to speak with as much in the mouth as allows the speech to be complete.

Piṇḍukkhepakanti piṇḍaṃ ukkhipitvā ukkhipitvā. Kabaḷāvacchedakanti kabaḷaṃ avachinditvā [V 2.0013] avachinditvā. Avagaṇḍakārakanti makkaṭo viya gaṇḍe katvā katvā. Hatthaniddhunakanti hatthaṃ niddhunitvā niddhunitvā. Sitthāvakārakanti sitthāni avakiritvā avakiritvā. Jivhānicchārakanti jivhaṃ nicchāretvā nicchāretvā. Capucapukārakanti “capucapū”ti evaṃ saddaṃ katvā katvā. Surusurukārakanti “surusurū”ti evaṃ saddaṃ katvā katvā. Hatthanillehakanti hatthaṃ nillehitvā nillehitvā. Bhuñjantena hi aṅgulimattampi nillehituṃ na vaṭṭati, ghanayāguphāṇitapāyāsādike pana aṅgulīhi gahetvā aṅguliyo mukhe pavesetvā bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Pattanillehakaoṭṭhanillehakesupi eseva nayo, tasmā aṅguliyāpi patto na nillehitabbo, ekaoṭṭhopi jivhāya na nillehitabbo, oṭṭhamaṃsehi eva pana gahetvā anto pavesetuṃ vaṭṭati.

`Piṇḍukkhepakaṃ` means tossing up the morsel repeatedly. `Kabaḷāvacchedakaṃ` means cutting off the morsel repeatedly. `Avagaṇḍakārakaṃ` means stuffing the cheeks repeatedly like a monkey. `Hatthaniddhunakaṃ` means shaking the hand repeatedly. `Sitthāvakārakaṃ` means scattering rice-grains repeatedly. `Jivhānicchārakaṃ` means sticking out the tongue repeatedly. `Capucapukārakaṃ` means repeatedly making a 'chapu chapu' sound. `Surusurukārakaṃ` means repeatedly making a 'suru suru' sound. `Hatthanillehakaṃ` means licking the hand repeatedly. Indeed, while eating, it is not proper to lick even a finger. However, when eating thick gruel, molasses, or rice porridge, it is permissible to take it with the fingers and insert the fingers into the mouth. The same applies to licking the bowl (`pattanillehaka`) or licking the lips (`oṭṭhanillehaka`). Therefore, one should not lick the bowl even with a finger, nor should one lick even a single lip with the tongue. Instead, it is permissible to gather it with the lips themselves and then bring it inside.

Na sāmisena hatthena pānīyathālakoti etaṃ paṭikūlavasena paṭikkhittaṃ, tasmā saṅghikampi puggalikampi gihisantakampi attano santakampi saṅkhampi sarāvampi āmisamakkhitaṃ na gahetabbameva, gaṇhantassa dukkaṭaṃ. Sace pana hatthassa ekadeso āmisamakkhito na hoti, tena padesena gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Na sasitthakaṃ pattadhovanaṃ antaraghare chaḍḍetabbanti ettha uddharitvā vāti sitthāni ekato uddharitvā ekasmiṃ ṭhāne rāsiṃ katvā udakaṃ chaḍḍeti. Bhinditvā vā udakagatikāni katvā chaḍḍeti, paṭiggahena sampaṭicchanto naṃ paṭiggahe chaḍḍeti, bahi nīharitvā vā chaḍḍeti, evaṃ chaḍḍentassa anāpatti. Na tāva therena udakanti idaṃ hatthadhovanaudakaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Antarā pipāsitena[M 2.0018], pana gale vilaggāmisena vā pānīyaṃ pivitvā na dhovitabbāti.

Not with a hand soiled by food should one touch the water vessel. This is prohibited on account of its being disagreeable. Therefore, a conch-shell or a dish, whether belonging to the Sangha, an individual, a householder, or oneself, if smeared with food, should not be taken at all. For one who takes it, there is an offense of wrong conduct. However, if a part of the hand is not smeared with food, it is permissible to take it with that part. Regarding 'Water from washing the bowl containing rice-grains should not be discarded inside the house': here, one either scoops them up, or having gathered the rice-grains together in one place and made a pile, one discards the water. Or, having broken them up to make channels for the water, one discards it. Or, receiving it in a receptacle, one discards it into the receptacle. Or, having taken it outside, one discards it. For one who discards it in this way, there is no offense. The phrase 'Not yet, elder, the water' is said with reference to hand-washing water. However, if one is thirsty in the meantime, or has food stuck in the throat, one may drink water but should not wash afterward.

Bhattaggavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the discourse on the observances in the meal-hall is concluded.

Anumodanavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Observance of Appreciation

Anumodanavatte anu punappunaṃ modiyate pamodiyateti anumodanā. Kā sā? Dhammakathā. Anumodanāya kattabbaṃ vattaṃ anumodanavattaṃ. Pañcame nisinneti anumodanatthāya nisinne. Upanisinnakathā nāma bahūsu sannipatitesu parikathākathanaṃ. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

In the observance of appreciation, 'anumodanā' is that by which one repeatedly rejoices and takes delight. What is that? A Dhamma talk. The observance to be performed for the sake of appreciation is the observance of appreciation. 'Seated in the fifth' means seated for the purpose of appreciation. 'Upanisinnakathā' is the telling of a preliminary talk among many who have gathered. The rest is easily understood.

Anumodanavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Observance of Appreciation is concluded.

Piṇḍacārikavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Alms-goer's Observances

189. Piṇḍacārikavatte [V 2.0014] piṇḍitabbo saṅgharitabboti piṇḍo, piṇḍapāto. Piṇḍāya caraṇaṃ sīlamassāti piṇḍacārī, so eva piṇḍacāriko sakatthe kapaccayavasena. Piṇḍacārikena vattitabbaṃ vattaṃ piṇḍacārikavattaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā – nivesanaṃ nāma itthikumārikādīnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ. Yasmā pavisananikkhamanadvāraṃ asallakkhetvā sahasā pavisanto visabhāgārammaṇaṃ vā passeyya, parissayo vā bhaveyya, tasmā “nivesanaṃ…pe… pavisitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Atidūre tiṭṭhanto apassanto vā bhaveyya, “aññassa gehe tiṭṭhatī”ti vā maññeyya. Accāsanne tiṭṭhanto apassitabbaṃ vā passeyya, asuṇitabbaṃ vā suṇeyya, tena manussānaṃ agāravo vā appasādo vā bhaveyya, tasmā “nātidūre nāccāsanne ṭhātabba”nti vuttaṃ. Aticiraṃ tiṭṭhanto adātukāmānaṃ [M 2.0019] manopadoso bhaveyya, aññattha bhikkhā ca parikkhayeyya, atilahukaṃ nivattanto dātukāmānaṃ puññahāni ca bhaveyya, bhikkhuno ca bhikkhāya asampajjanaṃ, tasmā “nāticiraṃ ṭhātabbaṃ, nātilahukaṃ nivattitabbaṃ, ṭhitena sallakkhetabba”nti vuttaṃ. Sallakkhaṇākāraṃ dasseti “sace kammaṃ vā nikkhipatī”tiādinā. Tattha kammaṃ vā nikkhipatīti kappāsaṃ vā suppaṃ vā musalaṃ vā yañca gahetvā kammaṃ karonti, ṭhitā vā nisinnā vā honti, taṃ nikkhipati. Parāmasatīti gaṇhāti. Ṭhapeti vāti “tiṭṭhatha bhante”ti vadantī ṭhapeti nāma. Avakkārapātīti atirekapiṇḍapātaṃ apanetvā ṭhapanatthāya ekā samuggapāti. Ettha ca samuggapāti nāma samuggapuṭasadisā pāti. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva.

189. In the alms-goer's observance, 'piṇḍa' is that which is to be collected or gathered; it is almsfood. One whose practice is to go for alms is a 'piṇḍacārī'; the same is called 'piṇḍacārika' by way of the affix 'ka' in the same sense. The observance to be practiced by an alms-goer is the 'piṇḍacārikavatta'. Herein, this is the explanation of the obscure terms: 'Nivesana' (dwelling) refers to the living place of women, young girls, and so on. Since one who enters hastily without observing the entrance and exit might see an unsuitable object or face danger, it is said, 'A dwelling... should be entered.' Standing too far away, one might not be seen, or they might think, 'He is standing at another house.' Standing too close, one might see what should not be seen or hear what should not be heard, whereby disrespect or displeasure may arise in those people. Therefore, it is said, 'One should stand neither too far nor too close.' Standing too long may cause mental vexation in those unwilling to give, and the opportunity for alms elsewhere may be lost. Leaving too quickly may cause a loss of merit for willing donors, and a failure for the monk to obtain alms. Thus, it is said, 'One should not stand too long, nor leave too quickly; while standing, one should observe.' The manner of observation is shown with, 'If she puts aside her work,' and so on. Here, 'puts aside her work' means she sets aside cotton, a winnowing basket, a pestle, or whatever she has taken up to do work with, whether standing or sitting. 'Touches' (parāmasati) means she takes. Or 'places it' (ṭhapeti): saying, 'Wait, venerable sir,' she places it down. 'Avakkārapāti' is a type of samuggapāti for setting aside and removing excess almsfood. Here, 'samuggapāti' means a bowl similar to a samuggapuṭa. The rest is as has been explained.

Piṇḍacārikavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Alms-goer's Observances is concluded.

Āraññikavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Forest-dweller's Observances

190. Āraññikavatte na ramanti janā etthāti araññaṃ. Vuttañhi –

190. In the forest-dweller's observance, 'arañña' (forest) is that in which people do not delight. For it is said:

“Ramaṇīyāni araññāni, yattha na ramatī jano;

Vītarāgā ramissanti, na te kāmagavesino”ti. (dha. pa. 99);

“Delightful are the forests where people find no delight; the passion-free will find delight there, for they are not seekers of sensual pleasures.”

Araññe [V 2.0015] vasatīti āraññiko, tena vattitabbaṃ vattaṃ āraññikavattaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ visesapadānamattho – kālasseva uṭṭhāyāti araññasenāsanassa gāmato dūrattā vuttaṃ, teneva kāraṇena “pattaṃ gahetvā cīvaraṃ pārupitvā gacchanto parissamo hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Pattaṃ thavikāya pakkhipitvā aṃse laggetvā cīvaraṃ khandhe karitvā araññamaggo na dussodhano hoti, tasmā kaṇṭakasarīsapādiparissayavimocanatthaṃ upāhanā ārohitvā. Araññaṃ nāma [M 2.0020] yasmā corādīnaṃ vicaraṭṭhānaṃ hoti, tasmā “dārubhaṇḍaṃ mattikābhaṇḍaṃ paṭisāmetvā dvāravātapānaṃ thaketvā vasanaṭṭhānato nikkhamitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Ito parāni bhattaggavattapiṇḍacārikavattesu vuttasadisāneva. Gāmato nikkhamitvā sace bahigāme udakaṃ natthi, antogāmeyeva bhattakiccaṃ katvā, atha bahigāme atthi, bhattakiccaṃ katvā pattaṃ dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā thavikāya pakkhipitvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitvā aṃse karitvā upāhanā ārohitvā gantabbaṃ.

One who dwells in the forest is an 'āraññika'; the observance to be practiced by him is the 'āraññikavatta'. Herein, this is the meaning of the special terms: 'Rising early' is said because the forest dwelling is far from the village. For that same reason, it is said, 'Taking the bowl, putting on the robe, and then going is fatiguing.' Having placed the bowl in a bag and hung it on the shoulder, and having carried the robe on the shoulder—the forest path is not easy to clear—therefore, to be free from the danger of thorns, reptiles, and so on, one should put on sandals. Since the forest is a place frequented by thieves and others, it is said, 'Wooden and clay utensils should be put away, doors and windows should be closed, and then one should leave the dwelling place.' From here onward, it is similar to what has been said in the observances for the meal-hall and for the alms-goer. After leaving the village, if there is no water outside the village, the meal duties should be performed within the village itself. But if there is water outside, after performing the meal duties, the bowl should be washed and dried, placed in the bag, the robe folded and placed on the shoulder, sandals put on, and then one should go.

Bhājanaṃ alabhantenātiādi araññasenāsanassa dullabhadabbasambhārattā vuttaṃ, aggi upaṭṭhāpetabbotiādi vāḷamigasarīsapādibāhiraparissayakāle ca vātapittādiajjhattapaassayakāle ca icchitabbattā. Bahūnaṃ pana vasanaṭṭhāne tādisāni sulabhāni hontīti āha “gaṇavāsino pana tena vināpi vaṭṭatī”ti. Kattaradaṇḍo nāma parissayavinodano hoti, tasmā araññe viharantena avassaṃ icchitabboti vuttaṃ “kattaradaṇḍo upaṭṭhāpetabbo”ti. Nakkhattāneva nakkhattapadāni. Corādīsu āgantvā “ajja, bhante, kena nakkhattena cando yutto”ti pucchitesu “na jānāmā”ti vutte kujjhanti, tasmā vuttaṃ “nakkhattapadāni uggahetabbāni sakalāni vā ekadesāni vā”ti, tathā disāmūḷhesu “katamāyaṃ, bhante, disā”ti pucchitesu, tasmā “disākusalena bhavitabba”nti.

'If one does not obtain a vessel,' and so on, is said because in a forest dwelling, materials and requisites are difficult to obtain. 'A fire should be prepared,' and so on, is said because it is desirable both in times of external dangers such as beasts of prey and reptiles, and in times of internal afflictions such as wind and bile disorders. But in places where many reside, such things are easily available, hence it is said, 'For those living in a group, it is permissible even without that.' A staff serves to ward off dangers, therefore, for one dwelling in the forest it is certainly desirable—thus it is said, 'A staff should be kept at hand.' The terms for the constellations are simply the constellations. If thieves and others come and ask, 'Venerable sir, with which constellation is the moon conjoined today?' and one says, 'I do not know,' they become angry. Therefore, it is said, 'The terms for the constellations should be learned, either in full or in part.' Similarly, when asked by those who are lost, 'Venerable sir, which direction is this?' therefore it is said, 'One should be skilled in directions.'

Āraññikavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Forest-dweller's Observances is concluded.

Senāsanavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Observances concerning Lodgings

191. Senāsanavatte sayanti etthāti senaṃ, sayananti attho. Āvasanti etthāti āsanaṃ. Senañca āsanañca senāsanaṃ. Senāsanesu kattabbaṃ vattaṃ senāsanavattaṃ[M 2.0021]. Idha pana yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ upajjhāyavattakathāyaṃ (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 183 ) vuttameva. Tattha pana upajjhāyena vutthavihāro vutto, idha pana attanā vutthavihāroti ayameva viseso. Na vuḍḍhaṃ anāpucchāti [V 2.0016] ettha tassa ovarake tadupacāre ca āpucchitabbanti vadanti. Bhojanasālādīsupi evameva paṭipajjitabbanti bhojanasālādīsupi uddesadānādi āpucchitvāva kātabbanti attho.

191. In the observances concerning lodgings: they lie down (sayanti) in it, thus it is 'sena'; the meaning is 'a bed' (sayana). They dwell (āvasanti) in it, thus it is 'āsana'. 'Sena' and 'āsana' together are 'senāsana'. The observance to be performed concerning lodgings is 'senāsanavatta'. Here, however, what is to be said has already been stated in the discourse on the observances toward a preceptor. There, the dwelling occupied by the preceptor was discussed; here, however, it is the dwelling occupied by oneself—this is the only difference. Regarding 'without asking a senior monk,' they say that here one should ask permission concerning his private room and its vicinity. 'And in dining halls, etc., one should practice in the same way' means that in dining halls and so on, tasks such as the assignment and giving out of things should be done only after asking permission.

Senāsanavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Observances concerning Lodgings is concluded.

Jantāgharavattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Observances concerning the Steam-bath House

192. Jantāgharavatte jāyatīti jaṃ, kiṃ taṃ? Sarīraṃ. Jaṃ tāyati rakkhatīti jantā, kā sā? Tikicchā. Gayhateti gharaṃ, kiṃ taṃ? Nivesanaṃ, jantāya sarīratikicchāya kataṃ gharaṃ jantāgharaṃ, jantāghare kattabbaṃ vattaṃ jantāgharavattaṃ. Tattha paribhaṇḍanti bahijagati. Sesaṃ upajjhāyavatte vuttanayattā suviññeyyameva.

192. In the section on the duties concerning the hot-bath house: that which is born is 'jaṃ'; what is that? The body. That which protects 'jaṃ' is 'jantā'; what is that? Medical treatment. That which is taken is 'ghara'; what is that? A dwelling. A house made for 'jantā', the medical treatment of the body, is a 'jantāghara'. The duty to be performed in the hot-bath house is 'jantāgharavatta'. Therein, 'paribhaṇḍa' means the outer ground. The rest is easily understood because it is stated in the manner of the duties toward the preceptor.

Jantāgharavattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Duties Concerning the Hot-Bath House is concluded.

Vaccakuṭivattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Duties Concerning the Latrine Hut

193. Vaccakuṭivatte vaccayate ūhadayateti vaccaṃ, karīsaṃ. Kuṭīyati chindīyati ātapo etāyāti kuṭi, vaccatthāya katā kuṭi vaccakuṭi, vaccakuṭiyā vattitabbaṃ vattaṃ vaccakuṭivattaṃ, idha ca vattakkhandhake ācamanavattaṃ paṭhamaṃ āgataṃ, pacchā vaccakuṭivattaṃ. Imasmiṃ pana pakaraṇe paṭhamaṃ vaccaṃ katvā pacchā ācamatīti [M 2.0022] adhippāyena vaccakuṭivattaṃ paṭhamaṃ āgataṃ, tasmā tadanukkamena kathayissāma. Dantakaṭṭhaṃ khādantenāti ayaṃ vaccakuṭiyāpi sabbattheva paṭikkhepo. Nibaddhagamanatthāyāti attanā nibaddhagamanatthāya. Puggalikaṭṭhānaṃ vāti attano vihāraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sesaṃ suviññeyyamevāti.

193. In the section on the duties concerning the latrine hut: it is excreted and expelled, thus 'vacca'; excrement. Sunlight is cut off by it, thus 'kuṭi'. A hut made for excrement is 'vaccakuṭi'. The duty to be performed at the latrine hut is 'vaccakuṭivatta'. And here, in the Vattakkhandhaka, the duty of rinsing comes first, followed by the duty concerning the latrine hut. In this treatise, however, the duty concerning the latrine hut comes first with the intention that one defecates first and then rinses afterward; therefore, we will explain them in that order. Regarding 'chewing a toothstick,' this is a prohibition everywhere, even at the latrine hut. Regarding 'for the purpose of regular visits,' it means for one's own purpose of regular visits. Regarding 'or a personal place,' it is said with reference to one's own dwelling. The rest is easily understood.

Vaccakuṭivattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Duties Concerning the Latrine Hut is concluded.

Iti vinayasaṅgahasaṃvaṇṇanābhūte vinayālaṅkāre

Thus, in the Vinayālaṅkāra, which is an explanation of the Vinayasaṅgaha,

Upajjhāyavattādivattavinicchayakathālaṅkāro nāma

Named the Ornament of the Discourse on the Analysis of Duties, Beginning with the Duties Toward the Preceptor,

Sattavīsatimo paricchedo.

The Twenty-Seventh Chapter.

28. Catupaccayabhājanīyavinicchayakathā

28. The Discourse on the Analysis of the Division of the Four Requisites

Cīvarabhājanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Division of Robes

194. Evaṃ [V 2.0017] upajjhāyādivattasaṅkhātāni cuddasa khandhakavattāni kathetvā idāni catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ bhājanaṃ kathento “catupaccayabhājana”ntiādimāha. Tattha catūti saṅkhyāsabbanāmapadaṃ. Paṭicca eti sītapaṭighātādikaṃ phalaṃ etasmāti paccayo, cīvarādi, paccayo ca paccayo ca paccayā, cattāro paccayā catupaccayaṃ, bhājīyate vibhājīyate bhājanaṃ. Catupaccayassa bhājanaṃ catupaccayabhājanaṃ. Tenāha “cīvarādīnaṃ catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ bhājana”nti. Tattha tasmiṃ catupaccayabhājane samabhiniviṭṭhe cīvarabhājane tāva paṭhamaṃ cīvarapaṭiggāhako…pe… veditabbo. Kasmā? Saṅghikacīvarassa dukkarabhājanattāti sambandho. Tattha āgatāgataṃ cīvaraṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, paṭiggahaṇamattamevassa bhāroti cīvarapaṭiggāhako. Cīvarapaṭiggāhakena paṭiggahitaṃ cīvaraṃ nidahati, nidahanamattamevassa bhāroti cīvaranidahako. Bhaṇḍāgāre niyutto bhaṇḍāgāriko. Cīvarādikassa bhaṇḍassa ṭhapanaṭṭhānabhūtaṃ agāraṃ bhaṇḍāgāraṃ. Cīvaraṃ bhājeti bhāgaṃ karotīti [M 2.0023] cīvarabhājako. Cīvarassa bhājanaṃ vibhāgakaraṇaṃ cīvarabhājanaṃ, vibhajanakiriyā.

194. Having thus explained the fourteen duties of the sections known as the duties beginning with those toward the preceptor, now, speaking of the division of the four requisites, he begins with 'the division of the four requisites,' and so on. Herein, 'catu' (four) is a numerical pronoun. 'Paccaya' is that from which a result, such as warding off cold, etc., comes; it refers to robes, etc. A requisite and a requisite are 'requisites' (paccayā); four requisites are 'the four requisites' (catupaccayaṃ). That which is divided or distributed is 'bhājana'. The division of the four requisites is 'catupaccayabhājana'. Therefore, it is said, 'the division of the four requisites: robes, etc.' Therein, within that division of the four requisites, when considering the division of robes, first, the robe-receiver... should be understood. Why? The connection is that the division of communal robes is difficult. Herein, the robe-receiver accepts any robe that comes; his duty is merely to receive it. The robe-storer stores the robe received by the robe-receiver; his duty is merely to store it. The storekeeper is appointed to the storeroom. The storeroom is the house that serves as the place for storing goods like robes. The robe-divider divides the robes, making shares. The division of robes is the act of dividing, the process of allocation.

Tattha “cīvarapaṭiggāhako veditabbo”ti vutto, so kuto labbhateti āha “pañcahaṅgehi…pe… sammannitabbo”ti. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti āha “anujānāmi…pe… vacanato”ti. Chandanaṃ chando, icchanaṃ pihananti attho. Gamanaṃ karaṇaṃ gati, kiriyā. Gāreyhā gati agati, chandena agati chandāgati. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Kathaṃ chandāgatiṃ gacchatīti āha “tattha pacchā āgatānampī”tiādi. Evamitaresupi. Pañcamaṅgaṃ pana satisampajaññayuttābhāvaṃ dasseti. Sukkapakkhepi ito paṭipakkhavasena veditabbo. Tenāha “tasmā”tiādi.

There, it is said, 'the robe-receiver should be understood.' From where is he obtained? He says, 'He should be appointed with five factors... and so on.' How is it known? He says, 'I allow... and so on... by the statement.' 'Chandana' is 'chando'; 'icchana' and 'pihana' are the meaning. 'Gamana' is 'karaṇa', 'gati', 'kiriyā'. A reprehensible course is a wrong course; a wrong course by desire is 'chandāgati'. The same method applies to the rest. How does one follow a wrong course due to desire? He says, 'There, even for those who came later... and so on.' The same applies to the others. The fifth factor, however, indicates the absence of being endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension. In the positive case, it should be understood as the opposite of this. Therefore, he says, 'Therefore... and so on.'

Imāya kammavācāya vā apalokanena vāti idaṃ imassa sammutikammassa lahukakammattā vuttaṃ. Tathā hi vuttaṃ parivāraṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pari. aṭṭha. 482) “avasesā terasa sammutiyo senāsanaggāhamatakacīvaradānādisammutiyo cāti etāni lahukakammāni apaloketvāpi kātuṃ vaṭṭantī”ti. Antovihāre sabbasaṅghamajjhepi khaṇḍasīmāyampi sammannituṃ vaṭṭatīti ettha antovihāreti [V 2.0018] baddhasīmavihāraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Na hi abaddhasīmavihāre apalokanādicatubbidhakammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati dubbisodhanattā. Dhuravihāraṭṭhāneti vihāradvārassa sammukhaṭṭhāne.

Regarding 'by this formal motion or by announcement,' this is said because this act of agreement is a light formal act. For it is stated in the Parivāra Aṭṭhakathā: 'The remaining thirteen agreements, such as the agreements for assigning lodgings and for giving the robes of the deceased, and so on—these are light formal acts that can be performed even by announcement.' Regarding 'even within a monastery, in the midst of the entire Sangha, or even within a delimited boundary, it is permissible to appoint,' here 'within a monastery' is said with reference to a monastery with established boundaries. For in a monastery without established boundaries, it is not permissible to perform the fourfold formal act, including announcement, due to the difficulty of verification. 'The place in front of the monastery' means the place directly facing the monastery's entrance.

197. Bhaṇḍāgārasammutiyaṃ vihāramajjheyevāti avippavāsasīmāsaṅkhātamahāsīmā vihārassa majjheyeva sammannitabbā. Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne imaṃ pana bhaṇḍāgāraṃ khaṇḍasīmaṃ gantvā khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ nisinnehi sammannituṃ na vaṭṭati, vihāramajjheyeva “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho [M 2.0024] itthannāmaṃ vihāraṃ bhaṇḍāgāraṃ sammanneyyā”tiādinā nayena “kammavācāya vā apalokanena vā sammannitabba”nti vacanaṃ nissāya ñattidutiyakammaṃ upacārasīmāyaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti gahetvā kathinadānakammampi abaddhasīmābhūte vihāre upacārasīmāyaṃ karonti, ekacce ñattikammampi tatheva gahetvā abaddhasīmavihāre upacārasīmāmatteyeva uposathapavāraṇaṃ karonti, tadayuttaṃ, kāraṇaṃ panettha kathinavinicchayakathāyaṃ (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 226) āvi bhavissati.

197. Regarding the agreement on the storeroom, 'right in the middle of the monastery' means the great boundary, known as the non-separation boundary, should be established right in the middle of the monastery. However, in this instance, it is not permissible for those seated within a fragmented boundary to establish this storeroom by going to the fragmented boundary; it must be established right in the middle of the monastery. Relying on the statement 'it should be appointed by formal motion or by announcement' in the manner of 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it seems proper to the Sangha, let the Sangha designate the monastery named so-and-so as the storeroom,' and so on, some, taking that it is permissible to perform a formal act consisting of a motion and one announcement in an adjacent boundary, also perform the kathina-cloth donation ceremony in a monastery without established boundaries within an adjacent boundary. Similarly, some, taking even the formal act consisting of a motion in the same way, conduct the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā ceremonies in a monastery without established boundaries, limiting it merely to the adjacent boundary. This is inappropriate. The reason for this will become clear in the discourse on the analysis of the kathina.

198. Tulābhūtoti tulāsadiso. Idanti sāmaṇerānaṃ upaḍḍhapaṭivīsadānaṃ. Imaṃ kira pāṭhaṃ amanasikarontā idāni kālacīvarampi sāmaṇerānaṃ upaḍḍhapaṭivīsaṃ denti. Phātikammanti pahonakakammaṃ, yattakena vinayāgatena sammuñjanībandhanādihatthakammena vihārassa ūnatā na hoti, tattakaṃ katvāti attho. Sabbesanti tatruppādavassāvāsikaṃ gaṇhantānaṃ sabbesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sāmaṇerānañca. Bhaṇḍāgāracīvarepīti akālacīvaraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ukkuṭṭhiṃ karontīti mahāsaddaṃ karonti. Etanti ukkuṭṭhiyā katāya samabhāgadānaṃ. Virajjhitvā karontīti kattabbakālesu akatvā yathārucitakkhaṇe karonti. Samapaṭivīso dātabboti karissāmāti yācantānaṃ paṭiññāmattenapi samako koṭṭhāso dātabbo.

198. Regarding 'being like a balance,' it means similar to a balance. Regarding 'this,' it refers to the giving of a half-share to novices. Indeed, disregarding this teaching, nowadays they give even the timely robes to novices as a half-share. Regarding 'phātikamma,' it means sufficient work, meaning doing just enough manual work, such as sweeping and binding, as is allowed by the Vinaya, so that the monastery does not become deficient. Regarding 'all,' it means all the monks and novices who receive what arises there while taking up residence for the rains. Regarding 'even in the storeroom robe,' it is said with reference to the off-season robe. Regarding 'making a clamor,' it means making a loud noise. Regarding 'this,' it refers to the equal distribution made when a clamor is made. Regarding 'doing after neglecting,' it means not doing what needs to be done at the proper times but doing it at a moment one pleases. Regarding 'an equal share should be given,' it means that an equal portion should be given even with just a promise from those requesting, 'We will do it.'

Atirekabhāgenāti dasa bhikkhū honti, sāṭakāpi daseva, tesu eko dvādasa agghati, sesā dasagghanakā. Sabbesu dasagghanakavasena kuse pātite yassa bhikkhuno dvādasagghanako kuso pātito, so “ettakena mama cīvaraṃ pahotī”ti tena atirekabhāgena gantukāmo hoti. Ettha ca ettakena mama cīvaraṃ pahotīti dvādasagghanakena mama cīvaraṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hoti, na tato ūnenāti sabbaṃ gahetukāmoti [M 2.0025] attho. Bhikkhū “atirekaṃ āvuso saṅghassa santaka”nti vadanti, taṃ sutvā bhagavā “saṅghike ca gaṇasantake ca appakaṃ nāma natthi, sabbattha [V 2.0019] saṃyamo kātabbo, gaṇhantenapi kukkuccāyitabba”nti dassetuṃ “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anukkhepe dinne”ti āha. Tattha anukkhepo nāma yaṃ kiñci anukkhipitabbaṃ anuppadātabbaṃ kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ, yattakaṃ tassa paṭivīse adhikaṃ, tattake agghanake yasmiṃ kismiñci kappiyabhaṇḍe dinneti atthoti imamatthaṃ saṅkhepena dassetuṃ “sace dasa bhikkhū honti”tyādi vuttaṃ.

By an excess portion: There are ten monks, and there are also ten robe-cloths. Among them, one is worth twelve, and the rest are worth ten each. When lots are cast for all based on the value of ten, if the lot for the one worth twelve falls to a monk, he wishes to go with that excess portion, thinking, 'With this, my robe-cloth is sufficient.' Here, 'With this, my robe-cloth is sufficient' means that with the twelve-value portion, my robe-cloth is complete, not less than that; this is the meaning of wanting to take it all. The monks say, 'The excess, friend, belongs to the Sangha.' Hearing this, to show that 'in what belongs to the Sangha or to a group, there is no such thing as a small amount; restraint should be practiced in all cases, and even when taking, one should be scrupulous,' the Blessed One said, 'Monks, I allow it when compensation has been given.' Here, 'compensation' means any allowable item that is to be given as compensation or in addition. The meaning is that whatever is in excess of his share, that much value is given in some allowable item. To show this meaning briefly, it was said, 'If there are ten monks,' and so forth.

Vikalake tosetvāti ettha cīvaravikalakaṃ puggalavikalakanti dve vikalakā. Tattha cīvaravikalakaṃ nāma sabbesaṃ pañca pañca vatthāni pattāni, sesānipi atthi, ekekaṃ pana na pāpuṇāti, chinditvā dātabbāni. Chindantehi ca aḍḍhamaṇḍalādīnaṃ vā upāhanathavikādīnaṃ vā pahonakāni khaṇḍāni katvā dātabbāni, heṭṭhimaparicchedena caturaṅgulavitthārampi anuvātappahonakāyāmaṃ khaṇḍaṃ katvā dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Aparibhogaṃ pana na kātabbanti evamettha cīvarassa appahonakabhāvo cīvaravikalakaṃ. Chinditvā dinne panetaṃ tositaṃ hoti. Atha kusapāto kātabbo, sacepi ekassa bhikkhuno koṭṭhāse ekaṃ vā dve vā vatthāni nappahonti, tattha aññaṃ sāmaṇakaṃ parikkhāraṃ ṭhapetvā yo tena tussati, tassa taṃ bhāgaṃ datvā pacchā kusapāto kātabbo. Idampi cīvaravikalakanti andhaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ.

Having satisfied the incomplete portions: Here, there are two kinds of incomplete portions: deficiency in robe-cloths and deficiency in persons. Deficiency in robe-cloths is when, for instance, everyone has received five pieces of cloth each, and there are other pieces remaining, but not enough for one each; these should be cut and given. When cutting, they should be made into pieces sufficient for half-moons, sandal-bags, and so forth, and then given. According to the lower limit, it is permissible to cut and give a piece four fingers in width with a length sufficient for a window-covering. However, it should not be made unusable. Thus, in this case, the insufficiency of the robe-cloth is the 'deficiency in robe-cloths.' When it has been cut and given, this is considered 'satisfied.' Then the casting of lots should be done. And if, in one monk's share, one or two pieces of cloth are insufficient, another monastic requisite should be placed there. Whoever is satisfied with that should be given that portion, and afterward, the casting of lots should be done. This too is called 'deficiency in robe-cloths,' as stated in the Andhaṭṭhakathā.

Puggalavikalakaṃ nāma dasa dasa bhikkhū gaṇetvā vaggaṃ karontānaṃ eko vaggo na pūrati, aṭṭha vā nava vā honti, tesaṃ aṭṭha vā nava vā koṭṭhāsā “tumhe ime gahetvā visuṃ bhājethā”ti dātabbā. Evamayaṃ puggalānaṃ appahonakabhāvo puggalavikalakaṃ nāma. Visuṃ dinne pana taṃ tositaṃ [M 2.0026] hoti, evaṃ tosetvā kusapāto kātabboti. Atha vā vikalake tosetvāti yo cīvaravibhāgo ūnako, taṃ aññena parikkhārena samaṃ katvā kusapāto kātabboti imamatthaṃ dasseti “sace sabbesaṃ pañca pañca vatthānī”tiādinā.

'Deficiency in persons' is when, in counting monks ten by ten to form a group, one group is not completed—there are only eight or nine. To them, eight or nine portions should be given, saying, 'You take these and divide them separately.' In this way, this insufficiency of persons is called 'deficiency in persons.' When it has been given separately, this is considered 'satisfied,' and having thus satisfied them, the casting of lots should be done. Alternatively, 'having satisfied the incomplete portions' indicates this meaning: if a share of robe-cloth is deficient, it should be made equal with another requisite, and then the casting of lots should be done. This meaning is shown by the passage beginning, 'If for all there are five pieces of cloth each...'

199. Ito paraṃ tesu tesu vatthūsu āgatavasena aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttesu vinicchayesu santesupi tesaṃ vinicchayānaṃ aṭṭhamātikāvinicchayato avimuttattā aṭṭhamātikāvinicchayesveva pakkhipitvā dassetuṃ “idāni aṭṭhimā, bhikkhave”tiādimāha. Yā tā aṭṭha mātikā bhagavatā vuttā, tāsaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ mātikānaṃ vasena vinicchayo idāni veditabboti yojanā. Parikkhepārahaṭṭhānena paricchinnāti iminā aparikkhittassa vihārassa dhuvasannipātaṭṭhānādito paṭhamaleḍḍupātassa [V 2.0020] anto upacārasīmāti dasseti. Idāni dutiyaleḍḍupātassa antopi upacārasīmāyevāti dassetuṃ “apicā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Dhuvasannipātaṭṭhānampi pariyantagatameva gahetabbaṃ. “Evaṃ sante tiyojane ṭhitā lābhaṃ gaṇhissantī”tiādinā ime lābhaggahaṇādayo upacārasīmāvaseneva hoti, na avippavāsasīmāvasenāti dasseti, tena ca imāni lābhaggahaṇādīniyeva upacārasīmāyaṃ kattabbāni, na apalokanakammādīni cattāri kammāni, tāni pana avippavāsasīmādīsuyeva kattabbānīti pakāseti. Tathā hi vuttaṃ sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.379) “bhikkhunīnaṃ ārāmappavesanasenāsanapucchanādi parivāsamānattārocanavassacchedanissayasenāsanaggāhādi vidhānanti idaṃ sabbaṃ imissāyeva upacārasīmāya vasena veditabba”nti.

199. From here onward, although there are decisions given in the commentary concerning various cases as they have arisen, because those decisions are not separate from the decision based on the eight matrices, to show them by including them within the decisions of the eight matrices, the passage beginning, 'Now, monks, these are the eight...' is stated. The connection is: the decision should now be understood in accordance with those eight matrices spoken by the Blessed One. By the phrase 'defined by a place suitable for an enclosure,' it is shown that for an unenclosed monastery, the area within the first clod-throw from the permanent meeting place is the proximity boundary. Now, to show that the area within the second clod-throw is also the proximity boundary, the passage beginning 'Moreover...' is introduced. The permanent meeting place should also be taken as having a defined boundary. By the passage beginning, 'If so, those standing three leagues away will receive a share,' it is shown that these acts of receiving shares, and so forth, occur by reason of the proximity boundary, not the non-separation boundary. And by this, it is made clear that these acts of receiving shares, and so forth, are to be done within the proximity boundary, but not the four formal acts, such as the act of seeking permission; those are to be done within the non-separation boundary, and so forth. For so it is said in the Sāratthadīpanī (Sārattha. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 3.379): 'For nuns, entering the monastery, inquiring about lodgings, announcing probation and penance, interrupting the rains-residence, taking dependence, accepting lodgings, and so forth—all this procedure should be understood by reason of this very proximity boundary.'

Lābhatthāya [M 2.0027] ṭhapitā sīmā lābhasīmā. Loke gāmasīmādayo viya lābhasīmā nāma visuṃ pasiddhā natthi, kenāyaṃ anuññātāti āha “neva sammāsambuddhenā”tiādi. Etena nāyaṃ sāsanavohārasiddhā, lokavohārasiddhā evāti dasseti. Janapadaparicchedoti idaṃ lokapasiddhasīmāsaddatthavasena vuttaṃ, paricchedabbhantarampi sabbaṃ janapadasīmāti gahetabbaṃ. Janapado eva janapadasīmā, evaṃ raṭṭhasīmādīsupi. Tenāha “āṇāpavattiṭṭhāna”ntiādi. Pathavīvemajjhagatassāti yāva udakapariyantā khaṇḍasīmattā vuttaṃ. Upacārasīmādīsu pana abaddhasīmāsu heṭṭhāpathaviyaṃ sabbattha ṭhitānaṃ na pāpuṇāti, kūpādipavesārahaṭṭhāne ṭhitānaññeva pāpuṇātīti heṭṭhā sīmakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva taṃtaṃsīmaṭṭhabhāvo veditabbo. Cakkavāḷasīmāya dinnaṃ pathavīsandhārakaudakaṭṭhānepi ṭhitānaṃ pāpuṇāti sabbattha cakkavāḷavohārattāti. Samānasaṃvāsaavippavāsasīmāsu dinnassa idaṃ nānattaṃ – “avippavāsasīmāya dammī”ti dinnaṃ gāmaṭṭhānaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Kasmā? “Ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañcā”ti (mahāva. 144) vuttattā. “Samānasaṃvāsakasīmāyadammī”ti dinnaṃ pana gāme ṭhitānampi pāpuṇātīti.

A boundary established for the sake of gain is a 'gain-boundary.' In the world, unlike village boundaries and so forth, a 'gain-boundary' is not separately established. To the question, 'By whom was this permitted?' it is said, 'Not by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One,' and so on. By this, it is shown that this is not established by the usage of the Dispensation, but solely by worldly usage. 'The demarcation of a country' is stated with reference to the meaning of the word 'boundary' as established in the world; everything within the demarcation should be understood as the country-boundary. The country itself is the country-boundary; similarly for kingdom-boundaries, and so forth. Therefore, it is said, 'the place where authority is exercised,' and so on. As for 'one who has gone to the middle of the earth,' this is stated with reference to a delimited boundary, extending as far as the water's edge. However, in the case of proximity boundaries and other unmarked boundaries, it does not apply to those standing everywhere below the ground, but only to those standing in places suitable for entering, such as a well. The state of being within each respective boundary should be understood according to the method stated in the discussion on lower boundaries. What is given within a world-sphere boundary applies even to those standing on the water that supports the earth, because the usage is of the entire world-sphere. Regarding what is given within the boundaries of common communion and non-separation, this is the difference: what is given with the words, 'I give within the non-separation boundary,' does not apply to those in a village. Why? Because it is said, 'Excluding the village and the village-precinct' (Mahāvagga 144). But what is given with the words, 'I give within the boundary of common communion,' applies even to those staying in a village.

200-1. Buddhādhivutthoti buddhena bhagavatā adhivuttho. Ekasminti ekasmiṃ vihāre. Pākavattanti nibaddhadānaṃ. Vattatīti pavattati. Tehi vattabbanti yesaṃ sammukhe esa deti, tehi bhikkhūhi vattabbaṃ.

'Inhabited by the Buddha' means inhabited by the Buddha, the Blessed One. 'In one' means in one monastery. 'A regular provision' means a continuous gift. 'It occurs' means it proceeds. 'It should be said by them' means it should be said by those monks in whose presence one gives this.

202. Dutiyabhāge pana therāsanaṃ āruḷheti yāva saṅghanavakaṃ ekavāraṃ sabbesaṃ bhāgaṃ datvā [V 2.0021] cīvare aparikkhīṇe puna sabbesaṃ dātuṃ dutiyabhāge therassa dinneti attho. Pubbe vuttanayenāti “tuyheva bhikkhu tāni cīvarānī”ti (mahāva. 363) bhagavatā [M 2.0028] vuttanayena. Paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭatīti “tuyhaṃ demā”ti avatvā, ‘bhikkhūnaṃ dema, therānaṃ demā”ti vuttattā “paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭatī”ti sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.379) vuttaṃ. Vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.379) pana paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭatīti ettha “tuyhaṃ demā”ti avuttattāti kāraṇaṃ vadanti. Yadi evaṃ “saṅghassa demā”ti vuttepi vaṭṭeyya, “bhikkhūnaṃ dema, therānaṃ dema, saṅghassa demā”ti vacanato bhedo na dissati, vīmaṃsitabbamettha kāraṇanti. Pārupituṃ vaṭṭatīti paṃsukūlikānaṃ vaṭṭati. Sāmikehi vicāritamevāti upāhanatthavikādīnamatthāya vicāritameva.

202. In the second portion, however, 'it ascends to the elder's seat' means that after giving a share to everyone once, up to the newest member of the Sangha, if the robe-cloths are not exhausted, it is given to the elder in the second portion to give again to everyone. By the previously stated method—that is, by the method stated by the Blessed One: “Monk, these robe-cloths are yours” (Mahāvagga 363). It applies even to the rag-robe wearers—because it was not said, “We give to you,” but rather, “We give to the monks, we give to the elders,” it is stated in the Sāratthadīpanī (Sārattha. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 3.379) that it applies even to the rag-robe wearers. However, in the Vimativinodanī (Vi. Vi. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 2.379) they state the reason here for 'it applies even to the rag-robe wearers' as: since it was not said, “We give to you.” If that is the case, then even if it were said, “We give to the Sangha,” it would still apply. Since no distinction is seen in the statements “We give to the monks, we give to the elders, we give to the Sangha,” the reason here should be carefully examined. It is permissible to wear—meaning it is permissible for the rag-robe wearers. It is only to be managed by the owners—meaning it is only to be managed for the purpose of sandals, bags, and so forth.

203. Upaḍḍhaṃ dātabbanti yaṃ ubhatosaṅghassa dinnaṃ, tato upaḍḍhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ upaḍḍhaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ dātabbaṃ. Sacepi eko bhikkhu hoti, ekā vā bhikkhunī, antamaso anupasampannassapi upaḍḍhameva dātabbaṃ. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīnañca dammī”ti vutte pana na majjhe bhinditvā dātabbanti ettha yasmā bhikkhunipakkhe saṅghassa paccekaṃ aparāmaṭṭhattā bhikkhunīnaṃ gaṇanāya bhāgo dātabboti dāyakassa adhippāyoti sijjhati, tathā dānañca bhikkhūpi gaṇetvā dinne eva yujjati. Itarathā hi “kittakaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dātabbaṃ, kittakaṃ bhikkhunīna”nti na viññāyati, tasmā “bhikkhusaṅghassā”ti vuttavacanampi “bhikkhūna”nti vuttavacanasadisamevāti āha “bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvā dātabba”nti. Tenāha “puggalo…pe… bhikkhusaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā”ti. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañcā”ti vutte pana puggalo visuṃ na labhatīti idaṃ aṭṭhakathāpamāṇeneva gahetabbaṃ, na hettha visesakāraṇaṃ upalabbhati. Tathā hi “ubhatosaṅghassa ca tuyhañca dammī”ti vutte sāmaññavisesavacanehi saṅgahitattā yathā puggalo visuṃ labhati, evamidhāpi “bhikkhusaṅghassa ca tuyhañcā”ti [M 2.0029] sāmaññavisesavacanasabbhāvato bhavitabbameva visuṃ puggalapaṭivīsenāti viññāyati, tasmā aṭṭhakathāvacanamevettha pamāṇaṃ. Pāpuṇanaṭṭhānato ekameva labhatīti attano vassaggena pattaṭṭhānato ekameva koṭṭhāsaṃ labhati. Tattha kāraṇamāha “kasmā? Bhikkhusaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā”ti, bhikkhusaṅghaggahaṇeneva puggalassapi gahitattāti adhippāyoti sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.379) vuttaṃ.

203. “Half to be given” means that of what is given to both Sanghas, half should be given to the bhikkhus and half to the bhikkhunīs. Even if there is only one bhikkhu or one bhikkhunī, or even one not yet fully ordained, half should be given. However, when it is said, “I give to the Sangha of bhikkhus and to the bhikkhunīs,” it should not be divided in the middle. Here, because on the side of the bhikkhunīs the Sangha is not individually addressed, it is established that the donor's intention is that the share should be given by counting the bhikkhunīs; and in the same way, it is proper that the gift is given by counting the bhikkhus also. Otherwise, it would not be known how much should be given to the bhikkhus and how much to the bhikkhunīs. Therefore, he said that even the statement “to the Sangha of bhikkhus” is the same as the statement “to the bhikkhus,” thus: “it should be given after counting the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs.” Therefore, he said, “The individual… because of being included by the term ‘Sangha of bhikkhus.’” But when it is said, “to the Sangha of bhikkhus and to the bhikkhunīs and to you,” the individual does not receive a separate share; this should be taken only on the authority of the commentary, for no special reason is found here. For, when it is said, “I give to both Sanghas and to you,” just as the individual receives a separate share because of being included by general and specific terms, so too here, in “to the Sangha of bhikkhus and to you,” it is understood that there must be a separate portion for the individual due to the presence of general and specific terms. Therefore, the statement of the commentary is the authority here. “From the position of attainment, one receives only one”—meaning, from the position attained by one's seniority, one receives only one portion. Therein, he states the reason: “Why? Because of being included by the term ‘Sangha of bhikkhus.’” The meaning is that the individual is also included by the term ‘Sangha of bhikkhus,’ so it is said in the Sāratthadīpanī (Sārattha. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 3.379).

Vimativinodaniyaṃ [V 2.0022] (vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.379) pana bhikkhusaṅghasaddena bhikkhūnaññeva gahitattā, puggalassa pana “tuyhañcā”ti visuṃ gahitattā ca tatthassa aggahitattā daṭṭhabbā, “bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañcā”ti vuttaṭṭhānasadisattāti adhippāyo. Puggalappadhāno hettha saṅgha-saddo daṭṭhabbo. Keci pana “bhikkhusaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā”ti pāṭhaṃ likhanti, taṃ na sundaraṃ tassa visuṃ lābhaggahaṇe kāraṇavacanattā. Tathā hi “visuṃ saṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā”ti visuṃ puggalassapi bhāgaggahaṇe kāraṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Yathā cettha puggalassa aggahaṇaṃ, evaṃ upari “bhikkhusaṅghassa ca tuyhañcā”tiādīsupi visuṃ saṅghādisaddehi puggalassa aggahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yadi hi gahaṇaṃ siyā, saṅghatopi visumpīti bhāgadvayaṃ labheyya ubhayattha gahitattāti vuttaṃ. Pūjetabbantiādi gihikammaṃ na hotīti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Bhikkhusaṅghassa harāti idaṃ piṇḍapātaharaṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tenāha “bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa harā”ti vuttepi haritabbanti īdisaṃ gihiveyyāvaccaṃ na hotīti katvā vuttaṃ.

However, in the Vimativinodanī (Vi. Vi. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 2.379), the meaning is that since only the bhikkhus are included by the term “Sangha of bhikkhus,” and the individual is included separately by “and to you,” it should be understood that he is not included therein, this being similar to the instance where it is said, “for the bhikkhus and for the bhikkhunīs and to you.” Here, the term “Sangha” should be understood as primarily referring to individuals. Some, however, write the reading as “because of being included by the term ‘Sangha of bhikkhus,’” but that is not good, as it is a statement of reason for the separate receiving of a share. For indeed, “because of being included by the separate term ‘Sangha’” is stated as a reason for the individual’s separate receiving of a share. Just as here there is no inclusion of the individual, so too above in “for the Sangha of bhikkhus and to you,” etc., it should be understood that there is no inclusion of the individual by the separate terms “Sangha,” etc. For if there were inclusion, one would receive a double portion—from the Sangha and also separately—because of being included in both places, so it is said. “Should be honored,” etc., is stated to show that it is not a layperson’s task. “Brings for the Sangha of bhikkhus”—this is said with reference to bringing almsfood. Therefore, he said, “it is proper to eat.” Even when it is said, “Bring for the Sangha of bhikkhus,” it is stated to show that this is not a layperson’s service, such as “it should be brought.”

204. Antohemanteti iminā anatthate kathine vassānaṃ pacchime māse dinnaṃ purimavassaṃvutthānaññeva pāpuṇāti, tato paraṃ hemante dinnaṃ pacchimavassaṃvutthānampi vutthavassattā [M 2.0030] pāpuṇāti, hemantato pana paraṃ piṭṭhisamaye “vassaṃvutthasaṅghassā”ti evaṃ paricchinditvā dinnaṃ anantare vasse vā tato paresu vā yattha katthaci tasmiṃ bhikkhubhāve vutthavassānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Ye pana sabbathā avutthavassā, tesaṃ na pāpuṇātīti dasseti. Lakkhaṇaññū vadantīti vinayalakkhaṇaññuno ācariyā vadanti. Lakkhaṇaññū vadantīti idaṃ sanniṭṭhānavacanaṃ, aṭṭhakathāsu anāgatattā pana evaṃ vuttaṃ. Bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ…pe… sabbesaṃ pāpuṇātīti yattha katthaci vutthavassānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇātīti adhippāyo. Teneva mātikāṭṭhakathāyampi (kaṅkha. aṭṭha. akālacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “sace pana bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhito ‘vassaṃvutthasaṅghassa dammī’ti vadati, yattha katthaci vutthavassānaṃ sabbesaṃ sampattānaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti vuttaṃ. Gaṇṭhipadesu pana “vassāvāsassa ananurūpe padese ṭhatvā vuttattā vassaṃvutthānañca avutthānañca sabbesaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Na hi “vassaṃvutthasaṅghassa dammī”ti vutte avutthavassānaṃ pāpuṇāti. Sabbesampīti tasmiṃ bhikkhubhāve vutthavassānaṃ sabbesampīti attho daṭṭhabbo “vassaṃvutthasaṅghassā”ti vuttattā. Sammukhībhūtānaṃ sabbesampīti etthāpi eseva nayo. Evaṃ vadatīti vassaṃvutthasaṅghassa dammīti vadati. Atītavassanti anantarātītavassaṃ.

204. “Within the winter”—by this it is shown that when the kathina has not been spread, what is given during the last month of the rains reaches only those who have completed the first rains-residence. After that, what is given during the winter reaches even those who have completed the later rains-residence, since they are considered to have resided for the rains. But if given after the winter, during the piṭṭhisamaya season, specifying “for the Sangha who have completed the rains-residence,” it reaches all who have completed the rains-residence anywhere, whether in the immediately following year or in subsequent years, as long as they are in that state of being a bhikkhu. However, it shows that it does not reach those who have not completed the rains-residence at all. The teachers who understand the characteristics say so—meaning the teachers who are knowledgeable in the characteristics of the Vinaya. “The teachers who understand the characteristics say so” is a statement of conclusion; it is stated thus because it is not found in the commentaries. “Outside the boundary of the monastery precincts… it reaches all”—the meaning is that it reaches all who have completed the rains-residence, wherever they may have resided. Therefore, even in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā (commentary on the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, explanation of the Akālacīvara Sikkhāpada), it is said: “If, however, one stands outside the boundary of the monastery precincts and says, ‘I give this to the Sangha who have completed the rains-residence,’ it reaches all of those who have completed the rains-residence, wherever they may be, who have arrived.” However, in the Gaṇṭhipada, it is said: “Since it is spoken in a place unsuitable for the rains-residence, it reaches all, both those who have completed the rains-residence and those who have not.” This should not be accepted, for when one says, “I give this to the Sangha who have completed the rains-residence,” it does not reach those who have not completed the rains-residence. “All”—the meaning “all who have completed the rains-residence in that state of being a bhikkhu” should be understood, since it is said, “for the Sangha who have completed the rains-residence.” “All who are present”—here too, the same principle applies. “Thus he says”—meaning he says, “I give this to the Sangha who have completed the rains-residence.” “The past rains” means the immediately preceding past rains.

205. Idāni [V 2.0023] “ādissa detī”ti padaṃ vibhajanto “ādissa detīti etthā”tiādimāha. Tattha yāguyā vā…pe… bhesajje vā ādisitvā paricchinditvā dento dāyako ādissa deti nāmāti yojanā. Sesaṃ pākaṭameva.

205. Now, analyzing the phrase “ādissa deti,” he begins with “ādissa detīti ettha.” Herein, a donor who gives after specifying and delimiting, such as with rice gruel… or with medicine, is called one who “gives having specified”—this is the construction. The rest is clear.

206. Idāni “puggalassa detī”ti padaṃ vibhajanto āha “puggalassa deti etthā”tiādi. Saṅghato ca gaṇato ca vinimuttassa [M 2.0031] attano kulūpakādipuggalassa dento dāyako puggalassa deti nāma. Taṃ pana puggalikadānaṃ parammukhā vā hoti sammukhā vā. Tattha parammukhā dento “idaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti nāmaṃ uddharitvā deti, sammukhā dento ca bhikkhuno pādamūle cīvaraṃ ṭhapetvā “idaṃ, bhante, tumhākaṃ dammī”ti vatvā deti, tadubhayathāpi dento puggalassa deti nāmāti attho. Na kevalaṃ ekasseva dento puggalassa deti nāma, atha kho antevāsikādīhi saddhiṃ dentopi puggalassa deti nāmāti dassetuṃ “sace panā”tiādimāha. Tattha uddesaṃ gahetuṃ āgatoti tassa santike uddesaṃ aggahitapubbassapi uddesaṃ gaṇhissāmīti āgatakālato paṭṭhāya antevāsikabhāvūpagamanato vuttaṃ. Gahetvā gacchantoti pariniṭṭhitauddeso hutvā gacchanto. Vattaṃ katvā uddesaparipucchādīni gahetvā vicarantānanti idaṃ “uddesantevāsikāna”nti imasseva visesanaṃ. Tena uddesakāle āgantvā uddesaṃ gahetvā gantvā aññattha nivasante anibaddhacārike nivatteti.

206. Now, explaining the phrase 'gives to an individual,' he says: 'gives to an individual here,' and so forth. A donor who gives to an individual separate from the Sangha or a group—such as his own family supporters—is said to give to an individual. That giving to an individual can be either in absence or in presence. In this regard, when giving in absence, one mentions the name, saying, 'I give this robe to so-and-so,' and then gives it. When giving in presence, one places the robe at the bhikkhu’s feet and says, 'Venerable sir, I give this to you,' and then gives it. In both cases, the giver is said to give to an individual—this is the meaning. Not only does giving to a single individual constitute giving to an individual, but also giving together with pupils and others is called giving to an individual. To illustrate this, it is said: 'But if…,' and so forth. Here, 'having come to receive instruction' is said of one who has not previously received instruction from that teacher but comes intending to receive it, from the time of his arrival onward to becoming a pupil. 'Having received it, he goes' means having completed the instruction and then departing. 'Having performed duties, receiving instruction and questioning, etc., while wandering' is a qualification of 'pupils receiving instruction.' Thus, this excludes those unattached wanderers who come at the time for instruction, receive the instruction, go away, and live elsewhere.

Evaṃ cīvarakkhandhake (mahāva. 379) āgataaṭṭhamātikāvasena cīvaravibhajanaṃ dassetvā idāni tasmiṃyeva cīvarakkhandhake majjhe āgatesu vatthūsu āgatanayaṃ nivattetvā dassento “sace koci bhikkhū”tiādimāha. Tattha kiṃ kātabbanti pucchāya tasseva tāni cīvarānīti vissajjanā, sesāni ñāpakādivasena vuttāni. Pañca māseti accantasaṃyoge upayogavacanaṃ. Vaḍḍhiṃ payojetvā ṭhapitaupanikkhepatoti vassāvāsikatthāya veyyāvaccakarehi vaḍḍhiṃ payojetvā ṭhapitaupanikkhepato. Tatruppādatoti nāḷikerārāmāditatruppādato. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “idaṃ idha vassaṃvutthasaṅghassa demāti vā vassāvāsikaṃ demāti vā vatvā [M 2.0032] dinnaṃ taṃ anatthatakathinassapi pañca māse pāpuṇātī”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ vassāvāsikalābhavasena uppanne labbhamānavisesaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha idhāti abhilāpamattamevetaṃ, idha-saddaṃ vinā “vassaṃvutthasaṅghassa demā”ti vuttepi so eva nayo. Anatthatakathinassapi pañca māse pāpuṇātīti vassāvāsikalābhavasena uppannattā anatthatakathinassapi vutthavassassa pañca māse pāpuṇāti, tato paraṃ pana uppannavassāvāsikaṃ pucchitabbaṃ [V 2.0024] “kiṃ atītavasse idaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ, udāhu anāgatavasse”ti. Tattha tato paranti pañcamāsato paraṃ, gimhānassa paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāyāti attho.

Thus, in the Robe Chapter (Mahāvagga 379), having shown the distribution of robes according to the eight categories that are mentioned, now, reverting to explain the method that arises in the middle of that same Robe Chapter, he says, beginning with 'If any bhikkhu...' Here, to the question 'What is to be done?', the answer is: 'Those robes belong to him.' The rest is stated by way of notification, and so forth. 'Five months' is a term used in the sense of absolute connection. 'From a deposit placed with interest' means from a deposit placed by those who manage affairs, having applied interest, for the purpose of the rains-residence. 'From what is produced there' means from what is produced there, such as from coconut groves. In the commentary, however, it is said: 'Having said, “We give this here to the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence,” or “We give this for the rains-residence,” that which is given is available for five months even for one whose kathina has not been withdrawn.' This is stated to show the special gain that is obtainable, which arises by way of the rains-residence gain. Here, 'here' is merely an expression; even without the word 'here,' if it is said, 'We give this to the Sangha that has completed the rains-residence,' the same principle applies. 'It is available for five months even for one whose kathina has not been withdrawn' means that because it arises by way of the rains-residence gain, it is available for five months for one who has completed the rains-residence, even if his kathina has not been withdrawn. After that, however, regarding the rains-residence gain that has arisen, one should ask, 'Is this rains-residence offering for the past rains-residence or the future one?' Here, 'after that' means after the five months, that is, starting from the first day of the hot season.

Ṭhitikā pana na tiṭṭhatīti ettha aṭṭhitāya ṭhitikāya puna aññasmiṃ cīvare uppanne sace eko bhikkhu āgacchati, majjhe chinditvā dvīhipi gahetabbaṃ. Ṭhitāya pana ṭhitikāya puna aññasmiṃ cīvare uppanne sace navakataro āgacchati, ṭhitikā heṭṭhā gacchati. Sace vuḍḍhataro āgacchati, ṭhitikā uddhaṃ ārohati. Atha añño natthi, puna attano pāpetvā gahetabbaṃ. Duggahitānīti aggahitāni, saṅghikāneva hontīti attho. “Pātite kuse”ti ekakoṭṭhāse kusadaṇḍake pātitamatte sacepi bhikkhusahassaṃ hoti, gahitameva nāma cīvaraṃ. “Nākāmā bhāgo dātabbo”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 363), tattha gahitameva nāmāti “imassa idaṃ patta”nti kiñcāpi na viditaṃ, te pana bhāgā atthato tesaṃ pattāyevāti adhippāyo.

Here, regarding 'the standing portion, however, does not remain standing': if, when a standing portion is not established, another robe arises and one bhikkhu arrives, it should be divided in the middle and taken by both. If, however, when a standing portion is established, another robe arises and a more junior bhikkhu arrives, the standing portion goes down. If a more senior bhikkhu arrives, the standing portion goes up. If there is no other, it should be taken again by causing it to accrue to oneself. 'Improperly taken' means not taken; they remain the property of the Sangha—this is the meaning. 'When a kusa stick is dropped' means that even if a thousand bhikkhus are present, as soon as a kusa stick for one portion is dropped, the robe is considered taken. 'A share should not be given to the unwilling' is a saying from the commentary (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 363). There, 'considered taken' means that even if it is not known that 'this has fallen to this person,' those shares have in essence fallen to them—this is the intention.

Sattāhavārena aruṇameva uṭṭhāpetīti idaṃ nānāsīmavihāresu kattabbanayena ekasmimpi vihāre dvīsu senāsanesu nivutthabhāvadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, aruṇuṭṭhāpaneneva tattha vuttho hoti, na pana vassacchedaparihārāya. Antoupacārasīmāya [M 2.0033] hi yattha katthaci aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpento attanā gahitasenāsanaṃ appaviṭṭhopi vutthavasso eva hoti. Gahitasenāsane pana nivuttho nāma na hoti, tattha aruṇuṭṭhāpane sati hoti. Tenāha “purimasmiṃ bahutaraṃ nivasati nāmā”ti. Etena ca itarasmiṃ sattāhavārenapi aruṇuṭṭhāpane sati eva appataraṃ nivasati nāma hoti, nāsatīti dīpitaṃ hoti. Idanti ekādhippāyadānaṃ. Nānālābhehītiādīsu nānā visuṃ visuṃ lābho etesūti nānālābhā, dve vihārā, tehi nānālābhehi. Nānā visuṃ visuṃ pākārādīhi paricchinno upacāro etesanti nānūpacārā, tehi nānūpacārehi. Ekasīmavihārehīti ekasīmāyaṃ dvīhi vihārehīti sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.364) vuttaṃ. Nānālābhehīti visuṃ visuṃ nibaddhavassāvāsikalābhehi. Nānūpacārehīti nānāparikkhepanānādvārehi. Ekasīmavihārehīti dvinnaṃ vihārānaṃ ekena pākārena parikkhittattā ekāya upacārasīmāya antogatehi dvīhi vihārehīti vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.364). Senāsanaggāho paṭippassambhatīti paṭhamaṃ gahito paṭippassambhati. Tatthāti yattha senāsanaggāho paṭippassambhati, tattha.

Regarding 'by the seven-day period, he causes only the dawn to rise': this is said to show the state of having dwelt in two lodgings even within one monastery, according to the method to be followed in monasteries with separate boundaries. By causing the dawn to rise there, one is considered to have dwelt there, but not for the purpose of avoiding a break in the rains-residence. For within the surrounding boundary, wherever one causes the dawn to rise, even if one has not entered the lodging that was taken, one is still considered to have completed the rains-residence. However, one is not considered to have dwelt in the lodging that was taken; one is considered to have dwelt there only when the dawn is caused to rise there. Therefore, he says, 'In the former, one is said to dwell more.' And by this, it is shown that in the other case, if the dawn is caused to rise within the seven-day period, one is said to dwell less; it is shown that it is not that one has not dwelt there at all. This is the giving with a single intention. In 'with various gains,' etc.: those in which there are various, that is, distinct, gains are 'various-gained'—namely, two monasteries; thus, 'with various gains.' Those whose surrounding areas are delimited by various, that is, distinct, walls, etc., are 'various-surrounded'; thus, 'with various surrounding areas.' 'With monasteries of a single boundary' means with two monasteries within a single boundary, as stated in the Sāratthadīpanī (Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā, Mahāvagga 3.364). 'With various gains' means with distinct, fixed rains-residence gains. 'With various surrounding areas' means with various enclosures and various gates. 'With monasteries of a single boundary' means with two monasteries enclosed by a single wall, thus included within one surrounding boundary, as stated in the Vimativinodanī (Vimativinodanī-ṭīkā, Mahāvagga 2.364). 'The taking of a lodging ceases' means the one initially taken ceases. 'There' means where the taking of a lodging ceases.

207. Bhikkhussa [V 2.0025] kālakateti ettha kālakata-saddo bhāvasādhanoti āha “kālakiriyāyā”ti. Pāḷiyaṃ gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ cīvaradāne sāmaṇerānaṃ ticīvarādhiṭṭhānābhāvā “cīvarañca pattañcā”tiādi sabbattha vuttaṃ.

207. Here, regarding 'when a bhikkhu has died' (bhikkhussa kālakate), he says that the word 'kālakata' (died) is a derivative signifying an action, meaning 'by the act of dying' (kālakiriyāya). In the Pāḷi, concerning the giving of robes to those attending the sick, since novices lack the formal determination of the three robes, it is said everywhere: 'both the robe and the bowl,' and so forth.

208. Sacepi sahassaṃ agghati, gilānupaṭṭhākānaññeva dātabbanti sambandho. Aññanti ticīvarapattato aññaṃ. Appagghanti atijiṇṇādibhāvena nihīnaṃ. Tatoti avasesaparikkhārato. Sabbanti pattaṃ cīvarañca. Tattha tattha saṅghassevāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ [M 2.0034] vihāre saṅghasseva. Bhikkhuno kālakataṭṭhānaṃ sandhāya “idhā”ti vattabbe “tatthā”ti vuttattā vicchāvacanattā ca parikkhārassa ṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ vuttanti viññāyati. Pāḷiyaṃ avissajjikaṃ avebhaṅgikanti āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghasseva santakaṃ hutvā kassaci avissajjikaṃ avebhaṅgikañca bhavituṃ anujānāmīti attho. “Sante patirūpe gāhake”ti vuttattā gāhake asati adatvā bhājitepi subhājitamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Dakkhiṇodakaṃ pamāṇanti ettha sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.376) tāva “yattha pana dakkhiṇodakaṃ pamāṇanti bhikkhū yasmiṃ raṭṭhe dakkhiṇodakapaṭiggahaṇamattenapi deyyadhammassa sāmino hontīti adhippāyo”ti vuttaṃ. Vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.376) pana “dakkhiṇodakaṃ pamāṇanti ettakāni cīvarāni dassāmīti paṭhamaṃ udakaṃ pātetvā pacchā denti, taṃ yehi gahitaṃ, te bhāginova hontīti adhippāyo”ti vuttaṃ. Parasamuddeti jambudīpe. Tambapaṇṇidīpañhi upādāyesa evaṃ vutto.

208. Even if it is worth a thousand, the connection is that it should be given only to those who attend to the sick. 'Other' means other than the three robes and the bowl. 'Of little value' means inferior due to being extremely worn, and so on. 'From that' means from the remaining requisites. 'All' means the bowl and the robe. 'There and there for the Saṅgha alone' means in each monastery, for the Saṅgha alone. Regarding the place where a bhikkhu has passed away, since 'there' is said when 'here' should have been said, and because of the varied nature of the expression, it is understood that the place where the requisites are kept is meant. In the Pāḷi, 'not to be relinquished, not to be divided' means: 'I allow it to become the property of the Saṅgha of the four directions, both present and future, and thus not to be relinquished to anyone nor to be divided.' This is the meaning. Since it is said, 'when a suitable receiver is present,' it should be understood that even if it is divided without being given when a receiver is not present, it is well divided. Regarding 'water of dedication as the measure,' in the Sāratthadīpanī (Sārattha. ṭī. Mahāvagga 3.376), it is stated: 'Where "water of dedication as the measure" is mentioned, the intention is that bhikkhus in whatever country become owners of the giftable items by the mere receiving of the water of dedication.' In the Vimativinodanī (Vi. Vi. ṭī. Mahāvagga 2.376), however, it is stated: 'Water of dedication as the measure' means that first they pour water, saying, 'We will give this many robes,' and then they give them. Those by whom it is received become the shareholders. This is the intended meaning. 'Beyond the ocean' refers to Jambudīpa. For this is said with reference to Tambapaṇṇidīpa.

“Matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātī”ti ettha maggaṃ gacchanto tassa kālakiriyaṃ sutvā avihāraṭṭhāne ce dvādasahatthabbhantare aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhāvaṃ ñatvā “idaṃ cīvaraṃ mayhaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti adhiṭṭhāti, svādhiṭṭhitaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu bahubhaṇḍo bahuparikkhāro kālakato hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ, “bhikkhussa, bhikkhave, kālakate saṅgho sāmī pattacīvare. Apica gilānupaṭṭhākā bahupakārā, anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātuṃ. Yaṃ tattha lahubhaṇḍaṃ lahuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetuṃ. Yaṃ tattha garubhaṇḍaṃ garuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa [M 2.0035] saṅghassa avissajjikaṃ avebhaṅgika”nti (mahāva. 369) iminā pāṭhena bhagavā sabbaññū bhikkhūnaṃ āmisadāyajjaṃ vicāresi.

Regarding 'One appropriates the robe of the deceased': if, while traveling on the path, upon hearing of his death, in a place that is not a monastery, within a distance of twelve cubits, knowing there are no other bhikkhus, one appropriates it, thinking, 'This robe falls to me'—it is properly appropriated. Now, at that time, a certain bhikkhu with many goods and many requisites passed away. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu has passed away, the Saṅgha is the owner of his bowl and robes. Moreover, those who attended to the sick have been of great assistance. I allow, bhikkhus, that the three robes and the bowl be given to those who attended to the sick. Whatever light goods and light requisites there are, that should be divided by the Saṅgha that is present. Whatever heavy goods and heavy requisites there are, that is not to be relinquished, not to be divided, belonging to the Saṅgha of the four quarters, both present and future.' (Mahāva. 369) By this passage, the Blessed One, the All-Knowing One, established the rules for the material inheritance for the bhikkhus.

Tattha [V 2.0026] ticīvarapattaavasesalahubhaṇḍagarubhaṇḍavasena āmisadāyajjaṃ tividhaṃ hoti. Tesu ticīvarapattaṃ gilānupaṭṭhākassa bhāgo hoti, avasesalahubhaṇḍaṃ sammukhībhūtasaṅghassa, pañcavīsatividha garubhaṇḍaṃ cātuddisasaṅghassa. Iminā ito tividhabhaṇḍato aññaṃ bhikkhubhaṇḍaṃ nāma natthi, imehi tividhehi puggalehi añño dāyādo nāma natthīti dasseti. Idāni pana vinayadharā “bhikkhūnaṃ akappiyabhaṇḍaṃ gihibhūtā ñātakā labhantī”ti vadanti, taṃ kasmāti ce? “Ye tassa dhane issarā gahaṭṭhā vā pabbajitā vā, tesaṃ dātabba”nti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ āgatattāti. Saccaṃ āgato, so pana pāṭho vissāsaggāhavisaye āgato, na dāyajjagahaṇaṭṭhāne. “Gahaṭṭhā vā pabbajitā vā”icceva āgato, na “ñātakā aññātakā vā”ti, tasmā ñātakā vā hontu aññātakā vā, ye taṃ gilānaṃ upaṭṭhahanti, te gilānupaṭṭhākabhāgabhūtassa dhanassa issarā gahaṭṭhapabbajitā, antamaso mātugāmāpi. Te sandhāya “tesaṃ dātabba”nti vuttaṃ, na pana ye gilānaṃ nupaṭṭhahanti, te sandhāya. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 369) “gilānupaṭṭhāko nāma gihī vā hotu pabbajito vā, antamaso mātugāmopi, sabbe bhāgaṃ labhantī”ti.

Herein, the material inheritance is of three kinds, by way of the three robes and bowl, the remaining light goods, and the heavy goods. Among these, the three robes and the bowl are the share of the attendant of the sick; the remaining light goods belong to the Saṅgha that is present; and the twenty-five kinds of heavy goods belong to the Saṅgha of the four quarters. By this it is shown that, apart from these three kinds of goods, there is no other property belonging to a bhikkhu, and apart from these three kinds of persons, there is no other heir. Now, however, the Vinaya masters say, 'The unsuitable goods of bhikkhus are received by their lay relatives.' If it is asked why, it is because it is stated in the commentary: 'It should be given to those who have authority over that property, whether they are householders or renunciants.' It is true that this passage occurs, but it occurs in the context of taking something in trust, not in the place of receiving an inheritance. The passage states 'householders or renunciants,' not 'relatives or non-relatives.' Therefore, whether they are relatives or not, those who attend to that sick person—be they householders or renunciants, even women—are the ones with authority over the property that constitutes the share of the attendant of the sick. It is with reference to them that it is said, 'It should be given to them,' and not with reference to those who do not attend to the sick. For it is stated in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 369): 'An attendant of the sick, whether a householder or a renunciant, even a woman—all receive a share.'

Atha vā yo bhikkhu attano jīvamānakāleyeva sabbaṃ attano parikkhāraṃ nissajjitvā kassaci ñātakassa vā aññātakassa vā gahaṭṭhassa vā pabbajitassa vā adāsi, koci ca ñātako vā aññātako vā gahaṭṭho vā pabbajito vā vissāsaṃ aggahesi, tādise sandhāya “ye tassa dhanassa issarā gahaṭṭhā vā pabbajitā vā, tesaṃ dātabba”nti [M 2.0036] vuttaṃ, na pana atādise ñātake. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 369) “sace pana so jīvamānoyeva sabbaṃ attano parikkhāraṃ nissajjitvā kassaci adāsi, koci vā vissāsaṃ aggahesi, yassa dinnaṃ, yena ca gahitaṃ, tasseva hoti, tassa ruciyā eva gilānupaṭṭhākā labhantī”ti. Evaṃ hotu, kappiyabhaṇḍe pana kathanti? Tampi “gihiñātakānaṃ dātabba”nti pāḷiyaṃ vā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vā ṭīkāsu vā natthi, tasmā vicāretabbametaṃ.

Alternatively, if a bhikkhu, while still alive, relinquished all his requisites and gave them to someone—whether a relative or a non-relative, a householder or a renunciant—or if someone, whether a relative or a non-relative, a householder or a renunciant, accepted them in trust, it is with reference to such a case that it is said, 'It should be given to those who have authority over that property, whether they are householders or renunciants,' but not to relatives in other circumstances. For it is stated in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 369): 'But if, while still alive, he relinquished all his requisites and gave them to someone, or if someone accepted them in trust, it belongs to the one to whom it was given or by whom it was accepted. The attendants of the sick receive it only with his consent.' So be it. But what about suitable goods? That these too 'should be given to lay relatives' is not found in the Pāḷi, the commentaries, or the sub-commentaries. Therefore, this matter should be investigated.

Cīvarabhājanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the exposition on the discussion of the division of robes.

Piṇḍapātabhājanakathāvaṇṇanā

Exposition on the Discussion of the Division of Almsfood

209. Idāni [V 2.0027] piṇḍapātabhājanavinicchayaṃ kathetuṃ “piṇḍapātabhājane panā”tiādimāha. Tattha senāsanakkhandhake senāsanabhājaneyeva paṭhamaṃ āgatepi catupaccayabhājanavinicchayattā paccayānukkamena piṇḍapātabhājanaṃ paṭhamaṃ dasseti. Piṇḍapātabhājane pana saṅghabhattādīsu ayaṃ vinicchayoti sambandho. Kathaṃ etāni saṅghabhattādīni bhagavatā anuññātānīti āha “anujānāmi…pe… anuññātesū”ti. Saṅghassa atthāya ābhataṃ bhattaṃ saṅghabhattaṃ yathā “āgantukassa ābhataṃ bhattaṃ āgantukabhatta”nti. Saṅghato uddissa uddisitvā dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ uddesabhattaṃ. Nimantetvā dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ nimantanabhattaṃ. Salākaṃ pātetvā gāhetabbaṃ bhattaṃ salākabhattaṃ. Pakkhe pakkhadivase dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ pakkhabhattaṃ. Uposathe uposathadivase dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ uposathabhattaṃ. Pāṭipade uposathadivasato dutiyadivase dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ pāṭipadabhattanti viggaho. Ṭhitikā nāma natthīti saṅghattherato paṭṭhāya vassaggena gāhaṇaṃ ṭhitikā nāma.

209.
