Now, to explain the determination concerning the division of almsfood, he begins with 'Now, regarding the division of almsfood…' Herein, although the division of dwellings was mentioned first in the Chapter on Dwellings, because this is the determination concerning the division of the four requisites, he presents the division of almsfood first, following the sequence of the requisites. The connection is: 'Now, regarding the division of almsfood, this is the determination concerning Saṅgha meals and so on.' To explain how these Saṅgha meals and others were permitted by the Blessed One, he states, 'I allow… (etc.) …among those permitted.' A meal brought for the benefit of the Saṅgha is a 'Saṅgha meal,' just as 'a meal brought for a guest is a guest meal.' A meal to be given after having been designated from the Saṅgha is a 'designated meal.' A meal to be given after an invitation is an 'invitation meal.' A meal to be received by drawing a ticket is a 'ticket meal.' A meal to be given on the day of the fortnight is a 'fortnightly meal.' A meal to be given on the Uposatha day is an 'Uposatha meal.' A meal to be given on the day following the Uposatha day, the first day of the fortnight, is a 'first-day meal'—this is the analysis. 'There is no such thing as a fixed portion' means that the practice of receiving according to seniority by rains-residence, starting from the Saṅgha elder, is called a 'fixed portion.'

Attano [M 2.0037] vihāradvāreti vihārassa dvārakoṭṭhakasamīpaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Bhojanasālāyāti bhattuddesaṭṭhānabhūtāya bhojanasālāyaṃ. Vassaggenāti vassakoṭṭhāsena. Dinnaṃ panāti vatvā yathā so dāyako vadati, taṃ vidhiṃ dassetuṃ “saṅghato bhante”tiādimāha. Antaraghareti antogehe. Antoupacāragatānanti ettha gāmadvāravīthicatukkesu dvādasahatthabbhantaraṃ upacāro nāma.

The phrase 'at the door of one's own dwelling' refers to the vicinity of the monastery's gatehouse. The phrase 'in the dining hall' means in the dining hall, which is the place designated for meals. The phrase 'by seniority' (vassaggena) means by the portion according to years of ordination. Having stated 'given,' to show the procedure as the donor speaks, he says, 'From the Sangha, venerable sir,' and so forth. The phrase 'inside the house' (antaraghare) means inside the inner house. Here, 'those who have gone within the vicinity' (antoupacāragatānaṃ) refers to the vicinity, which is a distance of twelve cubits within the village gate, street, or crossroads.

Antaragharassa upacāre pana labbhamānavisesaṃ dassetuṃ “gharūpacāro cetthā”tiādimāha. Ekavaḷañjanti ekena dvārena vaḷañjitabbaṃ. Nānānivesanesūti nānākulassa nānūpacāresu nivesanesu. Lajjī pesalo agatigamanaṃ vajjetvā medhāvī ca upaparikkhitvā uddisatīti āha “pesalo lajjī medhāvī icchitabbo”ti. Nisinnassapi niddāyantassapīti anādare sāmivacanaṃ, vuḍḍhatare niddāyante navakassa gāhitaṃ suggāhitanti attho. Ticīvaraparivāraṃ vāti ettha “udakamattalābhī viya aññopi uddesabhattaṃ alabhitvā vatthādianekappakārakaṃ labhati ce, tasseva ta”nti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Attano rucivasena yaṃ kiñci vatvā āharituṃ vissajjitattā vissaṭṭhadūto nāma. Yaṃ icchatīti “uddesabhattaṃ dethā”tiādīni vadanto yaṃ icchati. Pucchāsabhāgenāti pucchāsadisena.

To show the special quality obtainable in the vicinity of the house, he begins with 'Here, the vicinity of the house...' The phrase 'to be entered by one entrance' (ekavaḷañjaṃ) means it should be entered by a single entrance. The phrase 'in various residences' (nānānivesanesu) means in residences with various families and various vicinities. He says, 'One who is amiable, modest, and wise should be desired,' meaning one who avoids going to wrong destinations and examines carefully before assigning. The phrase 'even if he is sitting, even if he is sleeping' (nisinnassapi niddāyantassapi) is a genitive case of disrespect; it means that if an elder is sleeping, the acceptance by a junior is considered well-accepted. Here, regarding 'or accompanied by the three robes,' it is stated in the Gaṇṭhipada texts: 'If someone, like one who receives only a water pot, does not receive the designated meal but receives many other kinds of things like cloth, then that belongs to him.' One who is called a 'sent messenger' (vissaṭṭhadūto) is one who is sent to bring whatever is requested based on his own preference. The phrase 'what he desires' (yaṃ icchati) means what he desires, saying 'Give the designated meal,' and so forth. The phrase 'by way of a question' (pucchāsabhāgena) means like a question.

“Ekā [V 2.0028] kūṭaṭṭhitikā nāma hotī”ti vatvā tameva ṭhitikaṃ vibhāvento “rañño vā hī”tiādimāha. Aññehi uddesabhattādīhi amissetvā visuṃyeva ṭhitikāya gahetabbattā “ekacārikabhattānī”ti vuttaṃ. Theyyāya harantīti pattahārakā haranti. Gīvā hotīti āṇāpakassa gīvā hoti. Sabbaṃ pattassāmikassa hotīti cīvarādikampi sabbaṃ pattassāmikasseva hoti, “mayā [M 2.0038] bhattameva sandhāya vuttaṃ, na cīvarādi”nti vatvā gahetuṃ vaṭṭatīti attho. Manussānaṃ vacanaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti vuttā gacchantīti manussānaṃ vacanaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti tena bhikkhunā vuttā gacchanti. Akatabhāgo nāmāti āgantukabhāgo nāma, adinnapubbabhāgoti attho. Sabbo saṅgho paribhūñjatūti vutteti ettha “paṭhamameva ‘sabbasaṅghikabhattaṃ dethā’ti vatvā pacchā ‘sabbo saṅgho paribhuñjatū’ti avuttepi bhājetvā paribhuñjitabba”nti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Kiṃ āharīyatīti avatvāti “katarabhattaṃ tayā āharīyatī”ti dāyakaṃ apucchitvā. Pakatiṭhitikāyāti uddesabhattaṭhitikāya.

Having stated, 'There is one called a 'fixed allocation' (kūṭaṭṭhitikā),' he explains that very fixed allocation, beginning with 'for the king or...' Since it should be taken separately without mixing with other designated meals and the like, it is called 'meals for a single wanderer.' They carry it by theft—the bowl-carriers carry it. The phrase 'it becomes the neck' means it becomes the neck of the one who commands. The phrase 'everything belongs to the owner of the bowl' means that even the robes and other items all belong solely to the owner of the bowl; the meaning is that it is permissible to take them, saying, 'I spoke only concerning the meal, not the robes and so forth.' The phrase 'it is proper to convey the words of people' means that those who go, having been told by that bhikkhu, 'it is proper to convey the words of people,' actually go. The phrase 'the portion not made' means the newcomer's portion, meaning the portion not previously given. Regarding the phrase 'Let the entire Sangha partake,' it is stated in the Gaṇṭhipada texts: 'Even if, after first saying, "Give a meal for the entire Sangha," it is not later said, "Let the entire Sangha partake," it should still be divided and partaken of.' The phrase 'without saying what is to be brought' means without asking the donor, 'Which meal will you bring?' The phrase 'by the usual fixed allocation' means by the fixed allocation for designated meals.

Piṇḍapātabhājanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Discourse on the Distribution of Almsfood is concluded.

Nimantanabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Elucidation of the Discourse on Invitation Meals

210. “Ettake bhikkhū saṅghato uddisitvā dethā”tiādīni avatvā “ettakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhattaṃ dethā”ti vatvā dinnaṃ saṅghikaṃ nimantanaṃ nāma. Piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭatīti bhikkhāpariyāyena vuttattā vaṭṭati. Paṭipāṭiyāti laddhapaṭipāṭiyā. Vicchinditvāti “bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti padaṃ avatvā. Tenevāha “bhattanti avadantenā”ti. Ālopasaṅkhepenāti ekekapiṇḍavasena. Ayañca nayo nimantaneyeva, na uddesabhatte. Tassa hi ekassa pahonakappamāṇaṃyeva bhājetabbaṃ, tasmā uddesabhatte ālopaṭṭhitikā nāma natthi.

210. Without saying, 'Designate this many monks from the Sangha and give,' etc., but saying, 'Give a meal to this many monks,' what is given is called a Sangha invitation. It is valid even for alms-goers because it is spoken of in the context of alms-gathering. 'In order' means according to the order received. 'Having interrupted' means without saying the words, 'Take the meal.' Therefore, it is said, 'by one not saying "meal."' 'By way of a morsel' means according to individual lumps. And this method applies only to an invitation meal, not to a designated meal. For in the case of a designated meal, only an amount sufficient for one person should be divided. Therefore, in a designated meal, there is no such thing as 'the allocation of morsels.'

Āruḷhāyeva mātikaṃ. Saṅghato aṭṭha bhikkhūti ettha ye mātikaṃ āruḷhā, te aṭṭha bhikkhūti yojetabbaṃ. Uddesabhattanimantanabhattādisaṅghikabhattamātikāsu nimantanabhattamātikāya ṭhitikāvasena āruḷhe bhattuddesakena vā sayaṃ vā saṅghato uddisāpetvā gahetvā gantabbaṃ, na attanā [M 2.0039] rucite gahetvāti adhippāyo. Mātikaṃ āropetvāti “saṅghato gaṇhāmī”tiādinā vuttamātikābhedaṃ dāyakassa viññāpetvāti attho. “Ekavāranti yāva tasmiṃ āvāse vasanti bhikkhū[V 2.0029], sabbe labhantī”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha adhippāyo – ekavāranti na ekadivasaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, yattakā pana bhikkhū tasmiṃ āvāse vasanti, te sabbe. Ekasmiṃ divase gahitabhikkhū aññadā aggahetvā yāva ekavāraṃ sabbe bhikkhū bhojitā hontīti jānāti ce, ye jānanti, te gahetvā gantabbanti. Paṭibaddhakālato paṭṭhāyāti tattheva vāsassa nibaddhakālato paṭṭhāya.

The matrix has been entered. Here, the eight monks from the Sangha—those who have entered the matrix—should be connected. In the case of Sangha meals such as designated meals, invitation meals, etc., when one has entered the matrix of invitation meals according to the established rule, one should go having had it designated by the Sangha, either by the meal announcer or by oneself, and having taken it. The meaning is that one should not take it based on personal preference. 'Having caused the matrix to be entered' means informing the donor of the stated type of matrix, such as, 'I receive from the Sangha.' It is stated in the Gaṇṭhipada texts: 'One time' means that all monks residing in that monastery receive the meal. Here, the intended meaning is this: 'One time' is not said with reference to a single day, but rather to all the monks, however many are residing in that monastery. If one knows that the monks who have taken the meal on one day do not take it again until all monks have been fed once, then those who know should take the meal and go. 'From the bound time onward' means starting from the time residence is established there.

Nimantanabhattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Discourse on Invitation Meals is concluded.

Salākabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Elucidation of the Discourse on Meal Tickets

211. Upanibandhitvāti likhitvā. Gāmavasenapīti yebhuyyena samalābhagāmavasenapi. Bahūni salākabhattānīti tiṃsaṃ vā cattārīsaṃ vā bhattāni. Sace hontīti ajjhāharitvā yojetabbaṃ. Sallakkhetvāti tāni bhattāni pamāṇavasena sallakkhetvā. Niggahena datvāti dūraṃ gantuṃ anicchantassa niggahena sampaṭicchāpetvā. Puna vihāraṃ āgantvāti ettha vihāraṃ anāgantvā bhattaṃ gahetvā pacchā vihāre attano pāpetvā bhuñjitumpi vaṭṭati. Ekagehavasenāti vīthiyampi ekapasse gharapāḷiyā vasena. Uddisitvāpīti “asukakule salākabhattāni tuyhaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti vatvā.

211. 'Upanibandhitvā' means having written it down. 'Gāmavasenapī' means even by way of residence in a village where gains are equal for the most part. 'Bahūni salākabhattānī' means thirty or forty meals. 'Sace honti' should be connected by supplying the words. 'Sallakkhetvā' means assessing those meals by way of measure. 'Niggahena datvā' means compelling one who is unwilling to go far to accept it. 'Puna vihāraṃ āgantvā' here means that it is also allowable to take the meal without returning to the monastery, and later bring it to one's own residence in the monastery to eat. 'Ekagehavasenā' means by way of a row of houses on one side of a street. 'Uddisitvāpī' means saying, 'The meal tickets from such-and-such a family will reach you.'

212. Vāragāmeti atidūrattā vārena gantabbagāme. Saṭṭhito vā paṇṇāsato vāti daṇḍakammatthāya udakaghaṭaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vihāravāroti sabbabhikkhūsu bhikkhāya [M 2.0040] gatesu vihārarakkhaṇavāro. Nesanti vihāravārikānaṃ. Phātikammamevāti vihārarakkhaṇakiccassa pahonakapaṭipādanameva. Dūrattā niggahetvāpi vārena gahetabbo gāmo vāragāmo. Vihāravāre niyuttā vihāravārikā, vārena vihārarakkhaṇakā. Aññathattanti pasādaññathattaṃ. Phātikammameva bhavantīti vihārarakkhaṇatthāya saṅghena dātabbā atirekalābhā honti. Ekasseva pāpuṇantīti divase divase ekekasseva pāpitānīti attho. Saṅghanavakena laddhakāleti divase divase ekekassa pāpitāni dve tīṇi ekacārikabhattāni teneva niyāmena attano pāpuṇanaṭṭhāne saṅghanavakena laddhakāle.

212. A 'turn-village' is a village that must be gone to by turns because it is too distant. 'Sixty or fifty' refers to the water pot, spoken in connection with a disciplinary action. 'Monastery duty' means the duty of guarding the monastery when all the monks have gone for alms. 'Nesaṃ' means 'of those on monastery duty.' 'Only a suitable arrangement' means only the provision of what is sufficient for the duty of monastery protection. Because of its distance, even if compelled, a village to be taken by turns is a 'turn-village.' Those assigned to monastery duty are the monastery duty keepers, responsible for guarding the monastery in turns. 'A change in state' means a change in faith. The phrase 'they become only a suitable arrangement' means that they are extra gains to be given by the Sangha for the purpose of guarding the monastery. 'Reaching only one' means that those things were caused to reach only one each day. 'When the time for receiving arrived, by the junior monk of the Sangha' means that two or three meals for a single alms-round, caused to reach each one daily, following the same method, at the time when the occasion for his receiving them arrived, by the junior monk of the Sangha.

Yassa [V 2.0030] kassaci sammukhībhūtassa pāpetvāti ettha “yebhuyyena ce bhikkhū bahisīmagatā honti, sammukhībhūtassa yassa kassaci pāpetabbaṃ sabhāgattā ekena laddhaṃ sabbesaṃ hoti, tasmimpi asati attano pāpetvā dātabba”nti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Rasasalākanti ucchurasasalākaṃ. Salākavasena pana gāhitattā na sāditabbāti idaṃ asāruppavasena vuttaṃ, na dhutaṅgabhedavasena. “Saṅghato nirāmisasalākā…pe… vaṭṭatiyevā”ti hi visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 1.26) vuttaṃ. Sāratthadīpaniyampi (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.325) – saṅghato nirāmisasalākāpi vihāre pakkabhattampi vaṭṭatiyevāti sādhāraṇaṃ katvā visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 1.26) vuttattā, “evaṃ gāhite sāditabbaṃ, evaṃ na sāditabba”nti visesetvā avuttattā ca “bhesajjādisalākāyo cettha kiñcāpi piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭanti, salākavasena pana gāhitattā na sāditabbā”ti ettha adhippāyo vīmaṃsitabbo. Yadi hi bhesajjādisalākā salākavasena gāhitā na sāditabbā siyā, “saṅghato nirāmisasalākā vaṭṭatiyevā”ti [M 2.0041] na vadeyya, “atirekalābho saṅghabhattaṃ uddesabhatta”ntiādivacanato (mahāva. 128) ca “atirekalābhaṃ paṭikkhipāmī”ti salākavasena gāhetabbaṃ bhattameva paṭikkhittaṃ, na bhesajjaṃ. Saṅghabhattādīni hi cuddasa bhattāniyeva tena na sāditabbānīti vuttāni. Khandhakabhāṇakānaṃ vā matena idha evaṃ vuttanti gahetabbanti vuttaṃ. Aggato dātabbā bhikkhā aggabhikkhā. Aggabhikkhāmattanti ekakaṭacchubhikkhāmattaṃ. Laddhā vā aladdhā vā svepi gaṇheyyāsīti laddhepi appamattatāya vuttaṃ. Tenāha “yāvadatthaṃ labhati…pe… alabhitvā sve gaṇheyyāsīti vattabbo”ti. Aggabhikkhamattanti hi ettha matta-saddo bahubhāvaṃ nivatteti.

Regarding 'it should be caused to reach whomever is present,' it is said in the glosses: 'If most monks have gone outside the boundary, what is to be given to whomever is present, being obtained by one due to their shared portion, belongs to all. Even in the absence of such a person, it should be given after causing it to reach oneself.' 'Juice-stick' means a sugarcane juice-stick. However, 'because it is taken by means of a stick, it should not be consumed'—this is said in terms of inappropriateness, not as a violation of ascetic practices. For in the Visuddhimagga it is stated: 'A non-material allocation-stick from the Sangha... is indeed permissible.' The Sāratthadīpanī also says—since it is stated in the Visuddhimagga as a general rule that a non-material allocation-stick from the Sangha and even cooked food in the monastery are permissible, and because it is not stated with distinctions like 'it should be consumed this way, it should not be consumed that way'—here, the intention of 'although medicinal allocation-sticks, etc., are permissible even for alms-goers, yet because they are taken by means of a stick, they should not be consumed' should be investigated. For if medicinal allocation-sticks, etc., taken by means of a stick, were not to be consumed, then it would not be said, 'a non-material allocation-stick from the Sangha is permissible.' And from statements like 'excess gains, the Sangha’s meal, the designated meal,' it is only the meal to be taken by means of a stick that is rejected by the words, 'I reject the excess gain,' not medicine. Indeed, it is said that the fourteen types of meals, such as the Sangha’s meal, are precisely those that are not to be consumed by him. Or, it is said that this should be understood as being stated here according to the opinion of the Khandhaka reciters. 'Alms to be given from the first portion' is 'foremost alms.' 'Only the foremost alms' means only a single ladle of alms. 'Whether obtained or not obtained, you may take it the next day'—this is said out of diligence even when it has been obtained. Therefore, it is said: 'As much as one obtains... if not obtained, one should be told, "You may take it the next day."' Here, in 'only the foremost alms,' the word 'matta' excludes abundance.

Salākabhattaṃ nāma vihāreyeva uddisīyati vihārameva sandhāya dīyamānattāti āha “vihāre apāpitaṃ panā”tiādi. Tatra āsanasālāyāti tasmiṃ gāme āsanasālāya. Vihāraṃ ānetvā gāhetabbanti tathā vatvā tasmiṃ divase dinnabhattaṃ vihārameva ānetvā ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ. Tatthāti tasmiṃ disābhāge. Taṃ gahetvāti taṃ vāragāmasalākaṃ attanā gahetvā. Tenāti yo attano pattavāragāme salākaṃ disāgamikassa adāsi, tena. Anatikkamanteyeva tasmiṃ tassa salākā gāhetabbāti yasmā upacārasīmaṭṭhasseva salākā pāpuṇāti, tasmā tasmiṃ disaṃgamike upacārasīmaṃ anatikkanteyeva tassa disaṃgamikassa pattasalākā attano pāpetvā gāhetabbā.

The meal offering by lot is designated within the monastery itself, as it is given with reference to the monastery; hence it is said, 'But in the monastery, not having been caused to reach,' and so on. There, 'in the assembly hall' means in the assembly hall in that village. 'It should be brought to the monastery and taken' means that, having said so, the meal given on that day should be brought to the monastery itself and received according to the established rule. 'There' means in that direction. 'Having taken that' means having personally taken the lot for the village turn. 'By him' means by the one who gave the lot for his own village turn to a monk traveling to another region. 'His lot should be taken from him while he is not yet overstepping' means that since the lot only reaches one who is within the boundary of proximity, therefore, before that monk traveling to another region crosses the proximity boundary, the lot that has reached that monk should be caused to reach oneself and be taken.

Devasikaṃ [V 2.0031] pāpetabbāti upacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitassa yassa kassaci vassaggena pāpetabbā. Evaṃ etesu anāgatesu āsannavihāre bhikkhūnaṃ bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati, itarathā saṅghikaṃ hoti. Anāgatadivaseti ettha kathaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgatānāgatabhāvo [M 2.0042] viññāyatīti ce? Yasmā tato tato āgatā bhikkhū tasmiṃ gāme āsanasālāya sannipatanti, tasmā tesaṃ āgatānāgatabhāvo sakkā viññātuṃ. Amhākaṃ gocaragāmeti salākabhattadāyakānaṃ gāme. Bhuñjituṃ āgacchantīti “mahāthero ekakova vihāre ohīno avassaṃ sabbasalākā attano pāpetvā ṭhito”ti maññamānā āgacchanti.

‘It should be caused to reach them daily’ means it should be caused to reach whomever is staying within the boundary of proximity, according to seniority. Thus, when these monks have not arrived, it is allowable for monks in nearby monasteries to eat; otherwise, it belongs to the Sangha. Regarding 'on a day when they have not arrived,' if it is asked how the arrival and non-arrival of those monks is to be known: since monks arriving from various places gather in the assembly hall in that village, their arrival and non-arrival can be ascertained. 'In our alms-resort village' means in the village of the donors of the meal-tickets. 'They come to eat'—they come thinking, 'The great elder has been left behind alone in the monastery; surely he has caused all the meal-tickets to reach himself and is staying there.'

Salākabhattakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Elucidation of the Discourse on Meal Tickets is concluded.

Pakkhikabhattādikathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Account of Fortnightly Meals, and so on.

213. Abhilakkhitesu catūsu pakkhadivasesu dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ pakkhikaṃ. Abhilakkhitesūti ettha abhīti upasāramattaṃ, lakkhaṇiyesuiccevattho, uposathasamādānadhammassavanapūjāsakkārādikaraṇatthaṃ lakkhitabbesu sallakkhetabbesu upalakkhetabbesūti vuttaṃ hoti. Sve pakkhoti ajjapakkhikaṃ na gāhetabbanti aṭṭhamiyā bhuñjitabbaṃ, sattamiyā bhuñjanatthāya na gāhetabbaṃ, dāyakehi niyamitadivaseneva gāhetabbanti attho. Tenāha “sace panā”tiādi. Sve lūkhanti ajja āvāhamaṅgalādikaraṇato atipaṇītaṃ bhojanaṃ karīyati, sve tathā na bhavissati, ajjeva bhikkhū bhojessāmāti adhippāyo. Sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.325) pana aññathā vuttaṃ. Pakkhikabhattato uposathikabhattassa bhedaṃ dassento āha “uposathaṅgāni samādiyitvā”tiādi. Uposathe dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ uposathikaṃ.

213. The meal to be given on the four designated fortnightly days is a 'fortnightly meal.' Here, in 'designated' (abhilakkhitesu), 'abhi' is merely an intensive prefix; the meaning is 'to be marked'—that is to say, to be marked, considered, and noted for the purpose of undertaking the Uposatha, listening to the Dhamma, paying respects, making offerings, and so forth. 'Tomorrow is the fortnightly day' means the fortnightly meal is not to be taken today. It is to be eaten on the eighth day; it is not to be taken on the seventh day for the purpose of eating. The meaning is that it should be taken only on the day fixed by the donors. Therefore, it is said, 'But if…' and so on. 'Tomorrow it will be coarse'—the intention is: 'Today, due to marriage ceremonies, auspicious ceremonies, and so forth, very fine food is prepared; tomorrow it will not be so, so we will feed the monks today itself.' In the Sāratthadīpanī, however, it is stated differently. Showing the distinction of the Uposatha meal from the fortnightly meal, it is said: 'Having undertaken the Uposatha factors…' and so on. The meal to be given on the Uposatha day is the 'Uposatha meal.'

Pakkhikabhattādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Account of Fortnightly Meals, and so on, is concluded.

Āgantukabhattādikathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Account of Guest Meals, and so on.

214. Nibandhāpitanti [M 2.0043] “asukavihāre āgantukā bhuñjantū”ti niyamitaṃ. Gamiko āgantukabhattampīti gāmantarato āgantvā avūpasantena gamikacittena vasitvā puna aññattha gacchantaṃ [V 2.0032] sandhāya vuttaṃ, āvāsikassa pana gantukāmassa gamikabhattameva labbhati. “Lesaṃ oḍḍetvā”ti vuttattā lesābhāvena yāva gamanaparibandho vigacchati, tāva bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatīti ñāpitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

214. 'Arranged' means it is designated thus: 'Let the guests eat in such-and-such a monastery.' 'A traveler is also entitled to the guest meal' is said with reference to one who, having come from another village, stays with the unsettled mind of a traveler and then goes elsewhere again. For a resident monk who wishes to travel, however, only the traveler's meal is available. Because it is said, 'having set up a pretext,' it should be understood that it is indicated that, in the absence of a pretext, it is permissible to eat until the obstacle to departure is removed.

Dhurabhattādikathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Account of Meals for Special Occasions, and so on.

215. Taṇḍulādīni pesenti…pe… vaṭṭatīti abhihaṭabhikkhattā vaṭṭati.

215. They send rice, and so forth... It is permissible—meaning it is permissible because it is alms brought near.

216. Tathā paṭiggahitattāti bhikkhānāmena paṭiggahitattā. Pattaṃ pūretvā thaketvā dinnanti “guḷakabhattaṃ demā”ti dinnaṃ. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

216. “Because it was received in that way” means because it was received in the name of alms. “Given after filling and covering the bowl” means it was given with the words, “We give a rice-ball meal.” The rest is easily understood.

Piṇḍapātabhājanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Account of the Distribution of Almsfood is concluded.

Gilānapaccayabhājanakathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Account of the Distribution of Requisites for the Sick.

217. Ito paraṃ paccayānukkamena senāsanabhājanakathāya vattabbāyapi tassā mahāvisayattā, gilānapaccayabhājanīyakathāya pana appavisayattā, piṇḍapātabhājanīyakathāya anulomattā ca tadanantaraṃ taṃ dassetumāha “gilānapaccayabhājanīyaṃ panā”tiādi. Tattha rājarājamahāmattāti upalakkhaṇamattamevetaṃ. Brāhmaṇamahāsālagahapatimahāsālādayopi evaṃ karontiyeva. Ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvātiādi heṭṭhā vuttanayattā ca pākaṭattā [M 2.0044] ca suviññeyyameva. Upacārasīmaṃ…pe… bhājetabbanti idaṃ saṅghaṃ uddissa dinnattā vuttaṃ. Kumbhaṃ pana āvajjetvāti kumbhaṃ disāmukhaṃ katvā. Sace thinaṃ sappi hotīti kakkhaḷaṃ sappi hoti. Thokaṃ thokampi pāpetuṃ vaṭṭatīti evaṃ kate ṭhitikāpi tiṭṭhati. Siṅgiveramaricādibhesajjampi avasesapattathālakādisamaṇaparikkhāropīti iminā na kevalaṃ bhesajjameva gilānapaccayo hoti, atha kho avasesaparikkhāropi gilānapaccaye antogadhoyevāti dasseti.

217. From here onward, though the discussion of lodgings and their distribution should follow in order of requisites, due to its vast scope, the topic of requisites for the sick and their distribution, however, is of limited scope and follows naturally after the discussion of the distribution of almsfood. Therefore, to show that next, it is presented: “Now, as for the requisites for the sick and their distribution,” and so forth. Herein, “kings, royal ministers” is merely illustrative. Brahmin magnates, wealthy householders, and others also act similarly. “Striking the bell,” and so forth, is easily understood as previously explained and obvious. “Within the boundary… should be distributed”—this is said because it was given specifically for the Sangha. “Turning the pot” means placing the pot facing a direction. “If the ghee is thick”—if the ghee is hard. “It is permissible to pour it little by little”—doing so allows it to remain stable. “Medicines like ginger and pepper, as well as spare bowls and plates, and other monastic accoutrements”—this shows that not only medicines are considered requisites for the sick, but all other accessories are also included under the requisites for the sick.

Gilānapaccayabhājanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Account of the Distribution of Requisites for the Sick is concluded.

Senāsanaggāhakathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Account of Accepting Lodgings.

218. Senāsanabhājanakathāyaṃ [V 2.0033] senāsanaggāhe vinicchayoti senāsanabhājanamevāha. Tattha utukāle senāsanaggāho ca vassāvāse senāsanaggāho cāti kālavasena senāsanaggāho nāma duvidho hotīti yojanā. Tattha utukāleti hemantagimhānautukāle. Vassāvāseti vassānakāle. Bhikkhuṃ uṭṭhāpetvā senāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, akālo nāma natthi dāyakehi “āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa dammī”ti dinnasaṅghikasenāsanattā. Ekekaṃ pariveṇanti ekekassa bhikkhussa ekekaṃ pariveṇaṃ. Tatthāti tasmiṃ laddhapariveṇe. Dīghasālāti caṅkamanasālā. Maṇḍalamāḷoti upaṭṭhānasālā. Anudahatīti pīḷeti. Adātuṃ na labhatīti iminā sañcicca adentassa paṭibāhane pavisanato dukkaṭanti dīpeti. Jambudīpe panāti ariyadese bhikkhū sandhāya vuttaṃ. Te kira tathā paññāpenti.

218. In the discussion on the distribution of lodgings, the decision regarding the accepting of lodgings is itself the distribution of lodgings. Herein, the accepting of lodgings is twofold based on time: the accepting of lodgings during the season and the accepting of lodgings during the rains-residence. Herein, “during the season” refers to the winter and summer seasons. “During the rains-residence” refers to the rainy season. A lodging should be given after making a bhikkhu rise; there is no inappropriate time, because the lodging has been given to the Sangha by donors saying, “We give to the Sangha of the four directions, present and future.” “One dwelling per bhikkhu” means one dwelling for each bhikkhu. “Therein” means in that acquired dwelling. “A long hall” refers to a walking meditation hall. “A circular pavilion” refers to an assembly hall. “Oppresses” means harasses. “It is not permissible not to give” indicates that for one who intentionally does not give, there is a dukkaṭa offense for obstructing entry. “But in Jambudīpa” is said with reference to bhikkhus in the noble land. It is said they prescribe it thus.

219. Na [M 2.0045] gocaragāmo ghaṭṭetabboti vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāveti “na tattha manussā vattabbā”tiādinā. Vitakkaṃ chinditvāti “iminā nīhārena gacchantaṃ disvā nivāretvā paccaye dassantī”ti evarūpaṃ vitakkaṃ anuppādetvā. Tesu ce ekoti tesu manussesu eko paṇḍitapuriso. Bhaṇḍapaṭicchādananti paṭicchādanabhaṇḍaṃ, sarīrapaṭicchādanaṃ cīvaranti attho. Suddhacittattāva anavajjanti idaṃ pucchitakkhaṇe kāraṇācikkhaṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ na hoti asuddhacittassapi pucchitapañhavissajjane dosābhāvā. Evaṃ pana gate maṃ pucchissantīti saññāya agamanaṃ sandhāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

219. He clarifies the meaning of what was stated, “The alms-resort village should not be disturbed,” with “one should not speak with the people there,” and so forth. “Having cut off the thought” means not giving rise to a thought such as, “Seeing me going in this manner, they will stop me and offer requisites.” “If among them there is one” means one wise person among those people. “Covering for goods” means goods for covering; the meaning is a robe for covering the body. “Blameless only because of purity of mind”—this is said with reference to explaining the reason at the moment of being asked; it is not that there is no fault in answering a question asked even for one with an impure mind. However, it should be understood that this is said with reference to not going, out of the perception that, “If I go in this way, they will question me.”

Paṭijaggitabbānīti khaṇḍaphullābhisaṅkharaṇasammajjanādīhi paṭijaggitabbāni. Muṇḍavedikāyāti cetiyassa hammiyavedikāya ghaṭākārassa upari caturassavedikāya. Kattha pucchitabbanti pucchāya yato pakatiyā labbhati, tattha pucchitabbanti vissajjanā. Kasmā pucchitabbantiādi yato pakatiyā labbhati, tatthāpi pucchanassa kāraṇasandassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Paṭikkammāti vihārato apasakkitvā. Tamatthaṃ dassento “yojanadviyojanantare hotī”ti āha. Upanikkhepanti khettaṃ vā nāḷikerādiārāmaṃ vā kahāpaṇādīni vā ārāmikānaṃ niyyātetvā “ito uppannā vaḍḍhi vassāvāsikatthāya hotū”ti dinnaṃ. Vattaṃ katvāti tasmiṃ senāsane [V 2.0034] kattabbavattaṃ katvā. Iti saddhādeyyeti evaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayena saddhāya dātabbe vassāvāsikalābhavisayeti attho.

“Should be maintained” means they should be maintained by repairing what is broken and ruined, sweeping, and so forth. “On the shaven platform” refers to the square platform above the pot-shaped structure of the upper railing of the shrine. “Where should one ask?”—the reply to the question is that one should ask where it is naturally obtained. “Why should one ask?” and so forth, is stated to show the reason for asking even where it is naturally obtained. “Withdrawing” means moving away from the monastery. To explain this meaning, it is said: “It is within one or two yojanas.” “A deposit” means giving fields, coconut groves or other gardens, or money, and so forth, to the monastery attendants, saying, “Let the increase arising from this be for the purpose of the rains-residence.” “Having performed the duties” means having performed the duties to be done at that lodging. “Thus, a gift of faith”—the meaning is, in the matter of the gain related to the rains-residence that should be given in faith in the manner described previously.

Vatthu panāti tatruppāde uppannarūpiyaṃ, tañca “tato catupaccayaṃ paribhuñjathā”ti dinnakhettādito uppannattā kappiyakārakānaṃ hatthe “kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ paribhuñjathā”ti dāyakehi dinnavatthusadisaṃ hotīti āha “kappiyakārakānañhī”tiādi. Saṅghasuṭṭhutāyāti saṅghassa hitāya[M 2.0046]. Puggalavaseneva kātabbanti parato vakkhamānanayena bhikkhū cīvarena kilamanti, ettakaṃ nāma taṇḍulabhāgaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvaraṃ kātuṃ ruccatītiādinā puggalaparāmāsavaseneva kātabbaṃ, “saṅgho cīvarena kilamatī”tiādinā pana saṅghaparāmāsavasena na kātabbaṃ. Kappiyabhaṇḍavasenāti sāmaññato vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “cīvarataṇḍulādivaseneva cā”ti vuttaṃ. Ca-kāro cettha panasaddatthe vattati, na samuccayattheti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Puggalavaseneva kappiyabhaṇḍavasena ca apalokanappakāraṃ dassetuṃ “taṃ pana evaṃ kattabba”ntiādi vuttaṃ.

The basis, however, is the money that has arisen from that produce. And because it has arisen from a field and so forth, given with the words, “From this, enjoy the four requisites,” it is similar to an item given by donors into the hands of those who make things allowable, saying, “Enjoy the allowable goods.” Hence, it is stated, “for those who make it allowable,” and so forth. “For the welfare of the Sangha” means for the benefit of the Sangha. “It should be done solely by individual consideration”—it should be done based on consideration of individuals, according to the method to be explained later, such as: “Bhikkhus are troubled for robes; it is approved to use such and such a portion of rice to make robes for the bhikkhus.” It should not be done by collective Sangha consideration, such as “the Sangha is troubled for robes,” and so forth. “By way of allowable goods”—to clarify this meaning, which was stated generally, it is said, “and by way of robes, rice, and so forth.” Here, the particle “ca” functions in the sense of “pana” (but), not in the sense of conjunction—this should be understood. To show the manner of seeking approval by way of individual consideration and by way of allowable goods, it is said, “But it should be done thus,” and so forth.

Cīvarapaccayaṃ sallakkhetvāti saddhādeyyatatruppādavasena tasmiṃ vassāvāse labbhamānacīvarasaṅkhātaṃ paccayaṃ “ettaka”nti paricchinditvā. Senāsanassāti senāsanaggāhāpaṇassa. Vuttanti mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Kasmā evaṃ vuttanti āha “evañhī”tiādi, senāsanaggāhāpakassa attanāva attano gahaṇaṃ asāruppaṃ, tasmā ubho aññamaññaṃ gāhessantīti adhippāyo. Sammatasenāsanaggāhāpakassa āṇattiyā aññena gahitopi gāho ruhatiyevāti veditabbaṃ. Aṭṭhapi soḷasapi jane sammannituṃ vaṭṭatīti visuṃ visuṃ sammannituṃ vaṭṭati, udāhu ekatoti? Ekatopi vaṭṭati. Ekakammavācāya sabbepi ekato sammannituṃ vaṭṭati. Niggahakammameva hi saṅgho saṅghassa na karoti. Sammutidānaṃ pana bahūnampi ekato kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Teneva sattasatikakkhandhake ubbāhikasammutiyaṃ aṭṭhapi janā ekato sammatāti. Āsanagharanti paṭimāgharaṃ. Maggoti upacārasīmabbhantaragate gāmābhimukhamagge katasālā vuccati, evaṃ pokkharaṇirukkhamūlādīsupi. Rukkhamūlādayo [M 2.0047] channā kavāṭabaddhāva senāsanaṃ. Ito parāni suviññeyyāni.

“Having considered the robe requisite”: This means having determined as ‘this much’ the requisite, designated as robes, obtainable during that rains-residence by way of the produce from a gift of faith. “Of the lodging”: This means of the lodging assigner. “It is stated”: It is stated in the Great Commentary. Why is it stated thus? He says, ‘For this reason,’ and so on. It is unsuitable for the lodging assigner to assign a lodging to himself; therefore, the intention is that both should assign to each other. It should be understood that even if another person makes the assignment by the command of the appointed lodging assigner, the assignment is indeed valid. Is it proper to appoint eight or sixteen people, either separately or all together? It is proper to appoint them all together. By a single formal act, all can be appointed together. Indeed, the Sangha does not perform an act of censure against the Sangha. However, it is proper to grant an appointment to many at once. Therefore, in the Chapter of the Seven Hundred, eight people were appointed together for the Ubbāhika appointment. “Sitting hall”: This means an image house. “Path”: This refers to a pavilion built on the path facing a village, within the boundary of the vicinity; similarly, for lotus ponds, tree roots, and so on. Tree roots and the like, if covered and enclosed with doors, are lodgings. The following are easily understood.

220. Mahālābhapariveṇakathāyaṃ labhantīti tatra vāsino bhikkhū labhanti. Vijaṭetvāti ekekassa pahonakappamāṇena viyojetvā. Āvāsesūti senāsanesu. Pakkhipitvāti ettha pakkhipanaṃ [V 2.0035] nāma tesu vasantānaṃ ito uppannavassāvāsikadānaṃ. Pavisitabbanti aññehi bhikkhūhi tasmiṃ mahālābhe pariveṇe vasitvā cetiye vattaṃ katvāva lābho gahetabboti adhippāyo.

220. In the account of the great-gain dwelling, ‘they obtain’ means the bhikkhus residing there obtain. ‘Having distributed’ means having divided it individually according to the suitable measure for each. ‘In the dwellings’ means in the lodgings. ‘Having placed’ here means the act of placing is the giving of the rains-residence offering that has arisen from this to those dwelling there. ‘One should enter’ means the intention is that other bhikkhus should take the gain only after having resided in that great-gain dwelling and performed their duties at the shrine.

221. Paccayaṃ vissajjetīti cīvarapaccayaṃ nādhivāseti. Ayampīti tena vissajjitapaccayopi. Pādamūle ṭhapetvā sāṭakaṃ dentīti paccayadāyakā denti. Etena gahaṭṭhehi pādamūle ṭhapetvā dinnampi paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Atha vassāvāsikaṃ demāti vadantīti ettha “paṃsukūlikānaṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti ajjhāharitvā yojetabbaṃ. Vassaṃ vutthabhikkhūnanti paṃsukūlikato aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ. Upanibandhitvā gāhetabbanti “imasmiṃ rukkhe vā maṇḍape vā vasitvā cetiye vattaṃ katvā gaṇhathā”ti evaṃ upanibandhitvā gāhetabbaṃ.

221. “He relinquishes the requisite” means he does not accept a robe-requisite. “This one also” means a requisite relinquished by him. “Having placed a cloth at the feet, they give” means the donors of requisites give it. This shows that what is given by householders, having been placed at the feet, is suitable even for rag-robe wearers. Then, when they say, “We give the rains-residence offering”—here, it should be connected by supplying the words, “It is not suitable for rag-robe wearers.” “For bhikkhus who have dwelt the rains” means for bhikkhus other than rag-robe wearers. “Having stipulated, it should be taken” means it should be taken after having stipulated thus: “Having resided by this tree or in this pavilion and having performed your duties at the shrine, you may take it.”

Pāṭipadaaruṇatotiādi vassūpanāyikadivasaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Antarāmuttakaṃ pana pāṭipadaṃ atikkamitvāpi gāhetuṃ vaṭṭati. “Kattha nu kho vasissāmi, kattha vasantassa phāsu bhavissati, kattha vā paccaye labhissāmī”ti evaṃ uppannena vitakkena caratīti vitakkacāriko. Idāni yaṃ dāyakā pacchimavassaṃvutthānaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ deti, tattha paṭipajjanavidhiṃ dassetuṃ “pacchimavassūpanāyikadivase panā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Āgantuko ce bhikkhūti cīvare gāhite pacchā āgato āgantuko bhikkhu. Pattaṭṭhāneti vassaggena āgantukabhikkhuno [M 2.0048] pattaṭṭhāne. Paṭhamavassūpagatāti āgantukassa āgamanato puretarameva pacchimikāya vassūpanāyikāya vassūpagatā. Laddhaṃ laddhanti punappunaṃ dāyakānaṃ santikā āgatāgatasāṭakaṃ.

The phrase beginning with ‘from the dawn of the first day’ is said with reference to the day of entering the rains-residence. But the allowance for the intervening month may be accepted even after passing the first day. One who wanders with such thoughts having arisen as, “Where indeed shall I reside? Where will it be comfortable for me to reside? Or where shall I obtain requisites?” is a ‘vitakkacāriko’ (one who wanders with thought). Now, to explain the procedure when donors offer a rains-residence offering to those who have completed the later rains-residence, the passage beginning with ‘But on the day of entering the later rains-residence…’ is introduced. “If a visiting bhikkhu” means a visiting bhikkhu who has arrived after the robe-cloth has been taken. “In the bowl’s place” means in the place for the visiting bhikkhu’s bowl at the end of the rains. “Those who entered the first rains” refers to those who entered the rains during the later rains-entry period, before the arrival of the visiting bhikkhu. “Whatever is received” means the cloth that comes again and again from the donors.

Sādiyantāpi hi teneva vassāvāsikassa sāminoti chinnavassattā vuttaṃ. Paṭhamameva katikāya katattā “neva adātuṃ labhantī”ti vuttaṃ, dātabbaṃ vārentānaṃ gīvā hotīti adhippāyo. Tesameva dātabbanti vassūpagatesu aladdhavassāvāsikānaṃ ekaccānameva dātabbaṃ. Bhatiniviṭṭhanti bhatiṃ katvā viya niviṭṭhaṃ pariyiṭṭhaṃ. Bhatiniviṭṭhanti vā pānīyupaṭṭhānādibhatiṃ katvā laddhaṃ. Saṅghikaṃ panātiādi kesañci vādadassanaṃ. Tattha saṅghikaṃ pana apalokanakammaṃ katvā gāhitanti tatruppādaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tattha apalokanakammaṃ katvā gāhitanti “chinnavassāvāsikañca idāni uppajjanakavassāvāsikañca imesaṃ dātuṃ ruccatī”ti anantare vuttanayena [V 2.0036] apalokanaṃ katvā gāhitaṃ saṅghena dinnattā vibbhantopi labhateva, pageva chinnavasso. Paccayavasena gāhitaṃ pana temāsaṃ vasitvā gahetuṃ attanā dāyakehi ca anumatattā bhatiniviṭṭhampi chinnavassopi vibbhantopi na labhatīti keci ācariyā vadanti. Idañca pacchā vuttattā pamāṇaṃ, teneva vassūpanāyikadivase evaṃ dāyakehi dinnaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ gahitabhikkhuno vassacchedaṃ akatvā vāsova heṭṭhā vihito, na pānīyupaṭṭhānādibhatikaraṇamattaṃ. Yadi hi taṃ bhatiniviṭṭhameva siyā, bhatikaraṇameva vidhātabbaṃ, tasmā vassaggena gāhitaṃ chinnavassādayo na labhantīti veditabbaṃ.

For even while accepting, it is said that because of the broken rains-residence, he is not the owner of the rains-residence offering. Since an agreement was made at the very beginning, it is said, ‘They are not able to not give,’ the intention being that those who prevent what should be given are at fault. ‘It should be given only to them’ means it should be given only to some of those who have entered the rains but have not received the rains-residence offering. ‘Established by service’ means established as if having performed a service, sought out. Or, ‘established by service’ means obtained by performing a service such as providing drinking water and attendance. The passage beginning ‘But what is communal…’ is the presentation of the view of some. Therein, ‘but what is communal, having been taken after performing an act of announcement,’ is said with reference to what has arisen there. Therein, ‘taken after performing an act of announcement’ means: having made an announcement in the aforementioned way, saying, ‘It is agreeable to give the rains-residence offering for the broken rains and the one now arising to these ones,’ what is taken, because it is given by the Saṅgha, is obtained even by one who has left the order, let alone one with a broken rains-residence. But some teachers say that what is taken on the basis of a requisite, because it was agreed upon by oneself and the donors to be taken after residing for three months, even if established by service, is not obtained by one with a broken rains-residence or one who has left the order. And this, because it is stated later, is the authority. For that reason, for a bhikkhu who has accepted a rains-residence offering given thus by donors on the very day of entering the rains, residence without a break in the rains is prescribed below, not merely the performance of a service like providing drinking water and attendance. For if it were only established by service, only the performance of service would be prescribed. Therefore, it should be understood that what is taken at the end of the rains is not obtained by those with a broken rains-residence and so on.

“Idha, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuttho bhikkhu vibbhamati, saṅghasseva ta”nti (mahāva. 374-375) vacanato “vataṭṭhāne…pe… saṅghikaṃ hotī”ti vuttaṃ[M 2.0049]. Saṅghikaṃ hotīti etena vutthavassānampi vassāvāsikabhāgo saṅghikato amocito tesaṃ vibbhamena saṅghiko hotīti dasseti. Manusseti dāyakamanusse. Labhatīti “mama pattabhāvaṃ etassa dethā”ti dāyake sampaṭicchāpenteneva saṅghikato viyojitaṃ hotīti vuttaṃ. Varabhāgaṃ sāmaṇerassāti tassa paṭhamagāhattā, therena pubbe paṭhamabhāgassa gahitattā, idāni gayhamānassa dutiyabhāgattā ca vuttaṃ.

In accordance with the statement, ‘Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has completed the rains-residence leaves the order—that belongs to the Saṅgha’ (Mahāvagga 374-375), it is said, ‘in the designated place… it becomes communal.’ ‘It becomes communal’—by this it shows that even the share of the rains-residence offering of those who have completed the rains, not having been released from the Saṅgha, becomes communal through their leaving the order. ‘Humans’ means the donor humans. ‘He receives’—it is said that by getting the donors to agree, ‘Give my due share to this one,’ it becomes separated from what is communal. ‘The choice portion for the novice’—this is said because he is the first to take it, because the elder had previously taken the first portion, and because what is now being taken is the second portion.

222. Idāni antarāmuttasenāsanaggāhaṃ dassetuṃ “ayamaparopī”tyādimāha. Tattha aparopīti pubbe vuttasenāsanaggāhadvayato aññopīti attho. Nanu ca “ayaṃ senāsanaggāho nāma duvidho hoti utukāle ca vassāvāse cā”ti vutto, atha kasmā “ayamaparopī”tyādi vuttoti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “divasavasena hī”tiādi. Aparajjugatāya āsāḷhiyāti paṭhamavassūpanāyikadivasabhūtaṃ āsāḷhipuṇṇamiyā pāṭipadaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, māsagatāya āsāḷhiyāti dutiyavassūpanāyikadivasabhūtasāvaṇapuṇṇamiyā pāṭipadaṃ. Aparajjugatāya pavāraṇāti assayujapuṇṇamiyā pāṭipadaṃ.

222. Now, to show the acceptance of lodging during the interim period, he says, ‘This is another…’ and so on. Herein, ‘another’ means another different from the two types of lodging acceptance mentioned previously. With reference to the objection, ‘But was it not said, “This acceptance of lodging is of two kinds: during the seasons and during the rains-residence”? Why then is it said, “This is another…” and so on?’, he says, ‘By way of days…’ and so on. ‘By the latter part of Āsāḷhī’ is said with reference to the first day after the Āsāḷhī full moon, which is the day of entering the first rains-residence. ‘When a month has passed since Āsāḷhī’ refers to the first day after the Sāvaṇa full moon, which is the day of entering the second rains-residence. ‘By the latter part of the Pavāraṇā’ refers to the first day after the Assayuja full moon.

223. Utukāle paṭibāhituṃ na labhatīti hemantagimhesu aññe sampattabhikkhū paṭibāhituṃ na labhati. Navakammanti navakammasammuti. Akatanti aparisaṅkhataṃ. Vippakatanti aniṭṭhitaṃ. Ekaṃ mañcaṭṭhānaṃ datvāti ekaṃ mañcaṭṭhānaṃ puggalikaṃ datvā. Tibhāganti tatiyabhāgaṃ. Evaṃ vissajjanampi thāvarena thāvaraṃ parivattanaṭṭhāneyeva pavisati, na itarathā sabbasenāsanavissajjanato[V 2.0037]. Sace saddhivihārikādīnaṃ dātukāmo hotīti sace so saṅghassa bhaṇḍaṭhapanaṭṭhānaṃ vā aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vā dātuṃ na icchati, attano saddhivihārikādīnaññeva dātukāmo hoti, tādisassa [M 2.0050] “tuyhaṃ puggalikameva katvā jaggāhī”ti na sabbaṃ dātabbanti adhippāyo. Tatthassa kattabbavidhiṃ dassento āha “kamma”ntiādi. Evañhītiādimhi cayānurūpaṃ tatiyabhāge vā upaḍḍhabhāge vā gahite taṃ bhāgaṃ dātuṃ labhatīti attho. Yenāti tesu dvīsu tīsu bhikkhūsu yena. So sāmīti tassā bhūmiyā vihārakaraṇe sova sāmī, taṃ paṭibāhitvā itarena na kātabbanti adhippāyo.

223. ‘He is not able to prevent during the season’ means during the winter and summer seasons, he is not able to prevent other bhikkhus who have arrived. ‘New work’ means the authorization for new work. ‘Not done’ means not repaired. ‘Incomplete’ means not finished. ‘Having given one bed-space’ means having given one bed-space as personal property. ‘A third part’ means the third part. Even such a relinquishment is included only in the case of exchanging one permanent item for another, and not otherwise, as in the relinquishment of all lodgings. ‘If he wishes to give to his co-residents, etc.’ means if he does not wish to give the Saṅgha’s storage place or the dwelling place of other bhikkhus, but wishes to give only to his own co-residents, etc., the intention is that not everything should be given to such a person, saying, ‘Having made it your personal property, look after it.’ Showing the procedure to be followed by him in that case, he said, ‘action…’ and so on. In the passage beginning ‘For thus…’, the meaning is that when a third part or a half part corresponding to the accumulation has been taken, he is able to give that part. ‘By whom’ means by whichever of those two or three bhikkhus. ‘He is the owner’ means he is the owner in the matter of building a monastery on that land; the intention is that it should not be done by another, having prevented him.

224. Akataṭṭhāneti senāsanato bahi cayādīnaṃ akataṭṭhāne. Cayaṃ vā pamukhaṃ vāti saṅghikasenāsanaṃ nissāya tato bahi bandhitvā ekaṃ senāsanaṃ vā. Bahikuṭṭeti kuṭṭato bahi, attano kataṭṭhāneti attho. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

224. ‘In an undone place’ means in a place outside the lodging where an accumulation, etc., has not been made. ‘An accumulation or a porch’ means, depending on a communal lodging, having built one lodging outside of it. ‘Outside the wall’ means outside the wall; the meaning is in a place made by oneself. The rest is easily understood.

Senāsanaggāhakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the talk on the acceptance of lodgings is finished.

Catupaccayasādhāraṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discussion on the Four Shared Requisites.

225. Catupaccayasādhāraṇakathāyaṃ sammatena appamattakavissajjakenāti ñattidutiyakammavācāya vā apalokanakammena vā sammatena appamattakavissajjakasammutiladdhena. Avibhattaṃ saṅghikabhaṇḍanti pucchitabbakiccaṃ natthīti ettha avibhattaṃ saṅghikabhaṇḍanti kukkuccuppattiākāradassanaṃ, evaṃ kukkuccaṃ katvā pucchitabbakiccaṃ natthi, apucchitvāva dātabbanti adhippāyo. Kasmāti ce? Ettakassa saṅghikabhaṇḍassa vissajjanatthāyeva samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā katasammutikammattā. Guḷapiṇḍe…pe… dātabboti ettha guḷapiṇḍaṃ tālapakkappamāṇanti veditabbaṃ. Piṇḍāya paviṭṭhassapīti idaṃ upalakkhaṇamattaṃ. Aññena kāraṇena bahisīmagatassapi eseva [M 2.0051] nayo. Odanapaṭivīsoti saṅghabhattādisaṅghikaodanapaṭivīso. Antoupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitassāti anādare sāmivacanaṃ, antoupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitasseva gāhetuṃ vaṭṭati, na bahiupacārasīmaṃ pattassāti attho. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 325) “bahiupacārasīmāya ṭhitānaṃ gāhethāti vadanti, na gāhetabba”nti. Antogāmaṭṭhānampīti ettha pi-saddo avuttasampiṇḍanattho, antogāmaṭṭhānampi bahigāmaṭṭhānampi [V 2.0038] gāhetuṃ vaṭṭatīti attho. Sambhāvanattho vā, tena antogāmaṭṭhānampi gāhetuṃ vaṭṭati, pageva bahigāmaṭṭhānanti.

225. In the discussion on the four shared requisites, 'by one appointed as a distributor of minor items' means by one appointed either by a motion with a second announcement (ñattidutiyakamma) or by an act of seeking consent (apalokanakamma), having obtained the appointment as a distributor of minor items. 'The undistributed property of the Saṅgha—is there a need to ask?' Here, 'undistributed property of the Saṅgha' is mentioned to show the occasion for scruple. Having had such a scruple, there is no need to ask; the intention is that it should be given without asking. Why is that? Because the act of appointment was made with the consent of a united Saṅgha solely for the purpose of distributing this much of the Saṅgha's property. Regarding 'a lump of sugar... should be given'—here, the lump of sugar should be understood to be the size of a ripe palmyra fruit. 'Even for one who has entered for alms-round'—this is merely an indication. The same principle applies to one who has gone outside the boundary for another reason. 'A portion of rice' means a portion of rice from the Saṅgha's meal or other provisions belonging to the Saṅgha. 'For one standing within the approach boundary'—this is the genitive case used to show disregard. The meaning is that it is permissible for one standing within the approach boundary to receive it, but not for one who has reached beyond the approach boundary. For it is said in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 325): 'They say, "Let those standing beyond the approach boundary receive it," but it should not be received.' 'Even for one in a place within the village'—here, the particle 'pi' serves to include what is unstated. The meaning is that it is permissible for one in a place within the village to receive it, as well as for one in a place outside the village. Or, it is for the sake of emphasis; thus, it is permissible for one in a place within the village to receive it, and all the more so for one in a place outside the village.

Catupaccayasādhāraṇakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discussion on the Four Shared Requisites is concluded.

Iti vinayasaṅgahasaṃvaṇṇanābhūte vinayālaṅkāre

Thus, in the Vinayālaṅkāra, which is a commentary on the Vinaya Saṅgaha.

Catupaccayabhājanīyavinicchayakathālaṅkāro nāma

The Ornament Called 'The Discussion on the Determination of the Distribution of the Four Requisites'.

Aṭṭhavīsatimo paricchedo.

The Twenty-Eighth Chapter.

Vihāravinicchayakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discussion of the Determination of Dwellings.

Idāni catupaccayantogadhattā vihārassa catupaccayabhājanakathānantaraṃ vihāravinicchayakathā ārabhīyate. Tatridaṃ vuccati –

Now, since the dwelling is included within the four requisites, following the discussion on the distribution of the four requisites, the discussion on the determination of dwellings begins. Herein, this is said:

“Ko vihāro kenaṭṭhena;

Vihāro so katividho;

Kena so kassa dātabbo;

Kathaṃ ko tassa issaro.

"What is a dwelling, and in what sense? How many kinds of dwellings are there? By whom should it be given, and to whom? How is one its master?

“Kena so gāhito kassa;

Anuṭṭhāpaniyā kati;

Katihaṅgehi yuttassa;

Dhuvavāsāya dīyate”ti.

"By whom is it received, and for whom? How many are not to be removed? To one endowed with how many factors is it given for permanent residence?"

Tattha [M 2.0052] ko vihāroti catūsu paccayesu senāsanasaṅkhāto catūsu senāsanesu vihārasenāsanasaṅkhāto bhikkhūnaṃ nivāsabhūto patissayaviseso. Kenaṭṭhena vihāroti viharanti etthāti vihāro, iriyāpathadibbabrahmaariyasaṅkhātehi catūhi vihārehi ariyā ettha viharantītyattho. [V 2.0039] So katividhoti saṅghikavihāragaṇasantakavihārapuggalikavihāravasena tibbidho. Vuttañhetaṃ samantapāsādikāyaṃ “cātuddisaṃ saṅghaṃ uddissa bhikkhūnaṃ dinnaṃ vihāraṃ vā pariveṇaṃ vā āvāsaṃ vā mahantampi khuddakampi abhiyuñjato abhiyogo na ruhati, acchinditvā gaṇhitumpi na sakkoti. Kasmā? Sabbesaṃ dhuranikkhepābhāvato. Na hettha sabbe cātuddisā bhikkhū dhuranikkhepaṃ karontīti. Dīghabhāṇakādibhedassa pana gaṇassa, ekapuggalassa vā santakaṃ abhiyuñjitvā gaṇhanto sakkoti te dhuraṃ nikkhipāpetuṃ, tasmā tattha ārāme vuttanayeneva vinicchayo veditabbo”ti. Iminā dāyakasantako vihāro nāma natthīti dīpeti.

Here, what is a dwelling? It is designated as a lodging among the four requisites, specifically a dwelling-lodging among the four lodgings, serving as a residence for monks, a special shelter. What is the meaning of a dwelling? It is called a dwelling because they dwell there—meaning, noble ones dwell here with the four abidings, namely, postures, divine, brahma, and noble. How many kinds are there? It is threefold: a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, a dwelling belonging to a group, and a dwelling belonging to an individual. For it is said in the Samantapāsādikā: "A dwelling, a cell, or a residence—whether large or small—given to the Saṅgha of the four directions for the use of monks, anyone who attempts to seize it cannot succeed, nor can they take it by force. Why? Because there is no relinquishing of responsibility by all. Not all monks of the four directions relinquish responsibility here. However, if it belongs to a particular group, such as the Long Reciters, or to an individual, one can seize it by pressing the claim and make them relinquish responsibility. Therefore, in such a monastery, the decision should be understood according to the method stated." By this, it is shown that there is no dwelling belonging solely to the donor.

Kena so dātabboti khattiyena vā brāhmaṇena vā yena kenaci so vihāro dātabbo. Kassa dātabboti saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā puggalassa vā dātabbo. Kathaṃ dātabboti yadi saṅghassa deti, “imaṃ vihāraṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa dammī”ti, yadi gaṇassa, “imaṃ vihāraṃ āyasmantānaṃ dammī”ti, yadi puggalassa, “imaṃ vihāraṃ āyasmato dammī”ti dātabbo. Ko tassa issaroti yadi saṅghassa deti, saṅgho tassa vihārassa issaro. Yadi gaṇassa deti, gaṇo tassa issaro. Yadi puggalassa deti, puggalo tassa issaroti. Tathā [M 2.0053] hi vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “dīghabhāṇakādikassa pana gaṇassa ekapuggalassa vā santaka”nti.

By whom should it be given? By a noble, a brahmin, or anyone whosoever, that dwelling should be given. To whom should it be given? It should be given to the Saṅgha, to a group, or to an individual. How should it be given? If giving to the Saṅgha, one should say, "I give this dwelling to the Saṅgha of the four quarters, to those who have come and those who will come." If giving to a group, one should say, "I give this dwelling to the venerable ones." If giving to an individual, one should say, "I give this dwelling to the venerable one." Who has authority over it? If given to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha has authority over that dwelling. If given to a group, the group has authority over it. If given to an individual, the individual has authority over it. Thus it is said in the commentary: "But for the group of Long-reciters and so on, or for a single individual, it is their property."

Kena so gāhitoti senāsanaggāhāpakena so vihāro gāhito. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannituṃ, yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, evañca, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo, paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo, yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

By whom is it assigned? It is assigned by the lodging-assigner. For this was said by the Blessed One: 'I allow, monks, that a lodging-assigner possessing five qualities be appointed: one who would not go to partiality through desire, would not go to partiality through aversion, and would not go to partiality through delusion. And thus, monks, should he be appointed: first, a monk should be asked; having asked, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and able monk—'

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammanneyya, esā ñatti.

"Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If the Saṅgha is ready, let the Saṅgha appoint the monk named so-and-so as the lodging-assigner. This is the motion."

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno senāsanaggāhāpakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

"Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha is appointing the monk named so-and-so as the lodging-assigner. If it is agreeable to the venerable ones that the monk named so-and-so be appointed as the lodging-assigner, let them be silent. If it is not agreeable to anyone, let them speak."

“Sammato [V 2.0040] saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu senāsanaggāhāpako, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti (cūḷava. 317).

"The monk named so-and-so has been appointed by the Saṅgha as the lodging-assigner. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha; therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it." (Cūḷavagga 317).

Kassa so gāhitoti bhikkhūnaṃ so vihāro gāhito. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ bhikkhū gaṇetuṃ, bhikkhū gaṇetvā seyyā gaṇetuṃ, seyyā gaṇetvā seyyaggena gāhetu”nti (cūḷava. 318). Anuṭṭhāpaniyā katīti cattāro anuṭṭhāpanīyā vuḍḍhataro gilāno bhaṇḍāgāriko saṅghato laddhasenāsanoti. Vuttañhetaṃ kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ (kaṅakhā. aṭṭha. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “vuḍḍho hi attano vuḍḍhatāya anuṭṭhāpanīyo[M 2.0054], gilāno gilānatāya, saṅgho pana bhaṇḍāgārikassa vā dhammakathikavinayadharagaṇavācakācariyānaṃ vā bahūpakārataṃ guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhetvā dhuvavāsatthāya vihāraṃ sallakkhetvā sammannitvā deti, tasmā yassa saṅghena dinno, sopi anuṭṭhāpanīyo”ti.

"To whom was it assigned?" The dwelling was assigned to the monks. For this was said by the Blessed One: "I allow, monks, first to count the monks, then to count the lodgings, and after counting the lodgings, to assign it by allotment of lodgings" (Cūḷavagga 318). "How many cannot be removed?" Four cannot be removed: an elderly monk, a sick monk, the storekeeper, and one who has been given a dwelling by the Saṅgha. For this was stated in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī (Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā): "An elder should not be removed due to his old age, a sick monk due to his illness, but the Saṅgha, considering the great help and special qualities of the storekeeper, or the Dhamma speaker, the Vinaya holder, the group reciter, or the teacher, having carefully considered a monastery for permanent residence, having agreed, gives it; therefore, whoever has been given a dwelling by the Saṅgha, he also cannot be removed."

Katihaṅgehi yuttassa dhuvavāsāya dīyateti ukkaṭṭhaparicchedena dvīhi aṅgehi yuttassa dhuvavāsatthāya vihāro dīyate. Katamehi dvīhi? Bahūpakāratāya guṇavisiṭṭhatāya ceti. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Bahūpakāratanti bhaṇḍāgārikatādibahuupakārabhāvaṃ, na kevalaṃ idamevāti āha ‘guṇavisiṭṭhatañcā’ti. Tena bahūpakārattepi guṇavisiṭṭhattābhāve guṇavisiṭṭhattepi bahūpakārattābhāve dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti dassetī”ti vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ (kaṅakhā. abhi. ṭī. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vacanato. Omakaparicchedena ekena aṅgena yuttassapi. Katamena ekena aṅgena? Bahūpakāratāya vā guṇavisiṭṭhatāya vā. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Bahūpakārataṃ guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhentoti bhaṇḍāgārikassa bahūpakārataṃ, dhammakathikādīnaṃ guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhento”ti sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.119-121) vacanato.

"To whom endowed with how many factors is a permanent dwelling given?" According to the strict definition, a dwelling is given for permanent residence to one endowed with two factors. Which two? Being of great assistance and being distinguished by virtue. How is this understood? It is stated in the Vinayatthamañjūsā: “‘Being of great assistance’ refers to the state of providing much help, such as serving as a storekeeper. It is not limited to this alone; hence it is said, ‘and being distinguished by virtue.’ Thus, it is shown that it is permissible to give even if one is of great assistance but lacks distinction in virtue, or is distinguished in virtue but lacks great assistance.” According to the lenient definition, it may be given even to one endowed with a single factor. Which single factor? Either being of great assistance or being distinguished by virtue. How is this understood? It is stated in the Sāratthadīpanī: “Considering being of great assistance and being distinguished by virtue, that is, considering the great assistance of a storekeeper and the distinguished virtue of Dhamma preachers and others.”

Senāsanaggāho pana duvidho utukāle ca vassāvāse cāti kālavasena. Atha vā tayo senāsanaggāhā purimako pacchimako antarāmuttakoti. Tesaṃ viseso heṭṭhā vuttova. “Utukāle senāsanaggāho antarāmuttako ca taṅkhaṇapaṭisallāno cāti dubbidho. Vassāvāse senāsanaggāho purimako ca pacchimako cāti dubbidhoti cattāro senāsanaggāhā”ti ācariyā [V 2.0041] vadanti, taṃ vacanaṃ pāḷiyampi aṭṭhakathāyampi na āgataṃ[M 2.0055]. Pāḷiyaṃ (cūḷava. 318) pana “tayome, bhikkhave, senāsanaggāhā purimako pacchimako antarāmuttako”icceva āgato, aṭṭhakathāyampi (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) “tīsu senāsanaggāhesu purimako ca pacchimako cāti ime dve gāhā thāvarā, antarāmuttake ayaṃ vinicchayo”ti āgato.

The appropriation of lodgings is of two kinds according to time: during the regular season and during the rains residence. Alternatively, there are three kinds of lodging appropriation: the initial, the subsequent, and the intermediate. Their distinctions have been explained above. Some teachers say, “During the regular season, lodging appropriation is of two kinds: the intermediate and the momentary. During the rains residence, lodging appropriation is of two kinds: the initial and the subsequent. Thus, there are four kinds of lodging appropriation.” But this statement is not found in the Pāli Canon or the commentaries. In the Pāli Canon (Cūḷavagga 318), however, it appears thus: “Monks, there are these three kinds of lodging appropriation: the initial, the subsequent, and the intermediate.” In the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 318), it appears thus: “Among the three kinds of lodging appropriation, these two—the initial and the subsequent—are permanent. Regarding the intermediate, this is the determination.”

Idāni pana ekacce ācariyā “imasmiṃ kāle sabbe vihārā saṅghikāva, puggalikavihāro nāma natthi. Kasmā? Vihāradāyakānaṃ vihāradānakāle kulūpakā ‘imaṃ vihāraṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa demā’ti vacībhedaṃ kārāpenti, tasmā navavihārāpi saṅghikā eva. Ekaccesu vihāresu evaṃ avatvā dentesupi ‘tasmiṃ jīvante puggaliko hoti, mate saṅghikoyevā’ti vuttattā porāṇakavihārāpi saṅghikāva hontī”ti vadanti. Tatrevaṃ vicāretabbo – vacībhedaṃ kārāpetvā dinnavihāresupi dāyakā saṅghaṃ uddissa karontā nāma appakā, “imaṃ nāma bhikkhuṃ imaṃ nāma theraṃ vasāpessāmī”ti cintetvā puttadāramittāmaccādīhi sammantetvā patiṭṭhāpenti, patiṭṭhānakāle avadantāpi dānakāle yebhuyyena vadanti. Atha pana kulūpakā dānakāle sikkhāpetvā vadāpenti, evaṃ vadantāpi dāyakā appakā saṅghaṃ uddissa denti, bahutarā attano kulūpakameva uddissa denti. Evaṃ sante kulūpakānaṃ vacanaṃ navasu adhammikadānesu “puggalassa pariṇataṃ saṅghassa pariṇāmetī”ti (pārā. 660; pāci. 492) vuttaṃ ekaṃ adhammikadānaṃ āpajjati. “Tasmiṃ jīvante puggaliko, mate saṅghiko”ti ayaṃ pāṭho mūlapuggalikavisaye na āgato, mūlasaṅghikavihāraṃ jaggāpetuṃ puggalikakārāpanaṭṭhāne āgato, tasmā navavihārāpi puggalaṃ uddissa dinnā santiyeva. Porāṇakavihārāpi mūle puggalikavasena [M 2.0056] dinnā saddhivihārikādīnaṃ puggalikavaseneva dīyamānāpi tasmiṃ jīvanteyeva vissāsavasena gayhamānāpi puggalikā hontiyeva, tasmā sabbaso puggalikavihārassa abhāvavādo vicāretabbova.

Now, however, some teachers say: “At this time, all monasteries are communal; there is no such thing as a personal monastery. Why? Because at the time of donating a monastery, the attendant monks make the donors make a verbal declaration, saying, ‘We give this monastery to the Sangha of the four quarters, to those who have come and those who will come.’ Therefore, even new monasteries are communal. Even in some monasteries where it is not stated but given, it is said, ‘While that person lives, it is personal; after death, it becomes communal.’ Thus, even ancient monasteries are communal.” In this regard, it should be considered thus: Even in monasteries given with a verbal declaration, donors who dedicate them to the Sangha are few. Most think, “We will have this monk or this elder reside here,” and after consulting with their sons, wives, friends, and ministers, they establish them. Though they may not speak at the time of establishment, they mostly speak at the time of donation. Furthermore, the attendant monks instruct them on what to say at the time of donation. Even when they speak thus, few donors give to the Sangha; most give to their own attendant monk. In such cases, the attendants’ words fall under one of the nine improper donations, as stated: “What is intended for an individual is diverted to the Sangha” (Pārā. 660; Pāci. 492). The phrase, “While that person lives, it is personal; after death, it is communal,” does not appear in the context of what was originally a personal monastery. It appears in the context of making an originally communal monastery personal for the sake of its upkeep. Therefore, new monasteries given to individuals do indeed exist. Ancient monasteries, originally given as personal, even when given personally to co-residents, or even when held by trust as personal while the original recipient lives, remain personal. Therefore, the claim that there are no personal monasteries at all should be carefully examined.

Aññe pana ācariyā “imasmiṃ kāle saṅghikavihārā nāma na santi, sabbe puggalikāva. Kasmā? Navavihārāpi patiṭṭhāpanakāle dānakāle ca kulūpakabhikkhuṃyeva uddissa katattā puggalikāva, porāṇakavihārāpi sissānusissehi vā aññehi vā puggalehi eva pariggahitattā, na kadāci saṅghena pariggahitattā puggalikāva honti, na saṅghikā”ti vadanti. Tatrāpyevaṃ vicāretabbaṃ – navavihārepi patiṭṭhānakālepi dānakālepi ekacce saṅghaṃ uddissa [V 2.0042] karonti, ekacce puggalaṃ. Pubbeva puggalaṃ uddissa katepi atthakāmānaṃ paṇḍitānaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā puggalikadānato saṅghikadānameva mahapphalataranti saddahitvā saṅghike karontāpi dāyakā santi, puggalikavasena paṭiggahite porāṇakavihārepi keci bhikkhū maraṇakāle saṅghassa niyyātenti. Keci kassaci adatvā maranti, tadā so vihāro saṅghiko hoti. Savatthukamahāvihāre pana karontā rājarājamahāmattādayo “pañcavassasahassaparimāṇaṃ sāsanaṃ yāva tiṭṭhati, tāva mama vihāre vasitvā saṅgho cattāro paccaye paribhuñjatū”ti paṇidhāya cirakālaṃ saṅghassa paccayuppādakaraṃ gāmakhettādikaṃ “amhākaṃ vihārassa demā”ti denti, vihārassāti ca vihāre vasanakasaṅghassa uddissa denti, na kulūpakabhūtassa ekapuggalassa eva, tasmā yebhuyyena saṅghikā dissanti, pāsāṇesu akkharaṃ likhitvāpi ṭhapenti, tasmā sabbaso saṅghikavihārābhāvavādopi vicāretabbova.

Other teachers, however, say: “At this time, there are no Sangha-owned monasteries—all are personal. Why? Even newly built monasteries, because they are established and offered with a specific attendant monk in mind, are personal. Ancient monasteries, too, being taken over by disciples, successors, or other individuals, and never having been possessed by the Sangha, are personal, not Sangha-owned.” Here, too, this should be considered: Even with newly built monasteries, at the time of establishment or offering, some dedicate them to the Sangha, while others dedicate them to an individual. Even when previously offered to an individual, some donors, hearing the words of wise people who desire their benefit, and believing that offering to the Sangha yields far greater fruit than personal offerings, dedicate them to the Sangha. In ancient monasteries received as personal property, some monks, at the time of death, bequeath them to the Sangha. Others pass away without giving them to anyone—then, that monastery becomes Sangha-owned. In the great monasteries, however, kings, royal ministers, and others, when making offerings, resolve: “For as long as the Dispensation lasts—five thousand years—may the Sangha dwell in my monastery and enjoy the four requisites.” They provide villages, fields, and other long-term support that generates resources for the Sangha, saying, “We give this to our monastery,” meaning they dedicate it to the Sangha residing there, not to a single attendant monk. Thus, for the most part, they are seen to be Sangha-owned. They even inscribe these words in stone. Therefore, the claim that there are no Sangha-owned monasteries at all must also be carefully examined.

Apare [M 2.0057] pana ācariyā “imasmiṃ kāle vihāradāyakasantakāva, tasmā dāyakāyeva vicāretuṃ issarā, na saṅgho, na puggalo. Vihāradāyake asantepi tassa puttadhītunattapanattādayo yāva kulaparamparā tassa vihārassa issarāva honti. Kasmāti ce? ‘Yena vihāro kārito, so vihārasāmiko’ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 116) āgatattā ca ‘tassa vā kule yo koci āpucchitabbo’ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 116) ca vacanato vihārassāmibhūto dāyako vā tassa vaṃse uppanno vā vicāretuṃ issaro. ‘Pacchinne kulavaṃse yo tassa janapadassa sāmiko, so acchinditvā puna deti cittalapabbate bhikkhunā nīhaṭaṃ udakavāhakaṃ aḷanāgarājamahesī viya, evampi vaṭṭatī’ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.538-539) vacanato vihāradāyakassa kulavaṃse pacchinnepi tassa janapadassa issaro rājā vā rājamahāmatto vā yo koci issaro vā vihāraṃ vicāretuṃ yathājjhāsayaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vadanti, tampi aññe paṇḍitā nānujānanti.

Still other teachers say: “At this time, monasteries are the property of the donors; therefore, the donors alone have the authority to decide, not the Sangha or an individual. Even if the original donor of the monastery is no longer alive, his sons, daughters, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and so on, for as long as the family line continues, remain the owners of that monastery. Why is this? Because it is stated, ‘The one by whom the monastery was built is the owner of the monastery’ (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 116), and also, ‘Or whoever in his family should be asked’ (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 116). Thus, the donor who is the owner of the monastery, or anyone born in his lineage, has the authority to decide. The commentary states (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.538-539): ‘When the family line has ended, the ruler of that region may, without confiscating it, give it again; this is permissible, just as the chief queen of King Aḷanāga did with the water conduit on Cittalapabbata that had been taken by a monk.’ Thus, when the donor's family line has ended, the ruler of that region—be it a king, a royal minister, or any other authority—is permitted to administer the monastery and donate it according to their inclination.” But other wise ones do not approve of this view either.

Kathaṃ? “Yena vihāro kārito, so vihārasāmiko”ti vacanaṃ pubbavohāravasena vuttaṃ, na idāni issaravasena yathā jetavanaṃ, pattassāmikotyādi. Yathā hi jetassa rājakumārassa vanaṃ uyyānaṃ jetavananti viggahe kate yadipi anāthapiṇḍikena kiṇitvā vihārapatiṭṭhāpanakālato paṭṭhāya rājakumāro tassa uyyānassa issaro na hoti, tathāpi anāthapiṇḍikena kiṇitakālato pubbe issarabhūtapubbattā pubbavohāravasena sabbadāpi jetavanantveva [V 2.0043] voharīyati. Yathā ca pattassa sāmiko pattassāmikoti viggahe kate yadipi dāyakehi kiṇitvā bhikkhussa dinnakālato paṭṭhāya kammāro pattassa issaro na hoti, tathāpi dāyakena kiṇitakālato [M 2.0058] pubbe issarabhūtapubbattā pubbavohāravasena pattassāmikotveva voharīyati, evaṃ yadipi bhikkhussa dinnakālato paṭṭhāya dāyako vihārassa issaro na hoti vatthupariccāgalakkhaṇattā dānassa, tathāpi dānakālato pubbe issarabhūtapubbattā pubbavohāravasena vihārassāmikotveva voharīyati, na mukhyato issarabhāvatoti viññāyati, tasmā saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā puggalassa vā dinnakālato paṭṭhāya saṅghādayo paṭiggāhakā eva vicāretuṃ issarā, na dāyako.

How so? The statement, “The one who had the monastery built is the owner of the monastery,” is said by way of past convention, not in the sense of present ownership, as in the case of Jetavana, the owner of a bowl, and so forth. For example, when Prince Jeta’s grove, his park, was analyzed as Jetavana, even though from the time Anāthapiṇḍika purchased it and established the monastery the prince was no longer the owner of that park, still, because he had formerly been the owner before Anāthapiṇḍika bought it, it is always referred to by way of past convention as Jetavana. Similarly, when ‘owner of a bowl’ is analyzed, even though from the time the donors purchased it and gave it to a bhikkhu the craftsman is no longer the owner of the bowl, still, because he had formerly been the owner before the donor bought it, he is referred to by way of past convention as the owner of the bowl. Likewise, even though from the time the donor gave the monastery to a bhikkhu the donor is no longer the owner of the monastery—because the characteristic of a gift is the relinquishment of the object—still, because he had formerly been the owner before the giving, he is referred to by way of past convention as the owner of the monastery; it is understood that this is not ownership in the primary sense. Therefore, from the time the gift is given to the Sangha, a group, or an individual, the recipients, such as the Sangha, are the ones with the authority to administer it, not the donor.

Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? Santesupi anāthapiṇḍikādīsu vihāradāyakesu “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannitu”ntiādinā (cūḷava. 317) saṅghena sammataṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ anujānitvā, “anujānāmi, bhikkhave…pe… seyyaggena gāhetu”ntiādinā (cūḷava. 318) senāsanaggāhāpakasseva vicāretuṃ issarabhāvassa vacanato ca “dve bhikkhū saṅghikaṃ bhūmiṃ gahetvā sodhetvā saṅghikaṃ senāsanaṃ karonti, yena sā bhūmi paṭhamaṃ gahitā, so sāmī”ti ca “ubhopi puggalikaṃ karonti, soyeva sāmī”ti ca “yo pana saṅghikaṃ vallimattampi aggahetvā āharimena upakaraṇena saṅghikāya bhūmiyā puggalikavihāraṃ kāreti, upaḍḍhaṃ saṅghikaṃ upaḍḍhaṃ puggalika”nti ca saṅghapuggalānaṃyeva sāmibhāvassa aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttattā ca viññāyati.

If it is asked, 'How is this known?' It is known because, even though there were monastery donors like Anāthapiṇḍika, the Buddha allowed the appointment of an assigner of lodgings approved by the Sangha, saying, “Bhikkhus, I allow you to appoint a bhikkhu possessing five qualities as an assigner of lodgings” (Cūḷavagga 317), and so on; and because of the statement of the authority of that very assigner of lodgings to administer, “Bhikkhus, I allow… to assign by the best lodging” (Cūḷavagga 318), and so on; and because it is stated in the commentary that ownership belongs only to the Sangha and to individuals, as in: “Two bhikkhus take land belonging to the Sangha, clear it, and build a dwelling for the Sangha. The one who first took that land is the owner,” and “If both make it for individual use, that same one is the owner,” and “But one who, without taking even so much as a creeper’s worth of what belongs to the Sangha, has an individual monastery built on the Sangha’s land with materials brought from elsewhere, half belongs to the Sangha and half is for individual use.”

“Tassa vā kule yo koci āpucchitabbo”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanampi tesaṃ vihārassa issarabhāvadīpakaṃ na hoti, atha kho gamiko bhikkhu disaṃ gantukāmo vihāre āpucchitabbabhikkhusāmaṇeraārāmikesu [M 2.0059] asantesu te āpucchitvā gantabbabhāvameva dīpeti. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “imaṃ pana dasavidhampi seyyaṃ saṅghike vihāre santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā pakkamantena āpucchitvā pakkamitabbaṃ, āpucchantena ca bhikkhumhi sati bhikkhu āpucchitabbo…pe… tasmiṃ asati ārāmiko, tasmimpi asati yena vihāro kārito, so vihārassāmiko, tassa vā kule yo koci āpucchitabbo”ti. Evaṃ ārāmikassapi āpucchitabbato olokanatthāya vattasīseneva āpucchitabbo, na tesaṃ saṅghikasenāsanassa issarabhāvatoti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

The commentary's statement, 'or whoever is in that family should be asked,' also does not indicate their ownership of the monastery. Rather, it clarifies that a bhikkhu who is a traveler, intending to go to another region, should ask them before leaving only in the absence of bhikkhus, sāmaṇeras, and monastery attendants in the monastery who ought to be asked. For it is stated in the commentary: 'However, having spread or had spread any of these ten kinds of bedding in a monastery belonging to the Sangha, one who is departing should depart after asking. And when asking, if there is a bhikkhu, a bhikkhu should be asked… if there is none, a monastery attendant; if even he is absent, then the one by whom the monastery was built—he is the owner of the monastery—or whoever is in his family should be asked.' Thus, it should be understood that since even a monastery attendant is to be asked, he is to be asked for the sake of looking after things, simply as a matter of duty, not because they have ownership of the Sangha's lodging.
