“Pacchinne [V 2.0044] kulavaṃse”tyādivacanañca akappiyavasena katānaṃ akappiyavohārena paṭiggahitānaṃ khettavatthutaḷākādīnaṃ akappiyattā bhikkhūhi pariccattānaṃ kappiyakaraṇatthāya rājādīhi gahetvā puna tesaṃyeva bhikkhūnaṃ dānameva dīpeti, na tesaṃ rājādīnaṃ tehi bhikkhūhi aññesaṃ saṅghagaṇapuggalacetiyānaṃ dānaṃ. Yadi dadeyyuṃ, adhammikadānaadhammikapaaggahaadhammikaparibhogā siyuṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre (pari. aṭṭha. 329) “nava adhammikāni dānāni saṅghassa pariṇataṃ aññasaṅghassa vā cetiyassa vā puggalassa vā pariṇāmeti, cetiyassa pariṇataṃ aññacetiyassa vā saṅghassa vā puggalassa vā pariṇāmeti, puggalassa pariṇataṃ aññapuggalassa vā saṅghassa vā cetiyassa vā pariṇāmetī”ti. Aṭṭhakathāyañca (pari. aṭṭha. 329) “nava adhammikāni dānānīti…pe… evaṃ vuttāni. Nava paṭiggahaparibhogāti etesaṃyeva dānānaṃ paṭiggahā ca paribhogā cā”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā yadi rājādayo issarāti gahetvā aññassa deyyuṃ, tampi dānaṃ adhammikadānaṃ hoti, taṃ dānaṃ paṭiggahā [M 2.0060] ca adhammikapaṭiggahā honti, taṃ dānaṃ paribhuñjantā ca adhammikaparibhogā hontīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

And the statement ‘when the family line is cut off,’ etc., indicates only the giving back to those very same bhikkhus by kings and others, after they have taken fields, grounds, reservoirs, etc., that were relinquished by the bhikkhus on account of being unallowable—having been made in an unallowable manner and accepted through an unallowable transaction—for the purpose of making them allowable. It does not indicate a gift by those kings and others to another Sangha, group, individual, or cetiya of what was received from those bhikkhus. If they were to give it, there would be an unrighteous gift, unrighteous acceptance, and unrighteous use. For it is stated in the Parivāra (Pari. Aṭṭha. 329): ‘There are nine unrighteous gifts: one diverts what has been designated for the Sangha to another Sangha, or to a cetiya, or to an individual; one diverts what has been designated for a cetiya to another cetiya, or to the Sangha, or to an individual; one diverts what has been designated for an individual to another individual, or to the Sangha, or to a cetiya.’ And in the commentary (Pari. Aṭṭha. 329) it is stated: ‘“Nine unrighteous gifts”… and so on… are thus stated. “Nine unrighteous acceptances and uses” refers to the acceptances and uses of these very gifts.’ Therefore, it should be understood that if kings or others, considering themselves owners, were to give it to another, that gift too would be an unrighteous gift, the acceptance of that gift would be an unrighteous acceptance, and those using that gift would be engaging in unrighteous use.

Athāpi evaṃ vadeyyuṃ “vihāradānaṃ saṅghassa, aggaṃ buddhena vaṇṇitantiādīsu (cūḷava. 295, 315) ‘saṅghassā’ti ayaṃ saddo ‘dāna’nti ettha sāmisambandho na hoti, atha kho sampadānameva, ‘dāyakassā’ti pana sāmisambandho ajjhāharitabbo, tasmā sāmibhūto dāyakova issaro, na sampadānabhūto saṅgho”ti. Te evaṃ vattabbā – “vihāradānaṃ saṅghassā”ti idaṃ dānasamaye pavattavasena vuttaṃ, na dinnasamaye pavattavasena. Dānakāle hi dāyako attano vatthubhūtaṃ vihāraṃ saṅghassa pariccajitvā deti, tasmā tasmiṃ samaye dāyako sāmī hoti, saṅgho sampadānaṃ, dinnakāle pana saṅghova sāmī hoti vihārassa paṭiggahitattā, na dāyako pariccattattā, tasmā saṅgho vicāretuṃ issaro. Tenāha bhagavā “pariccattaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, dāyakehī”ti (cūḷava. 273). Idaṃ pana saddalakkhaṇagarukā saddahissantīti vuttaṃ, atthato pana cīvarādīnaṃ catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ dānakāleyeva dāyakasantakabhāvo dinnakālato paṭṭhāya paṭiggāhakasantakabhāvo sabbesaṃ pākaṭo, tasmā idampi vacanaṃ dāyakasantakabhāvasādhakaṃ na hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Or if they should say thus: 'In phrases such as “the gift of a monastery to the Sangha, declared supreme by the Buddha” (Cūḷavagga 295, 315), the word “to the Sangha” does not here imply a possessive relationship to “gift,” but rather indicates the recipient. However, a possessive relationship to “donor” must be supplied. Therefore, the donor, being the owner, is the one with authority, not the Sangha, which is merely the recipient.' They should be told thus: 'The phrase “the gift of a monastery to the Sangha” is stated with reference to the time of giving, not with reference to the time after it has been given. For at the time of giving, the donor relinquishes the monastery, which is his property, and gives it to the Sangha. Therefore, at that time, the donor is the owner, and the Sangha is the recipient. But after the gift has been given, the Sangha itself becomes the owner of the monastery because it has been accepted, while the donor is no longer the owner, having relinquished it. Hence, the Sangha has the authority to administer it.' Thus the Blessed One said: 'Bhikkhus, it has been relinquished by the donors' (Cūḷavagga 273). This, however, is stated for those who give weight to grammatical points. But in reality, regarding the four requisites—robes, and so on—it is clear to all that ownership by the donor applies only at the time of giving, whereas from the time of acceptance onward, ownership belongs to the recipient. Therefore, it should be understood that this statement also does not serve to prove the donor’s ownership.

Evaṃ hotu, tathāpi “sace bhikkhūhi pariccattabhāvaṃ ñatvā sāmiko vā tassa puttadhītaro [V 2.0045] vā añño vā koci vaṃse uppanno puna kappiyavohārena deti, vaṭṭatī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.538-539) vuttattā vihārassāmikabhūtadāyakassa vā tassa puttadhītādīnaṃ vaṃse uppannānaṃ vā dātuṃ issarabhāvo siddhoyevāti. Na siddho. Kasmāti ce? Nanu vuttaṃ “bhikkhūhi pariccattabhāvaṃ ñatvā”ti, tasmā akappiyattā bhikkhūhi pariccattameva kappiyakaraṇatthāya dāyakādīhi puna [M 2.0061] kappiyavohārena deti, vaṭṭati. Yathā appaṭiggahitattā bhikkhūhi aparibhuttameva khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ bhikkhusantakaṃyeva āpattimocanatthaṃ dāyakādayo paṭiggahāpeti, na paribhuttaṃ, yathā ca bījagāmapariyāpannaṃyeva bhikkhusantakaṃ bījagāmabhūtagāmabhāvato parimocanatthaṃ kappiyakārakādayo kappiyaṃ karonti, na apariyāpannaṃ, evaṃ akappiyaṃ bhikkhūhi pariccattaṃyeva taḷākādikaṃ kappiyakaraṇatthaṃ dāyakādayo puna denti, na apariccattaṃ, tasmā idampi vacanaṃ kappiyakaraṇattaṃyeva sādheti, na issarattanti viññāyati.

So let it be. Nevertheless, since it is stated in the commentary (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.538-539): 'If, knowing that the monks have relinquished it, the owner or his sons and daughters or anyone else born in his lineage gives it again through allowable means, it is valid,' the authority of the donor, who is the owner of the monastery, or his sons and daughters or others born in his lineage to give is indeed established. It is not established. Why? Was it not said, 'knowing that the monks have relinquished it'? Therefore, because it is unallowable, only what has been relinquished by the monks is given again by the donors or others through allowable means for the purpose of making it allowable, and this is valid. Just as, because it has not been accepted, the food and drink that belongs to the monks, which has not been consumed by them, is caused to be accepted by the donors or others for the purpose of freeing them from an offense—not what has been consumed—and just as only seeds and plants belonging to the monks are made allowable by those who make things allowable for the purpose of freeing them from the state of being seeds and plants—not what is not included within those categories—so too, only what is unallowable and relinquished by the monks, such as a pond, is given again by the donors or others for the purpose of making it allowable—not what has not been relinquished. Therefore, this statement too serves only to establish the making of things allowable, not authority. Thus it should be understood.

Tathāpi evaṃ vadeyyuṃ “jātibhūmiyaṃ jātibhūmikā upāsakā āyasmantaṃ dhammikattheraṃ sattahi jātibhūmikavihārehi pabbājayiṃsūti vacanato dāyako vihārassa issaroti viññāyati. Issarattāyeva hi te theraṃ pabbājetuṃ sakkā, no anissarā”ti, na kho panevaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kasmā? “Jātibhūmikā upāsakā”icceva hi vuttaṃ, na “vihāradāyakā”ti, tasmā tasmiṃ dese vasantā bahavo upāsakā āyasmantaṃ dhammikattheraṃ ayuttacārittā sakalasattavihārato pabbājayiṃsu, na attano vihāradāyakabhāvena issarattā, tasmā idampi udāharaṇaṃ na issarabhāvadīpakaṃ, atha kho aparādhānurūpakaraṇabhāvadīpakanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ yadā dāyako vihāraṃ patiṭṭhāpetvā deti, tassa muñcacetanaṃ patvā dinnakālato paṭṭhāya so vā tassa vaṃse uppanno vā janapadassāmikarājādayo vā issarā bhavituṃ vā vicāretuṃ vā na labhanti, paṭiggāhakabhūto saṅgho vā gaṇo vā puggalo vā soyeva issaro bhavituṃ vā vicāretuṃ vā labhatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Even so, they might say: 'The lay devotees native to the birthplace expelled the Venerable Dhammika Thera from the seven monasteries in his birthplace. From this, it is understood that the donor is the owner of the monastery. For only as owners could they expel the elder, not as non-owners.' But this should not be seen thus. Why? Because it is said 'native lay devotees,' not 'donors of the monastery.' Therefore, many lay devotees living in that region expelled the Venerable Dhammika Thera from all seven monasteries due to his improper conduct, not by the authority of being donors of the monastery. Thus, this example too does not illustrate ownership, but rather illustrates the act of applying punishment befitting the offense. This should be understood. So when a donor establishes a monastery and gives it, once his intention to relinquish is fulfilled, from the moment of giving onward, neither he nor anyone born in his lineage, nor the local ruler or others, can become its owner or administer it. Rather, the Sangha, the group, or the individual who receives it is the one who can become its owner or administer it. This should be understood.

Tattha dāyakādīnaṃ issaro bhavituṃ alabhanabhāvo kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Vatthupariccāgalakkhaṇattā dānassa, pathavādivatthupariccāgena [M 2.0062] ca puna gahaṇassa ayuttattā”ti vimativinodaniyaṃ vacanato “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yaṃ dīyamānaṃ patati, taṃ sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjituṃ, pariccattaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, dāyakehī”ti (cūḷava. 273) bhagavatā vuttattā ca “pariccattaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, dāyakehīti vacanena panettha parasantakābhāvo dīpito”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ [V 2.0046] vuttattā ca viññāyati. Saṅghādīnaṃ issaro bhavituṃ labhanabhāvo kathaṃ ñātabboti ce? Saṅghiko nāma vihāro saṅghassa dinno hoti pariccatto, “puggalike puggalikasaññī aññassa puggalike āpatti dukkaṭassa, attano puggalike anāpattī”ti pācittiyapāḷiyaṃ (pāci. 117, 127) āgamanato ca “antamaso caturaṅgulapādakaṃ gāmadārakehi paṃsvāgārakesu kīḷantehi katampi saṅghassa dinnato paṭṭhāya garubhaṇḍaṃ hotī”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321) samantapāsādikāyaṃ vacanato ca “abhiyogepi cettha cātuddisaṃ saṅghaṃ uddissa bhikkhūnaṃ dinnaṃ vihāraṃ vā pariveṇaṃ vā āvāsaṃ vā mahantampi khuddakampi abhiyuñjato abhiyogo na ruhati, acchinditvā gaṇhitumpi na sakkoti. Kasmā? Sabbesaṃ dhuranikkhepābhāvato. Na hettha sabbe cātuddisā bhikkhū dhuranikkhepaṃ karontīti. Dīghabhāṇakādibhedassa pana gaṇassa ekapuggalassa vā santakaṃ abhiyuñjitvā gaṇhanto sakkoti te dhuraṃ nikkhipāpetu”nti dutiyapārājikavaṇṇanāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.102) vacanato ca viññāyati.

Here, if it is asked how it is understood that donors and others cannot be owners, it is understood from the statement in the Vimativinodanī: 'Because relinquishment is the characteristic of giving, and it is inappropriate to take back what has been relinquished, such as land and other items,' and because the Blessed One said: 'I allow, monks, that what is being given and falls may be taken up by oneself and used. That, monks, has been relinquished by the donors' (Cūḷavagga 273), and because it is stated in the commentary: 'The phrase “That, monks, has been relinquished by the donors” indicates that it is not the property of another here.' If it is asked how it is known that the Sangha and others can be owners, it is known because a monastery called 'Sanghika' is one that has been given and relinquished to the Sangha; and from its occurrence in the Pācittiya Pāḷi: 'In a personal [dwelling], if one perceives it as personal and [then gives it] to another's personal [dwelling], there is an offense of wrongdoing. But in one’s own personal [dwelling], there is no offense' (Pācittiyas 117, 127); and from the statement in the Samantapāsādikā (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 321): 'Even a small structure, such as a four-finger-high base made by village children playing in dust heaps, becomes a significant possession once given to the Sangha'; and from the statement in the commentary to the second Pārājika (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 1.102): 'Even if someone tries to claim a monastery, dwelling, or residence—large or small—given to the Sangha of the four directions, the claim does not hold. One cannot seize it by force. Why? Because there is no relinquishment of responsibility by everyone. Not all monks of the four directions relinquish responsibility here. However, if it belongs to a particular group, such as the Dīghabhāṇakas, or to an individual, then one who claims it can compel them to relinquish the responsibility.' Thus, it is understood.

Kathaṃ dāyakādīnaṃ vicāretuṃ alabhanabhāvo viññāyatīti ce? Santesupi veḷuvanavihārādidāyakesu tesaṃ vicāraṇaṃ ananujānitvā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannitu”nti bhikkhusseva senāsanaggāhāpakasammutianujānato ca bhaṇḍanakārakesu [M 2.0063] kosambakabhikkhūsu sāvatthiṃ āgatesu anāthapiṇḍikena ca visākhāya mahāupāsikāya ca “kathāhaṃ, bhante, tesu bhikkhūsu paṭipajjāmī”ti (mahāva. 468) evaṃ jetavanavihāradāyakapubbārāmavihāradāyakabhūtesu ārocitesupi tesaṃ senāsanavicāraṇaṃ avatvā āyasmatā sāriputtattherena “kathaṃ nu kho, bhante, tesu bhikkhūsu senāsane paṭipajjitabba”nti ārocite “tena hi, sāriputta, vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ dātabba”nti vatvā “sace pana, bhante, vivittaṃ na hoti, kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba”nti vutte “tena hi vivittaṃ katvāpi dātabbaṃ, na tvevāhaṃ, sāriputta, kenaci pariyāyena vuḍḍhatarassa bhikkhuno senāsanaṃ paṭibāhitabbanti vadāmi, yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 473) therasseva senāsanassa vicāraṇassa anuññātattā ca viññāyati.

How is it understood that donors and others cannot administer lodgings? Even though there were donors like those of the Veḷuvana Monastery and others, the Blessed One did not permit them to administer lodgings. Instead, by allowing a monk himself to be appointed as an assigner of lodgings, he said: “Monks, I allow a monk endowed with five qualities to be appointed as an assigner of lodgings.” Moreover, when the quarrelsome Kosambī monks arrived in Sāvatthī, and donors like Anāthapiṇḍika and the great lay devotee Visākhā—who were donors of the Jetavana Monastery and the Pubbārāma Monastery—asked: “Venerable sir, how should I behave toward these monks?”—even though they had informed him, the Blessed One did not instruct them regarding the administration of lodgings. When Venerable Sāriputta asked: “Venerable sir, how should lodgings be arranged for these monks?” the Blessed One replied: “Well then, Sāriputta, secluded lodgings should be given.” When asked further: “But, venerable sir, if secluded lodgings are not available, what should be done?” the Blessed One said: “Then, even having made lodgings secluded, they should be given. However, Sāriputta, I do not say that in any way should lodging be denied to a senior monk. Whoever denies it commits an offense of wrongdoing.” Thus, it is understood that the administration of lodgings was allowed only to the elder.

Kathaṃ pana saṅghādīnaṃ senāsanaṃ vicāretuṃ labhanabhāvo viññāyatīti? “Evañca, bhikkhave, [V 2.0047] sammannitabbo – paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo, yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

How then is it understood that the Saṅgha and others are able to administer lodgings? “And, monks, thus should he be appointed: first, a monk is to be requested. Having requested, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk—

Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho…pe… sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu senāsanaggāhāpako, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti (cūḷava. 317).

‘Let the Saṅgha hear me, venerable sirs… the monk named so-and-so has been appointed by the Saṅgha as the assigner of lodgings. The Saṅgha approves; therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.’”

Evaṃ saṅghena senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannāpetvā puna tena saṅghasammatena senāsanaggāhāpakena senāsanaggāhakavidhānaṃ anujānituṃ anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ bhikkhū gaṇetuṃ, bhikkhū gaṇetvā seyyā gaṇetuṃ, seyyā gaṇetvā seyyaggena gāhetu”nti vacanato saṅghikasenāsanassa [M 2.0064] saṅghena vicāretuṃ labhanabhāvo viññāyati.

Thus, after the Saṅgha has appointed an assigner of lodgings, the procedure for assigning lodgings by that Saṅgha-appointed assigner is authorized thus: 'Monks, I allow first to count the monks; having counted the monks, to count the beds; having counted the beds, to assign by the order of beds.' From this statement, it is understood that the Saṅgha has the ability to administer communal lodgings.

“Dīghabhāṇakādibhedassa pana gaṇassa ekapuggalassa vā dinnavihārādiṃ acchinditvā gaṇhante dhuranikkhepasambhavā pārājika”nti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.102) āgamanato ca “attano puggalike anāpattī”ti pāḷiyaṃ (pāci. 117) āgamanato ca “yasmiṃ pana vissāso ruhati, tassa santakaṃ attano puggalikamiva hotīti mahāpaccariādīsu vutta”nti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 112) vacanato ca gaṇassa dinno gaṇasantakavihāro gaṇeneva vicārīyate, no dāyakādīhi. Puggalassa dinno puggalikavihāropi paṭiggāhakapuggaleneva vicārīyate, no dāyakādīhīti viññāyati. Evaṃ vinayapāḷiyaṃ aṭṭhakathāṭīkāsu ca vihārassa saṅghikagaṇasantakapuggalikavasena tividhasseva vacanato ca tesaṃyeva saṅghagaṇapuggalānaṃ vihāravicāraṇassa anuññātattā ca dāyakasantakassa vihārassa visuṃ avuttattā ca dāyakānaṃ vihāravicāraṇassa ananuññātattā ca saṅghādayo eva vihārassa issarā honti, teyeva ca vicāretuṃ labhantīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

“However, if a group, such as the Dīghabhāṇakas, or even a single individual, seizes a dwelling or other property given to them, thereby abandoning their duties, it can result in a pārājika offense,” as stated in the commentary (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 1.102). And from the Pāli text: “For one’s personal property, there is no offense” (Pāci. 117). Further, as mentioned in the commentary (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 112): “Where trust is established, what belongs to that person becomes like one’s own personal property,” as stated in the Mahāpaccarī and other texts. Thus, a dwelling given to a group is considered the group’s property and is to be managed by the group itself, not by the donors or others. A dwelling given to an individual is considered personal property and is to be managed by the recipient individual alone, not by the donors or others. This is understood from the Vinaya Pāli, commentaries, and sub-commentaries, which state that dwellings are of three types: belonging to the Saṅgha, belonging to a group, and personal. Since only the Saṅgha, the group, or the individual are permitted to manage their respective dwellings, and since donor-owned dwellings are not separately mentioned, and donors are not permitted to manage dwellings, it should be seen that the Saṅgha, groups, and individuals are the rightful owners of the dwellings, and only they are able to manage them.

Evaṃ hotu, tesu paṭiggāhakabhūtesu saṅghagaṇapuggalesu so vihāro kassa santako hoti, kena ca vicāretabboti? Vuccate – saṅghikavihāre tāva “āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa dammī”ti dinnattā paṭiggāhakesu kālakatesupi tadañño cātuddisasaṅgho ca anāgatasaṅgho ca issaro, tassa santako, tena vicāretabbo. Gaṇasantake pana tasmiṃ gaṇe yāva ekopi atthi, tāva gaṇasantakova, tena avasiṭṭhena bhikkhunā vicāretabbo. Sabbesu kālakatesu [V 2.0048] yadi sakalagaṇo vā taṃgaṇapariyāpannaavasiṭṭhapuggalo [M 2.0065] vā jīvamānakāleyeva yassa kassaci dinno, yena ca vissāsaggāhavasena gahito, so issaro. Sacepi sakalagaṇo jīvamānakāleyeva aññagaṇassa vā saṅghassa vā puggalassa vā deti, te aññagaṇasaṅghapuggalā issarā honti. Puggalikavihāre pana so vihārassāmiko attano jīvamānakāleyeva saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā puggalassa vā deti, te issarā honti. Yo vā pana tassa jīvamānasseva vissāsaggāhavasena gaṇhāti, sova issaro hotīti daṭṭhabbo.

So be it. Among the Saṅgha, groups, and individuals who are the recipients, to whom does that dwelling belong, and by whom should it be managed? It is said—first, in the case of a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, since it was given with the words, “I give this to the Saṅgha of the four directions, present and future,” even if the recipients have passed away, the rest of the Saṅgha of the four directions and the future Saṅgha are the owners. It belongs to them, and they should manage it. In the case of a group-owned dwelling, as long as even one member of that group exists, it remains the group’s property, and the remaining monk should manage it. If all have passed away, and if the entire group or a remaining individual included in that group, while still alive, gave it to someone, and that person has accepted it based on trust, that person is the owner. Even if the entire group, while still alive, gives it to another group, the Saṅgha, or an individual, those other groups, the Saṅgha, or individuals become the owners. In the case of a personal dwelling, the owner of that dwelling, while still alive, may give it to the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual, and they become the owners. Alternatively, whoever takes possession of it during the owner’s lifetime based on trust, that person is the owner—this should be understood.

Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? Saṅghike vihārassa garubhaṇḍattā avissajjiyaṃ avebhaṅgikaṃ hoti, na kassaci dātabbaṃ. Gaṇasantakapuggalikesu pana tesaṃ sāmikattā dānavissāsaggāhā ruhanti, “tasmā so jīvamānoyeva sabbaṃ attano parikkhāraṃ nissajjitvā kassaci adāsi, koci vā vissāsaṃ aggahesi. Yassa dinnaṃ, yena ca gahitaṃ, tasseva hotī”ti ca “dvinnaṃ santakaṃ hoti avibhattaṃ, ekasmiṃ kālakate itaro sāmī, bahūnampi santake eseva nayo”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 369) ca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttattā viññāyati.

How is this understood? In the case of a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, because it is heavy property, it is not to be given away or divided; it should not be given to anyone. However, in the case of property belonging to a group or an individual, since they are the owners, giving and taking in trust are allowable. “Therefore, while still alive, one gave all one’s belongings to someone, or someone accepted them in trust. To whomever it is given, and by whomever it is taken, it belongs to them.” And further: “Property owned jointly by two and not divided, when one dies, the other is the owner; this is the same principle with property owned by many,” as stated in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 369). Thus, it is understood.

Evaṃ pana vissajjetvā adinnaṃ “mamaccayena asukassa hotū”ti dānaṃ accayadānattā na ruhati. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 419) “sace hi pañcasu sahadhammikesu yo koci kālaṃ karonto ‘mamaccayena mayhaṃ parikkhāro upajjhāyassa hotu, ācariyassa hotu, saddhivihārikassa hotu, antevāsikassa hotu, mātu hotu, pitu hotu, aññassa vā kassaci hotū’ti vadati, tesaṃ na hoti, saṅghasseva hoti. Na hi pañcannaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ accayadānaṃ ruhati, gihīnaṃ pana ruhatī”ti. Ettha ca ekacce pana vinayadharā “gihīnanti [M 2.0066] padaṃ sampadānanti gahetvā bhikkhūnaṃ santakaṃ accayadānavasena gihīnaṃ dadante ruhati, pañcannaṃ pana sahadhammikānaṃ dento na ruhatī”ti vadanti. Evaṃ sante mātāpitūnaṃ dadantopi ruheyya tesaṃ gihibhūtattā. “Atha ca pana ‘mātu hotu, pitu hotu, aññassa vā kassaci hotū’ti vadati, tesaṃ na hotī”ti vacanato na ruhatīti viññāyati, tasmā “gihīnaṃ panā”ti idaṃ na sampadānavacanaṃ, atha kho sāmivacanamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tena gihīnaṃ pana santakaṃ accayadānaṃ ruhatīti sambandho kātabbo.

However, a gift not relinquished during life—“After my death, let this belong to so-and-so”—does not take effect because it is a deathbed gift. For it is stated in the commentary (Cūḷava. Aṭṭha. 419): “If anyone among the five co-religionists, at the time of death, says, ‘After my death, let my requisites go to my preceptor, teacher, fellow resident, pupil, mother, father, or anyone else,’ it does not belong to them—it belongs only to the Saṅgha. For a deathbed gift does not take effect for the five co-religionists, but it does take effect for laypeople.” Here, however, some Vinaya experts say, “Taking the word ‘for laypeople’ as being in the dative case, if monks give their property as a deathbed gift to laypeople, it takes effect. But if they give to the five co-religionists, it does not take effect.” If this were so, then even giving to one’s mother and father should take effect, since they are laypeople. But the statement, “If he says, ‘Let it go to my mother, father, or anyone else,’ it does not belong to them,” shows that it does not take effect. Therefore, the phrase “but for laypeople” should not be understood as referring to the recipient, but rather as referring to the owner. Thus, the connection should be made that a deathbed gift of what belongs to laypeople does take effect.

Kiñca bhiyyo – “sace hi pañcasu sahadhammikesu yo koci kālaṃ karonto mamaccayena [V 2.0049] mayhaṃ parikkhāro”ti ārabhitvā “na hi pañcannaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ accayadānaṃ ruhati, gihīnaṃ pana ruhatī”ti vuttattā sāmyatthe chaṭṭhībahuvacanaṃ samatthitaṃ bhavati. Yadi evaṃ “gihīna”nti padassa asampadānatte sati katamaṃ sampadānaṃ hotīti? “Yassa kassacī”ti padaṃ. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 419) “mātu hotu, pitu hotu, aññassa vā kassaci hotū”ti. Ayamattho ajjukavatthunā (pārā. 158) dīpetabbo. Evaṃ jīvamānakāleyeva datvā matesu vinicchayo amhehi ñāto, kassaci adatvā matesu vinicchayo kathaṃ ñātabboti? Tatthāpi saṅghike tāva heṭṭhā vuttanayena saṅghova issaro, gaṇasantake pana ekaccesu avasesā issarā, sabbesu matesu saṅghova issaro. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 369) “sabbesu matesu saṅghikaṃ hotī”ti. Puggalike pana vihārassa garubhaṇḍattā avissajjiyaṃ avebhaṅgikaṃ saṅghikameva hoti.

Furthermore, starting with “If any one of the five co-religionists were to pass away, ‘After my death, my requisites…’” it is said that “a deathbed gift does not take effect for the five co-religionists, but it does take effect for laypeople.” Therefore, the sixth case plural is justified in the sense of ownership. If this is so, and the word “for laypeople” does not have the sense of dative, then what has the sense of dative? The phrase “to whomever.” For it is stated in the commentary (Cūḷava. Aṭṭha. 419): “Let it be for the mother, for the father, or for anyone else.” This meaning should be explained according to the case of Ajjuka (Pārā. 158). Thus, the ruling regarding those who have died after giving while still alive is known to us. But if they die without having given it to anyone, how is the ruling to be known? In that case, regarding property belonging to the Saṅgha, as previously stated, the Saṅgha is the owner. In the case of property belonging to a group, when some have died the remaining members are the owners, but if all die, the Saṅgha is the owner. For it is stated in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 369): “If all die, it belongs to the Saṅgha.” But regarding personal property, because a dwelling is heavy property, it is not to be given away and is indivisible—it becomes property of the Saṅgha.

Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Bhikkhussa, bhikkhave, kālakate saṅgho sāmī pattacīvare, apica gilānupaṭṭhākā bahūpakārā, anujānāmi[M 2.0067], bhikkhave, saṅghena ticīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātuṃ. Yaṃ tattha lahubhaṇḍaṃ lahuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetuṃ. Yaṃ tattha garubhaṇḍaṃ garuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa avissajjiyaṃ avebhaṅgika”nti (mahāva. 369) tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena vuttattā viññāyati. Evampi “garubhaṇḍaṃ garuparikkhāraṃ”icceva bhagavatā vuttaṃ, na “vihāra”nti, tasmā kathaṃ vihārassa garubhaṇḍabhāvoti viññāyatīti? “Vihāro vihāravatthu, idaṃ dutiyaṃ avebhaṅgika”nti pāḷiyaṃ,

How is this understood? “Monks, when a bhikkhu has passed away, the Saṅgha is the owner of his bowl and robes. Moreover, if the attendants of the sick have been very helpful, I allow, monks, the Saṅgha to give the three robes and the bowl to the attendants of the sick. Whatever light goods and light requisites there are, the Saṅgha present should divide them. Whatever heavy goods and heavy requisites there are, they are not to be disposed of and not to be divided, belonging to the Saṅgha of the four quarters, present and future.” (Mahāva. 369) Thus, because it was spoken by the Blessed One, the Knower and Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, it is understood. Even so, the Blessed One spoke only of “heavy goods and heavy requisites,” not of “a dwelling.” Therefore, how is it understood that a dwelling is classified as heavy goods? From the Pāli text: “A dwelling, a dwelling-site: this is the second indivisible item,”

“Dvisaṅgahāni dve honti, tatiyaṃ catusaṅgahaṃ;

Catutthaṃ navakoṭṭhāsaṃ, pañcamaṃ aṭṭhabhedanaṃ.

Two are the twofold collections, the third is the fourfold collection; the fourth is the ninefold division, the fifth is the eightfold distinction.

“Iti pañcahi rāsīhi, pañcanimmalalocano;

Pañcavīsavidhaṃ nātho, garubhaṇḍaṃ pakāsayī”ti. (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321) –

“Thus, with five aggregates, the One with five stainless eyes, the Lord, expounded the heavy property in twenty-five ways.” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 321)

Aṭṭhakathāyañca vuttattā viññāyati.

And it is understood because it is stated in the commentary.

Iti [V 2.0050] dāyako vihāraṃ katvā kulūpakabhikkhussa deti, tassa muñcacetanuppattito pubbakāle dāyako vihārassāmiko hoti, dātuṃ vā vicāretuṃ vā issaro, muñcacetanuppattito paṭṭhāya paṭiggāhakabhikkhu sāmiko hoti, paribhuñjituṃ vā aññesaṃ dātuṃ vā issaro. So puggalo attano jīvamānakkhaṇeyeva saddhivihārikādīnaṃ nissajjitvā deti, tadā te saddhivihārikādayo sāmikā honti, paribhuñjituṃ vā aññassa vā dātuṃ issarā. Yadi pana kassaci adatvāva kālaṃ karoti, tadā saṅghova tassa vihārassa sāmiko hoti, na dāyako vā puggalo vā, saṅghānumatiyā eva puggalo paribhuñjituṃ labhati, na attano issaravatāyāti daṭṭhabbo.

Thus, a donor, having built a monastery, gives it to a monk who frequents families. In the period before the arising of the intention to relinquish, the donor is the owner of the monastery, having authority to give it or to manage it. From the arising of the intention to relinquish onward, the receiving monk becomes the owner, having authority to use it or to give it to others. That individual, while still alive, may relinquish it to his co-residents and so on, and at that time those co-residents and so on become the owners, having authority to use it or give it to another. However, if he passes away without giving it to anyone, then the Saṅgha becomes the owner of that monastery—not the donor or any individual. Only with the Saṅgha’s approval may an individual use it, not by his own authority—this should be understood.

Evaṃ [M 2.0068] mūlatoyeva saṅghassa dinnattā saṅghikabhūtavihāro vā mūle gaṇapuggalānaṃ dinnattā gaṇasantakapuggalikabhūtopi tesaṃ gaṇapuggalānaṃ aññassa nissajjanavasena adatvā kālakatattā pacchā saṅghikabhāvaṃ pattavihāro vā saṅghena vicāretabbo hoti. Saṅghenapi bhagavato anumatiyā senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannitvā gāhāpetabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ senāsanakkhandhake (cūḷava. 317) “atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi ‘kena nu kho senāsanaṃ gāhetabba’nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – ‘anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannitu’nti”ādi.

Thus, a dwelling that has become Saṅgha property, since it was given to the Saṅgha from the very beginning; or a dwelling that, having been given to a group of individuals at the beginning, became their personal property, but those individuals passed away without relinquishing it to another, thereby later attaining Saṅgha ownership—such a dwelling must be administered by the Saṅgha. Moreover, with the Blessed One’s approval, the Saṅgha should appoint a lodging-allocator and have it assigned. For this was said in the Senāsanakkhandhaka (Cūḷavagga 317): “Then the bhikkhus had this thought, ‘By whom should lodgings be assigned?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘I allow, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu endowed with five qualities be appointed as a lodging-allocator,’” and so on.

Imasmiṃ ṭhāne “senāsanaggāho nāma vassakālavasena senāsanaggāho, utukālavasena senāsanaggāho, dhuvavāsavasena senāsanaggāhoti tividho hoti. Tesu vassakālavasena senāsanaggāho purimavassavasena senāsanaggāho, pacchimavassavasena senāsanaggāhoti duvidho. Utukālavasena senāsanaggāhopi antarāmuttakavasena senāsanaggāho, taṅkhaṇapaṭisallānavasena senāsanaggāhoti duvidho”ti ācariyā vadanti, etaṃ pāḷiyā ca aṭṭhakathāya ca asamentaṃ viya dissati. Pāḷiyañhi (cūḷava. 318) “atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi ‘kati nu kho senāsanaggāho’ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – tayome, bhikkhave, senāsanaggāhā purimako pacchimako antarāmuttako. Aparajjugatāya āsāḷhiyā purimako gāhetabbo, māsagatāya āsāḷhiyā pacchimako gāhetabbo, aparajjugatāya pavāraṇāya āyatiṃ vassāvāsatthāya antarāmuttako gāhetabbo. Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo senāsanaggāhā”ti evaṃ āgato, aṭṭhakathāyampi [M 2.0069] (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) “tīsu senāsanaggāhesu purimako ca pacchimako [V 2.0051] cāti ime dve gāhā thāvarā. Antarāmuttake ayaṃ vinicchayo…pe… ayaṃ tāva antovasse vassūpanāyikādivasena pāḷiyaṃ āgatasenāsanaggāhakathā, ayaṃ pana senāsanaggāho nāma duvidho hoti utukāle ca vassāvāse cā”ti evaṃ āgato, tasmā saṅghena sammatasenāsanaggāhāpakena vicāretabbā.

In this context, the teachers say, “The taking up of lodgings is threefold: taking up lodgings according to the rainy season, taking up lodgings according to the season, and taking up lodgings for permanent residence. Among these, taking up lodgings according to the rainy season is twofold: taking up lodgings for the early rains-residence and taking up lodgings for the late rains-residence. Taking up lodgings according to the season is also twofold: taking up lodgings for the interim period and taking up lodgings for momentary seclusion.” This seems inconsistent with the Pāli and its commentary. For in the Pāli (Cūḷavagga 318), it is said: “Then the bhikkhus had this thought, ‘How many kinds of taking up lodgings are there?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, there are these three kinds of taking up lodgings: the early, the late, and the interim. The early should be taken up on the day following the Āsāḷhī full moon, the late when a month of Āsāḷhī has passed, and the interim should be taken up on the day following the Pavāraṇā for the purpose of the future rains-residence. These, monks, are the three kinds of taking up lodgings.’” Similarly, in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 318), it is said: “Among the three kinds of taking up lodgings, the early and the late are two fixed takings. Regarding the interim, this is the decision... So far, this is the discussion on the taking up of lodgings that comes in the Pāli by way of the commencement of the rains-residence and so on. But this taking up of lodgings is twofold: during the season and during the rains-residence.” Therefore, these matters should be administered by the lodging-allocator appointed by the Saṅgha.

Senāsanaggāho nāma utukāle senāsanaggāho, vassāvāse senāsanaggāhoti duvidho. Tattha utukālo nāma hemantautugimhautuvasena aṭṭha māsā, tasmiṃ kāle bhikkhū aniyatāvāsā honti, tasmā ye yadā āgacchanti, tesaṃ tadā bhikkhū uṭṭhāpetvā senāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, akālo nāma natthi. Ayaṃ utukāle senāsanaggāho nāma. Vassāvāse senāsanaggāho pana “purimako pacchimako antarāmuttako”ti pāḷiyaṃ āgatanayena tividho hoti. Antarāmuttakopi hi āyatiṃ vassāvāsatthāya gāhitattā vassāvāse senāsanaggāhameva pavisati, na utukāle senāsanaggāho. Vuttañhi bhagavatā “aparajjugatāya pavāraṇāya āyatiṃ vassāvāsatthāya antarāmuttako gāhetabbo”ti. Taṅkhaṇapaṭisallānavasena senāsanaggāhoti ca neva pāḷiyaṃ na aṭṭhakathāyaṃ visuṃ āgato, utukāle senāsanaggāhoyeva tadaṅgasenāsanaggāhotipi taṅkhaṇapaṭisallānavasena senāsanaggāhotipi vadanti, tasmā utukālavasena senāsanaggāhopi “antarāmuttakavasena senāsanaggāho taṅkhaṇapaṭisallānavasena senāsanaggāhoti dubbidho”ti na vattabbo.

The allocation of lodgings is of two kinds: the allocation during the season and the allocation during the rains-residence. Here, ‘the season’ refers to the eight months comprising the cool season and the hot season. During this time, monks do not have a fixed residence. Therefore, whenever monks arrive, lodging should be assigned to them, having a resident monk vacate his place; there is no ‘improper time’. This is called the allocation of lodgings during the season. The allocation of lodgings during the rains-residence, however, is threefold according to the method stated in the Pāli: the early, the late, and the interim. Even the interim allocation, since it is taken for the purpose of the future rains-residence, is included in the allocation for the rains-residence, not the allocation during the season. For the Blessed One has said, “The interim lodging should be taken up on the day following the Pavāraṇā for the purpose of the future rains-residence.” The ‘allocation of lodgings for momentary seclusion’ is not mentioned separately in either the Pāli or the commentary. Some, however, refer to it as a subsidiary aspect of the allocation during the season or as the allocation for momentary seclusion. Therefore, it should not be said that the allocation during the season is twofold—as the allocation for the interim period and the allocation for momentary seclusion.

Athāpi [M 2.0070] vadanti “yathāvuttesu pañcasu senāsanaggāhesu cattāro senāsanaggāhā pañcaṅgasamannāgatena senāsanaggāhāpakasammutiladdhena bhikkhunā antoupacārasīmaṭṭhena hutvā antosīmaṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yathāvinayaṃ vicāretabbā honti, te pana vicāraṇā yāvajjakālā thāvarā hutvā na tiṭṭhanti, dhuvavāsavasena vicāraṇameva yāvajjakālā thāvaraṃ hutvā tiṭṭhatī”ti, tampi tathā na sakkā vattuṃ. Kasmā? Senāsanaggāhāpakabhede “dhuvavāsavasena senāsanaggāho”ti pāḷiyaṃ aṭṭhakathāyañca natthi. Dhuvavāsavasena vicāraṇañca sammutiladdhena senāsanaggāhāpakena vicāretabbaṃ na hoti, atha kho samaggena saṅghena apalokanakammavasena duvaṅgasamannāgatassa bhikkhussa anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā dānameva, tasmā samaggo saṅgho bahūpakāratāguṇavisiṭṭhatāsaṅkhātehi dvīhi aṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ apalokanakammavasena sammannitvā [V 2.0052] tassa phāsukaṃ āvāsaṃ dhuvavāsavasena anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā deti, taṃ yāvajjakālā thāvaraṃ hutvā tiṭṭhatīti vattabbaṃ.

They also say, “Among the five kinds of lodging allocations mentioned, four should be administered according to the Vinaya by a monk endowed with five factors, who has received formal authorization as a lodging-allocator, acting within the boundary vicinity for the monks within the boundary. However, these allocations do not remain permanent for life, whereas an allocation for permanent residence does remain permanent for life.” But this too cannot be rightly said. Why? In the classification of lodging-allocators, there is no mention in the Pāli or its commentary of ‘lodging allocation for permanent residence.’ Moreover, an allocation for permanent residence is not to be administered by a formally authorized lodging-allocator. Rather, it is simply a gift from the harmonious Saṅgha, made by means of an act of proclamation, making it non-revocable for a monk endowed with two factors. Therefore, it should be said: the harmonious Saṅgha, by means of an act of proclamation, having authorized a monk endowed with the two factors known as being of great service and being distinguished by virtue, gives him a comfortable dwelling as a permanent residence, making it non-revocable, and it remains permanent for life.

Samaggo saṅghova dhuvavāsavasena deti, na senāsanaggāhāpakoti ayamattho kathaṃ ñātabboti ce? “Saṅgho pana bhaṇḍāgārikassa vā dhammakathikavinayadharādīnaṃ vā gaṇavācakaācariyassa vā bahūpakārataṃ guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhento dhuvavāsatthāya vihāraṃ sammannitvā detī”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 120; kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “saṅgho pana bahussutassa uddesaparipucchādīhi bahūpakārassa bhāranitthārakassa phāsukaṃ āvāsaṃ anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā detī”ti ca “saṅgho pana bhaṇḍāgārikassa vā dhammakathikavinayadharagaṇavācakācariyānaṃ vā bahūpakārataṃ guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhetvā dhuvavāsatthāya vihāraṃ sallakkhetvā sammannitvā detī”ti ca “bahussutassa saṅghabhāranitthārakassa [M 2.0071] bhikkhuno anuṭṭhāpanīyasenāsanampī”ti (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496) ca “apalokanakammaṃ nāma sīmaṭṭhakaṃ saṅghaṃ sodhetvā chandārahānaṃ chandaṃ āharitvā samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā tikkhattuṃ sāvetvā kattabbaṃ kamma”nti ca aṭṭhakathāsu (pari. aṭṭha. 482) vacanato sādhukaṃ nissaṃsayena ñātabboti.

The united Saṅgha gives a dwelling for permanent residence, not the assigner of lodgings—how should this meaning be understood? It should be understood properly and without doubt from these statements in the commentaries: “The Saṅgha, considering the great service and distinguished qualities of the storekeeper or of the Dhamma preachers, Vinaya experts, etc., or of the group reciter or teacher, having sanctioned a dwelling for permanent residence, gives it.” (Pācittiya Aṭṭhakathā 120; Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Aṭṭhakathā, Anupakhajja Sikkhāpada Vaṇṇanā) “Moreover, the Saṅgha, recognizing the great assistance of one who is learned, who is very helpful with recitations, questionings, etc., who removes burdens, makes a comfortable dwelling not to be displaced, and gives it.” And: “The Saṅgha, having considered the great service and distinguished qualities of the storekeeper or of the Dhamma preachers, Vinaya experts, group reciters, or teachers, having considered a dwelling, and having sanctioned it, gives it for permanent residence.” And: “Even a dwelling not to be displaced may be given to a learned monk who removes the Saṅgha’s burdens.” (Parivāra Aṭṭhakathā 495–496) And: “An announcement action is an act that, after purifying the Saṅgha within the boundary, gathering the consent of those eligible for consent, and announcing it three times with the agreement of the united Saṅgha, must be performed.” (Parivāra Aṭṭhakathā 482).

Kathaṃ pana apalokanakammena dātabbabhāvo viññāyatīti? “Bahussutassa saṅghabhāranitthārakassa bhikkhuno anuṭṭhāpanīyasenāsanampi saṅghakiccaṃ karontānaṃ kappiyakārakādīnaṃ bhattavetanampi apalokanakammena dātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti parivāraṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496) kammavagge āgatattā viññāyati. Kathaṃ pana duvaṅgasamannāgatassa bhikkhunoyeva dātabbabhāvo viññāyatīti? “Bahūpakāratanti bhaṇḍāgārikatādibahuupakārabhāvaṃ. Na kevalaṃ idamevāti āha ‘guṇavisiṭṭhatañcā’tiādi. Tena bahūpakārattepi guṇavisiṭṭhattābhāve, guṇavisiṭṭhattepi bahūpakārattābhāve dātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dassetī”ti vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. ṭī. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vuttattā viññāyati.

How is it understood that it is fit to be given by an act of announcement? It is understood because it is stated in the Parivāra Commentary (Parivāra Aṭṭhakathā 495-496) in the section on formal acts: “It is proper to give by an act of announcement even a dwelling not to be displaced for a learned monk who removes the Saṅgha’s burdens, and even food and wages for those performing Saṅgha duties, such as suitable attendants.” How is it understood that it is fit to be given only to a monk possessed of two qualities? It is understood because it is stated in the Vinayatthamañjūsā (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Aṭṭhakathā, Anupakhajjasikkhāpada Vaṇṇanā): “‘Being of great assistance’ refers to the state of being of great assistance, such as being a storekeeper, etc. And it is not only this, as it says, ‘and being distinguished in virtue,’ etc. Thus, it shows that even with being of great assistance, if there is a lack of distinction in virtue, or with being distinguished in virtue, if there is a lack of being of great assistance, it is not proper to give.”

Kasmā pana senāsanaggāhāpakena vicāretabbo senāsanaggāho yāvajjakālā na tiṭṭhatīti? Pañcaṅgasamannāgatassa senāsanaggāhāpakassa bhikkhuno dullabhattā, nānādesavāsīnaṃ nānācariyakulasambhavānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ekasambhogaparibhogassa dukkarattā ca imehi dvīhi kāraṇehi [V 2.0053] na tiṭṭhati. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannituṃ, yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya[M 2.0072], gahitāgahitañca jāneyyā”ti (cūḷava. 317). Aṭṭhakathāyampi (pāci. aṭṭha. 122) “evarūpena hi sabhāgapuggalena ekavihāre vā ekapariveṇe vā vasantena attho natthī”ti vuttaṃ. Kasmā pana dhuvavāsatthāya dānavicāro yāvajjakālā tiṭṭhatīti? Pañcaṅgasamannāgatābhāvepi sīmaṭṭhakassa samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā kattabbattā. Vuttañhi “apalokanakammaṃ nāma sīmaṭṭhakaṃ saṅghaṃ sodhetvā chandārahānaṃ chandaṃ āharitvā samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā tikkhattuṃ sāvetvā kattabbaṃ kamma”nti (pari. aṭṭha. 482).

Why then does the lodging assignment determined by the assigner of lodgings not last for a long time? Because a monk qualified with five factors for assigning lodgings is rare, and because it is difficult for monks from different regions and different teacher lineages to have shared communion and use of facilities. For these two reasons, it does not last. The Blessed One has said: “I allow, monks, a monk endowed with five factors to be appointed as an assigner of lodgings—one who does not proceed through favoritism, hostility, delusion, or fear, and who knows what has and has not been assigned.” (Cūḷavagga 317) The commentary also states: “For there is no benefit from such a suitable person residing in one monastery or one enclosure.” (Pācittiya Aṭṭhakathā 122) Why then does the consideration for a donation for permanent residence last for a long time? Because even in the absence of one endowed with the five factors, it must be done with the approval of a harmonious Saṅgha within the boundary. For it is said: “An announcement action is an act that, after purifying the Saṅgha within the boundary, gathering the consent of those eligible for consent, and announcing it three times with the agreement of the united Saṅgha, must be performed.” (Parivāra Aṭṭhakathā 482)

Utukāle saṅghikasenāsane vasantena āgato bhikkhu na paṭibāhetabbo aññatra anuṭṭhāpanīyā. Vuttañhi bhagavatā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassānaṃ temāsaṃ paṭibāhituṃ, utukālaṃ pana na paṭibāhitu”nti (cūḷava. 318). “Aññatra anuṭṭhāpanīyā”ti vuttaṃ, katame anuṭṭhāpanīyāti? Cattāro anuṭṭhāpanīyā vuḍḍhataro, bhaṇḍāgāriko, gilāno, saṅghato laddhasenāsano ca. Tattha vuḍḍhataro bhikkhu tasmiṃ vihāre antosīmaṭṭhakabhikkhūsu attanā vuḍḍhatarassa aññassa abhāvā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ kenaci anuṭṭhāpanīyo. Bhaṇḍāgāriko saṅghena sammannitvā bhaṇḍāgārassa dinnatāya saṅghassa bhaṇḍaṃ rakkhanto gopento vasati, tasmā so bhaṇḍāgāriko kenaci anuṭṭhāpanīyo. Gilāno gelaññābhibhūto attano laddhasenāsane vasanto kenaci anuṭṭhāpanīyo. Saṅghato laddhasenāsano samaggena saṅghena dinnasenāsanattā kenaci anuṭṭhāpanīyo. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 343) “cattāro hi na vuṭṭhāpetabbā vuḍḍhataro, bhaṇḍāgāriko, gilāno, saṅghato laddhasenāsanoti. Tattha vuḍḍhataro attano vuḍḍhatāya navakatarena na [M 2.0073] vuṭṭhāpetabbo, bhaṇḍāgāriko saṅghena sammannitvā bhaṇḍāgārassa dinnatāya, gilāno attano gilānatāya, saṅgho pana bahussutassa uddesaparipucchādīhi bahūpakārassa bhāranitthārakassa phāsukaṃ āvāsaṃ anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā deti, tasmā so upakārakatāya ca saṅghato laddhatāya ca na vuṭṭhāpetabbo”ti. Ṭhapetvā ime cattāro avasesā vuṭṭhāpanīyāva honti.

During the seasonal period, a visiting monk should not be turned away by a resident in a Saṅgha dwelling, except for those who are not to be displaced. For the Blessed One has said: “I allow, monks, that during the three months of the rains, residence may be restricted, but not during the seasonal period.” (Cūḷavagga 318) When it is said, “except for those who are not to be displaced,” who are these? There are four who are not to be displaced: the elder, the storekeeper, the sick, and one who has received a dwelling from the Saṅgha. Herein, the elder monk in that monastery, in the absence of any other monk more senior than himself among the monks within the boundary, is not to be displaced by anyone, in accordance with seniority. The storekeeper, having been appointed by the Saṅgha and given the storehouse, dwells there guarding and protecting the Saṅgha’s goods; therefore, that storekeeper is not to be displaced by anyone. The sick, being overcome by illness while residing in the dwelling he has received, is not to be displaced by anyone. One who has received a dwelling from the Saṅgha, because the dwelling was given by the harmonious Saṅgha, is not to be displaced by anyone. For it is stated in the commentary (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 343): “Indeed, four are not to be made to vacate: the elder, the storekeeper, the sick, and one who has received a dwelling from the Saṅgha. Among these, the elder should not be made to vacate by a junior due to his seniority; the storekeeper, because he has been appointed by the Saṅgha and given the storehouse; the sick, due to his illness. The Saṅgha, moreover, gives a comfortable dwelling, making it non-displaceable, to a learned monk who is of great assistance with recitations, questionings, etc., and who removes burdens; therefore, he should not be made to vacate because of his helpfulness and because he has received it from the Saṅgha.” Apart from these four, the rest are displaceable.

Aparasmiṃ bhikkhumhi āgate vuṭṭhāpetvā senāsanaṃ dāpetabbaṃ. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) “utukāle tāva keci āgantukā bhikkhū purebhattaṃ āgacchanti, keci [V 2.0054] pacchābhattaṃ paṭhamayāmaṃ vā majjhimayāmaṃ vā pacchimayāmaṃ vā, ye yadā āgacchanti, tesaṃ tadāva bhikkhū uṭṭhāpetvā senāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, akālo nāma natthī”ti. Etarahi pana saddhā pasannā manussā vihāraṃ katvā appekacce paṇḍitānaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā “saṅghe dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti ñatvā cātuddisaṃ saṅghaṃ ārabbha “imaṃ vihāraṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa demā”ti vatvā denti, appekacce attanā pasannaṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha vihāraṃ katvāpi dānakāle tena uyyojitā hutvā cātuddisaṃ saṅghaṃ ārabbha vuttanayena denti, appekacce karaṇakālepi dānakālepi attano kulūpakabhikkhumeva ārabbha pariccajanti, tathāpi dakkhiṇodakapātanakāle tena sikkhāpitā yathāvuttapāṭhaṃ vacībhedaṃ karonti, cittena pana kulūpakasseva denti, na sabbasaṅghasādhāraṇatthaṃ icchanti.

When another monk arrives, a resident monk should be made to vacate and lodging should be provided. As stated in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 318): “During the seasonal period, some visiting monks arrive before the meal, some after the meal, or in the first, middle, or last watch of the night. Whenever they arrive, a monk should be made to vacate at that very moment and lodging should be provided for them; there is no such thing as an inappropriate time.” Nowadays, however, some devout and faithful people, having built a monastery and having heard the words of the wise, understanding that “what is given to the Saṅgha bears great fruit,” give it with reference to the Saṅgha of the four directions, saying, “We give this monastery to the Saṅgha of the four directions, both present and future.” Some, though having built a monastery with reference to a monk who has their confidence, at the time of giving are urged by him and give it with reference to the Saṅgha of the four directions in the manner described. Some, both at the time of construction and at the time of giving, relinquish it with reference only to their own family-monk; yet, at the time of pouring the water of dedication, being instructed by him, they alter their words according to the prescribed text, but in their hearts they give it only to their family-monk and do not wish it to be for the common use of the entire Saṅgha.

Imesu tīsu dānesu paṭhamaṃ pubbakālepi dānakālepi saṅghaṃ uddissa pavattattā sabbasaṅghikaṃ hoti. Dutiyaṃ pubbakāle puggalaṃ uddissa pavattamānampi dānakāle saṅghaṃ uddissa pavattattā saṅghikameva. Tatiyaṃ pana pubbakālepi dānakālepi [M 2.0074] kulūpakapuggalameva uddissa pavattati, na saṅghaṃ, kevalaṃ bhikkhunā vuttānusāreneva vacībhedaṃ karonti. Evaṃ sante “kiṃ ayaṃ vihāro cittavasena puggaliko hoti, vacībhedavasena saṅghiko”ti cintāyaṃ ekacce evaṃ vadeyyuṃ –

Among these three gifts, the first is for the entire Sangha because it is made with the Sangha in mind both beforehand and at the time of giving. The second, though made with an individual in mind beforehand, becomes for the Sangha because at the time of giving it is made with the Sangha in mind. The third, however, is made solely with a family-attending monk in mind both beforehand and at the time of giving, and not for the Sangha. They merely alter the verbal declaration according to the monk’s instruction. This being so, one might wonder, “Does this monastery become personal by intention but for the Sangha by verbal declaration?” Some might say—

“Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā;

Manasā ce pasannena, bhāsati vā karoti vā;

Tato naṃ sukhamanveti, chāyāva anapāyinīti. (dha. pa. 2) –

“Mind precedes all phenomena, mind is their chief, they are mind-made. If one speaks or acts with a pure mind, happiness follows him like a never-departing shadow.”

Vacanato cittavasena puggaliko hotī”ti. Aññe “yathā dāyakā vadanti, tathā paṭipajjitabbanti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 325) vacanato vacībhedavasena saṅghiko hotī”ti.

‘By that statement, it becomes personal by way of intention.’ Others say: ‘According to the statement, “As the donors state, so should it be undertaken” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 325), it becomes for the Sangha by way of the verbal declaration.’”

Tatrāyaṃ vicāraṇā – idaṃ dānaṃ pubbe puggalassa pariṇataṃ pacchā saṅghassa pariṇāmitaṃ, tasmā “saṅghiko”ti vutte navasu adhammikadānesu “puggalassa pariṇataṃ saṅghassa pariṇāmetī”ti (pārā. 660) vuttaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ adhammikadānaṃ hoti, tassa dānassa paṭiggahāpi paribhogāpi adhammikapaṭiggahā adhammikaparibhogā honti. “Puggaliko”ti vutte tīsu dhammikadānesu “puggalassa dinnaṃ puggalasseva detī”ti vuttaṃ tatiyadhammikadānaṃ hoti, tassa [V 2.0055] paṭiggahāpi paribhogāpi dhammikapaṭiggahā dhammikaparibhogā honti, tasmā puggalikapakkhaṃ bhajati. Appekacce suttantikādigaṇe pasīditvā vihāraṃ kāretvā gaṇassa denti “imaṃ vihāraṃ āyasmantānaṃ dammī”ti. Appekacce puggale pasīditvā vihāraṃ katvā puggalassa denti “imaṃ vihāraṃ āyasmato dammī”ti. Ete pana gaṇasantakapuggalikā vihārā dānakālato paṭṭhāya paṭiggāhakasantakāva honti, na dāyakasantakā. Tesu gaṇasantako tāva ekaccesu matesu avasesānaṃ santako, tesu dharamānesuyeva [M 2.0075] kassaci denti, tassa santako. Kassaci adatvā sabbesu matesu saṅghiko hoti. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 369) “dvinnaṃ santakaṃ hoti avibhattaṃ, ekasmiṃ kālakate itaro sāmī, bahūnaṃ santakepi eseva nayo. Sabbesu matesu saṅghikaṃva hotī”ti.

Here is the deliberation: This gift was first allocated to an individual, then transferred to the Sangha. Therefore, when it is called “for the Sangha,” according to the nine improper gifts, it becomes the eighth improper gift, as stated: “What was allocated to an individual is transferred to the Sangha” (Pārā. 660). The acceptance and use of such a gift are improper acceptance and improper use. When it is called “personal,” according to the three proper gifts, it becomes the third proper gift, as stated: “Given to an individual, it is given to that individual alone.” The acceptance and use of such a gift are proper acceptance and proper use. Therefore, it favors the individual side. Some, having gained faith in a group such as Sutta experts, build a monastery and give it to the group, saying, “I give this monastery to the venerable ones.” Others, having gained faith in an individual, build a monastery and give it to that individual, saying, “I give this monastery to the venerable one.” However, these monasteries belonging to a group or an individual become the property of the recipients from the time of the gift, not the donors. Regarding those belonging to a group, when some die, it becomes the property of the remaining ones; if they give it to someone while still alive, it becomes that person’s property; if they do not give it to anyone and all die, it becomes for the Sangha. As stated in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 369): “When it is the undivided property of two, if one dies, the other is the owner; the same principle applies when it is the property of many. When all die, it becomes for the Sangha.”

Puggalikavihāropi yadi so paṭiggāhakapuggalo attano jīvamānakāleyeva saddhivihārikādīnaṃ deti, koci vā tassa vissāsena taṃ vihāraṃ aggahesi, tassa santako hoti. Kassaci adatvā kālakate saṅghiko hoti. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “so jīvamānoyeva sabbaṃ attano parikkhāraṃ nissajjitvā kassaci adāsi, koci vā vissāsaṃ aggahesi. Yassa dinno, yena ca gahito, tasseva hotī”ti. Pāḷiyañca (mahāva. 369) “bhikkhussa, bhikkhave, kālakate saṅgho sāmī pattacīvare, apica gilānupaṭṭhākā bahūpakārā. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghena ticīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātuṃ, yaṃ tattha lahubhaṇḍaṃ lahuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetuṃ, yaṃ tattha garubhaṇḍaṃ garuparikkhāraṃ, taṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa avissajjiyaṃ avebhaṅgika”nti (mahāva. 369) vuttaṃ, tasmā iminā nayena vinicchayo kātabbo.

Regarding a personal monastery, if that individual recipient gives it to his co-residents or others while he is still alive, or if someone accepts that monastery out of trust in him, then it belongs to that person. If he passes away without giving it to anyone, it becomes for the Sangha. As stated in the commentary: “While still alive, he relinquished all his requisites and gave them to someone, or someone accepted them out of trust. To whomever it was given, and by whom it was accepted, it belongs to them.” Moreover, in the Pāḷi (Mahāvagga 369): “Monks, when a monk passes away, the Sangha is the owner of his bowl and robes. And the attendants who cared for the sick were very helpful. I allow, monks, the Sangha to give the three robes and the bowl to the attendants who cared for the sick. Whatever light goods and minor requisites there are, they should be distributed by the Sangha that is present. Whatever heavy goods and major requisites there are, they are not to be given away and are not to be divided, belonging to the Sangha of the four directions, of those who have come and who are yet to come.” Therefore, the decision should be made in this manner.

Saṅghike pana pāḷiyaṃ āgatānaṃ “purimako pacchimako antarāmuttako cā”ti (cūḷava. 318) vuttānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ senāsanaggāhānañca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) āgatānaṃ “utukāle ca vassāvāse cā”ti vuttānaṃ dvinnaṃ senāsanaggāhānañca etarahi asampajjanato anuṭṭhāpanīyapāḷiyaṃ āgatassa attano sabhāvena anuṭṭhāpanīyassa dhuvavāsatthāya saṅghena dinnatāya anuṭṭhāpanīyassa vaseneva vinicchayo hoti. Vuḍḍhataragilānā hi [M 2.0076] attano sabhāvena anuṭṭhāpanīyā honti. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 343) “vuḍḍhataro attano vuḍḍhatāya navakatarena na vuṭṭhāpetabbo, gilāno attano gilānatāyā”ti. Bhaṇḍāgārikadhammakathikādayo [V 2.0056] dhuvavāsatthāya saṅghena dinnatāya anuṭṭhāpanīyā honti. Vuttañhi “saṅgho pana bhaṇḍāgārikassa vā dhammakathikavinayadharādīnaṃ vā…pe… dhuvavāsatthāya vihāraṃ sammannitvā deti, tasmā yassa saṅghena dinno, sopi anuṭṭhāpanīyo”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 120; kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā). So evaṃ veditabbo – etarahi saṅghikavihāresu saṅghattheresu yathākammaṅgatesu tasmiṃ vihāre yo bhikkhu vuḍḍhataro, sopi “ayaṃ vihāro mayā vasitabbo”ti vadati. Yo tattha byatto paṭibalo, sopi tatheva vadati. Yena so vihāro kārito, sopi “mayā pasīditapuggalo āropetabbo”ti vadati. Saṅghopi “mayameva issarā, tasmā amhehi icchitapuggalo āropetabbo”ti vadati. Evaṃdvidhā vā tidhā vā catudhā vā bhinnesu mahantaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ hoti.

In the case of dwellings belonging to the Sangha, the decision is made thus: The three lodging-allocators mentioned in the Pāḷi as “the first, the last, and the one released in between” (Cūḷavagga 318), and the two lodging-allocators mentioned in the commentary as “in the proper season and during the rains-residence” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 318), do not occur nowadays. Therefore, the decision is made only by way of those who are not to be removed: those who are inherently not to be removed, as stated in the Anuṭṭhāpanīya Pāḷi, and those given a dwelling by the Sangha for permanent residence. For, the more senior and the sick are inherently not to be removed. As it was said in the commentary: “A more senior monk should not be removed by a more junior monk on account of his seniority, nor a sick monk on account of his sickness” (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 343). Storekeepers, Dhamma preachers, and the like, who have been given a dwelling by the Sangha for permanent residence, are not to be removed. For it was said: “The Sangha, having authorized a monastery for the storekeeper, or the Dhamma preacher, Vinaya master, and so on... for permanent residence, gives it. Therefore, he to whom it has been given by the Sangha is also not to be removed” (Pācittiya Aṭṭhakathā 120; Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Aṭṭhakathā, Anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā). This should be understood thus: nowadays, in monasteries belonging to the Sangha, when the senior monks of the Sangha have passed away according to their kamma, the most senior monk in that monastery says, “This monastery should be resided in by me.” Whoever is competent and capable there also says the same. The one by whom that monastery was built says, “A person in whom I have faith should be installed.” The Sangha also says, “We ourselves are the masters; therefore, a person desired by us should be installed.” When they are divided in this twofold, threefold, or fourfold manner, a great dispute arises.

Tesu vuḍḍhataro “na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, kenaci pariyāyena vuḍḍhatarassa āsanaṃ paṭibāhitabbanti vadāmi, yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti pāḷipāṭhañca (mahāva. 473; cūḷava. 316), “vuḍḍhataro attano vuḍḍhatāya navakatarena na vuṭṭhāpetabbo”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanañca (pāci. aṭṭha. 119 ādayo; kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) gahetvā “ahameva ettha vuḍḍhataro, mayā vuḍḍhataro añño natthi, tasmā ahameva imasmiṃ vihāre vasitumanucchaviko”ti saññī hoti. Byattopi “bahussutassa saṅghabhāranitthārakassa bhikkhuno anuṭṭhāpanīyasenāsanampī”ti parivāraṭṭhakathāvacanañca (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496), “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena [M 2.0077] bhikkhunā paṭibalena dasavassena vā atirekadasavassena vā upasampādetuṃ, nissayaṃ dātu”ntiādipāḷivacanañca (mahāva. 76, 82) gahetvā “ahameva ettha byatto paṭibalo, na mayā añño byattataro atthi, tasmā ahameva imassa vihārassa anucchaviko”ti saññī. Vihārakārakopi “yena vihāro kārito, so vihārasāmikoti vinayapāṭho (pāci. aṭṭha. 116) atthi, mayā ca bahuṃ dhanaṃ cajitvā ayaṃ vihāro kārito, tasmā mayā pasannapuggalo āropetabbo, na añño”ti saññī. Saṅghopi “saṅghiko nāma vihāro saṅghassa dinno hoti pariccatto”tiādipāḷivacanañca (pāci. 116, 121, 126, 131), antamaso caturaṅgulapādakaṃ gāmadārakehi paṃsvāgārakesu kīḷantehi katampi saṅghassa dinnakālato paṭṭhāya garubhaṇḍaṃ hotī”tiādiaṭṭhakathāvacanañca (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321) gahetvā “ayaṃ vihāro saṅghiko [V 2.0057] saṅghasantako, tasmā amhehi abhirucitapuggalova āropetabbo, na añño”ti saññī.

Among them, the more senior one, taking the Pāli passage, “Indeed, monks, I do not say that in any way should a seat be denied to one who is more senior. Whoever should deny it, commits an offense of wrongdoing” (Mahāva. 473; Cūḷava. 316), and the commentary statement, “A more senior one, on account of his seniority, should not be made to rise by a more junior one” (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 119 ff.; Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha., Anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā), thinks, “I alone am the most senior here; there is no other more senior than me. Therefore, I alone am suitable to reside in this monastery.” The competent one, taking the commentary statement from the Parivāra, “For a monk who is learned and carries through the Sangha’s burden, there is also a non-removable lodging” (Pari. Aṭṭha. 495-496), and the Pāli passage, “I allow, monks, a competent and capable monk of ten years or more than ten years to give higher ordination and to provide dependence” (Mahāva. 76, 82), thinks, “I alone am competent and capable here; there is no other more competent than me. Therefore, I alone am suitable for this monastery.” The monastery builder, recalling the Vinaya passage, “He by whom the monastery was built is the owner of the monastery” (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 116), thinks, “I have spent much wealth to build this monastery. Therefore, a person of my pleasing should be installed here, not another.” The Sangha, considering the Pāli passage, “A monastery called ‘Sanghika’ is one given and relinquished to the Sangha” (Pāci. 116, 121, 126, 131), and the commentary statement, “Even a four-finger-wide base made by village children playing in sand-houses becomes a grave item of property from the time it is given to the Sangha” (Cūḷava. Aṭṭha. 321), thinks, “This monastery is Sanghika, it is the Sangha’s possession. Therefore, only the person agreeable to us should be installed here, not another.”

Tattha vuḍḍhatarassa vacanepi “na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave”tyādivacanaṃ (cūḷava. 316) tesu tesu āsanasālādīsu aggāsanassa vuḍḍhatarārahattā bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā nisinnopi bhikkhu vuḍḍhatare āgate vuṭṭhāya āsanaṃ dātabbaṃ sandhāya bhagavatā vuttaṃ, na dhuvavāsaṃ sandhāya. “Vuḍḍhataro attano vuḍḍhatāya”tyādivacanañca (pāci. aṭṭha. 120; kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) yathāvuḍḍhaṃ senāsane dīyamāne vuḍḍhatare āgate navakataro vuṭṭhāpetabbo, vuṭṭhāpetvā vuḍḍhatarassa senāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, vuḍḍhataro pana navakatarena na vuṭṭhāpetabbo. Kasmā? “Attano vuḍḍhataratāyā”ti utukāle yathāvuḍḍhaṃ senāsanadānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na dhuvavāsatthāya dānaṃ sandhāya[M 2.0078], tasmā idampi vacanaṃ upaparikkhitabbaṃ, na sīghaṃ anujānitabbaṃ.

Therein, regarding the statement of the more senior one, the words “Indeed, monks, I do not say…” and so on (Cūḷava. 316) were spoken by the Blessed One with reference to the fact that in various assembly halls and so forth, a monk, even one seated after having eaten his meal, should rise and give his seat when a more senior one arrives, because the more senior one is worthy of the chief seat; it was not spoken with reference to a permanent dwelling. And the statement, “A more senior one, on account of his seniority…” and so on (Pāci. Aṭṭha. 120; Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha., Anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā), means that when lodgings are being given according to seniority, a more junior one should be made to rise when a more senior one arrives; having been made to rise, the lodging should be given to the more senior one. But a more senior one should not be made to rise by a more junior one. Why? Because “on account of his seniority” was spoken with reference to the seasonal giving of lodgings according to seniority, not with reference to a giving for the purpose of permanent dwelling. Therefore, this statement too should be examined and not hastily approved.

Byattavacanepi “bahussutassa saṅghabhāranitthārakassa”tyādivacanañca (pari. aṭṭha. 445-496) na bahussutamattena saṅghikavihārassa issarabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, atha kho tassa bhikkhussa bahūpakārataṃ guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhetvā saṅghena phāsukaṃ āvāsaṃ anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā dinne so bhikkhu kenaci tamhā vihārā anuṭṭhāpanīyo hoti, imamatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave”tyādivacanañca (mahāva. 82) nissayācariyānaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ pakāsetuṃ bhagavatā vuttaṃ, na saṅghikavihārassa issarattaṃ, tasmā idampi vacanaṃ upaparikkhitabbaṃ, na sīghaṃ anujānitabbaṃ.

Regarding the competent one's statement, the words “for one who is learned and carries through the Sangha’s burden…” and so on (Pari. Aṭṭha. 445-496) were not spoken with reference to lordship over a Sanghika monastery by means of mere learning. Rather, it was spoken with reference to this meaning: having considered that monk's great helpfulness and distinction in qualities, when the Sangha has made a comfortable dwelling non-removable and given it, that monk is not to be removed from that monastery by anyone. And the statement, “I allow, monks…” and so on (Mahāva. 82) was spoken by the Blessed One to declare the characteristics of preceptors of dependence, not lordship over a Sanghika monastery. Therefore, this statement too should be examined and not hastily assented to.

Dāyakavacanaṃ pana nānujānitabbaṃ paṭibāhitabbaṃ. Kasmā? “Yena vihāro kārito”tyādipāṭhassa amukhyavohārattā. Yathā hi puthujjanakāle rūpādīsu sañjanassa bhūtapubbattā bhūtapubbagatiyā arahāpi “satto”ti, evaṃ dānakālato pubbe tassa vihārassa sāmibhūtapubbattā dāyako “vihārasāmiko”ti vuccati, na issarattā. Na hi sakale vinayapiṭake aṭṭhakathāṭīkāsu ca “vissajjetvā dinnassa vihārassa dāyako issaro”ti vā “dāyakena vicāretabbo”ti vā “dāyakasantakavihāro”ti vā pāṭho atthi, “saṅghiko, gaṇasantako, puggaliko”icceva atthi, tasmā tassa vacanaṃ nānujānitabbaṃ.

But the donor's statement should not be assented to; it should be rejected. Why? Because the passage “He by whom the monastery was built…” and so on is a non-primary usage. For just as an Arahant is also called “a being” by way of a former state, because of the former existence of attachment to forms and so on in the time of being a worldling, so too, because of the former state of being the owner of that monastery before the time of the donation, the donor is called “the owner of the monastery,” but not because of authority. Indeed, in the entire Vinaya Piṭaka, its commentaries, and sub-commentaries, there is no passage stating, “The donor is the owner of a monastery that has been relinquished and given away,” or “It should be managed by the donor,” or “A monastery belonging to the donor.” Only “Sanghika,” “belonging to a group,” and “belonging to an individual” are found. Therefore, his statement should not be assented to.

Saṅghassa [V 2.0058] vacanepi “saṅghiko nāma vihāro”tyādivacanaṃ (pāci. 116, 121, 126, 131) saṅghasantakabhāvaṃ saṅghena vicāretabbabhāvaṃ dīpeti, saṅgho pana vicārento pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ sammannitvā tena yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vicāretabbo vā hoti, samaggena saṅghena duvaṅgasamannāgatassa bhikkhuno apalokanakammena [M 2.0079] dhuvavāsatthāya dātabbo vā. Tesu pañcaṅgasamannāgatassa bhikkhuno dullabhattā senāsanaggāhāpakasammutiyā abhāve sati duvaṅgasamannāgato bhikkhu pariyesitabbo. Evaṃ pana apariyesitvā bhaṇḍāgārikatādibahaūpakāratāyuttassa bahussutatādiguṇavisiṭṭhatāvirahassa bhikkhuno āmisagarukatādivasena saṅghena vihāro dātabbo na hoti, tasmā saṅghavacanampi upaparikkhitabbaṃ, na tāva anujānitabbaṃ.

Regarding the Sangha's statement, the words “A monastery called ‘Sanghika’…” and so on (Pāci. 116, 121, 126, 131) indicate its state of belonging to the Sangha and its state of being subject to the Sangha's management. When the Sangha manages it, they should either appoint a monk endowed with five qualities as the assigner of lodgings, by whom it should be managed according to seniority, or it may be given for the purpose of permanent dwelling to a monk endowed with two qualities through an act of announcement by a united Sangha. Among these, since a monk endowed with five qualities is difficult to find, if there is no appointment of an assigner of lodgings, a monk endowed with two qualities should be sought. However, without seeking in this way, a monastery should not be given by the Sangha to a monk who is endowed with much usefulness, such as being a storekeeper, but is devoid of distinguished qualities like being learned, etc., by way of having a high regard for material things. Therefore, the Sangha's statement too must be examined and should not yet be assented to.

Atha tīṇipi vacanāni saṃsandetabbāni. Tattha saṅghassa issarattā saṅgho pucchitabbo “ko puggalo tumhehi abhirucito”ti, pucchitvā “eso”ti vutte “kasmā abhirucito”ti pucchitvā “eso puggalo amhe cīvarādipaccayehi anuggahetā, amhākaṃ ñātisālohito, upajjhāyo, ācariyo, saddhivihāriko, antevāsiko, samānupajjhāyako, samānācariyako, piyasahāyo, lābhī, yasassī, tasmā amhehi abhirucito”ti vutte “na ettāvatā dhuvavāsatthāya vihāro dātabbo”ti paṭikkhipitabbo. Atha “eso puggalo sabbehi amhehi vuḍḍhataro aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍaṃ arahati, dhuvavāsatthāya vihāro pana tassa dātabboti aṭṭhakathācariyehi na vutto”ti vatvā paṭikkhipitabbo. Atha “dhammakathiko, vinayadharo, gaṇavācakaācariyo”ti vutte “eso dhuvavāsatthāya dinnavihārassa anucchaviko, etassa dātabbo”ti anumoditabbo. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Saṅgho pana bhaṇḍāgārikassa vā dhammakathikavinayadharādīnaṃ vā gaṇavācakaācariyassa vā bahūpakārataṃ guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhento dhuvavāsatthāya vihāraṃ sammannitvā detī”ti vacanato viññāyati (pāci. aṭṭha. 129; kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā).

Then these three statements should be correlated. In that case, due to the Sangha's authority, the Sangha must be asked: 'Which individual is agreeable to you?' When asked and they reply, 'This one,' then ask, 'Why is he agreeable?' If they say, 'This individual supports us with robes and other requisites, is our kinsman, preceptor, teacher, fellow resident, pupil, one with the same preceptor, one with the same teacher, a dear friend, one who has gains, one who has renown—therefore he is agreeable to us,' then it should be rejected by saying, 'A dwelling should not be given for permanent residence for this reason alone.' Next, it should be rejected by stating: 'This individual is the eldest among us all, deserving the best seat, the best water, and the best almsfood, but the commentary teachers have not stated that a dwelling should be given to him for permanent residence.' Then, if they say, 'He is a Dhamma speaker, a Vinaya expert, a teacher who recites for the group,' it should be approved by saying, 'This one is suitable for a dwelling given for permanent residence; it should be given to him.' How is this understood? It is understood from the statement: 'The Sangha, considering the great helpfulness and distinguished qualities of the storekeeper, or of the Dhamma speaker, the Vinaya expert, etc., or of the teacher who recites for the group, approves and gives a dwelling for permanent residence' (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 129; Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā).

Idha [M 2.0080] pana sādhakapāṭhe “bhaṇḍāgārikassa vā”ti vijjamāne kasmā sādhyavacane bhaṇḍāgāriko na vuttoti? Etarahi bhaṇḍāgārassa abhāvā. Yadi kesuci vihāresu bhaṇḍāgāraṃ sammanneyya, so bhaṇḍāgāravihāre nisinno saṅghassa pattacīvararakkhaṇādikaṃ upakāraṃ kareyya, tassa bahūpakārataṃ sallakkhento saṅgho bhaṇḍāgārikassa phāsukaṃ āvāsaṃ etarahipi dhuvavāsatthāya [V 2.0059] dadeyya, so tassa visuṃ dhuvavāsavihāroti. Ettha sādhakapāṭhe “dhammakathikavinayadharādīnaṃ vā”tiādisaddena bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmoti vuttaguṇavante saṅgaṇhāti. Athāpi “eso puggalo bahussuto uddesaparipucchādīhi bhikkhūnaṃ bahūpakāro saṅghabhāranitthārako”ti vadati, “sādhu esopi phāsukāvāsassa araho, anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā dhuvavāsatthāya vihāro etassapi dātabbo”ti vatvā anumoditabbo. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Saṅgho pana bahussutassa uddesaparipucchādīhi bahūpakārassa bhāranitthārakassa phāsukaṃ āvāsaṃ anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā detī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 343) vacanato viññāyati.

Here, however, in the supporting passage, when it is stated, 'or for the storekeeper,' why is the storekeeper not mentioned in the statement to be established? At present, because there is no storehouse. If in some monasteries a storehouse were to be established, he, residing in the storehouse dwelling, would perform services for the Sangha, such as guarding the bowls and robes. Recognizing his great helpfulness, the Sangha could grant him a comfortable dwelling even now for permanent residence—that would be his separate dwelling for permanent residence. Here, in the supporting passage, the phrase 'or for a Dhamma speaker, a Vinaya expert, etc.' includes those who are learned, possess tradition, upholders of the Dhamma, upholders of the Vinaya, upholders of the Mātikā, wise, skilled, intelligent, modest, scrupulous, and desirous of training—it embraces those endowed with such qualities. Furthermore, if it is said, 'This individual is learned and greatly helpful to the bhikkhus through instruction and questioning, a reliever of the Sangha's burden,' it should be assented to, saying, 'Good, this one too is worthy of a comfortable dwelling. Having made it non-removable, a dwelling should be given to him for permanent residence.' How is this to be understood? It is understood from the statement: 'The Sangha grants a comfortable dwelling, having made it non-removable, to one who is learned and greatly helpful through instruction and questioning, a reliever of the burden' (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 343).

Athāpi “ayaṃ puggalo dhammakathiko vinayadharo gaṇavācakācariyo saṅghassa bahūpakāro visiṭṭhaguṇayutto”ti vadati, “sādhu etassapi puggalassa dhuvavāsatthāya vihāraṃ sallakkhetvā sammannitvāva dātabbo”ti vatvā anumoditabbo. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Saṅgho pana bhaṇḍāgārikassa vā dhammakathikavinayadharādīnaṃ vā gaṇavācakācariyassa vā bahūpakārataṃ guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhetvā dhuvavāsatthāya [M 2.0081] vihāraṃ sammannitvā detī”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 120; kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vacanato viññāyati.

Furthermore, if they say, 'This individual is a Dhamma speaker, a Vinaya expert, a teacher who recites for the group, and is greatly helpful to the Sangha, endowed with distinguished qualities,' then it should be assented to, saying, 'Good, having carefully considered and designated a dwelling for the permanent residence of this individual as well, it should be given.' How is this understood? It is understood from the statement: 'The Sangha, considering the great helpfulness and distinguished qualities of the storekeeper, or of the Dhamma speaker, the Vinaya expert, etc., or of the teacher who recites for the group, approves and gives a dwelling for permanent residence' (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 120; Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Anupakhajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā).

Athāpi “eso puggalo bahussuto saṅghabhāranitthārako”ti vadati, “sādhu etassapi anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā dātabbo”ti vatvā anumoditabbo. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Bahussutassa saṅghabhāranitthārakassa bhikkhuno anuṭṭhāpanīyasenāsanampī”ti parivāraṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496) vuttattā viññāyati. Tato “evaṃ duvaṅgasampanno puggalo antosīmaṭṭho vā bahisīmaṭṭho vā”ti pucchitvā “antosīmaṭṭho”ti vutte “sādhu suṭṭhu tassa dātabbo”ti sampaṭicchitabbaṃ. “Bahisīmaṭṭho”ti vutte “na dātabbo”ti paṭikkhipitabbaṃ. Kasmāti ce? “Na, bhikkhave, nissīme ṭhitassa senāsanaṃ gāhetabbaṃ, yo gāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 318) vacanatoti.

Furthermore, if they say, 'This individual is learned and a reliever of the Sangha's burden,' it should be assented to, saying, 'Good, having made it non-removable, it should be given to him as well.' How is this understood? It is understood from the statement in the Parivāra Commentary (Pari. Aṭṭha. 495-496): 'Even a non-removable lodging is for a learned bhikkhu who is a reliever of the Sangha's burden.' Then, having asked, 'Is such an individual endowed with these two qualities within the boundary or outside the boundary?' if it is said, 'Within the boundary,' it should be assented to, saying, 'Good, it should be given well to him.' If it is said, 'Outside the boundary,' it should be rejected, saying, 'It should not be given.' Why is that? Because of the statement: 'Bhikkhus, a lodging should not be assigned to one staying outside the boundary; whoever assigns it incurs an offense of wrong-doing' (Cūḷavagga 318).

Atha “duvaṅgasamannāgate antosīmaṭṭhe asati ekaṅgasamannāgato antosīmaṭṭho atthī”ti pucchitvā “atthī”ti vutte “sādhu suṭṭhu etassa dātabbo”ti sampaṭicchitabbaṃ.
