Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Bahūpakārataṃ guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhentoti bhaṇḍāgārikassa bahūpakārataṃ dhammakathikādīnaṃ [V 2.0060] guṇavisiṭṭhatañca sallakkhento”ti sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.119-121) ekekaṅgavasena āgatattā viññāyati. “Antosīmaṭṭho ekaṅgasamannāgatopi natthi, bahisīmaṭṭhova atthī”ti vutte “āgantvā antosīme ṭhitassa dātabbo”ti vattabbo. Kasmāti ce? “Asampattānampi upacārasīmaṃ paviṭṭhānaṃ antevāsikādīsu gaṇhantesu dātabbamevā”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) vacanato viññāyati.

Then, having asked, 'If one endowed with two qualities within the boundary is absent, is there an individual endowed with a single quality within the boundary?' and being told, 'There is,' it should be assented to, saying, 'Good, it should certainly be given to him.' How is this understood? It is understood because it is presented in terms of each single quality in the Sāratthadīpanī (Sārattha. Ṭī. Pācittiya 3.119-121): 'By considering the great helpfulness and distinguished qualities—that is, considering the great helpfulness of the storekeeper and the distinguished qualities of the Dhamma speakers, etc.' If it is said, 'There is none endowed with even a single quality within the boundary, but there is one outside the boundary,' it should be stated, 'It should be given to one who comes and stands within the boundary.' Why is that? Because it is understood from the statement in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379): 'Even for those who have not yet arrived, if they have entered the boundary of proximity, it should be given when their pupils and others receive it for them.'

Sace [M 2.0082] pana ekaṅgayuttabhāvena vā duvaṅgayuttabhāvena vā samānā dve tayo bhikkhū antosīmāyaṃ vijjamānā bhaveyyuṃ, kassa dātabboti? Vaḍḍhatarassāti. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Na ca, bhikkhave, saṅghikaṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ paṭibāhitabbaṃ, yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 311) vacanatoti. Sace pana antosīmāyaṃ ekaṅgayutto vā duvaṅgayutto vā bhikkhu natthi, sabbeva āvāsikā bālā abyattā, evaṃ sati kassa dātabboti? Yo taṃ vihāraṃ āgacchati āgantuko bhikkhu, so ce lajjī hoti pesalo bahussuto sikkhākāmo, so tehi āvāsikehi bhikkhūhi aññattha agamanatthaṃ saṅgahaṃ katvā so āvāso dātabbo.

If, however, two or three bhikkhus, equal in their endowment with one or two factors, should be present within the boundary, to whom should it be given? To the more senior. How is this to be known? Because of the statement: 'And, bhikkhus, what belongs to the Sangha should not be withheld from distribution according to seniority. Whoever should withhold it incurs an offense of wrong-doing' (Cūḷavagga 311). But if within the boundary there is no bhikkhu endowed with one or two factors, and all the resident bhikkhus are foolish and unskilled, in such a case, to whom should it be given? To whichever visiting bhikkhu comes to that monastery—if he is conscientious, amiable, learned, and desirous of training—he should be welcomed by those resident bhikkhus so that he does not depart elsewhere, and that dwelling should be given to him.

Ayamattho kathaṃ jānitabboti ce? “Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse sambahulā bhikkhū viharanti bālā abyattā, te na jānanti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Tattha añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo, tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi so bhikkhu saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabbo upalāpetabbo upaṭṭhāpetabbo cuṇṇena mattikāya dantakaṭṭhena mukhodakena. No ce saṅgaṇheyyuṃ anuggaṇheyyuṃ upalāpeyyuṃ upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ cuṇṇena mattikāya dantakaṭṭhena mukhodakena, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (mahāva. 163) sammāsambuddhena paññattattā, aṭṭhakathāyañca (mahāva. aṭṭha. 163) “saṅgahetabboti ‘sādhu, bhante, āgatattha, idha bhikkhā sulabhā sūpabyañjanaṃ atthi, vasatha anukkaṇṭhamānā’ti evaṃ piyavacanena saṅgahetabbo, punappunaṃ tathākaraṇavasena anuggahetabbo, ‘āma vasissāmī’ti paṭivacanadāpanena [M 2.0083] upalāpetabbo. Atha vā catūhi paccayehi saṅgahetabbo ceva anuggahetabbo ca, piyavacanena upalāpetabbo, kaṇṇasukhaṃ ālapitabboti attho, cuṇṇādīhi upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Āpatti dukkaṭassāti sace sakalopi saṅgho na karoti, sabbesaṃ dukkaṭaṃ. Idha neva therā, na daharā [V 2.0061] muccanti, sabbehi vārena upaṭṭhātabbo, attano vāre anupaṭṭhahantassa āpatti. Tena pana mahātherānaṃ pariveṇasammajjanadantakaṭṭhadānādīni na sāditabbāni. Evampi sati mahātherehi sāyaṃpātaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgantabbaṃ. Tena pana tesaṃ āgamanaṃ ñatvā paṭhamataraṃ mahātherānaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ gantabbaṃ. Sacassa saddhiṃcarā bhikkhū upaṭṭhākā atthi, ‘mayhaṃ upaṭṭhākā atthi, tumhe appossukkā viharathā’ti vattabbaṃ. Athāpissa saddhiṃ carā natthi, tasmiṃyeva pana vihāre eko vā dve vā vattasampannā vadanti ‘mayhaṃ therassa kattabbaṃ karissāma, avasesā phāsu viharantū’ti, sabbesaṃ anāpattī”ti vuttattā. Evaṃ tādisaṃ bahisīmato antosīmamāgataṃ lajjīpesalabahussutasikkhākāmabhūtaṃ bhikkhuṃ antosīmāya dhuvanivāsatthāya phāsukaṃ āvāsaṃ anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā dātabboti viññāyati.

How is this meaning to be understood? “Here, bhikkhus, in a certain residence, several bhikkhus dwell who are foolish and unskilled. They do not know the Uposatha, the Uposatha observance, the Pātimokkha, or the Pātimokkha recitation. Then another bhikkhu arrives—learned, versed in the tradition, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the mātikā, wise, expert, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, should welcome that bhikkhu, assist him, persuade him, and attend to him with powder, clay, tooth-sticks, and mouth-rinsing water. If they do not welcome him, assist him, persuade him, or attend to him with powder, clay, tooth-sticks, and mouth-rinsing water, they incur an offence of wrong-doing.” Because this was laid down by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One (Mahāvagga 163), and the commentary (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 163) explains: “‘Should welcome him’ means they should welcome him with kind words such as, ‘It is good, venerable sir, that you have come. Here almsfood is easily obtained, and there are curries and sauces. Please stay without discontent.’ They should assist him by repeatedly acting in this way. They should persuade him by getting him to reply, ‘Yes, I will stay.’ Alternatively, they should welcome and assist him with the four requisites. They should persuade him with kind words, that is, by speaking in a way that is pleasant to the ear. They should attend to him with powder and so on. ‘They incur an offence of wrong-doing’ means if the entire Saṅgha fails to do so, all incur an offence of wrong-doing. Here, neither the elders nor the young ones are exempt. All must take turns attending to him. If one does not attend to him when it is his turn, he incurs an offence. However, the great elders should not be made to sweep the monastery precincts or give tooth-sticks and the like. Even so, the great elders should come in the evening and morning for attendance. But he, knowing of their arrival, should go first to attend to the great elders. If he has companion bhikkhus who are attendants, he should say: ‘I have attendants; you may dwell without concern.’ But if he has no companions, and in that very monastery one or two bhikkhus who are complete in their duties say: ‘We will do what needs to be done for our elder; let the rest dwell at ease,’ then there is no offence for anyone.” Thus, it is understood that such a bhikkhu—who has come from outside the boundary into the boundary, who is conscientious, amiable, learned, and desirous of training—should be given a comfortable dwelling within the boundary for the purpose of stable residence, one made suitable so that he will not have to depart.

Nanu ca “na, bhikkhave, nissīme ṭhitassa senāsanaṃ gāhetabbaṃ, yo gāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 318) bhagavatā vuttaṃ, atha kasmā nissīmato āgatassa dhuvavāsatthāya vihāro dātabboti? Vuccate – “nissīme ṭhitassā”ti idaṃ anādare sāmivacanaṃ, tasmā nissīme ṭhitaṃyeva senāsanaṃ na gāhetabbanti attho daṭṭhabbo, na nissīme ṭhitassa tassa bhikkhussa antosīmaṃ paviṭṭhassapi senāsanaṃ na gāhetabbanti attho, tasmā pubbe bahisīmāyaṃ ṭhitepi idāni antosīmaṃ paviṭṭhakālato paṭṭhāya catupaccayabhāgo labbhati. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ [M 2.0084] (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) “asukavihāre kira bahuṃ cīvaraṃ uppannanti sutvā yojanantarikavihāratopi bhikkhū āgacchanti, sampattasampattānaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya dātabba”nti. Antosīmaṭṭhesu pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ asakkontesu yattha pātimokkhuddesako atthi, so āvāso gantabbo hoti. Antovassepi pātimokkhuddesakena vinā vassaṃ vasituṃ na labhati. Yattha pātimokkhuddesako atthi, tattha gantvā vassaṃ vasitabbaṃ, tasmā bahisīmato āgatopi lajjīpesalabahussutasikkhākāmabhikkhu saṅgahetabbo hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā –

But surely, was it not said by the Blessed One: “Bhikkhus, a dwelling should not be allocated for one staying outside the boundary. Whoever should do so incurs an offence of wrong-doing” (Cūḷavagga 318)? Then why should a monastery be given for permanent residence to one who has come from outside the boundary? It is said: The phrase ‘for one staying outside the boundary’ here is a genitive of disregard. Therefore, the meaning should be understood as: a dwelling should not be allocated for one who is actually staying outside the boundary. It does not mean that a dwelling should not be allocated to that bhikkhu once he has entered the boundary, even though he was previously staying outside it. Hence, even if he was previously staying outside the boundary, from the time he has now entered the boundary, he obtains a share of the four requisites. For it was said in the commentary (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 379): “Having heard that much robe-cloth had arisen in such-and-such a monastery, bhikkhus came even from a monastery a yojana away. It should be given to all who have arrived, from the moment of their arrival.” If those within the boundary are unable to recite the Pātimokkha, they should go to a residence where there is a Pātimokkha reciter. Even during the rains-residence, one is not permitted to dwell without a Pātimokkha reciter. One must go where there is a Pātimokkha reciter and dwell there for the rains. Therefore, a bhikkhu who has come from outside the boundary—if he is conscientious, amiable, learned, and desirous of training—should be welcomed. For this has been said by the Blessed One:

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā bhikkhū viharanti bālā abyattā, te na jānanti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo ‘gacchāvuso saṃkhittena vā vitthārena vā pātimokkhaṃ pariyāpuṇitvā āgacchā’ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi sabbeheva yattha jānanti [V 2.0062] uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā, so āvāso gantabbo. No ce gaccheyyuṃ, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse sambahulā bhikkhū vassaṃ vasanti bālā abyattā, te na jānanti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo ‘gacchāvuso saṃkhittena vā vitthārena vā pātimokkhaṃ pariyāpuṇitvā āgacchā’ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, eko bhikkhu sattāhakālikaṃ [M 2.0085] pāhetabbo ‘gacchāvuso saṃkhittena vā vitthārena vā pātimokkhaṃ pariyāpuṇitvā āgacchā’ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, na, bhikkhave, tehi bhikkhūhi tasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃ vasitabbaṃ, vaseyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassāti” (mahāva. 163).

“Here, bhikkhus, in a certain residence, on that Uposatha day, several bhikkhus are dwelling who are foolish and unskilled. They do not know the Uposatha, the Uposatha observance, the Pātimokkha, or the Pātimokkha recitation. Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, should promptly send one bhikkhu to a nearby residence with the instruction: ‘Go, friend, learn the Pātimokkha briefly or in detail and return.’ If this can be achieved, that is skilful. If it cannot be achieved, those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, should all go to a residence where they know the Uposatha, the Uposatha observance, the Pātimokkha, or the Pātimokkha recitation. If they do not go, they incur an offence of wrong-doing. Here, bhikkhus, in a certain residence, several bhikkhus are spending the Rains who are foolish and unskilled. They do not know the Uposatha, the Uposatha observance, the Pātimokkha, or the Pātimokkha recitation. Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, should promptly send one bhikkhu to a nearby residence with the instruction: ‘Go, friend, learn the Pātimokkha briefly or in detail and return.’ If this can be achieved, that is skilful. If it cannot be achieved, they should send one bhikkhu with a seven-day leave: ‘Go, friend, learn the Pātimokkha briefly or in detail and return.’ If this can be achieved, that is skilful. If it cannot be achieved, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus should not spend the Rains in that residence. If they should spend it there, they incur an offence of wrong-doing.” (Mahāvagga 163)

Evaṃ bahisīmato āgatassapi saṅghassa upakāraṃ kātuṃ sakkontassa visiṭṭhaguṇayuttassa dātabbabhāvo viññāyati, tasmā “amhākaṃ gaṇo na hoti, amhākaṃ vaṃso paveṇī na hoti, amhākaṃ sandiṭṭhasambhatto na hotī”tiādīni vatvā na paṭikkhipitabbo. Gaṇādibhāvo hi appamāṇaṃ, yathāvuttabahūpakāratādibhāvoyeva pamāṇaṃ. Sāmaggikaraṇato paṭṭhāya hi samānagaṇo hoti. Tathā hi ukkhittānuvattakānaṃ laddhinānāsaṃvāsakānampi laddhivissajjanena tividhaukkhepanīyakammakatānaṃ kammanānāsaṃvāsakānampi osāraṇaṃ katvā sāmaggikaraṇena saṃvāso bhagavatā anuññāto. Alajjiṃ pana bahussutampi saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. So hi alajjīparisaṃ vaḍḍhāpeti, lajjīparisaṃ hāpeti. Bhaṇḍanakārakaṃ pana vihāratopi nikkaḍḍhitabbaṃ. Tathā hi “bhaṇḍanakārakakalahakārakameva sakalasaṅghārāmato nikkaḍḍhituṃ labhati. So hi pakkhaṃ labhitvā saṅghampi bhindeyya. Alajjīādayo pana attano vasanaṭṭhānatoyeva nikkaḍḍhitabbā, sakalasaṅghārāmato nikkaḍḍhituṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 128) vuttaṃ.

Thus, even one who comes from outside the boundary is understood to be worthy of being given a dwelling if he is capable of benefiting the Saṅgha and endowed with distinguished qualities. Therefore, one should not refuse him by saying, “He is not of our group, he is not of our lineage or tradition, he is not one we have personally known or associated with,” and so on. For being of a certain group is not the measure; only being greatly beneficial, as described, is the measure. Indeed, from the act of reconciliation, one becomes of the same group. Thus, even for those who follow expelled monks—those who are not in communion due to differing views—communion has been permitted by the Blessed One through their abandoning of those views, and even for those on whom the threefold act of expulsion has been performed—those who are not in communion due to the act—communion has been permitted by restoring them and making them unified. However, it is not proper to welcome even a learned but shameless person, for he increases the assembly of the shameless and diminishes the assembly of the conscientious. But a quarrelsome person should be expelled even from the monastery. As stated in the commentary (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 128): “One is indeed permitted to expel a quarrelsome and contentious person from the entire Saṅgha’s monastery, for if he gains a faction, he might even split the Saṅgha. But the shameless and others should be expelled only from their own dwelling place; it is not proper to expel them from the entire Saṅgha’s monastery.”

Vuḍḍhāpacāyanādisāmaggirasarahitaṃ visabhāgapuggalampi saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ na labhati. Vuttañhi “evarūpena hi visabhāgapuggalena ekavihāre vā ekapariveṇe vā vasantena attho natthi, tasmā sabbatthevassa nivāso vārito”ti (pāci. aṭṭha. 122), tasmā āvāsiko vā hotu [V 2.0063] āgantuko vā, sagaṇo vā hotu aññagaṇo [M 2.0086] vā, bahussutasīlavantabhūto bhikkhu saṅgahetabbo. Vuttañhi bhagavatā –

One cannot include even a person of dissimilar qualities who lacks the essence of concord, such as respect for elders. For it is said: “Indeed, there is no benefit in dwelling together in the same monastery or enclosure with such a person of dissimilar qualities; therefore, his dwelling is forbidden everywhere” (Pāc. Aṭṭha. 122). Therefore, whether he is a resident or a visitor, whether he belongs to the same community or another, a monk who is learned and virtuous should be included. For the Blessed One has said:

“Bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ, sappaññaṃ buddhasāvakaṃ;

Nekkhaṃ jambonadasseva, ko taṃ nanditumarahati;

Devāpi naṃ pasaṃsanti, brahmunāpi pasaṃsito”ti. (a. ni. 4.6) –

“One who has heard much, a bearer of the Dhamma, wise, a disciple of the Buddha, like an ornament of Jambu gold—who is fit to censure him? Even the gods praise him; he is praised by Brahmā as well.”

Ayaṃ antosīmaṭṭhena saṅghena bahūpakāratāguṇavisiṭṭhatāsaṅkhātehi guṇehi yuttassa saṅghabhāranitthārakassa bhikkhuno phāsukaṃ āvāsaṃ anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā dāne vinicchayo.

This is the decision regarding the giving of a comfortable dwelling, made un-abandonable, by the Saṅgha within the boundary, to a monk who bears the burden of the Saṅgha and is endowed with qualities reckoned as being of great benefit and distinguished virtue.

Yadā pana saṅghatthero jarādubbalatāya vā rogapīḷitatāya vā vivekajjhāsayatāya vā gaṇaṃ apariharitukāmo aññassa dātukāmo, attano accayena vā kalahavivādābhāvamicchanto saddhivihārikādīnaṃ niyyātetukāmo hoti, tadā na attano issaravatāya dātabbaṃ, ayaṃ vihāro saṅghiko, tasmā saṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā taṃ kāraṇaṃ ācikkhitvā bahūpakāratāguṇavisiṭṭhatāyuttapuggalo vicināpetabbo. Tato saṅgho cattāri agatigamanāni anupagantvā bhagavato ajjhāsayānurūpaṃ lajjīpesalabahussutasikkhākāmabhūtaṃ puggalaṃ vicinitvā “ayaṃ bhikkhu imassa vihārassa anucchaviko”ti āroceti. Mahātherassapi tameva ruccati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce ruccati, attano bhārabhūtaṃ vuttappakāraaṅgaviyuttaṃ puggalaṃ dātukāmo hoti. Evaṃ sante saṅgho chandādiagatiṃ na gacchati, puggalova gacchati, tasmā saṅghasseva anumatiyā vihāro dātabbo.

When the senior monk of the Saṅgha, due to old age and weakness, illness and affliction, or a desire for solitude, wishes not to maintain the community, wishes to give it to another, or wishes to hand it over to his disciples upon his passing to prevent quarrels and disputes, then it should not be given by his own authority. This monastery belongs to the Saṅgha. Therefore, the Saṅgha should be assembled, the reason should be explained, and an individual endowed with the qualities of being greatly beneficial and distinguished in virtue should be sought. Then, the Saṅgha, without resorting to the four courses of partiality, should choose a person in accordance with the Blessed One’s intention—one who is conscientious, amiable, learned, and desirous of training—and declare: “This monk is fitting for this monastery.” If this also pleases the senior monk, then that is skillful. If it does not please him, and he wishes to give it to someone who is a burden and lacks the qualities described, in such a case, the Saṅgha does not proceed with partiality; only the individual does. Therefore, the monastery should be given only with the Saṅgha’s approval.

Sace pana saṅgho yaṃ kañci āmisaṃ labhitvā yathāvuttaguṇaviyuttassa bhikkhuno dātukāmo hoti, puggalo [M 2.0087] pana bhagavato ajjhāsayānurūpaṃ vuttappakāraaṅgayuttabhūtasseva bhikkhussa dātukāmo, tadā puggalopi saṅghapariyāpannoyevāti katvā dhammakammakārakassa puggalasseva anumatiyā vihāro dātabbo, na saṅghānumatiyā. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.538-539) “sace saṅgho kiñci labhitvā āmisagarukatāya na nivāreti, eko bhikkhu nivāreti, sova bhikkhu issaro. Saṅghikesu hi kammesu yo dhammakammaṃ karoti, sova issaro”ti. Vuttañhi –

If the Saṅgha, having obtained some material offering, wishes to give it to a monk who lacks the aforementioned qualities, but an individual monk wishes to give it to a monk who possesses the qualities in accordance with the Blessed One’s intention and is endowed with the characteristics mentioned, then considering that the individual is also included within the Saṅgha, the dwelling should be given with the consent of the individual who performs the lawful act, not with the consent of the Saṅgha. For it is stated in the commentary (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.538-539): “If the Saṅgha obtains something and does not prevent it out of regard for material gain, but a single monk prevents it, that monk is the authority. For in Saṅgha matters, whoever performs the lawful act is the authority.” Indeed, it is said:

“Chandā [V 2.0064] dosā bhayā mohā;

Yo dhammaṃ ativattati;

Nihīyati tassa yaso;

Kāḷapakkheva candimā.

“Through desire, hatred, fear, or delusion, whoever transgresses the Dhamma, their glory wanes, like the moon during the dark fortnight.

“Chandā dosā bhayā mohā;

Yo dhammaṃ nātivattati;

Āpūrati tassa yaso;

Sukkapakkheva candimā”ti. (dī. ni. 3.246; a. ni. 4.17-18; pāri. 382, 386);

Through desire, hatred, fear, or delusion, whoever does not transgress the Dhamma, their glory waxes full, like the moon in the bright fortnight.”

Yadā pana theropi kiñci avatvā yathākammaṅgato, saṅghopi na kassaci vicāreti, evaṃ saṅghikavihāre abhikkhuke suññe vattamāne tasmiṃ dese yena kenaci sāsanassa vuddhimicchantena ācariyena antosīmaṭṭhakā bhikkhū evaṃ samussāhetabbā “mā tumhe āyasmanto evaṃ akattha, antosīmaṭṭhakesu bhikkhūsu bahūpakāratādiyuttaṃ puggalaṃ vicinatha, vicinitvā labhantā tassa puggalassa samaggena saṅghena dhuvavāsatthāya vihāraṃ anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā detha, no ce antosīmaṭṭhakesu bhikkhūsu alattha, atha bahisīmaṭṭhakesu bhikkhūsu vicinatha. Bahisīmaṭṭhakesu bhikkhūsu vicinitvā yathāvuttaaṅgayuttapuggale labbhamāne taṃ puggalaṃ antosīmaṃ pavesetvā [M 2.0088] antosīmaṭṭhakassa saṅghassa anumatiyā dhuvavāsatthāya vihāraṃ sammannitvā anuṭṭhāpanīyaṃ katvā detha. Evaṃ karontā hi tumhe āyasmanto appicchakathā-santosakathā-sallekhakathā-pavivittakathāvīriyārambhakathā-sīlakathā-samādhikathā-paññākathā-vimuttikathā-vimuttiñāṇadassanakathāsaṅkhātadasakathāvatthusampannaṃ puggalaṃ upanissāya assutapubbaṃ dhammaṃ suṇissatha, sutapubbaṃ dhammaṃ pariyodāpissatha, kaṅkhaṃ vinodissatha, diṭṭhiṃ ujuṃ karissatha, cittaṃ pasādessatha. Yassa lajjino pesalassa bahussutassa sikkhākāmassa bhikkhuno bhikkhaṃ anusikkhamānā saddhāya vaḍḍhissanti, sīlena vaḍḍhissanti, sutena vaḍḍhissanti, cāgena vaḍḍhissanti, paññāya vaḍḍhissantī”ti. Vuttañhetaṃ visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 1.14) “katamo upanissayagocaro dasakathāvatthuguṇasamannāgato kalyāṇamitto, yaṃ nissāya assutaṃ suṇāti, sutaṃ pariyodapeti, kaṅkhaṃ vitarati, diṭṭhiṃ ujuṃ karoti, cittaṃ pasādeti. Yassa vā anusikkhamāno saddhāya vaḍḍhati, sīlena vaḍḍhati, sutena vaḍḍhati[V 2.0065], cāgena vaḍḍhati, paññāya vaḍḍhati, ayaṃ vuccati upanissayagocaro”ti. Evaṃ samussāhetvā dhammakathaṃ katvā antosīmaṭṭhakasaṅgheneva dhuvavāsavihāro dāpetabboti.

When the elder passes away according to his kamma without saying anything, and the Saṅgha does not investigate anyone, then, while the Saṅgha-owned monastery remains without monks and empty in that region, any teacher desiring the growth of the Dispensation should encourage the monks within the boundary thus: “Venerable sirs, do not act in this way. Among the monks within the boundary, seek out an individual endowed with qualities such as being of great benefit. Having found such a person, let the united Saṅgha grant him the monastery for permanent residence, having made it un-abandonable. If no such person is found among the monks within the boundary, then search among the monks outside the boundary. Having searched among the monks outside the boundary, if a person endowed with the qualities as described is found, bring him within the boundary and, with the permission of the Saṅgha within the boundary, appoint the monastery for his permanent residence, having made it un-abandonable. By acting thus, venerable sirs, relying on a person endowed with the ten topics of discussion—namely, talk on fewness of wishes, contentment, effacement, seclusion, energetic striving, virtue, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation—you will hear the Dhamma not heard before, clarify what has been heard, dispel doubt, straighten your views, and gladden your minds. Following the training of a conscientious, amiable, learned monk who is desirous of training, you will grow in faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom.” For it is said in the Visuddhimagga (Visuddhi. 1.14): “What is the resort of reliance? A good friend endowed with the qualities of the ten topics of discussion, relying on whom one hears what has not been heard, clarifies what has been heard, gets through doubt, straightens one’s view, and gladdens the mind. Or one who, by following his example, grows in faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom—this is called the resort of reliance.” Having thus encouraged them and given a Dhamma talk, the monastery for permanent residence should be granted by the Saṅgha within the boundary itself.

Evaṃ jinasāsanassa, vaḍḍhikāmo supesalo;

Akāsi paññavā bhikkhu, suṭṭhu āvāsanicchayanti.

Thus, the wise and amiable monk, desiring the growth of the Victor's Dispensation, made an excellent determination concerning dwellings.

Iti vinayasaṅgahasaṃvaṇṇanābhūte vinayālaṅkāre

Thus, in the Vinayālaṅkāra, which is a commentary on the Vinayasaṅgaha.

Vihāravinicchayakathālaṅkāro.

The Ornament of the Discourse on the Determination of Monasteries.

29. Kathinatthāravinicchayakathā

29. Discourse on the Determination of the Spreading of the Kathina.

226. Evaṃ [M 2.0089] catupaccayabhājanavinicchayaṃ kathetvā idāni kathinavinicchayaṃ kathetumāha “kathinanti ettha panā”tiādi. Tattha kathinanti katamaṃ kathinaṃ? Samūhapaññatti. Na hi paramatthato kathinaṃ nāma eko dhammo atthi, purimavassaṃvutthā bhikkhū, anūnapañcavaggasaṅgho, cīvaramāso, dhammena samena uppannacīvarantiādīsu yesu nāmarūpesu samuppajjamānesu tesaṃ nāmarūpadhammānaṃ samūhasamavāyasaṅkhātaṃ samūhapaññattimattameva kathinaṃ. Ayamattho kathaṃ jānitabboti? “Tesaññeva dhammānaṃ saṅgaho samavāyo nāmaṃ nāmakammaṃ nāmadheyyaṃ nirutti byañjanaṃ abhilāpo, yadidaṃ kathina”nti parivārapāḷiyaṃ (pari. 412) āgatattā ca, “tesaññeva dhammānanti yesu rūpādidhammesu sati kathinaṃ nāma hoti, tesaṃ samodhānaṃ missībhāvo. Nāmaṃ nāmakammantiādinā pana ‘kathina’nti idaṃ bahūsu dhammesu nāmamattaṃ, na paramatthato eko dhammo atthīti dassetī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pari. aṭṭha. 412) āgatattā ca, “yesu rūpādidhammesūti purimavassaṃvutthā bhikkhū, pañcahi anūno saṅgho, cīvaramāso, dhammena samena samuppannaṃ cīvaranti evamādīsu yesu rūpārūpadhammesu. Satīti santesu. Missībhāvoti saṃsaggatā samūhapaññattimattaṃ. Tenāha na paramatthato eko dhammo atthīti dassetī”ti vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. parivāra 2.412) āgatattā ca jānitabboti.

226. Having thus explained the determination of the distribution of the four requisites, now the determination of the Kathina is to be explained, beginning with, “Now, as to the Kathina…” and so on. Herein, what is the Kathina? It is a collective designation. For ultimately, there is no single phenomenon called the Kathina. When monks who have completed the rains-residence, a Saṅgha of at least five members, the robe season, a robe properly and lawfully acquired, and so forth—when these name-and-form phenomena arise, the Kathina is merely a collective designation, reckoned as the aggregation and association of these name-and-form phenomena. How is this meaning to be understood? Because it is stated in the Parivāra Pāḷi (Pari. 412): “The gathering, the coming together of those very phenomena is called the name, the naming, the designation, the term, the expression, the appellation—that is, the Kathina.” And because it is stated in the commentary (Pari. Aṭṭha. 412): “‘Those very phenomena’ means the phenomena in which the Kathina exists, their combination, their mingling. By ‘the name, the naming,’ etc., it shows that ‘Kathina’ is merely a name applied to many phenomena, not an ultimate single phenomenon.” And because it is stated in the Vimativinodanī (Vi. Vi. Ṭī. Parivāra 2.412): “‘In which phenomena of form, etc.’ refers to those phenomena of form and formlessness, such as monks who have completed the rains-residence, a Saṅgha of no less than five, the robe season, a robe properly and lawfully acquired, and so on. ‘Exists’ means when they are present. ‘Mingling’ means their association, merely a collective designation. Therefore, he said, ‘it shows that there is no ultimate single phenomenon.’” This is to be understood.

Kenaṭṭhena [V 2.0066] kathinanti? Thiraṭṭhena. Kasmā thiranti? Anāmantacāraasamādānacāragaṇabhojanayāvadatthacīvarayocatatthacīvaruppādasaṅkhāte pañcānisaṃse antokaraṇasamatthatāya. Vuttañhi sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.306) “pañcānisaṃse antokaraṇasamatthatāya thiranti attho”ti, tathā vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.306) vajirabuddhiṭīkāyañca [M 2.0090] (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306). Atha vā kenaṭṭhena kathinanti? Saṅgaṇhanaṭṭhena. Kathaṃ saṅgaṇhātīti? Pañcānisaṃse aññattha gantuṃ adatvā saṅgaṇhāti saṅkhipitvā gaṇhāti. Vuttañhi vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. abhi. ṭī. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “pañcānisaṃse aññattha gantuṃ adatvā saṅgaṇhanaṭṭhena kathina”nti.

By what meaning is it called Kathina? By the meaning of firmness. Why is it firm? Because it has the capacity to contain the five benefits, namely: going about without informing, going about without taking the set of robes, group meals, as many robes as are needed, and the arising of robes there. As stated in the Sāratthadīpanī (Sārattha. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 3.306): “The meaning is ‘firm’ because of its capacity to contain the five benefits.” Similarly, in the Vimativinodanī (Vi. Vi. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 2.306) and the Vajirabuddhiṭīkā (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 306). Alternatively, by what meaning is it called Kathina? By the meaning of encompassing. How does it encompass? It encompasses, that is, it gathers together and holds the five benefits by not allowing them to go elsewhere. As stated in the Vinayatthamañjūsā (Kaṅkhā. Abhi. Ṭī. Kathinasikkhāpada-vaṇṇanā): “By the meaning of encompassing, because it does not allow the five benefits to go elsewhere, it is called Kathina.”

Kathina-saddo kāya dhātuyā kena paccayena sijjhatīti? Ṭīkācariyā dhātupaccaye acintetvā anipphannapāṭipadikavaseneva vaṇṇenti, tasmā ayaṃ saddo ruḷhīsuddhanāmabhūto anipphannapāṭipadikasaddoti vuccati. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? Tīsupi vinayaṭīkāsu (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.306; vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.306; vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306; kaṅkhā. abhi. ṭī. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “thiranti attho” icceva vaṇṇitattā. Pañcānisaṃse antokaraṇasamatthatāyāti pana thiratā cassa hetupadameva. Atha vā kathina-saddo kathadhātuyā inapaccayena sijjhati. Kathaṃ? Katha saṅgahaṇetimassa laddhadhātusaññādissa pañcānisaṃse aññattha gantuṃ adatvā saṅgaṇhātīti atthe “ina sabbatthā”ti yogavibhāgena vā “supato cā”ti ettha ca-saddena vā inapaccayaṃ katvā parakkharaṃ netvā kathinasaddato syuppattādimhi kate rūpaṃ. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Saṅgaṇhanaṭṭhenā”ti vuttaṃ kaṅkhāvitaraṇīṭīkāpāṭhaṃ nissāya viññāyati. Atha vā kaṭha kicchajīvaneti dhātuto inapaccayaṃ katvā sijjhati. Ayamattho “kaṭha kicchajīvane, muddhajadutiyanto dhātu, ino”ti abhidhānappadīpikāṭīkāyaṃ vuttattā viññāyati.

From which root and by which suffix is the word “Kathina” formed? The sub-commentary teachers, without considering the root and suffix, explain it merely as an underived nominal stem. Therefore, this word is called an underived nominal stem, being a purely conventional name. How is this to be known? Because in all three Vinaya sub-commentaries (Sārattha. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 3.306; Vi. Vi. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 2.306; Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 306; Kaṅkhā. Abhi. Ṭī. Kathinasikkhāpada-vaṇṇanā), it is explained only as “‘firm’ is the meaning.” However, “due to its capacity to contain the five benefits” is merely the causal term for its firmness. Alternatively, the word “Kathina” is formed from the root `kath` with the suffix `ina`. How? From the root `kath` in the sense of ‘to collect,’ which has received the designation of a root, etc., in the sense that it collects the five benefits by not allowing them to go elsewhere, the suffix `ina` is applied, either by `yogavibhāga` of the rule `ina sabbatthā` or by the word `ca` in `supato cā`. Then, by taking the subsequent letter, the form is made when the case endings, beginning with `si`, are applied to the word `kathina`. How is this to be known? It is to be known by relying on the passage in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-ṭīkā, which states, “in the sense of gathering.” Alternatively, it is formed from the root `kaṭha`, meaning “to live with difficulty,” by applying the suffix `ina`. This meaning is to be known from what is stated in the Abhidhānappadīpikā-ṭīkā: “`kaṭha` in the sense of ‘to live with difficulty,’ the root ending in the second cerebral consonant, with `ina`.”

Bahū pana paṇḍitā imaṃ pāṭhaṃyeva gahetvā “kathina-saddo muddhajadutiyantoyeva hoti, na dantajo”ti vadanti ceva likhanti ca, na panevaṃ ekantato vattabbaṃ. Kasmā? Abhidhānappadīpikāṭīkāyaṃ kakkhaḷapariyāyaṃ guṇasaddabhūtaṃ kaṭhinasaddaṃ [M 2.0091] sandhāya vuttaṃ, na sāsanavohārato nāmasaddabhūtaṃ. Tenevāha “pañcakaṃ kakkhaḷe”ti. Anekesu pana pāḷiaṭṭhakathādipotthakesu jinasāsanavohārato nāmasaddabhūto kathina-saddo dantajoyeva yebhuyyena paññāyati[V 2.0067], teneva ca kāraṇena abhidhānappadīpikāṭīkāyampi vaṇṇavipariyāye kathinantipi vuttaṃ. Atha vā kattha silāghāyanti dhātuto inapaccayaṃ katvā sasaṃyogatthakāraṃ nisaṃyogaṃ katvā sijjhati. Ayamattho silāghādisuttassa vuttiyaṃ “silāgha katthane”ti vacanato, saddanītiyañca “katthanaṃ pasaṃsana”nti vaṇṇitattā ca viññāyati. Idañca vacanaṃ “idañhi kathinavattaṃ nāma buddhappasattha”nti aṭṭhakathāvacanena (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) sameti. Ācariyā pana “kaṭhadhātu inapaccayo”ti vikappetvā “kaṭha samatthane”ti atthaṃ vadanti, taṃ ṭīkāsu (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.306; vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.306; vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306; kaṅkhā. abhi. ṭī. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “thiranti attho”ti vacanaṃ anapekkhitvā “pañcānisaṃse antokaraṇasamatthatāyā”ti hetumeva atthabhāvena gahetvā vuttaṃ siyā, taṃ pana thirabhāvassa hetuyeva.

Many learned ones, taking this very passage, say and write that the word “kathina” has only the second cerebral consonant, not a dental one. However, this should not be stated so absolutely. Why? In the Abhidhānappadīpikā-ṭīkā, the word “kaṭhina” is mentioned in reference to the synonym for hardness, as an adjective, not as a noun in the context of the Dispensation’s usage. Hence, it says, “the five on hardness.” Yet, in many Pāli texts, commentaries, and other books, the word “kathina,” as a noun in the context of the Victor's Dispensation, is predominantly found with the dental consonant. For this very reason, even in the Abhidhānappadīpikā-ṭīkā, the form “kathina” is also mentioned in the context of letter transposition. Alternatively, it is formed from the root `kattha` meaning 'to praise', by adding the suffix `ina` and by making the conjunct consonant `tth` disjoined. This meaning is to be known from the statement in the Vutti on the Silāghādisutta: “`silāgha` in the sense of `katthana` (praise),” and from the explanation in the Saddanīti: “`katthanaṃ` is `pasaṃsanaṃ` (praising).” This explanation also accords with the commentary passage: “For this is called the Kathina observance, praised by the Buddha” (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 306). However, some teachers propose the alternative analysis “the root `kaṭha` with the suffix `ina`,” explaining the meaning as “`kaṭha` in the sense of establishment.” This might have been said in the sub-commentaries (Sārattha. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 3.306; Vi. Vi. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 2.306; Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 306; Kaṅkhā. Abhi. Ṭī. Kathinasikkhāpada-vaṇṇanā) by disregarding the statement “‘firm’ is the meaning” and instead taking the reason, namely “by its capacity to contain the five benefits,” as the meaning itself. But that is merely the reason for the state of firmness.

Kathaṃ viggaho kātabboti? Ayaṃ kathina-saddo catūsu padesu nāmapadaṃ, pañcasu nāmesu suddhanāmaṃ, catūsu suddhanāmesu ruḷhīsuddhanāmaṃ, dvīsu pāṭipadikasaddesu anipphannapāṭipadikasaddo, tasmā viggaho na kātabbo. Vuttañhi –

How should the grammatical analysis be done? This word 'kathina' is a noun among the four parts of speech, a pure noun among the five kinds of nouns, a conventional pure noun among the four pure nouns, and an underived nominal stem among the two kinds of nominal stems. Therefore, a grammatical analysis should not be done. For it is said:

“Ruḷhīkhyātaṃ nipātañcu-pasaggālapanaṃ tathā;

Sabbanāmikametesu, na kato viggaho chasū”ti.

“Conventional terms, verbs, particles, prefixes, vocatives, and likewise pronouns—for these six, no grammatical analysis is made.”

Ayamattho “kathinanti…pe… thiranti attho”ti ṭīkāsu (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.306; vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.306; vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306; kaṅkhā. abhi. ṭī. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) vacanato viññāyati. Atha vā pañcānisaṃse aññattha gantuṃ [M 2.0092] adatvā kathati saṅgaṇhātīti kathinaṃ, ayaṃ vacanattho yathāvuttavinayatthamañjūsāpāṭhavasena (kaṅkhā. abhi. ṭī. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) viññāyati. Atha vā kaṭhati kicchena jīvatīti kathino, rukkho, tassa esoti kathino, thirabhāvo, so etassa atthīti kathinaṃ, paññattijātaṃ ṭha-kārassa tha-kāraṃ katvā kathinanti vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ nayo “kaṭha kicchajīvane”ti dhātvatthasaṃvaṇṇanāya ca “pañcānisaṃse antokaraṇasamatthatāya thiranti attho”ti ṭīkāvacanena (sārattha. ṭī. mahāvagga 3.306; vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.306; vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306; kaṅkhā. abhi. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) ca sametīti daṭṭhabbo. Atha vā kathīyate [V 2.0068] silāghate pasaṃsīyate buddhādīhīti kathinaṃ, ayaṃ nayo “kattha silāghāya”nti dhātvatthasaṃvaṇṇanāya ca “idañhi kathinavattaṃ nāma buddhappasattha”nti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) aṭṭhakathāvacanena ca sametīti daṭṭhabbo.

This meaning is understood from the sub-commentaries: “`Kathina`…pe… ‘firm’ is the meaning” (Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā, Mahāvagga 3.306; Vimativinodanī-ṭīkā, Mahāvagga 2.306; Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā, Mahāvagga 306; Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-abhidhamma-ṭīkā, Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā). Alternatively, because it speaks of (`kathati`) or gathers (`saṅgaṇhāti`) the five benefits, not allowing one to go elsewhere for them, it is called `kathina`. This verbal meaning is understood according to the text of the aforesaid Vinayatthamañjūsā (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-abhidhamma-ṭīkā, Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā). Or, `kaṭhati` means one lives with difficulty (`kicchena jīvati`), hence `kathino`, a tree. That which belongs to it is `kathina`, meaning firmness. Since it possesses this, it is called `kathinaṃ`. The term `kathina` is stated by changing the letter `ṭha` to `tha` in the derived designation. This interpretation is to be seen as consistent with the explanation of the root meaning “`kaṭha` in the sense of difficult living” and with the sub-commentary statement: “The meaning is ‘firm’ by its capacity to include the five benefits” (Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā, Mahāvagga 3.306; Vimativinodanī-ṭīkā, Mahāvagga 2.306; Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā, Mahāvagga 306; Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-abhidhamma-ṭīkā, Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā). Alternatively, because it is spoken of (`kathīyate`), praised (`silāghate`), and commended (`pasaṃsīyate`) by the Buddha and others, it is called `kathina`. This interpretation is to be seen as consistent with the explanation of the root meaning “`kattha` in the sense of praise” and with the commentary statement: “For this Kathina observance is indeed praised by the Buddha” (Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā 306).

Ettha pana saṅkheparucittā ācariyassa saddalakkhaṇaṃ avicāretvā atthameva pucchaṃ katvā vissajjetuṃ “kathinaṃ attharituṃ ke labhanti, ke na labhantī”tiādimāha. Tattha ke labhantīti ke sādhentīti attho. Pañca janā labhantīti pañca janā sādhenti. Kathinadussassa hi dāyakā pacchimakoṭiyā cattāro honti, eko paṭiggāhakoti. “Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ catuvaggo bhikkhusaṅgho ṭhapetvā tīṇi kammāni upasampadaṃ pavāraṇaṃ abbhāna”nti campeyyakkhandhake (mahāva. 388) vuttattā na pañcavaggakaraṇīyanti gahetabbaṃ. Paṭhamappavāraṇāya pavāritāti idaṃ vassacchedaṃ akatvā vassaṃvutthabhāvasandassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ antarāyena apavāritānampi vutthavassānaṃ kathinatthārasambhavato. Teneva “appavāritā vā”ti avatvā “chinnavassā vā pacchimikāya upagatā vā na labhantī”ti ettakameva vuttaṃ. Aññasmiṃ vihāre vutthavassāpi [M 2.0093] na labhantīti nānāsīmāya aññasmiṃ vihāre vutthavassā imasmiṃ vihāre kathinatthāraṃ na labhantīti attho. Sabbeti chinnavassādayo, anupagatāpi tattheva saṅgahitā. Ānisaṃsanti kathinānisaṃsacīvaraṃ. Ekaṃ atthatacīvaraṃyeva hi kathinacīvaraṃ nāma hoti, avasesāni cīvarāni vā sāṭakā vā kathinānisaṃsāyeva nāma. Vakkhati hi “avasesakathinānisaṃse balavavatthāni vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya dātabbānī”ti. (Vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 226) itaresanti purimikāya upagatānaṃ.

Here, however, those who prefer brevity, without investigating the definition of the term from the teacher, directly ask the question and provide the answer: “Who is entitled to spread the kathina, and who is not?” Herein, “who is entitled” means who accomplishes it. Five individuals are entitled—five accomplish it. Regarding the kathina cloth, the donors are at a minimum four, and one is the recipient. Because it is stated in the Campeyya chapter: “In this case, monks, the fourfold community of monks, excluding three acts—ordination, pavāraṇā, and rehabilitation” (Mahāvagga 388), it should not be taken as requiring a group of five to perform the act. The statement “those who have made the first pavāraṇā” is said to show that they have completed the rains-residence without breaking it, for the spreading of the kathina is possible even for those who have completed the rains-residence but did not make the pavāraṇā due to an obstacle. Therefore, instead of saying “or those who have not made pavāraṇā,” it is simply stated, “those who have broken their rains-residence or those who have undertaken it on the later occasion are not entitled.” Those who have observed the rains-residence in another monastery are also not entitled—meaning those who have observed the rains-residence in a different boundary are not eligible to spread the kathina in this monastery. By “all,” those with a broken rains-residence and so on are meant; even those who have not undertaken the rains-residence are included there. The term “benefits” refers to the kathina-benefit robe. For only one spread robe is called the kathina robe; the remaining robes or garments are simply called kathina benefits. For it will be said, “The remaining kathina benefits, durable cloths, should be given for the stability of the rains-residence dwelling.” (Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā 226). “Others” refers to those who have undertaken the rains-residence on the earlier occasion.

So ce pacchimikāya upasampajjati, gaṇapūrako ceva hoti, ānisaṃsañca labhatīti iminā sāmaṇerānaṃ vassūpagamanaṃ anuññātaṃ hoti. So hi purimikāya vassūpagatattā ānisaṃsaṃ labhati, pacchimikāya pana upasampajjitattā gaṇapūrako hotīti. Sace purimikāya upagatā kathinatthārakusalā na hontītiādinā “aṭṭhadhammakovido bhikkhu, kathinatthāramarahatī”ti vinayavinicchaye (vi. vi. 2704) āgatattā sayaṃ ce aṭṭhadhammakusalo, sayameva attharitabbaṃ. No ce, aññe aṭṭhadhammakusale pariyesitvā netabbā, evaṃ akatvā kathinaṃ attharituṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Kathinaṃ attharāpetvāti sakāritavacanena tehi bāhirato āgatattherehi sayaṃ kathinaṃ na attharitabbaṃ, sabbapubbakiccādikaṃ saṃvidahitvā te [V 2.0069] purimikāya vassūpagatā antosīmaṭṭhabhikkhūyeva attharāpetabbāti dasseti, aññathā añño kathinaṃ attharati, añño ānisaṃsaṃ labhatīti āpajjati, na panevaṃ yujjati. Vakkhati hi “ānisaṃso pana itaresaṃyeva hotī”ti. Dānañca bhuñjitvāti khādanīyabhojanīyabhūtaṃ annapānādidānaṃ bhuñjitvā. Na hi te vatthudānaṃ labhanti.

If he receives the higher ordination on the later occasion, he both completes the quorum and receives the benefits. By this, the undertaking of the rains-residence by novices is permitted. For he receives the benefits because he undertook the rains-residence on the earlier occasion, but he completes the quorum because he received the higher ordination on the later occasion. If those who undertook the rains-residence on the earlier occasion are not skilled in spreading the Kathina, and so on, as it is stated in the Vinayavinicchaya (VI.VI.2704): “A monk expert in the eight factors is worthy to spread the Kathina,” then if he himself is skilled in the eight factors, it should be spread by himself. If not, others skilled in the eight factors should be sought and brought. It is shown that without doing so, it is not proper to spread the Kathina. “Having had the Kathina spread”—by the use of the causative verb, it is shown that those elders who have come from outside should not spread the Kathina themselves; rather, after arranging all the preliminary duties, only those monks who undertook the rains-residence on the earlier occasion and are within the boundary should have it spread. Otherwise, it would result that one spreads the Kathina while another receives the benefits, and this is not fitting. For it will be said: “But the benefits belong only to the others.” And “having partaken of the offering” means having consumed the gift of food and drink, such as edibles and soft foods. For they do not receive the gift of cloth.

Kathinacīvaraṃ [M 2.0094] demāti dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti ettha “saṅghassa kathinacīvaraṃ demā”ti vattabbaṃ. Evañhi sati “idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppanna”nti (mahāva. 307) kammavācāya sameti. Atha ca pana pubbe kataparicayattā “saṅghassā”ti avuttepi sampadānaṃ pākaṭanti katvā avuttaṃ siyāti. Ettheke ācariyā vadanti “saṅghassāti avuttepi kāle dinnaṃ saṅghikaṃ hotī”ti, tatrevaṃ vattabbaṃ “na kāle dinnaṃ sabbaṃ saṅghikaṃ hotī”ti. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Yañca kālepi saṅghassa vā idaṃ akālacīvaranti, puggalassa vā idaṃ tuyhaṃ dammītiādinā nayena dinnaṃ, etaṃ akālacīvaraṃ nāmā”ti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. akālacivarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) āgatattā puggalikampi hotīti viññāyati, tasmā parammukhāpi nāmaṃ vatvā sammukhāpi pādamūle ṭhapetvā dinnaṃ puggalikameva hoti, na saṅghikaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) “puggalassa detīti ‘imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī’ti evaṃ parammukhā vā, pādamūle ṭhapetvā ‘imaṃ, bhante, tumhākaṃ dammī’ti evaṃ sammukhā vā detī”ti. Evaṃ puggalike sati taṃ cīvaraṃ saṅghassa bhājetabbaṃ hoti vā na hoti vāti? So puggalo attano saddhivihārikaantevāsikabhūtassa saṅghassa vā aññassa sahadhammikasaṅghassa vā bhājetukāmo bhājeyya, abhājetukāmo “bhājetū”ti na kenaci vacanīyo. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Na hi puggalassa ādissa dinnaṃ kenaci bhājanīyaṃ hotī”ti ṭīkāsu āgamanato viññāyati. Atheke ācariyā evaṃ vadanti “kathinassa ekaṃ mūlaṃ saṅghoti (pari. 408) vuttattā puggalaṃ uddissa dinnepi saṅghāyattaṃ saṅghikaṃ hoti. Yathā kiṃ ‘sīmāya dammi, senāsanassa dammī’ti vuttepi taṃ dānaṃ saṅghikaṃ hoti, yathā ca ‘kathinacīvaraṃ dammī’ti vutte saṅghikaṃ hotī”ti.

Regarding “We give the Kathina robe,” meaning it is proper to give, here it should be said, “We give the Kathina robe to the Sangha.” For if this is so, it accords with the formal procedure (kammavācā): “This Kathina cloth has arisen for the Sangha” (Mahāvagga 307). However, due to previous acquaintance, even if “to the Sangha” is not said, the recipient is evident, and so it might be unstated. Here, some teachers say, “Even if ‘to the Sangha’ is not stated, if given at the proper time, it becomes communal.” To this it should be said, “Not everything given at the proper time becomes communal.” How is this understood? Because it is stated in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-aṭṭhakathā, Akālacivarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā): “That which is given even at the proper time, either to the Sangha as ‘This is an out-of-season robe,’ or to an individual by the method of ‘This I give to you,’ and so on—this is called an out-of-season robe.” Thus, it is understood that it can also be personal. Therefore, what is given either in the person's absence by stating their name, or in their presence by placing it at their feet, is personal only, not communal. This is stated in the commentary (Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā 379): “One gives to an individual thus: ‘I give this robe to so-and-so,’ either in their absence, or in their presence by placing it at their feet and saying, ‘Venerable sir, I give this to you.’” When it is personal, should that robe be distributed to the Sangha or not? That individual, if wishing to distribute it, may distribute it either to the Sangha of his own co-residents and pupils, or to another Sangha of fellow practitioners of the Dhamma. If not wishing to distribute it, he should not be told by anyone, “Distribute it.” How is this understood? Because it is stated in the sub-commentaries: “For what is given designated for an individual is not to be distributed by anyone.” But some teachers say this: “Since it is said, ‘The Sangha is the one root of the Kathina’ (Parivāra 408), even if given designated for an individual, it is dependent on the Sangha and becomes communal. Just as when it is said, ‘I give to the boundary,’ or ‘I give to the lodging,’ that gift becomes communal, so too when it is said, ‘I give the Kathina robe,’ it becomes communal.”

Tatrevaṃ [M 2.0095] vicāretabbaṃ – “kathinassa ekaṃ mūlaṃ saṅgho”ti vacanaṃ (pari. 408) kathinassa mūlaṃ kathinassa kāraṇaṃ dasseti. Yathā hi mūle vijjamāne rukkho tiṭṭhati, avijjamāne na tiṭṭhati, tasmā mūlaṃ rukkhassa kāraṇaṃ hoti, patiṭṭhaṃ hoti, evaṃ saṅghe vijjamāne [V 2.0070] kathinaṃ hoti, no avijjamāne, tasmā saṅgho kathinassa mūlaṃ kathinassa kāraṇaṃ nāma hoti. Kathaṃ saṅghe vijjamāne kathinaṃ hoti? Sabbantimena paricchedena catuvaggabhūtena saṅghena atthārārahassa bhikkhuno ñattidutiyakammavācāya kathinacīvare dinneyeva tena cīvarena atthataṃ kathinaṃ nāma hoti, no adinne, tasmā catuvaggasaṅghe alabbhamāne sahassakkhattuṃ “kathinaṃ dammī”ti vuttepi kathinaṃ nāma na hoti, tasmā upacārasīmāya paricchinne vihāre eko vā dve vā tayo vā cattāro vā bhikkhū viharanti, tattha kathinacīvare uppanne aññato pariyesitvā catuvaggasaṅgho eko paṭiggāhakoti pañcannaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pūraṇe sati kathinaṃ attharituṃ labhati, nāsati, evaṃ saṅghe vijjamāneyeva kathinaṃ nāma hoti, no avijjamāne, tasmā saṅghassa kathinassa mūlabhūtataṃ kāraṇabhūtataṃ sandhāya “kathinassa ekaṃ mūlaṃ saṅgho”ti vuttaṃ. “Kathina”nti vutte saṅghikaṃyeva hoti, no puggalikanti adhippāyo etasmiṃ pāṭhe na labbhati. Yathā kiṃ “kiccādhikaraṇassa ekaṃ mūlaṃ saṅgho”ti (cūḷava. 219) ettha apalokanakammañattikammañattidutiyakammañatticatutthakammasaṅkhātaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ catuvaggādike saṅghe vijjamāneyeva hoti, no avijjamāne, tasmā saṅghassa kiccādhikaraṇassa mūlabhūtataṃ kāraṇabhūtataṃ sandhāya “kiccādhikaraṇassa ekaṃ mūlaṃ saṅgho”ti vuccati, evaṃsampadamidaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In this regard, it should be considered thus: The statement “the Sangha is the single root of the Kathina” (Pari. 408) indicates that the Sangha is the root and cause of the Kathina. Just as a tree stands when its root exists and does not stand when it is absent, so the root is the cause and support of the tree. Similarly, the Kathina exists when the Sangha is present and does not exist when it is absent. Therefore, the Sangha is called the root and cause of the Kathina. How does the Kathina exist when the Sangha is present? When a kathina robe-cloth is given to a monk worthy of spreading it by a Sangha consisting of at least four monks through an act of motion and one proclamation, only then is the Kathina said to be spread with that cloth; not if it is not given. Therefore, if a Sangha of four monks is not obtainable, even if one says a thousand times, 'I give the Kathina,' it does not become a Kathina. Therefore, in a monastery delimited by a conventional boundary where one, two, three, or four monks reside, if kathina robe-cloth arises there and a Sangha of four is sought from elsewhere, with one monk as the recipient, and when the full complement of five monks is complete, it is possible to spread the Kathina; if not, it is not possible. Thus, the Kathina exists only when the Sangha is present, not when it is absent. Therefore, the statement “the Sangha is the single root of the Kathina” refers to the Sangha being the root and cause of the Kathina. When “Kathina” is mentioned, it pertains only to the Sangha, not to an individual—this meaning is not found in this passage. Just as it is said, “the Sangha is the single root of the kiccādhikaraṇa” (Cūḷav. 219), here the kiccādhikaraṇa—which consists of the act of declaration, the act of motion, the act of motion with one proclamation, and the act of motion with three proclamations—exists only when a Sangha of four or more monks is present, not when it is absent. Therefore, the statement “the Sangha is the single root of the kiccādhikaraṇa” refers to the Sangha being the root and cause of the kiccādhikaraṇa. This should be understood in the same way.

Yadipi [M 2.0096] vuttaṃ “yathā ‘sīmāya dammi, senāsanassa dammī’tiādīsu taṃ dānaṃ saṅghāyattameva hoti, tathā ‘kathina dammī’ti vutte puggalaṃ uddissa dinnepi saṅghāyattameva saṅghikameva hotī”ti, tathāpi evaṃ vicāraṇā kātabbā – “sīmāya dammi, senāsanassa dammī”tiādīsu sīmā ca senāsanañca dānapaṭiggāhakā na honti, tasmā sīmaṭṭhassa ca senāsanaṭṭhassa ca saṅghassa āyattaṃ hoti, puggalo pana dānapaṭiggāhakova, tasmā “imaṃ kathinacīvaraṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dammī”ti parammukhā vā tassa bhikkhuno pādamūle ṭhapetvā sammukhā vā dinnaṃ kathaṃ saṅghāyattaṃ saṅghasantakaṃ bhaveyya, evaṃ saṅghassa apariṇataṃ puggalikacīvaraṃ saṅghassa pariṇāmeyya, navasu adhammikadānesu ekaṃ bhaveyya, tassa cīvarassa paṭiggahopi navasu adhammikapaṭiggahesu eko bhaveyya, tassa cīvarassa paribhogopi navasu adhammikaparibhogesu eko bhaveyya. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? Nava adhammikāni dānānīti saṅghassa pariṇataṃ aññasaṅghassa vā cetiyassa vā puggalassa vā pariṇāmeti, cetiyassa pariṇataṃ aññacetiyassa vā saṅghassa vā puggalassa vā pariṇāmeti, puggalassa pariṇataṃ aññapuggalassa [V 2.0071] vā saṅghassa vā cetiyassa vā pariṇāmeti, “nava adhammikā paribhogā”ti āgataṃ parivārapāḷiñca (pari. 329) “nava paṭiggahaparibhogāti etesaṃyeva dānānaṃ paṭiggahā ca paribhogā cā”ti āgataṃ aṭṭhakathañca (pari. aṭṭha. 329) oloketvā viññāyatīti.

Although it is said, "Just as in cases like 'I give to the boundary,' 'I give to the dwelling,' that gift is solely dependent on the Sangha, so too when it is said, 'I give the kathina,' even if given intending an individual, it is solely dependent on the Sangha and belongs to the Sangha," nevertheless, the following consideration should be made: In cases like "I give to the boundary," "I give to the dwelling," the boundary and the dwelling are not the receivers of the gift. Therefore, it is dependent on the Sangha associated with the boundary and the Sangha associated with the dwelling. However, an individual is indeed the receiver of the gift. Thus, if one says, "I give this kathina robe to the monk named so-and-so," and gives it either in his absence, or by placing it at his feet in his presence, how could it be dependent on the Sangha or belong to the Sangha? In this way, a personal robe not yet designated for the Sangha would be designated for the Sangha. This would become one of the nine improper gifts. The acceptance of that robe would become one of the nine improper acceptances, and the use of that robe would become one of the nine improper uses. How is this understood? The nine improper gifts are: designating for another Sangha, or a shrine, or an individual what has been designated for the Sangha; designating for another shrine, or the Sangha, or an individual what has been designated for a shrine; designating for another individual, or the Sangha, or a shrine what has been designated for an individual. The "nine improper uses" are mentioned in the Parivāra Pāḷi (Pari. 329), and the commentary (Pari. Aṭṭha. 329) states, "The nine improper acceptances and uses are the acceptances and uses of these very gifts." By examining these, it is understood.

Athāpi evaṃ vadanti – dāyako saṅghattherassa vā ganthadhutaṅgavasena abhiññātassa vā bhattuddesakassa vā pahiṇati “amhākaṃ bhattaggahaṇatthāya aṭṭha bhikkhū gahetvā āgacchathā”ti, sacepi ñātiupaṭṭhākehi pesitaṃ [M 2.0097] hoti, ime tayo janā pucchituṃ na labhanti. Āruḷhāyeva mātikaṃ, saṅghato aṭṭha bhikkhū uddisāpetvā attanavamehi gantabbaṃ. Kasmā? Bhikkhusaṅghassa hi ete bhikkhū nissāya lābho uppajjatīti. Ganthadhutaṅgādīhi pana anabhiññāto āvāsikabhikkhu pucchituṃ labhati, tasmā tena “kiṃ saṅghato gaṇhāmi, udāhu ye jānāmi, tehi saddhiṃ āgacchāmī”ti mātikaṃ āropetvā yathā dāyakā vadanti, tathā paṭipajjitabbanti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 325), īdisesu ṭhānesu “saṅghassa lābho puggalaṃ upanissāya uppajjatī”ti vacanaṃ upanidhāya “saṅghassa lābho puggalaṃ nissāya uppajjati, puggalassa pattalābho saṅghaṃ āmasitvā dento saṅghāyatto hotī”ti viññāyatīti.

Furthermore, they say this—the donor sends word to the elder of the Sangha, or one well-known for his textual scholarship and ascetic practice, or to the meal distributor: "Take eight monks and come for our meal offering." Even if it is sent by relatives or attendants, these three individuals cannot be questioned. The procedure is already established: having the Sangha designate eight monks, one should go with them, making oneself the ninth. Why? For indeed, gain arises for the community of monks in dependence on these monks. However, a resident monk not well-known for textual scholarship and ascetic practice can be questioned. Therefore, having raised the matter, he should consider: "Shall I take from the Sangha, or shall I go with those I know?" and act as the donors instruct (Cūḷava. Aṭṭha. 325). In such cases, bearing in mind the statement, "The gain for the Sangha arises in dependence on an individual," it is understood: "The gain for the Sangha arises in dependence on an individual, and when an individual receives a gain and gives it after referring it to the Sangha, it becomes dependent on the Sangha."

Imasmimpi vacane evaṃ vicāraṇā kātabbā – tasmiṃ tu nimantane na puggalaṃyeva nimanteti, atha kho sasaṅghaṃ puggalaṃ nimanteti. Tattha tu “saṅgha”nti avatvā “aṭṭha bhikkhū”ti vuttattā “kiṃ saṅghato gaṇhāmi, udāhu ye jānāmi, tehi saddhiṃ āgacchāmī”ti anabhiññāto puggalo pucchituṃ labhati. Saṅghattherassa pana saṅghaṃ pariharitvā vasitattā “aṭṭha bhikkhū”ti vutte saṅghaṃ ṭhapetvā aññesaṃ gahaṇakāraṇaṃ natthi, ganthadhutaṅgavasena abhiññātapuggalopi saṅghassa puññanissitattā “aṭṭha bhikkhū”ti vutte saṅghatoyeva gaṇhāti, bhattuddesakassapi devasikaṃ saṅghasseva bhattavicāraṇattā “aṭṭha bhikkhū”ti vutte saṅghaṃ ṭhapetvā aññesaṃ gahaṇakāraṇaṃ natthi. Evaṃ “aṭṭha bhikkhū gahetvā āgacchathā”ti saha saṅghena nimantitattā “ime tayo janā pucchituṃ na labhantī”ti vuttaṃ, na “tvaṃ āgacchāhī”ti puggalasseva nimantane satipi saṅghaṃ [M 2.0098] gahetvā āgantabbatoti. Evaṃ “aṭṭha bhikkhū gahetvā āgacchathā”ti sasaṅghasseva puggalassa nimantitattā saṅgho gahetabbo hoti, na “tumhe āgacchathā”ti puggalasseva nimantitattā, tasmā “puggalassa lābho saṅghāyatto”ti na sakkā vattuṃ[V 2.0072], aṭṭhakathādīsu pakaraṇesupi “puggalaṃ nissāya saṅghassa lābho uppajjati” icceva vutto, na “puggalassa lābho saṅghāyatto”ti. Cīvaralābhakhettabhūtāsu aṭṭhasu mātikāsu ca “saṅghassa detī”ti ca visuṃ, “puggalassa detī”ti ca visuṃ āgataṃ. Puggalassa detīti “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti evaṃ parammukhā vā, pādamūle ṭhapetvā “imaṃ bhante tumhākaṃ dammī”ti evaṃ sammukhā vā detīti.

In this statement too, such a consideration should be made: in that invitation, it is not merely an individual who is invited, but rather an individual along with the Sangha. Here, however, since 'eight bhikkhus' is stated without saying 'Sangha,' an unacquainted individual may ask, 'Shall I take from the Sangha, or shall I come with those I know?' For the elder of the Sangha, however, because he lives upholding the Sangha, when 'eight bhikkhus' is stated, there is no reason to take others apart from the Sangha. Even a person well-known for his textual scholarship and ascetic practice, because he is dependent on the merit of the Sangha, when 'eight bhikkhus' is stated, takes them from the Sangha itself. Similarly, for the meal distributor, because of his daily arrangement of meals for the Sangha, when 'eight bhikkhus' is stated, there is no reason to take others apart from the Sangha. Thus, because the invitation is made to the individual together with the Sangha by saying, 'Come bringing eight bhikkhus,' it is said that 'these three persons do not get to ask.' This does not mean that even when an individual is invited with the words, 'You come,' he should come bringing the Sangha. In this way, when it is said, 'Come bringing eight bhikkhus,' the invitation is made to the individual along with the Sangha, and thus the Sangha is to be included, not when an invitation is made solely to an individual, saying 'You all come.' Therefore, it cannot be said that 'an individual’s gain is dependent on the Sangha.' In the commentaries and other treatises, it is only stated that 'the Sangha’s gain arises in dependence on an individual,' not that 'an individual’s gain is dependent on the Sangha.' And in the eight lists that are the fields for the gain of robes, it is stated separately, 'one gives to the Sangha,' and separately, 'one gives to an individual.' Giving to an individual is when one says, 'I give this robe to so-and-so,' either in his absence, or by placing it at his feet and saying, 'Venerable sir, I give this to you,' in his presence.

Idāni pana cīvaraṃ dātukāmā upāsakā vā upāsikāyo vā sayaṃ anāgantvā puttadāsādayo āṇāpentāpi “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa therassa dethā”ti vatvā puggalasseva dāpenti, sāmaṃ gantvā dadantāpi pādamūle ṭhapetvā vā hatthe ṭhapetvā vā hatthena phusāpetvā vā dadanti “imaṃ, bhante, cīvaraṃ tumhe uddissa ettakaṃ dhanaṃ pariccajitvā kataṃ, evañca evañca hatthakammaṃ katvā sampāditaṃ, tasmā tumhe nivāsatha pārupatha paribhuñjathā”tiādīni vadanti, tassa puggalassa paribhogakaraṇameva icchanti, na saṅghassa dānaṃ. Keci atuṭṭhakathampi kathenti. Evaṃ puggalameva uddissa dinnacīvarassa saṅghena āyattakāraṇaṃ natthi. “Sace pana ‘idaṃ tumhākañca tumhākaṃ antevāsikānañca dammī’ti evaṃ vadati, therassa ca antevāsikānañca pāpuṇātī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) āgamanato evaṃ vatvā dente pana ācariyantevāsikānaṃ pāpuṇāti, anantevāsikassa pana na pāpuṇāti. “Uddesaṃ gahetuṃ āgato gahetvā gacchanto ca atthi, tassapi pāpuṇātī”ti āgamanato [M 2.0099] bahisīmaṭṭhassa dhammantevāsikassapi pāpuṇāti. “Tumhehi saddhiṃ nibaddhacārikabhikkhūnaṃ dammīti vutte uddesantevāsikānaṃ vattaṃ katvā uddesaparipucchādīni gahetvā vicarantānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) āgamanato evaṃ vatvā dente dhammantevāsikānaṃ vattapaṭipattikārakānañca antevāsikānaṃ pāpuṇāti. Evaṃ dāyakānaṃ vacanānurūpameva dānassa pavattanato “yathā dāyakā vadanti, tathā paṭipajjitabba”nti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 325) aṭṭhakathācariyā vadanti.

Now, however, when laymen or laywomen wish to give robes, if they do not come themselves but send their sons, servants, or others, instructing them, 'Give this robe to such-and-such an elder,' they cause it to be given to that individual. Even when they come themselves to give it, they place it at his feet, place it in his hands, or have him touch it with his hand, and give it, saying, 'Venerable sir, this robe was made for you by spending such-and-such wealth, and it was produced by doing such-and-such handiwork. Therefore, wear it as a lower garment, wear it as an upper garment, and make use of it,' and so on. They intend for that individual to use it, not for it to be a gift to the Sangha. Some even speak words of discontent. Thus, for a robe given designated for an individual, there is no reason for it to be under the authority of the Sangha. From the textual tradition, 'If, however, one says, "I give this to you and your resident pupils," then it reaches the elder and his resident pupils' (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379). When it is given with such words, it reaches the teacher's resident pupils, but it does not reach one who is not a resident pupil. From the textual tradition, 'If one comes to receive an instruction, takes it, and departs, it also reaches him,' it also reaches a Dhamma pupil who is outside the boundary. From the textual tradition, 'When it is said, "I give this to the bhikkhus who regularly travel with you," it reaches all those who, having performed the duties of a pupil receiving instruction, wander about receiving instructions, asking questions, and so on' (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379). When it is given with such words, it reaches the Dhamma pupils and the resident pupils who perform their duties and practices. Since the gift proceeds according to the donors' words, the commentary teachers say, 'One should act in accordance with what the donors say' (Cūḷava. Aṭṭha. 325).

Evaṃ idāni dāyakā yebhuyyena puggalasseva denti, satesu sahassesu ekoyeva paṇḍito bahussuto dāyako saṅghassa dadeyya, puggalikacīvarañca saṅghikabhavanatthāya akariyamānaṃ na ñattiyā kammavācāya ca arahaṃ hoti. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? Ñattikammavācāvirodhato. Kathaṃ virodhoti ce? Ñattiyā kammavācāya ca “idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppanna”nti kathinacīvarassa [V 2.0073] saṅghikabhāvo vutto, idāni pana taṃ cīvaraṃ “puggalassa dinnaṃ puggalika”nti vacanatthānurūpato puggalikaṃ hoti, evampi virodho. “Saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dadeyya kathinaṃ attharitu”nti ettha ca saṅghoti dhātuyā kattā hoti, bhikkhunoti sampadānaṃ, idha pana saṅghassa tasmiṃ kathinacīvare anissarabhāvato saṅgho kattā na hoti, bhikkhu paṭiggāhalakkhaṇābhāvato sampadānaṃ na hoti, evampi virodho. Dāyakena pana saṅghassa pariccattattā saṅghikabhūtaṃ kathinacīvaraṃ yasmiṃ kāle saṅgho kathinaṃ attharituṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatassa bhikkhuno deti, tasmiṃ kāle ñattidutiyakammavācaṃ idāni manussā “ñattī”ti voharanti, tañca cīvaraṃ “ñattiladdhacīvara”nti, taṃ cīvaradāyakañca “ñattiladdhadāyako”ti[M 2.0100], tasmā saṅghikacīvarameva ñattiladdhaṃ hoti, no puggalikacīvaraṃ. Ñattiladdhakālato pana paṭṭhāya taṃ cīvaraṃ puggalikaṃ hoti. Kasmā? Atthārakapuggalassa cīvarabhāvatoti.

Thus, nowadays donors mostly give to individuals. Among hundreds or thousands, only one wise and learned donor might give to the Sangha. And a personal robe, not being made for the purpose of becoming communal, is not fit for a motion and formal act. If it is asked, 'How is this known?' From the contradiction with the motion and formal act. If it is asked, 'How is there a contradiction?' In the motion and formal act, the communal nature of the Kaṭhina robe is stated: 'This Kaṭhina cloth has arisen for the Sangha.' But now, that robe is personal according to the meaning of the words, 'given to an individual, it is personal.' Thus there is a contradiction. And in the phrase, 'May the Sangha give this Kaṭhina cloth to a bhikkhu of such-and-such a name to spread the Kaṭhina,' 'the Sangha' is the agent of the verb, and 'the bhikkhu' is the recipient. Here, however, since the Sangha has no authority over that Kaṭhina robe, the Sangha is not the agent, and since the bhikkhu does not have the characteristic of a recipient, he is not the recipient. Thus there is also a contradiction. However, when a Kaṭhina robe that has become communal, having been relinquished to the Sangha by the donor, is given by the Sangha to a bhikkhu endowed with the eight qualities to spread the Kaṭhina, at that time people nowadays refer to the formal act preceded by a motion as simply 'the motion' (ñatti). And they call that robe 'the robe obtained by motion' and the donor of that robe 'the donor of the robe obtained by motion.' Therefore, only a communal robe is obtained by motion, not a personal robe. From the time it is obtained by motion, however, that robe becomes personal. Why? Because it becomes the robe of the individual who spreads it.

Athāpi vadanti “dinnanti pāṭhañca ‘sādhentī’ti pāṭhañca ‘ānisaṃsaṃ labhantī’ti pāṭhañca upanidhāya ayamattho viññāyatī”ti, tatthāyamācariyānamadhippāyo – “dinnaṃ idaṃ saṅghenā”ti ettha dā-dhātuyā saṅghenāti kattā, idanti kammaṃ, imassa kathinacīvarassa saṅghikattā saṅghena dinnaṃ hoti, tena viññāyati “kathina”nti vutte saṅghikaṃ hotīti. “Kathinatthāraṃ ke labhantīti ettha ke labhantīti ke sādhentīti attho. Pañca janā sādhentī”ti vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306) vuttaṃ. Tattha pañca janāti saṅgho vutto, imināpi viññāyati “kathinanti vutte saṅghikaṃ hotī”ti. Ānisaṃsaṃ labhantīti ettha ca saṅghikattā sabbe sīmaṭṭhakabhikkhū ānisaṃsaṃ labhanti, imināpi viññāyati “kathinanti vutte saṅghikaṃ hotī”ti.

Furthermore, they say that this meaning is understood by relying on the textual passages 'given,' 'they accomplish,' and 'they obtain the benefits.' Herein, this is the intention of the teachers: in the phrase 'This has been given by the Sangha,' with the verbal root 'dā' (to give), 'by the Sangha' is the agent, and 'this' is the object. Because this Kaṭhina cloth is communal, it has been given by the Sangha. From this it is understood that when 'Kaṭhina' is mentioned, it is communal. In the question, 'Who obtains the spreading of the Kaṭhina?' 'who obtains' means 'who accomplishes.' It is said in the Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā: 'Five persons accomplish it' (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 306). There, by 'five persons,' the Sangha is meant. From this too, it is understood that when 'Kaṭhina' is mentioned, it is communal. And in the phrase 'they obtain the benefits,' because it is communal, all the bhikkhus within the boundary obtain the benefits. From this too, it is understood that when 'Kaṭhina' is mentioned, it is communal.

Tatrāpyevaṃ vicāraṇā kātabbā – pubbedāyakā cattāropi paccaye yebhuyyena saṅghasseva denti, tasmā saṅghassa catupaccayabhājanakathā ativitthārā hoti. Appakato pana puggalassa denti, tasmā saṅghassa dinnaṃ kathinacīvaraṃ saṅghena atthārakassa puggalassa dinnaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sādhentīti ca kathinadussassa dāyakā cattāro, paṭiggāhako ekoti pañca janā kathinadānakammaṃ sādhentīti vuttaṃ. Ānisaṃsaṃ labhantīti idañca atthārakassa ca anumodanānañca bhikkhūnaṃ ānisaṃsalābhameva vuttaṃ, na etehi pāṭhehi “kathina”nti vutte saṅghikaṃ hotīti attho viññātabbo hotīti daṭṭhabbo. Saṅghassa uppannacīvaraṃ saṅghena atthārakassa [V 2.0074] dinnabhāvo kathaṃ viññāyatīti? “Idaṃ [M 2.0101] saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno deti kathinaṃ attharitu”nti vuttaṃ pāḷipāṭhañca (mahāva. 307) “saṅgho ajja kathinadussaṃ labhitvā punadivase deti, ayaṃ nicayasannidhī”ti vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāpāṭhañca disvā viññāyatīti. Saṅghasantakabhūtaṃ cīvarameva dānakiriyāya kammaṃ, saṅgho kattā, puggalo sampadānaṃ bhavituṃ arahabhāvo ca yathāvuttapāḷipāṭhameva upanidhāya viññāyatīti.

Here too, this consideration should be made: Donors in the past, for the most part, gave the four requisites to the Sangha. Therefore, the discussion on the Sangha being the recipient of the four requisites is extensive. But they gave little to an individual. Hence, the Kathina robe given to the Sangha is spoken of in reference to it being given by the Sangha to an individual who is the spreader. And as for 'they accomplish,' it is said that the donors of the Kathina cloth are four and the recipient is one—thus, five persons accomplish the act of the Kathina donation. 'They obtain the benefit'—this refers to the obtaining of the benefit by both the spreader and the monks who rejoice. It should be seen that from these passages, it should not be understood that when 'Kathina' is said, the meaning is that it is communal. How is it understood that the robe cloth that has arisen for the Sangha is given by the Sangha to the spreader? It is understood by seeing the Pāli passage: 'This Kathina cloth has arisen for the Sangha. The Sangha gives this Kathina cloth to the monk named so-and-so to spread the Kathina,' and the commentary passage: 'The Sangha, having received the Kathina cloth today, gives it on the next day—this is hoarding and storing.' The robe that has become the property of the Sangha is the object of the act of giving; the Sangha is the agent, and the fitness of the individual to be the recipient is to be understood by relying on the aforementioned Pāli passage.

Evaṃ sante puggalassa dinnaṃ puggalikacīvaraṃ saṅghikaṃ kātuṃ kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti? Sace so paṭiggāhakapuggalo dāyakānaṃ evaṃ vadati “upāsaka dānaṃ nāma puggalassa dinnato saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphalataraṃ hoti, tasmā saṅghassa dehi, saṅghassa datvā puna saṅghena atthārārahassa bhikkhuno kammavācāya datvā tena puggalena yathāvinayaṃ atthateyeva kathinaṃ nāma hoti, na puggalassa datvā puggalena sāmaṃyeva atthate, tasmā saṅghassa dehī”ti uyyojetvā saṅghassa dāpitepi taṃ cīvaraṃ saṅghikaṃ hoti kathinatthārārahaṃ. Yadi pana dāyako appassutatāya “nāhaṃ, bhante, kiñci jānāmi, imaṃ cīvaraṃ tumhākameva dammī”ti vakkhati, evaṃ sati puggalikavaseneva sampaṭicchitvā tena puggalena taṃ cīvaraṃ saṅghassa dinnampi saṅghikaṃ hoti.

This being so, how should one proceed to make a personal robe given to an individual into communal property? If the recipient individual says to the donors: 'Lay devotee, an offering given to the Sangha is of greater fruit than one given to an individual. Therefore, give it to the Sangha. After it is given to the Sangha, and then given by the Sangha through a formal act to a monk worthy of spreading the Kathina, only when it is spread by that individual according to the Vinaya does it become what is called “Kathina”—not when it is given to an individual and spread by that individual himself. Therefore, give it to the Sangha.' Even when, having been urged, it is caused to be given to the Sangha, that robe becomes communal property and suitable for spreading the Kathina. If, however, the donor, due to lack of learning, says: 'Venerable sir, I do not know anything; I give this robe only to you,' then, having accepted it as a personal possession, even when that robe is given by that individual to the Sangha, it becomes communal property.

Yadi evaṃ samaṇeneva samaṇassa dinnaṃ cīvaraṃ kathaṃ kathinatthārārahaṃ bhaveyyāti? No na bhaveyya. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) “kathinaṃ kena dinnaṃ vaṭṭati? Yena kenaci devena vā manussena vā pañcannaṃ vā sahadhammikānaṃ aññatarena dinnaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. Atha kasmā paramparabhūtehi ācariyehi ñattiladdhacīvarato avasesāni cīvarāni saṅghassa bhājetvā eva paribhuñjitānīti? Vuccate – ekacce bhikkhū ācariyaparamparāgataanausāreneva [M 2.0102] paṭipajjanti, keci bahūnaṃ kiriyaṃ disvā diṭṭhānugativasena paṭipajjanti, bahussutāpi keci therā aruccantāpi paveṇibhedabhayena paṭipajjanti, apare rucivasena atthañca adhippāyañca pariṇāmetvā gaṇhanti, pakaraṇamevānugatabhikkhū pana yathāpakaraṇāgatameva atthaṃ gahetvā saṅghikañca puggalikañca amissaṃ katvā, kālacīvarañca akālacīvarañca amissaṃ katvā gaṇhanti. Bhikkhunivibhaṅge (pāci. 738) “thūlanandā bhikkhunī akālacīvaraṃ ‘kālacīvara’nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpessati, atha bhagavā nissaggiyapācittiyāpattiṃ paññapesī”ti āgataṃ, tasmā lajjīpesalabahussutasikkhākāmabhūtena bhikkhunā aneka-pāḷiaṭṭhakathādayo [V 2.0075] pakaraṇe oloketvā saṃsanditvā pakaraṇamevānugantabbaṃ, na aññesaṃ kiriyaṃ saddahitabbaṃ, na ca anugantabbaṃ. Bhagavato hi dharamānakāle vā tato pacchā vā pubbe dāyakā yebhuyyena cattāro paccaye saṅghasseva denti, tasmā saṅghikasenāsanassa saṅghikacīvarassa ca bāhullato pubbācariyā saṅghassa bhājetvā eva paribhuñjiṃsu.

If so, how could a robe given by one ascetic to another ascetic be suitable for spreading the Kathina? It is not that it would not be suitable. For it is stated in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 306): 'Given by whom is a Kathina robe valid? It is valid when given by anyone—a deva or a human, or by any one of the five fellow practitioners.' Then why did the teachers in succession distribute to the Sangha the robes remaining after the one obtained by formal motion, and only then use them? It is said: some monks act only according to the tradition handed down by their teachers; some, seeing the actions of many, act by following what they have seen; some learned elders, even if they disapprove, act out of fear of breaking the tradition; others, according to their preference, adapt and grasp the meaning and intention. Monks who follow the treatises, however, take the meaning just as it comes in the treatises, keeping what is communal and what is personal unmixed, and keeping timely robes and untimely robes unmixed. In the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga (Pāci. 738), it is said: 'The bhikkhunī Thūlanandā, having determined an untimely robe to be a “timely robe,” will have it distributed. Thereupon, the Blessed One laid down an offense of forfeiture with confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).' Therefore, a monk who is conscientious, amiable, learned, and desirous of training should examine and compare the many Pāli texts, commentaries, and so on in the treatises and follow the treatises alone. The actions of others should not be trusted, nor should they be followed. For during the Blessed One’s lifetime or afterward, donors for the most part gave the four requisites to the Sangha. Hence, the ancient teachers, due to the abundance of communal lodgings and communal robes, distributed them to the Sangha and only then used them.

Idāni pana dāyakā yebhuyyena cattāro paccaye puggalasseva denti, tasmā senāsanampi abhinavabhūtaṃ puggalikameva bahulaṃ hoti, cīvarampi puggalikameva bahulaṃ. Daliddāpi suttakantanakālato paṭṭhāya “imaṃ cīvaraṃ kathinakāle itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dassāmī”ti cintetvā ca tatheva vatvā ca sabbakiccāni karonti, mahaddhanā ca sāṭakassa kīṇitakālato paṭṭhāya tatheva cintetvā kathetvā karonti, dānakāle ca “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dehī”ti puttadāsādayo vā pesenti, sāmaṃ vā gantvā cīvaraṃ tassa bhikkhussa pādamūle vā hatthe vā ṭhapetvā “imaṃ cīvaraṃ tuyhaṃ [M 2.0103] dammī”ti vatvā vā cintetvā vā denti, satesu vā sahassesu vā eko paṇḍitapuriso “puggalassa dinnadānato saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti ñatvā “imaṃ kathinacīvaraṃ saṅghassa dammī”ti vatvā vā cintetvā vā deti, tassa sā dakkhiṇā saṅghagatā hoti. Sace pana dāyako puggalassa dātukāmo hoti, puggalo pana tassa mahapphalabhāvamicchanto dakkhiṇā-vibhaṅgasuttādidhammadesanāya (ma. ni. 3.376 ādayo) puggalikadānato saṅghikadānassa mahapphalabhāvaṃ jānāpetvā “imaṃ tava cīvaraṃ saṅghassa dehī”ti uyyojeti, dāyakopi tassa vacanaṃ sampaṭicchitvā “imaṃ kathinacīvaraṃ saṅghassa dammī”ti vatvā vā cintetvā vā deti, evampi sā dakkhiṇā saṅghagatā hoti.

But nowadays, donors for the most part give the four requisites to individuals. Therefore, newly acquired lodgings are mostly personal property, and robes are also mostly personal property. Even the poor, from the time of spinning the thread, think, 'I will give this robe to such-and-such a monk at the Kathina time,' and having spoken thus, they perform all the necessary tasks. The wealthy, too, from the time of buying the cloth, think and speak in the same way and perform the tasks. At the time of giving, they either send their children, servants, and so on, saying, 'Give this robe to such-and-such a monk,' or they go themselves and, placing the robe at that monk’s feet or in his hands, give it, saying or thinking, 'I give this robe to you.' Among hundreds or thousands, one wise person, knowing that 'a gift given to the Sangha is of greater fruit than one given to an individual,' gives, saying or thinking, 'I give this Kathina robe to the Sangha,' and that offering thus goes to the Sangha.
