If, however, a donor wishes to give to an individual, but that individual, desiring a state of great fruit for the donor, makes known through a Dhamma discourse, such as the Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅga Sutta (Majjhima Nikāya 3.376, etc.), that a gift to the Sangha is of greater fruit than a gift to an individual, and urges, 'Give this robe of yours to the Sangha,' and the donor accepts his words and gives, saying or thinking, 'I give this Kathina robe to the Sangha,' in that case too, the offering goes to the Sangha.

Yadi pana bhikkhunā uyyojitopi duppañño dāyako tassa vacanaṃ anādiyitvā puggalasseva deti, tassa sā dakkhiṇā puggalagatā hoti. Atha pana so puggalo sayaṃ sampaṭicchitvā puna saṅghassa pariccajati, evampi taṃ cīvaraṃ saṅghikaṃ hoti, taṃ saṅghikavasena bhājetabbaṃ. Yadi pana dāyakopi puggalasseva deti, puggalopi sampaṭicchitvā na pariccajati, evaṃ sante taṃ cīvaraṃ puggalikaṃ hoti, na kathinakālamattena vā kathinavacanamattena vā saṅghikaṃ hoti. Idāni pana iminā nayena puggalikacīvaraṃyeva bahulaṃ hoti. Evaṃ santepi ācariyaparamparā paveṇiṃ abhinditukāmā saṅghikaṃ viya katvā bhājetvā paribhuñjiṃsu[V 2.0076]. Yadi mukhyato saṅghikaṃ siyā, saṅghena dinnato paraṃ ekasūcimattampi puggalo adhikaṃ gaṇhituṃ na labheyya.

If, however, even when urged by a monk, an unwise donor disregards his words and gives to an individual, that offering belongs to the individual. But if that individual, having received it himself, then relinquishes it to the Sangha, in that case, that robe becomes Sangha property and should be distributed as such. However, if the donor gives to an individual, and the individual, having accepted it, does not relinquish it, then that robe is personal property. It does not become Sangha property merely by virtue of the Kathina season or the mention of the word 'Kathina'. Nowadays, according to this principle, robes are mostly personal property. Even so, wishing not to break the lineage-tradition of their teachers, they have distributed and used them as if they were Sangha property. If it were primarily Sangha property, after it has been given by the Sangha, an individual would not be able to take even so much as a needle extra.

Ekacce therā saṅghikanti pana vadanti, bhājanakāle pana issaravatāya yathāruci vicārenti, ekacce bhikkhū mukhyasaṅghikanti [M 2.0104] maññamānā abhājetukāmampi puggalaṃ abhibhavitvā bhājāpenti, tassa puggalassa mātā pitā ñātakā upāsakādayo “amhākaṃ puttassa dema, amhākaṃ ñātakabhikkhussa dema, amhākaṃ kulūpakassa demā”ti, aññepi saddhā pasannā dāyakā “itthannāmassa puggalassa demā”ti vicāretvā parammukhāpi “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti vatvā sammukhāpi pādamūle vā hatthe vā ṭhapetvā denti, evarūpaṃ cīvaraṃ puggalikaṃ hoti, saṅghaṃ āmasitvā avuttattā saṅghāyattaṃ na hoti, “kathinaṃ dassāmī”ti vā “kathinaṃ dātuṃ gato”ti vā “kathinacīvara”nti vā pubbāparakālesu vacanaṃ pana mukhyakathinabhūtassa saṅghikacīvarassa kāle dinnattā tadupacārato vohāramattaṃ hoti. Yathā kiṃ? “Uposathika”nti vuttaṃ bhattaṃ cuddasasu saṅghikabhattesu antogadhaṃ mukhyasaṅghikaṃ hoti, samādinnauposathā dāyakā sāyaṃ bhuñjitabbabhattabhāgaṃ saṅghassa denti, taṃ saṅgho salākabhattaṃ viya ṭhitikaṃ katvā bhuñjati, iti saṅghassa dinnattā saṅghikaṃ hoti. Idāni pana dāyakā attano attano kulūpakassa vā ñātibhikkhussa vā uposathadivasesu bhattaṃ denti, taṃ saṅghassa adinnattā saṅghikaṃ na hoti. Evaṃ santepi uposathadivase dinnattā mukhyavasena pavattauposathabhattaṃ viya tadupacārena “uposathabhatta”nti voharīyati, evaṃsampadamidaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Some elders, however, say it is Sangha property, but at the time of distribution, they act with authority and decide as they please. Some monks, thinking it is primarily Sangha property, overpower even an individual who is unwilling to distribute and compel him to do so. The mother, father, relatives, lay devotees, and so on of that individual say, 'We give to our son,' 'We give to our relative monk,' 'We give to the monk who attends on our family.' Other faithful and devoted donors also, having decided, 'We give to such-and-such an individual,' say, even in his absence, 'I give this robe to so-and-so,' or they give it directly, placing it at his feet or in his hands. A robe of this kind is personal property. Because it is given without addressing the Sangha, it is not under the Sangha's authority. As for statements made before or after, such as 'I will give a kathina,' 'I went to give a kathina,' or 'a kathina robe,' these are merely conventional expressions by way of figurative speech, because they are given at the time of the primary Kathina robe, which is Sangha property. How so? A meal called an 'Uposatha meal' is included among the fourteen types of Sangha meals and is primarily Sangha property. Donors who have undertaken the Uposatha give the portion of the meal that would be eaten in the evening to the Sangha. The Sangha, having established a rule for it as for a meal distributed by ticket, partakes of it. Thus, because it is given to the Sangha, it is Sangha property. Nowadays, however, donors give meals on Uposatha days to their own family's attendant monk or to a relative monk. Since it is not given to the Sangha, it is not Sangha property. Even so, because it is given on an Uposatha day, it is conventionally called an 'Uposatha meal' by way of figurative speech, like the primary Uposatha meal that is established as such. This should be understood in this very way.

Evaṃ imasmiṃ kāle yebhuyyena puggalasseva dinnattā puggalikabhūtaṃ cīvaraṃ ñattikammavācārahaṃ na hoti, saṅghikameva ñattikammavācārahaṃ hoti, tadeva ca pañcānisaṃsakāraṇaṃ hoti, tasmā paṇḍitena puggalena “upāsakā saṅghe detha, saṅghe dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ hotī”tiādinā niyojetvā dāpetabbaṃ, sayaṃ vā sampaṭicchitvā saṅghassa pariccajitabbaṃ. Evaṃ pariccajitattā saṅghikabhūtaṃ cīvaraṃ ñattikammavācārahañca [M 2.0105] hoti pañcānisaṃsanipphādakañca. Evaṃ niyojanañca “saṅghe gotami dehi, saṅghe te dinne ahañceva pūjito bhavissāmi saṅgho cā”ti (ma. ni. 3.376) bhagavatā vuttavacanaṃ anugataṃ hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Thus, at this time, since for the most part it is given to an individual, a robe that has become personal property is not fit for the formal act of a motion and announcement; only Sangha property is fit for the formal act of a motion and announcement. And only that is the cause of the five benefits. Therefore, a wise individual should, by urging them with such words as, 'Lay supporters, give to the Sangha; what is given to the Sangha is of great fruit,' cause it to be given. Or, having accepted it himself, he should relinquish it to the Sangha. A robe that has become Sangha property by being relinquished in this way is both fit for the formal act of a motion and announcement and productive of the five benefits. And it should be understood that such urging is in accordance with the word spoken by the Blessed One: 'Gotami, give to the Sangha. When it is given to the Sangha, both I and the Sangha will be honored' (MN 3.376).

Parikammaṃ [V 2.0077] karontānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yāgubhattañca dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti idaṃ pucchitattā doso natthīti katvā vuttaṃ, apucchite pana evaṃ kathetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Khalimakkhitasāṭakoti ahatavatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Suṭṭhu dhovitvātiādinā sapubbakaraṇaṃ atthāraṃ dasseti. Dhovanasibbanarajanakappakaraṇena hi vicāraṇachedanabandhanānipi dassitāniyeva honti, atthāradassanena paccuddhāraadhiṭṭhānānipi dasseti. Sūciādīni cīvarakammupakaraṇāni sajjetvā bahūhi bhikkhūhi saddhinti idaṃ pana sibbanassa upakaraṇanidassanaṃ. Tadahevāti idaṃ pana karaṇasannidhimocanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Dāyakassa hatthato sāṭakaṃ laddhadivaseyeva saṅghena atthārakassa bhikkhuno dātabbaṃ, evaṃ adente nicayasannidhi hoti. Atthārakenapi saṅghato laddhadivaseyeva kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ, evaṃ akaronte karaṇasannidhi hoti.

That it is permissible to give rice gruel and food to monks who are doing the preliminary work—this was said on the grounds that, since it was asked, there is no fault; but if unasked, it is not proper to speak thus. The term 'a cloth smeared with paste' is said in reference to new cloth. By 'having washed it well,' and so on, he indicates the spreading along with the preliminary actions. For by the acts of washing, sewing, dyeing, and marking, the acts of inspecting, cutting, and binding are also indicated. By showing the spreading, he also indicates the removal and determination. 'Having prepared needles and other implements for the robe-work, together with many monks'—this is an indication of the equipment for sewing. 'On that very day'—this is said for the purpose of being free from the fault of delaying the procedure. On the very day the cloth is received from the donor's hand, it should be given by the Sangha to the monk who is to spread the kathina. If they do not give it thus, there is the fault of hoarding. The one who is to spread it should also spread the kathina on the very day he receives it from the Sangha. If he does not do so, there is the fault of delaying the procedure.

Aññāni ca bahūni ānisaṃsavatthāni detīti iminā attharitabbasāṭakoyeva kathinasāṭako nāma, tato aññe sāṭakā bahavopi kathinānisaṃsāyeva nāmāti dasseti. Etena ca “kathinānisaṃso”ti vatthāniyeva vuttāni na agghoti dīpeti. Yadi aggho vutto siyā, evaṃ sati “bahvānisaṃsāni kathinavatthāni detī”ti vattabbaṃ, evaṃ pana avatvā “bahūni kathinānisaṃsavatthāni detī”ti vuttaṃ, tena ñāyati “na aggho vutto”ti, tasmā bahvānisaṃsabhāvo agghavasena na gahetabbo, atha kho vatthavaseneva gahetabboti. Itaroti añño dāyako. Tathā [M 2.0106] tathā ovaditvā saññāpetabboti “upāsaka dānaṃ nāma saṅghassa dinnakālato paṭṭhāya mahapphalaṃ hoti mahānisaṃsaṃ, atthāro pana bhikkhūnaṃ upakāratthāya bhagavatā anuññāto, tasmā ñattiladdhampi aladdhampi mahapphalamevā”ti vā “upāsaka ayampi dāyako saṅghasseva deti, tvampi saṅghasseva desi, bhagavatā ca –

By the words, 'And he gives many other beneficial items,' it is shown that only the cloth that is to be spread is called the 'Kathina cloth,' and that many other cloths are called 'Kathina benefits.' And by this, it is clarified that by 'Kathina benefits,' it is the cloths themselves that are meant, not their value. If the value were meant, then it should have been said, 'He gives many Kathina cloths of great benefit.' But since it was not said thus, and instead it was said, 'He gives many cloths that are Kathina benefits,' by this it is known that 'the value is not meant.' Therefore, the state of having many benefits should not be understood in terms of value, but rather should be understood only in terms of the cloths. 'The other' means another donor. He should be instructed and made to understand in various ways, such as: 'Lay supporter, a gift, from the time it is given to the Sangha, is of great fruit and great benefit. The spreading, however, was permitted by the Blessed One for the welfare of the monks. Therefore, whether it is received through a formal motion or not, it is still of great fruit.' Or: 'Lay supporter, this donor also gives only to the Sangha, and you too give only to the Sangha. And by the Blessed One it was said—'

‘Yo sīlavā sīlavantesu dadāti dānaṃ;

Dhammena laddhaṃ supasannacitto;

Abhisaddahaṃ kammaphalaṃ uḷāraṃ;

Taṃ ve dānaṃ vipulaphalanti brūmī’ti. (ma. ni. 3.382) –

‘He who is virtuous gives a gift to the virtuous, a gift obtained by righteous means, with a serene mind, firmly believing in the sublime result of kamma—that, indeed, is a gift of vast fruit, I say.’

Vuttaṃ, tasmā saṅghassa dinnakālato paṭṭhāya mahapphalamevā”ti vā itiādīni vatvā saññāpetabbo.

—was said. Therefore, he should be made to understand by saying this or other such things, for instance: 'From the time it is given to the Sangha, it is indeed of great fruit.'

Yassa [V 2.0078] saṅgho kathinacīvaraṃ deti, tena bhikkhunā kathinaṃ attharitabbanti yojanā. Yo jiṇṇacīvaro hoti bhikkhu, tassa dātabbanti sambandho. Imasmiṃ ṭhāne idāni bhikkhū –

The construal is: 'The monk to whom the Sangha gives the Kathina robe, by that monk the Kathina should be spread.' The connection is: 'It should be given to that monk who has a worn-out robe.' At this point, the monks now—

“Paṭiggahaṇañca sappāyaṃ, ñatti ca anusāvanaṃ;

Kappabindu paccuddhāro, adhiṭṭhānattharāni ca;

Niyojanānumodā ca, iccayaṃ kathine vidhī”ti. –

“Acceptance and suitability, the motion and the proclamation, the marking and the withdrawal, the determination and the spreading, the entrusting and the approval: this is the procedure in the Kathina.”

Imaṃ gāthaṃ āharitvā kathinadānakammavācāya paṭhamaṃ kathinacīvarassa paṭiggahaṇañca sappāyapucchanañca karonti, tadayuttaṃ viya dissati. Kasmāti ce? “Aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharituṃ…pe… pubbakaraṇaṃ jānāti, paccuddhāraṃ jānāti, adhiṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, atthāraṃ jānāti, mātikaṃ jānāti, palibodhaṃ jānāti, uddhāraṃ jānāti, ānisaṃsaṃ jānātī”ti parivārapāḷiyañca (pari. 409),

Having cited this verse, they first perform the acceptance of the Kathina robe and the inquiry about suitability with the formal act of giving the Kathina, which seems inappropriate. Why is that? Because in the Parivāra Pāḷi (Pari. 409) it is stated: “A person endowed with eight qualities is capable of spreading the Kathina… he knows the preliminary actions, he knows the withdrawal, he knows the determination, he knows the spreading, he knows the outline, he knows the impediments, he knows the lifting, he knows the benefits.”

“Aṭṭhadhammavido [M 2.0107] bhikkhu, kathinatthāramarahati;

Pubbapaccuddhārādhiṭṭhā-natthāro mātikāti ca;

Palibodho ca uddhāro, ānisaṃsā panaṭṭhime”ti. (vi. vi. 2704, 2706) –

“A monk who knows eight things is worthy of spreading the Kathina: preliminary action, withdrawal, determination, spreading, and the outline; and the impediment, the lifting, and the benefits—these are the eight.”

Vinayavinicchayappakaraṇe ca āgatesu aṭṭhasu aṅgesu anāgatattā ca “pubbakaraṇaṃ sattahi dhammehi saṅgahitaṃ dhovanena vicāraṇena chedanena bandhanena sibbanena rajanena kappakaraṇenā”ti parivārapāḷiyañca (pari. 408),

and because they are not included among the eight factors mentioned in the Vinayavinicchayappakaraṇa; and in the Parivāra Pāḷi (Pari. 408) it is stated: “The preliminary action is comprised of seven factors: washing, examining, cutting, binding, sewing, dyeing, and making fit.”

“Dhovanañca vicāro ca, chedanaṃ bandhanampi ca;

Sibbanaṃ rajanaṃ kappaṃ, pubbakiccanti vuccatī”ti. (vi. vi. 2707) –

“Washing and examining, cutting and binding; sewing, dyeing, and making fit—these are called preliminary actions.”

Vinayavinicchayappakaraṇe ca vuttesu sattasu pubbakaraṇesu anāgatattā ca.

and because they are not included among the seven preliminary actions mentioned in the Vinayavinicchayappakaraṇa.

Na [V 2.0079] kevalañca pakaraṇesu anāgatameva, atha kho yuttipi na dissati. Kathaṃ? Paṭiggahaṇaṃ nāma “yo pana bhikkhu adinnaṃ mukhadvāraṃ āhāraṃ āhāreyya aññatra udakadantaponā, pācittiya”nti (pāci. 265) yāvakālikādīsu ajjhoharitabbesu catūsu kālikavatthūsu bhagavatā vuttaṃ, na cīvare, taṃ pana pādamūle ṭhapetvā dinnampi parammukhā dinnampi labbhateva. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammīti evaṃ parammukhā vā pādamūle ṭhapetvā ‘imaṃ tumhāka’nti evaṃ sammukhā vā detī”ti, tasmā paṭiggahaṇakiccaṃ natthi, dāyakena cīvare dinne saṅghassa cittena sampaṭicchanamattameva pamāṇaṃ hoti.

Not only are they not found in the treatises, but their validity is also not seen. How so? The term ‘acceptance’ (paṭiggahaṇa) was spoken by the Blessed One regarding the four kinds of allowable items that are to be consumed, such as those for a limited time, as in: “Should any bhikkhu take into his mouth food that has not been given, except for water and a tooth-cleaner, it is an offense entailing confession” (Pācittiya 265). It was not spoken regarding robes. However, even if a robe is given by placing it at one's feet or given indirectly, it is still obtained. For it is stated in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379): “One gives either indirectly, saying, ‘I give this robe to so-and-so,’ or directly, placing it at the feet and saying, ‘This is yours.’” Therefore, there is no need for an act of acceptance (paṭiggahaṇakicca); when a donor gives a robe, the mere mental acceptance by the Saṅgha is sufficient.

Sappāyapucchanañca evaṃ karonti – ekena bhikkhunā “bhonto saṅghā saṅghassa kathine sampatte kassa puggalassa sappāyārahaṃ hotī”ti pucchite eko bhikkhu nāmaṃ [M 2.0108] vatvā “itthannāmassa therassa sappāyārahaṃ hotī”ti vadati, sappāyaiti ca nivāsanapārupanatthaṃ gahetvā vadanti. Etasmiṃ vacane saddato ca atthato ca adhippāyato ca yutti gavesitabbā hoti. Kathaṃ? Saddato vaggabhede satiyeva bahuvacanaṃ kattabbaṃ, na abhede, evaṃ saddato. Sappāyaitivacanañca anurūpattheyeva vattabbaṃ, na nivāsanapārupanatthe, evaṃ atthato. Idañca cīvaraṃ saṅgho kathinaṃ attharituṃ puggalassa deti, na nivāsanapārupanatthaṃ. Vuttañhi pāḷiyaṃ (mahāva. 307) “saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno deti kathinaṃ attharitu”nti, tasmā yutti gavesitabbā hoti. “Paṭiggahaṇañca sappāya”ntiādigāthāpi katthaci pāḷiyaṃ aṭṭhakathāṭīkādīsu ca na dissati, tasmā idha vuttanayeneva paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

And they inquire about suitability thus: When one bhikkhu asks, “Venerable sirs, the Saṅgha's Kathina cloth having been obtained, for which person is it suitable?” another bhikkhu states a name, saying, “It is suitable for the elder named so-and-so.” And they say “suitable” taking it to mean for the purpose of an under-robe and an upper-robe. In this statement, the validity must be investigated in terms of its wording, meaning, and intention. How? In terms of wording, the plural form should be used only when there is a division into groups, not when there is no division; thus, in terms of wording. And the word ‘suitable’ should be spoken only in its appropriate meaning, not in the meaning of an under-robe and an upper-robe; thus, in terms of meaning. And this robe is given by the Saṅgha to a person for spreading the Kathina, not for an under-robe and an upper-robe. For it is stated in the Pāḷi (Mahāva. 307): “The Saṅgha gives this Kathina cloth to the bhikkhu named so-and-so for spreading the Kathina.” Therefore, the validity must be investigated. And the verse beginning “Acceptance and suitability” is not found anywhere in the Pāḷi, commentaries, or sub-commentaries. Therefore, one should proceed here according to the method stated.

Sace bahū jiṇṇacīvarā, vuḍḍhassa dātabbanti idaṃ kathinacīvarassa saṅghikattā “na ca, bhikkhave, saṅghikaṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ paṭibāhitabbaṃ, yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti iminā pāḷinayena (cūḷava. 311) vuttaṃ. Eteneva nayena sabbesu balavacīvaresu santesupi vuḍḍhasseva dātabbanti siddhaṃ. Vuḍḍhesu…pe… dātabbanti karaṇasannidhimocanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tenevāha “sace vuḍḍho”tyādi. Navakatarenapi hi karaṇasannidhiṃ mocetvā kathine atthate anumodanaṃ karontassa saṅghassa pañcānisaṃsalābho hotīti. Apicātiādinā saṅghena kattabbavattaṃ dasseti. Vacanakkamo pana evaṃ kātabbo – kathinadussaṃ labhitvā saṅghe sīmāya sannipatite ekena bhikkhunā “bhante, saṅghassa idaṃ kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ kathannāmassa bhikkhuno [V 2.0080] dadeyya kathinaṃ attharitu”nti vutte aññena “yo jiṇṇacīvaro, tassā”ti vattabbaṃ, tato purimena “bahū [M 2.0109] jiṇṇacīvarā”ti vā “natthi idha jiṇṇacīvarā”ti vā vutte aparena “tena hi vuḍḍhassā”ti vattabbaṃ, puna purimena “ko ettha vuḍḍho”ti vutte itarena “itthannāmo bhikkhū”ti vattabbaṃ, puna purimena “so bhikkhu tadaheva cīvaraṃ katvā attharituṃ sakkotī”ti vutte itarena “so sakkotī”ti vā “saṅgho mahātherassa saṅgahaṃ karissatī”ti vā vattabbaṃ, puna purimena “so mahāthero aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgato”ti vutte itarena “āma samannāgato”ti vattabbaṃ, tato “sādhu suṭṭhu tassa dātabba”nti vutte byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñātabbo.

If there are many bhikkhus with worn-out robes, it should be given to the most senior. This is stated because the Kathina robe belongs to the Saṅgha, according to the Pāḷi rule (Cūḷava. 311): “Monks, what belongs to the Saṅgha should not be denied to the most senior according to seniority. Whoever denies it commits an offense of wrong-doing.” By this same principle, it is established that even if there are many strong robes available, it should still be given to the most senior. The phrase “among the senior ones… it should be given” is stated for the purpose of removing the need for proximity regarding the action. Therefore, it is said: “If the senior…” and so on. For even if the Kathina is spread by a more junior monk—after he has been released from the requirement of proximity for the action—the Saṅgha that rejoices gains the five benefits. Furthermore, the duty to be performed by the Saṅgha is shown. The order of speaking, however, should be done as follows: Having obtained the Kathina cloth, when the Saṅgha has assembled within the boundary, one bhikkhu should say: “Venerable sirs, this Kathina cloth has arisen for the Saṅgha. To which bhikkhu should the Saṅgha give this Kathina cloth for spreading the Kathina?” Then another should say: “To the one with worn-out robes.” After that, the first one should say: “There are many with worn-out robes,” or “There are no bhikkhus here with worn-out robes.” Then another should say: “Then to the most senior.” Again, the first one should say: “Who is the most senior here?” The other should reply: “The bhikkhu named so-and-so.” Again, the first one should say: “Is that bhikkhu able to make the robe and spread it on the same day?” The other should reply: “He is able,” or “The Saṅgha will support the great elder.” Again, the first one should say: “Is that great elder endowed with eight qualities?” The other should reply: “Yes, he is endowed.” Then, when it is said: “Good, very good, it should be given to him,” a bhikkhu who is competent and able should make the Saṅgha aware.

Ettha ca “bhante, saṅghassā”tiādivacanaṃ “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dadeyya kathinaṃ attharitu”nti imāya ñattipāḷiyā sameti. “Yo jiṇṇacīvaro, tassā”tiādi “saṅghena kassā”tiādi “saṅghena kassa dātabbaṃ, yo jiṇṇacīvaro hotī”tiādinā aṭṭhakathāvacanena (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) sameti. “So mahāthero aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato”tiādi “aṭṭhahaṅgehi samannāgato puggalo bhabbo kathinaṃ attharitu”ntiādikāya parivārapāḷiyā (pari. 409) sametīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yassa pana dīyati, tassa ñattidutiyakammavācāya dātabbanti sambandho. Iminā imassa kathinadānakammassa garukattā na apalokanamattena dātabbanti imamatthaṃ pakāseti. Garukalahukānaṃ bhedo kammākammavinicchayakathāyaṃ āvi bhavissati.

Here, the statement beginning “Venerable sirs, to the Saṅgha” corresponds with this motion formula: “May the Saṅgha hear me, Venerable sirs. This Kathina cloth has arisen for the Saṅgha. If it is ready for the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha give this Kathina cloth to the bhikkhu named so-and-so for spreading the Kathina.” The phrase beginning “To the one whose robe is worn out” corresponds with the commentary statement beginning “To whom by the Saṅgha,” and “To whom should it be given by the Saṅgha? It should be given to the one whose robe is worn out,” as found in the Mahāvagga Commentary (Mahāva. aṭṭha. 306). The statement beginning “That great elder is endowed with eight qualities” corresponds with the Parivāra Pāḷi (Pari. 409) beginning “A person endowed with eight qualities is fit for spreading the Kathina,” and so forth. This should be understood. As for the one to whom it is given, the connection is that it should be given by a formal act with a motion and one announcement. By this, it is shown that due to the importance of this Kathina-giving act, it should not be given merely by announcement. The distinction between weighty and light matters will become clear in the discussion on determining what constitutes a formal act and what does not.

Evaṃ dinne pana kathine paccuddharitabbā adhiṭṭhātabbā vācā bhinditabbāti sambandho. Sace taṃ kathinadussaṃ niṭṭhitaparikammameva hotīti iminā kathinadussaṃ nāma na kevalaṃ pakatisāṭakameva [M 2.0110] hoti, atha kho pariniṭṭhitasattavidhapubbakiccacīvarampi hotīti dasseti, tasmā niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṃ dinne sattavidhapubbakiccakaraṇena attho natthi, kevalaṃ paccuddharaṇādīniyeva kātabbāni. Sace pana kiñci apariniṭṭhitaṃ hoti, antamaso kappabindumattampi, taṃ niṭṭhāpetvāyeva paccuddharaṇādīni kātabbāni. Gaṇṭhikapaṭṭapāsakapaṭṭāni pana sibbanantogadhāni, tānipi niṭṭhāpetvāyeva kātabbāni. Aniṭṭhāpento aniṭṭhitasibbanakiccameva hoti. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.462-463) “tattha katanti sūcikammapariyosānena [V 2.0081] kataṃ, sūcikammapariyosānaṃ nāma yaṃ kiñci sūciyā kattabbaṃ. Pāsakapaṭṭagaṇṭhikapaṭṭapariyosānaṃ katvā sūciyā paṭisāmana”nti. Idañhi kathinavattaṃ nāma buddhappasatthanti “atthatakathinānaṃ vo bhikkhave pañca kappissantī”tiādinā pasatthaṃ.

When the kaṭhina has been given thus, the connection is that [the old robe] is to be withdrawn, [the new one] determined, and the utterance broken. If that kaṭhina cloth is already finished in its preparation, this shows that a kaṭhina cloth is not merely an ordinary piece of cloth, but is also a robe for which the seven preliminary duties have been fully completed. Therefore, when a finished robe has been given, there is no need to perform the seven preliminary duties—only the withdrawal and other such actions need to be done. But if anything remains unfinished, even as little as the kappabindu mark, then only after completing it should the withdrawal and other such actions be done. As for the loops, reinforcing tapes, and fastenings, which are included in the sewing, these too must be completed before those actions are taken. Not completing them means the sewing task remains unfinished. For it is stated in the commentary (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.462-463): “Here, ‘completed’ means finished with the needlework. ‘Needlework’ refers to whatever needs to be done with a needle. After completing the fastenings, reinforcing tapes, and loops, the needle is to be put away.” Indeed, this kaṭhina practice is praised by the Buddha, as it is praised in statements such as: “For you, O monks, who have spread the kaṭhina, five things will be allowable,” and so forth.

Katapariyositaṃ pana kathinaṃ gahetvāti –

Having taken the kaṭhina that has been completed and finished,

“Dhovanañca vicāro ca, chedanaṃ bandhanampi ca;

Sibbanaṃ rajanaṃ kappaṃ, pubbakiccanti vuccatī”ti. (vi. vi. 2707) –

“Washing and examining, cutting and binding; sewing, dyeing, and making it allowable—these are called preliminary duties.” (vi. vi. 2707)

Vuttāni sattavidhapubbakaraṇāni katvā pariyosāpitaṃ kathinacīvaraṃ gahetvā. Atthārakena bhikkhunā paccuddharitabbā adhiṭṭhātabbā vācā bhinditabbāti sambandho. Saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharitukāmo bhikkhu pubbe ticīvarādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhitaṃ porāṇikaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paccuddharāmī”ti vatvā paccuddharitabbā, tato anadhiṭṭhitaṃ navaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti vatvā adhiṭṭhātabbā, tato attharaṇakāle tameva adhiṭṭhitasaṅghāṭiṃ “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vācā bhinditabbāti attho. Esa nayo itaresu. Etena kathinatthāraṇaṃ nāma vacībhedakaraṇameva hoti, na kiñci kāyavikārakaraṇanti imamatthaṃ dīpeti[M 2.0111]. Tathā hi vuttaṃ vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. abhi. ṭī. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “attharitabbanti attharaṇaṃ kātabbaṃ, tañca kho tathāvacībhedakaraṇamevāti daṭṭhabba”nti.

Having taken the kaṭhina robe, which has been completed by performing the seven aforementioned preliminary duties, the connection is that by the monk who spreads [the kaṭhina], [the old robe] is to be withdrawn, [the new one] is to be determined, and the utterance is to be broken. A monk who wishes to spread the kaṭhina with the outer robe should first withdraw the old outer robe that was previously determined by the determination of the three robes, saying, 'I withdraw this outer robe.' Then, he should determine a new, undetermined outer robe, saying, 'I determine this outer robe.' After that, at the time of spreading, he should break the utterance with that very determined outer robe, saying, 'I spread the kaṭhina with this outer robe'—this is the meaning. This is the method for the other [robes]. By this, it is shown that the spreading of the kaṭhina is merely the act of breaking an utterance, not any act of physical modification. For it is stated in the Vinayatthamañjūsā (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Abhinavaṭīkā, Commentary on the Kaṭhina Training Rule): '“Is to be spread” means the spreading is to be done, and it should be understood as merely the act of breaking such an utterance.'

Tattha paccuddhāro tividho “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paccuddharāmī”ti saṅghāṭiyā paccuddhāro, “imaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ paccuddharāmī”ti uttarāsaṅgassa paccuddhāro, “imaṃ antaravāsakaṃ paccuddharāmī”ti antaravāsakassa paccuddhāroti. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre (pari. 408) “paccuddhāro tīhi dhammehi saṅgahito saṅghāṭiyā uttarāsaṅgena antaravāsakenā”ti. Adhiṭṭhānaṃ tividhaṃ “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti saṅghāṭiyā adhiṭṭhānaṃ, “imaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti uttarāsaṅgassa adhiṭṭhānaṃ, “imaṃ antaravāsakaṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti antaravāsakassa adhiṭṭhānanti. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre (pari. 408) “adhiṭṭhānaṃ tīhi dhammehi saṅgahitaṃ saṅghāṭiyā uttarāsaṅgena antaravāsakenā”ti.

In this context, withdrawal is threefold: 'I withdraw this outer robe' is the withdrawal of the outer robe; 'I withdraw this upper robe' is the withdrawal of the upper robe; 'I withdraw this lower robe' is the withdrawal of the lower robe. This is stated in the Parivāra (Pari. 408): 'Withdrawal is comprised of three things: the outer robe, the upper robe, and the lower robe.' Determination is threefold: 'I determine this outer robe' is the determination of the outer robe; 'I determine this upper robe' is the determination of the upper robe; 'I determine this lower robe' is the determination of the lower robe. This is stated in the Parivāra (Pari. 408): 'Determination is comprised of three things: the outer robe, the upper robe, and the lower robe.'

Atha [V 2.0082] vā adhiṭṭhānaṃ duvidhaṃ kāyena adhiṭṭhānaṃ, vācāya adhiṭṭhānanti. Tattha porāṇikaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paccuddharāmī”ti paccuddharitvā navaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ hatthena gahetvā “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti cittena ābhogaṃ katvā kāyavikārakaraṇena kāyena vā adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, vacībhedaṃ katvā vācāya vā adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.469; kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “tattha yasmā dve cīvarassa adhiṭṭhānāni kāyena vā adhiṭṭheti, vācāya vā adhiṭṭhetīti vuttaṃ, tasmā…pe… adhiṭṭhātabbā”ti. Atha vā adhiṭṭhānaṃ duvidhaṃ sammukhādhiṭṭhānaparammukhādhiṭṭhānavasena. Tattha yadi cīvaraṃ hatthapāse ṭhitaṃ hoti, “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti vacībhedaṃ katvā adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ, atha antogabbhe vā sāmantavihāre vā hoti, ṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ sallakkhetvā “etaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti vacībhedaṃ katvā adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Vuttañhi [M 2.0112] aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.469; kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “tatra duvidhaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ sace hatthapāse hotī”tiādi, vinayatthamañjūsāyañca (kaṅkhā. abhi. ṭī. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “duvidhanti sammukhāparammukhābhedena duvidha”nti.

Alternatively, determination is twofold: determination by body and determination by speech. In this context, having withdrawn the old outer robe by saying, 'I withdraw this outer robe,' and taking a new outer robe in hand, one should determine it either by body—by making a mental advertence, 'I determine this outer robe,' and performing a physical action—or by speech, by breaking the utterance. For it is stated in the Aṭṭhakathā (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.469; Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā): 'Here, since it is said that there are two determinations of a robe—one determines either by body or by speech—therefore... it should be determined.' Alternatively, determination is twofold: by way of determination in one's presence and determination in one's absence. In this context, if the robe is within arm's length, one should determine it by breaking the utterance, saying, 'I determine this outer robe.' But if it is inside a chamber or in a nearby monastery, one should determine it by noting the place where it is kept and breaking the utterance, saying, 'I determine that outer robe.' For it is stated in the Aṭṭhakathā (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 2.469; Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā): 'Here, determination is twofold: if it is within arm's length...' and so on. And in the Vinayatthamañjūsā (Kaṅkhā. Abhi. Ṭī. Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā), it is said: '“Twofold” means twofold by the distinction of presence and absence.'

Atthāro katividho? Atthāro ekavidho. Vacībhedakaraṇeneva hi atthāro sampajjati, na kāyavikārakaraṇena. Ayamattho yathāvutta-parivārapāḷiyā ca “attharitabbanti attharaṇaṃ kātabbaṃ, tañca kho tathāvacībhedakaraṇamevāti daṭṭhabba”nti vinayatthamañjūsāvacanena ca viññāyati. Atha vā atthāro tividho vatthuppabhedena. Tattha yadi saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇikā saṅghāṭi paccuddharitabbā, navā saṅghāṭi adhiṭṭhātabbā, “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vācā bhinditabbā. Atha uttarāsaṅgena kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇako uttarāsaṅgo paccuddharitabbo, navo uttarāsaṅgo adhiṭṭhātabbo, “iminā uttarāsaṅgena kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vācā bhinditabbā. Atha antaravāsakena kathinaṃ attharitukāmo hoti, porāṇako antaravāsako paccuddharitabbo, navo antaravāsako adhiṭṭhātabbo, “iminā antaravāsakena kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vācā bhinditabbā. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre (pari. 413) “sace saṅghāṭiyā”tiādi.

How many kinds of spreading [of the kaṭhina] are there? Spreading is of one kind. For spreading is accomplished solely by the act of breaking an utterance, not by any physical action. This meaning is understood from the aforementioned Parivāra Pāḷi and from the statement in the Vinayatthamañjūsā: '“Is to be spread” means the spreading is to be done, and it should be understood as merely the act of breaking such an utterance.' Alternatively, spreading is of three kinds, by way of the distinction of the cloth. In this context, if one wishes to spread the kaṭhina with the outer robe, the old outer robe is to be withdrawn, a new outer robe is to be determined, and the utterance is to be broken: 'I spread the kaṭhina with this outer robe.' If one wishes to spread the kaṭhina with the upper robe, the old upper robe is to be withdrawn, a new upper robe is to be determined, and the utterance is to be broken: 'I spread the kaṭhina with this upper robe.' If one wishes to spread the kaṭhina with the lower robe, the old lower robe is to be withdrawn, a new lower robe is to be determined, and the utterance is to be broken: 'I spread the kaṭhina with this lower robe.' This is stated in the Parivāra (Pari. 413): 'If with the outer robe,' etc.

Ettha siyā – kiṃ pana “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paccuddharāmī”ti visesaṃ katvāva paccuddharitabbā, udāhu “imaṃ paccuddharāmī”ti sāmaññatopi paccuddharitabbāti? Parikkhāracoḷādhiṭṭhānena [V 2.0083] adhiṭṭhitaṃ cīvaraṃ “imaṃ paccuddharāmī”ti sāmaññato paccuddharitabbaṃ, na “imaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paccuddharāmī”ti visesato paccuddharitabbaṃ. Kasmā? Pubbe aladdhanāmattā. Ticīvarādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhitaṃ pana cīvaraṃ visesatoyeva paccuddharitabbaṃ, na sāmaññato. Kasmā? Paṭiladdhavisesanāmattā[M 2.0113]. Idha pana kathinādhikāre pubbeva ticīvarādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhitattā visesatoyeva paccuddharitabbanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre (pari. 408) kathinādhikāre “paccuddhāro tīhi dhammehi saṅgahito saṅghāṭiyā uttarāsaṅgena antaravāsakenā”ti. Kiṃ pana niccatecīvarikoyeva kathinaṃ attharituṃ labhati, udāhu avatthātecīvarikopīti? Tecīvariko duvidho dhutaṅgatecīvarikavinayatecīvarikavasena. Tattha dhutaṅgatecīvariko “atirekacīvaraṃ paṭikkhipāmi, tecīvarikaṅgaṃ samādiyāmī”ti adhiṭṭhahitvā dhāraṇato sabbakālameva dhāreti. Vinayatecīvariko pana yadā ticīvarādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhahitvā dhāretukāmo hoti, tadā tathā adhiṭṭhahitvā dhāreti. Yadā pana parikkhāracoḷādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhahitvā dhāretukāmo hoti, tadā tathā adhiṭṭhahitvā dhāreti, tasmā ticīvarādhiṭṭhānassa dupparihārattā sabbadā dhāretuṃ asakkonto hutvā parikkhāracoḷavasena dhārentopi taṃ paccuddharitvā āsanne kāle ticīvarādhiṭṭhānena adhiṭṭhahantopi kathinaṃ attharituṃ labhatiyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Here, the question arises: Should the robe be revoked specifically by stating, 'I revoke this outer robe,' or can it be revoked generally by stating, 'I revoke this'? A robe determined as an accessory cloth should be revoked generally by stating, 'I revoke this,' and not specifically by stating, 'I revoke this outer robe.' Why? Because it had not previously obtained a specific name. However, a robe determined by the determination of the three robes must be revoked specifically, not generally. Why? Because it has obtained a specific name. Here, however, in the context of the Kathina, since it was previously determined by the determination of the three robes, it should be revoked specifically. This is to be understood. As stated in the Parivāra (Par. 408) regarding the Kathina procedure: 'Revocation is comprised of three items: the outer robe, the upper robe, and the lower robe.' Now, can only one who is a constant three-robed monk spread the Kathina, or can even one who is not a constant three-robed monk do so? The three-robed monk is of two kinds: by way of being a dhutaṅga three-robed monk and a Vinaya three-robed monk. Among them, the dhutaṅga three-robed monk, having determined, 'I reject extra robes, I undertake the ascetic practice of the three robes,' wears them at all times. The Vinaya three-robed monk, however, when he wishes to wear them after determining them by the determination of the three robes, then he determines and wears them thus. But when he wishes to wear them after determining them by the determination of an accessory cloth, then he determines and wears them thus. Therefore, since the determination of the three robes is difficult to maintain, even one who is unable to wear them at all times and wears them as an accessory cloth, by revoking that and then determining them by the determination of the three robes when the time is near, can indeed spread the Kathina. This is to be understood.

Kacci nu bho kathinadānakammavācābhaṇanasīmāyameva kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ, udāhu aññasīmāyāti? Yadi kathinadānakammavācābhaṇanabaddhasīmā vassūpanāyikakhettabhūtaupacārasīmāya anto ṭhitā, evaṃ sati tasmiṃyeva sīmamaṇḍale attharaṇaṃ kātabbaṃ. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Pariniṭṭhitapubbakaraṇameva ce dāyako saṅghassa deti, sampaṭicchitvā kammavācāya dātabbaṃ. Tena ca tasmiṃyeva sīmamaṇḍale adhiṭṭhahitvā attharitvā saṅgho anumodāpetabbo”ti vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 308) āgatattā viññāyatīti. Yadi evaṃ “tasmiṃyeva sīmamaṇḍale”icceva ṭīkāyaṃ vuttattā “yasmiṃ kismiñci [M 2.0114] sīmamaṇḍale kammavācaṃ bhaṇitvā tasmiṃyeva sīmamaṇḍale attharitabba”nti vattabbaṃ, na “kathinadānakammavācābhaṇanabaddhasīmā vassūpanāyikakhettabhūtaupacārasīmāya anto ṭhitā”ti visesaṃ katvā vattabbanti? Na na vattabbaṃ. Kammavācābhaṇanasīmā hi baddhasīmābhūtā, kathinatthārasīmā pana upacārasīmābhūtā, upacārasīmā ca nāma baddhasīmaṃ avattharitvāpi gacchati, tasmā sā sīmā baddhasīmā ca hoti upacārasīmā cāti tasmiṃyeva sīmamaṇḍale kathinadānakammavācaṃ [V 2.0084] bhaṇitvā tattheva attharaṇaṃ kātabbaṃ, na yasmiṃ kismiñci sīmamaṇḍale kammavācaṃ bhaṇitvā tattheva attharaṇaṃ kattabbanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evampi “upacārasīmāya”icceva vattabbaṃ, na “vassūpanāyikakhettabhūtaupacārasīmāyā”ti, tampi vattabbameva. Tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vassūpanāyikakhettabhūtāya eva upacārasīmāya kathinatthāraṃ kātuṃ labhati, na aññaupacārasīmāya. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) “aññasmiṃ vihāre vutthavassāpi na labhantīti mahāpaccariyaṃ vutta”nti.

Is the Kathina to be spread only within the boundary where the Kathina-donation kammavācā is recited, or within another boundary? If the baddha boundary for reciting the Kathina-donation kammavācā is located within the upacāra boundary that serves as the rains-residence field, then the spreading should be done within that same boundary circle. How is this understood? It is understood from what is stated in the Vajirabuddhi commentary (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 308): “If the donor gives to the Saṅgha what has already been prepared beforehand, it should be given after acceptance through the kammavācā. Having determined it and spread it within that very boundary circle, the Saṅgha should be made to rejoice.” Thus, it is understood. If so, since it is said in the commentary, “within that very boundary circle,” should it be said that “having recited the kammavācā in any boundary circle whatsoever, the spreading must be done in that very same boundary circle,” without making the distinction that “the baddha boundary for reciting the Kathina-donation kammavācā is located within the upacāra boundary that serves as the rains-residence field”? No, it should not be said so. The boundary for reciting the kammavācā is indeed a baddha boundary, whereas the boundary for spreading the Kathina is an upacāra boundary. An upacāra boundary, by nature, can extend beyond a baddha boundary. Therefore, that boundary is both a baddha boundary and an upacāra boundary. Thus, the Kathina-donation kammavācā should be recited within that very boundary circle, and the spreading should be done there—it should be understood that it is not the case that having recited the kammavācā in any boundary circle whatsoever, the spreading should be done there. Even so, one might argue that it should simply be said “the upacāra boundary,” and not “the upacāra boundary that serves as the rains-residence field”—yet this latter phrase should indeed be said. Those bhikkhus are permitted to spread the Kathina only within the upacāra boundary that serves as their rains-residence field, not within any other upacāra boundary. For it is stated in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 306): “It is stated in the Mahāpaccariya that even those who have completed the rains-residence in another monastery do not obtain it.”

Yathicchasi, tathā bhavatu, api tu khalu “kammavācābhaṇanasīmā baddhasīmābhūtā, kathinatthārasīmā upacārasīmābhūtā”ti tumhehi vuttaṃ, tathābhūtabhāvo kathaṃ jānitabboti? Vuccate – kathinatthārasīmāyaṃ tāva upacārasīmābhūtabhāvo “sace pana ekasīmāya bahū vihārā honti, sabbe bhikkhū sannipātetvā ekattha kathinaṃ attharitabba”nti imissā aṭṭhakathāya (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) atthaṃ saṃvaṇṇetuṃ “ekasīmāyāti ekaupacārasīmāyāti attho yujjatī”ti vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306) āgatattā viññāyati. Kammavācābhaṇanasīmāya baddhasīmābhūtabhāvo pana “te ca kho hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā ekasīmāyaṃ ṭhitā. Sīmā ca nāmesā baddhasīmā [M 2.0115] abaddhasīmāti duvidhā hotī”ti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) āgatattā ca “sīmā ca nāmesā katamā, yattha hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā ṭhitā kammappattā nāma hontīti anuyogaṃ sandhāya sīmaṃ dassento vibhāgavantānaṃ sabhāvavibhāvanaṃ vibhāgadassanamukheneva hotīti ‘sīmā ca nāmesā’tiādimāhā”ti vinayatthamañjūsāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. abhi. ṭī. nidānavaṇṇanā) āgatattā ca viññāyati.

As you wish, so be it. However, since you have said, “The boundary for reciting the kammavācā is a baddha boundary, while the boundary for the Kathina spreading is an upacāra boundary,” how is such a state of affairs to be known? It is said: First, regarding the Kathina-spreading boundary being an upacāra boundary, it is known from what is stated in the Vajirabuddhi sub-commentary (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 306) to explain the meaning of this commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 306), “If there are many monasteries within a single boundary, all the bhikkhus should gather and spread the Kathina in one place”: “’Within a single boundary’ means within a single upacāra boundary; this meaning is suitable.” As for the boundary for reciting the kammavācā being a baddha boundary, this is known from what is stated in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī (Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Nidānavaṇṇanā): “They must stand within a single boundary without leaving arm’s reach. And this boundary is of two kinds: baddha boundaries and abaddha boundaries.” And it is also known from what is stated in the Vinayatthamañjūsā (Kaṅkhā. Abhi. Ṭī. Nidānavaṇṇanā): “In reference to the question, ‘What is this boundary, where those qualified for the act stand without leaving arm’s reach?’, he shows the boundary, and since the elucidation of the nature of those who are distinguished is by means of showing the distinction, he stated the passage beginning ‘And this boundary...’”

Tattha katividhā baddhasīmā, katividhā abaddhasīmāti? Tividhā baddhasīmā khaṇḍasīmāsamānasaṃvāsasīmāavippavāsasīmāvasena. Tividhā abaddhasīmā gāmasīmāudakukkhepasīmāsattabbhantarasīmāvasenāti daṭṭhabbā. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Evaṃ ekādasa vipattisīmāyo atikkamitvā tividhasampattiyuttā nimittena nimittaṃ sambandhitvā sammatā sīmā baddhasīmāti veditabbā. Khaṇḍasīmā samānasaṃvāsasīmā avippavāsasīmāti tassāyeva bhedo. Abaddhasīmā pana gāmasīmā sattabbhantarasīmā udakukkhepasīmāti tividhā”ti kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) āgatattā viññāyati. Evaṃ tīsu baddhasīmāsu[V 2.0085], tīsu abaddhasīmāsūti chasuyeva sīmāsu kammappattasaṅghassa catuvaggakaraṇīyādikammassa kattabbabhāvavacanato suddhāya upacārasīmāya kammavācāya abhaṇitabbabhāvo viññāyati. Antoupacārasīmāya baddhasīmāya sati taṃ baddhasīmaṃ avattharitvāpi upacārasīmāya gamanato sā baddhasīmā kammavācābhaṇanārahā ca hoti kathinatthārārahā cāti veditabbaṃ.

Here, how many kinds of baddha boundaries are there, and how many kinds of abaddha boundaries? There are three kinds of baddha boundaries: a khaṇḍa boundary, a samānasaṃvāsa boundary, and an avippavāsa boundary. Three kinds of abaddha boundaries should be understood: a village boundary, a water-tossing boundary, and a seven-abbhantara boundary. How is this to be understood? It is understood from what is stated in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī (Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Nidānavaṇṇanā) as follows: “Having thus avoided the eleven defective boundaries, a boundary established by connecting marker to marker, endowed with the three kinds of accomplishment, is to be known as a baddha boundary. The khaṇḍa boundary, the samānasaṃvāsa boundary, and the avippavāsa boundary are divisions of that very boundary. The abaddha boundary, however, is of three kinds: the village boundary, the seven-abbhantara boundary, and the water-tossing boundary.” Thus, from the statement that for a Saṅgha qualified to perform acts, acts such as those requiring a four-member Saṅgha are to be done within these six boundaries—the three baddha boundaries and the three abaddha boundaries—it is understood that the kammavācā should not be recited within a pure upacāra boundary. When there is a baddha boundary within an upacāra boundary, since the upacāra boundary can extend without being coextensive with that baddha boundary, it should be understood that that baddha boundary is suitable for reciting the kammavācā and for the spreading of the Kathina.

Nanu ca pannarasavidhā sīmā aṭṭhakathāsu (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379; kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. akālacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) āgatā, atha kasmā chaḷeva vuttāti? Saccaṃ, tāsu pana pannarasasu sīmāsu upacārasīmā saṅghalābhavibhajanādiṭṭhānameva hoti, lābhasīmā [M 2.0116] tatruppādagahaṇaṭṭhānameva hotīti imā dve sīmāyo saṅghakammakaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ na honti, nigamasīmā nagarasīmā janapadasīmā raṭṭhasīmā rajjasīmā dīpasīmā cakkavāḷasīmāti imā pana sīmāyo gāmasīmāya samānagatikā gāmasīmāyameva antogadhāti na visuṃ vuttāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ettha ca upacārasīmāya baddhasīmaṃ avattharitvā gatabhāvo kathaṃ jānitabboti? “Upacārasīmā parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepena, aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānena paricchinnā”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) vuttattā parikkhepaparikkhepārahaṭṭhānānaṃ anto baddhasīmāya vijjamānāya taṃ avattharitvā upacārasīmā gatā. Tathā hi “imissā upacārasīmāya ‘saṅghassa dammī’ti dinnaṃ pana khaṇḍasīmasīmantarikāsu ṭhitānampi pāpuṇātī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) vuttaṃ. Tena ñāyati “upacārasīmāya anto ṭhitā baddhasīmā upacārasīmāpi nāma hotī”ti. Hotu, evaṃ sati antoupacārasīmāyaṃ baddhasīmāya sati tattheva kathinadānakammavācaṃ vācāpetvā tattheva kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ bhaveyya, antoupacārasīmāyaṃ baddhasīmāya avijjamānāya kathaṃ karissantīti? Antoupacārasīmāyaṃ baddhasīmāya avijjamānāya bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ vijjamānabaddhasīmaṃ vā udakukkhepalabhanaṭṭhānaṃ vā gantvā kammavācaṃ vācāpetvā puna vihāraṃ āgantvā vassūpanāyikakhettabhūtāya upacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhatvā kathinaṃ attharitabbanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

But are not fifteen kinds of boundaries mentioned in the commentaries (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379; Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Akālacīvarasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā)? So why are only six mentioned here? Indeed, that is so. However, among those fifteen boundaries, the upacāra boundary is only the place for distributing Saṅgha gains, and the lābha boundary is only the place for receiving what arises there. These two boundaries are not the place for performing Saṅgha acts. The nigama boundary, nagara boundary, janapada boundary, raṭṭha boundary, rajja boundary, dīpa boundary, and cakkavāḷa boundary—these boundaries are of similar scope to the village boundary and are included within the village boundary itself, so they are not mentioned separately; this should be understood. Here, how is it to be known that the upacāra boundary extends beyond the baddha boundary? Because it is said in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379): “The upacāra boundary is defined by the enclosure of an enclosed monastery, or by the area suitable for enclosure for an unenclosed one.” Therefore, when a baddha boundary exists within the enclosure or the area suitable for enclosure, the upacāra boundary extends beyond it. For instance, it is said (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379): “What is given within this upacāra boundary with the words, ‘I give this to the Saṅgha,’ reaches even those standing in khaṇḍa boundaries or between boundaries.” From this it is known that “a baddha boundary situated within an upacāra boundary is also called an upacāra boundary.” So be it. If that is so, when there is a baddha boundary within an upacāra boundary, the Kathina-donation kammavācā should be recited right there and the Kathina should be spread right there. But what should they do when there is no baddha boundary within the upacāra boundary? When there is no baddha boundary within the upacāra boundary, they should go to an existing baddha boundary outside the upacāra boundary, or to a place where a water-tossing boundary is obtained, recite the kammavācā, and then return to the monastery. Standing within the upacāra boundary that serves as the area for the rains-residence, they should then spread the Kathina. This is how it should be understood.

Nanu ca bho evaṃ sante aññissā sīmāya ñatti, aññissā atthāro hoti, evaṃ sante “pariniṭṭhitapubbakaraṇameva ce dāyako saṅghassa deti, sampaṭicchitvā kammavācāya dātabbaṃ. Tena ca tasmiṃyeva sīmamaṇḍale adhiṭṭhahitvā attharitvā saṅgho anumodāpetabbo”ti vuttena [V 2.0086] vajirabuddhiṭīkāvacanena (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 308) virujjhatīti? Nanu [M 2.0117] avocumha “kammavācābhaṇanasīmā baddhasīmābhūtā, kathinatthārasīmā upacārasīmābhūtā”ti. Tasmā vajirabuddhiṭīkāvacanena na virujjhati. Tattha pubbe yebhuyyena baddhasīmavihārattā samaggaṃ saṅghaṃ sannipātetvā kammavācaṃ vācāpetvā upacārasīmabaddhasīmabhūte tasmiṃyeva vihāre attharaṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Baddhasīmavihāre ahontepi antoupacārasīmāyaṃ baddhasīmāya vijjamānāya tattheva sīmamaṇḍale kammavācaṃ vācāpetvā tattheva attharitabbabhāvo amhehipi vuttoyeva. Yadi pana na ceva baddhasīmavihāro hoti, na ca antoupacārasīmāyaṃ baddhasīmā atthi, evarūpe vihāre kammavācaṃ vācāpetuṃ na labhati, aññaṃ baddhasīmaṃ vā udakukkhepaṃ vā gantvā kammavācaṃ vācāpetvā attano vihāraṃ āgantvā vassūpanāyikakhettabhūtāya upacārasīmāya ṭhatvā kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ. Evameva paramparabhūtā bahavo ācariyavarā karontīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

But, sir, if that is the case, the ñatti is for one boundary, and the spreading is for another. If so, does this not contradict the statement in the Vajirabuddhiṭīkā (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 308), which says: “If a donor gives to the Saṅgha a robe with its preliminary work already completed, having accepted it, it should be given by means of a formal act (kammavācā). And by him, having determined it and spread it within that very boundary circle (sīmamaṇḍala), the Saṅgha should be invited to approve”? Did we not say, “The boundary for reciting the formal act is a baddhasīmā, while the boundary for spreading the kathina is an upacārasīmā”? Therefore, it does not contradict the statement in the Vajirabuddhiṭīkā. In that text, it was spoken with reference to a situation where, because in the past most monasteries were baddhasīmā monasteries, one would assemble the complete Saṅgha, have the formal act recited, and then spread the kathina within that very monastery, which was both an upacārasīmā and a baddhasīmā. We have also stated that even if it is not a baddhasīmā monastery, if a baddhasīmā exists within the upacārasīmā, the formal act should be recited in that very boundary circle and the kathina spread there. But if there is neither a baddhasīmā monastery nor a baddhasīmā within the upacārasīmā, in such a monastery one cannot have the formal act recited. One must go to another baddhasīmā or an udakukkhepa (water-tossing) boundary, have the formal act recited, return to one's own monastery, and then spread the kathina while standing within the upacārasīmā, which serves as the area for the rains-residence. It should be understood that many excellent teachers have acted thus in continuous tradition.

Apare pana ācariyā “baddhasīmavirahāya suddhaupacārasīmāya sati tassaṃyeva upacārasīmāyaṃ ñattikammavācāpi vācetabbā, kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ, na aññissā sīmāya ñatti, aññissā attharaṇaṃ kātabba”nti vadanti. Ayaṃ pana nesamadhippāyo – “kathinatthatasīmāyanti upacārasīmaṃ sandhāya vutta”nti vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306) kathinatthāraṭṭhānabhūtāya sīmāya upacārasīmābhāvo vutto, tassaṃyeva ṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 308) pubbe niddiṭṭhapāṭhe “tasmiṃyeva sīmamaṇḍale adhiṭṭhahitvā attharitvā saṅgho anumodāpetabbo”ti kammavācābhaṇanasīmāyameva attharitabbabhāvo ca vutto, tasmā aññissā sīmāya ñatti, aññissā attharaṇaṃ na kātabbaṃ, tassaṃyeva upacārasīmāyaṃ kammavācaṃ sāvetvā tasmiṃyeva atthāro kātabbo, upacārasīmato bahi ṭhitaṃ baddhasīmaṃ gantvā attharaṇakiccaṃ natthīti.

Other teachers, however, say: “When there is a pure upacārasīmā in the absence of a baddhasīmā, the ñattikammavācā should be recited and the kathina should be spread within that very upacārasīmā; the ñatti should not be in one boundary and the spreading in another.” This, however, is their intention: in the Vajirabuddhiṭīkā (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 306) it is stated that the boundary that is the place for spreading the kathina is an upacārasīmā, with reference to the phrase “in the boundary where the kathina is spread.” And in that same ṭīkā (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 308), in the passage previously cited—“having determined it and spread it within that very boundary circle, the Saṅgha should be invited to approve”—it is also stated that the spreading should be done in the very same boundary where the kammavācā is recited. Therefore, the ñatti should not be done in one boundary and the spreading in another. The kammavācā should be announced in that very upacārasīmā, and the spreading should be done in that same place. There is no duty of spreading to be done by going to a baddhasīmā situated outside the upacārasīmā.

Tatrevaṃ [M 2.0118] vicāraṇā kātabbā – idaṃ bhāsantaresu “ñattī”ti kathitaṃ kathinadānakammaṃ catūsu saṅghakammesu ñattidutiyakammaṃ hoti, ñattidutiyakammassa navasu ṭhānesu kathinadānaṃ, garukalahukesu garukaṃ, yadi “upacārasīmāyaṃ cattāri saṅghakammāni kātabbānī”ti pakaraṇesu āgataṃ abhavissā, evaṃ sante tesaṃ ācariyānaṃ vacanānurūpato upacārasīmāyaṃ kathinadānañattikammavācaṃ vācetabbaṃ abhavissā, na pana pakaraṇesu “upacārasīmāyaṃ cattāri saṅghakammāni kātabbānī”ti āgataṃ, atha kho “saṅghalābhavibhajanaṃ, āgantukavattaṃ katvā ārāmappavisanaṃ[V 2.0087], gamikassa bhikkhuno senāsanaāpucchanaṃ, nissayapaappassambhanaṃ, pārivāsikamānattacārikabhikkhūnaṃ aruṇuṭṭhāpanaṃ, bhikkhunīnaṃ ārāmappavisanaāpucchanaṃ iccevamādīni eva upacārasīmāya kattabbānī”ti āgataṃ, tasmā kathinadānañattidutiyakammavācā kevalāyaṃ upacārasīmāyaṃ na vācetabbāti siddhā. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Avippavāsasīmā nāma tiyojanāpi hoti, evaṃ sante tiyojane ṭhitā lābhaṃ gaṇhissanti, tiyojane ṭhatvā āgantukavattaṃ pūretvā ārāmaṃ pavisitabbaṃ bhavissati, gamiko tiyojanaṃ gantvā senāsanaṃ āpucchissati, nissayapaṭipannassa bhikkhuno tiyojanātikkame nissayo paṭippassambhissati, pārivāsikena tiyojanaṃ atikkamitvā aruṇaṃ uṭṭhapetabbaṃ bhavissati, bhikkhuniyā tiyojane ṭhatvā ārāmappavisanaṃ āpucchitabbaṃ bhavissati, sabbampetaṃ upacārasīmāya paricchedavaseneva kātuṃ vaṭṭati, tasmā upacārasīmāyameva bhājetabba”nti evamādiaṭṭhakathāpāṭhato (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) viññāyatīti.

Here, the following investigation should be made: This act of giving the kathina, called ‘ñatti’ in other languages, is a ñattidutiyakamma among the four Saṅgha acts. The giving of the kathina is one of the nine instances of ñattidutiyakamma, and among weighty and light matters, it is a weighty one. If it had been stated in the treatises that ‘the four Saṅgha acts should be performed within the upacārasīmā,’ then, in accordance with the words of those teachers, the ñattikammavācā for the giving of the kathina would have to be recited within the upacārasīmā. But it is not stated in the treatises that ‘the four Saṅgha acts should be performed within the upacārasīmā.’ Rather, it is stated: ‘The distribution of Saṅgha gains, entering the monastery after performing the duties for incoming monks, a traveling bhikkhu asking for lodging, the termination of dependence, announcing the dawn for bhikkhus undergoing probation or penance, and nuns asking for permission to enter the monastery—these and similar acts are to be performed within the upacārasīmā.’ Therefore, it is established that the ñattidutiyakamma for the giving of the kathina should not be recited solely within an upacārasīmā. How is this known? It is known from the commentary passage (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379) which states: “The avippavāsasīmā (non-separation boundary) can extend up to three yojanas. In that case, those standing within three yojanas would receive a share. A monk standing within three yojanas must fulfill the duties for incoming monks before entering the monastery. A traveling bhikkhu up to three yojanas away will ask for lodging. For a bhikkhu under dependence, his dependence is terminated upon crossing three yojanas. A probationer must not be beyond three yojanas when dawn arises. A nun must ask for permission to enter the monastery while standing within three yojanas. All this is allowable only within the confines of the upacārasīmā. Therefore, the distribution should be done only within the upacārasīmā.”

Athevaṃ [M 2.0119] vadeyyuṃ – “upacārasīmā ñattidutiyakammavācāya ṭhānaṃ na hotī”ti tumhehi vuttaṃ, atha ca pana katapubbaṃ atthi. Tathā hi cīvarapaṭiggāhakasammuticīvaranidahakasammuticīvarabhājakasammutīnaṃ “suṇātu me…pe… dhārayāmīti imāya kammavācāya vā apalokanena vā antovihāre sabbasaṅghamajjhepi khaṇḍasīmāyapi sammannituṃ vaṭṭatiyevā”ti upacārasīmāyaṃ ñattidutiyakammavācāya nipphādetabbabhāvo aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 194) āgato. Bhaṇḍāgārassa pana “imaṃ pana bhaṇḍāgāraṃ khaṇḍasīmaṃ gantvā khaṇḍasīmāya nisinnehi sammannituṃ na vaṭṭati, vihāramajjheyeva ‘suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ vihāraṃ bhaṇḍāgāraṃ sammanneyyā’tiādinā nayena kammavācāya vā apalokanena vā sammannitabba”nti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 197) upacārasīmāyameva ñattidutiyakammavācāya sammannitabbabhāvo āgatoti.

They might say: 'You have stated that the upacārasīmā (vicinity boundary) is not a place for a ñattidutiyakamma-kammavācā (a formal act preceded by a motion), yet it has been done before. Indeed, regarding the appointment of robe-receivers (cīvarapaṭiggāhakasammuti), robe-storers (cīvaranidahakasammuti), and robe-distributors (cīvarabhājakasammuti), it is said that with this formal motion (kammavācā), “Hear me… I hold it thus,” or by announcement (apalokana), it is indeed permissible to appoint them, even within a monastery (antovihāre), in the midst of the entire Sangha (sabbasaṅghamajjhe), or within a khaṇḍasīmā (fragmentary boundary). Thus, it is found in the commentary (Vin. Sangha. Aṭṭha. 194) that this is to be accomplished by a ñattidutiyakammavācā in the upacārasīmā. However, concerning the storeroom (bhaṇḍāgāra), the commentary (Vin. Sangha. Aṭṭha. 197) states: “But it is not permissible to appoint this storeroom by those who have gone to a khaṇḍasīmā and are seated within the khaṇḍasīmā. Instead, it must be appointed in the middle of the monastery (vihāramajjhe) either by the formal motion beginning, ‘Hear me, venerable Sangha. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the monastery named so-and-so as a storeroom,’ or by announcement (apalokana).” Thus, it is found that an appointment is to be made by a ñattidutiyakammavācā even within the upacārasīmā.'

Te evaṃ vattabbā – sacepi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ āgataṃ “antovihāre”ti pāṭho “vihāramajjhe”ti pāṭho ca upacārasīmaṃ sandhāya vuttoti maññamānā tumhe āyasmanto evaṃ avacuttha, te pana pāṭhā upacārasīmaṃ sandhāya aṭṭhakathācariyehi na vuttā, atha kho avippavāsasīmāsaṅkhātaṃ mahāsīmaṃ sandhāya vuttā. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? Khaṇḍasīmāya vakkhamānattā. Khaṇḍasīmāya hi mahāsīmā eva paṭiyogī hoti. Upacārasīmāti ayamattho kathaṃ [V 2.0088] jānitabboti ce? “Imaṃ pana samānasaṃvāsakasīmaṃ sammannantehi pabbajjūpasampadādīnaṃ saṅghakammānaṃ sukhakaraṇatthaṃ paṭhamaṃ khaṇḍasīmā sammannitabbā…pe… evaṃ baddhāsu pana sīmāsu khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhitā bhikkhū mahāsīmāya kammaṃ karontānaṃ na kopenti[M 2.0120], mahāsīmāya vā ṭhitā khaṇḍasīmāya kammaṃ karontānaṃ. Sīmantarikāya pana ṭhitā ubhinnampi na kopentī”ti vuttaaṭṭhakathāpāṭhavasena (mahāva. aṭṭha. 138) jānitabboti. Atha vā tehi āyasmantehi ābhatabhaṇḍāgārasammutipāṭhavasenapi ayamattho viññāyati. Kathaṃ? Cīvarapaṭiggāhakādipuggalasammutiyo pana antovihāre sabbasaṅghamajjhepi khaṇḍasīmāyampi sammannituṃ vaṭṭati, bhaṇḍāgārasaṅkhātavihārasammuti pana vihāramajjheyevāti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, tattha visesakāraṇaṃ pariyesitabbaṃ.

They should be told thus: Even if you, venerable ones, think that the passages 'within the monastery' (antovihāre) and 'in the middle of the monastery' (vihāramajjhe) found in the commentary refer to the upacārasīmā (vicinity boundary), those passages were not spoken by the commentary masters in reference to the upacārasīmā, but rather in reference to the great boundary (mahāsīmā), known as the avippavāsasīmā (non-separation boundary). How is this to be understood? Because the khaṇḍasīmā (fragmentary boundary) is about to be discussed. For the mahāsīmā is indeed the counterpart (paṭiyogī) to the khaṇḍasīmā. How, then, is this matter to be known? It is to be known through the passage in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 138): 'When those who establish a samānasaṃvāsakasīmā (common-residence boundary) first designate a khaṇḍasīmā for the sake of easily performing saṅghakammas (Sangha acts) such as ordination (pabbajjā) and higher ordination (upasampadā)... When the boundaries are thus fixed, monks standing in the khaṇḍasīmā do not invalidate the formal act (kamma) of those performing it in the mahāsīmā, nor do those standing in the mahāsīmā invalidate the formal act of those performing it in the khaṇḍasīmā. But those standing in the space between the boundaries (sīmantarikā) invalidate neither.' Alternatively, this matter can be understood by the venerable ones through the passage they cited concerning the appointment of the storeroom (bhaṇḍāgāra-sammuti). How so? While appointments of individuals such as robe-receivers (cīvarapaṭiggāhaka) can be made even within the monastery (antovihāre), in the midst of the entire Sangha (sabbasaṅghamajjhe), or in the khaṇḍasīmā, the appointment of the monastery as a storeroom (bhaṇḍāgārasaṅkhātavihārasammuti) must be made specifically in the middle of the monastery (vihāramajjhe)—so it is stated in the commentary. Therein, the special reason for this distinction should be sought.

Tatrevaṃ visesakāraṇaṃ paññāyati – “aññissā sīmāya vatthu aññissā kammavācā”ti vattabbadosaparihāratthaṃ vuttaṃ. Puggalasammutiyo hi puggalassa vatthuttā yadi mahāsīmabhūte antovihāre kattukāmā honti, sabbasaṅghamajjhe taṃ vatthubhūtaṃ puggalaṃ hatthapāse katvā kareyyuṃ. Yadi khaṇḍasīmāya kattukāmā, taṃ vatthubhūtaṃ puggalaṃ khaṇḍasīmaṃ ānetvā tattha sannipatitakammappattasaṅghassa hatthapāse katvā kareyyuṃ. Ubhayathāpi yathāvuttadoso natthi, bhaṇḍāgārasammuti pana bhaṇḍāgārassa vihārattā khaṇḍasīmaṃ ānetuṃ na sakkā, tasmā yadi taṃ sammutiṃ khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ ṭhatvā kareyyuṃ, vatthu mahāsīmāyaṃ hoti, kammavācā khaṇḍasīmāyanti yathāvuttadoso hoti, tasmiñca dose sati vatthuvipannattā kammaṃ vipajjati, tasmā mahāsīmabhūtavihāramajjheyeva sā sammuti kātabbāti aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ mati, na upacārasīmāya ñattidutiyakammaṃ kātabbanti.

Here, a special reason is discerned: it is stated to avoid the fault of having to say, 'The object is in one boundary, the formal act in another.' For appointments of individuals, since the individual is the basis (vatthu), if they wish to perform it within a great boundary that is a monastery, they should perform it by bringing that individual, who is the basis, within arm's reach in the midst of the entire Saṅgha. If they wish to perform it in a fragmentary boundary, they should bring that individual, who is the basis, to the fragmentary boundary and, having assembled the Saṅgha qualified for the act, perform it within arm's reach. In both cases, the aforementioned fault does not arise. However, as for the appointment of a storeroom, since the storeroom is the monastery, it is not possible to bring it to a fragmentary boundary. Therefore, if they were to perform that appointment while standing in the fragmentary boundary, the object would be in the great boundary, and the formal act in the fragmentary boundary—thus, the aforementioned fault would arise. And when that fault exists, the act fails due to the object being defective. Therefore, that appointment should be made only within the monastery that is the great boundary—this is the opinion of the commentary teachers. A ñattidutiyakamma should not be performed in a vicinity boundary.

Athāpi evaṃ vadeyyuṃ “vihārasaddena avippavāsasīmabhūtā mahāsīmāva vuttā, na upacārasīmā”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ kathaṃ paccetabbanti? Imināyeva aṭṭhakathāvacanena. Yadi hi upacārasīmā [M 2.0121] vuttā bhaveyya, upacārasīmā nāma baddhasīmaṃ avattharitvāpi pavattā āvāsesu vā bhikkhūsu vā vaḍḍhantesu aniyamavasena vaḍḍhati, tasmā khaṇḍasīmaṃ avattharitvā pavattanato vihārena saha khaṇḍasīmā ekasīmāyeva hoti, evaṃ sati vihāre ṭhitaṃ bhaṇḍāgāraṃ khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhatvā sammannituṃ sakkā bhaveyya, na pana sakkā “khaṇḍasīmāya nisinnehi sammannituṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 343) paṭisiddhattā. Tena ñāyati “imasmiṃ [V 2.0089] ṭhāne vihārasaddena avippavāsasīmabhūtā mahāsīmā vuttā, na upacārasīmā”ti. Upacārasīmāya aniyamavasena vaḍḍhanabhāvo kathaṃ jānitabboti? “Upacārasīmā parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepena, aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānena paricchinnā hoti. Apica bhikkhūnaṃ dhuvasannipātaṭṭhānato vā pariyante ṭhitabhojanasālato vā nibaddhavasanakaāvāsato vā thāmamajjhimassa purisassa dvinnaṃ leḍḍupātānaṃ anto upacārasīmā veditabbā, sā pana āvāsesu vaḍḍhantesu vaḍḍhati, parihāyantesu parihāyati. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana ‘bhikkhūsupi vaḍḍhantesu vaḍḍhatī’ti vuttaṃ, tasmā sace vihāre sannipatitabhikkhūhi saddhiṃ ekābaddhā hutvā yojanasatampi pūretvā nisīdanti, yojanasatampi upacārasīmāva hoti, sabbesaṃ lābho pāpuṇātī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) vacanatoti.

And if they were to say, 'By the word "monastery" is meant only the great boundary, which is the non-separation boundary, not the vicinity boundary,' how is this statement to be accepted? By this very statement of the commentary. For if the vicinity boundary were meant, the vicinity boundary, even without encompassing a bound boundary, extends and grows without fixed limits when dwellings or monks increase. Therefore, since it extends without being defined by a fragmentary boundary, the fragmentary boundary would be one and the same boundary with the monastery. In such a case, it would be possible to appoint a storeroom located in the monastery while standing in the fragmentary boundary. But this is not possible because the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 343) prohibits it, stating, 'It is not permissible for those seated in a fragmentary boundary to make an appointment.' By this it is known that in this context, by the word 'monastery' is meant the great boundary, which is the non-separation boundary, not the vicinity boundary. How is the unrestricted expansion of the vicinity boundary to be known? From this statement in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379): 'The vicinity boundary is delimited by the perimeter of an enclosed monastery, or by the place suitable for enclosure for an unenclosed one. Moreover, it should be understood as extending from the monks' regular assembly place, or from the edge of the dining hall, or from a fixed dwelling place, to a distance within two clod-throws of a man of average strength. This boundary expands when the dwellings increase and contracts when they decrease. The Mahāpaccarī, however, states, “It also expands when the monks increase.” Therefore, if monks assemble in the monastery and sit together in a single continuous session, even filling a hundred leagues, the vicinity boundary extends even to a hundred leagues, and all obtain the gains.'

Yadi evaṃ upacārasīmāya kathinatthatabhāvo kasmā vuttoti? Kathinattharaṇaṃ nāma na saṅghakammaṃ, puggalakammameva hoti, tasmā vassūpanāyikakhettabhūtāya upacārasīmāya kātabbā hoti. Ñattikammavācā pana saṅghakammabhūtā, tasmā upacārasīmāya kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, suvisodhitaparisāya baddhābaddhasīmāyameva vaṭṭatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Nanu ca bho “kathinaṃ attharituṃ ke labhanti, ke na labhanti? Gaṇanavasena [M 2.0122] tāva pacchimakoṭiyā pañca janā labhanti, uddhaṃ satasahassampi, pañcannaṃ heṭṭhā na labhantī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, atha kasmā “kathinattharaṇaṃ nāma na saṅghakammaṃ, puggalakammameva hotī”ti vuttanti? “Na saṅgho kathinaṃ attharati, na gaṇo kathinaṃ attharati, puggalo kathinaṃ attharatī”ti parivāre (pari. 414) vuttattā ca apalokanakammādīnaṃ catunnaṃ saṅghakammānaṃ ṭhānesu apaviṭṭhattā ca. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana kathinatthārassa upacārabhūtaṃ kathinadānakammavācābhaṇanakālaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tasmiñhi kāle kathinadāyakā cattāro, paṭiggāhako ekoti pacchimakoṭiyā pañca honti, tato heṭṭhā na labhatīti. Ñattikammavācāya saṅghakammabhāvo kathaṃ jānitabboti? “Catunnaṃ saṅghakammānaṃ ñattidutiyakammassa navasu ṭhānesu kathinadāna”nti āgatattā, “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppanna”ntiādinā vuttattā cāti.

If so, why was it said that the spreading of the kathina occurs in the proximity boundary? The spreading of the kathina is not a Saṅgha act, but a personal act; therefore, it should be done in the proximity boundary, which is the area for undertaking the rains-residence. However, a formal act preceded by a motion is a Saṅgha act; therefore, it is not permissible to perform it in the proximity boundary. It should be understood that it is permissible only in a well-purified assembly within a bound or unbound boundary. But, sirs, it was stated in the commentary: 'Who are able to spread the kathina, and who are not? In terms of number, at the very least, five persons are able, and upwards to a hundred thousand, but fewer than five are not able.' Then why is it said, 'The spreading of the kathina is not a Saṅgha act, but a personal act'? Because it is stated in the Parivāra (Pari. 414): 'The Saṅgha does not spread the kathina, nor does a group spread the kathina, but an individual spreads the kathina,' and also because it is not included among the four types of Saṅgha acts, such as the act of declaration. However, in the commentary, this was stated with reference to the time of reciting the formal act of giving the kathina, which is preliminary to the spreading of the kathina. For at that time, there are four givers of the kathina and one receiver, making five at the minimum, and fewer than that are not able. How is it to be known that a formal act preceded by a motion is a Saṅgha act? Because it is stated: 'Among the four Saṅgha acts, the giving of the kathina is one of the nine instances for a motion-and-second act,' and because it is stated: 'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This kathina cloth has arisen for the Saṅgha,' etc.

Apare pana ācariyā “bhāsantaresu ñattīti vuttā kathinadānakammavācā atthārakiriyāya pavisati, atthārakiriyā ca upacārasīmāyaṃ kātabbā, tasmā kathinadānakammavācāpi upacārasīmāyaṃ kātabbāyevā”ti vadanti, tesaṃ ayamadhippāyo – mahāvaggapāḷiyaṃ [V 2.0090] (mahāva. 306) “evañca pana, bhikkhave, kathinaṃ attharitabba”nti ārabhitvā “byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, atthataṃ hoti kathina”nti kathinadānañattikammavācāto paṭṭhāya yāva anumodanā pāṭho āgato, parivārapāḷiyañca (pari. 412) “kathinatthāro jānitabbo”ti uddesassa niddese “sace saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, saṅghena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ, atthārakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbaṃ, anumodakena kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba”nti pucchaṃ nīharitvā “saṅghena ñattidutiyena [M 2.0123] kammena kathinatthārakassa bhikkhuno dātabbaṃ…pe… anumodāmā”ti ñattito paṭṭhāya yāva anumodanā pāṭho āgato, tasmā ñattito paṭṭhāya yāva anumodanā sabbo vidhi kathinatthārakiriyāyaṃ pavisati, tato kathinatthārakiriyāya upacārasīmāyaṃ kattabbāya sati ñattisaṅkhātakathinadānakammavācāpi upacārasīmāyaṃ kattabbāyevāti.

Other teachers, however, say: 'The formal act of giving the kathina, which in some contexts is called the “motion,” is included in the act of spreading the kathina. And since the act of spreading must be performed in the proximity boundary, therefore the formal act of giving the kathina must also be performed in the proximity boundary.' Their intention is this: In the Mahāvagga Pāḷi (Mahāva. 306), beginning with 'And thus, monks, the kathina should be spread,' and continuing with 'A competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha…pe… thus, monks, the kathina is spread,' the text runs from the formal act with motion for giving the kathina up to the approval. And in the Parivāra Pāḷi (Pari. 412), in the explanation of the summary 'The spreading of the kathina should be understood,' after raising the question, 'If a kathina cloth has arisen for the Saṅgha, how should the Saṅgha proceed? How should the spreader proceed? How should the one who approves proceed?' the text runs from the motion up to the approval: 'The Saṅgha should give it to the monk who is to spread the kathina by a motion-and-second act…pe… we approve.' Therefore, from the motion up to the approval, the entire procedure is included in the act of spreading the kathina. Consequently, since the act of spreading the kathina must be performed in the proximity boundary, the formal act of giving the kathina, which is designated as the motion, must also be performed in the proximity boundary.

Tatrevaṃ vicāraṇā kātabbā – atthārakiriyāya visuṃ anāgatāya sati “sabbo vidhi atthārakiriyāyaṃ pavisatī”ti vattabbaṃ bhaveyya, atha ca pana mahāvaggapāḷiyañca parivārapāḷiyañca atthārakiriyā visuṃ āgatāyeva, tasmā ñattisaṅkhātā kathinadānakammavācā atthārakiriyāyaṃ na pavisati, kevalaṃ atthārakiriyāya upacārabhūtattā pana tato paṭṭhāya anukkamena vuttaṃ. Yathā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sīmaṃ sammannitu”nti sīmāsammutiṃ anujānitvā “evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā”ti sīmāsammutividhiṃ dassento “paṭhamaṃ nimittā kittetabbā…pe… evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti nimittakittanena saha sīmāsammutikammavācā desitā, tattha nimittakittanaṃ sīmāsammutikammaṃ na hoti, kammavācāyeva sīmāsammutikammaṃ hoti, tathāpi sīmāsammutikammavācāya upacārabhāvato saha nimittakittanena sīmāsammutikammavācā desitā. Yathā ca upasampadākammavidhiṃ desento “paṭhamaṃ upajjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo…pe… evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti upajjhāyagāhāpanādinā saha upasampadākammaṃ desitaṃ, tattha upajjhāyagāhāpanādi upasampadākammaṃ na hoti, ñatticatutthakammavācāyeva upasampadākammaṃ hoti, tathāpi upasampadākammassa samīpe bhūtattā upajjhāyagāhāpanādinā saha ñatticatutthakammavācā desitā, evamettha kathinadānakammavācā atthārakiriyā na hoti, tathāpi [M 2.0124] atthārakiriyāya upacārabhūtattā kathinadānañattidutiyakammavācāya saha kathinatthārakiriyā desitā, tasmā kathinadānakammavācā atthārakiriyāyaṃ na pavisatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Here, the following consideration should be made: If the act of spreading were not mentioned separately, it could be said, 'The entire procedure is included in the act of spreading.' However, in the Mahāvagga Pāḷi and the Parivāra Pāḷi, the act of spreading is indeed mentioned separately. Therefore, the formal act of giving the kathina, designated as the motion, is not included in the act of spreading. It is merely stated in sequence from that point onwards because it is auxiliary to the act of spreading. Just as when the Buddha said, 'Monks, I allow you to establish a boundary,' and after allowing the establishment of a boundary, when showing the procedure for establishing a boundary by saying, 'And thus, monks, it should be established,' the formal act of establishing a boundary was taught along with the declaration of landmarks: 'First, the landmarks should be announced…pe… thus we maintain this.' In that case, the declaration of landmarks is not the act of establishing a boundary; only the formal act is the act of establishing a boundary. Nevertheless, because it is auxiliary to the formal act of establishing a boundary, the formal act of establishing a boundary was taught along with the declaration of landmarks. And just as when explaining the procedure for higher ordination, the act of higher ordination was taught along with the appointment of a preceptor, etc.: 'First, a preceptor should be appointed…pe… thus we maintain this.' In that case, the appointment of a preceptor, etc., is not the act of higher ordination; only the formal act preceded by a motion and three proclamations is the act of higher ordination. Nevertheless, because it occurs in proximity to the act of higher ordination, the formal act preceded by a motion and three proclamations was taught along with the appointment of a preceptor, etc. In the same way here, the formal act of giving the kathina is not the act of spreading. Nevertheless, because it is auxiliary to the act of spreading, the act of spreading the kathina was taught along with the motion-and-second formal act of giving the kathina. Therefore, it should be understood that the formal act of giving the kathina is not included in the act of spreading.

Atha [V 2.0091] vā ñattidutiyakammavācā ca atthāro cāti ime dve dhammā atulyakiriyā atulyakattāro atulyakammā atulyakālā ca honti, tena viññāyati “bhāsantaresu ñattīti vuttā ñattidutiyakammavācā atthārakiriyāyaṃ na pavisatī”ti. Tattha kathaṃ atulyakiriyā honti? Kammavācā dānakiriyā hoti, atthāro pannarasadhammānaṃ kāraṇabhūtā atthārakiriyā, evaṃ atulyakiriyā. Kathaṃ atulyakattāroti? Kammavācāya kattā saṅgho hoti, atthārassa kattā puggalo, evaṃ atulyakattāro honti. Kathaṃ atulyakammā honti? Kammavācāya kammaṃ kathinadussaṃ hoti, atthārassa kammaṃ kathinasaṅkhātā samūhapaññatti, evaṃ atulyakammā honti. Kathaṃ atulyakālā honti? Kathinadānakammavācā pubbakaraṇapaccuddhāraadhiṭṭhānānaṃ pubbe hoti, atthāro tesaṃ pacchā, evaṃ atulyakālā hontīti. Atha vā atthāro “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”tiādinā vacībhedasaṅkhātena ekena dhammena saṅgahito, na ñattianussāvanādinā anekehi dhammehi saṅgahito. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre (pari. 408) “atthāro ekena dhammena saṅgahito vacībhedenā”ti. Imināpi kāraṇena jānitabbaṃ “na ñatti atthāre paviṭṭhā”ti.
