Alternatively, the motion-and-second formal act and the spreading are two things that are unequal in action, unequal in agents, unequal in object, and unequal in time. From this it is understood: “The motion-and-second formal act, which in some contexts is called the ‘motion,’ is not included in the act of spreading.” How are they unequal in action? The formal act is an act of giving, while the spreading is an action that is the cause for the fifteen benefits. Thus, they are unequal in action. How are they unequal in agents? The agent of the formal act is the Saṅgha, while the agent of the spreading is an individual. Thus, they are unequal in agents. How are they unequal in object? The object of the formal act is the kathina cloth, while the object of the spreading is the collective designation called ‘kathina.’ Thus, they are unequal in object. How are they unequal in time? The formal act of giving the kathina occurs before the preliminary duties, the withdrawal, and the determination, while the spreading occurs afterward. Thus, they are unequal in time. Alternatively, the spreading is comprised of one thing—namely, the verbal utterance designated as, ‘With this outer robe, I spread the kathina’—and not by many things such as the motion and proclamations. For this is stated in the Parivāra (Pari. 408): “The spreading is comprised of one thing, the verbal utterance.” By this reason too, it should be known: “The motion is not included within the spreading.”

Aññe pana ācariyā evaṃ vadanti – “kathinatthāraṃ ke labhanti, ke na labhantīti? Gaṇanavasena tāva pacchimakoṭiyā pañca janā labhanti, uddhaṃ satasahassampi, pañcannaṃ heṭṭhā na labhantī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) āgatattā “heṭṭhimantato [M 2.0125] pañca bhikkhū kathinatthāraṃ labhanti, tato appakatarā na labhantī”ti viññāyati. “Pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatīti pacchimakoṭiyā cattāro kathinadussassa dāyakā, eko paṭiggāhakoti pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti kaṅkhāvitaraṇīṭīkāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. abhi. ṭī. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) āgatattā tasmiṃ vākye “vaṭṭatī”ti kiriyāya kattā “so kathinatthāro”ti vuccati, tasmā atthāroti iminā “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vuttaattharaṇakiriyā na adhippetā, catūhi bhikkhūhi atthārakassa bhikkhuno ñattiyā dānaṃ adhippetanti viññāyati. “Kathinatthāraṃ ke labhanti…pe… uddhaṃ satasahassanti idaṃ atthārakassa bhikkhuno saṅghassa kathinadussadānakammaṃ sandhāya vutta”nti vinayavinicchayaṭīkāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmimpi pāṭhe ñattiyā dinnaṃyeva sandhāya “pañca janā atthāraṃ labhantī”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ aṭṭhakathācariyehi vuttaṃ, “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”tiādi puggalassa attharaṇaṃ sandhāya na vuttanti ṭīkācariyassa adhippāyo. Evaṃ kaṅkhāvitaraṇīṭīkā-vinayavinicchayaṭīkākārakehi ācariyehi “ñattidutiyakammaṃ atthāro nāmā”ti [V 2.0092] vinicchitattā upacārasīmāyaṃ kathinadānañattikammavācākaraṇaṃ yuttanti viññāyatīti vadanti.

Other teachers, however, say this: “Who obtains the laying down of the Kathina, and who does not?” According to the commentary (Mahāva.Aṭṭha. 306), “By way of counting, at a minimum five individuals obtain it, and upwards to a hundred thousand, but fewer than five do not obtain it.” Thus, it is understood that “at a minimum five bhikkhus obtain the laying down of the Kathina, and fewer than that do not.” “It is valid for five individuals: at a minimum, four are the donors of the Kathina cloth, and one is the receiver—thus, it is valid for five individuals,” as stated in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-ṭīkā (Kaṅkhā.Abhi.Ṭī. Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā). In that statement, the subject of the verb “is valid” is said to be “that laying down of the Kathina.” Therefore, by the word “laying down,” the act of spreading expressed by “With this outer robe, I lay down the Kathina,” is not intended; rather, it is understood that the giving by four bhikkhus through a formal motion to the bhikkhu who is to lay down the Kathina is intended. “Who obtains the laying down of the Kathina… up to a hundred thousand”—this is said in reference to the Saṅgha’s act of giving the Kathina cloth to the bhikkhu who lays it down, as explained in the Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā. In that passage too, the commentary teachers' statement, 'five individuals obtain the laying down,' refers only to what is given through the motion; it was not spoken in reference to the individual's act of laying down, such as 'With this outer robe, I lay down the Kathina'—this is the intention of the ṭīkā teacher. Thus, since the teachers who authored the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-ṭīkā and the Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā have determined that “the ñattidutiyakamma is called the laying down,” it is understood that performing the formal act with a motion for giving the Kathina within the precincts is appropriate, they say.

Tatrevaṃ vicāraṇā kātabbā – “ñattidutiyakammaṃyeva atthāro nāmā”ti ṭīkācariyā na vadeyyuṃ. Vadeyyuṃ ce, aṭṭhakathāya viruddho siyā. Kathaṃ viruddhoti ce? “Chinnavassā vā pacchimikāya upagatā vā na labhanti, aññasmiṃ vihāre vutthavassāpi na labhantīti mahāpaccariyaṃ vutta”nti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) āgatattā “te chinnavassādayo kathinatthāraṃ na labhantī”ti viññāyati. Yadi ñattidutiyakammaṃ atthāro nāma siyā, evaṃ sati te bhikkhū ñattidutiyakammepi gaṇapūrakabhāvena appaviṭṭhā siyuṃ. Atha ca pana “purimikāya [M 2.0126] upagatānaṃ pana sabbe gaṇapūrakā hontī”ti aṭṭhakathāya (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) vuttattā te ñattidutiyakamme paviṭṭhāva honti, tasmā aṭṭhakathācariyo pañcānisaṃsahetubhūtaṃ “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”tiādikaṃ vacībhedaṃyeva “atthāro”ti vadati, na ñattidutiyakammaṃ, tasmā te chinnavassādayo pañcānisaṃsahetubhūtaṃ kathinatthāraṃ na labhanti, ñattidutiyakamme pana catuvaggasaṅghapūrakabhāvaṃ labhantīti viññāyati. Punapi vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “sace purimikāya upagatā cattāro vā honti tayo vā dve vā eko vā, itare gaṇapūrake katvā kathinaṃ attharitabba”nti. Evaṃ alabbhamānakathinatthāreyeva chinnavassādayo gaṇapūrake katvā ñattidutiyakammavācāya kathinadussaṃ dāpetvā purimikāya upagatehi kathinassa attharitabbabhāvato “ñattidutiyakammaṃyeva atthāro nāmāti ṭīkācariyā na vadeyyu”nti avacimhāti.

Herein, the following consideration should be made: The ṭīkā teachers should not say, 'The ñattidutiyakamma itself is called the laying down.' If they were to say so, it would contradict the commentary. How would it contradict? Because it is stated in the commentary (Mahāva.Aṭṭha. 306): “Those who have broken their rains-residence or entered upon the later rains-residence do not obtain it. Even those who have spent the rains-residence in another monastery do not obtain it.” Thus, it is understood that those who have broken their rains-residence, etc., do not obtain the laying down of the Kathina. If the ñattidutiyakamma were called the laying down, then those bhikkhus would not have been included to complete the quorum for the ñattidutiyakamma. However, the commentary (Mahāva.Aṭṭha. 306) states: “But of those who entered upon the earlier rains-residence, all are included as completing the quorum.” Therefore, they are indeed included in the ñattidutiyakamma. Thus, the commentary teacher says that the verbal expression, such as ‘With this outer robe, I lay down the Kathina,’ which is the cause of the five benefits, is called the “laying down,” not the ñattidutiyakamma. Therefore, those who have broken their rains-residence, etc., do not obtain the laying down of the Kathina, which is the cause of the five benefits, but they do obtain the status of completing the quorum for the fourfold Saṅgha in the ñattidutiyakamma. Furthermore, the commentary states: “If those who entered upon the earlier rains-residence are four, three, two, or even one, the others should be made to complete the quorum, and then the Kathina should be laid down.” Thus, since those who have broken their rains-residence, etc., are not eligible for the laying down of the Kathina, they are made to complete the quorum, and after the Kathina cloth is given by the recitation of the formal act with a motion, the Kathina is to be laid down by those who entered upon the earlier rains-residence; therefore, we said: “The ṭīkā teachers should not say that the ñattidutiyakamma itself is called the laying down.”

Nanu ca bho imasmimpi aṭṭhakathāvacane “itare gaṇapūrake katvā kathinaṃ attharitabba”nti vacanena catuvaggasaṅghena kattabbaṃ ñattidutiyakammaṃyeva “atthāro”ti vuttanti? Na, pubbāparavirodhato. Pubbe hi chinnavassādīnaṃ kathinaṃ attharituṃ alabbhamānabhāvo vutto, idha “ñattidutiyakammaṃ atthāro”ti vutte tesampi labbhamānabhāvo vutto bhaveyya, na aṭṭhakathācariyā pubbāparaviruddhaṃ katheyyuṃ, tasmā “katvā”ti padaṃ “attharitabba”nti padena sambajjhantena samānakālavisesanaṃ akatvā pubbakālavisesanameva katvā sambandhitabbaṃ, evaṃ sati pubbavacanenāparavacanaṃ gaṅgodakena yamunodakaṃ viya saṃsandati, pacchāpi ca “kammavācaṃ sāvetvā kathinaṃ attharāpetvā dānañca bhuñjitvā gamissantī”ti visuṃ kammavācāsāvanaṃ visuṃ kathinattharaṇaṃ [V 2.0093] pubbāparānukkamato vuttaṃ[M 2.0127], tasmā ñattidutiyakammaṃ atthāro nāma na hoti, kevalaṃ atthārassa kāraṇameva upacārameva hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kiñca bhiyyo – “na saṅgho kathinaṃ attharati, na gaṇo kathinaṃ attharati, puggalo kathinaṃ attharatī”ti parivāravacanena (pari. 414) ayamattho jānitabboti.

“But, sir, is it not the case that in this very commentary statement, the phrase ‘having made the others complete the quorum, the Kathina should be laid down’ implies that the ñattidutiyakamma, which is to be performed by the fourfold Saṅgha, is called the ‘laying down’?” No, because of the contradiction between the earlier and later statements. Earlier, it was stated that those who had broken their rains-residence, etc., were not eligible to lay down the Kathina. Here, if it were said that ‘the ñattidutiyakamma is the laying down,’ then it would be said that they too are eligible. The commentary teachers would not make contradictory statements. Therefore, the word ‘having made’ (katvā) should be connected with the word ‘should be laid down’ (attharitabba) by construing it as indicating a prior action, not a simultaneous one. When this is done, the earlier statement harmonizes with the later statement, like the waters of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā merging. Furthermore, later it is stated: ‘having had the formal act announced, having had the Kathina laid down, and having partaken of the gift, they will depart.’ Here, the announcing of the formal act and the laying down of the Kathina are mentioned separately, in sequential order. Thus, the ñattidutiyakamma is not called the laying down; it should be seen as merely the cause or the figurative basis for the laying down. Moreover, this meaning should be understood from the statement in the Parivāra: ‘The Saṅgha does not lay down the Kathina, the group does not lay down the Kathina, an individual lays down the Kathina’ (Pari. 414).

Yadi evaṃ kaṅkhāvitaraṇīṭīkā-vinayavinicchayaṭīkāsu āgatapāṭhānaṃ adhippāyo kathaṃ bhāsitabbo bhaveyya. Nanu kaṅkhāvitaraṇīṭīkāyaṃ “vaṭṭatī”ti imissā kiriyāya kattā “so kathinatthāro”ti vutto, vinayavinicchayaṭīkāyañca “kathinadussadānakamma”nti padaṃ “sandhāyā”ti kiriyāya kammaṃ, kathinatthāro…pe… idaṃ “vutta”nti kiriyāya kammaṃ hoti. Evaṃ ṭīkāsu nītatthato āgatapāṭhesu santesu “ñattidutiyakammaṃyeva atthāro nāmāti ṭīkācariyā na vadeyyu”nti na vattabbanti? Yenākārena aṭṭhakathāvacanena ṭīkāvacanañca pubbāparaaṭṭhakathāvacanañca aviruddhaṃ bhaveyya, tenākārena ṭīkāpāṭhānaṃ adhippāyo gahetabbo. Kathaṃ? Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā) “so sabbantimena paricchedena pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti āgato, tasmiṃ aṭṭhakathāvacane codakena codetabbassa atthitāya taṃ pariharituṃ “pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatīti pacchimakoṭiyā cattāro kathinadussassa dāyakā, eko paṭiggāhakoti pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti pāṭho ṭīkācariyena vutto, kathaṃ codetabbaṃ atthīti? Bho aṭṭhakathācariya “so sabbantimena paricchedena pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vutto, evaṃ sati pañcannaṃ kathinatthārakānaṃ eva so kathinatthāro vaṭṭati, na ekadviticatupuggalānanti attho āpajjati, evaṃ sati “na saṅgho kathinaṃ attharati, na gaṇo kathinaṃ attharati, puggalo kathinaṃ attharatī”ti āgatapāḷiyā virujjhanato āgamavirodho [M 2.0128] āpajjati, taṃ codanaṃ pariharanto “pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatīti pacchimakoṭiyā cattāro kathinadussassa dāyakā, eko paṭiggāhakoti pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti pāṭho ṭīkācariyena vutto. Tatthāyamadhippāyo – bho codakācariya aṭṭhakathācariyena kathinatthārakāle pañcannaṃ atthārakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasena “so sabbantimena paricchedena pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti pāṭho na vutto, atha kho saṅghena atthārakassa kathinadussadānakāle pacchimakoṭiyā cattāro kathinadussassa dāyakā, eko paṭiggāhakoti pañcannaṃ dāyakapaṭiggāhakapuggalānaṃ atthitāya so pacchā kattabbo atthāro vaṭṭati, kāraṇasampattiyā phalasampatti hoti, tasmā tasmiṃ aṭṭhakathāvacane āgamavirodho nāpajjatīti.

If this is so, how should the meaning of the passages found in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-ṭīkā and the Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā be explained? Indeed, in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-ṭīkā, the agent of the verb 'vaṭṭati' is said to be 'that kathina-spreading'. And in the Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā, the term 'kathinadussadānakamma' (the act of giving the kathina cloth) is the object of the verb 'sandhāya' (referring to), and 'kathinatthāro…pe… idaṃ' is the object of the verb 'vuttaṃ' (is said). Thus, when such passages with a definitive meaning are present in the subcommentaries, should it not be said that the subcommentary teachers would not state, 'The spreading is only the act of a motion and a second announcement'? The meaning of the subcommentary passages should be understood in such a way that it does not contradict the words of the commentary, and the earlier and later words of the commentary. How? In the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī-aṭṭhakathā (Kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. Kathinasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā), it is stated: 'It, by the final limitation, is allowable for five persons.' Because that statement in the commentary is subject to being questioned by an objector, to resolve it, the subcommentary teacher stated the passage as: '“Is allowable for five persons” means: at the final limit, four are donors of the kathina cloth, and one is the recipient—thus it is allowable for five persons.' How is it subject to being questioned? 'Venerable commentary teacher, it is stated: “It, by the final limitation, is allowable for five persons.” If so, the meaning would be that that kathina-spreading is allowable only for five kathina-spreaders, not for one, two, three, or four individuals. If so, this would contradict the canonical text which states: “The Saṅgha does not spread the kathina, a group does not spread the kathina, an individual spreads the kathina.” Thus, a contradiction with the Āgama would arise.' Rebutting that objection, the subcommentary teacher stated the passage as: '“Is allowable for five persons” means: at the final limit, four are donors of the kathina cloth, and one is the recipient—thus it is allowable for five persons.' Herein, this is the intended meaning: 'Venerable objector, the commentary teacher did not state the passage, “It, by the final limitation, is allowable for five persons,” with reference to five bhikkhus who are spreaders at the time of the kathina-spreading. Rather, at the time of the Saṅgha's giving of the kathina cloth to the spreader, because there are five individuals—at the final limit, four donors of the kathina cloth and one recipient—that spreading to be done later is allowable. Through the fulfillment of the cause, there is the fulfillment of the result. Therefore, in that statement of the commentary, no contradiction with the Āgama arises.'

Vinayavinicchayaṭīkāyampi [V 2.0094] “kathinatthāraṃ ke labhanti, ke na labhantīti? Gaṇanavasena tāva pacchimakoṭiyā pañca janā labhanti, uddhaṃ satasahassampi, pañcannaṃ heṭṭhā na labhantī”ti aṭṭhakathāvacane parehi pucchitabbassa atthitāya taṃ pucchaṃ vissajjetuṃ “idaṃ atthārakassa bhikkhuno saṅghassa kathinadussadānakammaṃ sandhāya vutta”nti pāṭho ṭīkācariyena vutto. Kathaṃ pucchitabbanti ce? Bho aṭṭhakathācariya “heṭṭhimakoṭiyā pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ kiṃ pañcānisaṃsassa kāraṇabhūtaṃ “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”tiādiatthārakiriyaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, udāhu atthārassa kāraṇabhūtaṃ kathinadussadānakammanti. Kathaṃ vissajjanāti? Bho bhadramukha “heṭṭhimakoṭiyā pañcannaṃ janānaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti idaṃ pañcānisaṃsassa kāraṇabhūtaṃ “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”tiādikaṃ atthārakiriyaṃ sandhāya aṭṭhakathācariyena na vuttaṃ, atha kho atthārassa kāraṇabhūtaṃ kathinadānakammaṃ sandhāya vuttanti[M 2.0129]. Tatrāyamadhippāyo – saṅghena atthārakassa dinnadussena eva kathinatthāro sambhavati, na ṭhitikāya laddhacīvarena vā puggalikacīvarena vā sambhavati, tañca kathinadussadānakammaṃ cattāro kathinadussadāyakā, eko paṭiggāhakoti pañcasu bhikkhūsu vijjamānesuyeva sampajjati, na tato ūnesūti pacchimakoṭiyā pañcannaṃ vaṭṭati, kāraṇasiddhiyā phalasiddhi hoti, teneva ca kāraṇena “kathinadussadānakammaṃ vutta”nti mukhyavasena avatvā “sandhāya vutta”nti upacāravasenāha. Evaṃ vutteyeva aṭṭhakathāvacanassa pubbāparavirodho natthi, aṭṭhakathāvacanena ca ṭīkāvacanaṃ viruddhaṃ na hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ, “apalokanādisaṅghakammakaraṇatthaṃ baddhasīmā bhagavatā anuññātā”ti iminā vinayalakkhaṇena ca sameti.

In the Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā as well, concerning the commentary statement: 'Who receives the spreading of the kathina, and who does not? In terms of number, at the final limit, five persons receive it, and upwards to a hundred thousand, but those below five do not receive it.' Because this was subject to being questioned by others, to answer that question, the subcommentary teacher stated: 'This was said with reference to the Saṅgha’s act of giving the kathina cloth to the bhikkhu who is the spreader.' How should it be questioned? 'Venerable commentary teacher, was this statement, “At the lower limit, it is allowable for five persons,” said with reference to the act of spreading which is the cause of the five benefits, such as “I spread the kathina with this outer robe,” or does it refer to the act of giving the kathina cloth, which is the cause for the spreading?' How should the answer be given? 'Venerable sir, the commentary teacher did not state that “at the lower limit, it is allowable for five persons” with reference to the act of spreading which is the cause of the five benefits, such as “I spread the kathina with this outer robe”; rather, it was said with reference to the act of giving the kathina cloth, which is the cause for the spreading.' Herein, this is the intended meaning: The spreading of the kathina is possible only with the cloth given by the Saṅgha to the spreader, not with a robe obtained through a formal request or with a personal robe. That act of giving the kathina cloth is accomplished only when there are five bhikkhus present: four donors of the kathina cloth and one recipient; it is not accomplished with fewer than that. Thus, at the final limit, it is allowable for five. Through the accomplishment of the cause comes the accomplishment of the result. For that very reason, instead of stating in a primary sense, 'the act of giving the kathina cloth is stated,' it is stated in a figurative sense as 'said with reference to it.' When explained this way, there is no contradiction between the earlier and later parts of the commentary, and the subcommentary does not conflict with the commentary. It also aligns with this characteristic of the Vinaya: 'A bound sīmā has been permitted by the Blessed One for performing Saṅgha acts such as proclamations.'

“Imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”tiādikā pana atthārakiriyā apalokanādīsu catūsu saṅghakammesu appaviṭṭhā, adhiṭṭhānādayo viya pañcānisaṃsalābhakāraṇabhūtā puggalakiriyāva hotīti vassūpanāyikakhettabhūtāya antoupacārasīmāya kātabbā, tasmā antoupacārasīmāyaṃ baddhasīmāya avijjamānāya bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ baddhasīmaṃ vā udakukkhepasattabbhantaralabhamānaṭṭhānaṃ vā gantvā ñattidutiyakammena kathinadussaṃ dāpetvā puna vihāraṃ āgantvā antoupacārasīmāyameva kathinattharaṇaṃ pubbācariyehi kataṃ, taṃ sukatameva hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ aggahetvā suddhaupacārasīmāyameva ñattidutiyakammaṃ kātabbanti gayhamāne sati tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamānā sissānusissā dhuvavāsatthāya vihāradānādiapalokanakammaṃ vā uposathapavāraṇādiñattikammaṃ vā sīmāsammannanādiñattidutiyakammaṃ [V 2.0095] vā upasampadādiñatticatutthakammaṃ vā upacārasīmāyameva kareyyuṃ, evaṃ karontā bhagavato [M 2.0130] sāsane mahantaṃ jaṭaṃ mahantaṃ gumbaṃ mahantaṃ visamaṃ kareyyuṃ, tasmā tamakaraṇatthaṃ yuttito ca āgamato ca anekāni kāraṇāni āharitvā kathayimhāti.

However, the act of spreading, such as 'I spread the kathina with this outer robe,' is not included among the four Saṅgha acts, such as proclamations. It is merely a personal act, like determination and so forth, which is the cause for obtaining the five benefits, and thus should be performed within the inner boundary of proximity, which is the field for the rains-residence. Therefore, if a bound sīmā is not present within the inner boundary of proximity, one should go outside the boundary of proximity to a place where a bound sīmā is established, or to a place within seven `abbhantaras` of a water-throw. There, having had the kathina cloth given through an act of motion and a second announcement, and then returning to the monastery, the spreading of the kathina should be done within the inner boundary of proximity itself. This was done by the ancient teachers, and it should be seen as indeed well done. If, failing to grasp this, one insists that an act of motion and a second announcement should be done only within a pure boundary of proximity, then their disciples and grand-disciples, following the views of those venerable ones, might—for the sake of permanent residence, the giving of monasteries, etc.—perform an act of proclamation, or an act of motion for the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā, or an act of motion and a second announcement for consecrating a sīmā, or an act of motion and three announcements for higher ordination, etc., within the boundary of proximity itself. By doing so, they would create a great tangle, a great thicket, and a great unevenness in the Blessed One’s Dispensation. Therefore, to prevent this, we have brought forth and explained many reasons from logic and from scripture.

Sāsane gāravaṃ katvā, saddhammassānulomato;

Mayā kataṃ vinicchayaṃ, sammā cintentu sādhavo.

Having paid reverence to the Dispensation, in accordance with the true Dhamma, let the virtuous rightly consider the judgment I have made.

Punappunaṃ vicintetvā, yuttaṃ ce hoti gaṇhantu;

No ce yuttaṃ mā gaṇhantu, sammāsambuddhasāvakāti.

Having repeatedly reflected, if it is suitable, let them accept it; if it is not suitable, let them not accept it—such are the disciples of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Ito parānipi kāraṇasādhakāni āharanti ācariyā, tesaṃ paṭivacanena ativitthāro bhavissati, upacārasīmāya catunnaṃ saṅghakammānaṃ kataṭṭhānabhāvo pubbe vuttova, tasmā taṃ vacanaṃ manasi katvā saṃsayaṃ akatvā dhāretabboti.

Teachers bring forth even further justifying reasons. Responding to them would lead to excessive elaboration. The fact that the four Sangha acts are performed within the boundary of proximity has already been stated earlier. Therefore, that statement, having been taken to mind, should be retained without doubt.

“Imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”ti vācā bhinditabbāti kiṃ ettakena vacībhedena kathinaṃ atthataṃ hoti, udāhu añño koci kāyavikāro kātabbo? Na kātabbo. Ettakeneva hi vacībhedena atthataṃ hoti, kathinaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre (pari. 408) “atthāro ekena dhammena saṅgahito vacībhedenā”ti.

“I spread the Kathina with this outer robe”—this statement must be spoken aloud. Is the Kathina spread merely by this verbal declaration, or is some other physical action required? No other action is required. For the Kathina is spread by this verbal declaration alone. As it is stated in the Parivāra (Pari. 408): “The spreading is accomplished by a single factor, the verbal declaration.”

Evaṃ kathinatthāraṃ dassetvā anumodāpanaanumodane dassento “tena kathinatthārakenā”tiādimāha. Tattha yena bhikkhunā “imāya saṅghāṭiyā kathinaṃ attharāmī”tiādinā vacībhedena kathinaṃ atthataṃ, tena “kathinassa atthārā pannarasa dhammā jāyantī”ti parivāre (pari. 403) āgatattā kathinatthārena saheva pañca ānisaṃsā āgatā, atha kasmā saṅghaṃ anumodāpetīti? Kiñcāpi atthārakassa bhikkhuno pañca ānisaṃsā āgatā, saṅghassa pana anāgatā, tasmā saṅghassa ca āgamanatthaṃ saṅghaṃ anumodāpeti, saṅgho [M 2.0131] ca anumodanaṃ karoti, evaṃ kate ubhinnampi ānisaṃsā āgatā honti. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre (pari. 403) “dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ atthārakassa ca anumodakassa cā”ti. Ettha ca kathinatthārakabhikkhuto vuḍḍhataro bhikkhu tasmiṃ [V 2.0096] saṅghe atthi, idha vuttanayena atthārakena “bhante”ti vattabbaṃ, anumodakena “āvuso”ti. Yadi pana kathinatthārako bhikkhu sabbesaṃ vuḍḍhataro hoti, tena “āvuso”ti vattabbaṃ, itarehi “bhante”ti, evaṃ sesanayadvayepi. Evaṃ sabbesaṃ atthataṃ hoti kathinanti. Imesu pana saṅghapuggalesu ye tasmiṃ vihāre purimikāya vassaṃ upagantvā paṭhamapavāraṇāya pavāritā, teyeva anumodituṃ labhanti, chinnavassā vā pacchimikāya upagatā vā aññasmiṃ vihāre vutthavassā vā na labhanti, ananumodantāpi ānisaṃsaṃ na labhanti.

Having thus shown the spreading of the Kathina, he then presents the act of causing to rejoice and the rejoicing itself, saying, “By that spreader of the Kathina,” and so on. Herein, for the bhikkhu who spread the Kathina by the verbal declaration, “I spread the Kathina with this outer robe,” and so forth, five advantages accrue along with the spreading of the Kathina itself, since it is stated in the Parivāra (Pari. 403): “From the spreading of the Kathina, fifteen qualities arise.” But why does he cause the Sangha to rejoice? Although five advantages accrue to the bhikkhu who spreads it, they do not yet accrue to the Sangha. Therefore, in order for the Sangha to obtain them as well, he causes the Sangha to rejoice, and the Sangha performs the rejoicing. When this is done, advantages accrue to both. For it is stated in the Parivāra (Pari. 403): “The Kathina is spread for two persons: for the spreader and for the rejoicer.” Here, if there is a bhikkhu in that Sangha who is senior to the bhikkhu spreading the Kathina, the spreader should say, “Bhante,” and the rejoicer should say, “Āvuso.” However, if the bhikkhu spreading the Kathina is the most senior of all, he should say, “Āvuso,” and the others should say, “Bhante.” The same applies in the remaining two cases. Thus, the Kathina is spread for all. Among these members of the Sangha, only those who undertook the rains-residence in that monastery for the earlier period and performed the first Pavāraṇā are entitled to rejoice. Those who broke their rains-residence, or undertook it for the later period, or completed their rains-residence in another monastery are not entitled. And those who do not rejoice do not gain the advantages.

Evaṃ kathinatthāraṃ dassetvā idāni cīvaravibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ “evaṃ atthate pana kathine”tiādimāha. Tattha sace kathinacīvarena saddhiṃ ābhataṃ ānisaṃsanti iminā ekaṃ atthatacīvarameva kathinacīvaraṃ nāma, tato aññaṃ tena saddhiṃ ābhataṃ sabbaṃ cīvaraṃ kathinānisaṃsacīvaraṃ nāmāti dasseti. Vakkhati hi “avasesakathinānisaṃse balavavatthānī”tiādi. Tena ñāyati “vatthameva idha ānisaṃso nāma, na aggho, kathinasāṭakena saddhiṃ ābhatānaṃ aññasāṭakānaṃ bahulavasena attharitabbaṃ, na kathinasāṭakassa mahagghavasenā”ti. Bhikkhusaṅgho anissaro, atthatakathino bhikkhuyeva issaro. Kasmā? Dāyakehi vicāritattā. Bhikkhusaṅgho issaro, kasmā? Dāyakehi avicāritattā, mūlakathinassa ca saṅghe dinnattā. Avasesakathinānisaṃseti [M 2.0132] tassa dinnavatthehi avasesakathinānisaṃsavatthe. Balavavatthānīti attharitabbakathinasāṭakaṃyeva ahataṃ vā ahatakappaṃ vā dātuṃ vaṭṭati, ānisaṃsacīvaraṃ pana yathāsatti yathābalaṃ purāṇaṃ vā abhinavaṃ vā dubbalaṃ vā balavaṃ vā dātuṃ vaṭṭati, tasmā tesu dubbalavatthe ṭhitikāya dinne laddhabhikkhussa upakārakaṃ na hoti, tasmā upakāraṇayoggāni balavavatthāni dātabbānīti adhippāyo. Vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya dātabbānīti yattakā bhikkhū vassāvāsikacīvaraṃ labhiṃsu, te ṭhapetvā tesaṃ heṭṭhato paṭṭhāya yathākkamaṃ dātabbāni. Therāsanato paṭṭhāyāti yattakā bhikkhū tissaṃ kathinatthatasīmāyaṃ santi, tesu jeṭṭhakabhikkhuto paṭṭhāya dātabbāni. Āsanaggahaṇaṃ pana yathāvuḍḍhaṃ nisinne sandhāya kataṃ. Etena vassāvāsikakathinānisaṃsānaṃ samānagatikataṃ dīpeti. Garubhaṇḍaṃ na bhājetabbanti kathinasāṭakena saddhiṃ ābhatesu mañcapīṭhādikaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ na bhājetabbaṃ, saṅghikavaseneva paribhuñjitabbanti attho. Tattha garubhaṇḍavinicchayo anantarakathāyaṃ āvi bhavissati.

Having thus shown the spreading of the Kathina, he now speaks beginning with, “Thus, when the Kathina is spread,” in order to show the division of robes. Here, by “if the benefit is what is brought along with the Kathina robe,” it is shown that only one robe, the spread robe itself, is called the Kathina robe, and all other robes brought along with it are called Kathina-benefit robes. For it will be said, “the remaining Kathina-benefits are strong cloths,” and so on. From this it is understood that “here, the benefit refers to the cloth itself, not its value; the other cloths brought along with the Kathina cloth should be distributed based on their quantity, not on the high value of the Kathina cloth.” The Bhikkhu-Sangha has no authority; only the bhikkhu who has spread the Kathina has authority. Why? Because it has been designated by the donors. The Bhikkhu-Sangha has authority. Why? Because it has not been designated by the donors, and the original Kathina was given to the Sangha. “The remaining Kathina-benefits” means the remaining Kathina-benefit cloths from the cloths given to him. “Strong cloths” means that the Kathina cloth to be spread is suitable to be given whether new or nearly new; but the benefit-robe, according to one’s ability and strength, can be given whether it is old or new, weak or strong. Therefore, if weak cloths are given with the idea that they will last, they are not beneficial to the receiving bhikkhu. Hence, the intention is that strong cloths suitable for use should be given. “They should be given according to the rains-residence seniority” means that having set aside as many bhikkhus as have received the rains-residence robes, they should be given in order starting from those below them. “Starting from the senior seat” means that they should be given starting from the most senior bhikkhu among as many bhikkhus as are present within the boundary where the Kathina has been spread. However, the mention of the seat is with reference to those seated according to seniority. This indicates that the rains-residence and Kathina benefits follow the same procedure. “Heavy goods should not be divided” means that among the items brought with the Kathina cloth, heavy goods such as beds and chairs should not be divided but should be used as the property of the Sangha. Herein, the ruling on heavy goods will become clear in the immediately following section.

Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne vattabbaṃ atthi. Kathaṃ? Idāni bhikkhū kathinānisaṃsacīvaraṃ kusapātaṃ katvā [V 2.0097] vibhajanti, taṃ yuttaṃ viya na dissatīti. Kasmāti ce? “Avasesakathinānisaṃse balavavatthāni vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya dātabbāni, ṭhitikāya abhāve therāsanato paṭṭhāya dātabbānī”ti vacanatoti. Evaṃ sante kattha kusapāto kātabboti? Bhaṇḍāgāre ṭhapitacīvareti. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Ussannaṃ hotīti bahu rāsikataṃ hoti, bhaṇḍāgāraṃ na gaṇhāti. Sammukhībhūtenāti antoupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitena. Bhājetunti kālaṃ ghosāpetvā paṭipāṭiyā bhājetuṃ…pe… evaṃ ṭhapitesu cīvarapaṭivīsesu kuso pātetabbo”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ [M 2.0133] (mahāva. aṭṭha. 343) vuttattā, tasmā imissaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva bhājetabbanti amhākaṃ khanti.

Now, in this context, there is something to be said. How so? Nowadays, bhikkhus divide the Kathina-benefit robe by casting lots, and this does not seem proper. Why is that? Because of the saying: “The remaining Kathina-benefits, being strong cloths, should be given according to rains-residence seniority. If there is no seniority, they should be given starting from the senior seat.” If that is the case, where should lots be cast? On the robes kept in the storehouse. How is this known? Because it is stated in the commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 343): “‘It is excessive’ means there is a large quantity piled up, and the storehouse cannot hold it. ‘By one who is present’ means by one standing within the boundary of the enclosure. ‘To distribute’ means having announced the time, one should distribute in order… Thus, a lot should be cast upon the portions of robes set aside in this way.” Therefore, they should be distributed according to the method explained in this commentary—this is our conviction.

Ekacce pana bhikkhū ekekassa ekekasmiṃ cīvare appahonte cīvaraṃ parivattetvā akappiyavatthuṃ gahetvā bhājenti, taṃ atioḷārikameva. Aññepi ekaccānaṃ cīvarānaṃ mahagghatāya ekaccānaṃ appagghatāya samagghaṃ kātuṃ na sakkāti tatheva karonti, tampi oḷārikameva. Tattha hi akappiyavatthunā parivattanepi tassa vicāraṇepi bhāgaggahaṇepi āpattiyeva hoti. Eke “kathinaṃ nāma dubbicāraṇīya”nti vatvā attharaṇaṃ na karonti, puggalikavaseneva yathājjhāsayaṃ vicārenti, taṃ pana yadi dāyakehi puggalasseva dinnaṃ, puggalena ca saṅghassa apariccajitaṃ, evaṃ sati attano santakattā yuttaṃ viya dissati. Yadi pana saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā dinnaṃ, puggalassa dinnepi saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā pariccajitaṃ, evaṃ sante saṅghagaṇānaṃ santakattā ayuttaṃ bhaveyya. Apare pana kathinavasena paṭiggahite vicāretuṃ dukkaranti maññamānā “na mayaṃ kathinavasena paṭiggaṇhāma, vassāvāsikabhāveneva paṭiggaṇhāmā”ti vatvā yathāruci vicārenti, tampi ayuttaṃ. Vassāvāsikampi hi saṅghassa dinnaṃ saṅghikaṃ hotiyeva, puggalassa dinnaṃ puggalikaṃ. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Sace pana tesaṃ senāsane paṃsukūliko vasati, āgatañca taṃ disvā ‘tumhākaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ demā’ti vadanti, tena saṅghassa ācikkhitabbaṃ. Sace tāni kulāni saṅghassa dātuṃ na icchanti, ‘tumhākaṃyeva demā’ti vadanti, sabhāgo bhikkhu ‘vattaṃ katvā gaṇhāhī’ti vattabbo, paṃsukūlikassa panetaṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318; vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 219) vuttattā.

However, some bhikkhus, when a single robe is insufficient for each one, exchange robes and take unallowable material to divide among themselves—that is extremely coarse. Others, because some robes are of high value and others of low value, cannot equalize the value and do the same—that too is coarse. For in such cases, whether exchanging with unallowable material, deliberating over it, or taking a share, an offense is incurred. Some, saying, “The Kathina is difficult to administer,” do not establish it but administer it individually according to their own inclination. However, if it was given by the donors to an individual and that individual has not relinquished it to the Sangha, then it may seem proper as belonging to him. But if it was given to the Sangha or a group, or even if given to an individual but relinquished to the Sangha or a group, then, since it belongs to the Sangha or group, it would be improper. Others, thinking it difficult to administer what was received through the Kathina, say, “We do not receive it through the Kathina, but as rains-residence requisites,” and administer it as they please—that too is improper. For even rains-residence requisites, if given to the Sangha, are indeed Sangha property; if given to an individual, they are individual property. How is this known? Because it is stated in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 318; Vinaya Saṅgaha Aṭṭhakathā 219): “If, however, a rag-robe wearer is dwelling in their lodging, and having seen him, donors arrive and say, ‘We give this as rains-residence requisites to you,’ then it should be declared to the Sangha by him. If those families do not wish to give it to the Sangha but say, ‘We give it only to you,’ then a bhikkhu who has a share should be told, ‘Having performed the customary duty, take it.’ But this is not allowable for a rag-robe wearer.”

Vassāvāsikaṃ [M 2.0134] duvidhaṃ saddhādeyyatatruppādavasena. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) “iti [V 2.0098] saddhādeyye dāyakamanussā pucchitabbā, tatruppāde pana kappiyakārakā pucchitabbā”ti. Saddhādeyyavassāvāsikampi savihārāvihāravasena duvidhaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) “mahāpadumatthero panāha na evaṃ kātabbaṃ. Manussā hi attano āvāsapaṭijagganatthāya paccayaṃ denti, tasmā aññehi bhikkhūhi tattha pavisitabba”nti, “yesaṃ pana senāsanaṃ natthi, kevalaṃ paccayameva denti, tesaṃ paccayaṃ avassāvāsike senāsane gāhetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti ca. Tatruppādavassāvāsikaṃ nāma kappiyakārakānaṃ hatthe kappiyavatthupaabhuñjanatthāya dinnavatthuto nibbattaṃ. Vuttampi cetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) “kappiyakārakānañhi hatthe ‘kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ paribhuñjathā’ti dinnavatthuto yaṃ yaṃ kappiyaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ paribhuñjituṃ anuññāta”nti. Evaṃ vassāvāsikacīvarampi pubbe yebhuyyena saṅghasseva denti, tasmā “kathinacīvaraṃ demā”ti vutte kathinacīvarabhāvena paṭiggahetabbaṃ, “vassāvāsikaṃ demā”ti vutte vassāvāsikacīvarabhāveneva paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Kasmā? “Yathā dāyakā vadanti, tathā paṭipajjitabba”nti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 325) vacanato.

The rains-residence offering is of two kinds: by way of a gift of faith and by way of what arises from provision. As stated in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 318): "For offerings given out of faith, the donors should be asked; but for those arising from provision, the attendants should be asked." The rains-residence offering given out of faith is also of two kinds: with a dwelling or without a dwelling. As mentioned in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 318): "The Elder Mahāpaduma, however, said: 'It should not be done this way. For people give requisites for the purpose of maintaining their own dwelling; therefore, other bhikkhus should enter there.' But for those who have no lodging and give only requisites, it is permissible to accept those requisites even in a non-rains-residence dwelling." The rains-residence offering arising from provision refers to what arises from items given into the hands of the attendants for the purpose of using allowable items. As stated in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 318): "Whatever is allowable, from items given into the hands of the attendants with the words, 'Use these allowable items,' all of it is permitted to be used." Similarly, the rains-residence robe was mostly given to the Sangha in the past. Therefore, when it is said, "We give the Kathina robe," it should be accepted as a Kathina robe. When it is said, "We give the rains-residence robe," it should be accepted as a rains-residence robe. Why? Because of the statement (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 325): "One should act in accordance with what the donors say."

Kiñci avatvā hatthe vā pādamūle vā ṭhapetvā gate kiṃ kātabbanti? Tattha sace “idaṃ vatthu cetiyassa vā saṅghassa vā parapuggalassa vā atthāya pariṇata”nti jāneyya, tesaṃ atthāya paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Atha “mamatthāya pariṇata”nti jāneyya, attano atthāya paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ parivāre (pari. 329) “nava adhammikadānānī”tiādi. Atha na kiñci jāneyya, attano hatthe vā pādamūle vā kiñci avatvā ṭhapitaṃ tasseva puggalikaṃ hoti. Na hi cetiyādīnaṃ atthāya pariṇataṃ [M 2.0135] kiñci avatvā bhikkhussa hatthe vā pādamūle vā ṭhapetīti. Vuttañhetaṃ samantapāsādikāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) “puggalassa detīti ‘imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī’ti evaṃ parammukhā vā pādamūle ṭhapetvā ‘imaṃ, bhante, tumhākaṃ dammī’ti evaṃ sammukhā vā detī”tiādi.

If someone leaves something without saying anything, placing it in one's hand or at one's feet, and then departs, what should be done? In this case, if one knows, "This item is intended for the shrine, the Sangha, or another individual," then it should be accepted for their benefit. But if one knows, "This is intended for me," then it should be accepted for one's own benefit. As stated in the Parivāra (Pari. 329): "There are nine kinds of improper gifts," and so on. However, if one does not know anything, whatever is left without a word in one's hand or at one's feet becomes the personal property of that individual. For nothing intended for the shrine, etc., is placed in a bhikkhu's hand or at his feet without a word being spoken. As stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 379): 'Giving to an individual means one gives either in their absence, saying, “I give this robe to so-and-so,” and placing it at their feet, or one gives in their presence, saying, “Venerable, I give this to you,”' and so on.

“Imissaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva bhājetabba”nti vuttaṃ, kathaṃ bhājetabbanti? “Avasesakathinānisaṃse balavavatthāni vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya dātabbānī”ti vuttattā ye bhikkhū imasmiṃ vasse vassāvāsikaṃ na labhiṃsu, tesaṃ heṭṭhato paṭṭhāya ekekaṃ cīvaraṃ vā sāṭakaṃ vā dātabbaṃ. Atha cīvarānaṃ vā sāṭakānaṃ vā avasiṭṭhesu santesu puna therāsanato paṭṭhāya dutiyabhāgo dātabbo. Tato cīvaresu vā sāṭakesu vā khīṇesu ye labhanti, tesu pacchimassa [V 2.0099] vassādīni sallakkhetabbāni. Na kevalaṃ tasmiṃ kathinatthatadivase dinnadussāni eva kathinānisaṃsāni nāma honti, atha kho yāva kathinassa ubbhārā saṅghaṃ uddissa dinnacīvarānipi saṅghikena tatruppādena ārāmikehi ābhatacīvarānipi kathinānisaṃsāniyeva honti. Tasmā tādisesu cīvaresu uppajjamānesu yathāvuttasallakkhitavassassa bhikkhuno heṭṭhato paṭṭhāya punappunaṃ gāhetabbaṃ. “Ṭhitikāya abhāve therāsanato paṭṭhāya dātabbānī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) vacanato tasmiṃ vasse vassāvāsikacīvarānaṃ anuppajjanato vā uppajjamānesupi ṭhitikāya agāhāpanato vā vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya abhāve sati laddhabbakathinānisaṃse tassaṃ upacārasīmāyaṃ sabbe bhikkhū paṭipāṭiyā nisīdāpetvā therāsanato paṭṭhāya ṭhitikaṃ katvā ekekassa bhikkhuno ekekaṃ cīvaraṃ vā sāṭakaṃ vā dātabbaṃ. Saṅghanavakassa [M 2.0136] dānakālepi mahātherā āgacchanti, “bhante, vīsativassānaṃ dīyati, tumhākaṃ ṭhitikā atikkantā”ti na vattabbā, ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā tesaṃ datvā pacchā ṭhitikāya dātabbaṃ. Dutiyabhāge pana therāsanaṃ āruḷhe pacchā āgatānaṃ paṭhamabhāgo na pāpuṇāti, dutiyabhāgato vassaggena dātabbo. Ayaṃ ṭhitikāvicāro catupaccayabhājanakathāto (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 202) gahetabboti.

It is said, 'It should be distributed in the manner explained in this commentary.' How, then, should it be distributed? Since it is said, 'The remaining Kathina benefits, being strong cloths, should be given according to the rains-residence seniority,' one robe or one cloth should be given to each of those bhikkhus who did not receive a rains-residence robe during this rains-season, starting from the most junior. If robes or cloths are still remaining, then starting from the seat of the elders, a second portion should be given. When the robes or cloths are exhausted, the rains-residence seniority of the last recipient should be noted. Not only the cloths given on the day of the spreading of the Kathina are considered Kathina benefits, but also any robes given for the Sangha up until the withdrawal of the Kathina, as well as robes brought by monastery attendants that have arisen from Sangha property—all these are indeed Kathina benefits. Therefore, whenever such robes arise, they should be repeatedly given, starting from below the bhikkhu whose rains-residence was noted as stated. Due to the statement, 'In the absence of established seniority, distribution should begin from the seat of the elders' (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 306), if in that year rains-residence robes do not arise, or even if they arise but seniority is not established for their acceptance, then in the absence of rains-residence seniority, the Kathina benefits to be received should be distributed within that surrounding boundary. All bhikkhus should be seated in order, and starting from the seat of the elders, establishing seniority, one robe or one cloth should be given to each bhikkhu. Even at the time of giving to the most junior in the Sangha, if great elders arrive, it should not be said, 'Venerable, it is being given to those of twenty vassas; your turn according to seniority has passed.' Instead, setting aside the seniority, they should be given to them, and afterwards, distribution should proceed according to seniority. However, in the second portion, for those who arrive later, after the distribution has reached the elder's seat, the first portion is not obtained; it should be given from the second portion according to the seniority of vassas. This consideration of seniority should be understood from the discussion on the distribution of the four requisites (Vi. Saṅga. Aṭṭha. 202).

Nanu ca bho ekaccāni kathinānisaṃsacīvarāni mahagghāni, ekaccāni appagghāni honti, kathaṃ ekekassa ekekasmiṃ dinne agghasamattaṃ bhaveyyāti? Vuccate – bhaṇḍāgāracīvarabhājane agghasamattaṃ icchitabbaṃ. Tathā hi vuttaṃ cīvarakkhandhake (mahāva. 343) “tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa bhaṇḍāgāre cīvaraṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetuṃ…pe… atha kho cīvarabhājakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi ‘kathaṃ nu kho cīvaraṃ bhājetabba’nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ uccinitvā tulayitvā vaṇṇāvaṇṇaṃ katvā bhikkhū gaṇetvā vaggaṃ bandhitvā cīvarapaṭivīsaṃ ṭhapetu”nti. Aṭṭhakathāyañca (mahāva. aṭṭha. 343) “uccinitvāti ‘idaṃ thūlaṃ, idaṃ saṇhaṃ, idaṃ ghanaṃ, idaṃ tanukaṃ, idaṃ paribhuttaṃ, idaṃ aparibhuttaṃ, idaṃ dīghato ettakaṃ, puthulato ettaka’nti evaṃ vatthāni vicinitvā. Tulayitvāti ‘idaṃ ettakaṃ agghati, idaṃ ettaka’nti evaṃ agghaparicchedaṃ katvā. Vaṇṇāvaṇṇaṃ katvāti sace sabbesaṃ ekekameva dasadasaagghanakaṃ pāpuṇāti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce pāpuṇāti, yaṃ nava vā aṭṭha vā agghati, taṃ aññena ekaagghanakena ca dviagghanakena ca saddhiṃ bandhitvā etena upāyena [V 2.0100] same paṭivīse ṭhapetvāti attho[M 2.0137]. Bhikkhū gaṇetvā vaggaṃ bandhitvāti sace ekekassa dīyamāne divaso na pahoti, dasa dasa bhikkhū gaṇetvā dasa dasa cīvarapaṭivīse ekavaggaṃ bandhitvā ekaṃ bhaṇḍikaṃ katvā evaṃ cīvarapaṭivīsaṃ ṭhapetuṃ anujānāmīti attho. Evaṃ ṭhapitesu cīvarapaṭivīsesu kuso pātetabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Tena ñāyati “bhaṇḍāgāracīvarabhājane agghasamattaṃ icchitabbaṃ, kusapāto ca kātabbo”ti.

“But, sir, some Kathina-privilege robes are very valuable, while others are of little value. How can each monk receive an equal share when one is given to each?” It is said—equal value should be sought in the distribution of robes from the storehouse. For it is stated in the Cīvarakkhandhaka (Mahāvagga 343): “At that time, the Sangha’s storehouse had an excess of robes. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘I allow, monks, the Sangha, being assembled, to distribute them….’ Then it occurred to the monks distributing the robes, ‘How should the robes be distributed?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘I allow, monks, first to sort them, value them, grade them by quality, count the monks, form groups, and set aside portions of robes.’” And in the commentary (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 343): “‘Sorting them’ means examining the cloths thus: ‘This is coarse, this is fine, this is thick, this is thin, this is used, this is unused, this is so long, this is so wide.’ ‘Valuing them’ means determining their value thus: ‘This is worth so much, this is worth so much.’ ‘Grading them by quality’ means if each portion for all monks comes to ten units of value, that is good. If it does not, then what is worth nine or eight units should be bundled with another worth one or two units; by this method, they should be set aside in equal portions. ‘Counting the monks and forming groups’ means if the day is not sufficient when giving to each one, I allow you to count the monks in groups of ten, bind ten portions of robes into one group, make one bundle, and thus set aside the robe portions. When the robe portions are set aside in this way, lots should be cast.” Thus, it is known that “in the distribution of robes from the storehouse, equal value should be sought, and lots should be cast.”

Imasmiṃ pana kathinānisaṃsacīvarabhājane agghasamattaṃ na icchitabbaṃ, kusapāto ca na kātabbo. Tathā hi vuttaṃ kathinakkhandhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) “evaṃ atthate pana kathine sace kathinacīvarena saddhiṃ ābhataṃ ānisaṃsaṃ dāyakā ‘yena amhākaṃ kathinaṃ gahitaṃ, tasseva demā’ti denti, bhikkhusaṅgho anissaro. Atha avicāretvāva datvā gacchanti, bhikkhusaṅgho issaro, tasmā sace kathinatthārakassa sesacīvarānipi dubbalāni honti, saṅghena apaloketvā tesampi atthāya vatthāni dātabbāni, kammavācā pana ekāyeva vaṭṭati. Avasesakathinānisaṃse balavavatthāni vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya dātabbāni. Ṭhitikāya abhāve therāsanato paṭṭhāya dātabbāni”icceva vuttaṃ, na vuttaṃ “agghaparicchedaṃ katvā”ti vā “kusapāto kātabbo”ti vā. Tena ñāyati “kathinānisaṃsacīvarāni vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya vā vuḍḍhatarato vā paṭṭhāyeva dātabbāni, neva agghasamattaṃ kātabbaṃ, na kuso pātetabbo”ti.

However, in this distribution of Kathina-privilege robes, equal value should not be sought, and lots should not be cast. For it is stated in the Kathinakkhandhaka Commentary (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 306): “Now, when the Kathina has been spread thus, if the donors, bringing the privilege-robes along with the Kathina robe, give them saying, ‘We give these to the one who received our Kathina,’ the Sangha of monks has no authority. But if they give without specifying and then depart, the Sangha of monks has authority. Therefore, if the remaining robes of the monk who spread the Kathina are also weak, the Sangha, having announced it, should give cloths for the sake of those robes as well, but only one formal act is proper. The remaining Kathina-privilege robes, being strong cloths, should be given according to the seniority of the rains-residence. In the absence of such seniority, they should be given starting from the seat of the elders.” This is what is stated; it is not stated that “the value should be determined” or that “lots should be cast.” From this it is known that “Kathina-privilege robes should be given according to the seniority of the rains-residence or starting from the most senior; equal value should not be established, nor should lots be cast.”

Idāni pana vassāvāsikabhāvena adinnattā vassāvāsikaṭhitikāya akatattā ca kathinatthatacīvarato ca kathinatthārakassa avasesacīvaratthāya dinnavatthato ca avasesakathinānisaṃse balavavatthāni vuḍḍhatarato paṭṭhāya ekassa bhikkhussa ekaṃ vatthaṃ dātabbaṃ, tesu pana varaṃ varaṃ vuḍḍhassa dātabbaṃ[M 2.0138]. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Pacchimavassūpanāyikadivase pana sace kālaṃ ghosetvā sannipatite saṅghe koci dasahatthaṃ vatthaṃ āharitvā vassāvāsikaṃ deti, āgantuko sace bhikkhusaṅghatthero hoti, tassa dātabbaṃ. Navako ce hoti, sammatena bhikkhunā saṅghatthero vattabbo ‘sace, bhante, icchatha, paṭhamabhāgaṃ muñcitvā idaṃ vatthaṃ gaṇhathā’ti. Amuñcantassa na dātabbaṃ. Sace pana pubbe gāhitaṃ muñcitvā gaṇhāti, dātabbaṃ. Eteneva upāyena dutiyattherato paṭṭhāya parivattetvā pattaṭṭhāne āgantukassa dātabbaṃ. Sace paṭhamavassūpagatā dve tīṇi cattāri pañca vā vatthāni alatthuṃ, laddhaṃ laddhaṃ eteneva upāyena vissajjāpetvā yāva āgantukassa samakaṃ hoti, tāva dātabbaṃ. Tena pana samake laddhe avasiṭṭho anubhāgo therāsane dātabbo”ti [V 2.0101] senāsanakkhandhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 318) vacanato taṃsaṃvaṇṇanābhūtāyaṃ vimativinodaniyañca (vi. vi. ṭī. cūḷavagga 2.318) “āgantuko sace bhikkhūti cīvare gāhite pacchā āgato āgantuko bhikkhu. Pattaṭṭhāneti vassaggena pattaṭṭhāne. Paṭhamavassūpagatāti āgantukassa āgamanato puretarameva pacchimikāya vassūpanāyikāya vassūpagatā. Laddhaṃ laddhanti dāyakānaṃ santikā āgatāgatasāṭaka”nti vacanato, vajirabuddhiṭīkāyañca (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 318) “paṭhamabhāgaṃ muñcitvāti idaṃ ce paṭhamagāhitavatthuto mahagghaṃ hotīti likhita”nti vacanato ca viññāyati. Evaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ ṭīkāsu ca vassāvāsikadāne pacchā ābhataṃ mahagghavatthaṃ mahātherato paṭṭhāya parivattetvā tehi anicchitaṃyeva vassaggena pattassa pacchā āgatassa bhikkhuno dātabbabhāvassa vuttattā varaṃ varaṃ vuḍḍhassa dātabbanti viññāyati.

Now, regarding the strong cloths among the remaining Kathina-privileges—those not given as rains-residence gifts, for which a rains-residence rule was not established, from the Kathina-spreading robe, and from the cloth given for the remaining robes of the Kathina-spreader—one cloth should be given to each monk, starting from the most senior. Among these, the very best should be given to the most senior. How is this known? From the Senāsana Khandhaka Commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 318): “On the day of the later undertaking of the rains-residence, if, after the time has been announced and the Sangha has assembled, someone brings a cloth ten cubits long and offers it as a rains-residence gift, and if an incoming monk is the elder of the Sangha, it should be given to him. If he is a junior, the elder of the Sangha should be told by an appointed monk: ‘Venerable sir, if you wish, relinquish the first share and take this cloth.’ It should not be given to one who does not relinquish it. But if he relinquishes what was previously accepted and takes it, it should be given. By this same method, starting from the second elder, it should be offered in exchange down the line and given to the incoming monk at his turn. If those who undertook the first rains-residence have received two, three, four, or five cloths, each one received should be made to be relinquished by this method until the share is equal for the incoming monk; that much should be given. When he has received an equal share, the remaining portion should be given at the seat of the elders.” And from the Vimativinodanī (Vinayavinicchaya Ṭīkā, Cūḷavagga 2.318), which is a commentary on that: “‘An incoming monk’ means a monk who has arrived after the robe was accepted. ‘At his turn’ means at the place reached according to rains-residence seniority. ‘Those who undertook the first rains-residence’ means those who undertook the rains-residence on the earlier date, before the arrival of the incoming monk. ‘Each one received’ means the cloths that came one after another from the donors.” And from the Vajirabuddhi Ṭīkā (Vajirabuddhi Ṭīkā, Cūḷavagga 318): “It is written: ‘Relinquish the first share’—this is if this new cloth is more valuable than the first-accepted cloth.” From this, it is known. Thus, since it is stated in the commentary and sub-commentaries that in the giving of rains-residence gifts, a valuable cloth brought afterwards, having been offered in exchange starting from the great elder, and if not desired by them, should be given to the monk who arrived later and is eligible by seniority, it is understood that the very best should be given to the most senior.

“Sace [M 2.0139] paṭhamavassūpagatā dve tīṇi cattāri pañca vā vatthāni alatthu”nti vatthagaṇanāya eva vuttattā, agghagaṇanāya avuttattā ca kathinānisaṃsavatthassa ca vassāvāsikagatikabhāvassa vacanato kathinānisaṃsavatthāni vatthagaṇanāvaseneva bhājetabbāni, na agghasamabhāvenāti ca daṭṭhabbāni, teneva ca kāraṇena “yo bahūni kathinānisaṃsavatthāni deti, tassa santakeneva attharitabba”nti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) vuttaṃ. Bahūni hi kathinānisaṃsavatthāni vibhajanakāle saṅghassa upakārakāni hontīti.

Since it is stated, “If those who undertook the first rains-residence have received two, three, four, or five cloths,” only in terms of counting cloths and not in terms of counting value, and because the Kathina-privilege cloth has the same status as a rains-residence gift, it should be understood that Kathina-privilege cloths are to be divided by means of counting cloths, not by equal value. For this very reason, it is stated: “Whoever gives many Kathina-privilege cloths, it should be spread with what belongs to him” (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 306). For many Kathina-privilege cloths are helpful to the Sangha at the time of distribution.

Pāḷiaṭṭhakathādīhi, netvā vuttaṃ vinicchayaṃ;

Kathine cīvare mayhaṃ, cintayantu vicakkhaṇā.

Having drawn this stated decision from the Pāli, the commentaries, and other sources, may the wise consider my judgment concerning the Kathina robe.

Cintayitvā punappunaṃ, yuttaṃ ce dhārayantu taṃ;

Ayuttañce ito aññaṃ, pariyesantu kāraṇanti.

Having reflected again and again, if it is suitable, let them retain it; and if it is unsuitable, let them seek another reason than this.

“Yo ca tattha cīvaruppādo, so nesaṃ bhavissatī”ti cīvarasseva atthatakathinānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ santakabhāvassa bhagavatā vuttattā cīvarato aññāni saṅghaṃ uddissa dinnāni piṇḍapātādīni vatthūni upacārasīmaṃ paviṭṭhassa āgatāgatassa saṅghassa santakaṃ honti. Tathā hi vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) “kathinaṃ attharāpetvā dānañca bhuñjitvā gamissanti[V 2.0102], ānisaṃso pana itaresaṃyeva hotī”ti. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerānaṃ upaḍḍhapaṭivīsaṃ dātu”nti (mahāva. 343) pāṭhaṃ upanissāya kathinānisaṃsacīvarampi sāmaṇerānaṃ upaḍḍhapaṭivīsaṃyeva denti, na panevaṃ kātabbaṃ. Bhaṇḍāgāre ṭhapitañhi akālacīvarameva sāmaṇerānaṃ upaḍḍhapaṭivīsaṃ katvā dātabbaṃ. Vassāvāsikakathinānisaṃsādikālacīvaraṃ pana samakameva dātabbaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ cīvarakkhandhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 343) “sāmaṇerānaṃ upaḍḍhapaṭivīsanti ettha ye sāmaṇerā attissarā bhikkhusaṅghassa [M 2.0140] kattabbakammaṃ na karonti, uddesaparipucchāsu yuttā ācariyupajjhāyānaṃyeva vattapaṭipattiṃ karonti, aññesaṃ na karonti, etesaṃyeva upaḍḍhabhāgo dātabbo. Ye pana purebhattañca pacchābhattañca bhikkhusaṅghasseva kattabbakiccaṃ karonti, tesaṃ samako dātabbo. Idañca piṭṭhisamaye uppannena bhaṇḍāgāre ṭhapitena akālacīvareneva kathitaṃ, kālacīvaraṃ pana samakameva dātabba”nti.

“Whatever robe-cloth arises there, that will belong to them.” Since the Blessed One declared that the robe-cloth belongs to those monks for whom the Kathina is spread, other items such as alms-food and so on, given with the Sangha as the intended recipient, become the property of whichever members of the Sangha have entered the vicinity boundary. As stated in the Commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 306): “After having the Kathina spread and partaking of the gifts, they will depart; the benefit, however, belongs only to the others.” “I allow, monks, to give half a portion to the novices.” Based on this passage (Mahāva. 343), some give even the Kathina-privilege robe-cloth to the novices as only half a portion, but it should not be done in this way. For only out-of-season robe-cloth stored in the storeroom should be given to the novices after making it a half portion. However, in-season robe-cloth, such as that from the Kathina-privilege of the rains residence, should be given equally. As stated in the Commentary on the Robe Section (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 343): “Regarding ‘half a portion to the novices’—here, those novices who are independent, who do not perform duties for the Sangha of monks, who are engaged in recitation and questioning, attending to the duties only of their teachers and preceptors, and do not serve others—to these, only half a portion should be given. But to those who perform duties for the Sangha of monks both before and after the meal, to these, an equal portion should be given. This was spoken regarding out-of-season robe-cloth that arises at a later time and is stored in the storeroom. However, in-season robe-cloth should be given equally.”

Kacci nu kho sāmaṇerā vassaṃ upagatā, yena ānisaṃsaṃ labheyyunti? Āma upagatāti. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti? “Atha cattāro bhikkhū upagatā, eko paripuṇṇavasso sāmaṇero, so ce pacchimikāya upasampajjati, gaṇapūrako ceva hoti, ānisaṃsañca labhatī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 306) vacanato vajirabuddhiṭīkāyañca (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306) “pacchimikāya upasampanno paṭhamapavāraṇāya pavāretumpi labhati, vassiko ca hoti, ānisaṃsañca labhatīti sāmaṇerānaṃ vassūpagamanaṃ anuññātaṃ hoti. Sāmaṇerā kathinānisaṃsaṃ labhantīti vadantī”ti vacanatoti.

“Have the novices indeed undertaken the rains residence, so that they may gain the benefits?” “Yes, they have undertaken it.” How is this understood? “Then, four monks have undertaken the rains residence, and one novice has completed the rains. If he receives higher ordination in the final period, he both completes the quorum and gains the benefits,” as stated in the Commentary (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 306). And from the statement in the Vajirabuddhi Sub-commentary (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 306): “One who is ordained in the final period is also entitled to participate in the first Pavāraṇā, becomes a resident for the rains, and gains the benefits. Thus, undertaking the rains residence is permitted for novices. They say, ‘The novices gain the benefits of the Kathina.’”

Tatruppādesu kathinānisaṃsesu yadi ārāmikā taṇḍulādīhi vatthāni cetāpenti, vatthehipi taṇḍulādīni cetāpenti, tattha kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti? Vibhajanakāle vijjamānavatthuvasena kātabbaṃ. Tathā hi vuttaṃ vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306) “tatruppādena taṇḍulādinā vatthūsu cetāpitesu atthatakathinānameva tāni vatthāni pāpuṇanti. Vatthehi pana taṇḍulādīsu cetāpitesu sabbesaṃ tāni pāpuṇantīti vutta”nti. “Sace pana ekasīmāyaṃ bahū vihārā hontī”ti ettha katarasīmā adhippetāti? Upacārasīmā. Upacārasīmāyaṃyeva hi saṅghalābhavibhajanādikaṃ sijjhati. Vuttañhetaṃ [M 2.0141] vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. mahāvagga 306) “kathinatthatasīmāyanti [V 2.0103] upacārasīmaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, upacārasīmaṭṭhassa matakacīvarādibhāgiyatāya baddhasīmāya tatruppādābhāvato viññeyyametaṃ ‘upacārasīmāva adhippetā’ti”.

In the case of benefits arising there from the Kathina, if monastery workers use rice and other items to acquire cloth, or use cloth to acquire rice and other items, how should one proceed? At the time of distribution, it should be done according to the items available. As it is said in the Vajirabuddhi Sub-commentary (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 306): “When cloth is acquired with rice and other items that have arisen there, that cloth belongs only to those for whom the Kathina has been spread. But when rice and other items are acquired with cloth, they belong to everyone.” Regarding the phrase, “If, however, there are many monasteries within one boundary,” which boundary is intended here? The vicinity boundary. For it is only within the vicinity boundary that the distribution of the Sangha’s gains and so on is accomplished. As it is said in the Vajirabuddhi Sub-commentary (Vajira. Ṭī. Mahāvagga 306): “The phrase ‘in the boundary where the Kathina is spread’ is said in reference to the vicinity boundary. Because the right to a share of a deceased monk’s robes and so on belongs to one who is within the vicinity boundary, and because there is no such arising of a rule in the established boundary, it should be understood that ‘only the vicinity boundary is intended.’”

Evaṃ kathinatthāraṃ dassetvā saṅghe rucitāya mātikāpalibodhaubbhāre adassetvāva ante ānisaṃsaṃ dassetuṃ “atthatakathinānaṃ vo bhikkhave”tiādimāha. Tattha aṭṭhavidhā mātikā pakkamanantikā, niṭṭhānantikā, sanniṭṭhānantikā, nāsanantikā, savanantikā, āsāvacchedikā, sīmātikkantikā, sahubbhārāti. Tattha atthatakathino bhikkhu katapariyositaṃ cīvaraṃ ādāya “imaṃ vihāraṃ na paccessāmī”ti pakkamati, tassa bhikkhuno upacārasīmātikkameneva kathinubbhāro bhavati, pañcānisaṃsāni alabhaneyyo hoti. Ayaṃ kathinubbhāro pakkamanamevassa antabhūtattā pakkamanantiko nāma hoti.

Having thus shown the spreading of the Kathina, without yet showing the lifting of the Kathina—which is an impediment based on the schedule—by the Sangha's approval, he then proceeds to show the benefits at the end by saying, “For you, O monks, for whom the Kathina has been spread,” and so on. In this context, there are eight kinds of lifting of the Kathina: the one ending with departure, the one ending with completion, the one ending with decision, the one ending with destruction, the one ending with hearing, the one ending with the cutting off of hope, the one ending with transgressing the boundary, and the simultaneous lifting. Among these, a monk for whom the Kathina has been spread takes a completed robe and departs, thinking, “I will not return to this monastery.” For that monk, the lifting of the Kathina occurs as soon as he transgresses the vicinity boundary, and he becomes ineligible for the five benefits. This lifting of the Kathina is called “the one ending with departure” because departure itself is its end.

Atthatakathino bhikkhu aniṭṭhitameva attano bhāgabhūtaṃ cīvaraṃ ādāya aññaṃ vihāraṃ gato, tassa bahiupacārasīmagatassa evaṃ hoti “imasmiṃyeva vihāre imaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressāmi, na purāṇavihāraṃ paccessāmī”ti, so bahisīmāyameva taṃ cīvaraṃ kāreti, tassa bhikkhuno tasmiṃ cīvare niṭṭhite kathinubbhāro hoti. Ayaṃ kathinubbhāro cīvaraniṭṭhānamevassa antoti niṭṭhānantiko nāma.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, taking his own share of the unfinished robe-material, goes to another monastery. Having gone outside the vicinity boundary, he thinks, 'I will have this robe-material made right here in this monastery and will not return to the former monastery.' He has that robe-material made outside the boundary, and for that monk, the lifting of the Kathina occurs when that robe is completed. This lifting of the Kathina is called 'the one ending with completion' because its end is the completion of the robe.

Bhikkhu atthatakathino akatacīvaramādāya pakkamati, tassa bahiupacārasīmagatassa evaṃ hoti “imaṃ cīvaraṃ neva kāressāmi, porāṇavihārañca na paccessāmī”ti, tassa bhikkhuno tena sanniṭṭhānena kathinubbhāro hoti. Ayaṃ kathinubbhāro sanniṭṭhānamevassa antoti sanniṭṭhānantiko nāma.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, taking unfashioned robe-cloth, departs. Having gone outside the vicinity boundary, he thinks, 'I will not have this robe-cloth made, nor will I return to the former monastery.' For that monk, the lifting of the Kathina occurs by that decision. This lifting of the Kathina is called 'the one ending with decision' because its end is the decision.

Atthatakathino [M 2.0142] bhikkhu akatameva cīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati, bahisīmagatassa tassa evaṃ hoti “idhevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressāmi, na ca porāṇavihāraṃ paccessāmī”ti, tassa cīvaraṃ kurumānaṃ corādīhi nassati, agyādīhi vinassati, kathinubbhāro hoti. Ayaṃ kathinubbhāro nāsanamevassa antoti nāsanantiko nāma.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, taking unfashioned robe-cloth, departs. Having gone outside the boundary, he thinks, 'I will have this robe-cloth made right here, and I will not return to the former monastery.' While he is having the robe-cloth made, it is lost to thieves or others, or destroyed by fire or other causes, and the lifting of the Kathina occurs. This lifting of the Kathina is called 'the one ending with destruction' because its end is the loss or destruction.

Atthatakathino bhikkhu akatacīvaramādāya “imaṃ vihāraṃ paccessāmī”ti cintetvā pakkamati[V 2.0104], tassa bahisīmagatassa evaṃ hoti “idhevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressāmī”ti, so katacīvaro suṇāti “vihāre kira saṅghena kathinaṃ ubbhata”nti, tena savanamattenassa kathinaṃ ubbhataṃ hoti. Ayaṃ kathinabbhāro savanamevassa antoti savanantiko nāma.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, taking unfashioned robe-cloth, departs, thinking, 'I will return to this monastery.' Having gone outside the boundary, he thinks, 'I will have this robe-cloth made right here.' Having had the robe made, he hears, 'It seems the Sangha has lifted the Kathina in the monastery.' For him, the Kathina is lifted merely by that hearing. This lifting of the Kathina is called 'the one ending with hearing' because its end is the hearing.

Atthatakathino bhikkhu aññattha paccāsācīvarakāraṇā pakkamati, tassa bahisīmagatassa evaṃ hoti “idha bahisīmāyameva cīvarapaccāsaṃ payirupāsāmi, na vihāraṃ paccessāmī”ti, so tattheva taṃ cīvarapaccāsaṃ payirupāsati, so taṃ cīvarapaccāsaṃ alabhamāno cīvarāsā pacchijjati, teneva tassa bhikkhuno kathinubbhāro bhavati. Ayaṃ kathinubbhāro āsāvacchedasahitattā āsāvacchediko nāma.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread departs for another place because of an expectation of robe-cloth. Having gone outside the boundary, he thinks, 'I will pursue the expectation of robe-cloth right here outside the boundary and will not return to the monastery.' He pursues that expectation of robe-cloth there, but upon not obtaining it, his hope for the robe-cloth is cut off. For that monk, the lifting of the Kathina occurs for that very reason. This lifting of the Kathina is called 'the one ending with the cutting off of hope' because it is connected with the cutting off of hope.

Atthatakathino bhikkhu akatacīvaraṃ ādāya “imaṃ vihāraṃ paccessāmī”ti cintetvā pakkamati, so bahisīmagato taṃ cīvaraṃ kāreti, so katacīvaro “vihāraṃ paccessāmī”ti cintento bahiupacārasīmāyameva kathinubbhārakālaṃ vītināmeti, tassa kathinubbhāro bhavati. Ayaṃ kathinubbhāro cīvarakālassa antimadivasasaṅkhātāya sīmāya atikkantattā sīmātikkantiko nāma.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, taking an unmade robe, departs, thinking, 'I will return to this monastery.' Having gone outside the precinct boundary, he has that robe made. When the robe is completed, he thinks, 'I will return to the monastery,' but lets the time for the lifting of the Kathina pass while still outside the monastery's environs. For him, the Kathina is lifted. This lifting of the Kathina is called 'ending by crossing the boundary' because it occurs due to the boundary, reckoned as the last day of the robe season, being crossed.

Atthatakathino bhikkhu cīvaraṃ ādāya “imaṃ vihāraṃ paccessāmī”ti cintetvā pakkamati, so katacīvaro “vihāraṃ [M 2.0143] paccessāmī”ti cintento paccāgantvā vihāre kathinubbhāraṃ pappoti, tassa bhikkhuno vihāre bhikkhūhi saha kathinubbhāro bhavati. Ayaṃ kathinubbhāro vihāre bhikkhūhi saha katattā sahubbhāro nāma. Ayaṃ aṭṭhavidho kathinubbhāro aṭṭha mātikā nāma. Vuttañhetaṃ kathinakkhandhakapāḷiyaṃ (mahāva. 310) “aṭṭhimā, bhikkhave, mātikā kathinassa ubbhārāya pakkamanantikā niṭṭhānantikā sanniṭṭhānantikā nāsanantikā savanantikā āsāvacchedikā sīmātikkantikā sahubbhārāti. Bhikkhu atthatakathino katacīvaramādāya pakkamati ‘na paccessa’nti, tassa bhikkhuno pakkamanantiko kathinubbhāro”tiādi, vinayavinicchayappakaraṇe ca –

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, taking a robe, departs, thinking, 'I will return to this monastery.' Having completed the robe and thinking, 'I will return to the monastery,' he returns and attains the lifting of the Kathina in the monastery. For that monk, the lifting of the Kathina occurs together with the monks in the monastery. This lifting is called 'lifting together' because it is done together with the monks in the monastery. These eight kinds of Kathina lifting are called the eight matrices. For it is stated in the Kathina chapter of the Mahāvagga: 'Monks, there are these eight matrices for the lifting of the Kathina: ending by departure, ending by completion, ending by decision, ending by destruction, ending by hearing, ending by the cutting off of hope, ending by crossing the boundary, and lifting together. If a monk for whom the Kathina has been spread takes a completed robe and departs, thinking, “I will not return,” for that monk the Kathina is lifted by departure,' and so on. And in the Vinayavinicchayappakaraṇa:

“Pakkamanañca [V 2.0105] niṭṭhānaṃ, sanniṭṭhānañca nāsanaṃ;

Savanamāsā ca sīmā ca, sahubbhāroti aṭṭhimā”ti. (vi. vi. 2709);

'Departure and completion, decision and destruction; hearing and hope, and boundary, and lifting together—these are the eight.'

Palibodho duvidho āvāsapalibodho, cīvarapalibodhoti. Tattha “yasmiṃ vihāre kathinaṃ atthataṃ hoti, tasmiṃ vasissāmī”ti aññattha gacchantopi “puna taṃ vihāraṃ āgacchissāmī”ti sāpekkho hoti. Ayaṃ āvāsapalibodho nāma. Tassa bhikkhuno cīvaraṃ akataṃ vā hoti apariyositaṃ vā, “aññato cīvaraṃ lacchāmī”ti āsā vā anupacchinnā hoti. Ayaṃ cīvarapalibodho nāma. Vuttañhetaṃ kathinakkhandhake (mahāva. 325) “katame ca, bhikkhave, dve kathinassa palibodhā? Āvāsapalibodho ca cīvarapalibodho ca. Kathañca, bhikkhave, āvāsapalibodho hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vasati vā tasmiṃ āvāse, sāpekkho vā pakkamati ‘paccessa’nti, evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, āvāsapalibodho hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, cīvarapalibodho hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno cīvaraṃ akataṃ [M 2.0144] vā hoti vippakataṃ vā, cīvarāsā vā anupacchinnā, evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, cīvarapalibodho hotī”ti.

Hindrances are of two kinds: the hindrance of dwelling and the hindrance of robes. Herein, even when going elsewhere, a monk is expectant, thinking, 'I will dwell in the monastery where the Kathina has been spread,' or 'I will return to that monastery again.' This is called the hindrance of dwelling. For that monk, the robe may be unmade or unfinished, or his hope, 'I will receive a robe from elsewhere,' may not be cut off. This is called the hindrance of robes. For it is said in the Kathina chapter: 'And what, monks, are the two hindrances concerning the Kathina? The hindrance of dwelling and the hindrance of robes. And how, monks, is there the hindrance of dwelling? Here, monks, a monk either dwells in that dwelling, or departs with an expectation, thinking, “I will return.” Thus, monks, there is the hindrance of dwelling. And how, monks, is there the hindrance of robes? Here, monks, a monk’s robe is unmade or incomplete, or his hope for a robe is not cut off. Thus, monks, there is the hindrance of robes.'

Ubbhāro duvidho aṭṭhamātikāubbhāraantarubbhāravasena. Tattha bahiupacārasīmagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasena vuttā satta kathinubbhārā ca bahiupacārasīmaṃ gantvā nivattetvā kathinatthatavihāre antarubbhāraṃ patvā bhikkhūhi saha antarubbhārassa katattā sahubbhārasaṅkhāto eko kathinubbhāro cāti ime aṭṭha kathinubbhārā aṭṭhamātikāya paviṭṭhattā aṭṭhamātikāubbhāro nāma. Bahisīmaṃ agantvā tasmiṃyeva vihāre nisīditvā kathinubbhāraṃ ñattidutiyakammavācāya kathinubbhāro aṭṭhamātikāya appaviṭṭho hutvā kālaparicchedaṃ appatvā antarāyeva katattā antarubbhāro nāma.

The lifting is of two kinds: by way of the eight-matrix lifting and the internal lifting. Herein, there are the seven Kathina liftings stated with reference to monks who have gone outside the monastery's environs, and there is the one Kathina lifting called 'lifting together,' which occurs because, having gone outside the monastery's environs and returned, one attains the internal lifting in the monastery where the Kathina was spread, and it is done together with the monks. Thus, these eight Kathina liftings, being included in the eight matrices, are called the eight-matrix lifting. The Kathina lifting performed by means of a motion and a second announcement, without going outside the boundary but while sitting right there in the monastery, not being included in the eight matrices, not reaching the time limit, and being done in the interim, is called the internal lifting.

Antarubbhārasahubbhārā ñattidutiyakammavācāyeva katā, evaṃ sante ko tesaṃ visesoti? Antarubbhāro bahisīmaṃ agantvā antosīmāyameva ṭhitehi bhikkhūhi kato. Sahubbhāro bahisīmaṃ gatena bhikkhunā paccāgantvā taṃ antarubbhāraṃ patvā tehi antosīmaṭṭhehi bhikkhūhi saha katoti ayametesaṃ viseso. Pakkamanantikādayo satta kathinubbhārā na kammavācāya [V 2.0106] katā, kevalaṃ dvinnaṃ palibodhānaṃ upacchedena pañcahi ānisaṃsehi vigatattā kathinubbhārā nāma honti. Vuttañhetaṃ ācariyabuddhadattattherena vinayavinicchaye –

The internal lifting and the lifting together are performed only by a motion and a second announcement. If that is so, what is their difference? The internal lifting is performed by monks who remained within the boundary without going outside. The lifting together is performed by a monk who went outside the boundary, returned, attained that internal lifting, and then performed it together with those monks who remained within the boundary—this is their difference. The seven Kathina liftings, starting with ending by departure, are not performed by a formal act; they are called 'Kathina liftings' merely by the cutting off of the two hindrances, and because they are devoid of the five benefits. This was stated by the Elder Ācariya Buddhādatta in the Vinayavinicchaya:

“Aṭṭhannaṃ mātikānaṃ vā, antarubbhāratopi vā;

Ubbhārāpi duve vuttā, kathinassa mahesinā”ti.

'Or by the eight matrices, or by the internal lifting; two liftings of the Kathina are declared by the great sage.'

Taṭṭīkāyampi “aṭṭhannaṃ mātikānanti bahisīmagatānaṃ vasena vuttā. Pakkamanantikādayo satta mātikā bahisīmaṃ gantvā antarubbhāraṃ [M 2.0145] sampattassa vasena vuttā, sahubbhāro imāsaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ mātikānaṃ vasena ca. Antarubbhāratopi vāti bahisīmaṃ agantvā tattheva vasitvā kathinubbhārakammena ubbhatakathinānaṃ vasena labbhanato antarubbhāroti mahesinā kathinassa ubbhārā duve vuttāti yojanā. Bahisīmaṃ gantvā āgatassa vasena saubbhāro, bahisīmaṃ agatānaṃ vasena antarubbhāroti ekoyeva ubbhāro dvidhā vutto”ti vuttaṃ.

In its subcommentary also, it is said: 'The phrase 'by the eight matrices' refers to what is stated with reference to those who have gone outside the boundary. The seven matrices, beginning with ending by departure, are stated with reference to one who, having gone outside the boundary, attains the internal lifting; and the lifting together is also included among these eight matrices. The phrase 'and also by way of the internal lifting' means that because it is obtained by those for whom the Kathina has been lifted by the act of Kathina lifting while staying right there without going outside the boundary, it is called the internal lifting. Thus, the connection is that two liftings of the Kathina are declared by the great sage. It is said: 'The lifting together is with reference to one who has gone outside the boundary and returned, while the internal lifting is with reference to those who have not gone outside the boundary. Thus, the one lifting by formal act is spoken of in two ways.'

Kasmā pana antarubbhāravasena kammavācāya kathinaṃ ubbhatanti? Mahādānaṃ dātukāmehi upāsakehi āgatassa saṅghassa akālacīvaraṃ dātukāmehi yācitattā. Vuttañhi bhikkhunīvibhaṅgapāḷiyaṃ (pāci. 925) “tena kho pana samayena aññatarena upāsakena saṅghaṃ uddissa vihāro kārāpito hoti, so tassa vihārassa mahe ubhatosaṅghassa akālacīvaraṃ dātukāmo hoti. Tena kho pana samayena ubhatosaṅghassa kathinaṃ atthataṃ hoti. Atha kho so upāsako saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā kathinuddhāraṃ yācī”tiādi. Kathaṃ pana kammavācā kātabbāti? “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho kathinaṃ uddhareyya, esā ñatti. Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho, saṅgho kathinaṃ uddharati. Yassāyasmato khamati kathinassa uddhāro, so tuṇhassa. Yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Ubbhataṃ saṅghena kathinaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti evaṃ kātabbāti. Vuttañhi bhikkhunīvibhaṅge “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kathinaṃ uddharituṃ, evañca pana, bhikkhave, kathinaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo – suṇātu me…pe… dhārayāmī”ti.

Why then is the Kathina lifted by means of a formal act by way of an internal lifting? Because it was requested by lay devotees who wished to give a great offering and who wished to give out-of-season robes to the Sangha that had arrived. For it is said in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pāḷi: "At that time, a certain lay devotee had a monastery built for the Sangha. At the dedication ceremony of that monastery, he wished to offer out-of-season robes to both Sanghas. At that time, the Kathina had been spread for both Sanghas. Then that lay devotee approached the Sangha and requested the removal of the Kathina," and so on. How then should the formal act be performed? "Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should lift the Kathina. This is the motion. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha is lifting the Kathina. Whichever venerable one agrees to the lifting of the Kathina should remain silent. Whichever one does not agree should speak. The Kathina is lifted by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore they are silent. Thus do I take it." It should be performed thus. For it is said in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga: "I allow, monks, the lifting of the Kathina.
