And in that case, there would be no emergence from the offense incurred." If he has spent one, two, or three days more than the required probation period, surely this monk has completed his probation? Therefore, he should request mānatta. Why then, having undertaken the duties, should he request mānatta? Bearing this objection in mind, it is said: 'For this monk becomes worthy of mānatta only when the duties are undertaken, and not otherwise,' and so on. For since this monk is worthy of mānatta only when the duties are undertaken, and not when they are not undertaken, therefore the connection is that he must undertake the duties before requesting mānatta. But is it not stated in the formal act, 'He who has completed probation requests mānatta from the Saṅgha,' and not 'one who has undertaken the duties'? Why then is it said, 'He becomes worthy of mānatta only when the duties are undertaken'? Addressing this question, it is said, 'Because he has completed probation after relinquishing the duties.' Since this monk has completed probation having relinquished the duties, and not without relinquishing them, therefore, having completed probation by relinquishing the duties, this monk becomes worthy of mānatta only when the duties are undertaken, and not otherwise. This is the explanation. Thus it is said, 'But for one who has not relinquished the duties, there is no need to undertake them again. For he becomes worthy of mānatta simply by exceeding the days of concealment. Therefore, mānatta should indeed be given to him.'

Catūhi [V 2.0155] pañcahi vā bhikkhūhi saddhinti ūnegaṇecaraṇadosā vimuccanatthaṃ. Parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepatotiādi kiñcāpi pāḷiyaṃ natthi, atha kho aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ vacanena tathā eva paṭipajjitabbanti ca vuttaṃ. “Atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāti dvādasahatthe upacāre sallakkhetvā, anikkhittavattānaṃ upacārasīmāya āgatabhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā [M 2.0212] sahavāsādikaṃ veditabbanti ca vuttaṃ. ‘Nikkhipantena ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ payojanaṃ atthī’ti ca vuttaṃ, na pana taṃ payojanaṃ dassita”nti vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 97) vuttaṃ, vattabhedadukkaṭā muccanapayojanaṃ hotīti veditabbaṃ.

With four or five bhikkhus, it is said to be 'saddhiṃ' (together with)—for the purpose of being freed from the fault of wandering with an incomplete group. Although the phrase 'the enclosure of an enclosed monastery,' and so forth, is not found in the Pāḷi, it is nevertheless said that it should be practiced accordingly, by the word of the commentary teachers. 'Having noted the presence' means having noted the presence within the twelve-cubit proximity. It is also said that having noted the arrival of those who have not relinquished their duties within the boundary of proximity, co-residence and the like should be understood. 'There is a purpose in relinquishing after informing'—it is also said, but that purpose is not shown. This is stated in the Vajirabuddhiṭīkā (Vajira. Ṭī. Cūḷavagga 97). It should be understood that the purpose is to be freed from the dukkaṭa offense of breaking the duties.

239. Abbhānaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti katampi akatameva hotīti attho. “Tenāpi vattaṃ samādiyitvā ārocetvā abbhānaṃ yācitabba”nti vuttattā abbhānayācanatthaṃ mānattassa samādiyanakālepi ārocetabbameva. Pubbe mānattacāritakāle ārocitamevāti anārocetvā abbhānaṃ na yācitabbanti viññāyati. Evaṃ mānattayācanakālepi parivāsaṃ samādiyitvā ārocetabbamevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

239. It is not permissible to perform rehabilitation; the meaning is that even if performed, it is as if not performed. Since it is said, 'Even by him, having undertaken the duties and informed, rehabilitation should be requested,' therefore, even at the time of undertaking mānatta for the purpose of requesting rehabilitation, it must be informed. It is understood that rehabilitation should not be requested without informing, on the grounds that it was already informed during the period of practicing mānatta. Similarly, it should be seen that even at the time of requesting mānatta, one must undertake probation and inform.

240. Ciṇṇamānatto bhikkhu abbhetabboti ciṇṇamānattassa ca abbhānārahassa ca ninnānākaraṇattā vuttaṃ. Aññathā “abbhānāraho abbhetabbo”ti vattabbaṃ siyā. Ukkhepanīyakammakatopi attano laddhiggahaṇavasena sabhāgabhikkhumhi sati tassa anārocāpetuṃ na labhati.

240. ‘A bhikkhu who has completed mānatta should be rehabilitated’—this is said because there is no distinction made between one who has completed mānatta and one who is worthy of rehabilitation. Otherwise, it might have been said, ‘One worthy of rehabilitation should be rehabilitated.’ Even one against whom an act of suspension has been carried out, if there is a fellow bhikkhu who shares his view, cannot avoid informing him by virtue of his own acquired view.

“Anantarāyikassa pana antarāyikasaññāya chādayato acchannāvā”ti pāṭho. Averibhāvena sabhāgo averisabhāgo. “Sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ āpannassa pana santike āvi kātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti pasaṅgato idheva pakāsitaṃ. Lahukesu paṭikkhepo natthi. Tattha ñattiyā āvi katvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ anuññātattā lahukasabhāgaṃ āvi kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti. Sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ pana ñattiyā ārocanaṃ na vaṭṭatīti kira. “Tassa santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissatīti (mahāva. 171) vuttattā lahukassevāyaṃ samanuññātā. Na hi sakkā suddhassa ekassa santike saṅghādisesassa [M 2.0213] paṭikaraṇaṃ kātu”nti likhitaṃ. Lahukesupi sabhāgaṃ āvi kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti. Tasmā eva hi ñattiyā āvikaraṇaṃ anuññātaṃ, itarathā taṃ niratthakaṃ siyā. Aññamaññārocanassa vaṭṭati, tato na vaṭṭatīti dīpanatthameva ñattiyā āvikaraṇamanuññātaṃ[V 2.0156], teneva idha “sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ āpannassā”tiādi vuttaṃ, ayamattho “ettāvatā te dve nirāpattikā honti, tesaṃ santike sesehi sabhāgāpattiyo desetabbā”ti vacanena kaṅkhāvitaraṇiyampi (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) pakāsitova. Saṅghādisesaṃ pana ñattiyā ārocetvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Tassā ñattiyā ayamattho – yadā suddhaṃ bhikkhuṃ passissati, tassa santike aññamaññārocanavasena paṭikarissati, evaṃ paṭikate “na ca, bhikkhave, sāpattikena pātimokkhaṃ sotabbaṃ, yo suṇeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 386) vuttāpattito mokkho hoti, tasmā “garukaṃ vā hotu lahukaṃ vā, ñattiyā āvi kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Ubhosu nayesu yuttataraṃ gahetabbaṃ. “Nāmañceva āpatti cāti tena tena vītikkamenāpannāpatti āpatti. Nāmanti tassā āpattiyā nāma”nti likhitaṃ. Ārocetvā nikkhipitabbanti ettha ārocanaṃ vattabhedadukkaṭapariharaṇappayojananti veditabbaṃ.

The reading is: 'But for one without an obstacle who conceals with the perception of an obstacle, it is unconcealed.' One who is a fellow through being without enmity is an 'averisabhāga.' It is explained here in this context that 'it is not proper to reveal a Saṅghādisesa offense of the same group in the presence of one who has committed it.' For minor offenses, there is no prohibition. In that case, because it is permitted to perform the Uposatha after revealing the offense by a motion, it is proper to reveal it to a fellow with a minor offense. However, it is said that it is not proper to announce a Saṅghādisesa offense of the same group by a motion. Because it is said, 'He will make amends for that offense in his presence' (Mahāvagga 171), this is permitted only for a minor offense. It is written: 'For it is not possible to make amends for a Saṅghādisesa offense in the presence of a single pure bhikkhu.' It is not proper to reveal even minor offenses to a fellow. Indeed, for this very reason, revealing by a motion was permitted; otherwise, it would be pointless. Revealing by a motion was permitted precisely to show that mutual announcement is proper, but beyond that, it is not. For that reason, it is said here, 'of one who has committed a Saṅghādisesa offense of the same group,' and so forth. This meaning is also explained in the Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī by the words, 'By this much, those two become without offense; in their presence, the remaining offenses of the same group should be confessed.' However, it is proper to perform the Uposatha after announcing a Saṅghādisesa offense by a motion. This is the meaning of that motion: when he sees a pure bhikkhu, he will make amends in his presence by way of mutual announcement. When amends are thus made, there is freedom from the offense stated as, 'And, bhikkhus, one with an offense should not listen to the Pātimokkha; whoever should listen, commits a dukkaṭa offense' (Cūḷavagga 386). Therefore, it is said, 'Whether it be grave or minor, it is proper to reveal it by a motion.' Between the two methods, the more suitable one should be adopted. It is written: 'Both the name and the offense' means the offense incurred through this or that transgression is the offense. 'Name' means the name of that offense. Here, in 'having announced, one should relinquish,' the announcement should be understood as having the purpose of avoiding the dukkaṭa offense of breaking the duties.

“Satiyeva antarāye antarāyikasaññī chādeti, acchannā hoti. Antarāyikassa pana antarāyikasaññāya vā anantarāyikasaññāya vā chādayato acchannāvā”tipi pāṭho. Averīti hitakāmo. Uddhaste aruṇeti uṭṭhite aruṇe. Suddhassa santiketi sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ anāpannassa santike. Vatthunti asucimocanādivītikkamaṃ. Sukkavissaṭṭhīti vatthu ceva gottañcāti “sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti idaṃ asucimocanalakkhaṇassa vītikkamassa pakāsanato [M 2.0214] vatthu ceva hoti, sajātiyasādhāraṇavijātiyavinivattasabhāvāya sukkavissaṭṭhiyā eva pakāsanato gottañca hotīti attho. Gaṃ tāyatīti hi gottaṃ. Saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti cāti saṅghādisesoti tena tena vītikkamena āpannassa āpattinikāyassa nāmapakāsanato nāmañceva hoti, āpattisabhāvato āpatti ca.

There is also the reading: 'When there is indeed an obstacle, if one with perception of an obstacle conceals it, it is unconcealed. But for one with an obstacle, whether concealing it with the perception of an obstacle or with the perception of no obstacle, it is unconcealed.' 'Averī' means 'wishing well.' 'Uddhaste aruṇe' means 'when the dawn has arisen.' 'In the presence of the pure' means in the presence of one who has not incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense of the same group. 'Vatthu' (basis) refers to transgressions such as the emission of impurity. 'Sukkavissaṭṭhī' (emission of semen) is both the basis and the lineage. The meaning is that the term 'sukkavissaṭṭhī,' in that it reveals the transgression characterized by the emission of semen, is the basis; and in that it reveals the nature of the emission of semen itself, which is common to its own kind and distinct from other kinds, it is the lineage. For 'gotta' (lineage) is so called because it protects the family. 'Saṅghādisesa' is both the name and the offense. The meaning is that 'Saṅghādisesa,' in that it reveals the name of the category of offense incurred through various transgressions, is the name; and by its nature as an offense, it is the offense.

Suddhassāti sabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ anāpannassa, tato vuṭṭhitassa vā. Aññasminti suddhantaparivāsavasena āpattivuṭṭhānato aññasmiṃ āpattivuṭṭhāne. Paṭicchādiyitthāti paṭicchannā. Kā sā? Āpatti. Divasādīhi paricchinditvā vasanaṃ parivāso. Ko so? Vinayakammakaraṇaṃ. Paṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivāso paṭicchannaparivāso.

'Of the pure one' means of one who has not incurred a Saṅghādisesa offense of the same group, or of one who has emerged from it. 'In another' means in another emergence from an offense, different from the emergence from an offense by way of pure-end probation. 'It was concealed' means 'concealed.' What is that? The offense. 'Probation' is dwelling, having delimited it by days and so forth. What is that? The performance of a Vinaya act. Probation for a concealed offense is 'probation on account of a concealed offense'.

Paṭicchannaparivāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on probation on account of a concealed offense is concluded.

Suddhantaparivāsakathā

The Account of Pure-End Probation

242. Sujjhanaṃ [V 2.0157] suddho, ko so? Āpattivigamo. Amati osānabhāvaṃ gacchatīti anto, suddho anto yassa parivāsassāti suddhanto, suddhanto ca so parivāso cāti suddhantaparivāso, suddhakālaṃ pariyantaṃ katvā asuddhakālappamāṇena paricchinditvā kataparivāso.

242. Purification is 'pure'; what is that? The freedom from an offense. 'End' (anto) means reaching the state of conclusion. 'Pure-end' (suddhanto) is that probation whose end is pure. 'Pure-end probation' (suddhantaparivāso) is that probation which is pure-end, meaning it is a probation undertaken by making a pure period the limit, having defined it by the measure of an impure period.

Suddhantaparivāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of Pure-End Probation is concluded.

Odhānasamodhānaparivāsakathā

The Discussion on Suspension, Reinstatement, and Probation

243. Samodhīyate samodhānaṃ, nānākālikā nānāvatthukā āpattiyo agghādivasena samodhānaṃ ekīkaraṇaṃ[M 2.0215], samodhānetvā kato parivāso samodhānaparivāsoti viggaho. Kammavācāyaṃ “paṭikassito saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ appaṭicchannānaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanā, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti ettha gatyatthadhātuyā kammani ca nayanatthadhātuyā kammani ca tadatthasampadāne ca vibhattipariṇāme cāti imesu catūsu ṭhānesu āyādesassa vuttattā, paṭipubbakasadhātuyā ca nayanatthattā “mūlāyā”ti idaṃ “paṭikassito”ti ettha kammaṃ, tasmā “paṭikassito…pe… mūlāya” iti ettakameva bhavitabbaṃ, na “mūlāyapaṭikassanā”ti evaṃ maññamānā saddaviduno “paṭikassanā”ti idaṃ adhikanti vā vadeyyuṃ makkheyyuṃ vā, na panetaṃ vattabbaṃ. Navapāṭhesuyeva ayaṃ pāṭho saddalakkhaṇayutto vā ayutto vāti cintetabbo, na pana pāḷiyaṭṭhakathādito āgatesu porāṇapāṭhesu. Tesu pana kathaṃ yojiyamāno ayaṃ pāṭho saddayuttiyā ca atthayuttiyā ca samannāgato bhaveyyāti yojanākāroyeva cintetabbo. Ayañca pāṭho porāṇapāḷipāṭhova, tasmā “mūlāyapaṭikassanā”ti idaṃ karaṇavasena vipariṇāmetvā “mūlāyapaṭikassanāya paṭikassito”ti yojetabbaṃ.

243. Compounding is that which is compounded; it is the unification of various offenses, occurring at different times and based on different grounds, by means of valuation and so forth. The probation undertaken after such compounding is called 'compounding-probation'—this is the analysis. In the formal act, regarding the text: 'The bhikkhu of such a name has been sent back by the Saṅgha for many unconcealed offenses in the interim, a sending back to the origin. This is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent; thus do I understand it,' here, because the substitution of 'āya' has been stated in these four instances—in the object of a root with the meaning of 'going,' in the object of a root with the meaning of 'leading,' in the dative of purpose for that meaning, and in the change of case-ending—and because the root 'sad' preceded by 'paṭi' has the meaning of 'leading,' this 'mūlāya' is the object of 'paṭikassito.' Therefore, it should only be 'paṭikassito…pe… mūlāya,' not 'mūlāyapaṭikassanā.' Grammarians, thinking thus, might say or disparage this 'paṭikassanā' as redundant, but this should not be said. Only in new readings should this reading be considered as to whether it is grammatically correct or incorrect, but not in the ancient readings that have come down from the Pāḷi and its commentaries. In those, however, one should only consider the manner of construction by which this reading, being construed, might be endowed with both grammatical correctness and correctness of meaning. And this reading is indeed an ancient Pāḷi reading. Therefore, this 'mūlāyapaṭikassanā' should be construed by changing it into the instrumental case as 'sent back by means of the sending back to the origin' (mūlāyapaṭikassanāya paṭikassito).

Kathaṃ panetassa porāṇapāṭhabhāvo jānitabboti? Pakaraṇe āgatattā. Vuttañhi vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. cūḷavagga 2.102) “pāḷiyaṃ paṭikassito saṅghena udāyi bhikkhu antarā ekissā āpattiyā…pe… mūlāyapaṭikassanāti idaṃ karaṇavasena vipariṇāmetvā [V 2.0158] mūlāyapaṭikassanāya paṭikassitoti yojetabba”nti. Atha vā “mūlāya paṭikassanā mūlāyapaṭikassanā”ti aluttasamāsavasena uttarapadena samāsaṃ katvā saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu antarā sambahulānaṃ āpattīnaṃ [M 2.0216] appaṭicchannānaṃ hetu paṭikassito. Sā mūlāyapaṭikassanā khamati saṅghassāti yojetabbaṃ. Tathā hi vuttaṃ tattheva (vi. vi. ṭī. cūḷavagga 2.102) “atha vā mūlāyapaṭikassanā khamati saṅghassāti uttarapadena saha paccattavaseneva yojetumpi vaṭṭatī”ti.

But how is the fact of this being an ancient reading to be known? Because it has come down in the treatise. For it is said in the Vimativinodanī: 'In the Pāḷi, the phrase, “The bhikkhu Udāyi was sent back by the Saṅgha for one offense in the interim…pe… a sending back to the origin,” this should be construed by changing it into the instrumental case as “sent back by means of the sending back to the origin.”' Alternatively, having formed a non-elided compound with the latter word, 'mūlāya paṭikassanā' becomes 'mūlāyapaṭikassanā,' and it should be construed thus: 'The bhikkhu of such a name was sent back by the Saṅgha on account of many unconcealed offenses in the interim. That sending back to the origin is agreeable to the Saṅgha.' For so it is said in that same text: 'Alternatively, it is also proper to construe “mūlāyapaṭikassanā is agreeable to the Saṅgha” with the latter word in the nominative case.'

Taṃ dentena paṭhamaṃ mūlāya paṭikassitvā pacchāparivāso dātabboti ettha taṃ odhānasamodhānaparivāsaṃ dentena paṭhamaṃ taṃ bhikkhuṃ mūlāya paṭikassitvā mūladivase ākaḍḍhitvā tassa antarāpattiyā samodhānaparivāso dātabboti attho. Yathā kiṃ vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. cūḷavagga 2.102) “udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ antarā ekissā āpattiyā…pe… mūlāya paṭikassitvāti ettha antarā ekissā āpattiyā hetubhūtāya udāyiṃ bhikkhuṃ mūlāya paṭikassitvā mūladivase ākaḍḍhitvā tassā antarāpattiyā samodhānaparivāsaṃ detūti yojanā”ti vuttaṃ. Mahāsumattheravāde āvikārāpetvā vissajjetabboti tassa atekicchabhāvaṃ teneva saṅghassa pākaṭaṃ kāretvā lajjīgaṇato viyojanavasena vissajjetabboti attho.

Regarding the statement, 'When giving that, having first sent him back to the origin, probation should be given afterwards,' here the meaning is: when giving that suspension-compounding-probation, having first sent that bhikkhu back to the origin, having drawn him back to the first day, compounding-probation should be given for his offense in the interim. For example, in the Vimativinodanī it is said: 'Regarding the phrase, “the bhikkhu Udāyi, for one offense in the interim…pe… having sent back to the origin,” here the construction is that, on account of one offense in the interim being the cause, having sent the bhikkhu Udāyi back to the origin, having drawn him back to the first day, let them give compounding-probation for that offense in the interim.' In the tradition of the Elder Mahāsumana, it is said that he should be dismissed after having it made manifest. The meaning is that, having had his incurable state made evident to that very Saṅgha, he should be dismissed by way of separation from the group of the conscientious.

Odhānasamodhānaparivāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on suspension-compounding-probation is concluded.

Agghasamodhānaparivāsakathā

The Discussion on Valuation-Compounding-Probation

244. Agghena agghavasena arahavasena samodhānaṃ agghasamodhānaṃ, āpannāsu sambahulāsu āpattīsu yā āpattiyo ciratarappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhāya tāsaṃ rattiparicchedavasena avasesānaṃ ūnatarappaṭicchannānaṃ āpattīnaṃ parivāso dīyati, ayaṃ vuccati agghasamodhāno [M 2.0217] . Sataṃ āpattiyoti kāyasaṃsaggādivasena ekadivase āpannā sataṃ āpattiyo. Dasasatanti sahassaāpattiyo. Rattisataṃ chādayitvānāti yojetabbaṃ. “Agghasamodhāno nāma sabhāgavatthukāyo sambahulā āpattiyo āpannassa bahurattiṃ paṭicchāditāpattiyaṃ nikkhipitvā dātabbo, itaro nānāvatthukānaṃ vasenāti ayametesaṃ viseso”ti vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 102) vuttaṃ.

244. Valuation-compounding is compounding by means of valuation, that is, by way of value or by way of worthiness. When many offenses have been committed, having compounded by their valuation those offenses that have been concealed for a longer time, probation is given for the remaining offenses concealed for a shorter time, based on the calculation of nights for those former offenses. This is called valuation-compounding. 'A hundred offenses' means a hundred offenses committed in one day, such as through bodily contact and so forth. 'Ten hundred' means a thousand offenses. It should be construed with 'having concealed for a hundred nights.' In the Vajirabuddhiṭīkā, it is said: 'Valuation-compounding should be given to one who has committed many offenses of a similar ground by consolidating them into the offense concealed for many nights, whereas the other type is based on offenses of different grounds. This is the difference between them.'

Agghasamodhānaparivāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on valuation-compounding-probation is concluded.

246. Liṅgaparivattanakakathāyaṃ [V 2.0159] yadi kassaci bhikkhuno itthiliṅgaṃ pātu bhaveyya, kiṃ tena puna upajjhā gahetabbā, puna upasampadā kātabbā, kiṃ bhikkhūpasampadāto paṭṭhāya vassagaṇanā kātabbā, udāhu ito paṭṭhāyāti pucchāya sati taṃ pariharitumāha “sace”tiādi. Evaṃ sante sā bhikkhunī bhikkhūnaṃ majjheyeva vasitabbaṃ bhaveyyāti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “appatirūpa”ntiādi. Evaṃ sante bhikkhubhūtakāle āpajjitāpattiyo kathaṃ kātabbāti codanaṃ manasi katvā āha “yā desanāgāminiyo vā”tiādi. Tattha bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīhi sādhāraṇāti sañcarittādayo. Asādhāraṇāti sukkavissaṭṭhiādayo. Hotu bhagavato anuññātavasena liṅge parivatte asādhāraṇāpattīhi vuṭṭhitabhāvo, puna pakatiliṅge uppanne puna āpatti siyāti āsaṅkaṃ pariharituṃ “puna pakatiliṅge”tiādi vuttaṃ. Idāni tamatthaṃ pāḷiyā sādhetuṃ “vuttañceta”ntiādimāha. Tassattho paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanāya ṭīkāsu (sārattha. ṭī. 2.69; vajira. ṭī. pārājika 69) vuttanayeneva daṭṭhabbo, idha pana garukāpattivuṭṭhānakathābhūtattā sāyeva kathā vuccate.

246. In the discussion on the change of gender, if the female gender should appear in any bhikkhu, what should be done by him? Should a preceptor be taken again? Should ordination be performed again? Should the counting of years be done from the time of his ordination as a bhikkhu, or from this point? When such a question arises, to resolve it, he says, 'If...' and so forth. Referring to the objection, 'If this were so, that bhikkhunī would have to dwell right in the midst of the bhikkhus,' he says, 'unseemly,' and so forth. Keeping in mind the objection, 'If this were so, what should be done about the offenses committed when he was a bhikkhu?', he says, 'Those that are confessable or...' and so forth. Here, those offenses common to bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs are such as acting as a go-between, and so forth. Those not common are such as seminal emission, and so forth. To resolve the doubt that, 'Granted, by the Blessed One's allowance, with the change of gender there is emergence from the non-common offenses, but if the original gender arises again, the offense might occur again,' it is said, 'if the original gender...' and so forth. Now, to establish that meaning with the Pāḷi, he says, 'And this has been stated...' and so forth. Its meaning should be understood in the same way as explained in the subcommentaries on the explanation of the first Pārājika. Here, however, since the discussion concerns the emergence from grave offenses, that same discussion is presented.

247. Tattha [M 2.0218] bhikkhunīhi sādhāraṇāya paṭicchannāya āpattiyāti sañcarittādiāpattiyā, hetvatthe cetaṃ karaṇavacanaṃ. Parivasantassāti anādare sāmivacanaṃ. Pakkhamānattameva dātabbaṃ, na puna parivāso dātabbo bhikkhunibhāve aparivāsārahattāti adhippāyo. Mānattaṃ carantassāti anādareyeva sāmivacanaṃ, chārattamānatte āciṇṇeyeva parivattati, puna pakkhamānattameva dātabbanti. Tena vakkhati “sace ciṇṇamānattassā”tiādi. Akusalavipāke parikkhīṇeti purisindriyassa antaradhānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Itthindriyapatiṭṭhānaṃ pana kusalavipākameva. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “ubhayampi akusalena antaradhāyati, kusalena paṭilabbhatī”ti. Chārattaṃ mānattameva dātabbaṃ, na parivāso dātabbo, na vā pakkhamānattaṃ dātabbaṃ.

247. Herein, 'by a concealed offense common with bhikkhunīs' refers to an offense such as acting as a go-between; and this is an instrumental case in the sense of cause. 'Of one undergoing probation' is a genitive of disregard. The meaning is that only fortnight-mānatta should be given, not probation again, because in the state of being a bhikkhunī she is not worthy of probation. 'Of one undergoing mānatta' is also a genitive of disregard; when the six-night mānatta has been completed, it changes over, and fortnight-mānatta should be given again. Therefore, he will say, 'If, for one who has completed mānatta...' and so forth. The phrase 'when the unwholesome result is exhausted' is said with reference to the disappearance of the male faculty. The establishment of the female faculty, however, is solely a wholesome result. For it is said in the commentary: 'Both disappear due to the unwholesome and are regained through the wholesome.' Only the six-night mānatta should be given; probation should not be given, nor should fortnight-mānatta be given.

“Ayaṃ pana viseso”ti vatvā taṃ visesaṃ dassetumāha “sace”tiādi. Parivāsadānaṃ natthi, chārattaṃ mānattameva dātabbaṃ. Kasmā? Bhikkhunikāle paṭicchannattā. Bhikkhukāle channāyeva hi āpatti parivāsārahā hoti, no bhikkhunikāleti ayametāsaṃ viseso. Pakkhamānattaṃ carantiyāti anādare sāmivacanaṃ, pakkhamānatte āciṇṇeyevāti attho. Tathā hi vakkhati “ciṇṇamānattāyā”tiādi. Chārattaṃ mānattaṃ carantassātiādi vuttanayameva.

Having said, 'But this is the distinction,' to show that distinction, he says, 'If,' and so forth. There is no granting of probation; only mānatta for six nights should be given. Why? Because it was concealed during the time as a bhikkhunī. For an offense is worthy of probation only when it is concealed during the time as a bhikkhu, not during the time as a bhikkhunī—this is their distinction. 'While practicing pakkha mānatta' is a genitive absolute, meaning 'when pakkha mānatta has been completed.' Therefore, he will say, 'For one who has completed the mānatta,' and so forth. 'While practicing mānatta for six nights,' and so forth, is in the same manner as stated.

Parivāsavinicchayakathā

The Discourse on the Determination of Probation

Idāni [V 2.0160] saṅghādisesāpatti yasmā sāvasesagarukāpatti hoti satekicchā, tasmā yathā nāma rogāturo puggalo kiñci attano hitasukhakāraṇaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, tamenaṃ kāruṇiko tikicchako karuṇāsañcodito tikicchaṃ katvā gelaññato vuṭṭhāpetvā [M 2.0219] hitasukhaṃ janeti, evaṃ saṅghādisesāpattisamaṅgī puggalo āṇāvītikkamantarāyikabhāvato saggamokkhamaggaṃ sodhetuṃ na sakkoti, tamenaṃ mahākāruṇiko bhagavā mahākaruṇāya sañcoditamānaso anekehi nayehi āpattito vuṭṭhānaṃ katvā saggamokkhasukhe patiṭṭhapeti, bhagavato adhippāyaññuno aṭṭhakathācariyāpi anekehi kāraṇehi bhagavato vacanassa atthaṃ pakāsetvā visuddhakāmānaṃ nayaṃ denti, tathā ṭīkācariyādayopi. Evaṃ dinne pana naye yoniso manasi kātuṃ sakkontā paṇḍitā yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjanti, asakkontā aññathā atthaṃ gahetvā na yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjanti, tesaṃ diṭṭhānugatiṃ anugacchantā sissādayopi tatheva karonti, tasmā bhagavato vacanañca pubbenāparaṃ saṃsanditvā aṭṭhakathāṭīkādivacanañca sammā tulayitvā tathato bhagavato adhippāyaṃ ñatvā yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjantehi garukāpattito vuṭṭhahanatthaṃ yogo karaṇīyo.

Now, because a Saṅghādisesa offense is a grave offense with a remainder, requiring remedy, it is just as a person afflicted by illness is unable to do anything for their own welfare and happiness, and a compassionate physician, moved by compassion, treats them, raises them up from their illness, and brings them welfare and happiness. Even so, a person who has committed a Saṅghādisesa offense is unable to purify the path to heaven and liberation due to the hindrance of transgressing the precepts. The greatly compassionate Blessed One, with a mind impelled by great compassion, raises them up from the offense through various means and establishes them in the happiness of heaven and liberation. The commentary teachers, understanding the Blessed One’s intention, also reveal the meaning of the Blessed One’s words through various reasons and offer the method to those who desire purity, and likewise the subcommentary teachers and others. When such a method is given, wise people, attending carefully, practice as instructed, while those who are unable misunderstand the meaning and do not practice as instructed. Disciples and others, following their example, also act in the same way. Therefore, having harmonized the Blessed One’s words from beginning to end, properly weighed the statements of the commentaries, subcommentaries, and so forth, and thus understood the true intention of the Blessed One, effort should be made to rise up from a grave offense by practicing as instructed.

Tasmā yadā bhikkhū āgacchanti vinayadharassa santikaṃ “garukāpattivuṭṭhānaṃ karissāmā”ti, tadā vinayadharena “tvaṃ katarāpattiṃ āpanno”ti pucchitabbo. “Saṅghādisesaṃ āpanno”ti vutte “katarasaṅghādisesa”nti pucchitvā “imaṃ nāmā”ti vutte sukkavissaṭṭhiyaṃ mocetukāmacetanā, upakkamo, muccananti tīṇi aṅgāni. Kāyasaṃsagge manussitthī, itthisaññitā, kāyasaṃsaggarāgo, tena rāgena vāyāmo, hatthaggāhādisamāpajjananti pañca aṅgāni. Duṭṭhullavācāyaṃ manussitthī, itthisaññitā, duṭṭhullavācassādarāgo, tena rāgena obhāsanaṃ, taṅkhaṇavijānananti pañca aṅgāni. Attakāme manussitthī, itthisaññitā, attakāmapāricariyāya rāgo, tena rāgena vaṇṇabhaṇanaṃ, taṅkhaṇavijānananti pañca aṅgāni. Sañcaritte yesu sañcarittaṃ samāpajjati, tesaṃ manussajātikatā[M 2.0220], nālaṃvacanīyatā, paṭiggaṇhanavīmaṃsanapaccāharaṇānīti pañca aṅgāni. Kuṭikāre ullittādīnaṃ aññataratā, heṭṭhimapamāṇasambhavo, adesitavatthukatā, pamāṇātikkantatā, attuddesikatā, vāsāgāratā, lepaghaṭanāti satta pamāṇayuttādīsu chadhā aṅgāni. Vihārakāre tāniyeva cha aṅgāni. Duṭṭhadose yaṃ codeti, tassa upasampannoti saṅkhyupagamanaṃ, tasmiṃ suddhasaññitā, yena pārājikena codeti[V 2.0161], tassa diṭṭhādivasena amūlakatā, cāvanādhippāyena sammukhācodanā, tassa taṅkhaṇavijānananti pañca aṅgāni. Aññabhāgiye aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kañcidesaṃ lesamattaṃ upādiyanatā, purimāni pañcāti cha aṅgāni. Saṅghabhede bhedāya parakkamanaṃ, dhammakammena samanubhāsanaṃ, kammavācāpariyosānaṃ, appaṭinissajjananti cattāri aṅgāni. Bhedānuvattake aṅgesu yathā tattha parakkamanaṃ, evaṃ idha anuvattananti cattāri aṅgāni. Dubbace aṅgesu yathā tattha parakkamanaṃ, evaṃ idha avacanīyakaraṇatāti cattāri aṅgāni. Kuladūsake aṅgesu yathā tattha parakkamanaṃ, evaṃ idha chandādīhi pāpananti cattāri aṅgāni. Iti imāni aṅgāni sodhetvā sace aṅgapāripūrī hoti, “saṅghādiseso”ti vattabbo. No ce, “nāyaṃ saṅghādiseso, thullaccayādīsu aññatarāpattī”ti vatvā “nāyaṃ vuṭṭhānagāminī, desanāgāminī ayaṃ āpatti, tasmā patirūpassa bhikkhussa santike desehī”ti vatvā desāpetabbo.

Therefore, when monks come to a Vinaya expert intending to undertake rehabilitation from a grave offense, the Vinaya expert should ask, “What offense have you committed?” If he says, “I have committed a Saṅghādisesa,” then ask, “Which Saṅghādisesa?” When he replies, “This one,” then for emission of semen, there are three factors: the intention to emit with the desire for release, the effort, and the actual emission. For physical contact, there are five factors: a human female, the perception of her as a female, lustful desire for physical contact, the effort driven by that lust, and the actual engagement in physical contact such as seizing of hands. For lewd speech, there are five factors: a human female, the perception of her as a female, lustful desire for lewd speech, the utterance motivated by that lust, and her understanding it at that moment. For praising personal service, there are five factors: a human female, the perception of her as a female, lustful desire for personal service, the praise spoken due to that lust, and her understanding it at that moment. For acting as a go-between, there are five factors: those for whom the act is performed are of human birth, they are capable of understanding words, and the act involves receiving, investigating, and delivering the message. For building a hut, there are factors such as: the site not being designated, exceeding the prescribed size, being built for oneself, and being a dwelling with plastering. Among those related to measurements and so forth, there are six types of factors. For constructing a vihāra, the same six factors apply. For a malicious accusation, there are five factors: the one being accused is a fully ordained monk, the perception of him as pure, the Pārājika offense with which he is accused is groundless in terms of what was seen, heard, or suspected, the accusation is made face-to-face with the intention of disrobing him, and his understanding it at that moment. For a partial accusation, there are six factors: taking up even a minor aspect or a trace of another party's case in a dispute, plus the previous five factors. For causing schism in the Saṅgha, there are four factors: striving for division, being admonished through a formal act of the Dhamma, the conclusion of the formal announcement, and not abandoning the view. For supporting a schism, there are four factors: just as striving is a factor there, here it is following along. For being difficult to correct, there are four factors: just as striving is a factor there, here it is making oneself uncorrectable. For corrupting families, there are four factors: just as striving is a factor there, here it is causing harm through favoritism and so forth. Thus, having examined these factors, if there is a full complement of factors, it should be declared, “This is a Saṅghādisesa.” If not, it should be said, “This is not a Saṅghādisesa; it is one of the Thullaccaya or other offenses. This offense does not lead to rehabilitation; it is an offense leading to confession. Therefore, confess it in the presence of a suitable monk,” and he should be instructed to confess.

Atha pana anāpatticchāyā paññāyati, “anāpattī”ti vatvā uyyojetabbā. Sace pana saṅghādisesacchāyā paññāyati, “tvaṃ imaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā chādesi, na chādesī”ti pucchitvā “na chādemī”ti vutte “tena hi tvaṃ na parivāsāraho, mānattārahova hotī”ti vattabbo. “Chādemī”ti pana vutte “dasasu ākāresu aññatarakāraṇena [M 2.0221] chādesi, udāhu aññakāraṇenā”ti pucchitvā “dasasu aññatarakāraṇenā”ti vutte “evampi mānattāraho hoti, na parivāsāraho”ti vattabbo. Atha “aññakāraṇenā”ti vadati, evaṃ santepi “tvaṃ āpattiāpannabhāvaṃ jānanto paṭicchādesi, udāhu ajānanto”ti pucchitvā “ajānanto paṭicchādemī”ti vutte ca “āpattiāpannabhāvaṃ saranto paṭicchādesi, udāhu visaritvā paṭicchādesī”ti pucchitvā “visaritvā paṭicchādemī”ti vutte ca “āpattiāpannabhāve vematiko hutvā paṭicchādesi, udāhu nibbematiko hutvā”ti pucchitvā “vematiko hutvā”ti vutte ca “na tvaṃ parivāsāraho, mānattārahova hotī”ti vattabbo.

But if a semblance of no offense is apparent, he should be told, "There is no offense," and dismissed. However, if a semblance of a Saṅghādisesa offense is apparent, he should be asked, "Having committed this offense, did you conceal it, or not conceal it?" If he says, "I did not conceal it," he should be told, "Then you are not fit for probation—you are only fit for mānatta." But if he says, "I concealed it," he should be asked, "Did you conceal it for one of the ten reasons, or for another reason?" If he says, "For one of the ten reasons," he should be told, "Even so, you are fit for mānatta, not fit for probation." Then, if he says, "For another reason," even so he should be asked, "Knowing that you had committed an offense, did you conceal it, or unknowingly?" And if he says, "I concealed it unknowingly," he should be asked further, "Remembering that you had committed an offense, did you conceal it, or having forgotten?" And if he says, "I concealed it having forgotten," he should be asked, "Being doubtful about having committed an offense, did you conceal it, or being without doubt?" And if he says, "While being doubtful," he should be told, "You are not fit for probation—you are only fit for mānatta."

Atha “jānanto paṭicchādemī”ti vutte ca “saranto paṭicchādemī”ti vutte ca “nibbematiko hutvā paṭicchādemī”ti vutte ca “tvaṃ parivāsāraho”ti vattabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ samuccayakkhandhake (cūḷava. 144) “so evaṃ vadati ‘yāyaṃ, āvuso, āpatti jānapaṭicchannā, dhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ, dhammattā ruhati. Yā ca khvāyaṃ, āvuso, āpatti ajānappaṭicchannā, adhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ, adhammattā na [V 2.0162] ruhati. Ekissā, āvuso, āpattiyā bhikkhu mānattāraho’”ti ca, “so evaṃ vadati ‘yāyaṃ āpatti saramānapaṭicchannā, dhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ, dhammattā ruhati. Yā ca khvāyaṃ āpatti asaramānapaṭicchannā, adhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ, adhammattā na ruhati. Ekissā, āvuso, āpattiyā bhikkhu mānattāraho’”ti ca, “so evaṃ vadati ‘yāyaṃ, āvuso, āpatti nibbematikapaṭicchannā, dhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ, dhammattā ruhati. Yā ca khvāyaṃ, āvuso, āpatti [M 2.0222] vematikapaṭicchannā, adhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ, adhammattā na ruhati. Ekissā, āvuso, āpattiyā bhikkhumānattāraho’”ti ca.

Then, when it is said, "I conceal knowing," and when it is said, "I conceal remembering," and when it is said, "I conceal without uncertainty," it should be said to him, "You are fit for probation." For it is said in the Samuccayakkhandhaka (Cūḷavagga 144): "He speaks thus: 'This offense, friend, which is concealed knowingly—the giving of probation for that offense is lawful; because it is lawful, it is valid. But this offense, friend, which is concealed unknowingly—the giving of probation for that offense is unlawful; because it is unlawful, it is not valid. For one offense, friend, a monk is fit for mānatta.'" And: "He speaks thus: 'This offense, friend, which is concealed remembering—the giving of probation for that offense is lawful; because it is lawful, it is valid. But this offense, friend, which is concealed not remembering—the giving of probation for that offense is unlawful; because it is unlawful, it is not valid. For one offense, friend, a monk is fit for mānatta.'" And: "He speaks thus: 'This offense, friend, which is concealed without uncertainty—the giving of probation for that offense is lawful; because it is lawful, it is valid. But this offense, friend, which is concealed with uncertainty—the giving of probation for that offense is unlawful; because it is unlawful, it is not valid. For one offense, friend, a monk is fit for mānatta.'"

Evaṃ parivāsārahabhāvaṃ pakāsetvā “ayaṃ bhikkhu parivāsāraho, tīsu parivāsesu kataraparivāsāraho”ti cintetvā “bhikkhu tvaṃ kati āpattiyo chādesī”ti pucchitvā “ekaṃ āpatti”nti vā “dve tīṇi tatuttari vā āpattiyo chādemī”ti vā vutte “katīhaṃ tvaṃ āpattiṃ paṭicchādesī”ti pucchitvā “ekāhamevāhaṃ paṭicchādemī”ti vā “dvīhaṃ tīhaṃ tatuttari vā paṭicchādemī”ti vā vutte “yāvatīhaṃ paṭicchādesi, tāvatīhaṃ tvaṃ paṭivasissasī”ti vattabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā “yāvatīhaṃ jānaṃ paṭicchādeti, tāvatīhaṃ tena bhikkhunā akāmā parivatthabba”nti. Tato “ayaṃ bhikkhu āpattipariyantaṃ jānāti, tasmā paṭicchannaparivāsāraho”ti (pārā. 442) ñatvā tadanurūpā kammavācā kātabbā.

Having thus declared his eligibility for probation, one should consider: "This monk is fit for probation; for which of the three probations is he fit?" Then, having asked him: "Monk, how many offenses have you concealed?" and when he has said, "I have concealed one offense," or "two, three, or more offenses," one should ask: "For how many days have you concealed the offense?" When he has answered, "I have concealed it for one day," or "two days, three days, or more," he should be told: "For as many days as you concealed it, for that many days you must undergo probation." For this was declared by the Blessed One: "For as many days as one knowingly conceals an offense, for that many days must that monk unwillingly undergo probation." Then, knowing: "This monk knows the extent of his offenses; therefore he is fit for concealed probation" (Pārā. 442), the appropriate formal act should be performed accordingly.

Ettha ca āpattipariyantapucchanaṃ kammavācākaraṇatthameva hoti, rattipariyantapucchanaṃ pana tadatthañceva suddhantaparivāsassa ananurūpabhāvadassanatthañca hoti. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cuḷava. aṭṭha. 102) “so duvidho cūḷasuddhanto mahāsuddhantoti, duvidhopi cesa rattiparicchedaṃ sakalaṃ vā ekaccaṃ vā ajānantassa ca asarantassa ca tattha vematikassa ca dātabbo. Āpattipariyantaṃ pana ‘ahaṃ ettakā āpattiyo āpanno’ti jānātu vā, mā vā, akāraṇameta”nti. Tato tassa bhikkhuno nisīdanaṭṭhānaṃ jānitabbaṃ. Duvidhañhi nisīdanaṭṭhānaṃ anikkhittavattena nisīditabbaṭṭhānaṃ, nikkhittavattena nisīditabbaṭṭhānanti.

Here, the questioning about the extent of offenses is solely for the purpose of performing the formal act. The questioning about the extent of nights, however, is both for that purpose and for the purpose of showing the unsuitability of the suddhanta probation. For it is stated in the commentary (Cuḷava. Aṭṭha. 102): “This suddhanta is twofold: minor suddhanta and major suddhanta. Both of these should be given to one who does not know the entire or a part of the number of nights, or who does not remember, or who is in doubt about it. But as for the extent of offenses, whether he knows or not, ‘I have committed this many offenses,’ that is not a factor.” Then, the seating place for that monk should be known. For the seating place is twofold: the place where one should sit without having laid aside the observances, and the place where one should sit having laid aside the observances.

Tattha [M 2.0223] appabhikkhuke vihāre sabhāgabhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne upacārasīmāparicchinno antovihāro anikkhittavattena nisīditabbaṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Upacārasīmaṃ atikkamma mahāmaggato okkamma [V 2.0163] gumbavatipaṭicchannaṭṭhānaṃ nikkhittavattena nisīditabbaṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) “sace appabhikkhuko vihāro hoti, sabhāgā bhikkhū vasanti, vattaṃ anikkhipitvā vihāreyeva rattipariggaho kātabbo. Atha na sakkā sodhetuṃ, vuttanayeneva vattaṃ nikkhipitvā paccūsasamaye ekena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ mānattavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayeneva upacārasīmaṃ atikkamitvā mahāmaggā okkamma paṭicchannaṭṭhāne nisīditvā antoaruṇeyeva vuttanayeneva vattaṃ samādiyitvā tassa bhikkhuno parivāso ārocetabbo”ti. “Mānattavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayenevā”ti ca “sace appabhikkhuko vihāro hoti, sabhāgā bhikkhū vasanti, vattaṃ anikkhipitvā antovihāreyeva rattiyo gaṇetabbā. Atha na sakkā sodhetuṃ, vuttanayeneva vattaṃ nikkhipitvā paccūsasamaye catūhi pañcahi vā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepato, aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānato dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā mahāmaggato okkamma gumbena vā vatiyā vā paṭicchannaṭṭhāne nisīditabba”nti (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 238) idaṃ vacanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

In this regard, in a monastery with few monks, in a residence of monks of the same affiliation, the inner monastery delimited by the proximity boundary is the place where one should sit without having laid aside the observances. Having crossed the proximity boundary and gone off the main road to a place concealed by bushes or a fence, this is the place where one should sit having laid aside the observances. For it was said in the commentary (Cūḷava. Aṭṭha. 102): “If it is a monastery with few monks, and monks of the same affiliation reside there, the reckoning of nights should be done within the monastery itself without laying aside the observances. But if it is not possible to investigate, then having laid aside the observances in the manner described, at dawn, together with one monk, having crossed the proximity boundary in the manner described in the explanation of Mānatta, and having gone off the main road to a concealed spot, one should sit there. Just before sunrise, in the manner described, having undertaken the observances again, the probation of that monk should be announced.” And “in the manner described in the explanation of Mānatta” is said in reference to this statement (Vinayasangaha-aṭṭhakathā 238): “If it is a monastery with few monks, and monks of the same affiliation reside there, the nights should be counted within the inner monastery itself without laying aside the observances. But if it is not possible to investigate, then having laid aside the observances in the manner described, at dawn, together with four or five monks, having gone two stone-throws beyond the enclosure of an enclosed monastery, or from a place fit for an enclosure of an unenclosed one, and having gone off the main road, one should sit in a place concealed by bushes or a fence.”

Tattha appabhikkhuko vihāro hotīti idaṃ bahubhikkhuke vihāre aññe bhikkhū gacchanti, aññe bhikkhū āgacchanti, tasmā ratticchedavattabhedakāraṇāni sodhetuṃ dukkarattā vuttaṃ. Vakkhati hi “atha na sakkā sodhetu”nti. Sabhāgā bhikkhū vasantīti idaṃ visabhāgānaṃ verībhikkhūnaṃ santike vattaṃ ārocento pakāsetukāmo hoti[M 2.0224], tasmā vuttaṃ. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102; vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 236) “tasmā averisabhāgassa santike ārocetabbā. Yo pana visabhāgo hoti sutvā pakāsetukāmo, evarūpassa upajjhāyassapi santike nārocetabbā”ti, tasmā visabhāgānaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne vattaṃ asamādiyitvā bahiyeva kātumpi vaṭṭatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vihāreyevāti antoupacārasīmāyameva. Vakkhati hi “atha na sakkā…pe… upacārasīmaṃ atikkamitvā”ti. Rattipariggaho kātabboti rattigaṇanā kātabbā. Vuttañhi mānattavaṇṇanāyaṃ “rattiyo gaṇetabbā”ti. Atha na sakkā sodhetunti bahubhikkhukattā vā vihārassa visabhāgānaṃ vasanaṭṭhānattā vā ratticchedavattābhedakāraṇānipi sodhetuṃ na sakkā. Vattaṃ nikkhipitvāti parivāsavattaṃ nikkhipitvā. Paccūsasamayeti pacchimayāmakāle aruṇodayato puretarameva. Tathā hi vakkhati “antoaruṇeyeva vuttanayena vattaṃ samādiyitvā tassa bhikkhuno parivāso ārocetabbo”ti. Ekena bhikkhunā saddhinti vippavāsaratticchedavimuccanatthaṃ vinā pakatattena sabhikkhukaāvāsaabhikkhukaanāvāsagamanasaṅkhātavattabhedavimuccanatthañca [V 2.0164] vuttaṃ. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo aññatra pakatattena aññatra antarāyā”ti (cūḷava. 76).

Here, the phrase ‘it is a monastery with few monks’ is stated because in a monastery with many monks, some monks are leaving and other monks are arriving, and therefore it is difficult to investigate the reasons for the interruption of nights and the breaking of observances. For it will be said, ‘Then it is not possible to investigate.’ The phrase ‘monks of the same affiliation are dwelling’ is stated because to announce the observance in the presence of hostile monks of a different affiliation is to wish to reveal it. For it is stated in the commentary (Cūḷava. Aṭṭha. 102; Vinayasangaha-aṭṭhakathā 236): ‘Therefore, it should be announced in the presence of one who is not hostile and is of the same affiliation. But if one is of a different affiliation and wishes to reveal it after hearing, it should not be announced even in the presence of one’s own preceptor.’ Thus, it should be understood that it is permissible to perform it entirely outside, without undertaking the observance in a dwelling place of those of a different affiliation. ‘In the monastery itself’ means within the proximity boundary itself. For it will be said, ‘Then it is not possible…pe… having crossed the proximity boundary.’ ‘The reckoning of nights should be done’ means the counting of nights should be done. For it is stated in the explanation of the Mānatta: ‘The nights should be counted.’ ‘Then it is not possible to investigate’ means that because the monastery has many monks or is a dwelling place of those of a different affiliation, it is not possible to investigate the reasons for the interruption of nights and the breaking of observances. ‘Having laid aside the observance’ means having laid aside the probationary observance. ‘At dawn-time’ means in the last watch of the night, just before sunrise. For thus it will be said, ‘Just before sunrise, in the prescribed manner, the observance should be undertaken, and then the probation of that monk should be announced.’ ‘With one monk’ is stated for the purpose of being free from the interruption of nights due to absence, and for the purpose of being free from the breaking of observances known as going from a residence with monks to a residence without monks or to a non-residence without a regular monk. For it is said (Cūḷava. 76): ‘Monks, a monk on probation should not go from a residence with monks to a residence without monks or to a non-residence, except with a regular monk or unless there is an obstacle.’

Mānattavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayenāti “parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepato, aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānato dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā”ti vuttanayena. Yadi evaṃ visamamidaṃ nayadassanaṃ, parikkhepaparikkhepārahaṭṭhāne eva hi upacārasīmā hoti, kasmā tattha upacārasīmato dveleḍḍupātātikkamo vutto, idha pana upacārasīmātikkamo evāti[M 2.0225]? Saccaṃ, tathāpi vihāre bhikkhūnaṃ sajjhāyādisaddasavanasabbhāvato suvidūrātikkamo vutto, idha pana upacārasīmato atikkamamattopi atikkamoyevāti katvā vutto. Buddhamataññuno hi aṭṭhakathācariyā. Tathā hi vuttaṃ vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 97) “parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepatotiādi kiñcāpi pāḷiyaṃ natthi, atha kho aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ vacanena tathā eva paṭipajjitabbanti ca vutta”nti.

In the explanation of the Mānatta, it is in the manner stated: “Having gone beyond two stone-throws from the surrounding area of an enclosed monastery, or from a place fit to be a surrounding area of an unenclosed monastery,” as stated. If this is an inconsistent presentation of the method, since the surrounding area or the place fit to be a surrounding area is indeed the proximity boundary, why is it stated there that the transgression is beyond two stone-throws from the proximity boundary, while here it is simply the transgression of the proximity boundary itself? It is true. However, in the case of the monastery, a very distant transgression is mentioned, because of the possibility of hearing the monks’ recitation and other sounds. Here, however, even merely a transgression beyond the proximity boundary is considered a transgression. The commentary teachers are indeed knowers of the Buddha’s intention. Thus, it is stated in the Vajirabuddhi sub-commentary (Vajira. Ṭī. Cūḷavagga 97): “Although the phrase ‘from the surrounding area of an enclosed monastery’ etc. is not found in the Pāli text, it should nevertheless be practiced accordingly according to the word of the commentary teachers.”

Mānattavaṇṇanāyaṃ catūhi pañcahi vā bhikkhūhi saddhinti idaṃ pana ūnegaṇecaraṇaratticchedavimuccanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvātiādi aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ savanūpacāradassanūpacāravijahanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tenevāha ṭīkācariyo “dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvāti idaṃ vihāre bhikkhūnaṃ sajjhāyādisaddasavanūpacāravijahanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, ‘mahāmaggato okkammāti idaṃ maggapaṭipannānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ savanūpacāravijahanatthaṃ, gumbena vātiādi dassanūpacāravijahanattha”nti. Tasmā yathāvuttaṃ duvidhaṃ ṭhānaṃ parivasantamānattacārikabhikkhūhi nisīditabbaṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Tesu ca yadi antovihāreyeva nisīditvā parivasati, upacārasīmagatānaṃ sabbesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ārocetabbaṃ hoti. Atha bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ, diṭṭharūpānaṃ sutasaddānaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Adiṭṭhaasutānampi antodvādasahatthagatānaṃ ārocetabbameva. Vuttañhi vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ “vattaṃ nikkhipitvā vasantassa upacārasīmagatānaṃ sabbesaṃ ārocanakiccaṃ natthi, diṭṭharūpānaṃ sutasaddānaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Adiṭṭhaassutānampi antodvādasahatthagatānaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Idaṃ vattaṃ nikkhipitvā vasantassa lakkhaṇanti vutta”nti. Idañca vattaṃ anikkhipitvā vasantassa antovihāreyeva rattipariggahassa ca nikkhipitvā vasantassa upacārasīmaṃ atikkamitvā vattasamādānassa ca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttattā vuttaṃ. Upacāro pana [M 2.0226] antosīmāya [V 2.0165] ṭhitānaṃ sakalaupacārasīmā hoti, bahiupacārasīmāya ṭhitānaṃ dvādasahatthamattaṃ. Teneva hi uddesabhattādisaṅghalābho yadi antosīmāya uppajjati, sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghassa hoti. Yadi bahisīmāyaṃ, dvādasahatthabbhantare pattabhikkhūnaṃ, tasmā upacāravasenapi esa attho viññāyati. Tathā hi vuttaṃ vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 97) “atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāti dvādasahatthe upacāre sallakkhetvā anikkhittavattānaṃ upacārasīmāya āgatabhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā sahavāsādikaṃ veditabbanti ca vutta”nti.

In the explanation of the Mānatta, the phrase “together with four or five monks” is stated for the purpose of being free from the interruption of nights due to going with an incomplete group. The phrase “having gone beyond two stone-throws” and so on is stated for the purpose of avoiding the proximity of hearing and the proximity of seeing of other monks. Therefore, the sub-commentary teacher says: “‘Having gone beyond two stone-throws’—this is stated for avoiding the proximity of hearing sounds like recitation of monks in the monastery. ‘Turning away from the great road’—this is stated for avoiding the proximity of hearing of monks walking along the path. ‘By a clump of trees’ and so on—this is stated for avoiding the proximity of seeing.” Thus, the two kinds of places as described are the places where monks observing probation and Mānatta should sit. Among these, if one observes probation sitting within the monastery itself, one must inform all the monks within the proximity boundary. If one is outside the proximity boundary, one must inform those whose forms are seen or whose voices are heard. Even those whose forms are not seen or voices not heard must be informed if they are within twelve cubits. As stated in the Vajirabuddhi sub-commentary: “For one who is staying having laid aside the observances, there is no duty to inform all those within the proximity boundary. Only those whose forms are seen or whose voices are heard must be informed. Even those whose forms are not seen or voices not heard must be informed if they are within twelve cubits. This is the characteristic for one who is staying having laid aside the observances.” This is stated because it is mentioned in the commentary regarding the reckoning of nights for one staying within the monastery itself without having laid aside the observances, and regarding the undertaking of observances for one who, having laid them aside, stays after transgressing the proximity boundary. The proximity, however, for those standing within the boundary is the entire proximity boundary, while for those standing outside the proximity boundary, it is only twelve cubits. Therefore, if alms by invitation and other gains for the Sangha arise within the boundary, they belong to the Sangha within the boundary. If they arise outside the boundary, they belong to the monks who have arrived within twelve cubits. Thus, this meaning is understood by way of proximity. As further stated in the Vajirabuddhi sub-commentary (Vajira. Ṭī. Cūḷavagga 97): “‘Having considered the existence’—means having considered the twelve-cubit proximity; having considered that those who have not laid aside the observances have come within the proximity boundary, co-residence and so on should be understood.”

Evaṃ anikkhittavattānaṃ hutvā parivasantānaṃ antovihāreyeva vasanassa, nikkhittavattānaṃ hutvā parivasantānaṃ vihārato bahi dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā vasanassa ca aṭṭhakathādīsu pakaraṇesu āgatattā tathāgatanayo pakaraṇāgatanayo hoti. Idāni pana ācariyā anikkhittavattassa ca ratticchedavattabhedadose pariharituṃ atidukkarattā, nikkhittavattassa ca devasikaṃ paccūsasamaye bahisīmagamanassa dukkhattā, vāḷasarīsapādiparisayassa ca āsaṅkitabbabhāvato ratticchedavattabhedapariharaṇavasena lakkhaṇapāripūrimeva manasi karontā nikkhittavattāpi samānā antovihāreyeva parivāsavasanañca mānattacaraṇañca karonti.

Thus, the dwelling within the monastery for those who observe probation without having laid aside their observances, and the dwelling outside the monastery beyond two clod-throws for those who observe probation having laid aside their observances, are both methods that have come down in the commentaries and other treatises, and are therefore the traditional method, the method found in the treatises. However, at present, the teachers, considering the extreme difficulty of avoiding the faults of breaking the night and breaking the observance for one who has not laid aside his observances, and the hardship for one who has laid aside his observances to go outside the boundary every dawn, as well as the possibility of danger from wild animals, reptiles, and so forth—and focusing solely on the complete fulfillment of the characteristics by avoiding the breaking of the night and the breaking of the observance—even while having laid aside their observances, undertake their probationary residence and mānatta practice within the monastery itself.

Ekacce ācariyā bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ patirūpaṭṭhāne pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasanasālaṃ kārāpetvā pārivāsikabhikkhūnaṃ nipajjanamañcaṃ sabbato channaparicchinnaṃ sadvārabandhanaṃ suguttaṃ kārāpetvā taṃ padesaṃ vatiyā parikkhipāpetvā sāyanhasamaye tattha gantvā upaṭṭhākasāmaṇerādayo nivattāpetvā purimayāme vā majjhimayāme vā samantato saddachijjanakāle pakatattabhikkhū sālāyaṃ nipajjāpetvā pārivāsikabhikkhū [M 2.0227] vattaṃ samādāpetvā ārocāpetvā attano attano mañcakesu nipajjāpetvā pacchimayāmakāle uṭṭhāpetvā aruṇe uṭṭhite ārocāpetvā vattaṃ nikkhipāpenti. Esa nayo pakaraṇesu anāgatattā ācariyānaṃ matena katattā ācariyanayo nāma. Esa nayopi yathārutato pakaraṇesu anāgatopi pakaraṇānulomavasena ratticchedavattabhedadose pariharitvā lajjipesalehi bahussutehi sikkhākāmehi vinaye pakataññūhi vicārito samāno sundaro pasatthova hoti, tasmā “anulomanayo”tipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati.

Some teachers, having had a dwelling hall built for monks of normal status in a suitable place outside the proximity boundary, and having had a sleeping couch prepared for the probationary monks that is covered on all sides, enclosed, securely fastened with a door, and well-guarded, and having had that area enclosed with a fence, go there in the evening. They dismiss the attendant novices and others, and during the first or middle watch of the night, at the time when sounds cease, they have the monks of normal status lie down in the hall. They then have the probationary monks undertake their observance and report it, and have each of them lie down on his own couch. In the last watch of the night, they rouse them, and when dawn has risen, they have them report and lay aside their observance. This method is called the 'teachers’ method' because it is not found in the treatises and was established according to the teachers’ opinion. Even though this method is not found in the treatises according to its literal wording, when it is examined by modest, scrupulous, learned monks who are desirous of training and well-versed in the Vinaya, while avoiding the faults of breaking the night and breaking the observance in a way that conforms to the treatises, it is indeed excellent and praiseworthy. Therefore, it is also proper to call it the 'conforming method'.

Nanu ca anikkhittavattānaṃyeva antovihāre vasanaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, atha kasmā nikkhittavattāpi samānā vasantīti? Saccaṃ, tattha pana appabhikkhukattā sabhāgabhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānattā [V 2.0166] ca ratticchedavattabhedadose ca pariharituṃ sakkuṇeyyabhāvato sakalarattindivampi vattaṃ anikkhipitvā vasanaṃ vuttaṃ, idha pana tathā asakkuṇeyyabhāvato divā vattaṃ nikkhipitvā rattiyaṃ samādiyanto āgantukānaṃ anāgamanakālabhāvato, saddachijjanakālabhāvato ca ratticchedādidose pariharituṃ sakkuṇeyyattā tadanulomoyeva hotīti mantvā ācariyā evaṃ karontīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

But is it not stated in the commentary that only those who have not laid aside their observances should dwell within the monastery? Then why do those who have laid aside their observances also dwell there? It is true. However, in that case, due to there being few monks and because it was a dwelling place for monks of similar standing, and because they were able to avoid the faults of breaking the night and breaking the observance, it was stated that one should dwell without laying aside the observance for the entire day and night. Here, however, since it is not possible to do so, one lays aside the observance during the day and undertakes it at night. Because it is a time when visiting monks do not arrive, and a time when sounds cease, one is able to avoid faults such as breaking the night. Considering that this is in conformity with that, the teachers act in this way—this should be understood.

Evaṃ hotu, bahiupacārasīmāya vasantānaṃ paṭicchannaṭṭhāne nisīdanameva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, na pakatattasālākaraṇamañcakaraṇādīni, atha kasmā etāni karontīti? Saccaṃ, tathāpi pakatattasālākaraṇaṃ pārivāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pakatattehi bhikkhūhi vippavāsaratticchedavattabhedadosapariharaṇatthaṃ, taṃ “tayo kho, upāli, pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā sahavāso, vippavāso, anārocanā”ti vuttapāṭhaṃ [M 2.0228] (cūḷava. 83) anulometi. Mañcakaraṇaṃ sahavāsaratticchedavattabhedadosapariharaṇatthaṃ, taṃ “na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabba”nti vuttapāṭhañca (cūḷava. 81) yathāvuttapāṭhañca anulometi. Ādi-saddena sāyanhasamaye gamanādīni saṅgaṇhāti. Tesu aṭṭhakathāyaṃ paccūsasamaye gamane eva vuttepi sāyanhasamaye gamanaṃ rattigamanassa bahuparissayattā parissayavinodanatthaṃ, taṃ “antarāyato parimuccanatthāya gantabbamevā”ti vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāpāṭhaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76) anulometi. Upaṭṭhākasāmaṇerādīnaṃ nivattāpanaṃ anupasampannena sahaseyyasaṅkānivattanatthaṃ, taṃ “yo pana bhikkhu anupasampannena sahaseyyaṃ kappeyya, pācittiya”nti vuttaṃ mātikāpāṭhaṃ (pāci. 49) anulometi. Purimayāme vā majjhimayāme vā samantato saddachijjanakāle pakatattabhikkhū sālāyaṃ nipajjāpetvā pārivāsikabhikkhūnaṃ vattasamādāpanaṃ aññabhikkhūnaṃ saddasavanavivajjanatthaṃ, taṃ anārocanaratticchedadosapariharaṇatthaṃ, taṃ yathāvuttaratticchedapāṭhaṃ anulometi.

So be it. The commentary states that for those dwelling outside the precinct boundary, sitting in a secluded place is allowed, but not constructing a hall for monks in good standing, making a bed, and so forth. Then why do they do these things? Indeed, constructing a hall for monks in good standing is for the purpose of avoiding the faults of breaking the night and breaking the observance due to separation from monks in good standing for those monks undergoing probation. This conforms to the passage: 'There are, Upāli, three ways a monk on probation breaks his nights: by co-residence, by separation, and by non-reporting' (Cūḷavagga 83). Making a bed is for the purpose of avoiding the faults of breaking the night and breaking the observance due to co-residence. This conforms to the passage: 'Monks, a monk on probation should not dwell in a single covered dwelling with a monk in good standing, nor in a single uncovered dwelling, nor in a single covered or uncovered dwelling' (Cūḷavagga 81), and also to the previously mentioned passage. The word 'and so forth' includes going in the evening and so on. Among these, although the commentary only mentions going in the dawn, going in the evening is for the purpose of removing dangers, as traveling at night involves many dangers. This conforms to the commentary passage: 'One should go only to be freed from dangers' (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 76). Dismissing attendant novices and others is to remove the suspicion of sleeping together with an unordained person. This conforms to the rule in the Vinaya code: 'If a monk sleeps together with an unordained person, it is an offense of expiation' (Pācittiya 49). Having the monks in good standing lie down in the hall during the first or middle watch, when sounds are completely cut off everywhere, and having the probationary monks undertake their observance, is to prevent other monks from hearing the sound. This is to avoid the fault of breaking the night due to non-reporting, and it conforms to the previously mentioned passage on breaking the night.

Nanu ca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ antoaruṇeyeva vattasamādāpanaṃ vuttaṃ, atha kasmā “purimayāmamajjhimayāmesū”ti vuttanti? Nāyaṃ doso, hiyyoaruṇuggamanato paṭṭhāya hi yāva ajjaaruṇuggamanā eko rattindivo ajjaaruṇassa anto nāma, ajjaaruṇato paṭṭhāya pacchākālo aruṇassa bahi nāma, tasmā purimamajjhimayāmesu katavattasamādānampi aruṇodayato [V 2.0167] pure katattā antoaruṇe kataṃyeva hoti. Vattaṃ asamādiyitvā nipajjane ca sati niddāvasena aruṇuggamanakālaṃ ajānitvā vattasamādānaṃ atikkantaṃ [M 2.0229] bhaveyya, tasmā puretarameva samādānaṃ katvā nipajjanaṃ ñāyāgataṃ hoti, “antoaruṇeyeva vuttanayeneva vattaṃ samādiyitvā”ti vuttaaṭṭhakathāpāṭhañca (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) anulometi.

But is it not said in the commentary that the undertaking of the observance is done only within the dawn? Then why is it said, 'in the first and middle watches'? There is no fault here. For indeed, from the rising of dawn yesterday until the rising of dawn today, one day and night is called 'within today's dawn,' while the time after today's dawn is called 'outside the dawn.' Therefore, even an undertaking of the observance made in the first or middle watches is still considered done within the dawn because it is done before the rising of dawn. And if one lies down without undertaking the observance, due to sleep one might not know the time of dawn, and the undertaking of the observance would be missed. Hence, it is reasonable to undertake the observance earlier and then lie down. This also conforms to the commentary's statement, 'having undertaken the observance in the manner said only within the dawn' (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102).

Evaṃ hotu, evaṃ santepi kasmā “ārocāpetvā”ti vuttaṃ, nanu māḷakasīmāyaṃ samādinnakāleyeva vattamārocitanti? Saccaṃ ārocitaṃ, ayaṃ pana bhikkhu divā vattaṃ nikkhipitvā nisinno, idāni samādinno, tasmā māḷakasīmāya ārocitampi puna ārocetabbaṃ hoti. Idampi “antoaruṇeyeva vuttanayeneva vattaṃ samādiyitvā tassa bhikkhuno parivāso ārocetabbo”ti pāṭhaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) anulometi. Atha “attano attano mañcakesu nipajjāpetvā”ti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu aññamaññassa mañcesu nipajjamānāpi pakatattasālato nibbodakapatanaṭṭhānato bahi nipajjamānā sahavāsaratticchedadosato muttāyevāti? Na panevaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Na hi pārivāsiko pakatattabhikkhūheva ekacchanne nipanno sahavāsaratticchedappatto hoti, atha kho aññamaññampi hotiyeva. Vuttañcetaṃ samantapāsādikāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 81) “sace hi dve pārivāsikā ekato vaseyyuṃ, te aññamaññassa ajjhācāraṃ ñatvā agāravā vā vippaṭisārino vā hutvā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ vā āpattiṃ āpajjeyyuṃ vibbhameyyuṃ vā, tasmā nesaṃ sahaseyyā sabbappakārena paṭikkhittā”ti. “Pacchimayāmakāle uṭṭhāpetvā aruṇe uṭṭhite ārocāpetvā vattaṃ nikkhipāpentī”ti ettha aruṇe anuṭṭhiteyeva vattanikkhipane kariyamāne ratticchedo hoti, sā ratti gaṇanūpagā na hoti, tasmā paṭhamaparicchede vuttaṃ aruṇakathāvinicchayaṃ oloketvā aruṇuggamanabhāvo suṭṭhu jānitabbo.

Let it be so. Even if it is thus, why is it said, 'having caused to announce'? Surely, the observance was announced when the undertaking was made at the Māḷaka boundary? Indeed, it was announced. But this monk, having laid aside the observance during the day and sat down, now undertakes it. Therefore, even if announced within the Māḷaka boundary, it must be announced again. This also conforms to the passage: 'Having undertaken the observance in the manner stated only within the dawn, the probation of that monk should be caused to be announced' (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102). Then, why is it said, 'having made them lie down on their own beds'? Surely, even if they lie down on each other's beds, lying outside the hall of monks in good standing or the place where the water for washing is poured, they are free from the fault of breaking the night due to co-residence? But it should not be seen thus. For a probationer does not incur the breaking of the night due to co-residence only when lying down under the same roof with monks in good standing; it also occurs among themselves. And this is stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 81): 'If two probationers were to dwell together, knowing each other's transgression, being disrespectful or remorseful, they might commit a worse offense or become confused. Therefore, their sleeping together is entirely prohibited.' As for 'In the last watch of the night, having roused them, when dawn has risen, having caused to announce, they make them lay aside the observance'—here, if the laying aside of the observance is done before dawn has risen, the night is broken. That night is not counted. Therefore, the discussion on the determination of dawn stated in the first section should be examined, and the state of dawn’s rising should be well understood.

“Ārocāpetvā [M 2.0230] vattaṃ nikkhipāpetabba”nti vuttaṃ. Kasmā ārocāpeti, nanu samādinnakāleyeva ārocitanti? Saccaṃ, tathāpi pārivāsikavattasamādānakāle ārocitesu bhikkhūsu ekacce nikkhipanakāle gacchanti, aññe āgacchanti, evaṃ parisasaṅkamanampi siyā, tathā ca sati abhinavāgatānaṃ sabbhāvā ārocetabbaṃ hoti, asati pana abhinavāgatabhikkhumhi ārocanakiccaṃ natthi. Evaṃ santepi ārocane dosābhāvato puna ārocanaṃ ñāyāgataṃ hoti, mānattacaraṇakāle pana samādāne ārocitepi nikkhipane avassaṃ ārocetabbameva[V 2.0168]. Kasmā? Divasantarabhāvato. “Devasikaṃ ārocetabba”nti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 90) hi vuttaṃ. Evaṃ santepi sāyaṃ samādānakāle ārocessati, tasmā nikkhipane ārocanakiccaṃ natthīti ce? Na, sāyaṃ samādānakāle ete bhikkhū āgacchissantipi, na āgacchissantipi, anāgatānaṃ kathaṃ ārocetuṃ labhissati, anārocane ca sati ratticchedo siyā, tasmā tasmiṃ divase aruṇe uṭṭhite vattanikkhipanato pureyeva ārocetabbanti no mati, suṭṭhutaraṃ upadhāretvā gahetabbaṃ. Evaṃ pakaraṇāgatanayena vā pakaraṇānulomaācariyanayena vā sammāsambuddhassa āṇaṃ patiṭṭhāpentena vinayakovidena bahussutena lajjīpesalabhūtena vinayadharena visuddhikāmānaṃ pesalānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sīlavisuddhatthāya suṭṭhu vicāretvā parivāsavattāmānattacaraṇavattāni ācikkhitabbānīti.

“It should be announced before laying down the observance,” it is said. Why announce it? Was it not already announced at the time of undertaking? True, but when the probationary observance is undertaken, some monks who were informed leave at the time of laying it down, while others arrive. Thus, there may be a shifting of the assembly, and in such cases, the presence of those newly arrived must be announced. However, if no new monks have arrived, there is no need for an announcement. Even so, since there is no fault in announcing again, a repeated announcement is justifiable. But during the period of mānatta, even if it was announced at the time of undertaking, it must still be announced when laying it down. Why? Because of the interval of days. For it is said, “It should be announced daily” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 90). Even so, one might think, “It will be announced in the evening at the time of undertaking, so there is no need to announce it when laying it down.” But no—those monks may or may not arrive in the evening. How can one announce it to those who have not yet come? And if it is not announced, there could be a break in the observance. Therefore, our view is that on that day, when dawn has arisen, it should be announced just before laying down the observance. This should be carefully considered and appropriately understood. Thus, following either the method derived from the context or the method aligned with the tradition of the teachers, one who establishes the Buddha’s command—a skilled Vinaya expert, learned, modest, and virtuous—should thoroughly deliberate and explain the observances of probation and the practice of mānatta for the sake of the purity of virtue of virtuous monks who desire purity.

Imasmiṃ ṭhāne lajjībhikkhūnaṃ parivāsādikathāya kusalatthaṃ nānāvādanayo vuccate – keci bhikkhū “pakatattasālaṃ kurumānena tassā sālāya majjhe thambhaṃ nimittaṃ katvā tato dvādasahatthamattaṃ padesaṃ sallakkhetvā yathā paññatte [M 2.0231] pārivāsikānaṃ mañce nipannassa bhikkhussa gīvā tassa padesassa upari hoti, tathā paññāpetabbo. Evaṃ kate sukataṃ hotī”ti vadanti karonti ca. Ekacce “mañce nipannassa bhikkhussa kaṭi tassa padesassa upari hoti, yathā paññāpetabbo, evaṃ kate sukataṃ hotī”ti vadanti karonti ca, taṃ vacanaṃ neva pāḷiyaṃ, na aṭṭhakathāṭīkādīsu vijjati, kevalaṃ tesaṃ parikappameva. Ayaṃ pana nesaṃ adhippāyo siyā – “dvādasahatthaṃ pana upacāraṃ muñcitvā nisīdituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttavacanañca “atha dvādasahatthaṃ upacāraṃ okkamitvā ajānantasseva gacchati, ratticchedo hoti eva, vattabhedo pana natthī”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanañca (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97) “adiṭṭhaassutānampi antodvādasahatthagatānaṃ ārocetabba”nti vuttaṭīkāvacanañca (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.97) “adiṭṭhaassutānampi antodvādasahatthagatānaṃ ārocetabbaṃ, ‘idaṃ vattaṃ nikkhipitvā vasantassa lakkhaṇa’nti vutta”nti vuttavajirabuddhiṭīkāvacanañca (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 97) “atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāti dvādasahatthe upacāre sallakkhetvā, anikkhittavattānaṃ upacārasīmāya āgatabhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā sahavāsādikaṃ veditabba”nti vuttaṃ vajirabuddhiṭīkāvacanañca passitvā ayoniso atthaṃ gahetvā sabbattha dvādasahatthameva pamāṇaṃ, tato ūnampi adhikampi na vaṭṭati, tasmā yathāvuttanayena majjhe thambhato dvādasahatthamatte padese nipannassa bhikkhussa [V 2.0169] gīvā vā kaṭi vā hotu, evaṃ sante dvādasahatthappadese pārivāsikabhikkhu hoti, tato sahavāsato vā vippavāsato vā ratticchedavattabhedadosā na hontīti.

In this matter, various opinions are expressed for the benefit of scrupulous monks concerning the discussion of probation and so forth. Some monks say and do thus: “Having prepared a common hall, a pillar should be marked in the middle of that hall, and then a space measuring twelve cubits should be observed. The bed of a monk undergoing probation should be arranged so that when he lies down, his neck is above that space. When done thus, it is well done.” Some others say and do thus: “The bed should be arranged so that when the monk lies down, his waist is above that space. When done thus, it is well done.” That statement is not found in the Pāli Canon, nor in the commentaries or sub-commentaries; it is merely their own conjecture. However, this may be their intention: having seen the statement in the commentary, “It is permissible to sit, having left a twelve-cubit proximity;” and the statement in the commentary, “But if one enters the twelve-cubit proximity unknowingly, the night is broken, yet there is no breach of the observance” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 97); and the statement in the sub-commentary, “Even for those unseen and unheard, who have come within twelve cubits, they should be informed” (Sārattha-ṭīkā, Cūḷavagga 3.97); and the statement in the Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā, “Even for those unseen and unheard, who have come within twelve cubits, they should be informed, ‘This is the characteristic of one dwelling having laid aside the observance’” (Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā, Cūḷavagga 97); and the statement in the Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā, “Having observed the presence—that is, having observed the twelve-cubit proximity—co-residence, etc., should be understood by observing the arrival within the proximity boundary of those who have not laid aside the observance” (Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā, Cūḷavagga 97), they grasp the meaning improperly, making twelve cubits the measure everywhere—neither less nor more is permissible. Therefore, they think that if it is arranged so that when a monk lies down, his neck or waist is above a space of twelve cubits measured from the central pillar, then the monk undergoing probation is within the twelve-cubit space. Thus, the faults of breaking the night and breaching the observance, arising from co-residence or from separation, will not occur.

Tatrevaṃ yuttāyuttavicāraṇā kātabbā. Yathāvuttapāṭhesu paṭhamapāṭhassa ayamadhippāyo – pakatattabhikkhumhi chamāya [M 2.0232] nisinne yadi pārivāsikabhikkhu āsane nisīditukāmo, pakatattassa bhikkhuno nisinnaṭṭhānato dvādasahatthaṃ upacāraṃ muñcitvāva nisīdituṃ vaṭṭati, na dvādasahatthabbhantareti. Etena dvīsupi chamāya nisinnesu dvādasahatthabbhantarepi vaṭṭati, dvādasahatthappadesato bahi nisīdanto āsanepi nisīdituṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Tenāha “na chamāya nisinneti pakatatte bhūmiyaṃ nisinne itarena antamaso tiṇasantharepi uccatare vālikatalepi vā na nisīditabbaṃ, dvādasahatthaṃ pana upacāraṃ muñcitvā nisīdituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 81). Iti pakatatte chamāya nisinne pārivāsikena nisīditabbaṭṭhānadīpako ayaṃ pāṭho, na mañcapaññāpanaṭṭhānasayanaṭṭhānadīpako, taṃ pubbāparaparipuṇṇaṃ sakalaṃ pāṭhaṃ anoloketvā ekadesamattameva passitvā parikappavasena ayoniso adhippāyaṃ gaṇhanti.

In this case, the appropriateness or inappropriateness should be considered. As for the meaning of the first passage mentioned—when an ordinary monk is seated on the ground, if a probationary monk wishes to sit on a seat, it is permissible for him to sit only after leaving a twelve-cubit proximity from where the ordinary monk is seated, not within twelve cubits. By this, it is shown that even if both are seated on the ground, sitting within twelve cubits is permissible, and sitting on a seat outside the twelve-cubit area is also allowed. Therefore, it is said: Regarding the rule ‘When [an ordinary monk] is seated on the ground…,’ this means that when an ordinary monk is seated on the ground, the other (the probationary monk) should not sit even on a grass mat or a higher sandy surface, but it is permissible to sit after leaving a twelve-cubit proximity (Cūḷava. Aṭṭha. 81). Thus, this passage clarifies the seating position for a probationary monk when an ordinary monk is seated on the ground, not the place for arranging beds or the place for sleeping. Without examining the entire passage complete with its preceding and succeeding parts, some grasp the meaning improperly by seeing only a part and speculating.

Dutiyapāṭhassa pana ayamadhippāyo – bahi upacārasīmāya paṭicchannaṭṭhāne vattaṃ samādiyitvā nisinne bhikkhusmiṃ tassa nisinnaṭṭhānato dvādasahatthaṃ upacāraṃ okkamitvā tassa ajānantasseva añño bhikkhu gacchati, tassa pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedo hoti, vattabhedo pana natthi. Kasmā ratticchedo hoti? Upacāraṃ okkamitattā. Kasmā na vattabhedo? Ajānantattāti. Etena bahiupacārasīmāya upacāro dvādasahatthappamāṇo hoti ārocanakkhettabhūtoti dasseti. Tenāha “gumbena vā vatiyā vā paṭicchannaṭṭhāne nisīditabbaṃ, antoaruṇeyeva vuttanayena vattaṃ samādiyitvā ārocetabbaṃ. Sace añño koci bhikkhu kenacideva karaṇīyena taṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati, sace esa taṃ passati, saddaṃ vāssa suṇāti, ārocetabbaṃ. Anārocentassa ratticchedo ceva vattabhedo ca. Atha dvādasahatthaṃ [M 2.0233] upacāraṃ okkamitvā ajānantasseva gacchati, ratticchedo hoti eva, vattabhedo pana natthī”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97). Iti ayampi pāṭho ārocanakkhettadīpako hoti, na mañcapaññāpanādidīpakoti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

As for the meaning of the second passage—when a monk, having undertaken the observance in a concealed place outside the proximity boundary, is seated, and another monk, without the knowledge of the first, enters within twelve cubits of his seated position, the probationary monk’s night is broken, but there is no breach of the observance. Why is the night broken? Because the proximity has been entered. Why is there no breach of the observance? Because it was done unknowingly. By this, it is shown that outside the proximity boundary, the proximity is of twelve cubits in measure, being the field for announcement. Therefore, it is said: “One should sit in a concealed place, such as a thicket or a fence, undertake the observance in the manner described, and make the announcement only before dawn. If another monk comes to that place for some reason, if the first monk sees him or hears his voice, the announcement should be made. If it is not announced, both the night is broken and the observance is breached. But if someone, without the knowledge of the first monk, enters within twelve cubits of the proximity, the night is broken, but there is no breach of the observance” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 97).
