Thus, this passage also clarifies the field for announcement, not the positioning of beds or other arrangements—this should be understood.

Tatiyapāṭhassa pana ayamadhippāyo – kiṃ bahiupacārasīmāya vattasamādānaṭṭhānaṃ āgatabhikkhūnaṃ [V 2.0170] diṭṭharūpānaṃ sutasaddānaṃyeva ārocetabbanti pucchāya sati adiṭṭhaassutānampi antodvādasahatthagatānaṃ ārocetabbanti vissajjetabbanti. Etena adiṭṭhaassutānaṃ pana antodvādasahatthagatānaṃyeva ārocetabbaṃ, na bahidvādasahatthagatānaṃ, diṭṭhasutānaṃ pana antodvādasahatthagatānampi bahidvādasahatthagatānampi ākāsādigatānampi ārocetabbamevāti dasseti. Tenāha “ayaṃ panettha therassa adhippāyo – vattaṃ nikkhipitvā parivasantassa upacāragatānaṃ sabbesaṃ ārocanakiccaṃ natthi, diṭṭharūpānaṃ sutasaddānaṃ ārocetabbaṃ, adiṭṭhaassutānampi antodvādasahatthagatānaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Idaṃ vattaṃ nikkhipitvā parivasantassa lakkhaṇa”nti (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.97). Iti ayampi pāṭho ārocetabbalakkhaṇadīpako hoti, na mañcapaññāpanādidīpakoti. Catutthapāṭhassa adhippāyopi tatiyapāṭhassa adhippāyasadisova.

The meaning of the third passage is this: when there is a question whether only to those monks who have come to the place of undertaking the observance outside the proximity boundary, whose forms are seen and whose sounds are heard, should the announcement be made, the answer should be given that even to those unseen and unheard who have come within twelve cubits, it should be announced. This shows that for unseen and unheard monks, only those who have come within twelve cubits should be announced, not those beyond twelve cubits. However, for seen and heard monks, they should be announced whether they have come within twelve cubits, beyond twelve cubits, or even into the sky and so forth. Therefore, it is said: “Here, the Elder’s intention is this: for one dwelling having laid aside the observance, there is no obligation to announce to all who have entered the proximity. To those whose forms are seen and whose sounds are heard, it should be announced, and even to those unseen and unheard who have come within twelve cubits, it should be announced. This is the characteristic of one dwelling having laid aside the observance” (Sārattha-ṭīkā, Cūḷavagga 3.97). Thus, this passage also serves as an indicator of what should be announced, not as an indicator of bed or bench preparation, etc. The meaning of the fourth passage is similar to that of the third passage.

Pañcamapāṭhassa pana ayamadhippāyo – atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāti ettha etasmiṃ aṭṭhakathāvacane nikkhittavattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ attano nisinnaṭṭhānato dvādasahatthe upacāre aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā anikkhittavattānaṃ upacārasīmāya aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgatabhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā sahavāsādikaṃ veditabbaṃ. Ādi-saddena vippavāsaanārocanaūnegaṇecaraṇāni saṅgaṇhāti. Ayañca yasmā gaṇassa ārocetvā bhikkhūnañca atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā vasi[M 2.0234], tasmā nikkhittavattānaṃ bahiupacārasīmāya samādinnattā attano nisinnaṭṭhānato dvādasahatthe upacāre aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā anikkhittavattānaṃ antovihāre samādinnattā upacārasīmāya aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgatabhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā sahavāsavippavāsaanārocanaūnegaṇecaraṇasaṅkhātāni vattacchedakāraṇāni veditabbānīti. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97) “ayañca yasmā gaṇassa ārocetvā bhikkhūnañca atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāva vasi, tenassa ūnegaṇecaraṇadoso vā vippavāso vā na hotī”ti. Iti ayañca pāṭho pakatattabhikkhūsu gatesupi vattaṃ ārocetvā bhikkhūnaṃ atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā vasitattā dosābhāvameva dīpeti, na mañcapaññāpanādīni. Iti imesaṃ pāṭhānaṃ ayoniso adhippāyaṃ gahetvā “sabbattha dvādasahatthameva pamāṇa”nti maññamānā vicāriṃsu, tesaṃ diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamānā sissānusissādayopi tatheva karonti, tadetaṃ appamāṇaṃ.

The meaning of the fifth passage is as follows: Regarding the commentary statement, "having observed the presence," for monks who have laid aside their duties, it means having observed the presence of other monks within the twelve-cubit proximity from their seated position. For those who have not laid aside their duties, it means having observed the arrival of other monks within the boundary of proximity. Co-residence and related matters should be understood. The term "etc." includes temporary absence, failure to inform, an incomplete quorum, and improper movement. And because he lived after informing the Sangha and observing the presence of the monks, therefore, for those who have laid aside their duties, having undertaken the rule beyond the proximity boundary, they must observe the presence of other monks within twelve cubits from their seated position. And for those who have not laid aside their duties, having undertaken the rule within the monastery, they must observe the arrival of other monks within the proximity boundary. The factors that interrupt duties—namely, co-residence, temporary absence, failure to inform, an incomplete quorum, and improper movement—should be understood. For it is stated in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 97): "Because he lived only after informing the Sangha and observing the presence of the monks, there is no fault for him of an incomplete quorum, improper movement, or temporary absence." Thus, this passage clarifies the absence of fault because he lived after informing the Sangha and observing the presence of the monks, even when the regular monks had left, and not because of preparing beds, etc. Thus, having grasped the improper meaning of these passages, some thought, "Everywhere, only twelve cubits is the measure," and they deliberated accordingly. Their disciples and followers, conforming to their view, acted in the same way. But this is without authority.

Kathaṃ? Yaṃ tattha pakatattasālāya majjhe thambhaṃ nimittaṃ katvā dvādasahatthaṃ miniṃsu, tadappamāṇaṃ[V 2.0171]. Na hi thambhena vā sālāya vā sahavāso vā vippavāso vā vutto, atha kho pakatattabhikkhunāva. Vuttañhi samantapāsādikāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 83) “tattha sahavāsoti yvāyaṃ pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchannetiādinā nayena vutto ekato vāso. Vippavāsoti ekakasseva vāso”ti. Yañhi tato dvādasahatthamattaṭṭhāne bhikkhussa gīvāṭṭhapanaṃ vā kaṭiṭṭhapanaṃ vā vadanti, tadapi appamāṇaṃ. Bahiupacārasīmāya hi parivasantassa bhikkhussa sakalasarīraṃ pakatattabhikkhūnaṃ antodvādasahatthe upacāre ṭhapetabbaṃ hoti, na ekadesamattaṃ.

How so? That which they measured as twelve cubits, taking the pillar in the middle of the regular hall as the marker, that is without authority. For neither co-residence nor separate residence is defined by the pillar or the hall, but rather by the regular monk. As stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 83): "Here, co-residence means dwelling together with a regular monk, according to the method described by 'under one roof,' etc. Separate residence means dwelling alone." Furthermore, what some say about a monk's neck or waist being within a space of just twelve cubits, that too is without authority. For a monk dwelling outside the proximity boundary must keep his entire body within twelve cubits of the regular monks—not just a part of it.

Tesaṃ [M 2.0235] pana ayamadhippāyo siyā – dvādasahatthappadesato sakalasarīrassa antokaraṇe sati sahavāso bhaveyya, bahikaraṇe sati vippavāso, tena upaḍḍhaṃ anto upaḍḍhaṃ bahi hotūti, taṃ micchāñāṇavasena hoti. Na hi sahavāsadoso dvādasahatthena kathito, atha kho ekacchanne sayanena. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā pārivāsikakkhandhake (cūḷava. 81) “na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pakatattena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne āvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne anāvāse vatthabbaṃ, na ekacchanne āvāse vā anāvāse vā vatthabba”nti. Aṭṭhakathāyampi (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 81) vuttaṃ “ekacchanne āvāse”tiādīsu āvāso nāma vasanatthāya katasenāsanaṃ. Anāvāso nāma cetiyagharaṃ bodhigharaṃ sammuñjaniaṭṭako dāruaṭṭako pānīyamāḷo vaccakuṭi dvārakoṭṭhakoti evamādi. Tatiyapadena tadubhayampi gahitaṃ, ‘etesu yattha katthaci ekacchanne chadanato udakapatanaṭṭhānaparicchinne okāse ukkhittako vasituṃ na labhati, pārivāsiko pana antoāvāseyeva na labhatī’ti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttaṃ. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana ‘avisesena udakapātena vārita’nti vuttaṃ. Kurundiyaṃ ‘etesu ettakesu pañcavaṇṇachadanabaddhaṭṭhānesu pārivāsikassa ca ukkhittakassa ca pakatattena saddhiṃ udakapātena vārita’nti vuttaṃ, tasmā nānūpacārepi ekacchanne na vaṭṭati. Sace panettha tadahupasampannepi pakatatte paṭhamaṃ pavisitvā nipanne saṭṭhivassopi pārivāsiko pacchā pavisitvā jānanto nipajjati, ratticchedo ceva vattabhedadukkaṭañca, ajānantassa ratticchedova, na vattabhedadukkaṭaṃ. Sace pana tasmiṃ paṭhamaṃ nipanne pacchā pakatatto pavisitvā nipajjati, pārivāsiko ca jānāti, ratticchedo ceva vattabhedadukkaṭañca. No ce jānāti[M 2.0236], ratticchedova, na vattabhedadukkaṭanti, tasmā sālāyapi vihārepi chadanato udakapatanaṭṭhānato muttamatteyeva sahavāsadoso na vijjatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

For them, this might be the intention: co-residence would occur if the entire body is brought within a twelve-cubit area, and separation if it is outside; thus they think it may be half inside and half outside. But this is due to wrong knowledge. For the fault of co-residence is not described in terms of twelve cubits, but rather in terms of lying under a single roof. This was stated by the Blessed One in the Pārivāsika Section (Cūḷavagga 81): "Monks, a monk undergoing probation should not dwell under the same roof with a regular monk—not in a residence, not in a non-residence, not in either a residence or a non-residence." The commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 81) also explains: In the phrase "'Under the same roof in a residence,' etc.," 'residence' means a dwelling place made for living. 'Non-residence' means a shrine house, a Bodhi-tree house, a place for sweeping, a timber shed, a water pavilion, a restroom, a gatehouse, and so on. The third phrase covers both. It is stated in the Mahāpaccariya: 'In any of these places, wherever there is a single roof delimited by the area where rainwater falls, a suspended monk is not allowed to dwell; a probationer, however, is not allowed to dwell only inside a residence.' In the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā, it is said: 'It is generally prohibited by the rainwater drip line.' In the Kurundī, it is said: 'In these places bound by the five-colored covering, it is prohibited for both a probationer and a suspended monk to be with a regular monk within the rainwater drip line.' Therefore, even if not in close proximity, it is not permissible under a single roof. If, in such a place, a regular monk, even one ordained that very day, enters first and lies down, and a probationer, even one of sixty years' standing, enters afterward knowing this and lies down, it is both an interruption of the night and a dukkaṭa offense for breaking the rule. If he does not know, there is only an interruption of the night, not a dukkaṭa offense for breaking the rule. But if the probationer lies down first and afterward the regular monk enters and lies down, and the probationer knows, then there is both an interruption of the night and a dukkaṭa offense for breaking the rule. If he does not know, there is only an interruption of the night, not a dukkaṭa offense for breaking the rule. Therefore, it should be understood that in a hall or a monastery, the fault of co-residence is absent only when one is outside the area where water drips from the roof.

Ekacce [V 2.0172] pana majjhimatthambhato dvādasahatthāyāmena daṇḍakena cakkaṃ bhamitvā samantato bāhire lekhaṃ karonti, evaṃ kate sā bāhiralekhā āvaṭṭato dvāsattatihatthamattā hoti, tato taṃ padesaṃ dvādasahatthena daṇḍakena minitvā bhājiyamānaṃ chabhāgameva hoti, tato tesaṃ chabhāgānaṃ sīmāya ekekasmiṃ mañce paññapiyamāne chaḷeva mañcaṭṭhānāni honti, tasmā ekasmiṃ vaṭṭamaṇḍale cha bhikkhūyeva apubbaṃ acarimaṃ vasituṃ labhanti, na tato uddhanti vadanti. Kasmā pana evaṃ karontīti? Pubbe vuttanayena “sabbattha dvādasahatthamattameva pamāṇa”nti gahitattā. Evaṃ kira nesamadhippāyo – pārivāsiko pakatattassa bhikkhuno dvādasahatthabbhantare sayamāno sahavāso siyā, bāhire sayamāno vippavāso, tathā aññamaññassapīti. Evaṃ karontānaṃ pana nesaṃ sakaadhippāyopi na sijjhati, kuto bhagavato adhippāyo.

However, some, from the middle pillar, draw an outer line all around by swinging a twelve-cubit rod in a circle. When this is done, that outer line, being a circumference, becomes seventy-two cubits. Then, measuring that area with a twelve-cubit rod and dividing it, it results in six parts. Next, when one bed is designated for each of these six parts, there are only six bed-places. Therefore, they say, in one circular boundary, only six monks can reside simultaneously, not more than that. Why do they do this? Because, as stated previously, they have taken it that "everywhere, only twelve cubits is the measure." Indeed, their intention is this: if a monk undergoing probation lies within twelve cubits of a regular monk, there would be co-residence, and if he lies beyond, there would be separation—and likewise for each other. Yet, by doing so, even their own intention is not fulfilled—how much less the Blessed One’s intention?

Kathaṃ? Pārivāsiko bhikkhu pakatattabhikkhūnañca aññamaññassa ca dvādasahatthamatte padese hotūti nesamadhippāyo. Atha pana majjhimatthambhaṃ nimittaṃ katvā miniyamānā samantato bāhiralekhā thambhatoyeva dvādasahatthamattā hoti, na pakatattabhikkhūhi. Te hi thambhato bahi ekaratanadvitiratanādiṭṭhāne ṭhitā, bāhiratopi lekhāyeva thambhato dvādasahatthamattā hoti, na tassūpari nipannabhikkhu. So hi dviratanamattenapi tiratanamattenapi lekhāya antopi hoti bahipi. Aññamaññassapi chabhāgasīmāyeva aññamaññassa dvādasahatthamattā hoti[M 2.0237], na tassūpari paññattamañco vā tattha nipannabhikkhu vā. Mañco hi ekaratanamattena vā dviratanamattena vā sīmaṃ atikkamitvā ṭhito, bhikkhūpi sayamānā na sīmāya upariyeva sayanti, vidatthimattena vā ratanamattena vā sīmaṃ atikkamitvā vā appatvā vā sayanti, tasmā te pārivāsikā bhikkhū pakatattabhikkhūnampi aññamaññassapi dvādasahatthamattaṭṭhāyino na honti, tato ūnāva honti, tasmā sakaadhippāyopi na sijjhati.

How so? Their intention is that the probationer monk should be within a twelve-cubit distance from the regular monks and from each other. However, taking the middle pillar as a marker and measuring outward, the outer boundary line is twelve cubits from the pillar itself, not from the regular monks. For they stand outside the pillar at a distance of one or two cubits, etc. And the outer boundary line is also twelve cubits from the pillar, not from the monk lying upon it. For he may be inside or outside the boundary line by two or three cubits. Even among themselves, the twelve-cubit measure applies only to the six-part boundary, not to the designated bed or the monk lying there. For the bed may stand beyond the boundary by one or two cubits, and the monks lying down do not lie exactly on the boundary but may lie beyond or short of it by a span or a cubit. Therefore, those probationer monks are not within a twelve-cubit distance from the regular monks or from each other—they are indeed less than that. Thus, their own intention is also not fulfilled.

Bhagavato pana adhippāyo – yadi appabhikkhukādiaṅgasampannattā vihārassa vattaṃ anikkhipitvā antovihāreyeva parivasati, evaṃ sati pakatattena bhikkhunā na ekacchanne āvāse vasitabbaṃ. Yadi tādisaāvāse vā anāvāse vā chadanato udakapatanaṭṭhānassa anto sayeyya, sahavāso nāma, ratticchedo hotīti ayamattho yathāvutta-pāḷiyā ca aṭṭhakathāya ca pakāsetabbo. Na ekacchanne āvāse dvīhi vatthabbaṃ. Yadi vaseyya, vuḍḍhassa ratticchedoyeva, navakassa ratticchedo ceva vattabhedadukkaṭañca hoti. Samavassā ce, ajānantassa ratticchedoyeva[V 2.0173], jānantassa ubhayampīti ayamattho “tayo kho, upāli, pārivāsikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā sahavāso vippavāso anārocanā”ti ca “na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā pārivāsikena vuḍḍhatarena saddhiṃ na ekacchanne āvāse vatthabba”nti (cūḷava. 82) ca “vuḍḍhatarenāti ettha…pe… sace hi dve pārivāsikā ekato vaseyyuṃ, te aññamaññassa ajjhācāraṃ ñatvā agāravā vā vippaṭisārino vā hutvā pāpiṭṭhataraṃ vā āpattiṃ āpajjeyyuṃ vibbhameyyuṃ vā, tasmā nesaṃ sahaseyyā sabbappakārena paṭikkhittā”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 81) ca imehi pāḷiaṭṭhakathāpāṭhehi pakāsetabbo. Vippavāsepi pārivāsikena abhikkhuke [M 2.0238] āvāse na vatthabbaṃ, pakatattena vinā abhikkhuko āvāso na gantabbo, bahisīmāyaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānato dvādasahatthappamāṇassa upacārassa anto nisīditabbanti bhagavato adhippāyo.

The Blessed One's intention, however, is this: if, because the monastery is endowed with factors such as having few monks, one undergoes probation within the monastery itself without giving up the observance, in that case, one should not dwell with a regular monk in a single-roofed abode. If one sleeps inside such an abode or a non-abode, within the area where water drips from the roof, that is called cohabitation, and it is a breach of the night. This meaning should be explained according to the aforementioned Pāli and commentary. Two should not dwell in a single-roofed abode. If they do dwell there, for the senior, it is only a breach of the night, but for the junior, it is both a breach of the night and a dukkaṭa offense for breaking the observance. If they are of equal seniority, for the one who is unaware, it is only a breach of the night, but for the one who is aware, it is both. This meaning should be explained by these passages from the Pāli and commentary: “Upāli, there are three breaches of the night for a monk undergoing probation: cohabitation, separation, and non-reporting.” And, “Monks, a monk undergoing probation should not dwell in a single-roofed abode with a senior monk undergoing probation.” (Cūḷavagga 82) And, “Here, ‘senior’ means… For if two monks undergoing probation were to dwell together, knowing each other’s misconduct, they might become disrespectful or remorseful, or commit a worse offense, or even disrobe. Therefore, their lying together is entirely prohibited.” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 81). Regarding separation, a monk undergoing probation should not dwell in a monastery without monks. A monastery without monks should not be gone to without a regular monk. Outside the boundary, one should sit within the twelve-cubit proximity of the monks’ dwelling place. This is the intention of the Blessed One.

Ayamattho “na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo aññatra pakatattena aññatra antarāyā”tiādi (cūḷava. 76) ca “tayo kho, upāli…pe… anārocanā”ti ca “cattāro kho, upāli, mānattacārikassa bhikkhuno ratticchedā sahavāso, vippavāso, anārocanā, ūnegaṇecaraṇa”nti (cūḷava. 92) ca “vippavāsoti ekakasseva vāso”ti ca “ayañca yasmā gaṇassa ārocetvā bhikkhūnañca atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāva vasi, tenassa ūnegaṇecaraṇadoso vā vippavāso vā na hotī”ti ca “atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāti dvādasahatthe upacāre sallakkhetvā, anikkhittavattānaṃ upacārasīmāya āgatabhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā sahavāsādikaṃ veditabba”nti ca āgatehi pāḷiyaṭṭhakathā-vajirabuddhiṭīkāpāṭhehi pakāsetabbo, tasmā vihāre parivasantassa upacārasīmāya abbhantare yattha katthaci vasantassa natthi vippavāso, bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ parivasantassa bhikkhūnaṃ nisinnapariyantato dvādasahatthabbhantare vasantassa ca natthi vippavāsoti, tañca parivāsakāle “ekena bhikkhunā saddhi”nti vacanato ekassapi bhikkhuno, mānattacaraṇakāle “catūhi pañcahi vā bhikkhūhi saddhi”nti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) vacanato ca catunnaṃ pañcannampi bhikkhūnaṃ hatthapāsabhūte dvādasahatthabbhantarepi vasituṃ labhati, natthi vippavāsoti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

This meaning should be explained by these passages from the Pāli, the commentary, and the Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā: “A monk on probation, monks, should not go from a residence with monks to a residence without monks, except with a regular monk or in case of an obstacle” (Cūḷavagga 76); and “Three, Upāli… non-reporting”; and “Four, Upāli, are the breaches of the night for a monk undergoing mānatta: cohabitation, separation, non-reporting, and going about with an incomplete group” (Cūḷavagga 92); and “Separation means dwelling by oneself”; and “And since he dwelt having announced to the group and having ascertained the presence of monks, there is no fault of going about with an incomplete group or separation for him”; and “Having ascertained the presence means having ascertained [their presence] within the twelve-cubit proximity. Having ascertained the presence of those who have not abandoned their observances within the precinct boundary, cohabitation etc. should be understood.” Therefore, for one dwelling in a monastery on probation, there is no separation if he dwells anywhere within the precinct boundary. For one dwelling outside the precinct boundary, there is no separation if he dwells within twelve cubits from the limit of where the monks are seated. And during the probation period, because of the phrase “with one monk,” it is permissible to dwell even with one monk. During the mānatta period, because of the phrase “with four or five monks” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭha. 102), it is permissible to dwell even within the twelve-cubit proximity, which is within arm's reach, of four or five monks. It should be understood that there is no separation.

Vattaṃ samādiyitvā tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ārocitakālato pana paṭṭhāya kenaci karaṇīyena tesu [V 2.0174] bhikkhūsu gatesupi [M 2.0239] yathāvuttaaṭṭhakathāpāṭhanayena vippavāso na hoti. Tathā hi vuttaṃ vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. cūḷavagga 2.97) “sopi kenaci kammena purearuṇe eva gacchatīti iminā ārocanāya katāya sabbesupi bhikkhūsu bahivihāraṃ gatesu ūnegaṇecaraṇadoso vā vippavāsadoso vā na hoti ārocitattā sahavāsassāti dasseti. Tenāha ‘ayañcā’tiādī”ti. Apare pana ācariyā “bahisīmāya vattasamādānaṭṭhāne vatiparikkhepopi pakatattabhikkhūheva kātabbo, na kammārahabhikkhūhi. Yathā loke bandhanāgārādi daṇḍakārakehi eva kattabbaṃ, na daṇḍārahehi, evamidhāpī”ti vadanti, tampi aṭṭhakathādīsu na dissati. Na hi vatiparikkhepo daṇḍakammatthāya kārito, atha kho dassanūpacāravijahanatthameva. Tathā hi vuttaṃ sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.97) “gumbena vā vatiyā vā paṭicchannaṭṭhāneti dassanūpacāravijahanattha”nti. Tathā vimativinodaniyampi (vi. vi. ṭī. cūḷavagga 2.97) “gumbena vātiādi dassanūpacāravijahanattha”nti. Ito paraṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva parivāsadānañca mānattadānañca veditabbaṃ. Yattha pana saṃsayitabbaṃ atthi, tattha saṃsayavinodanatthāya kathetabbaṃ kathayāma.

Having undertaken the observance, from the time of announcing it to those monks onward, even if those monks depart for some duty, there is no separation, as explained in the commentary. For it is stated in the Vimativinodanī (Vinaya Vibhaṅga, Cūḷavagga 2.97): “Even if he goes before dawn for some task, once the announcement has been made, even if all the monks go outside the monastery, there is no fault of going about with an incomplete group or separation, because cohabitation has been announced. Therefore, it says ‘And this…’ and so on.” Some teachers, however, say: “Even the enclosing with a fence of the place for undertaking the observance outside the boundary should be done only by regular monks, not by monks who are subject to a formal act. Just as in the world, prisons and the like are to be handled by those who administer punishment, not by those who are subject to punishment, so too here.” But this is not found in the commentaries. For the enclosing with a fence is not done for the purpose of punishment, but rather merely for abandoning the range of sight. As stated in the Sāratthadīpanī (Sāratthaṭīkā, Cūḷavagga 3.97): “Concealed by a bush or a fence means for abandoning the range of sight.” Similarly, in the Vimativinodanī (Vinaya Vibhaṅga, Cūḷavagga 2.97): “By a bush or the like means for abandoning the range of sight.” From here onward, the giving of probation and the giving of mānatta should be understood according to the method explained in the commentary. Where, however, there is something to be doubted, we shall explain it for the purpose of resolving the doubt.

Ekacce bhikkhū evaṃ vadanti – pārivāsiko bhikkhu vuḍḍhataropi samāno vatte samādinne navakaṭṭhāne ṭhito. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “yattha pana nisīdāpetvā parivisanti, tattha sāmaṇerānaṃ jeṭṭhakena, bhikkhūnaṃ saṅghanavakena hutvā nisīditabba”nti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 75) tasmā ārocitakālādīsu “ahaṃ bhante”icceva vattabbaṃ, na “ahaṃ āvuso”ti. Tatrevaṃ vicāraṇā kātabbā – pārivāsikādayo bhikkhū seyyāpariyantaāsanapariyantabhāgitāya navakaṭṭhāne ṭhitā, na ekantena [M 2.0240] navakabhūtattā. Tathā hi vuttaṃ bhagavatā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pārivāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañca yathāvuḍḍhaṃ uposathaṃ pavāraṇaṃ vassikasāṭikaṃ oṇojanaṃ bhatta”nti (cūḷava. 75). Aṭṭhakathāyañca (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 81) “pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, pakatatto bhikkhu āsanena nimantetabbo”ti etissā pāḷiyā saṃvaṇṇanāya “vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, nimantetabboti tadahupasampannampi disvā vuṭṭhātabbameva, vuṭṭhāya ca ‘ahaṃ iminā sukhanisinno vuṭṭhāpito’ti parammukhena na gantabbaṃ, ‘idaṃ ācariya āsanaṃ, ettha nisīdathā’ti evaṃ nimantetabboyevā”ti ettheva “ācariyā”ti ālapanaviseso vutto, na aññattha. Yadi vuḍḍhatarenapi “bhante”icceva vattabbo siyā, idhāpi “idaṃ, bhante, āsana”nti vattabbaṃ bhaveyya, na pana vuttaṃ, tasmā na tesaṃ taṃ vacanaṃ sārato paccetabbaṃ. Imasmiṃ [V 2.0175] pana vinayasaṅgahappakaraṇe (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 237) “ārocentena sace navakataro hoti, ‘āvuso’ti vattabbaṃ. Sace vuḍḍhataro, ‘bhante’ti vattabba”nti vuttaṃ, idañca “ekena bhikkhunā saddhi”nti heṭṭhā vuttattā taṃ paṭiggāhakabhūtaṃ pakatattaṃ bhikkhuṃ sandhāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Some monks say this: Even an elder monk under probation, having undertaken the observance, stands in the place of a junior. For it is said: “Wherever they make one sit and then serve, there the eldest among the novices and the newest among the Sangha of monks should sit.” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 75) Therefore, at the time of announcing and so on, one should say only “Venerable sir,” not “Friend.” Here, the matter should be considered thus: Monks under probation and others stand in the place of a junior by virtue of sharing the limit of bedding and seating, not because they are entirely junior. For the Blessed One has said: “Monks, I allow five things for monks undergoing probation according to seniority: Uposatha, Pavāraṇā, the rainy-season robe, the dedication of food, and the meal.” (Cūḷavagga 75) And in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 81): “Upon seeing a normal monk, one should rise from one’s seat; a normal monk should be invited to a seat.” In explaining this passage, it is said: “One should rise even upon seeing one ordained on that very day. Having risen, one should not go away with averted face, thinking, ‘I, who was comfortably seated, have been made to rise by this one.’ Instead, one should invite him thus: ‘Teacher, this is a seat, please sit here.’ Here, the specific address ‘teacher’ is mentioned, not elsewhere. If even an elder should be addressed only as “Venerable sir,” then here too one should say, “Venerable sir, this is a seat.” But since it is not stated, their statement should not be taken as authoritative. However, in this Vinaya Saṅgaha treatise (Vinaya Saṅgaha Aṭṭhakathā 237), it is said: “When announcing, if one is junior, one should say ‘Friend.’ If one is senior, one should say ‘Venerable sir.’” And since this is stated below as “with one monk,” it should be understood as referring to that normal monk who is the recipient.

Bahavo pana bhikkhū pārivāsikaṃ bhikkhuṃ saṅghamajjhe nisīdāpetvā vattaṃ yācāpetvā kammavācāpariyosāne samādāpetvā ārocanamakāretvā saṅghamajjhato nikkhamāpetvā parisapariyante nisīdāpetvā tattha nisinnena ārocāpetvā vattaṃ nikkhipāpenti, evaṃ karontānañca nesaṃ ayamadhippāyo – ayaṃ bhikkhu vatte asamādinne vuḍḍhaṭṭhāniyopi hoti, tasmā yācanakāle ca kammavācāsavanakāle ca vattasamādānakāle ca saṅghamajjhe nisīdanāraho hoti, vatte pana samādinne navakaṭṭhāniyo, tasmā na saṅghamajjhe nisīdanāraho, āsanapariyantabhāgitāya [M 2.0241] parisapariyanteyeva nisīdanārahoti, tadetaṃ evaṃ vicāretabbaṃ – ayaṃ bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe nisīdamāno āsanaṃ gahetvā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ nisinno na hoti, atha kho kammārahabhāvena āsanaṃ aggahetvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā ukkuṭikameva nisinno hoti, kammāraho ca nāma saṅghamajjheyeva ṭhapetabbo hoti, no bahi, tasmā “saṅghamajjhe nisīdanāraho na hotī”ti na sakkā vattuṃ tasmiṃ kāle, nikkhamāpite ca vattārocanavattanikkhipanānaṃ aniṭṭhitattā aññamaññaṃ āhacca suṭṭhu nisinnaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharitumasakkuṇeyyattā, cīvarakaṇṇapādapiṭṭhiādīhi bādhitattā agāravakiriyā viya dissati, ārocanakiriyañca vattanikkhipanañca saṅghamajjheyeva kattabbaṃ pariyante nisīditvā karonto aṭṭhakathāvirodho hoti. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 97) “vattaṃ samādiyitvā tattheva saṅghassa ārocetabbaṃ…pe… ārocetvā sace nikkhipitukāmo, vuttanayeneva saṅghamajjhe nikkhipitabba”nti. Kasmā? Samādānaṭṭhāneyeva ārocāpetvā tattheva nikkhipāpetvā niṭṭhitasabbakiccameva nikkhamāpetvā attano āsane nisīdāpento ñāyāgatoti amhākaṃ khanti.

Many monks, having seated a monk undergoing probation in the midst of the Saṅgha, having had him request the duties, and having had him undertake them at the conclusion of the formal act, then, without having him make an announcement, make him leave the midst of the Saṅgha and seat him at the edge of the assembly. There, while seated, they have him make an announcement and then lay aside the duties. Those who do so have this intention: “This monk, while the duties are not yet undertaken, is worthy even of a senior’s place. Therefore, at the time of requesting, at the time of hearing the formal act, and at the time of undertaking the duties, he is worthy of sitting in the midst of the Saṅgha. But when the duties are undertaken, he is in the position of a junior. Therefore, he is not worthy of sitting in the midst of the Saṅgha, but is worthy of sitting only at the edge of the assembly by virtue of sharing the limit of seating.” This should be considered thus: This monk, while sitting in the midst of the Saṅgha, does not take a seat and sit according to seniority. Rather, as one fit for the formal act, he does not take a seat but sits in the squatting posture with his hands raised in añjali. One fit for a formal act should indeed be placed in the midst of the Saṅgha, not outside. Therefore, it cannot be said that he is not worthy of sitting in the midst of the Saṅgha at that time. Moreover, when he is made to leave, since the announcement of the duties and the laying aside of the duties are not yet completed, and since they would be unable to avoid the well-seated Saṅgha of monks, being hindered by the edges of robes, feet, backs, and so forth, it appears as a disrespectful action. The act of announcement and the laying aside of duties should indeed be done in the midst of the Saṅgha. Doing so while seated at the edge is contrary to the commentary. For it is said in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 97): “Having undertaken the duties, they should be announced right there to the Saṅgha… Having announced, if one wishes to lay them aside, they should be laid aside in the midst of the Saṅgha in the prescribed manner.” Why? Because, having had them announced at the place of undertaking and laid aside right there, with all duties completed, making him leave and sit in his own seat is in accordance with what is proper—this is our view.

Tathā sāyaṃ vattārocanakāle bahūsu pārivāsikesu vuḍḍhataraṃ paṭhamaṃ samādāpetvā ārocāpetvā anukkamena sabbapacchā navakataraṃ samādāpenti ārocāpenti, pāto nikkhipanakāle pana navakataraṃ paṭhamaṃ ārocāpetvā nikkhipāpenti, tato anukkamena vuḍḍhataraṃ sabbapacchā ārocāpetvā nikkhipāpenti. Tesaṃ ayamadhippāyo siyā – yadā dasa bhikkhū pakatattā [V 2.0176] dasa bhikkhū pārivāsikā honti, tadā vuḍḍhatarena paṭhamaṃ samādiyitvā ārocite tassa ārocanaṃ avasesā ekūnavīsati bhikkhū [M 2.0242] suṇanti, dutiyassa aṭṭhārasa, tatiyassa sattarasāti anukkamena hāyitvā sabbanavakassa ārocanaṃ dasa pakatattā suṇanti sesānaṃ apakatattabhāvato. Tato nikkhipanakāle sabbanavako pubbe attanā ārocitānaṃ dasannaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ārocetvā nikkhipati, tato paṭilomena dutiyo ekādasannaṃ, tatiyo dvādasannanti anukkamena vaḍḍhitvā sabbajeṭṭhako attanā pubbe ārocitānaṃ ekūnavīsatibhikkhūnaṃ ārocetvā nikkhipati, evaṃ yathānukkamena nikkhipanaṃ hoti. Sabbajeṭṭhake pana paṭhamaṃ nikkhitte sati pubbe attanā ārocitānaṃ navannaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tadā apakatattabhāvato ārocitānaṃ santike nikkhipanaṃ na hoti, tathā sesānaṃ. Tesaṃ pana ekaccānaṃ ūnaṃ hoti, ekaccānaṃ adhikaṃ, tasmā yathāvuttanayena sabbanavakato paṭṭhāya anukkamena nikkhipitabbanti.

Similarly, in the evening, at the time of announcing the duties, among many probationers, they first have the most senior undertake and declare, then gradually have the newest undertake and declare last of all. In the morning, at the time of laying aside, they first have the newest declare and lay aside, then gradually have the most senior declare and lay aside last. Their intention may be as follows: When ten monks are of regular standing and ten are probationers, after the most senior first undertakes and declares, his declaration is heard by the remaining nineteen monks. For the second, eighteen hear it; for the third, seventeen—thus decreasing gradually until the declaration of the very newest is heard by the ten of regular standing, since the others are not of regular standing. Then, at the time of laying aside, the very newest one lays aside after declaring to the ten monks to whom he had previously declared. Next, in reverse order, the second declares to eleven, the third to twelve, and so on, increasing gradually until the most senior one lays aside after declaring to the nineteen monks to whom he had previously declared. Thus, laying aside proceeds in due order. However, if the most senior one lays aside first, since the nine monks to whom he had previously declared were at that time not of regular standing, there is no laying aside in their presence. The same applies to the others. For some, the count is less; for others, more. Therefore, starting from the very newest, laying aside should be done gradually in the manner described.

Evaṃvādīnaṃ pana tesamāyasmantānaṃ vāde pakatattāyeva bhikkhū ārocetabbā honti, no apakatattā. Pubbe ārocitānaṃyeva santike vattaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ hoti, no anārocitānaṃ. Evaṃ pana pakatattāyeva bhikkhū ārocetabbā na honti, atha kho apakatattāpi “sace dve pārivāsikā gataṭṭhāne aññamaññaṃ passanti, ubhohi aññamaññassa ārocetabba”nti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttattā. Pubbe ārocitānampi anārocitānampi santike ārocetvā nikkhipitabbameva “sace so bhikkhu kenacideva karaṇīyena pakkanto hoti, yaṃ aññaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ passati, tassa ārocetvā nikkhipitabba”nti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) vuttattā, tasmā tathā akarontepi sabbesaṃ ārocitattā natthi doso. Appekacce bhikkhū “pakatattassevāyaṃ ārocanā”ti maññamānā sāyaṃ vuḍḍhapaṭipāṭiyā vattaṃ samādiyitvā ārocetvā [M 2.0243] attano sayanaṃ pavisitvā dvārajagganasayanasodhanādīni karontā aññesaṃ ārocitaṃ na suṇanti. Appekacce pāto sayaṃ ārocetvā nikkhipitvā aññesaṃ ārocanaṃ vā nikkhipanaṃ vā anāgametvā bhikkhācārādīnaṃ atthāya gacchanti, evaṃ karontānaṃ tesaṃ ārocanaṃ ekaccānaṃ asutabhāvasambhavato sāsaṅko hoti pārivāsikānaṃ aññamaññārocanassa pakaraṇesu āgatattā. Na kevalaṃ sāratthadīpaniyaṃyeva, atha kho vajirabuddhiṭīkāyampi (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 76) “sace dve pārivāsikā gataṭṭhāne aññamaññaṃ passanti, ubhohipi aññamaññassa ārocetabbaṃ avisesena ‘āgantukena ārocetabbaṃ, āgantukassa ārocetabba’nti vuttattā”ti vuttaṃ.

In the view of those venerables who speak thus, monks should be informed only if they are of regular standing, not if they are not of regular standing. The observance should be laid aside only in the presence of those who have been previously informed, not in the presence of those who have not been informed. However, it is not the case that monks should be informed only if they are of regular standing; rather, even those not of regular standing should be informed, since it is stated in the commentary: “If two monks undergoing probation meet each other in the place they have gone to, both should inform each other.” The observance should be announced and laid aside in the presence of both those previously informed and those not previously informed, since it is stated: “If that monk has left for some reason, it should be announced to whomever one sees first and then laid aside” (Cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102). Therefore, even for one not acting thus, there is no fault, since it has been announced to all. Some monks, thinking, “This informing is only for those of regular standing,” undertake the observance in the evening according to seniority, inform others, enter their own dwelling, and then perform tasks like guarding the door and cleaning their bedding, without listening to the announcements of others. Some, after announcing and laying aside the observance themselves in the morning, go out for the alms-round or other purposes without awaiting the announcements or the laying aside of the observance by others. When they act thus, their informing becomes doubtful due to the possibility that some might not have heard it, since the mutual informing of probationers is mentioned in the treatises. Not only is this stated in the Sāratthadīpanī, but also in the Vajirabuddhiṭīkā (Vajira. ṭī. Cūḷavagga 76): “If two monks undergoing probation meet each other in the place they have gone to, both should inform each other without distinction, since it is said, ‘By the newcomer it should be announced, and to the newcomer it should be announced.’”

Tathā [V 2.0177] appekacce pakatattā bhikkhū pārivāsikesu bhikkhūsu sāyaṃ vattasamādānatthaṃ pakatattasālato nikkhamitvā attano attano sayanasamīpaṃ gatesu attano sayanapaññāpanapaakkhāraṭhapanaaññamaññaālāpasallāpakaraṇādivasena āḷolentā pārivāsikānaṃ vattārocanaṃ na suṇanti, na manasi karonti. Appekacce pāto vattanikkhipanakāle pārivāsikabhikkhūsu vattārocanavattanikkhipanāni karontesupi niddāpasutā hutvā na suṇanti. Evaṃ karontānampi tesaṃ ekaccānaṃ assutasambhavato vattārocanaṃ sāsaṅkaṃ hotīti. Hotu sāsaṅkaṃ, suṇantānaṃ assutasambhavepi ārocakānaṃ sammāārocanena vattassa paripuṇṇattā ko dosoti ce? Ārocakānaṃ sammā ārocitattā vatte paripuṇṇepi vattabhedadukkaṭatova vimutto siyā, na ratticchedato. Vuttañhi samantapāsādikāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76) “sace vāyamantopi sampāpuṇituṃ vā sāvetuṃ [M 2.0244] vā na sakkoti, ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhedadukkaṭa”nti.

Similarly, some monks of regular standing—when the probationary monks, having left the hall of the regular monks in the evening to undertake their observance, have gone to their respective sleeping places—being occupied with arranging their bedding, placing their requisites, engaging in mutual conversation, and so forth, fail to hear or pay attention to the probationary monks’ announcement of the observance. Some, at the time for laying aside the observance in the morning, remain overcome by sleep and do not hear, even while the probationary monks are announcing and laying aside the observance. Thus, for those who act in this way, the announcement of the observance becomes doubtful, due to the possibility that some of them might not have heard it. If it is said, “Let it be doubtful; even if there is a possibility that those listening did not hear, what fault is there, since the observance is complete due to the announcers having announced it properly?” Even if the observance is fully completed by the announcers properly announcing it, one would only be freed from the dukkata offense for breaking the observance, not from the breach of the night. For it is stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76): “If, even while striving, one is unable to reach them or to make oneself heard, it is a breach of the night, not a dukkata offense for breaking the observance.”

Athaññe bhikkhū vattaṃ samādiyitvā rattiṃ nipannā niddābhāvena manussasaddampi suṇanti, bheriādisaddampi suṇanti, sakaṭanāvādiyānasaddampi suṇanti, te tena saddena āsaṅkanti “bhikkhūnaṃ nu kho aya”nti, te tena kāraṇena ratticchedaṃ maññanti. Kasmā? “Ayañca nesaṃ chattasaddaṃ vā ukkāsitasaddaṃ vā khipitasaddaṃ vā sutvā āgantukabhāvaṃ jānāti, gantvā ārocetabbaṃ. Gatakāle jānantenapi anubandhitvā ārocetabbameva. Sampāpuṇituṃ asakkontassa ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhedadukkaṭa”nti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76) vuttattāti. Te evaṃ saññāpetabbā – māyasmanto evaṃ maññittha, nāyaṃ pāṭho bahisīmaṭṭhavasena vutto, atha kho upacārasīmaṭṭhavasena vutto. Vuttañhi tattheva “yepi antovihāraṃ appavisitvā upacārasīmaṃ okkamitvā gacchantī”ti. Tatthapi āgantukabhāvassa jānitattā ratticchedo hoti, tasmā dūresaddasavanamattena ratticchedo natthi, “ayaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ saddo, ayaṃ bhikkhūhi vāditabherighaṇṭādisaddo, ayaṃ bhikkhūhi pājitasakaṭanāvādisaddo”ti nisinnaṭṭhānato jānantoyeva ratticchedakaro hoti. Tenāha “āyasmā karavīkatissatthero ‘samaṇo aya’nti vavatthānameva pamāṇa”nti.

Then other monks, having undertaken the observance, lie down at night, and being unable to sleep, they hear human sounds, the sounds of drums and the like, and the sounds of carts, boats, and other vehicles. They become suspicious on account of those sounds, thinking, “Could this be the sound of monks?” For that reason, they consider it a breach of the night. Why? Because it is said: “And when this one hears their sound of an umbrella, a cough, or a finger-snap and recognizes that they are newcomers, he should go and inform them. Even if he knows when they have already gone, he should still follow and inform them. For one who is unable to reach them, it is a breach of the night, not a dukkata offense for breaking the observance” (Cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76). They should be instructed thus: “Venerable sirs, do not think so. This passage was not spoken with reference to being outside the boundary, but with reference to being within the proximity boundary. For it is said in that same place: ‘Even those who depart after stepping into the proximity boundary without entering the inner monastery…’ There too, because their status as newcomers is known, it is a breach of the night. Therefore, a breach of the night does not occur merely by hearing a distant sound. It becomes a cause for a breach of the night only for one who knows from where he is seated, ‘This is the sound of monks; this is the sound of drums, bells, and the like played by monks; this is the sound of carts, boats, and the like driven by monks.’ Therefore, the Venerable Karavīka Tissa Thera said: ‘The very determination, “This is a recluse,” is the standard.’”

Divā dūre gacchantaṃ janakāyaṃ disvāpi “ime bhikkhū nu kho”ti parikappentā ratticchedaṃ maññanti, tampi akāraṇaṃ. Kasmā? “Bhikkhū”ti vavatthānassa abhāvā. Vuttañhi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “nadīādīsu nāvāya gacchantampi paratīre ṭhitampi ākāse gacchantampi pabbatathalaaraññādīsu [V 2.0178] dūre ṭhitampi bhikkhuṃ disvā sace ‘bhikkhū’ti vavatthānaṃ atthi, nāvādīhi vā gantvā mahāsaddaṃ katvā [M 2.0245] vā vegena anubandhitvā vā ārocetabba”nti. Iti bhikkhuṃ disvāpi “bhikkhū”ti vavatthānameva pamāṇaṃ. Abhikkhuṃ pana “bhikkhū”ti vavatthāne santepi vā asantepi vā kiṃ vattabbaṃ atthi, bahavo pana bhikkhū idaṃ rūpadassanaṃ saddasavanañca āsaṅkantā “pabhāte sati taṃ dvayaṃ bhaveyya, tasmā manussānaṃ gamanakālasaddakaraṇakālato pubbeyeva vattaṃ nikkhipitabba”nti maññamānā anuggateyeva aruṇe vattaṃ nikkhipanti, tadayuttaṃ ratticchedattāti.

Even when seeing a crowd of people traveling in the distance during the day, some speculate, “Could these be monks?” and consider it a breach of the night—that too is without reason. Why? Because there is no determination, ‘These are monks.’ For it is said in the commentary: “Having seen a monk traveling by boat on a river or the like, or standing on the opposite shore, or traveling through the sky, or standing far away on a mountain plateau, in a forest, or the like—if there is the determination, ‘That is a monk,’ one should go by boat or other means, or make a loud noise, or quickly follow and inform him.” Thus, even upon seeing a monk, the very determination, ‘That is a monk,’ is the standard. As for a non-monk, whether one determines them to be ‘a monk’ or not, what is there to say? However, many monks, being apprehensive of this seeing of forms and hearing of sounds, think, “At daybreak, these two things might occur; therefore, the observance should be laid aside even before the time when people travel and make sounds.” Thinking thus, they lay aside their observance before the sun has risen—this is improper, because it constitutes a breach of the night.

Atha pana vinayadharena “kittakā te āpattiyo, chādesi, kīvatīhaṃ paṭicchādesī”ti puṭṭho samāno “ahaṃ, bhante, āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāmi, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, rattipariyantaṃ nassarāmi, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko”ti vutte “ayaṃ bhikkhu suddhantaparivāsāraho”ti ñatvā tassapi duvidhattā cūḷasuddhantamahāsuddhantavasena “tesu ayaṃ bhikkhu imassa araho”ti ñāpanatthaṃ upasampadato paṭṭhāya anulomakkamena vā ārocitadivasato paṭṭhāya paṭilomakkamena vā “kittakaṃ kālaṃ tvaṃ ārocanaāvikaraṇādivasena suddho”ti pucchitvā “āma bhante, ettakaṃ kālaṃ ahaṃ suddhomhī”ti vutte “ayaṃ bhikkhu ekaccaṃ rattipariyantaṃ jānāti, tasmā cūḷasuddhantāraho”ti ñatvā tassa suddhakālaṃ apanetvā asuddhakālavasena pariyantaṃ katvā cūḷasuddhantaparivāso dātabbo. Ayaṃ uddhampi ārohati, adhopi orohati. Yo pana anulomavasena vā paṭilomavasena vā pucchiyamāno “sakalampi rattipariyantaṃ ahaṃ na jānāmi nassarāmi, vematiko homī”ti vutte “ayaṃ bhikkhu sakalampi rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, tasmā mahāsuddhantāraho”ti ñatvā tassa upasampadato paṭṭhāya yāva vattasamādānā ettakaṃ kālaṃ pariyantaṃ katvā mahāsuddhantaparivāso [M 2.0246] dātabbo. Uddhaṃārohanaadhoorohanabhāvo panesaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) vuttoyeva. Ito parampi vidhānaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ āgatanayeneva daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Then, when questioned by the Vinaya master, "How many offenses have you concealed? For how long have you concealed them?" and he replies, "Venerable sir, I do not know the extent of the offenses, I do not know the extent of the nights, I do not remember the extent of the offenses, I do not remember the extent of the nights, I am uncertain about the extent of the offenses, I am uncertain about the extent of the nights," when this is said, knowing, "This monk is deserving of suddhanta probation," and due to its twofold nature—as minor suddhanta and major suddhanta—in order to make known which of these this monk is worthy of, starting from his higher ordination in forward order, or counting backward from the day of informing, he is asked, "For how long have you been pure through informing, disclosing, and so forth?" If he replies, "Yes, venerable sir, I have been pure for this long," then knowing, "This monk knows the extent of some nights, therefore he is worthy of minor suddhanta probation," after deducting the pure period and determining the period based on the impure time, minor suddhanta probation should be given. This one ascends upwards and descends downwards. However, if when questioned in forward or reverse order, he says, "I do not know, nor do I remember, the entire extent of the nights; I am uncertain," then knowing, "This monk does not know the entire extent of the nights, therefore he is worthy of major suddhanta probation," then, determining the period from his higher ordination up to the undertaking of the observance, major suddhanta probation should be given. The nature of their ascending upwards and descending downwards is indeed stated in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102). From here onwards, the procedure should be understood according to the method that has come down in the commentary.

Idāni pana bahavo bhikkhū “ayaṃ cūḷasuddhantāraho, ayaṃ mahāsuddhantāraho”ti avicinantā antokammavācāyaṃ “āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko”ti [V 2.0179] avisesavacanameva manasi karontā “imāya kammavācāya dinnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ gahetvā pañcāhamattaṃ vā dasāhamattaṃ vā parivasitvā apariyantarattipaṭicchāditāhi apariyantāhi āpattīhi mokkho hotī”ti maññantā pañcāhamattaṃ vā dasāhamattaṃ vā parivasitvā mānattaṃ yācanti, evaṃ karontā te bhikkhū sahassakkhattuṃ parivasantāpi āpattito na mucceyyuṃ. Kasmāti ce? Pāḷiyā ca aṭṭhakathāya ca virujjhanato. Vuttañhi pāḷiyaṃ (pārā. 442) “yāvatīhaṃ jānaṃ paṭicchādeti, tāvatīhaṃ tena bhikkhunā akāmā parivatthabbaṃ. Parivutthaparivāsena bhikkhunā uttari chārattaṃ bhikkhumānattāya paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Ciṇṇamānatto bhikkhu yattha siyā vīsatigaṇo bhikkhusaṅgho, tattha so bhikkhu abbhetabbo”ti, tasmā paṭicchannadivasamattaṃ aparivasitvā mānattāraho nāma na hoti, amānattārahassa mānattadānaṃ na ruhati, aciṇṇamānatto abbhānāraho na hoti, anabbhānārahassa abbhānaṃ na ruhati, anabbhito bhikkhu āpattimutto pakatatto na hotīti ayamettha bhagavato adhippāyo.

Now, however, many monks, without discerning, 'This one is worthy of minor suddhanta, this one is worthy of major suddhanta,' and taking to mind only the undifferentiated statement within the formal act, 'He does not know the extent of the offense, he does not know the extent of the nights, he does not remember the extent of the offense, he does not remember the extent of the nights, he is uncertain about the extent of the offense, he is uncertain about the extent of the nights,' think, 'Having received suddhanta probation given by this formal act, after observing probation for just five or ten days, one is freed from an unlimited number of offenses concealed for an unlimited number of nights,' and they request mānatta after observing probation for just five or ten days. By acting thus, even if those monks were to observe probation a thousand times, they would not be freed from the offense. If asked why, it is because it contradicts the Pāli and the commentary. For it is said in the Pāli (Pārājika 442): 'For as many days as he knowingly conceals, for that many days that monk must, against his will, undergo probation. A monk who has completed probation must undertake mānatta for a further six nights. A monk who has completed mānatta should be rehabilitated wherever there is a Saṅgha of twenty monks.' Therefore, without having observed probation for the same number of days as were concealed, one is not worthy of mānatta. The giving of mānatta to one not worthy of mānatta does not take effect. One who has not completed mānatta is not worthy of rehabilitation. The rehabilitation of one not worthy of rehabilitation does not take effect. A monk who has not been rehabilitated is not freed from the offense and is not restored to his original state. This is the Blessed One's intention here.

Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) pana cūḷasuddhante “taṃ gahetvā parivasantena yattakaṃ kālaṃ attano suddhiṃ jānāti, tattakaṃ apanetvā [M 2.0247] avasesaṃ māsaṃ vā dvimāsaṃ vā parivasitabba”nti, mahāsuddhante “taṃ gahetvā gahitadivasato yāva upasampadadivaso, tāva rattiyo gaṇetvā parivasitabba”nti vuttaṃ, tasmā paṭicchannarattippamāṇaṃ parivasantoyeva mānattāraho hoti, na pañcāhadasāharattippamāṇamattaṃ parivasantoti ayaṃ aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ adhippāyo. Teneva ca kāraṇena desanāārocanādīhi sabbakālaṃ āpattiṃ sodhetvā vasantānaṃ lajjīpesalānaṃ sikkhākāmānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ suddhantaparivāsaṃ dātuṃ ayuttarūpo, desanāārocanādīhi āpattiṃ asodhetvā pamādavasena cirakālaṃ vasantānaṃ janapadavāsikādīnaṃ dātuṃ yuttarūpoti veditabbaṃ. Etthāpi avasesavinicchayo aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

In the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102), however, regarding the minor suddhanta, it is stated: "One who has taken it and is observing probation should deduct whatever period he knows of his own purity, and observe probation for the remaining month or two months." Regarding the major suddhanta, it is said: "Having taken it, one should count the nights from the day it was taken up to the day of higher ordination and observe probation." Therefore, only one who observes probation for the duration of the concealed nights is worthy of mānatta, not one who observes probation merely for a period of five or ten nights. This is the intention of the commentary teachers. And for that very reason, it should be understood that it is inappropriate to grant suddhanta probation to conscientious, scrupulous, and training-loving monks who always purify their offenses through confession, informing, and so forth; it is appropriate to grant it to those such as country-dwellers and others who, due to negligence, dwell for a long time without purifying their offenses through confession, informing, and so forth. Here too, the remaining determination should be understood according to the method stated in the commentary.

Atha pana vinayadharena “tvaṃ, āvuso, kataraāpattiṃ āpanno, kati rattiyo te chāditā”ti puṭṭho “ahaṃ, bhante, saṅghādisesaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā pakkhamattaṃ paṭicchāditā, tenāhaṃ saṅghaṃ pakkhaparivāsaṃ yācitvā saṅghena dinne pakkhaparivāse parivasitvā anikkhittavattova hutvā antarā saṅghādisesāpattiṃ āpajjitvā pañcāhamattaṃ chāditā”ti vutte “ayaṃ bhikkhu samodhānaparivāsāraho, tīsu ca samodhānaparivāsesu odhānasamodhānāraho”ti ñatvā [V 2.0180] “tena hi bhikkhu tvaṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanāraho”ti vatvā taṃ mūlāya paṭikassitvā parivutthadivase adivase katvā antarā paṭicchanne pañca divase mūlāpattiyā paṭicchannesu divasesu samodhānetvā odhānasamodhāno dātabbo. Ito parāni odhānasamodhāne vattabbavacanāni pāḷiyaṃ aṭṭhakathāyañca vuttanayeneva veditabbāni.

Then, when asked by the Vinaya master, "Friend, what offense have you committed? For how many nights have you concealed it?" and he replied, "Venerable sir, having committed a saṅghādisesa offense, I concealed it for about half a month. For that, I requested the Saṅgha for a half-month's probation, and having been given the half-month’s probation by the Saṅgha, I underwent probation without having laid down the observance. In the meantime, having committed another saṅghādisesa offense, I concealed it for about five days." When this was said, knowing, 'This monk is worthy of combined probation, and among the three types of combined probation, he is worthy of odhāna-samodhāna,' it was said, 'Well then, monk, you are worthy of being sent back to the beginning.' Having sent him back to the beginning, making the days already spent on probation as non-days, and having combined the five days concealed in the interim with the days concealed for the root offense, odhāna-samodhāna is to be given. From this point onwards, the statements to be made regarding odhāna-samodhāna should be understood according to the method stated in the Pāli and the commentaries.

Atha pana vinayadharena puṭṭho “ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ, sambahulā āpattiyo [M 2.0248] ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo dasāhappaṭicchannāyo”ti vutte “ayaṃ bhikkhu agghasamodhānāraho”ti ñatvā tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ yā āpattiyo ciratarappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāso dātabbo. Tatrevaṃ vadanti – “yā āpattiyo ciratarappaṭicchannāyo, tāsaṃ agghena samodhānaparivāso dātabbo”ti vutto, evaṃ sante pakkhappaṭicchannamāsappaṭicchannādīsu kathanti? Tesupi “yā āpattiyo pakkhappaṭicchannāyo, yā āpattiyo māsappaṭicchannāyo”ti vattabboti. Yadi evaṃ pāḷivirodho āpajjati. Pāḷiyañhi dasāhappaṭicchannapariyosānā eva āpatti dassitā, na pakkhappaṭicchannamāsappaṭicchannādayoti? Saccaṃ, pāḷiyaṃ tathādassanaṃ pana nayadassanamattaṃ. Tathā hi vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) “pañcadasa divasāni paṭicchannāya ‘pakkhappaṭicchanna’nti vatvā yojanā kātabbā…pe… evaṃ yāva saṭṭhisaṃvaccharaṃ, atirekasaṭṭhisaṃvaccharappaṭicchannanti vā tato vā bhiyyopi vatvā yojanā kātabbā”ti. Mahāpadumattherenapi vuttaṃ “ayaṃ samuccayakkhandhako nāma buddhānaṃ ṭhitakālasadiso, āpatti nāma paṭicchannā vā hotu appaṭicchannā vā samakaūnataraatirekappaṭicchannā vā, vinayadharassa kammavācaṃ yojetuṃ samatthabhāvoyevettha pamāṇa”nti, tasmā pakkhappaṭicchannādīnaṃ kammavācākaraṇe kukkuccaṃ na kātabbanti.

Then, when questioned by the Vinaya expert, if he says: "Venerable sir, I have committed numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses, numerous offenses concealed for one day… up to… numerous offenses concealed for ten days," knowing that "this monk is worthy of rehabilitation by aggregation," probation by aggregation should be given based on the value of those offenses that were concealed for the longest time. Herein, they say: "Probation by aggregation should be given based on the value of those offenses that were concealed for the longest time." If this is so, what about offenses concealed for a fortnight, a month, and so on? In those cases too, it should be said: "The offenses concealed for a fortnight, the offenses concealed for a month." But if this is done, does it not contradict the Pāli? For in the Pāli, offenses are only shown up to those concealed for ten days, not those concealed for a fortnight, a month, and so on. True, but the Pāli shows it that way merely to indicate the principle. For it is stated in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102): "For an offense concealed for fifteen days, the wording should be applied by stating 'concealed for a fortnight'… up to sixty years, or even for more than sixty years, the wording should be applied by stating 'concealed for more than sixty years.'" The Elder Mahāpaduma also said: "This section on aggregation is like the fixed duration of the Buddhas. Whether an offense is concealed or unconcealed, or concealed for the same, a lesser, or a greater amount of time—the Vinaya expert's ability to apply the formal act is the measure here." Therefore, there should be no hesitation in performing the formal act for offenses concealed for a fortnight and so on.

Hotu, evampi pakkhappaṭicchannaṃ pariyantaṃ katvā katāya kammavācāya tato uddhaṃ āpatti natthīti kathaṃ jāneyyāti? Idāni sikkhākāmā bhikkhū devasikampi desanārocanāvikaraṇāni karonti ekāhikadvīhikādivasenapi, kiccapasutā hutvā tathā asakkontāpi uposathadivasaṃ nātikkamanti, gilānādivasena tadatikkantāpi atikkantabhāvaṃ [M 2.0249] jānanti, tasmā tadatikkantabhāve sati atirekapakkhappaṭicchannamāsappaṭicchannādivasena vaḍḍhetvā kammavācaṃ kareyya, tadatikkantabhāve pana asati pakkhappaṭicchannapariyantā [V 2.0181] hoti, tasmā pakkhapariyantakammavācākaraṇaṃ ñāyāgataṃ hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

So be it. Even so, if a formal act is performed by making a fortnight the limit, how would one know that there is no offense beyond that? Now, monks who desire training perform daily confession, announcement, and disclosure of offenses, even for periods of one or two days; even if they are busy with duties and unable to do so, they do not let the Uposatha day pass. And even if it passes due to illness or other reasons, they know that it has passed. Therefore, if that time has passed, they should perform the formal act by extending it with an additional fortnight, month, and so on. But if that time has not passed, the limit is a fortnight. Thus, it should be understood that performing the formal act with a fortnight as the limit is proper.

Evaṃ hotu, tathāpi yadetaṃ “sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo pakkhappaṭicchannāyo”ti vuttaṃ, tattha imināyeva anukkamena mayā paṭicchāditā āpattiyo hontīti kathaṃ jāneyya, ajānane ca sati “yā ca khvāyaṃ, āvuso, āpatti ajānappaṭicchannā, adhammikaṃ tassā āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ, adhammattā na ruhatī”ti idaṃ āpajjatīti? Nāpajjati. Tattha hi āpattiyā āpannabhāvaṃ ajānanto hutvā paṭicchādeti, tasmā “āpatti ca hoti āpattisaññī cā”ti vuttaāpattisaññitābhāvā appaṭicchannameva hoti, tasmā appaṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivāsadānaṃ adhammikaṃ hoti. Idha pana “ettakā rattiyo mayā chāditā”ti channakālameva na jānāti, tadajānabhāve satipi parivāsadānaṃ ruhati. Teneva ca kāraṇena suddhantaparivāse (cūḷava. 156-157) “āpattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, rattipariyantaṃ na jānāti, āpattipariyantaṃ nassarati, rattipariyantaṃ nassarati, āpattipariyante vematiko, rattipariyante vematiko”ti rattipariyantassa ajānanaasaraṇavematikabhāve satipi parivāsadānaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmā chāditakālaṃ tathato ajānantopi “sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo pakkhappaṭicchannāyo”ti ettha appaviṭṭhassa abhāvā sampajjatiyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

So be it. Yet, regarding what is said—"numerous offenses concealed for a day… up to… numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight"—how would one know that the offenses were concealed by me in this very sequence? And if one does not know, would it not lead to this: "Friend, this offense was concealed unknowingly; granting probation for such an offense is improper, and because it is improper, it does not take effect"? It does not lead to that. For in that case, one conceals it without knowing that an offense has been committed. Therefore, due to the absence of the perception of an offense as stated in 'there is an offense and one perceives it as an offense,' it is indeed unconcealed. Hence, granting probation for an unconcealed offense is improper. In this case, however, one simply does not know the exact duration of concealment—"I have concealed it for so many nights"—but even in that state of not knowing, the granting of probation takes effect. For this very reason, in the case of probation for an uncertain period (Cūḷavagga 156–157), the granting of probation is stated even in a state of not knowing, not recalling, or being uncertain about the extent of the nights: "One does not know the extent of the offense, does not know the extent of the nights, does not recall the extent of the offense, does not recall the extent of the nights, is uncertain about the extent of the offense, is uncertain about the extent of the nights." Therefore, it should be understood that even if one does not know the exact duration of concealment, regarding "numerous offenses concealed for a day… up to… numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight," since nothing is left unincluded, it is indeed accomplished.

Athāpi [M 2.0250] evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – “sambahulā āpattiyo ekāhappaṭicchannāyo…pe… sambahulā āpattiyo pakkhappaṭicchannāyo”ti vutte tesu divasesu āpattiyo atthi paṭicchannāyopi, atthi appaṭicchannāyopi, atthi cirappaṭicchannāyopi, atthi acirappaṭicchannāyopi, atthi ekāpi, atthi sambahulāpi, sabbā tā āpattiyo eteneva padena saṅgahitā siyunti? Saṅgahitā eva. Na hettha saṃsayo kātabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) “aññasmiṃ pana āpattivuṭṭhāne idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ – yo appaṭicchannaṃ āpattiṃ ‘paṭicchannā’ti vinayakammaṃ karoti, tassa āpatti vuṭṭhāti. Yo paṭicchannaṃ ‘appaṭicchannā’ti vinayakammaṃ karoti, tassa na vuṭṭhāti. Acirappaṭicchannaṃ ‘cirappaṭicchannā’ti karontassapi vuṭṭhāti, cirappaṭicchannaṃ ‘acirappaṭicchannā’ti karontassa na vuṭṭhāti. Ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā ‘sambahulā’ti karontassapi vuṭṭhāti ekaṃ vinā sambahulānaṃ abhāvato. Sambahulā pana āpajjitvā [V 2.0182] ‘ekaṃ āpajji’nti karontassa na vuṭṭhātī”ti, tasmā etehi padehi sabbāsaṃ paṭicchannāpattīnaṃ saṅgahitattā tāhi āpattīhi vuṭṭhānaṃ sambhavatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

And if they should say thus: When it is said, "Numerous offenses concealed for a day… up to… numerous offenses concealed for a fortnight," in those days there are offenses that are concealed, and offenses that are not concealed, and offenses that are long concealed, and offenses that are recently concealed, and a single offense, and numerous offenses—are all those offenses included in this very expression? They are indeed included. There should be no doubt about this. For this was said in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102): "However, in another case of rehabilitation from an offense, this is the characteristic: he who performs a formal act for an unconcealed offense, treating it as ‘concealed,’ is rehabilitated from his offense. He who performs a formal act for a concealed offense, treating it as ‘unconcealed,’ is not rehabilitated. He who treats a recently concealed offense as ‘long concealed’ is also rehabilitated; but he who treats a long concealed offense as ‘recently concealed’ is not rehabilitated. He who, having committed a single offense, treats it as ‘numerous’ is also rehabilitated, because without one, there is no multiplicity. But he who, having committed numerous offenses, treats it as ‘I committed one,’ is not rehabilitated." Therefore, it should be understood that since all concealed offenses are included by these expressions, rehabilitation from those offenses is possible.

Atha pana vinayadharena puṭṭho “ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekaṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ, ekaṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ, ekaṃ duṭṭhullavācaṃ, ekaṃ attakāmaṃ, ekaṃ sañcarittaṃ, ekaṃ kuṭikāraṃ, ekaṃ vihārakāraṃ, ekaṃ duṭṭhadosaṃ, ekaṃ aññabhāgiyaṃ, ekaṃ saṅghabhedaṃ, ekaṃ bhedānuvattakaṃ, ekaṃ dubbacaṃ, ekaṃ kuladūsaka”nti vutte “ayaṃ bhikkhu missakasamodhānaparivāsāraho”ti ñatvā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) āgatanayena parivāso dātabbo. Etthāha – agghasamodhānamissakasamodhānānaṃ ko viseso, kiṃ nānākaraṇanti? Vuccate – agghasamodhānaparivāso acirappaṭicchannā [M 2.0251] āpattiyo cirappaṭicchannāyaṃ āpattiyaṃ samodhānetvā tassā cirappaṭicchannāya āpattiyā agghavasena dīyati, missakasamodhānaparivāso nānāvatthukā āpattiyo samodhānetvā tāsaṃ missakavasena dīyati, ayametesaṃ viseso. Atha vā agghasamodhāno sabhāgavatthūnaṃ āpattīnaṃ samodhānavasena hoti, itaro visabhāgavatthūnanti ācariyā. Tenevāha ācariyavajirabuddhitthero (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 102) “agghasamodhāno nāma sabhāgavatthukāyo sambahulā āpattiyo āpannassa bahurattiṃ paṭicchāditāpattiyaṃ nikkhipitvā dātabbo, itaro nānāvatthukānaṃ vasenāti ayametesaṃ viseso”ti.

Then, when questioned by a Vinaya expert, he said: "Venerable sir, I have committed numerous Saṅghādisesa offenses: one Sukkavissaṭṭhi, one Kāyasaṃsagga, one Duṭṭhullavācā, one Attakāma, one Sañcaritta, one Kuṭikāra, one Vihārakāra, one Duṭṭhadosa, one Aññabhāgiya, one Saṅghabheda, one Bhedānuvattaka, one Dubbaca, and one Kuladūsaka." Upon hearing this, knowing that "This monk is deserving of probation by mixture," probation should be given according to the method found in the commentary (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102). Here, one might ask: What is the difference between probation by valuation and probation by mixture, and what is their distinction? It is said: Probation by valuation is given by combining recently concealed offenses with a long-concealed offense, based on the value of that long-concealed offense. Probation by mixture is given by combining offenses with different grounds, based on their mixture. This is the distinction between them. Alternatively, probation by valuation is for offenses of similar grounds, while the other is for those of dissimilar grounds—so say the teachers. Therefore, the elder teacher Vajirabuddhi (Vajira Ṭīkā, Cūḷavagga 102) states: "Probation by valuation is to be given to one who has committed numerous offenses of similar grounds by placing them into the offense concealed for many nights; the other is based on offenses of different grounds. This is the distinction between them."

Atha siyā “evaṃ cirappaṭicchannāyo ca acirappaṭicchannāyo ca nānāvatthukāyo āpattiyo āpajjantassa ko parivāso dātabbo agghasamodhāno vā missakasamodhāno vā, atha tadubhayā vā”ti. Kiñcettha – yadi agghasamodhānaṃ dadeyya, cirappaṭicchannāhi ca acirappaṭicchannāhi ca sabhāgavatthukāhi āpattīhi vuṭṭhito bhaveyya, cirappaṭicchannāhi ca acirappaṭicchannāhi ca no visabhāgavatthukāhi. Yadi ca missakasamodhānaṃ dadeyya, samānakālappaṭicchannāhi visabhāgavatthūhi āpattīhi vuṭṭhito bhaveyya, no asamānakaālappaṭicchannāhi sabhāgavatthukāhi ca, atha tadubhayampi dadeyya, “ekasmiṃ kamme dve parivāsā dātabbā”ti neva pāḷiyaṃ, na aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti? Vuccate – idañhi sabbampi parivāsādikaṃ vinayakammaṃ vatthuvasena vā gottavasena vā nāmavasena vā āpattivasena vā kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

Then it might be asked: "For one who has committed offenses of various grounds, some concealed for a long time and some for a short time, what probation should be given? Probation by valuation or probation by mixture, or both?" What then is the case here? If probation by valuation is given, he would be absolved of offenses of similar ground, whether concealed for a long time or a short time, but not of those of dissimilar ground. And if probation by mixture is given, he would be absolved of offenses of dissimilar ground concealed for the same period, but not of those of similar ground concealed for different periods. But if both were given, it would mean that "two periods of probation should be given for one act"—and this is not stated in the Pāḷi or the commentaries. It is said: All of this disciplinary action related to probation and so on is indeed suitable to be done based on the ground, or the lineage, or the name, or the offense.

Tattha [M 2.0252][V 2.0183] sukkavissaṭṭhīti vatthu ceva gottañca. Saṅghādisesoti nāmañceva āpatti ca. Tattha “sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ kāyasaṃsagga”ntiādivacanenāpi “nānāvatthukāyo”ti vacanenapi vatthu ceva gottañca gahitaṃ hoti, “saṅghādiseso”ti vacanenapi “āpattiyo”ti vacanenapi nāmañceva āpatti ca gahitā hoti, tasmā agghasamodhānavasena parivāse dinne “ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji”ntiādivacaneneva vatthussa ca gottassa ca nāmassa ca āpattiyā ca gahitattā cirappaṭicchannāhi acirappaṭicchannāhi ca sabhāgavatthukāhi ca visabhāgavatthukāhi ca sabbāhi āpattīhi vuṭṭhātīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ samantapāsādikāyaṃ “ettha ca ‘saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ nānāvatthukāyo’tipi ‘saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajji’ntipi evaṃ pubbe vuttanayena vatthuvasenapi gottavasenapi nāmavasenapi āpattivasenapi yojetvā kammavācaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyevāti ayaṃ missakasamodhāno”ti, imasmiñca vinayasaṅgahappakaraṇe (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 245) tatheva vatvā “tasmā na idha visuṃ kammavācaṃ yojetvā dassayissāma, pubbe sabbāpattisādhāraṇaṃ katvā yojetvā dassitāya eva kammavācāya nānāvatthukāhipi āpattīhi vuṭṭhānasambhavato sāyevettha kammavācā ala”nti.

Here, 'emission of semen' refers to both the ground and the lineage. 'Saṅghādisesa' refers to both the name and the offense. In this context, by the phrase 'emission of semen, bodily contact,' and so on, and by the phrase 'of various grounds,' both the ground and the lineage are taken. Similarly, by the term 'Saṅghādisesa' and by the phrase 'offenses,' both the name and the offense are taken. Therefore, when probation by valuation is given, by the statement 'Venerable sir, I have committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses,' and so on, since the ground, the lineage, the name, and the offense are all taken, it should be understood that one is absolved of all offenses—whether concealed for a long time or a short time, and whether of similar ground or dissimilar ground. This is stated in the Samantapāsādikā: 'Here, whether one says, “I have committed Saṅghādisesa offenses of various grounds,” or “I have committed Saṅghādisesa offenses,” the formal act can be performed by combining them according to the method stated previously, based on the ground, or the lineage, or the name, or the offense. This is probation by mixture.' Similarly, in this Vinaya Saṅgaha treatise (Vi. Saṅga. Aṭṭha. 245), having stated the same, it is said: 'Therefore, we will not separately formulate and show the formal act here. Since with the formal act previously shown, which was formulated to be common to all offenses, it is possible to be absolved even of offenses of various grounds, that same formal act suffices here.'

Yadi evaṃ ācariyavajirabuddhittherena dvinnaṃ viseso na vattabbo, atha kasmā vuttoti? Tīsu samodhānaparivāsesu odhānasamodhāno mūlāyapaṭikassanāya odhūnitakāleyeva dātabbo, agghasamodhānamissakasamodhānaparivāsā pana visuṃyeva dātabbā. “Evaṃ dinne etesaṃ [M 2.0253] ko viseso”ti cintāyaṃ visesasambhavamattadassanatthaṃ vutto. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana parivāsādikammassa lakkhaṇaṃ dassetuṃ “vatthuvasena vā”tiādimāha, tasmā lakkhaṇavaseneva sabhāgavatthukāhipi āpattīhi vuṭṭhānaṃ sambhavati. Teneva ca kāraṇena sāratthadīpanināmikāyaṃ vinayaṭīkāyañca vimativinodanināmikāyaṃ vinayaṭīkāyañca na koci viseso vuttoti daṭṭhabbo.

If this is so, the distinction between the two should not have been stated by the elder teacher Vajirabuddhi. Why then was it stated? Among the three kinds of probation by aggregation, probation by covering should be given only at the time of being sent back to the beginning, while probation by valuation and probation by mixture should be given separately. It was stated to show the mere possibility of a distinction when one considers, 'What is the distinction between these when given thus?' However, in the commentary, to show the characteristic of the formal act of probation and so on, it said 'based on the ground,' and so on. Therefore, absolution from offenses of similar ground is also possible based on the characteristic alone. And for that very reason, it should be understood that no distinction is mentioned in the Vinaya subcommentary named Sāratthadīpanī or in the Vinaya subcommentary named Vimativinodanī.

Yadi evaṃ missakasamodhānakammavācāyapi cirappaṭicchannāhi acirappaṭicchannāhipi āpattīhi vuṭṭhānaṃ sambhaveyya. Tatthapi hi “ahaṃ, bhante, sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ nānāvatthukāyo”tipi “ekā sukkavissaṭṭhi…pe… ekā kuladūsakā”tipi vattabbaṃ. Evaṃ sati “sambahulā”tipi “saṅghādisesā āpattiyo”tipi vatthugottanāmāpattīhi kittanasambhavato cirappaṭicchannāhipi acirappaṭicchannāhipi āpattīhi vuṭṭhānaṃ sambhaveyyāti? Na panevaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vatthādikittanañhi sabbāpattīnaṃ gaṇhanatthaṃ hoti. Evaṃ gaṇhantepi paṭicchannakālassa [V 2.0184] akathitattā “ettakaṃ nāma kālaṃ parivasitabba”nti na paññāyati, tasmiṃ apaññāyamāne tena pamāṇena parivāso na hoti, tasmiṃ asati āpattito vuṭṭhānaṃ na sambhavati, tasmā missakasamodhānakammavācāya cirappaṭicchannāhipi acirappaṭicchannāhipi āpattīhi vuṭṭhānaṃ na sambhavatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

If this is so, then even with the formal act for probation by mixture, absolution from offenses concealed for a long time and those concealed for a short time would be possible. For there too, one should say, 'Venerable sir, I have committed many Saṅghādisesa offenses of various grounds,' or 'One emission of semen... one corrupting of families,' and so on. If that is so, then because the mention of 'many' and 'Saṅghādisesa offenses' makes it possible to state the ground, lineage, name, and offense, would absolution from offenses concealed for a long time and those concealed for a short time be possible? But it should not be seen thus. For the stating of the ground and so on is for the purpose of including all offenses. Even when including them thus, because the period of concealment is not stated, it is not known 'for such and such a period probation must be undertaken.' When that is not known, probation of that measure does not occur; when that is absent, absolution from the offense is not possible. Therefore, it should be understood that with the formal act for probation by mixture, absolution from offenses concealed for a long time and those concealed for a short time is not possible.

Parivāsavinicchayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on the determination of probation is concluded.

Mānattavinicchayakathā

The Discussion on the Ascertainment of Penance

Mānattakathāyampi mānattaṃ nāma appaṭicchannamānattaṃ paṭicchannamānattaṃ pakkhamānattaṃ samodhānamānattanti catubbidhaṃ hoti. Tattha [M 2.0254] yo bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā taṃ divasameva āroceti, ekarattimattampi na paṭicchādeti, tassa parivāsaṃ adatvāva dinnaṃ mānattaṃ appaṭicchannamānattaṃ nāma. Yo āpajjitvā dasahi ākārehi vinā taṃ divasaṃ nāroceti, ekarattādivasena paṭicchādeti, tattha yathāpaṭicchannadivasaṃ parivāsaṃ datvā parivutthaparivāsassa dinnaṃ mānattaṃ paṭicchannamānattaṃ nāma. Āpattiṃ āpajjitvā paṭicchannāya vā appaṭicchannāya vā bhikkhuniyā pakkhamattameva dinnaṃ mānattaṃ pakkhamānattaṃ nāma. Bhikkhu pana paṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivasitvā anikkhittavattakāleyeva puna āpajjitvā na paṭicchādeti, tassa mūlāya paṭikassitvā parivutthadivase adivase katvā appaṭicchāditattā samodhānaparivāsaṃ adatvā dinnaṃ mānattaṃ samodhānamānattaṃ nāma. Mānattārahakālepi mānattacaraṇakālepi abbhānārahakālepi eseva nayo. Tesu tīṇi mānattāni aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayena suviññeyyattā na vuttāni. Pakkhamānattaṃ pacchā āgamissati.

In the discussion on mānatta, it is said that mānatta is of four kinds: unconcealed mānatta, concealed mānatta, fortnight mānatta, and combined mānatta. Herein, when a monk commits a saṅghādisesa offense and reports it on the very same day, not concealing it even for a single night, the mānatta given to him without assigning any parivāsa is called unconcealed mānatta. When one commits an offense and, without the ten conditions, does not report it on that day but conceals it for a night or more, the mānatta given to him after assigning parivāsa for the number of days it was concealed—once the parivāsa is completed—is called concealed mānatta. The mānatta given to a bhikkhunī for only a fortnight, for an offense whether concealed or unconcealed, is called fortnight mānatta. However, if a monk, after completing parivāsa for a concealed offense, commits another offense before the obligations have been relinquished and does not conceal it, he is sent back to the beginning. The days of completed parivāsa are made as not completed, and because he did not conceal it, combined parivāsa is not assigned, and the mānatta given to him is called combined mānatta. The same principle applies to the time when one is eligible for mānatta, the time of undergoing mānatta, and the time when one is eligible for reinstatement. Among these, three types of mānatta are not discussed here, as they are easily understood in accordance with the method stated in the commentary. Fortnight mānatta will be discussed later.

Yāni pana parivāsamānattāni anavaṭṭhitattā puthujjanassa gihiādivasena parivattane sati puna dātabbādātabbabhāve saṅkitabbāni, tāni dassetuṃ pāḷiyaṃ anekehi pakārehi vitthārato vuttāni. Tesu bhikkhūnaṃ saṃsayavinodanatthāya ekadesaṃ dassetuṃ “sace kocī”tiādimāha. Tattha vibbhamatīti virūpo hutvā bhamati, hīnāyāvattati gihī hotīti attho. Sāmaṇero hotīti upasampannabhāvaṃ jahitvā sāmaṇerabhāvaṃ upagacchati. Tattha pārājikappattabhāvena vā “gihīti maṃ dhārethā”tiādinā sikkhāpaccakkhānena vā gihī hoti[V 2.0185]. Tesu paṭhamena puna upasampadāya abhabbattā puna parivāso na ruhatiyeva, dutiyena pana puna upasampadāya bhabbattā “so ce puna upasampajjatī”ti [M 2.0255] vuttaṃ. Itaro pana pārājikappattabhāvena sāmaṇero na hoti. Kasmā? Saraṇagamanādīnaṃ vinassanato. Vuttañhi vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. mahāvagga 2.108) “upasampannānampi pārājikasamaāpattiyā saraṇagamanādisāmaṇerabhāvassapi vinassanato senāsanaggāho ca paṭippassambhati, saṅghalābhampi tena labhantīti veditabba”nti, gihī pana hutvā puna sāmaṇerabhāvamattaṃ laddhabbaṃ hoti. “Sāmaṇeroti maṃ dhārethā”tiādinā pana sikkhāpaccakkhāne kate siyā sāmaṇerabhāvo, tatopi puna upasampajjitukāmatāya sati siyā upasampannabhāvo. “Gihīti maṃ dhārethā”tiādinā sikkhāpaccakkhānaṃ katvā gihibhāvaṃ upagatepi puna sāmaṇerapabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā sāmaṇero hoti. Tato puna upasampajjituṃ laddhabbattā “puna upasampajjatī”ti vutto. Tesaṃ bhikkhubhāve parivāse aniṭṭhitepi gihisāmaṇerabhāvaṃ pattattā parivāso na ruhati upasampannānameva parivāsassa bhagavatā paññattattāti attho.

However, since probation and penance are unstable for an ordinary person, when one reverts to the state of a layperson or other status, there is doubt as to whether they should be given again. To show this, they are explained in detail in the Pāli Canon in many ways. To dispel the monks' doubts, a portion is explained starting with “if someone,” and so on. Here, “vibbhamati” means he wanders having changed his form; he reverts to a lower state, that is, he becomes a layperson. “Sāmaṇero hoti” means he abandons the status of a fully ordained monk and takes up the status of a novice. In this case, he becomes a layperson either by having committed an offense entailing expulsion (pārājika) or by renouncing the training, saying, “Consider me a layperson,” and so on. In the first case, since he is not eligible for reordination, probation does not take effect again.
