But in the second case, since reordination is possible, it is said, “if he is reordained.” However, one does not become a novice by having committed a pārājika offense. Why? Because the taking of refuge and other qualities are destroyed. As stated in the Vimativinodanī: “Even for the ordained, when an offense equal to a pārājika is committed, the taking of refuge and even the state of a novice are destroyed. The right to occupy a dwelling also ceases, and it should be understood that they receive no gains from the Saṅgha.” But if one becomes a layperson, one must first regain the mere status of a novice. If one renounces the training by saying, “Consider me a novice,” and so on, one may become a novice. If, after that, one wishes to be reordained, one may regain fully ordained status. Even if one renounces the training by saying, “Consider me a layperson,” and becomes a layperson, one may later go forth as a novice and become a novice again. Since reordination is then possible, it is said, “he is reordained.” For them, even if their probation was incomplete while they were monks, it does not take effect upon their reverting to the state of a layperson or novice—because the Blessed One prescribed probation only for the fully ordained. That is the meaning.

Evaṃ sante puna upasampajjantassa kiṃ parivāso puna dātabboti āha “so ce puna upasampajjatī”tiādi. Tassattho – so vibbhantako so vā sāmaṇero puna upasampannabhāvaṃ upagacchati, purimaṃ pubbe bhikkhubhūtakāle dinnaṃ parivāsadānaṃ eva idāni parivāsadānaṃ hoti. Yo parivāso pubbe bhikkhubhūtakāle dinno, so parivāso sudinno, dudinno na hoti. Yo yattako kālo parivuttho, so tattako kālo suparivutthoyeva hoti, na duparivuttho, tasmā avaseso kālo parivasitabboti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – pubbe bhikkhukāle pakkhappaṭicchannāya āpattiyā parivāsaṃ gahetvā dasadivasamattaṃ parivasitvā aniṭṭhiteyeva parivāse vibbhamitvā sāmaṇero [M 2.0256] vā hutvā puna upasampannena avasesapañcadivase parivasitvā parivāso niṭṭhāpetabboti. Mānattārahādīsupi eseva nayo. Ummattakādīsupi tasmiṃ kāle ajānantattā “parivāso na ruhatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tiṇṇampi ukkhittakānaṃ kammanānāsaṃvāsakattā tehi sahasaṃvāsoyeva natthīti ukkhittakānaṃ parivāso na ruhatīti vuttaṃ.

This being so, should probation be given again to one who reordains? To this, it is said, “If he reordains,” etc. The meaning is this: that deviant or that novice, having regained the state of being ordained, the probation that was given previously, when he was a bhikkhu, is still the valid probation. The probation given previously, when he was a bhikkhu, is well-given; it is not ill-given. Whatever period of time was spent in probation is well-spent; it is not ill-spent. Therefore, the remaining time must be spent. This is what is meant: if one, having taken probation for an offense concealed for a fortnight while he was a bhikkhu, spends only ten days in probation and then deviates before completing the probation, becoming a novice, and later reordains, he must complete the remaining five days to fulfill the probation. The same principle applies to those deserving mānatta and others. For the insane and others, because they were unaware at that time, it is said, “Probation does not take effect.” For the three types of those who have been suspended, because they are of a different communion due to the formal act, there is no communion with them at all. Thus, it is said, “Probation does not take effect for those who have been suspended.”

Sace puna osārīyatīti ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhanavasena samānasaṃvāsakabhāvaṃ pavesīyati. “Sace kassaci bhikkhuno itthiliṅgaṃ pātubhavatī”tiādīsu aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva attho suviññeyyo hoti. Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ “pakkhamānattaṃ pacchā āgamissatī”ti, tatrevaṃ [V 2.0186] jānitabbaṃ – pakkhamānattanti bhikkhuniyā dātabbamānattaṃ. Taṃ pana paṭicchannāyapi appaṭicchannāyapi āpattiyā aḍḍhamāsamattameva dātabbaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ “garudhammaṃ ajjhāpannāya bhikkhuniyā ubhatosaṅghe pakkhamānattaṃ caritabba”nti (pāci. 149; cūḷava. 403; a. ni. 8.51). Taṃ pana bhikkhunīhi attano sīmaṃ sodhetvā vihārasīmāya vā vihārasīmaṃ sodhetuṃ asakkontīhi khaṇḍasīmāya vā sabbantimena paricchedena catuvaggagaṇaṃ sannipātāpetvā dātabbaṃ. Sace ekā āpatti hoti, ekissā vasena, sace dve vā tisso vā sambahulā vā ekavatthukā vā nānāvatthukā vā, tāsaṃ tāsaṃ vasena vatthugottanāmaāpattīsu yaṃ yaṃ icchati, taṃ taṃ ādāya yojanā kātabbā.

“If he is reinstated” means he is restored to the status of equal communion by rescinding the act of suspension. The meaning of passages such as, “If female characteristics appear in a certain bhikkhu…” is easily understood in the manner explained in the commentary. But as for what was said, “Fortnight mānatta will be discussed later,” this should be understood thus: fortnight mānatta is the mānatta to be given to a bhikkhunī. That penance is to be given for only half a month, whether for a concealed or unconcealed offense. For it has been said, “A bhikkhunī who has transgressed a grave rule must undergo fortnight mānatta in both Saṅghas.” That mānatta, however, should be given by the bhikkhunīs after purifying their own boundary, or if they are unable to purify the monastery boundary, in a partial boundary or, as a final option, by assembling a chapter of four. If there is one offense, it is done on the basis of that single offense; if there are two, three, or many offenses, whether based on the same circumstance or different circumstances, then for each of those, the application should be made by taking up whichever subject, category, name, or offense one wishes.

Tatridaṃ ekāpattivasena mukhamattanidassanaṃ – tāya āpannāya bhikkhuniyā bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vuḍḍhānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo “ahaṃ[M 2.0257], ayye, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ gāmantaraṃ, sāhaṃ, ayya,e ekissā āpattiyā gāmantarāya pakkhamānattaṃ yācāmī”ti. Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ yācāpetvā byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo “suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho, ayaṃ itthannāmā bhikkhunī ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajji gāmantaraṃ, sā saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā gāmantarāya pakkhamānattaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā ekissā āpattiyā gāmantarāya pakkhamānattaṃ dadeyya, esā ñatti. Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho…pe… dutiyampi. Tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi. Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho…pe… bhāseyya. Dinnaṃ saṅghena itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā ekissā āpattiyā gāmantarāya pakkhamānattaṃ, khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Here is a mere outline for a single offense: The nun who has committed the offense should approach the community of nuns, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the senior nuns, sit in a squatting position, raise her hands in añjali, and say: “Venerables, I have committed one offense involving going to another village. I request the community for half-month mānatta for that single offense involving going to another village.” After having her make the request three times, a competent and capable nun should inform the community: “Venerables, may the community listen. This nun named so-and-so has committed one offense involving going to another village. She requests the community for half-month mānatta for that single offense involving going to another village. If the community is ready, it may grant her half-month mānatta for that single offense involving going to another village. This is the motion.” “Venerables, may the community listen… (second time).” “For the third time, I speak on this matter. Venerables, may the community listen… she who does not approve should speak.” “The community has granted half-month mānatta to the nun named so-and-so for that single offense involving going to another village. The community approves, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

Kammavācāpariyosāne vattaṃ samādiyitvā bhikkhumānattakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva saṅghassa ārocetvā nikkhittavattaṃ vasitukāmāya tatheva saṅghassa majjhe vā pakkantāsu bhikkhunīsu ekabhikkhuniyā vā dutiyikāya vā santike vuttanayeneva nikkhipitabbaṃ. Aññissā pana āgantukāya santike ārocetvā nikkhipitabbaṃ, nikkhittakālato paṭṭhāya pakatattaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati.

At the conclusion of the formal act, having undertaken the observance, she should inform the Saṅgha in the manner stated in the discussion on the mānatta for monks. If she wishes to reside after relinquishing the observance, she should relinquish it in the same way, either in the midst of the Saṅgha or, after the nuns have departed, in the presence of one nun or a second, as stated. But if another newly arrived nun arrives, she should announce it in her presence and then relinquish it. From the time of relinquishment, she stands in the position of one of good standing.

Puna samādiyitvā aruṇaṃ uṭṭhapentiyā pana bhikkhunīnaṃyeva santike vasituṃ na labbhati[V 2.0187]. “Ubhatosaṅghe pakkhamānattaṃ caritabba”nti hi vuttaṃ, tasmā assā ācariyupajjhāyāhi vihāraṃ gantvā saṅgāhakapakkhe ṭhito eko mahāthero vā dhammakathiko vā bhikkhu vattabbo “ekissā bhikkhuniyā vinayakammaṃ kattabbamatthi, tatra no ayyā cattāro bhikkhū pesethā”ti. Saṅgahaṃ akātuṃ na labbhati, “pesessāmā”ti vattabbaṃ. Catūhi pakatattabhikkhunīhi mānattacāriniṃ bhikkhuniṃ [M 2.0258] gahetvā antoaruṇeyeva nikkhipitvā gāmūpacārato dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā maggā okkamma gumbavatiādīhi paṭicchanne ṭhāne nisīditabbaṃ, vihārūpacāratopi dve leḍḍupātā atikkamitabbā. Catūhi pakatattabhikkhūhipi tattha gantabbaṃ, gantvā pana bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ na ekaṭṭhāne nisīditabbaṃ, paṭikkamitvā avidūre ṭhāne nisīditabbaṃ. Kurundimahāpaccarīsu pana “bhikkhunīhi byattaṃ ekaṃ vā dve vā upāsikāyo bhikkhūhipi ekaṃ vā dve vā upāsake attarakkhaṇatthāya gahetvā gantabba”nti vuttaṃ. Kurundiyaṃyeva ca “bhikkhunupassayassa ca vihārassa ca upacāraṃ muñcituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ, “gāmassā”ti na vuttaṃ.

Again, having undertaken the penance, it is not permissible for her to dwell near the bhikkhunīs themselves while dawn is rising. Indeed, it has been said: 'The half-month penance must be observed in both Saṅghas.' Therefore, her teachers and preceptors should go to the monastery and speak to a senior bhikkhu or Dhamma speaker who is supportive: 'There is a Vinaya act to be performed for a bhikkhunī; for that, venerable sirs, send us four bhikkhus.' It is not permissible to refuse support; one must say, 'We will send them.' Four ordinary bhikkhunīs should take the bhikkhunī observing the mānatta and, having brought her just before dawn, and having gone beyond two stone-throws from the village vicinity, they should step off the path and sit in a place concealed by bushes or similar. From the monastery vicinity too, two stone-throws should be crossed. Four ordinary bhikkhus should also go there. However, upon arriving, they should not sit in the same place with the bhikkhunīs but should withdraw and sit at a short distance. In the Kurundimahāpaccarī, it is said: 'For self-protection, the bhikkhunīs may take one or two competent laywomen, and the bhikkhus may take one or two laymen.' Furthermore, in the Kurundī itself, it is stated: 'It is permissible to leave the vicinity of the bhikkhunīs’ dwelling and the monastery,' but it does not say, 'of the village.'

Evaṃ nisinnesu pana bhikkhunīsu ca bhikkhūsu ca tāya bhikkhuniyā “mānattaṃ samādiyāmi, vattaṃ samādiyāmī”ti vattaṃ samādiyitvā bhikkhunisaṅghassa tāva evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ “ahaṃ, ayye, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ gāmantaraṃ, sāhaṃ saṅghaṃ ekissā āpattiyā gāmantarāya pakkhamānattaṃ yāciṃ, tassā me saṅgho ekissā āpattiyā gāmantarāya pakkhamānattaṃ adāsi, sāhaṃ mānattaṃ carāmi, vediyāmahaṃ ayye, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti.

When the bhikkhunīs and bhikkhus were thus seated, that bhikkhunī, having undertaken the observance by saying, 'I undertake the mānatta, I undertake the duty,' should then announce to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha as follows: 'Venerables, I committed one offense involving going to another village. I asked the Saṅgha for half-month mānatta for that one offense involving going to another village. The Saṅgha granted me half-month mānatta for that one offense involving going to another village. I am now observing the mānatta. I inform you, Venerables; may the Saṅgha remember me as one who informs.'

Tato bhikkhusaṅghassa santikaṃ gantvā evaṃ ārocetabbaṃ “ahaṃ, ayyā, ekaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjiṃ…pe… vediyāmahaṃ ayyā, vediyatīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti. Idhāpi yāya kāyaci bhāsāya ārocetuṃ vaṭṭati. Ārocetvā ca bhikkhunisaṅghasseva santike nisīditabbaṃ, ārocitakālato paṭṭhāya bhikkhūnaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace sāsaṅkā hoti, bhikkhuniyo tattheva ṭhānaṃ paccāsīsanti, ṭhātabbaṃ. Sace añño bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā taṃ ṭhānaṃ eti, passantiyā ārocetabbaṃ. No ce āroceti, ratticchedo ceva vattabhedadukkaṭañca[M 2.0259]. Sace ajānantiyā eva upacāraṃ okkamitvā gacchati, ratticchedova hoti, na vattabhedadukkaṭaṃ. Sace bhikkhuniyo upajjhāyādīnaṃ vattakaraṇatthaṃ pageva gantukāmā honti, rattivippavāsagaṇaohīyanagāmantarāpattirakkhaṇatthaṃ [V 2.0188] ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ ṭhapetvā gantabbaṃ, tāya aruṇe uṭṭhite tassā santike vattaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Etenupāyena akhaṇḍā pañcadasa rattiyo mānattaṃ caritabbaṃ.

Then, having approached the Bhikkhu Saṅgha, one should announce as follows: 'Venerable sirs, I committed one offense… (and so on) … I inform you, venerable sirs; may the Saṅgha remember me as one who informs.' Here too, it is permissible to announce in any language. After announcing, one should sit near the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha itself, and from the time of the announcement, it is permissible for the bhikkhus to leave. If she is fearful, the bhikkhunīs expect her to remain right there in that place; she should stay. If another bhikkhu or bhikkhunī comes to that place, she should announce it if she sees them. If she does not announce it, there is an interruption of the night and a dukkaṭa for breaking the duty. If she unknowingly enters the vicinity and leaves, there is only an interruption of the night, not a dukkaṭa for breaking the duty. If the bhikkhunīs wish to go beforehand for the sake of performing duties for their preceptor or others, they should go after leaving one bhikkhunī behind—for the sake of guarding against the offenses of spending the night apart, falling behind the group, and going to another village. When dawn has risen, the duty should be deposited with her. In this way, an unbroken fifteen nights of mānatta should be observed.

Anikkhittavattāya pana pārivāsikakkhandhake vuttanayeneva sammā vattitabbaṃ. Ayaṃ pana viseso – “āgantukassa ārocetabba”nti ettha yattakā purebhattaṃ vā pacchābhattaṃ vā taṃ gāmaṃ bhikkhū vā bhikkhuniyo vā āgacchanti, sabbesaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Anārocentiyā ratticchedo ceva vattabhedadukkaṭañca. Sacepi rattiṃ koci bhikkhu taṃ gāmūpacāraṃ okkamitvā gacchati, ratticchedo hotiyeva, ajānanapaccayā pana vattabhedato muccati. Kurundīādīsu pana “anikkhittavattabhikkhūnaṃ vuttanayeneva kathetabba”nti vuttaṃ, taṃ pārivāsikavattādīnaṃ upacārasīmāya paricchinnattā yuttataraṃ dissati. Uposathe ārocetabbaṃ, pavāraṇāya ārocetabbaṃ, catunnaṃ bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca devasikaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Sace bhikkhūnaṃ tasmiṃ gāme bhikkhācāro sampajjati, tattheva gantabbaṃ. No ce sampajjati, aññatra caritvāpi tatra āgantvā attānaṃ dassetvā gantabbaṃ, bahigāme vā saṅketaṭṭhānaṃ kātabbaṃ “asukasmiṃ nāma ṭhāne amhe passissatī”ti. Tāya saṅketaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā ārocetabbaṃ, saṅketaṭṭhāne adisvā vihāraṃ gantvā ārocetabbaṃ. Vihāre sabbabhikkhūnaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Sace sabbesaṃ sakkā na hoti ārocetuṃ, bahi upacārasīmāya ṭhatvā bhikkhuniyo pesetabbā, tāhi ānītānaṃ catunnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Sace vihāro dūro hoti sāsaṅko, upāsake ca upāsikāyo [M 2.0260] ca gahetvā gantabbaṃ. Sace pana ayaṃ ekā vasati, rattivippavāsaṃ āpajjati, tasmāssā ekā pakatattā bhikkhunī sammannitvā dātabbā ekacchanne vasanatthāya.

However, for one whose duty has not been laid aside, it should be properly conducted in the manner explained in the Pārivāsika Khandhaka. Here is the distinction: 'The incoming one should be informed.' In this case, whether before the meal or after the meal, all bhikkhus or bhikkhunīs who come to that village must be informed. If she fails to inform them, it entails both an interruption of the night and a dukkaṭa for breaking the duty. Even if a bhikkhu enters the vicinity of that village at night and leaves, the night is still interrupted, but on account of not knowing, she is exempt from the dukkaṭa for breaking the duty. In texts like the Kurundī, it is stated: 'One should speak to monks whose duty has not been laid aside in the prescribed manner.' This seems more appropriate because the probation duty and the like are defined by the boundary of the vicinity. It should be announced on the Uposatha day, on the Pavāraṇā day, and daily to four bhikkhus and four bhikkhunīs. If the bhikkhus' alms-round succeeds in that village, she should go there. If not, she should go elsewhere and then return to that village to show herself. Alternatively, a meeting place outside the village should be arranged, saying, 'You will see us at such-and-such a place.' Having gone to that meeting place, she should inform them. If she does not find them at the meeting place, she should go to the monastery and inform them there. All bhikkhus in the monastery must be informed. If it is not possible to inform all of them, bhikkhunīs should be sent after standing outside the boundary of the vicinity, and the four bhikkhus who have been brought by them should be informed. If the monastery is far and dangerous, laymen and laywomen should be taken along. If she lives alone, she incurs the offense of spending the night apart; therefore, one ordinary bhikkhunī should be appointed and given to her to dwell under one roof.

Evaṃ akhaṇḍaṃ mānattaṃ caritvā vīsatigaṇe bhikkhunisaṅghe vuttanayeneva abbhānaṃ kātabbaṃ. “Sace mānattaṃ caramānā antarāpattiṃ āpajjati, mūlāya paṭikassitvā tassā āpattiyā mānattaṃ dātabba”nti kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ, idaṃ pakkhamānattaṃ nāma. Idaṃ pana pakkhamānattaṃ samantapāsādikāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) pāḷimuttavinayavinicchayabhāvena āgatampi imasmiṃ vinayasaṅgahappakaraṇe ācariyena anuddhaṭaṃ. Ayaṃ panācariyassa adhippāyo siyā – idaṃ pakkhamānattaṃ bhikkhuniyoyeva sandhāya bhagavatā visuṃ paññattaṃ, bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇaṃ, imasmiñca kāle bhikkhunisaṅgho natthi, tasmā ganthassa lahubhāvatthaṃ idampi aññampi īdisaṃ ajjhupekkhitabbanti. Amhehi pana bhikkhunisaṅghe avijjamānepi “bhikkhusaṅgho [V 2.0189] bhikkhunīhi samādātabbavattaṃ jānissati. ‘Dubbalajātikā hi bhīrukajātikā bhikkhuniyo bhagavato āṇaṃ patiṭṭhāpentiyo evarūpaṃ dukkaraṃ durabhisambhavaṃ vattaṃ samādayiṃsu, kimaṅgaṃ pana maya’nti manasi karontā bhagavato āṇaṃ patiṭṭhāpentā parivāsādivattaṃ samādiyissantī”ti mantvā ācariyena anuddhaṭampi imasmiṃ vinayālaṅkārappakaraṇe uddhaṭaṃ, tasmā sammāsambuddhe sañjātasaddhāpemagāravādiyuttehi satthusāsanakarehi bhikkhūhi sammā sikkhitabbaṃ. Ito parāni aṭṭhakathāyaṃ āgatanayeneva veditabbāni.

Having thus completed the unbroken mānatta, reinstatement should be performed in a Bhikkhunī Saṅgha of twenty, in the manner stated. 'If, while observing mānatta, she incurs an intermediate offense, she should be sent back to the origin and mānatta should be given for that offense,' as stated in the Kurundī. This is called pakkhamānatta. This pakkhamānatta, though it appears in the Samantapāsādikā (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102) as a Vinaya decision not found in the Pāḷi, was not extracted by the teacher in this Vinaya compilation treatise. The teacher’s intention here might be this: that this pakkhamānatta was separately prescribed by the Blessed One specifically for bhikkhunīs and is not common to bhikkhus; and since the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha does not exist in this era, for the sake of brevity of the text, this and similar matters were overlooked. However, we considered that even though the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha is non-existent, 'The Bhikkhu Saṅgha will know the duty to be undertaken by bhikkhunīs. Reflecting, "Indeed, bhikkhunīs, being of weak and timid nature, undertook such a difficult and hard-to-achieve duty while establishing the Blessed One’s command—how much more should we?" and establishing the Blessed One’s command, they will undertake the duties of probation and so on.' Therefore, what was not extracted by the teacher has been extracted by us in this Vinayālaṅkāra treatise. Thus, bhikkhus who are endowed with faith, love, and respect towards the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, and are doers of the Teacher’s instruction, should train properly. Matters from here on should be understood according to the method presented in the commentary.

Mānattavinicchayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on the decision regarding mānatta is concluded.

248. Pārivāsikavattakathāyaṃ navakataraṃ pārivāsikanti attanā navakataraṃ pārivāsikaṃ. Pārivāsikassa hi [M 2.0261] attanā navakataraṃ pārivāsikaṃ ṭhapetvā aññe mūlāyapaṭikassanāraha mānattāraha mānattacārika abbhānārahāpi pakatattaṭṭhāneyeva tiṭṭhanti. Tenāha “antamaso mūlāyapaṭikassanārahādīnampī”ti. Antamaso mūlāyapaṭikassanārahādīnampīti ādi-saddena mānattārahamānattacārikaabbhānārahe saṅgaṇhāti. Te hi pārivāsikānaṃ, pārivāsikā ca tesaṃ pakatattaṭṭhāne eva tiṭṭhanti. Adhotapādaṭṭhapanakanti yattha ṭhatvā pāde dhovanti, tādisaṃ dāruphalakakhaṇḍādiṃ. Pādaghaṃsananti sakkharakathalādiṃ. Pāde ghaṃsanti etenāti pādaghaṃsanaṃ, sakkharakathalādi. Vuttañhi bhagavatā “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tisso pādaghaṃsaniyo sakkharaṃ kathalaṃ samuddapheṇa”nti (cūḷava. 269). Saddhivihārikānampi sādiyantassāti saddhivihārikānampi abhivādanādiṃ sādiyantassa. Vattaṃ karontīti ettakamattasseva vuttattā saddhivihārikādīhipi abhivādanādiṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. “Mā maṃ gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchathā”ti vutte anāpucchāpi gāmaṃ pavisituṃ vaṭṭati.

248. In the discussion on the duties of a probationer, 'one newer in probation' means a probationer newer than oneself. For a probationer, after excluding a probationer newer than oneself, others—such as those deserving to be sent back to the origin, those deserving mānatta, those observing mānatta, and those fit for reinstatement—remain in their ordinary positions. Hence it is said, 'even those deserving to be sent back to the origin, etc.' The phrase 'even those deserving to be sent back to the origin, etc.' includes, by the word 'etc.,' those deserving mānatta, those observing mānatta, and those fit for reinstatement. Indeed, they remain in the ordinary position relative to probationers, and probationers remain in the ordinary position relative to them. 'Foot-washing board' means a piece of wooden plank or the like on which one stands to wash one's feet. 'Foot-scraper' means gravel, potsherd, etc. It is called a foot-scraper because one scrapes one's feet with it—gravel, potsherd, etc. For the Blessed One has said, 'I allow, bhikkhus, three kinds of foot-scrapers: gravel, potsherd, and sea-foam' (Cūḷavagga 269). 'Even when accepting from one’s own pupils' means even when accepting bowing, etc., from one’s pupils. Regarding 'performing the duty': because only this much is stated, it is not proper for co-residents and others to perform acts of reverence and so on. When told, 'Do not ask my permission to enter the village,' it is permissible to enter the village without asking permission.

Yo yo vuḍḍhoti pārivāsikesu bhikkhūsu yo yo vuḍḍho. Navakatarassa sāditunti pārivāsikanavakatarassa abhivādanādiṃ sādituṃ. “Pārisuddhiuposathe kariyamāne”ti idaṃ pavāraṇadivasesu saṅghe pavārente anupagatachinnavassādīhi kariyamānaṃ pārisuddhiuposathampi sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tatthevāti saṅghanavakaṭṭhāneyeva. Attano pāḷiyā pavāretabbanti attano vassaggena pattapāḷiyā pavāretabbaṃ, na pana sabbesu pavāritesūti attho.

‘Whoever is senior’ means whoever is senior among the bhikkhus on probation. ‘To make a more junior one accept’ means to make a more junior probationer accept greetings and so on. ‘When the purity Uposatha is being performed’—this is said with reference also to the purity Uposatha performed on Pavāraṇā days, when the Saṅgha is inviting, by those who have not entered upon or have broken the rains residence, etc. ‘Right there’ means only in the place of the junior bhikkhus of the Saṅgha. ‘One should invite according to one’s own text’ means one should invite according to the text that has been reached based on one’s count of rains-residences; the meaning is not 'after all have invited'.

Oṇojanaṃ [V 2.0190] nāma vissajjanaṃ, taṃ pana pārivāsikena pāpitassa attanā sampaṭicchitasseva punadivasādiatthāya vissajjanaṃ kātabbaṃ. Asampaṭicchitvā ce vissajjeti, na labhatīti [M 2.0262] vuttaṃ. Yadi pana na gaṇhāti na vissajjetīti yadi purimadivase attano na gaṇhāti, gahetvā ca na vissajjeti.

‘Oṇojana’ means granting. However, this granting should be done only for what has been presented by the probationer and accepted by oneself, for the purpose of the next day and so on. If one grants without having accepted, it is said that it is not obtained. ‘But if one neither accepts nor grants’ means: if on the previous day one does not accept it, or if, having accepted it, one does not grant it.

Catussālabhattanti bhojanasālāya paṭipāṭiyā dīyamānaṃ bhattaṃ. Hatthapāse ṭhitenāti dāyakassa hatthapāse ṭhitena, paṭiggahaṇaruhanaṭṭhāneti adhippāyo. Mahāpeḷabhattepīti mahantesu bhattapacchiādibhājanesu ṭhapetvā dīyamānabhattesupi. Ito parampi pārivāsikavattaṃ pāḷiyaṃ (cūḷava. 75) āgatanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Tattha pana aṭṭhakathāyaṃ āgatanayeneva attho suviññeyyo hoti, tasmā dubbiññeyyaṭṭhāneyeva kathayissāma.

‘Catussālabhatta’ means food given in sequence in the dining hall. ‘Standing within arm’s reach’ means standing within the donor’s arm’s reach; the intention is the place suitable for receiving. ‘Even in a large basket meal’ applies also to food given after being placed in large vessels like food baskets. From here onward, the duties of a probationer should be understood according to the method found in the Pāḷi (Cūḷavagga 75). There, however, the meaning is easily understood according to the method presented in the commentary; therefore, we will discuss only the points that are difficult to understand.

“Na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo”ti ettha dubbidhaṃ sāmaṇeraṃ dassetuṃ “añño”tiādimāha. “Na bhikkhuniyo ovaditabbā”ti ettha laddhasammutikena āṇattopi garudhammehi aññehi vā ovadituṃ na labhatīti āha “paṭibalassa vā bhikkhussa bhāro kātabbo”ti. Āgatā bhikkhuniyo vattabbāti sambandho. Savacanīyanti sadosaṃ. Jeṭṭhakaṭṭhānaṃ na kātabbanti padhānaṭṭhānaṃ na kātabbaṃ. Kiṃ tanti āha “pātimokkhuddesakenā”tiādi.

Regarding ‘A novice should not be attended to,’ here, to indicate the two kinds of novices, it says ‘another,’ etc. Regarding ‘Nuns should not be advised,’ here it is said that even if instructed by one who has received authorization, he is not permitted to advise on the grave rules or other matters; therefore, it says, ‘the duty should be assigned to a capable monk.’ The connection is: ‘Nuns who have arrived should be addressed.’ ‘Savacaniya’ means with fault. ‘A senior position should not be taken’ means a leading position should not be taken. What is that? It explains, ‘by being the reciter of the Pātimokkha,’ etc.

Rajehi hatā upahatā bhūmi etissāti rajohatabhūmi, rajokiṇṇabhūmīti attho. Paccayanti vassāvāsikalābhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ekapasse ṭhatvāti pāḷiṃ vihāya bhikkhūnaṃ pacchato ṭhatvā. Senāsanaṃ na labhatīti seyyapariyantabhāgitāya vassaggena gaṇhituṃ na labhati. Assāti bhaveyya. “Āgantukena ārocetabbaṃ, āgantukassa ārocetabba”nti avisesena vuttattā sace dve pārivāsikā gataṭṭhāne aññamaññaṃ passanti, ubhohipi aññamaññassa ārocetabbaṃ. Yathā bahi disvā ārocitassa bhikkhuno [M 2.0263] vihāraṃ āgatena puna ārocanakiccaṃ natthi, evaṃ aññavihāraṃ gatenapi tattha pubbe ārocitassa puna ārocanakiccaṃ natthīti vadanti. Avisesenāti pārivāsikassa ca ukkhittakassa ca avisesena.

‘Rajohatabhūmi’ means ground struck by dust, that is, ground covered with dust. ‘Paccaya’ is said with reference to the gains of the rains-residence. ‘Ekapasse ṭhatvā’ means standing behind the monks, having left the line. ‘Senāsanaṃ na labhati’ means one does not obtain a share of the sleeping places by seniority of rains-residence. ‘Assa’ means ‘it might be.’ Since it is stated without distinction that ‘A newcomer should announce, a newcomer should be announced to,’ if two probationers see each other in a place they have gone to, both should announce to each other. Just as for a monk who has announced after seeing someone outside, there is no need to announce again upon arriving at the monastery, so also, for one who has gone to another monastery and announced there previously, there is no need to announce again—so they say. ‘Avisesena’ means without distinction for a probationer and a suspended monk.

Obaddhanti palibuddhaṃ. Sahavāsoti vuttappakāre channe bhikkhunā saddhiṃ sayanameva adhippetaṃ, na sesairiyāpathakappanaṃ. Sesamettha suviññeyyameva.

‘Obaddha’ means hindered. ‘Sahavāsa’ refers to living together with the monk Channa in the manner described; it specifically means lying down together, not the arranging of other postures. The rest here is easily understood.

Pāpiṭṭhatarāti [V 2.0191] pārājikāpattīti ukkaṃsavasena vuttaṃ. Sañcarittādipaṇṇattivajjato pana sukkavissaṭṭhādikā lokavajjāva. Tatthapi saṅghabhedādikā pāpiṭṭhatarā eva. Kammanti pārivāsikakammavācāti etena “kammabhūtā vācā kammavācā”ti kammavācāsaddassa atthopi siddhoti veditabbo. Savacanīyanti ettha sa-saddo “santi”atthaṃ vadati, attano vacanena attano pavattanakammanti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo, “mā pakkamāhī”ti vā “ehi vinayadharānaṃ sammukhībhāva”nti vā evaṃ attano āṇāya pavattanakakammaṃ na kātabbanti adhippāyo. Evañhi kenaci savacanīye kate anādarena atikkamituṃ na vaṭṭati, buddhassa saṅghassa āṇā atikkantā nāma hoti. Rajohatabhūmīti paṇṇasālāvisesanaṃ. Paccayanti vassāvāsikacīvaraṃ. Senāsanaṃ na labhatīti vassaggena na labhati. Apaṇṇakapaṭipadāti aviraddhapaṭipadā. Sace vāyamantopīti ettha avisayabhāvaṃ ñatvā avāyamantopi saṅgayhati. Avisesenāti pārivāsikukkhittakānaṃ sāmaññena. Pañcavaṇṇachadanabandhanaṭṭhānesūti pañcappakārachadanehi channaṭṭhānesu. Obaddhanti uṭṭhānādibyāpārapaṭibaddhaṃ, pīḷitanti attho. Mañce vā pīṭhe vāti ettha vāsaddo samuccayattho. Tena taṭṭikācammakhaṇḍādīsu dīghāsanesupi nisīdituṃ na vaṭṭatīti dīpitaṃ hoti. Na vattabhedadukkaṭanti vuḍḍhatarassa [M 2.0264] jānantassapi vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ natthīti dasseti. Vattaṃ nikkhipāpetvāti idampi parivāsādimeva sandhāya vuttaṃ, na sesakammāni.

‘Pāpiṭṭhatarā’ is said with reference to the pārājika offense, in the sense of being the most serious. However, apart from the stipulated offenses like sañcaritta, those like sukkavissaṭṭhi are worldly faults. Even among those, offenses like schism in the Sangha are indeed more serious. ‘Kamma’ means the formal procedure of probation. By this, it should be understood that the meaning of the term ‘kammavācā’ is also established as ‘a statement that constitutes an act.’ Regarding ‘Savacaniya,’ here the prefix ‘sa’ indicates the sense of ‘existing.’ The meaning here should be seen as ‘an act initiated by one’s own words;’ the intention is that one should not perform an act of instigation by one's own command, such as ‘Do not leave’ or ‘Come into the presence of the Vinaya experts.’ For if a formal admonition is made by someone, it is not proper to transgress it through disrespect; it would be called a transgression of the command of the Buddha and the Sangha. ‘Rajohatabhūmi’ is a qualification for a leaf hut. ‘Paccaya’ means the rains-residence robe. ‘Senāsanaṃ na labhati’ means one does not obtain it by seniority of rains-residence. ‘Apaṇṇakapaṭipadā’ means the unerring practice. Regarding ‘Sace vāyamantopi,’ here, one who does not strive, knowing it to be beyond one’s scope, is also included. ‘Avisesena’ means in general for those on probation and those suspended. ‘Pañcavaṇṇachadanabandhanaṭṭhānesu’ means in places covered with five kinds of roofing. ‘Obaddha’ means bound by activities such as getting up; the meaning is afflicted. Regarding ‘Mañce vā pīṭhe vā,’ here the word ‘vā’ has the meaning of inclusion. By this, it is shown that it is not proper to sit even on long seats such as mats or pieces of leather. ‘Na vattabhedadukkaṭa’ shows that even for a more senior monk who knows, there is no dukkaṭa offense for a breach of observance. ‘Vattaṃ nikkhipāpetvā’ is also said with reference only to probation and the like, not other formal acts.

“Senāsanaṃ na labhati seyyapariyantabhāgitāya. Uddesādīni dātumpi na labhatīti vadanti. ‘Tadahupasampannepi pakatatte’ti vacanato anupasampannehi vasituṃ vaṭṭati. Samavassāti etena apacchā apurimaṃ nipajjane dvinnampi vattabhedāpattibhāvaṃ dīpeti. Attano attano navakataranti pārivāsikādinavakataraṃ. Paṭhamaṃ saṅghamajjhe parivāsaṃ gahetvā nikkhittavattena puna ekassapi santike samādiyituṃ nikkhipituñca vaṭṭati, mānatte pana nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati. Ūnegaṇecaraṇadosattā na gahetunti eke. Paṭhamaṃ ādinnavattaṃ ekassa santike yathā nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭati, tathā samādiyitumpi vaṭṭatīti porāṇagaṇṭhipade”ti vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 76) vuttanti.

‘He does not obtain lodging as a share of the sleeping places.’ They say he is not permitted even to give recitation texts, etc. According to the phrase ‘Tadahupasampannepi pakatatte,’ it is proper to live with the unordained. By ‘Samavassā,’ this shows that in lying down neither after nor before, there is an offense of breach of observance for both. ‘Attano attano navakatara’ means the more junior of each respective group, that is, the more junior among those on probation, etc. First, having undertaken probation in the midst of the Sangha, with the observance relinquished, it is proper to undertake it again and to relinquish it in the presence of even a single monk; but during mānatta, it is only proper to relinquish it. Some say it should not be undertaken due to the fault of conduct with an incomplete group. ‘Just as it is proper to relinquish the initially undertaken observance in the presence of a single monk, so too is it proper to undertake it’—this is stated in the ancient glosses. Thus it is stated in the Vajirabuddhi sub-commentary.

Idaṃ ettha yaṃ vattaṃ “catunavutipārivāsikavatta”nti pārivāsikakkhandhakapāḷiyaṃ (cūḷava. 75) āgataṃ, samantapāsādikāyampi ettakāya pāḷiyā (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 75-84) vaṇṇanaṃ vatvā “pārivāsikavattakathā niṭṭhitā”ti āha. Imasmiṃ vinayasaṅgahapakaraṇe [V 2.0192] (vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 248) pana “na chamāyaṃ caṅkamante caṅkame caṅkamitabba”nti imassānantaraṃ “pārivāsikacatuttho ce, bhikkhave”tiādīni aggahetvā “na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sāditabba”ntiādīni paṭhamaṃ paññattapadāni gahetvā tesaṃ padānaṃ saṃvaṇṇanaṃ katvā “idaṃ pārivāsikavatta”nti aññathā anukkamo vutto, so pāḷiyā ca aṭṭhakathāya ca na sameti. Ācariyassa pana ayamadhippāyo siyā – “pārivāsikacatuttho ce, bhikkhave”tiādīni pārivāsikabhikkhūnaṃ samādiyitabbāni na honti[M 2.0265], atha kho kammakārakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kattabbākattabbakammadassanametaṃ, tasmā pārivāsikavatte na pavesetabbaṃ. “Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikena bhikkhunā sāditabba”ntiādīni pana pārivāsikabhikkhūnaṃ sammāvattitabbavattāniyeva honti, tasmā imāniyeva pārivāsikavatte pavesetabbānīti. Amhehi pana pāḷiaṭṭhakathāṭīkāsu āgatānukkamena paṭhamaṃ paññattavattānaṃ atthaṃ paṭhamaṃ dassetvā pacchā paññattapadānaṃ attho pacchā vuttoti daṭṭhabbo.

Here, the observance which is called the ‘ninety-four probationary observances’ comes in the Pāli of the Parivāsikakkhandhaka. In the Samantapāsādikā too, having given the explanation for this much of the Pāli text, it says, ‘The discourse on the probationary observances is finished.’ In this Vinayasaṅgaha text, however, after the rule, ‘While someone is walking on the ground, one should not walk on the walking path,’ the rules beginning, ‘Monks, if a probationer is the fourth...’ are not taken up. Instead, the rules prescribed first, beginning, ‘Monks, a probationary monk should not consent...’ are taken, and after giving their explanation, it is said, ‘This is the probationary observance.’ This sequence does not agree with the Pāli or the commentary. The teacher’s intention might be this: the rules beginning, ‘Monks, if a probationer is the fourth...’ are not to be undertaken by probationary monks, but rather, this is a demonstration of the acts to be done and not to be done by the monks performing the formal procedure; therefore, they should not be included in the probationary observance. The rules beginning, ‘Monks, a probationary monk should not consent...’ however, are indeed the observances to be properly practiced by probationary monks; therefore, only these should be included in the probationary observance. By us, however, it should be understood that the meaning of the observances prescribed first is shown first, and the meaning of the rules prescribed later is stated afterwards, according to the sequence that has come down in the Pāli, the commentary, and the sub-commentary.

Iti vinayasaṅgahasaṃvaṇṇanābhūte vinayālaṅkāre

Thus, in the Vinayālaṅkāra, which is an explanation of the Vinayasaṅgaha,

Garukāpattivuṭṭhānavinicchayakathālaṅkāro nāma

The Ornament Called ‘The Discourse on the Determination of Rising from Grave Offenses’,

Dvattiṃsatimo paricchedo.

The Thirty-second Chapter.

33. Kammākammavinicchayakathā

33. The Discourse on the Determination of Valid and Invalid Acts

249. Evaṃ garukāpattivuṭṭhānavinicchayakathaṃ kathetvā idāni kammākammavinicchayakathaṃ kathetuṃ “kammākammanti ettha panā”tiādimāha. Tattha samaggena saṅghena karīyate tanti kammaṃ, apalokanādicatubbidhavinayakammaṃ. Itarasmimpi eseva nayo. A-kāro vuddhiattho, na vuddhippattaṃ kammaṃ akammaṃ. Kammañca akammañca kammākammaṃ vajjāvajjaṃ viya, phalāphalaṃ viya ca. Tattha ca kammanti apalokanakammañattikammadvayaṃ. Akammanti ñattidutiyakammañatticatautthakammadvayaṃ. Atha vā kammanti catūsupi etesu lahukakammaṃ. Akammanti garukakammaṃ. Kammākammanti ettha pana vinicchayo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Tattha panāti pakkhantaratthe nipāto[V 2.0193], garukāpattivuṭṭhānavinicchayakathāpakkhato añño kammākammavinicchayakathāpakkho veditabboti vā mayā vuccateti vā attho.

249. Having thus explained the discussion on the determination concerning the rehabilitation from grave offenses, now, to explain the discussion on the determination of what is and is not a legal act, he says, beginning with “Now, as to what is and is not a legal act.” Here, what is done by a united Sangha is a 'legal act' (kamma), namely, the four kinds of Vinaya-kamma beginning with apalokana. The same method applies to the other terms. The prefix 'a-' (in 'akamma') has the meaning of increase; an act that has attained this increase is not a non-act. 'Kammākamma' (what is and is not a legal act) is like 'vajjāvajja' (what is blameworthy and blameless) or 'phalāphala' (fruitful and fruitless). In this context, 'kamma' refers to the two acts: the apalokana-kamma and the ñatti-kamma. 'Akamma' refers to the two acts: the ñatti-dutiya-kamma and the ñatti-catuttha-kamma. Alternatively, 'kamma' may refer to the lighter act among these four, while 'akamma' refers to the heavier act. “Now, as to what is and is not a legal act”—here, the determination should be understood thus. “Now” (tattha pana) is a particle indicating a different subject, meaning that a different section, the discussion on the determination of what is and is not a legal act, is to be understood as distinct from the section on the determination concerning the rehabilitation from grave offenses, or it may mean 'I will speak of this.'

Cattāri [M 2.0266] kammānīti ettha cattārīti paricchedanidassanaṃ. Tena vinayakammāni nāma cattāri eva honti, na ito ūnādhikānīti dasseti. Kammānīti paricchinnakammanidassanaṃ. Apalokanakammantiādīni paricchinnakammānaṃ uddesakathanaṃ. Tattha apalokīyate āyācīyate apalokanaṃ, apapubbalokadhātu āyācanatthe, yupaccayo bhāvatthavācako. Apalokanavasena kattabbaṃ kammaṃ apalokanakammaṃ, sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ apaloketvā saṅghānumatiyā kattabbaṃ kammaṃ. Ñāpanā ñatti, saṅghassa jānāpanāti attho. Ñattiyā kattabbaṃ kammaṃ ñattikammaṃ, anussāvanaṃ akatvā suddhañattiyāyeva kattabbakammaṃ. Dvinnaṃ pūraṇī dutiyā, ñatti dutiyā etassa kammassāti ñattidutiyaṃ, ñattidutiyañca taṃ kammañcāti ñattidutiyakammaṃ, ekāya ñattiyā ekāya anussāvanāya kattabbakammaṃ. Catunnaṃ pūraṇī catutthī, ñatti catutthī etassa kammassāti ñatticatutthaṃ, ñatticatutthañca taṃ kammañcāti ñatticatutthakammaṃ, ekāya ñattiyā tīhi anussāvanāhi kattabbakammaṃ. Tena vakkhati “apalokanakammaṃ nāma sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ sodhetvā”tiādi.

Four kinds of legal acts—here, 'four' indicates a delimitation. By this, it is shown that there are indeed only four kinds of Vinaya-kamma, neither fewer nor more. 'Legal acts' signifies the specification of delimited legal acts. The enumeration of apalokana-kamma and so forth is a statement of the delimited legal acts. Among these, 'apalokana' is so called because it is sought (apalokīyate) or requested (āyācīyate); the root lok with the prefix apa is in the sense of requesting, and the suffix yu expresses the abstract noun. A legal act to be performed by means of apalokana is called apalokana-kamma, a legal act that must be done after seeking the approval of the Sangha residing within the boundary and obtaining the Sangha’s consent. 'Ñāpanā' is ñatti, meaning 'making known to the Sangha'. A legal act to be performed by means of a ñatti is called a ñatti-kamma, a legal act to be performed solely by a ñatti itself, without any proclamation. 'The completion of two' is the second; the ñatti is the second for this legal act, therefore 'ñatti-dutiya'; and that ñatti-dutiya and that legal act are called a ñatti-dutiya-kamma, a legal act performed with one ñatti and one proclamation. 'The completion of four' is the fourth; the ñatti is the fourth for this legal act, therefore 'ñatti-catuttha'; and that ñatti-catuttha and that legal act are called a ñatti-catuttha-kamma, a legal act performed with one ñatti and three proclamations. Thus, it will be said: 'The apalokana-kamma is, for example, after purifying the Sangha residing within the boundary...' and so on.

Evaṃ cattāri kammāni uddisitvā parivāre (pari. 482 ādayo) kammavagge āgatanayeneva tesaṃ catunnaṃ kammānaṃ vipattikāraṇāni pucchitvā vissajjetuṃ “imāni cattāri kammāni katihākārehi vipajjanti? Pañcahākārehi vipajjantī”tiādimāha. Tattha vatthutoti vinayakammassa kāraṇabhūtavatthuto. Ñattito anussāvanatoti dvepi kammavācāyameva. Sīmatoti kammakaraṇaṭṭhānabhūtabaddhasīmato. Parisatoti kammappattachandārahabhūtakārakasaṅghato. Tāniyeva hi pañca sabbesaṃ vinayakammānaṃ vipattikāraṇāni honti.

Having thus enumerated the four legal acts, then, in order to ask about and explain the causes of failure for those four kinds of legal acts, following the method presented in the section on legal acts in the Parivāra (starting with Parivāra 482), he says, 'In how many ways do these four legal acts fail? They fail in five ways,' and so on. Here, 'from the basis' (vatthuto) refers to the substantive grounds that form the reason for the Vinaya-kamma. 'From the motion' (ñattito) and 'from the proclamation' (anussāvanato) both refer to the formal statement of the legal act itself. 'From the boundary' (sīmato) refers to the established boundary that serves as the place for performing the legal act. 'From the assembly' (parisato) refers to the Sangha, which is qualified to give consent and perform the legal act. Indeed, these same five are the causes of failure for all Vinaya-kamma.

Tato [M 2.0267] taṃ kammavipattikāraṇabhūtaṃ vatthuṃ pāḷinayena vitthāretuṃ “sammukhākaraṇīyaṃ kammaṃ asammukhā karoti, vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakamma”ntyādimāha. Tattha sammukhākaraṇīyaṃ paṭipucchākaraṇīyaṃ paṭiññāyakaraṇīyanti imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ atathākaraṇena, sativinayo amūḷhavinayo tassapāpiyasikā tajjanīyakammaṃ niyasakammaṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ ukkhepanīyakammaṃ parivāso mūlāyapaṭikassanā mānattaṃ abbhānaṃ upasampadanti [V 2.0194] imesaṃ terasakammānaṃ aññakammārahassa aññakammakaraṇena, uposatho pavāraṇāti imesaṃ dvinnaṃ adivase karaṇena, paṇḍako theyyasaṃvāsako titthiyapakkantako tiracchānagato mātughātako pitughātako arahantaghātako lohituppādako saṅghabhedako bhikkhunidūsako ubhatobyañjanako ūnavīsativasso antimavatthuajjhāpannapubboti imesaṃ terasannaṃ puggalānaṃ upasampadākammakaraṇena iti imāni ekatiṃsa kammāni vatthuvipannaṃ adhammakammaṃ hoti. Ñattito pañca, anussāvanato pañcāti imāni dasa kāraṇāni antokammavācāyameva labhanti, sīmato ekādasa kāraṇāni sīmāsammutivasena labhanti, parisato dvādasa kāraṇāni catuvaggapañcavaggadasavaggavīsativaggasaṅkhātesu catūsu saṅghesu ekekasmiṃ kammapattachandārahasammukhībhūtasaṅkhātānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇaṃ saṅghānaṃ vasena labhantīti.

Then, to elaborate on that basis, which is the cause of the failure of the legal act, in accordance with the Pāli, he says, beginning with: 'Performing a legal act that should be done in the presence of the individual without his presence, a legal act with a flawed basis is an unlawful act.' Here, by the improper execution of these three—an act that should be done in the presence of the individual, an act that requires questioning, and an act that requires acknowledgment—(the act becomes invalid). Also, by performing a different act for one who is liable to another in the case of these thirteen legal acts: the verdict of mindfulness, the verdict of past insanity, the verdict for specific depravity, the act of censure, the act of subordination, the act of banishment, the act of reconciliation, the act of suspension, probation, sending back to the beginning, penance, rehabilitation, and full ordination. Moreover, by performing these two, Uposatha or Pavāraṇā, on a day other than the proper day. Furthermore, by performing an ordination act for any of these thirteen individuals: a eunuch, one who lives in secret like a thief, one who has gone over to another sect, an animal, a matricide, a patricide, a murderer of an arahant, one who has maliciously shed the Buddha's blood, one who has caused a schism in the Sangha, one who has violated a bhikkhunī, a hermaphrodite, one under twenty years of age, or one who has previously committed a final offense. Thus, these thirty-one legal acts are invalid due to a flawed basis, becoming an unlawful act. From the standpoint of the motion, there are five causes; from the standpoint of the proclamation, another five—these ten causes are found within the formal statement of the legal act itself. From the standpoint of the boundary, there are eleven causes, which are found in relation to the consecration of the boundary. From the standpoint of the assembly, there are twelve causes, which are found in the four types of Sanghas—the fourfold, fivefold, tenfold, and twentyfold assemblies—by way of the Sangha in each case being threefold: fit for the act, worthy of giving consent, and present.

Evaṃ kammavipattikāraṇāni dassetvā puna catuvaggasaṅghādīsu sannisinnānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ visesanāmaṃ dassetuṃ “catuvaggakaraṇe kamme”tiādimāha. Taṃ suviññeyyameva.

Having thus shown the causes of the failure of legal acts, he then, in order to show the distinctive names for the bhikkhus assembled in the fourfold Sangha and so forth, says, beginning with 'In a legal act performed by a fourfold assembly,' and so on. That is easily understood.

250. Tato paraṃ catunnaṃ kammānaṃ ṭhānaṃ saṅkhepato dassetuṃ “apalokanakammaṃ kati ṭhānāni gacchatī”tiādimāha. Tampi suviññeyyameva.

250. Next, to briefly show the scope of the four kinds of legal acts, he says, beginning with 'How many grounds does the apalokana-kamma cover?'. That too is easily understood.

251. Tato [M 2.0268] tāniyeva kammāni tesu ṭhānesu pavattāni vitthārato pakāsetukāmo “ayaṃ tāva pāḷinayo. Ayaṃ panettha ādito paṭṭhāya vinicchayakathā”tiādimāha. Tattha tassaṃ vinicchayakathāyaṃ catūsu kammesu katamaṃ apalokanakammaṃ nāmāti pucchāyaṃ taṃ dassetumāha “apalokanakammaṃ nāmā”tiādi. Tattha sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ sodhetvāti avippavāsasaṅkhātamahāsīmaṭṭhakaṃ saṅghaṃ sodhetvā. Na hi khaṇḍasīmāya sannipatite saṅghe sodhetabbakiccaṃ atthi, avippavāsasīmāsaṅkhātāya mahāsīmāya pana vitthārattā bahūnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānattā samaggabhāvatthaṃ sodhetabbaṃ hoti. Chandārahānaṃ chandaṃ āharitvāti tissaṃ sīmāyaṃ catuvaggādigaṇaṃ pūretvā hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā ṭhitehi bhikkhūhi aññesaṃ hatthapāsaṃ anāgatānaṃ pakatattabhikkhūnaṃ chandaṃ āharitvā. Vuttañhi “catuvaggakaraṇe kamme cattāro bhikkhū pakatattā kammappattā, avasesā pakatattā chandārahā”ti (pari. 497). Samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyāti chandassa āharitattā hatthapāsaṃ āgatāpi anāgatāpi sabbe bhikkhū samaggāyeva honti, tasmā samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā. Tikkhattuṃ sāvetvāti “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho”tiādinā kammavācaṃ abhaṇitvā [V 2.0195] “ruccati saṅghassa. Dutiyampi…pe… tatiyampi ruccati saṅghassā”ti tikkhattuṃ sāvetvā kattabbakammaṃ apalokanakammaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Vuttanayenevāti apalokanakamme vuttanayeneva. Iminā “sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ sodhetvā, chandārahānaṃ chandaṃ āharitvā”ti idaṃ dvayaṃ atidisati. Itaresupi eseva nayo.

251. Then, desiring to explain in detail those very legal acts as they occur in those instances, he says, beginning with: 'This is the Pāḷi method. Now, here is the discussion of the determination from the beginning.' There, in that discussion of the determination, in answer to the question 'Among the four kinds of legal acts, which is called the apalokanakamma?', to show that, it is said: 'The apalokanakamma is called...' There, 'having purified the Sangha within the boundary' means having purified the Sangha within the great boundary, known as the non-separation boundary. For when the Sangha is assembled within a fragmented boundary, there is no duty of purification. But because the great boundary, known as the non-separation boundary, is extensive and the dwelling place of many bhikkhus, it must be purified for the sake of unity. 'Having brought the consent of those worthy of consent' means that, within this boundary, having completed the group of four or more, and without leaving the reach of hands, the bhikkhus who are present bring the consent of other bhikkhus in a normal state who have not arrived within hand’s reach. For it is said: 'In a legal act involving a group of four, four bhikkhus in a normal state are qualified for the legal act; the rest in a normal state are worthy of consent' (Parivāra 497). 'With the approval of the united Sangha' means that because consent has been brought, all bhikkhus—whether they have arrived within hand’s reach or not—are united. Therefore, it is with the approval of the united Sangha. 'Having announced three times' means not reciting the formal statement beginning with 'Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me,' but announcing three times: 'It is agreeable to the Sangha. A second time... for a third time, it is agreeable to the Sangha'—the legal act to be done in this way is called the apalokanakamma. 'By the same method' means by the same method as stated for the apalokanakamma. By this, he extends the principle to the two points: 'having purified the Sangha within the boundary' and 'having brought the consent of those worthy of consent.' The same method applies to the others as well.

Tattha [M 2.0269] tesu catūsu kammesu kiṃ aññakammaṃ itarakammavasena kātabbanti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “tatra”iccādi. Evaṃ hotu, evaṃ sante avisesena sabbampi kammaṃ aññavasena kattabbanti āha “ñattidutiyakammaṃ panā”tiādi. Tattha pana-saddo visesatthajotako, ñattidutiyakamme pana viseso atthīti attho. Ito parāni suviññeyyāneva. Paṭikkhittameva aṭṭhakathāyanti ajjhāhārasambandho. Yadi evaṃ akkharaparihīnādīsu santesu kammakopo siyāti codanaṃ manasi katvā āha “sace panā”tiādi. Tattha akkharaparihīnanti “suṇātu me”tiādīsu su-kāra ṇā-kāra tu-kārādīnaṃ bhassanaṃ. Padaparihīnanti suṇātūtiādīnaṃ vibhatyantapadānaṃ bhassanaṃ. Duruttapadaṃ pana upari vakkhati.

Here, concerning these four legal acts, in reference to the objection, 'Which legal act may be performed by means of another legal act?', he says, 'There,' and so on. So be it. If that is the case, would all legal acts have to be performed by means of another without distinction? He says, 'But the ñattidutiyakamma,' and so on. Here, the particle 'but' indicates a specific meaning; that is, there is a specific point concerning the ñattidutiyakamma. The rest is easily understood. 'It is rejected in the commentary'—this is the implied connection. If that is the case, if omissions of letters and so on occur, would the legal act be invalidated? Having considered this objection in mind, he says, 'But if,' and so on. Here, 'omission of letters' means the dropping of the syllables su, ṇā, tu, and so forth in 'Suṇātu me'. 'Omission of words' means the dropping of inflected words such as 'suṇātu,' and so forth. But he will explain 'a misspoken word' further on.

Idāni punappunavacane payojanaṃ dassento “idaṃ akuppakamme daḷhikammaṃ hoti, kuppakamme kammaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhatī”ti āha. Tattha idanti idaṃ punappunaṃ vuttakammaṃ. Akuppakammeti akuppe ṭhānārahe purekatakamme. Daḷhikammaṃ hotīti thiratarakammaṃ hoti ekāya rajjuyā bandhitabbabhāre dutiyatatiyādirajjūhi bandhanaṃ viya. Kuppakammeti akkharaparihīnādivasena kuppe aṭṭhānārahe purekatakamme. Kammaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhatīti punappunaṃ vutte sati tesaṃ akkharaparihīnādīnaṃ sodhitattā parisuddhakammaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhati. Akuppakamme kuppakammeti vā bhāvenabhāvalakkhaṇatthe bhummavacanaṃ. Puretaraṃ katakammasmiṃ akuppakamme sati pacchā idaṃ punappunaṃ vuttakammaṃ daḷhikammaṃ hoti, purekatakammasmiṃ kuppakamme sati idaṃ punappunaṃ vuttakammaṃ akuppaṃ ṭhānārahaṃ parisuddhakammaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhatīti. Imaṃ pāṭhaṃ nissāya ācariyavarā ekapuggalampi anekakkhattuṃ upasampadakammaṃ karonti. Kasmā pana te bhikkhū lajjīpesalabahussutasikkhākāmabhūtānaṃ attano [M 2.0270] ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ santike sikkhaṃ gaṇhantīti? Na te attano ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ santikā laddhasikkhaṃ paccakkhāya aññaṃ gaṇhanti, atha kho tāya eva saddhiṃ diguṇatiguṇaṃ karonti. Evaṃ santepi purimasikkhāya asaddahantāyeva kareyyuṃ, no saddahantāti? No asaddahantā[V 2.0196], saddahantāpi te bhikkhū punappunakaraṇe yuttitopi āgamatopi ādīnavaṃ apassantā ānisaṃsameva passantā karontīti.

Now, showing the purpose of repeated recitation, he says: 'This becomes a strengthening act in the case of an unshakeable act; in the case of a shakeable act, it stands as a valid act.' Herein, 'this' means this repeatedly recited act. 'In an unshakeable act' means in a previously performed act that is unshakeable and worthy of standing. 'It becomes a strengthening act' means it becomes a more stable act, like binding a load that is to be bound with one rope, with second and third ropes. 'In a shakeable act' means in a previously performed act that is shakeable and unworthy of standing due to deficiencies such as missing syllables. 'It stands as a valid act' means that when it is recited repeatedly, those deficiencies such as missing syllables are corrected, and so it stands as a purified act. Or, 'in an unshakeable act, in a shakeable act' is the locative case used to indicate a condition. When the previously performed act is unshakeable, this repeatedly recited act becomes a strengthening act; when the previously performed act is shakeable, this repeatedly recited act becomes an unshakeable, valid, and purified act. Relying on this text, eminent teachers perform the act of higher ordination for a single individual multiple times. But why do those bhikkhus, being conscientious, amiable, learned, and desirous of training, receive the training from their own teachers and preceptors? They do not reject the training received from their own teachers and preceptors and take up another; rather, they make it twofold or threefold along with that very training. Even so, would they do this only if they distrust the former training, and not if they trust it? It is not that they distrust it; even while trusting it, those bhikkhus do it repeatedly, seeing no fault but only benefit in doing so, both from reason and from scripture.

Kathaṃ yuttito ānisaṃsaṃ passanti? Yathā hi loke abhisittampi rājānaṃ punappunābhisiñcane ādīnavaṃ na passanti, atha kho abhisekānubhāvena rājiddhippattatādīhi kāraṇehi ānisaṃsameva passanti, yathā ca sāsane cetiyaṃ vā paṭimaṃ vā niṭṭhitasabbakiccaṃ “anekajātisaṃsāra”ntiādīhi bhagavato vacanehi abhisekamaṅgalaṃ karontāpi punappunakaraṇe ādīnavaṃ apassantā atirekataraṃ mahiddhikatāmahānubhāvatādiānisaṃsameva passantā punappunaṃ karontiyeva, evameva kataupasampadakammaṃ bhikkhuṃ punadeva kammavācābhaṇane ādīnavaṃ apassantā pubbe katakammasmiṃ vatthuādīsu pañcasu aṅgesu ekasmimpi aṅge aparipuṇṇe sati kammakopasambhavato idāni katakammena paripuṇṇaaṅge sati kammasampattisambhavañca pubbeva kammasampattisambhavepi daḷhikammathiratarasambhavañca ānisaṃsaṃ passantā karonti. Kathaṃ āgamato ānisaṃsaṃ passanti? Yathāvuttaparivāraṭṭhakathāpāṭhavinayasaṅgahapāṭhesu duruttapadassa sodhanatthaṃ punappunaṃ vattabbabhāvassa upalakkhaṇanayena vacanato. Sesañattidosaanussāvanadosānañca vatthuvipattisīmavipattiparisavipattidosānañca sodhanaṃ dassitaṃ hoti. Teneva ca kāraṇena ayampi pacchimapāṭho ācariyena vutto. Tassattho heṭṭhā [M 2.0271] vuttova. Iti pubbe katakammassa kopasambhavepi idāni katakammena sampajjanasaṅkhātaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ āgamato passantīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

How do they see the benefit from reasoning? Just as in the world, they see no fault in re-anointing a king who has already been anointed, but rather see only the benefit for reasons such as the attainment of royal majesty and power through the influence of the anointing. And just as in the Dispensation, when performing a consecration ceremony for a cetiya or an image for which all work has been completed, using the Blessed One’s words beginning with 'Through many a birth in saṃsāra...', they see no fault in performing it repeatedly, but seeing only the surpassing benefit of greater spiritual power and great might, they perform it again and again. In the same way, they see no fault in reciting the Kammavācā again for a bhikkhu who has already undergone the act of higher ordination. They see the benefit: because if even one of the five factors, such as the object, in the previously performed act was incomplete, the act could be invalid, whereas now, with the act performed with complete factors, the success of the act is possible; and even if the act was already successful before, the possibility of strengthening it and making it more stable is a benefit they see. How do they see the benefit from scripture? As stated in the texts of the Parivāra Commentary and the Vinayasaṅgaha, the need for repeated utterance for the purpose of correcting a misspoken word is indicated by way of an indicative method. Thereby, the correction of the remaining faults—faults in the motion, faults in the announcement, defects in the object, defects in the boundary, and defects in the assembly—is also shown. And for that very reason, this latter text was also spoken by the teacher. Its meaning has already been stated above. Thus, it should be understood that even if there was a possibility of the previously performed act being invalid, they see from scripture the benefit known as accomplishment through the act performed now.

Keci pana ācariyā imaṃ “punappunaṃ vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti pāṭhaṃ tasmiṃyeva paṭhamakammakaraṇakāle duruttasodhanatthaṃ vattabbataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na cirakāle”ti vadanti, tadetaṃ vacanaṃ neva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ āgataṃ, na ṭīkādīsu vinicchitaṃ, tesaṃ matimattameva, tasmā na gahetabbaṃ. Apica tasmiṃ khaṇe punappunaṃ vacanatopi aparabhāge vacanaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti mahānisaṃsaṃ. Tasmiñhi kāle punappunaṃ bhaṇane ñattidosaanussāvanadosāni pacchimabhaṇane suṭṭhu bhaṇanto sodhetuṃ sakkuṇeyya, na vatthuvipattisīmavipattiparisavipattidosāni. Tasmiñhi khaṇe tameva vatthu, sā eva sīmā, sā eva parisā, tasmā tāni punappunavacanena sodhetumasakkuṇeyyāni honti. Aparabhāge karonto pana pubbe aparipuṇṇavīsativassabhāvena vatthuvipattibhūtepi idāni paripuṇṇavīsativassattā vatthusampatti hoti, pubbe sīmasaṅkarādibhāvena sīmavipattisambhavepi idāni tadabhāvatthāya suṭṭhu sodhitattā sīmasampatti hoti, pubbe vaggakammādivasena [V 2.0197] parisavipattisambhavepi idāni tadabhāvatthāya suṭṭhu sodhitattā parisasampatti hoti, evaṃ pañca vipattiyo sodhetvā pañca sampattiyo sampādetvā kātuṃ sakkuṇeyyato paṭhamakāle punappunaṃ bhaṇanatopi aparabhāge bhaṇanaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti mahānisaṃsanti veditabbaṃ.

However, some teachers say that this passage—“it is appropriate to recite repeatedly”—was spoken with reference to the very first performance of the act, specifically for the purpose of correcting errors in pronunciation, and not for after a long time has passed. But this statement is neither found in the commentaries nor discussed in the sub-commentaries; it is merely their personal opinion and therefore should not be accepted. Moreover, reciting later is more fruitful and beneficial than reciting repeatedly at that moment. For at that time, by reciting repeatedly, one can thoroughly correct faults in the motion and proclamation during the final recitation, but not faults related to the object, boundary, or assembly. At that moment, the object remains the same, the boundary remains the same, and the assembly remains the same—thus, those faults cannot be corrected by repeated recitation. However, when acting later, even if the object was invalid previously due to the candidate being under twenty years of age, now, due to his having completed twenty years, there is success of the object. Even if there was the possibility of boundary invalidity previously due to boundary confusion, now, because it has been properly corrected to remove that possibility, there is success of the boundary. Even if there was the possibility of assembly invalidity previously due to a factional act, now, because it has been properly corrected to remove that possibility, there is success of the assembly. Thus, having corrected the five invalidities and achieved the five successes, one can perform the act. Therefore, it should be understood that reciting at a later stage is far more fruitful and beneficial than reciting repeatedly at the first stage.

Yadi evaṃ upasampadasikkhāya daharo bhaveyyāti? Na bhaveyya. Kasmā? Porāṇasikkhaṃ appaccakkhitvā tāya eva patiṭṭhitattāti. Evaṃ santepi purekatakammassa sampajjanabhāvena [M 2.0272] tiṭṭhante sati tāya ṭhitattā adaharo siyā. Purimakammassa asampajjanabhāvena idāni katakammeyeva upasampadabhāvena tiṭṭhante sati kasmā daharo na bhaveyyāti? Evaṃ sante daharo bhaveyya. Evaṃ daharo samāno purimasikkhāya vassaṃ gaṇetvā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vandanādīni sampaṭicchanto mahāsāvajjo bhaveyyāti? Evaṃ purimasikkhāya aṭṭhitabhāvaṃ pacchimasikkhāya eva laddhupasampadabhāvaṃ tathato jānanto evaṃ karonto sāvajjo hoti, evaṃ pana ajānanto “purimasikkhāyameva ṭhito”ti maññitvā evaṃ karonto anavajjoti veditabbo. Kathaṃ viññāyatīti ce? “Anāpatti ūnavīsativassaṃ paripuṇṇasaññīti ettha kiñcāpi upasampādentassa anāpatti, puggalo pana anupasampannova hoti. Sace pana so dasavassaccayena aññaṃ upasampādeti, taṃ ce muñcitvā gaṇo pūrati, sūpasampanno. Sopi ca yāva na jānāti, tāvassa neva saggantarāyo, na mokkhantarāyo. Ñatvā pana puna upasampajjitabba”nti samantapāsādikāyaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 406) āgatattā viññāyati. Evaṃ vatthuvipannattā kammakopato anupasampannassa puggalassa upajjhāyo bhavituṃ yuttakāle puna upasampajjanena upasampannabhūtabhāvassa aṭṭhakathāyaṃ āgatattā iminā nayena sīmavipannapaasavipannañattivipannaanussāvanavipannabhūtattā kammakopato pubbe anupasampannabhūtaṃ puggalampi aparabhāge vuḍḍhippattikālepi pañca vipattidosāni sodhetvā puna upasampadakammavācākaraṇena upasampādetuṃ vaṭṭati. Sopi puggalo pubbakammakāle anupasampanno hutvāpi aparakammakāle upasampanno hotīti daṭṭhabbo.

If that were so, would he be considered a junior in terms of the full admission training? No, he would not. Why? Because he has not rejected the former training and is established in that very training. Even so, if the previously performed act stands as successful, then by being established in that, he would not be a junior. If the former act was unsuccessful, and now he stands as fully admitted by the act performed now, why would he not be a junior? If that were the case, he would be a junior. If, being a junior in this way, he were to count the years under the former training and receive salutations and so forth according to seniority, would he incur a great offense? Indeed, knowing truly the state of not being established by the former training and having received full admission only by the later training, if he acts thus, he is blameworthy. But if he does not know this and thinks, “I am established only in the former training,” and acts accordingly, he should be understood as blameless. How is this to be understood? It is understood from what is stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Pācittiya Aṭṭhakathā 406): “There is no offense for one who ordains a person under twenty years of age, perceiving him to be of full age. However, the person is indeed unordained. But if, after ten years, he ordains another, and if the quorum is complete excluding him, then that other is well-ordained. And as for the first person, until he knows this, there is no obstacle to heaven or liberation for him. But upon knowing, he must be ordained again.” Thus, since it is stated in the commentary that a person who is unordained due to an invalid object and thus an invalid act becomes ordained by being re-ordained at the proper time to become a preceptor, in this way, it is proper to ordain a person who was previously unordained due to an invalid act—having been affected by invalidities of boundary, assembly, motion, and proclamation—by performing the act of full admission again in a later period, even at the time of attaining seniority, after purifying the five faults of invalidity. And that person, though unordained at the time of the former act, becomes ordained at the time of the later act. This should be understood.

Ekacce pana bhikkhū porāṇasikkhaṃ paccakkhāya navasikkhameva gaṇhiṃsu, te pana bhikkhū navasikkhāvasena daharāva bhavanti, evaṃ [M 2.0273] karaṇañca ativiya guṇavisiṭṭhaṃ attano navakataraṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā tasmiṃ puggale payirupāsitukāmo taṃ puggalaṃ attanā vuḍḍhataraṃ kātukāmo attānaṃ daharaṃ kātukāmo hutvā dhammagāravena karonto yutto bhaveyya. Atha pana sikkhāsampannaṃ [V 2.0198] kattukāmo evaṃ kareyya, sikkhā nāma pañcaṅgasamannāgate sati sampajjati, sīlavisuddhiyeva kāraṇaṃ hoti, tasmā yadi purimasikkhā aṭṭhitā bhaveyya, paccakkhānakiccaṃ natthi, sayameva patitā hoti. Purimasikkhāya ṭhitāya sati vibbhamitukāmoyeva paccakkhānaṃ kareyya, na bhikkhubhavitukāmo, so pana catupārisuddhisīlameva parisuddhaṃ kareyya, tasmā porāṇasikkhāya paccakkhānaṃ ayuttaṃ viya dissati. Tato porāṇasikkhaṃ paccakkhāya navasikkhāgahaṇato punappunaṃ karaṇaṃyeva yuttataraṃ dissati. Kasmā? Porāṇasikkhaṃ paccakkhāya navasikkhāgahaṇe purimakammaṃ asampajjitvā pacchimakammasampajjane sati kiñcāpi purimasikkhā natthi, yā paccakkhātabbā, tathāpi navasikkhāya sampajjitattā doso natthi, daharabhāvaṃ pattopi yuttarūpoyeva.

However, some monks, having renounced the old training, took up only the new training. These monks, by virtue of the new training, remain junior. Acting in this way—seeing a monk newer than oneself who is distinguished in qualities, and desiring to attend upon that person, wishing to make that person senior to oneself or to make oneself junior—would be fitting if done out of reverence for the Dhamma. Further, if one wishes to become accomplished in training, one should act accordingly. Training is accomplished when endowed with five factors, and purity of virtue is the reason. Therefore, if the former training was not established, there is no need for renunciation; it has fallen away by itself. If the former training is established, only one who wishes to disrobe would renounce it, not one who wishes to be a bhikkhu. Instead, one should purify only the fourfold purity of virtue. Hence, renouncing the old training seems inappropriate. Therefore, rather than renouncing the old training and taking up the new training, repeated performance seems more appropriate. Why? Because in renouncing the old training and taking up the new, if the former act was unsuccessful and the later act is successful, although there is no former training that needs to be renounced, there is no fault due to the success of the new training. Even attaining a junior status is quite appropriate.

Yadi purimakammampi pacchimakammampi sampajjatiyeva, evaṃ sati purimasikkhāya paccakkhānaṃ niratthakaṃ. Pacchimasikkhāya ṭhitopi daharabhāvaṃ pattattā ayuttarūpo. Yadi pana purimakammameva sampajjati, na pacchimakammaṃ, evaṃ sati pubbe ṭhitaporāṇasikkhāpi paccakkhānena patitā. Pacchimasikkhāpi pacchimakammassa pañcannaṃ vipattīnaṃ aññatarena yogato na sampajjati, tasmā purimasikkhāya ca patitattā pacchimasikkhāya ca aladdhattā ubhato bhaṭṭhattā ayuttova hoti. Porāṇasikkhaṃ appaccakkhāya navasikkhāgahaṇe pana sati purimakammaṃ sampannaṃ hutvā pacchimakammaṃ asampannaṃ hontampi purimasikkhāya patiṭṭhitoyeva, purimaṃ asampannaṃ hutvā pacchimaṃ sampannampi [M 2.0274] pacchimasikkhāya ṭhito eva. Purimapacchimakammadvayampi pañcahaṅgehi sampannampi daḷhikammathiratarabhūtāya purimasikkhāya ṭhitoyeva so bhikkhu hoti, tasmā purimasikkhaṃ paccakkhāya navasikkhāgahaṇato purimasikkhaṃ appaccakkhāya punappunaṃ navasikkhāgahaṇaṃ yuttataraṃ hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

If both the former and latter actions are successful, then the rejection of the former training is meaningless. Even if one remains in the latter training, having attained junior status, one is unsuitable. However, if only the former action is successful and not the latter action, then the previously established ancient training also falls away through rejection. The latter training, due to being connected with any of the five invalidities, does not succeed. Therefore, because the former training is lost and the latter training is not attained, one has lost out on both sides and is thus unsuitable. If one does not reject the ancient training but takes up a new training, then even if the former action is complete and the latter action is incomplete, one remains established in the former training. Similarly, if the former action is incomplete and the latter action is complete, one remains established in the latter training. Even if both the former and latter actions are complete in all five aspects, that monk remains established in the former training, which serves as a strengthening and more steadfast act. Therefore, it should be understood that rather than rejecting the former training to take up a new one, it is more suitable to take up a new training again without rejecting the former training.

Imaṃ pana punappunaṃ karontānaṃ ācariyānaṃ vādaṃ amanasikarontā aññe ācariyā anekappakāraṃ anicchitakathaṃ kathenti. Kathaṃ? Ekacce therā evaṃ vadanti “kiṃ ime bhikkhū evaṃ karontā pārājikappattaṃ bhikkhuṃ puna sikkhāya patiṭṭhāpessāmāti maññantī”ti. Te therā punappunaṃ kammavācaṃ bhaṇante bhikkhū disvā “ime bhikkhū iminā kāraṇena evaṃ karontī”ti cintetvā evamāhaṃsu. Ekacce pana therā “kasmā ime bhikkhū punappunaṃ karonti, yathā nāma asani ekavārameva patantī satte jīvitakkhayaṃ pāpeti, evameva bhagavato āṇābhūtā kammavācā [V 2.0199] ekavāraṃ bhaṇamānā kammaṃ sijjhāpeti, na anekavāra”nti, tepi “kammasijjhanatthāya punappunaṃ bhaṇantī”ti cintetvā evamāhaṃsu. Bahavo pana bhikkhū punappunaṃ karonte disvā evaṃ vadanti “ime bhikkhū ācariyupajjhāyehi dinnasikkhaṃ asaddahantā evaṃ karonti, ācariyupajjhāyaguṇāparādhakā ete samaṇā”ti. Te “pubbasikkhaṃ asaddahitvā punappunaṃ karontī”ti maññantā evamāhaṃsu.

But other teachers, not paying attention to the view of these teachers who perform this repeatedly, speak in various undesirable ways. How? Some elders say thus: "What do these monks think, that by doing so they will re-establish in the training a monk who has fallen into a pārājika offense?" Seeing the monks repeatedly reciting the formal act, those elders, thinking, "These monks are acting thus for this reason," spoke thus. Other elders say: "Why do these monks repeat it? Just as lightning, striking only once, brings about the destruction of life, so too the Blessed One’s authoritative pronouncement, the formal act, accomplishes the act when recited once, not repeatedly." They too, thinking, "They recite repeatedly to ensure the success of the act," spoke thus. Many monks, seeing them acting repeatedly, say thus: "These monks, not trusting the training given by their teachers and preceptors, act thus; these ascetics are offenders against the virtues of their teachers and preceptors." Thinking, "They act repeatedly because they do not trust the previous training," they spoke thus.

Apare pana therā “paṭhamaṃ upasampadakammavācābhaṇanakāleyeva punappunaṃ vattabbaṃ, na aparabhāge”ti, tattha kāraṇaṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Aññe evamāhaṃsu “ñattidutiyakammavācāyameva punappunaṃ vattabbanti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, na ñatticatutthakamme, atha ca panime bhikkhū ñatticatutthakammabhūtāya upasampadakammavācāya punappunaṃ karonti, etaṃ aṭṭhakathāya na sametī”ti, taṃ nītatthameva gahetvā [M 2.0275] vadiṃsu. Neyyatthato pana iminā nayena catūsupi kammesu punappunaṃ kātabbanti dasseti. Kammasaṅkarameva hi ñattidutiyakamme visesato vadati, punappunaṃ vattabbabhāvo pana sabbesūti daṭṭhabbo. Teneva hi ñatticatutthakammavācāya upasampannaṭṭhāneyeva pubbe anupasampannassa puggalassa pacchā upasampajjitabbabhāvo aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttoti.

Other elders, however, say, "It should be repeated only at the time of the first recital of the ordination formal act, not afterward." The reason for this has already been stated above. Others said thus: "It is stated in the commentary that only in the motion-and-second formal act should it be repeated, not in the motion-and-fourth. Yet these monks repeat the ordination formal act, which is a motion-and-fourth act. This does not agree with the commentary." They spoke, taking the definitive meaning alone. From the interpretable meaning, however, this method shows that repetition should be done in all four acts. For the commentary specifically mentions the confusion of acts in the motion-and-second formal act, but the aspect of needing repetition should be seen as applying to all. Therefore, it is stated in the commentary that, in the very context of an ordination by a motion-and-fourth formal act, the subsequent ordination of a person not previously ordained is provided for.

Paṭipucchākaraṇīyādīsupīti ettha ādisaddena paṭiṃññāya karaṇīyādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Tattha paṭipucchāya karaṇīyaṃ appaṭipucchā karotīti pucchitvā codetvā sāretvā kātabbaṃ apucchitvā acodetvā asāretvā karoti. Paṭiññāya karaṇīyaṃ appaṭiññāya karotīti paṭiññaṃ āropetvā yathādinnāya paṭiññāya kātabbaṃ apaṭiññāya paṭiññaṃ akarontassa vilapantassa balakkārena karoti. Sativinayārahassāti dabbamallaputtattherasadisassa khīṇāsavassa. Amūḷhavinayārahassāti gaggabhikkhusadisassa ummattakassa. Tassapāpiyasikakammārahassāti upavāḷabhikkhusadisassa ussannapāpassa. Tajjanīyakammārahassāti paṇḍakalohitakabhikkhusadisassa bhaṇḍanakārakassa. Niyasakammārahassāti seyyasakabhikkhusadisassa abhiṇhāpattikassa. Pabbājanīyakammārahassāti assajipunabbasukabhikkhusadisassa kuladūsakassa. Paṭisāraṇīyakammārahassāti sudhammabhikkhusaasassa upāsake jātiādīhi dūsentassa. Ukkhepanīyakammārahassāti channabhikkhusadisassa āpattiṃ apassantassa āpattiṃ adesentassa ariṭṭhabhikkhusadisassa micchādiṭṭhiṃ avissajjentassa. Parivāsārahassāti paṭicchannasaṅghādisesāpattikassa. Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahassāti antarāpattiṃ [V 2.0200] āpannassa. Mānattārahanti appaṭicchannasaṅghādisesāpattikaṃ. Abbhānārahanti ciṇṇamānattaṃ bhikkhuṃ. Upasampādetīti upasampadakammaṃ karoti.

In 'what should be done by questioning, and so on,' the term 'and so on' includes what should be done by acknowledgement and other duties. Therein, 'what should be done by questioning' refers to doing without questioning what should be done after asking, reproving, and reminding; he does it without asking, reproving, or reminding. 'What should be done by acknowledgement' refers to doing without acknowledgement what should be done by imposing acknowledgement according to the acknowledgement given; but he does it without acknowledgement, to one who is not making the acknowledgement and is lamenting, by force. One deserving of a resolution by mindfulness (sativinaya) is one like the Elder Dabbamallaputta, whose taints are destroyed. One deserving of a resolution for past insanity (amūḷhavinaya) is one like the monk Gagga, who was insane. One deserving of the act of further punishment (tassapāpiyasikā) is one like the monk Upavāḷa, who has abundant evil. One deserving of the act of rebuke (tajjanīyakamma) is one like the monks Paṇḍaka and Lohitaka, who are quarrelsome. One deserving of the act of guidance (niyassakamma) is one like the monk Seyyasaka, a frequent offender. One deserving of the act of banishment (pabbājanīyakamma) is one like the monks Assaji and Punabbasu, corrupters of families. One deserving of the act of reconciliation (paṭisāraṇīyakamma) is one like the monk Sudhamma, who disparages lay followers with remarks about birth and so on. One deserving of the act of suspension (ukkhepanīyakamma) is one like the monk Channa, who does not see an offense or does not confess an offense, or like the monk Ariṭṭha, who does not relinquish wrong view. One deserving of probation (parivāsa) is one who has concealed a Saṅghādisesa offense. One deserving of being sent back to the beginning (mūlāyapaṭikassanā) is one who has committed an offense in the interim. One deserving of penance (mānatta) is one who has not concealed a Saṅghādisesa offense. One deserving of reinstatement (abbhāna) is a monk who has completed penance. 'He ordains' means he performs the act of ordination.

Anuposathe [M 2.0276] uposathaṃ karotīti anuposathadivase uposathaṃ karoti. Uposathadivaso nāma ṭhapetvā kattikamāsaṃ avasesesu ekādasasu māsesu bhinnassa saṅghassa sāmaggidivaso ca yathāvuttā cātuddasapannarasā ca, etaṃ tippakārampi uposathadivasaṃ ṭhapetvā aññasmiṃ divase uposathaṃ karonto anuposathe uposathaṃ karoti nāma. Yatra hi pattacīvarādiatthāya appamattakena kāraṇena vivadantā uposathaṃ vā pavāraṇaṃ vā ṭhapenti, tattha tasmiṃ adhikaraṇe vinicchite “samaggā jātamhā”ti antarā sāmaggīuposathaṃ kātuṃ na labhanti, karontehi anuposathe uposatho kato nāma hoti.

Performing the Uposatha on a non-Uposatha day means performing the Uposatha on a day that is not an Uposatha day. An Uposatha day, excluding the month of Kattika, is, in the remaining eleven months, the day of concord for a divided Saṅgha, and the aforementioned fourteenth and fifteenth days. Setting aside these three kinds of Uposatha days, one who performs the Uposatha on any other day is said to perform the Uposatha on a non-Uposatha day. For where they postpone the Uposatha or Pavāraṇā while disputing over a trivial matter concerning bowls, robes, or the like, there, when that legal issue is settled, they are not allowed to perform a concord-Uposatha in the interim, saying, "We have become united." Those who do so are said to have performed the Uposatha on a non-Uposatha day.

Appavāraṇāya pavāretīti appavāraṇadivase pavāreti. Pavāraṇadivaso nāma ekasmiṃ kattikamāse bhinnassa saṅghassa sāmaggidivaso ca paccukkaḍḍhitvā ṭhapitadivaso ca dve ca puṇṇamāsiyo, etaṃ catubbidhaṃ pavāraṇadivasaṃ ṭhapetvā aññasmiṃ divase pavārento appavāraṇāya pavāreti nāma. Idhāpi appamattakassa vivādassa vūpasame sāmaggīpavāraṇaṃ kātuṃ na labhanti. Karontehi appavāraṇāya pavāraṇā katā hotīti ayaṃ aṭṭhakathāpāṭho (pari. aṭṭha. 483).

Performing Pavāraṇā on a non-Pavāraṇā day means performing Pavāraṇā on a day that is not a Pavāraṇā day. A Pavāraṇā day, in the single month of Kattika, is the day of harmony for a divided Saṅgha, the postponed day, and the two full-moon days. Setting aside these four kinds of Pavāraṇā days, one who performs Pavāraṇā on any other day is said to perform Pavāraṇā on a non-Pavāraṇā day.
