Here too, upon the settling of a minor dispute, they are not allowed to perform a concord-Pavāraṇā. By those who do so, a Pavāraṇā is performed on a non-Pavāraṇā day. This is the commentary passage (Pari. Aṭṭha. 483).

“Ummattakassa bhikkhuno ummattakasammuti ummattakena yācitvā kate asammukhāpi dātuṃ vaṭṭati, tattha nisinnepi na kuppati niyamābhāvato. Asammukhā kate pana dosābhāvaṃ dassetuṃ ‘asammukhā kataṃ sukataṃ hotī’ti vuttaṃ. Dūtena upasampadā pana sammukhā kātuṃ na sakkā kammavācānānattasambhavato. Pattanikkujjanādayo hatthapāsato apanītamattepi kātuṃ vaṭṭanti. Saṅghasammukhatātiādīsu yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ [M 2.0277] chando āhato hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti, ayaṃ saṅghasammukhatā. Yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, ayaṃ dhammasammukhatā vinayasammukhatā. Tattha dhammoti bhūtaṃ vatthu. Vinayoti codanā ceva sāraṇā ca. Satthusāsanaṃ nāma ñattisampadā ceva anussāvanasampadā [V 2.0201] ca. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, tassa sammukhābhāvo puggalasammukhatā. Kattikamāsassa pavāraṇamāsattā ‘ṭhapetvā kattikamāsa’nti vuttaṃ. Paccukkaḍḍhitvā ṭhapitadivaso cāti kāḷapakkhe cātuddasiṃ pannarasiṃ vā sandhāya vuttaṃ. Dve puṇṇamāsiyoti paṭhamapacchimavassūpagatānaṃ vasena vutta”nti sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. parivāra 3.483) āgataṃ.

"For an insane monk, the designation of insanity, when requested by the insane person, can be given even in absentia; it is permissible. In that case, even if he is seated, it does not become invalid due to the absence of a rule. However, to show the absence of fault in what was done in absentia, it is said, 'What was done in absentia is well done.' But ordination by means of a messenger cannot be done in person due to the possibility of the formal acts being diverse. Overturning the bowl and similar actions can be done even when the person has only moved out of arm's reach. As for 'in the presence of the Sangha' and so on, as many monks as are qualified to participate in the act must have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give it must have been brought, and those present must not object—this is the presence of the Sangha. By whatever Dhamma, whatever Vinaya, whatever Teacher's instruction the Sangha performs an act—this is the presence of the Dhamma and the presence of the Vinaya. Herein, 'Dhamma' means the actual matter. 'Vinaya' means both accusation and reminding. 'Teacher's instruction' refers to the accomplishment of the motion and the accomplishment of the proclamation. The presence of the person for whom the Sangha performs an act is the presence of the individual. Because the month of Kattika is the month for Pavāraṇā, it is said, 'except for the month of Kattika.' 'The day postponed and set aside' refers to the fourteenth or fifteenth day in the dark fortnight. 'Two full moons' is said with reference to those who entered the rains in the first or last period." This is from the Sāratthadīpanī (Sārattha. ṭī. parivāra 3.483).

“Ṭhapitauposathapavāraṇānaṃ kattikamāse sāmaggiyā katāya sāmaggīpavāraṇaṃ muñcitvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti āha ‘ṭhapetvā kattikamāsa’nti. Sace pana tesaṃ nānāsīmāsu mahāpavāraṇāya visuṃ pavāritānaṃ kattikamāsabbhantare sāmaggī hoti, sāmaggīuposatho eva tehi kātabbo, na pavāraṇā ekasmiṃ vasse katapavāraṇānaṃ puna pavāraṇāya avihitattā. Sāmaggīdivaso hotīti anuposathadivase sāmaggīkaraṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace pana cātuddasiyaṃ pannarasiyaṃ vā saṅgho sāmaggiṃ karoti, tadā sāmaggīuposathadivaso na hoti, cātuddasīpannarasīuposathova hoti. Upari pavāraṇāyapi eseva nayo. Paccukkaḍḍhitvā ṭhapitadivaso cāti bhaṇḍanakārakehi upaddutā vā kenacideva karaṇīyena pavāraṇasaṅgahaṃ vā katvā ṭhapito kāḷapakkhacātuddasīdivaso ca. Dve ca puṇṇamāsiyoti pubbakattikapuṇṇamā pacchimakattikapuṇṇamā cāti dve puṇṇamāsiyo. Etaṃ [M 2.0278] catubbidhanti puṇṇamāsidvayena saddhiṃ sāmaggīpavāraṇaṃ cātuddasīpavāraṇañca sampiṇḍetvā, idañca pakaticārittavasena vuttaṃ. Tathārūpapaccaye pana sati ubhinnaṃ puṇṇamāsīnaṃ purimā dve cātuddasiyo, kāḷapakkhacātuddasiyā anantarā pannarasīpīti imepi tayo divasā pavāraṇādivasā evāti imaṃ sattavidhampi pavāraṇādivasaṃ ṭhapetvā aññasmiṃ divase pavāretuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. parivāra 2.483) āgataṃ.

Regarding those for whom the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā have been set aside, when unity has been achieved in the month of Kattika, it is not permissible to perform the Uposatha, having abandoned the unity-Pavāraṇā; thus it is said, 'except for the month of Kattika.' If, however, for those who have separately performed the great Pavāraṇā in different boundaries, unity occurs within the month of Kattika, they should perform only the unity-Uposatha, not the Pavāraṇā, since performing Pavāraṇā again is not prescribed for those who have already performed Pavāraṇā once in a year. The phrase 'it is the day of unity' is said with reference to achieving unity on a non-Uposatha day. But if the Sangha achieves unity on the fourteenth or fifteenth day, then it is not a day of unity-Uposatha, but simply the fourteenth or fifteenth Uposatha. This same principle also applies to the Pavāraṇā above. And the 'day postponed and set aside' is the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, which has been set aside because of being troubled by quarrelsome ones, or because of some duty, or having made a collection for Pavāraṇā. 'And the two full moon days' means the earlier Kattika full moon and the later Kattika full moon—these are the two full moon days. 'This is fourfold' is said by combining the unity-Pavāraṇā and the fourteenth-day Pavāraṇā together with the two full moon days; and this is stated according to customary practice. But if there is such a condition, the two fourteenth days prior to the two full moons, and also the fifteenth day immediately following the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight—these three days are also Pavāraṇā days. Thus, setting aside these seven kinds of Pavāraṇā days, it is not permissible to perform Pavāraṇā on any other day.” This is stated in the Vimativinodanī (Vin. Vi. Ṭī. Parivāra 2.483).

Evaṃ vatthuvipattivinicchayaṃ dassetvā idāni ñattivipattivinicchayaṃ anussāvanavipattivinicchayañca dassento “ñattito vipattiyaṃ panā”tiādimāha. Tattha pañcamañattivipattiyaṃ “pacchā vā ñattiṃ ṭhapetī”ti etassa saṃvaṇṇanāyaṃ anussāvanakammaṃ katvāti paṭhamaṃ anussāvanaṃ sāvetvā “esā ñattī”ti anussāvanānantarameva sakalaṃ ñattiṃ vatvā, pariyosāne “esā ñattī”ti vatvāti adhippāyo.

Having thus shown the determination of defects in the subject matter, now, showing the determination of defects in the motion and the determination of defects in the proclamation, he says, 'But in the case of a defect from the motion,' and so on. Therein, in the explanation of the fifth defect in the motion, 'or he places the motion afterward,' the meaning is: having performed the act of proclamation, that is, having first made the proclamation heard, having stated the entire motion immediately after the proclamation, and having said, 'This is the motion,' at the conclusion.

252. Catutthaanussāvanavipattisaṃvaṇṇanāyaṃ [V 2.0202] “yvāyanti byañjanappabhedo adhippeto. Dasadhā byañjanabuddhiyā pabhedoti ettha dasadhā dasavidhena byañjanānaṃ pabhedoti yojetabbaṃ. Kenāyaṃ pabhedoti āha ‘byañjanabuddhiyā’ti. Yathādhippetatthabyañjanato byañjanasaṅkhātānaṃ akkharānaṃ janikā buddhi byañjanabuddhi, tāya byañjanabuddhiyā, akkharasamuṭṭhāpakacittabhedenevāti attho. Yaṃ vā saṃyogaparaṃ katvā vuccati, idampi garukanti yojanā”ti vimativinodaniyaṃ vuttaṃ.

252. In the explanation of the fourth defect in proclamation, 'in 'yvāyaṃ', a distinction of letters is intended.' Regarding 'The distinction is tenfold through the understanding of letters,' here 'tenfold' should be construed as 'a distinction of letters in ten ways.' As to 'By what is this distinction made?' he says, 'through the understanding of letters.' The understanding of letters is the intelligence that generates letters, which are known as expressions, from the expression of the intended meaning. 'Through that understanding of letters' means 'through the very difference in the mind that produces the letters.' Or, the construction is: 'What is said by making it followed by a conjunct consonant, this too is weighty.' So it is said in the Vimativinodanī.

Sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. parivāra 3.485) pana “ṭhānakaraṇāni sithilāni katvā uccāretabbamakkharaṃ sithilaṃ, tāniyeva dhanitāni asithilāni katvā uccāretabbamakkharaṃ dhanitaṃ. Dvimattakālaṃ dīghaṃ, ekamattakālaṃ rassaṃ. Dasadhā byañjanabuddhiyā pabhedoti evaṃ sithilādivasena byañjanabuddhiyā akkharuppādakacittassa dasappakārena [M 2.0279] pabhedo. Sabbāni hi akkharāni cittasamuṭṭhānāni yathādhippetatthabyañjanato byañjanāni ca. Saṃyogo paro etasmāti saṃyogaparo. Na saṃyogaparo asaṃyogaparo ‘āyasmato buddharakkhitatherassa yassa na khamatī’ti ettha ta-kāra na-kārasahitāro asaṃyogaparo. Karaṇānīti kaṇṭhādīni” iti ettakaṃ vuttaṃ.

In the Sāratthadīpanī (Sārattha. Ṭī. Parivāra 3.485), however, it is stated: “A letter to be pronounced by making the places and instruments of articulation lax is a lax letter; a letter to be pronounced by making those same ones tense, not lax, is a tense letter. A long vowel has a duration of two measures; a short vowel has a duration of one measure. Regarding 'The distinction is tenfold through the understanding of letters,' thus the distinction of the mind that produces letters is of ten kinds by way of laxity and so on, through the understanding of letters. For all letters arise from the mind, and they are expressions from expressing the intended meaning. 'A conjunct consonant is after this' is 'saṃyogaparo' (followed by a conjunct consonant). 'Not saṃyogaparo' is 'asaṃyogaparo' (not followed by a conjunct consonant). In 'āyasmato buddharakkhitatherassa yassa na khamatī,' here the vowel 'a' accompanied by the consonant 't' and the consonant 'n' is 'asaṃyogaparo'. 'Instruments' means the throat and so on.” This much is said.

Puna vimativinodaniyaṃ (vi. vi. ṭī. parivāra 2.485) “tattha āyasmatotiādīsu sarānantaritāni sa-kāra ma-kārādibyañjanāni ‘saṃyogo’ti vuccanti. Yo saṃyogo paro yassa a-kārādino, so saṃyogaparo nāma. Rassanti a-kārādibyañjanarahitaṃ padaṃ. Asaṃyogaparanti ‘yassa na khamatī’tiādīsu sa-kāra na-kārādibyañjanasahitaṃ padaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ta-kārassa tha-kāraṃ akatvā ‘suṇātu me’tiādiṃ avatvā vaggantare sithilameva katvā ‘suṇāṭu me’tiādiṃ vadantopi duruttaṃ karotiyeva ṭhapetvā anurūpaṃ ādesaṃ. Yañhi ‘saccikatthaparamatthenā’ti vattabbe ‘saccikaṭṭhaparamaṭṭhenā’ti ca ‘atthakathā’ti ca vattabbe ‘aṭṭhakathā’ti ca tattha tattha vuccati, tādisaṃ pāḷiaṭṭhakathādīsu diṭṭhapayogaṃ tadanurūpañca vattuṃ vaṭṭati, tato aññaṃ na vaṭṭati. Tenāha ‘anukkamāgataṃ paveṇiṃ avināsentenā’tiādi. ‘Dīghe vattabbe rassa’ntiādīsu ‘bhikkhūna’nti vattabbe ‘bhikkhuna’nti vā ‘bahūsū’ti vattabbe ‘bahusū’ti vā ‘nakkhamatī’ti vattabbe ‘na khamatī’ti vā ‘upasampadāpekkho’ti vattabbe ‘upasampadāpekho’ti vā evaṃ anurūpaṭṭhānesu eva dīgharassādirassadīghādivasena parivattetuṃ vaṭṭati, na pana ‘nāgo’ti vattabbe ‘nago’ti vā ‘saṅgho’ti [V 2.0203] vattabbe ‘sagho’ti vā ‘tisso’ti vattabbe ‘tiso’ti vā ‘yācatī’ti vattabbe ‘yācantī’ti vā evaṃ ananurūpaṭṭhānesu vattuṃ[M 2.0280]. Sambandhaṃ pana vavatthānañca sabbathāpi vaṭṭatīti gahetabba”nti āgataṃ. Sesāni aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva suṭṭhu sallakkhetabbāni.

Furthermore, in the Vimativinodanī (Vin. Vi. Ṭī. Parivāra 2.485), it is said: “Therein, in instances such as 'āyasmato,' consonants like the letter 's', the letter 'm', and so on, that are not separated by a vowel, are called 'saṃyoga' (conjunct consonant). A vowel, such as the letter 'a', which is followed by a conjunct consonant, is called 'saṃyogaparo'. 'Rassaṃ' (short) refers to a syllable without a conjunct consonant. 'Asaṃyogaparaṃ' is said with reference to a syllable containing a consonant like the letter 's' or the letter 'n' in examples such as 'yassa na khamatī'. Even one who, not making the letter 't' into the letter 'th', and not saying 'suṇātu me' and so on, but making it lax in another consonant class and saying 'suṇāṭu me' and so on, still commits a mispronunciation, except for an appropriate substitution. For where one should say 'saccikatthaparamatthenā', it is said 'saccikaṭṭhaparamaṭṭhenā'; and where one should say 'atthakathā', it is said 'aṭṭhakathā' in various places. It is permissible to say such usage seen in the Pāḷi, commentaries, and so on, and what is analogous to it; what is other than that is not permissible. Therefore, he said, 'by one not destroying the tradition that has come down in sequence,' and so on. Regarding 'when a long vowel should be said, a short one is said,' and so on, it is permissible to change by way of long-to-short or short-to-long only in appropriate places, such as saying 'bhikkhuna' when one should say 'bhikkhūna', or 'bahusu' when one should say 'bahūsu', or 'na khamatī' when one should say 'nakkhamatī', or 'upasampadāpekho' when one should say 'upasampadāpekkho'. But it is not permissible to speak in inappropriate places, such as saying 'nago' when one should say 'nāgo', or 'sagho' when one should say 'saṅgho', or 'tiso' when one should say 'tisso', or 'yācatī' when one should say 'yācantī'. It should be understood, however, that connection and determination are permissible in every way.” The remaining points should be well noted according to the method stated in the commentary.

253. Sīmavipattivinicchayo pana heṭṭhā sīmakathāyaṃ sabbena kathito, tasmā tattha vuttanayeneva gahetabbo.

253. The determination of defects concerning the boundary, however, has been fully explained below in the discussion on boundaries. Therefore, it should be understood according to the method stated there.

Parisavipattikathāya catuvaggakaraṇeti catuvaggena saṅghena kattabbe. Anissāritāti uposathaṭṭhapanādinā vā laddhinānāsaṃvāsakabhāvena vā na bahikatā. Aṭṭhakathāyañhi “apakatattassāti ukkhittakassa vā yassa vā uposathapavāraṇā ṭhapitā hontī”ti (pari. aṭṭha. 425) vuttattā ṭhapitauposathapavāraṇo bhikkhu apakatatto evāti gahetabbaṃ. Parisuddhasīlāti pārājikaṃ anāpannā adhippetā. Parivāsādikammesu pana garukaṭṭhāpi apakatattā evāti gahetabbaṃ. Avasesā…pe… chandārahāva hontīti hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā ṭhite sandhāya vuttaṃ, avijahitvā ṭhitā pana chandārahā na honti, tepi catuvaggādito adhikā hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvāva chandārahā honti, tasmā saṅghato hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā ṭhiteneva chando vā pārisuddhi vā dātabbā.

In the discussion of defects of the assembly, 'in the performance by a group of four' means 'to be done by a Sangha of four'. 'Not sent out' means not excluded by the setting aside of the Uposatha and so on, or by being of a different view and communion. For since it is said in the commentary: '“Of one not restored to normalcy” means of one who is suspended or of one for whom the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā have been set aside,' a bhikkhu for whom the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā have been set aside should be understood as one who is indeed not restored to normalcy. 'Of pure virtue' means those who have not fallen into a pārājika offense are intended. However, in formal acts such as probation, even those in a grave state should be understood as indeed not restored to normalcy. 'The remaining… are worthy of giving consent' is said with reference to those standing having left arm's reach. But those standing without having left arm's reach are not worthy of giving consent. Even those who are more than a group of four are worthy of giving consent only after having left arm's reach. Therefore, consent or a declaration of purity should be given only by one standing having left arm's reach of the Sangha.

Sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. parivāra 3.488) pana “anukkhittā pārājikaṃ anāpannā ca pakatattāti āha ‘pakatattā anukkhittā’tiādi. Tattha anissāritāti purimapadasseva vevacanaṃ. Parisuddhasīlāti pārājikaṃ anāpannā. Na tesaṃ chando vā pārisuddhi vā etīti tīsu dvīsu vā nisinnesu ekassa vā dvinnaṃ vā chandapārisuddhi āhaṭāpi anāhaṭāva hotīti adhippāyo”ti āgato. Evaṃ pāḷiyañca aṭṭhakathāya ca catunnampi kammānaṃ sampatti ca vipatti ca āgatā, ṭīkācariyehi ca vinicchitā, tasmā [M 2.0281] aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva cattāri kammāni kattabbāni, na avuttanayena. Vuttañhi samantapāsādikāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 1. ganthārambhakathā; 2.431) –

In the Sāratthadīpanī (Sārattha. Ṭī. Parivāra 3.488), however, it is stated: 'He said, “a normal monk, not suspended,” etc., meaning one who is not suspended, has not committed a pārājika offense, and is a normal monk. Here, `anissāritā` is a synonym for the preceding word. `Parisuddhasīlā` means one who has not committed a pārājika offense. The intended meaning of “Their consent or purity does not come” is that even if the consent and purity of one or two monks sitting among three or two are brought, it is as if they were not brought.’ Thus, in both the Pāli Canon and the commentaries, the success and failure of the four formal acts are found, and the sub-commentators have analyzed them. Therefore, the four formal acts should be performed according to the method described in the commentaries, not by an undescribed method. For it is stated in the Samantapāsādikā (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 1. Ganthārambhakathā; 2.431):—

“Buddhena [V 2.0204] dhammo vinayo ca vutto;

Yo tassa puttehi tatheva ñāto;

So yehi tesaṃ matimaccajantā;

Yasmā pure aṭṭhakathā akaṃsu.

“The Dhamma and the Discipline were spoken by the Buddha; It was known in that very way by His sons; Since they, not transgressing their understanding, Composed the commentaries in ancient times.”

“Tasmā hi yaṃ aṭṭhakathāsu vuttaṃ;

Taṃ vajjayitvāna pamādalekhaṃ;

Sabbampi sikkhāsu sagāravānaṃ;

Yasmā pamāṇaṃ idha paṇḍitāna”nti.

“Therefore, whatever is said in the commentaries, setting aside careless writing, is entirely a standard here for the wise who are respectful of the training.”

Imasmiñhi kammavagge apalokanādīnaṃ catunnaṃ kammānaṃ karaṇaṭṭhānaṃ ekādasavipattisīmavimuttaṃ baddhasīmabhūtaṃyeva vuttaṃ, “ekādasahi ākārehi sīmato kammāni vipajjantī”ti (pari. 486) vacanato na abaddhaupacārasīmabhūtaṃ. Na hi tattha ekādasavipatti atthi. Aṭṭhakathāyampi (pari. aṭṭha. 482) “apalokanakammaṃ nāma sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ sodhetvā chandārahānaṃ chandaṃ āharitvā samaggassa saṅghassa anumatiyā tikkhattuṃ sāvetvā kattabbaṃ kamma”nti apalokanakammassāpi baddhasīmāyameva kattabbabhāvo vutto, na upacārasīmāyaṃ. Na hi tattha sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghasodhanañca chandārahānañca atthi, antosīmaṃ paviṭṭhapaviṭṭhānaṃ saṅghalābho dātabboyeva hoti, tasmā “ñattikammabhūtaṃ uposathapavāraṇākammaṃ abaddhasīmavihārepi kattabba”nti gaṇhantānaṃ ācariyānaṃ vādopi “ñattidutiyakammabhūtaṃ kathinadānakammaṃ upacārasīmāyameva kattabba”nti gaṇhantānaṃ ācariyānaṃ vādopi pāḷivirodho aṭṭhakathāvirodho ca hotīti veditabbo. Yamettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ uposathapavāraṇakathāvaṇṇanāyañca [M 2.0282] kathinakathāvaṇṇanāyañca vuttaṃ, atthikehi tattha suṭṭhu oloketvā saṃsayo vinodetabbo.

In this section on formal acts, the place for performing the four types of acts—starting with the announcement—is said to be a bound boundary, free from the eleven boundary failures, according to the statement: “Formal acts fail in eleven ways regarding boundaries” (Pari. 486). It is not an unbound or proximity boundary, for the eleven failures do not exist there. The commentary also states (Pari. Aṭṭha. 482): “The announcement act is an act to be performed after purifying the Sangha residing within the boundary, obtaining consent from those eligible for giving consent, and declaring it three times with the approval of a united Sangha.” Thus, it is stated that the announcement act should be performed only within a bound boundary, not in a proximity boundary. For in the latter, neither the purification of the Sangha residing within the boundary nor those eligible for consent exist; those who have entered and are present within the boundary must indeed be granted inclusion in the Sangha. Therefore, it should be understood that the view of those teachers who hold that “the Uposatha and Pavāraṇa acts, being formal acts by declaration, should be performed even in a residence without a bound boundary,” and the view of those teachers who hold that “the Kathina-giving act, being a formal act by declaration and a second motion, should be performed only within a proximity boundary”—both contradict the Pāli Canon and the commentary. What should be said here has been explained in the expositions on the Uposatha, Pavāraṇa, and Kathina. Those interested should examine it thoroughly therein and resolve their doubts.

Idāni sabbe bhikkhū lekhakārehi paricayavasena sabbaganthānaṃ ādimhi likhitaṃ mahānamakkārapāṭhaṃ saraṇagamanassa, kammavācāya ca ārambhakāle mahatā ussāhena bhaṇanti, so pana pāṭho neva saraṇagamanapariyāpanno, na kammavācāpariyāpanno, nāpi kammavācāya pubbakaraṇapariyāpanno, tasmiṃ abhaṇitepi na saraṇagamanassa vā kammavācāya vā hāni atthi, na bhaṇite vaḍḍhi, tasmā pakaraṇācariyā saraṇagamanārambhepi kammavācārambhepi tassa mahānamakkārapāṭhassa [V 2.0205] vaṇṇanaṃ na vadanti, vadanto pana “bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa” iti padānaṃ attho visuddhimaggasamantapāsādikāsāratthadīpanīādippakaraṇesu “bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho” itipadānaṃ attho viya vitthārena vattabbo siyā, evaṃ santepi bhagavato yathābhūtaguṇadīpanavasena pavattattā sabbepi ācariyā sabbesu ganthārambhesu tikkhattuṃ maṅgalatthaṃ bhaṇanti. Bhaṇantehi ca pana na-kāra mo-kārādīnaṃ ṭhānakaraṇādisampadaṃ ahāpentena sithiladhanitadīgharassādivisesaṃ manasi karontena samaṇasāruppena parimaṇḍalena padabyañjanena bhaṇitabbo hoti, na atiāyatakena gītasaddasadisena saddena. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā “na, bhikkhave, āyatakena gītassarena dhammo gāyitabbo, yo gāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti (cūḷava. 249).

Now, all monks, due to familiarity with scribes, recite with great enthusiasm the great homage passage written at the beginning of all texts when taking refuge and at the start of a formal act. However, that passage is neither included in the taking of refuge, nor in the formal act, nor is it a preliminary to the formal act. Even if it is not recited, there is no loss to the taking of refuge or the formal act, nor any gain if it is recited. Therefore, the authors of the treatises do not expound on this great homage passage when beginning the taking of refuge or a formal act. Yet, if one were to expound on it, the meaning of the phrase “of the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One” should be elaborated in detail, just as the meaning of the phrase “the Blessed One is an Arahant, Perfectly Self-Enlightened” is explained in works like the Visuddhimagga, Samantapāsādikā, and Sāratthadīpanī. Even so, because it serves to illuminate the true qualities of the Blessed One, all teachers recite it three times at the beginning of all texts for auspicious purposes. When reciting, one should do so without diminishing the proper articulation and production of syllables like “na” and “mo,” paying attention to the distinctions between lax and tense sounds, long and short vowels, with a complete and rounded utterance of words and syllables befitting a renunciant, not with an excessively prolonged sound resembling a song. For this was said by the Blessed One: “Monks, the Dhamma should not be chanted with an elongated, singing tone. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong conduct” (Cūḷavagga 249).

“Ekamatto bhave rasso, dvimatto dīghamuccate;

Timatto tu pluto ñeyyo, byañjanañcaḍḍhamattika”nti. –

“A short vowel is one measure, a long vowel is called two measures; a pluta should be understood as three measures, and a consonant has half a measure.”

Saddappakaraṇācariyehi vuttaṃ saddalakkhaṇaṃ nissāya na-kārādīsu rassabhūte asare ekamattaṃ, na-byañjane aḍḍhamattaṃ sampiṇḍetvā [M 2.0283] diyaḍḍhamattakālaṃ pamāṇaṃ katvā uccārīyate. Mo-kārādīsu dīghabhūte o-kārādisare dvimattaṃ, ma-kārādibyañjane aḍḍhamattaṃ sampiṇḍetvā aḍḍhateyyamattākālaṃ pamāṇaṃ katvā uccārīyate, na tato uddhanti. Nanu “pluto timatto ñeyyo”ti vuttanti? Saccaṃ, sā pana dūrato avhāyanādīsuyeva labbhati, nāññattha. Vuttañhi kārikāyaṃ –

Relying on the characteristics of sound taught by the teachers of phonetics treatises, in syllables such as 'na', the short vowel 'a' has one mora and the consonant 'n' has half a mora; combining them, it is pronounced with a duration of one and a half morae. In syllables such as 'mo', the long vowel 'o' has two morae and the consonant 'm' has half a mora; combining them, it is pronounced with a duration of two and a half morae, and not more than that. Is it not said, “A pluta should be known as three morae”? True, but that is found only in such cases as calling from a distance, and not elsewhere. For it is stated in the verse:—

“Dūrato avhāne gīte, tatheva rodanepi ca;

Plutā timattikā vuttā, sabbete nettha gayhare”ti. –

“In calling from afar, in singing, and likewise in weeping, pluta vowels of three morae are stated; all these are not applicable here.”

Kittakena pana kālena ekamattā viññeyyāti? Akkhinimisaummisamattakālenāti ācariyā. Eke pana ācariyā “aṅguliphoṭanakālappamāṇenā”ti vadanti. Vuttañhi ācariyadhammasenāpatittherena –

By what duration, then, is a single mora to be known? The teachers say: “By the time of a blink or an opening of the eye.” Some teachers, however, say: “By the duration it takes to snap one’s fingers.” For it was said by the Elder Teacher Dhammasenāpati:—

“Pamāṇaṃ ekamattassa, nimisummisatobravuṃ;

Aṅguliphoṭakālassa, pamāṇenāpi abravu”nti.

“They spoke of the measure of a single mora as the time of a blink or an opening of the eye; they also spoke of it as the measure of the time of a finger-snap.”

Evaṃ [V 2.0206] saddasatthācariyehi vacanato suddharassasaraṭṭhāne ekamattāpamāṇaṃ, sabyañjanarassasaraṭṭhāne diyaḍḍhamattāpamāṇaṃ, suddhadīghasaraṭṭhāne dvimattāpamāṇaṃ, sabyañjanadīghasaraṭṭhāne aḍḍhateyyamattāpamāṇaṃ kālaṃ sallakkhetvā uccārīyate.

Thus, according to the teachers of the science of phonetics, in the case of a pure short vowel, the duration is a single mora; in the case of a short vowel with a consonant, the duration is one and a half morae; in the case of a pure long vowel, the duration is two morae; and in the case of a long vowel with a consonant, the duration is two and a half morae. Having determined the duration, it should be pronounced.

Idāni pana bhikkhū mahānamakkārabhaṇane balavaussāhaṃ katvā bhaṇantā rassaṭṭhānesu dvitimattākālaṃ dīghaṭṭhānesu catupañcamattākālaṃ saraṃ paṭhapetvā bhaṇanti, tadayuttaṃ viya dissati. Apare paṭhamavāre bhaṇitvā “sammāsambuddhassā”ti pariyosānapadaṃ patvāpi tattha aṭṭhapetvā puna “namo tassā”ti bhaṇitvā sa-kāre ṭhapetvā thokaṃ vissamitvā dutiyavāre “bhagavato”ti idaṃ ādiṃ katvā yāva pariyosānaṃ bhaṇitvā ṭhapenti. Tatiyavāre pana ādito paṭṭhāya pariyosāne ṭhapenti. Evaṃ bhaṇantañca bahū pasaṃsanti, evaṃ pana kātabbanti neva [M 2.0284] pāḷiyaṃ, na aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vijjati. Yathā ñatticatutthakamme kariyamāne tīṇi anussāvanāni saddato ca atthato ca abhinnāni aññamaññaṃ saṅkaravirahitāni katvā bhaṇitabbāni, evaṃ mahānamakkārapāṭhe tikkhattuṃ bhaññamāne tayo vārā saddato ca atthato ca abhinne katvā saṅkaravirahite katvā ādito ārabhitvā pariyosāne ṭhapetabbā hontīti.

But now, bhikkhus, when reciting the Great Homage, making a strong effort, they prolong the sound when reciting—making it two or three measures in short places and four or five measures in long places. This seems inappropriate. Others, after reciting in the first round and reaching the concluding phrase “sammāsambuddhassa,” pause there, and then reciting again “namo tassa,” they pause at the letter “sa,” rest briefly, and in the second round, begin with “bhagavato” and recite up to the conclusion before pausing. In the third round, they start from the beginning and pause at the conclusion. Many praise those who recite in this way, but such a method is not found in the Pāli Canon or the commentaries. Just as in an act concluded by a motion, the three announcements must be recited so that they are identical in sound and meaning, without confusion between them, so too in the recitation of the Great Homage, when recited three times, the three rounds should be made identical in sound and meaning, free from confusion, starting from the beginning and pausing at the conclusion.

Tatrāyamekeevaṃ vadanti – yathā nāma javena gacchantassa ṭhātabbaṭṭhānaṃ patvāpi sahasā ṭhātuṃ na sakkoti, ekapādamattaṃ gantvā tiṭṭhati, evaṃ ādito bhaṇantassa balavaussāhattā pariyosāne pattepi ṭhapetuṃ na sakkoti, “namo tassā”ti dvipadamattaṃ bhaṇitvā sakkotīti. Evaṃ sante dutiyatatiyavāresu kasmā sakkotīti? Tadā pana dutiyavāre thokaṃ vissamitattā laddhassāso hutvā sakkotīti. Evaṃ te āyasmanto sayameva attānaṃ vighātaṃ pāpenti. Na hi “mahānamakkāraṃ bhaṇantena paṭhamavāre balavaussāhena bhaṇitabbo”ti bhagavatā paññatto, dhammasaṅgāhakattherehi vā ṭhapito atthi. Evaṃ sante yathā pātimokkhuddesakena pātimokkhaṃ uddisantena yattakā bhikkhū pātimokkhaṃ suṇanti, tesaṃ savanappamāṇena yāva pariyosānā uddisituṃ attano sarappamāṇaṃ gahetvā pātimokkho uddisitabbo, evaṃ kammavācaṃ bhaṇantenapi sīmamaṇḍale nisinnabhikkhūnaṃ savanappamāṇena yāva pariyosānā attano sarappamāṇaṃ gahetvā bhaṇitabbāti.

Herein, some say thus: Just as one walking swiftly, even upon reaching the stopping place, cannot stop suddenly, but stops after taking one more step, so too, one who recites from the beginning, due to strong exertion, cannot stop even upon reaching the end, but can stop after reciting the two words, 'namo tassa.' If this is so, why is it possible in the second and third recitations? Then, in the second recitation, because one has rested a little and regained breath, it becomes possible. Thus, these venerable ones bring trouble upon themselves. For it has not been laid down by the Blessed One that one must recite the Great Homage in the first recitation with strong exertion, nor was it established by the Elders who compiled the Dhamma. If this is so, just as a bhikkhu reciting the Pātimokkha should gauge his own voice to the hearing range of as many bhikkhus as are listening to the Pātimokkha and recite to the very end, so too, when reciting a formal act, one should gauge one’s own voice to the hearing range of the bhikkhus seated within the boundary and recite to the very end.

Apare pana ācariyā mo-kārādīsu o-kārantapadesu aññesaṃ padānaṃ atirekena sarena dvattikkhattuṃ [V 2.0207] anukaraṇasaddaṃ anubandhāpayamānā bhaṇanti, tesaṃ ācariyānaṃ tādisaṃ bhaṇanaṃ sutvā paricayappattā aññe bhikkhū vā gahaṭṭhā vā aññesaṃ [M 2.0285] ācariyānaṃ kammavācaṃ na garuṃ karonti, tāya kammavācāya upasampadā alabhitabbā viya maññanti, tādisaṃ pana bhaṇanaṃ tesaṃ ācariyānaṃ sissānusissā eva tathā bhaṇanti, na aññe ācariyā. Te pana porāṇācariyānaṃ sarasampannānaṃ anukaraṇasaddarahitampi sahitaṃ viya khāyamānaṃ suṇantānaṃ atimanorathaṃ saddaṃ sutvā diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjantā evaṃ karonti maññe. Na hi vinaye vā saddasatthesu vā tathā bhaṇitabbanti atthi, tasmā vicāretabbametanti.

However, other teachers recite in such a way that for words ending in 'o', such as those beginning with 'mo', they cause an imitative sound to follow two or three times, with an extra tone for other words. Hearing such recitation from those teachers, other bhikkhus or lay followers who have become familiar with it do not respect the formal acts of other teachers. They think that ordination cannot be obtained through such a formal act. But only the disciples and grand-disciples of those teachers recite in that way; other teachers do not. I think they do so by following the precedent of what they have seen, having heard the very pleasing sound of the ancient, vocally gifted teachers, a sound which, though without imitative sounds, appeared to the listeners as if it were accompanied by them. For it is not found in the Vinaya or in the grammatical texts that one should recite in such a way. Therefore, this should be investigated.

Bahū pana bhikkhū “sithilaṃ dhanitañca dīgharassa”ntiādinā vinaye kathitavinicchayañca “ettha pañcasu vaggesū”tiādinā saddasatthesu katavinicchayañca ajānantā piṭakattayakovidānaṃ vinayadharabahussutattherānaṃ santikā aladdhopadesā hutvā tattha tattha upasampadaṃ karontānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vacanameva gahetvā heyyopādeyyaṃ ajānantā pubbe paradesato āgatānaṃ puññavantānaṃ sarasampannānaṃ mahātherānaṃ anosarena bhaṇamānānaṃ saraṃ sutvā tesaṃ theravarānaṃ matiṃ apucchitvāva yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathāsutaṃ likhitvā ṭhapentā anukkamena paṇḍitehi hasitabbaṃ ayuttaṃ kathaṃ dīpentā “imasmiṃ ṭhāne byagghiyā saddasadisaṃ saddaṃ karonti, imasmiṃ ṭhāne sakuṇiyā saddasadisaṃ saddaṃ karonti, imasmiṃ ṭhāne tambulakasaṭapātaṃ karonti, imasmiṃ ṭhāne dakkhiṇato namantā bhaṇanti, imasmiṃ ṭhāne vāmato namantā bhaṇanti, imasmiṃ ṭhāne vilāsaṃ kurumānā bhaṇantī”tiādīni vatvā tadeva saddahantā rukkhamūlaumaṅgaleṇādīsu nisīditvā tameva vacanaṃ anusikkhantā tadanurūpaṃ kammavācaṃ bhaṇantā “ahaṃ kammavācākusalo”ti vatvā bālajane saññāpetvā tesaṃ tesaṃ upasampadāpekkhānaṃ kammavācaṃ bhaṇanti, ime bhikkhū bhagavato āṇaṃ atikkāmenti, sāsanaṃ osakkāpentīti daṭṭhabbā.

But many bhikkhus, not knowing the decision given in the Vinaya beginning 'lax and tense, long and short,' nor the decision made in the grammatical texts beginning 'here in the five sections,' and not having received instruction from the elders who are experts in the three Piṭakas, bearers of the Vinaya, and greatly learned; taking only the words of bhikkhus performing ordinations here and there, not knowing what is to be rejected and what is to be adopted; having heard the recitation of the great, meritorious, and vocally gifted elders who came from foreign lands in the past and who recited without a model, and without asking the opinion of those excellent elders, they write down and preserve what they have seen and heard as it is. Gradually, they explain improper things at which the wise would laugh, saying: 'In this place, they make a sound like a tigress; in this place, they make a sound like a bird; in this place, they perform the tambulakasaṭapāta; in this place, they recite bowing to the right; in this place, they recite bowing to the left; in this place, they recite making playful gestures,' and so on. Believing this, they sit at the foot of trees, in tunnels, and in caves, practicing those very words and reciting the Kammavācā accordingly. Saying, 'I am skilled in the Kammavācā,' they convince the foolish and recite the Kammavācā for those seeking ordination. It should be seen that these bhikkhus transgress the Blessed One's command and cause the dispensation to decline.

Athāparepi [M 2.0286] bhikkhū gāmakāvāsādīsu vasantā paṇḍitānaṃ santike apayirupāsamānā vatthusampattimpi vatthuvipattimpi ñattianussāvanasīmaparisasampattimpi vipattimpi tathato ajānantā bahavo sisse ṭhapetvā pabbajjañca upasampadañca karontā parisaṃ vaḍḍhāpenti, tepi bhagavato sāsanaṃ osakkāpenti, tasmā bhagavato āṇaṃ karontehi lajjīpesalehi bahussutehi sikkhākāmehi sappurisabhikkhūhi evarūpānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sahāyakehi upatthambhakehi ekasambhogasaṃvāsakarehi na bhavitabbaṃ. Idāni bhikkhū –

Furthermore, other bhikkhus living in village residences and so on, not attending upon the wise, not truly understanding the success or failure of the basis, the success or failure of the motion and announcement, or the success or failure of the boundary and assembly, establish many disciples, giving both the going forth and the full ordination, thereby increasing their assembly. These bhikkhus also cause the Blessed One's dispensation to decline. Therefore, virtuous bhikkhus who act upon the Blessed One's command, who are conscientious, amiable, learned, and desire training, should not be companions, supporters, or co-residents with bhikkhus of this sort. Now, bhikkhus—

“Ca-kārantaṃ [V 2.0208] sa-kārantaṃ, ta-kārantasamaṃ vade;

Ña-kārantaṃ la-kārantaṃ, na-kārantasamaṃ vade”ti. –

'One should pronounce a word ending in 'ca' and a word ending in 'sa' like one ending in 'ta'; one should pronounce a word ending in 'ña' and a word ending in 'la' like one ending in 'na'.'

Imaṃ silokaṃ upanissāya saraṇagamanepi “buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti pāṭhaṃ “buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti paṭhanti. Kammavācāyampi “paṭhamaṃ upajjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo”tiādipāṭhaṃ “paṭhamaṃ upajjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo”tiādinā paṭhanti. Ettha yuttitopi āgamatopi kāraṇaṃ cintetabbaṃ.

Relying on this verse, even when going for refuge, they recite the text 'buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī' as 'buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī'. In a formal act too, they recite the text beginning 'paṭhamaṃ upajjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo' as 'paṭhamaṃ upajjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo' and so on. Here, the reason should be considered from the standpoint of both logic and scripture.

Tatrāyaṃ yutticintā – “ca-kārantaṃ sa-kārantaṃ, ta-kārantasamaṃ vade”ti ettha ca-kāro tālujo, ta-kāro dantajo, evamete akkharā ṭhānatopi asamānā. Ca-kāro jivhāmajjhakaraṇo, ta-kāro jivhaggakaraṇo, evaṃ karaṇatopi asamānā. Ca-kāro dutiyavaggapariyāpanno, ta-kāro catutthavaggapariyāpanno, evaṃ vaggatopi asamānā. Saṃyogakkharavasena na pubbakkharā sutiṃ labhantā saravisesaṃ pāpuṇanti, teneva ca-kārena saddasatthakārācariyā “saṃyoge pare rassatta”nti ca “saṃyogapubbā e-kāro-kārā rassāiva vattabbā”ti ca vadanti. Evaṃ sante kathaṃ asamānaṭṭhānikena asamānakaraṇena asamānavaggena saṃyogakkharena laddhasutikā akkharā tato aññena asamānaṭṭhānikena asamānakaraṇena asamānavaggena [M 2.0287] saṃyogakkharena laddhasamānasutikā bhaveyyuṃ. Na kevalañca ete akkharā asamānaṭṭhānikā asamānakaraṇā asamānavaggāva honti, atha kho anāsannaṭṭhānikā anāsannakaraṇā anāsannavaggā ca honti. Yathā ca vīṇaṃ vādentānaṃ dūre tantissarena tato dūre tantissaro asamāno hoti, evaṃ dūraṭṭhānikena akkharena dūrakaraṇena tato dūraṭṭhāniko dūrakaraṇo samānasutiko kathaṃ bhaveyya, vaggakkharānañca aññamaññaṃ asaṅkaravasena asamānasutivasena pavattanato “vaggantaṃ vā vagge”ti sutte niggahitassa vaggantakaraṇe sati aññavaggasmiṃ pare aññavaggantaṃ na pāpuṇāti, “vagge ghosāghosānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā”ti suttena ca asadisadvebhāvakaraṇe aññavagge aññavaggadvebhāvo na hoti.

Herein is the logical consideration: regarding the statement, 'A word ending in ca or sa should be pronounced like one ending in ta,' in this case, the letter ca is palatal, and the letter ta is dental; thus, these letters are dissimilar in their place of articulation. The letter ca is produced with the middle of the tongue, while the letter ta is produced with the tip of the tongue; thus, they are dissimilar in their means of production. The letter ca belongs to the second group of consonants, while the letter ta belongs to the fourth group; thus, they are dissimilar in their classification. Because of conjunct consonants, preceding letters do not obtain their sound and thus do not attain a special vowel. Therefore, the teachers of phonetics state, 'When a conjunct follows, the preceding vowel becomes short,' and 'The vowels e and o preceding a conjunct should always be pronounced short.' This being so, how could letters—which are dissimilar in place of articulation, means of production, and classification, and which have obtained their sound by means of a conjunct consonant—become similar in sound to another letter that is also dissimilar in place of articulation, means of production, and classification? Not only are these letters dissimilar in place of articulation, means of production, and classification, but they are also non-adjacent in place, non-adjacent in means of production, and non-adjacent in classification. And just as when playing a lute, the sound of a distant string is dissimilar to the sound of a string even more distant, so how could a letter with a distant place of articulation and a distant means of production become similar in sound to one with an even more distant place of articulation and means of production? Furthermore, because the letters of the groups proceed without intermixture and with dissimilar sounds, according to the rule, 'Or a nasal of the same group,' when the niggahīta is made into the nasal of a group, it does not become the nasal of a different group when a letter of a different group follows. And by the rule, 'Within a group, the third and first are for the voiced and unvoiced,' in the case of making a dissimilar doubling, the doubling of a letter from one group does not occur in another group.

Yadi ca ca-kārantakkharo ta-kārantakkharena samānasutiko siyā, evaṃ sati kiṃ ca-kārantakkharalekhanena sabbattha ta-kārantameva likheyya, tathā pana alikhitvā payogānurūpaṃ paṭhamakkharassa sadisadvebhāvaṭṭhāne “kacco kaccāyano”ti, asadisadvebhāvaṭṭhāne “vaccho vacchāyano”ti tatiyakkharassa sadisadvebhāvaṭṭhāne “majjaṃ sammajja”nti, asadisadvebhāvaṭṭhāne “upajjhā [V 2.0209] upajjhāyo”ti samānaṭṭhānasamānakaraṇasamānavaggakkharānameva dvebhāvo likhīyati, no itaresaṃ, tasmā payogānurūpaṃ ca-kāranta ja-kārantaṭṭhānesu sakavaggasutivaseneva vattabbaṃ, na aññavaggasutivasena. Sa-kārante pana sa-kārassa ta-kārena samānaṭṭhānikattā samānakaraṇattā ca vaggaavaggavasena bhinnepi avaggakkharānaṃ vaggakkharehi sādhāraṇattā ca avaggakkharānaṃ vaggakkharānaṃ viya visuṃ sutiyā abhāvato ca sa-kārantassa ta-kārantabhaṇanaṃ yuttaṃ siyā. Sa-kāropi hi dantajo, ta-kāropi, sa-kāropi jivhaggakaraṇo, ta-kāropi[M 2.0288], tasmā samānaṭṭhānikānaṃ samānakaraṇānaṃ akkharānaṃ samānasutibhāvo yutto. Ña-kāranta la-kārantānaṃ na-kārantabhaṇanepi iminā nayena ña-kāranta na-kārantānaṃ asamānasutibhāvo la-kāranta na-kārantānaṃ samānasutibhāvo daṭṭhabboti. Ayamettha yutticintā.

If a letter ending in ca were to have the same sound as a letter ending in ta, then what would be the point of writing the letter ending in ca? One should just write the letter ending in ta everywhere. However, since it is not written thus, according to usage, in a case of similar doubling of the first letter, it is written as 'kacco Kaccāyano,' and in a case of dissimilar doubling, as 'vaccho Vacchāyano.' In a case of similar doubling of the third letter, it is written as 'majjaṃ sammajja,' and in a case of dissimilar doubling, as 'upajjhā upajjhāyo.' Doubling is written only for letters that have the same place of articulation, the same articulator, and belong to the same phonetic group, not for others. Therefore, according to usage, in the case of letters ending in ca and ja, they should be pronounced according to the sound of their own group, not that of another group. In the case of a letter ending in sa, however, since sa has the same place of articulation and the same articulator as ta, and since, although they are different in that one is a non-group letter and the other a group letter, non-group letters share commonality with group letters, and since non-group letters do not have a distinct sound like group letters, it would be appropriate to pronounce a letter ending in sa as one ending in ta. For sa is dental, and so is ta; sa is produced with the tip of the tongue, and so is ta. Therefore, it is proper for letters with the same place of articulation and the same articulator to have a similar sound. Regarding the pronunciation of letters ending in ñā and la as ending in na, by this same method it should be understood that a letter ending in ñā and a letter ending in na have dissimilar sounds, whereas a letter ending in la and a letter ending in na have a similar sound. This is the logical consideration here.

Āgamacintā pana evaṃ kātabbā –

The consideration of the tradition, however, should be undertaken as follows:

“Ca-kārantaṃ sa-kārantaṃ, ta-kārantasamaṃ vade;

Ña-kārantaṃ la-kārantaṃ, na-kārantasamaṃ vade”ti. –

A letter ending in ca and a letter ending in sa should be pronounced the same as one ending in ta; a letter ending in ñā and a letter ending in la should be pronounced the same as one ending in na.

Ayaṃ siloko kuto pabhavo, kattha āgato, kena kāritoti? Tattha kuto pabhavoti bhagavantasmā vā dhammasaṅgāhakattherehi vā aṭṭhakathācariyehi vā pabhavo. Kattha āgatoti vinaye vā suttante vā abhidhamme vā pāḷiyaṃ vā aṭṭhakathāya vā ṭīkādīsu vā āgato. Kena kāritoti nettiniruttipeṭakopadesakaccāyanappakaraṇakārakena āyasmatā mahākaccāyanattherena vā mukhamattadīpanikārakena vajirabuddhācariyena vā padarūpasiddhikārakena buddhapiyācariyena vā saddanītippakaraṇakārakena aggavaṃsācariyena vā tadaññasatthakārakehi mahātherehi vā kāritoti evaṃ āgamacintāyaṃ sati ayaṃ siloko bhagavantasmā pabhavo dhammasaṅgāhakattherehi vā aṭṭhakathācariyehi vāti na paññāyati. “Vinaye vā suttante vā abhidhamme vā pāḷiyaṃ vā aṭṭhakathāya vā ṭīkāsu vā āgato”ti hi na sakkā vattuṃ. Kaccāyanācariyādīhi saddasatthakārakehi ācariyehi katotipi na dissati. Evaṃ sante appāṭihīrakataṃ idaṃ vacanaṃ āpajjati.

From where does this verse originate, where does it come from, and by whom was it composed? As to its origin, it could originate from the Blessed One, or from the Elder Compilers of the Dhamma, or from the teachers of the commentaries. As to where it comes from, it could come from the Vinaya, or the Suttanta, or the Abhidhamma, or from the Pāḷi Canon, or from a commentary, or from subcommentaries and the like. As to by whom it was composed, it could have been composed by the Venerable Mahākaccāyana Thera, author of the Nettinirutti, the Peṭakopadesa, and the Kaccāyana grammar; or by the teacher Vajirabuddhi, author of the Mukhamattadīpanī; or by the teacher Buddhapiya, author of the Padarūpasiddhi; or by the teacher Aggavaṃsa, author of the Saddanīti; or by other great elders who authored similar treatises. Thus, when considering the tradition, it is not apparent whether this verse originates from the Blessed One, the Elder Compilers of the Dhamma, or the teachers of the commentaries. Indeed, it cannot be said that it comes from the Vinaya, the Suttanta, the Abhidhamma, the Pāḷi Canon, a commentary, or the subcommentaries. Nor is it seen to have been composed by the authors of grammatical treatises, such as the teacher Kaccāyana and others. This being so, this statement becomes unauthoritative.

Evaṃ pana mayaṃ cintayimhā – rāmaññadese kira sakabhāsāyaṃ ca-kāranta ña-kārantā na santi[V 2.0210], teneva rāmaññadesiyā bhikkhū [M 2.0289] “sacca”iti imaṃ pāṭhaṃ vadantā “satca”iti vadanti, “pañcaṅga”iti pāṭhaṃ vadantā “pancaṅga”iti vadanti, tasmā attano visaye avijjamānaṃ ca-kāranta ña-kārantaṃ yathāpāṭhaṃ vattumasakkontehi tehi bhikkhūhi sakabhāsānurūpato ayaṃ siloko kārito bhavissatīti. Evaṃ santepi marammabhāsāya ca-kāranta ña-kārantapadānaṃ sutivisesavasena visuṃ paññāyanato marammadesiyā bhikkhū taṃ silokaṃ anuvattitvā “buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti vā “paṭhamaṃ upatjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo”ti vā “hetupatcayo ārammaṇapatcayo”ti vā vattuṃ na arahanti. Rāmaññadesiyāpi sakabhāsāya visuṃ avijjamānampi ca-kāranta ña-kārantapadaṃ sakabhāsākathanakāleyeva bhāsānurūpaṃ ta-kāranta na-kārantabhāvena kathetabbaṃ, māgadhabhāsākathanakāle pana māgadhabhāsāya ca-kāranta ña-kārantapadānaṃ visuṃ payogadassanato māgadhabhāsānurūpaṃ ca-kāranta ña-kārantapadānaṃ visuṃ sutivasena yathāpāṭhameva kathetabbānīti no mati. Ayamettha āgamacintā.

We, however, have reflected thus: It is said that in the Rāmañña country, their own language does not have ca-finals or ñā-finals. For that reason, when the monks of the Rāmañña country recite the text 'sacca,' they say 'satca,' and when they recite the text 'pañcaṅga,' they say 'pancaṅga.' Therefore, this verse must have been composed in accordance with their own language by those monks, who were unable to pronounce the ca-final and ñā-final according to the text, as these do not exist in their region. Even so, since in the Maramma language words with ca-finals and ñā-finals are distinctly perceived by way of their particular sound, the monks of the Maramma country, by following that verse, are not justified in saying 'buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī' or 'paṭhamaṃ upatjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo' or 'hetupatcayo ārammaṇapatcayo.' As for the monks of Rāmañña, although words with ca-finals and ñā-finals are distinctly absent in their own language, they should pronounce them as ta-finals and na-finals in accordance with their language only when speaking their own language. However, when speaking the Māgadha language, since words with ca-finals and ñā-finals are seen to be used distinctly in the Māgadha language, it is our opinion that they should be pronounced distinctly according to their sound, just as they are in the text, in conformity with the Māgadha language. This is the consideration of the tradition here.

Jinasāsanamārabbha, kathāyaṃ kathitā mayā;

Yuttāyuttaṃ cintayantu, paṇḍitā jinasāvakā.

Regarding the Dispensation of the Conqueror, this discourse has been delivered by me; let the wise disciples of the Conqueror reflect on what is proper and improper.

Yuttāyuttaṃ cintayitvā, yuttañce dhārayantu taṃ;

Ayuttañce pajahantu, mānadosavivajjitāti.

Having reflected on what is proper and improper, if it is proper, let them retain it; if it is improper, let them abandon it, being free from the fault of conceit.

254. Evaṃ catunnaṃ kammānaṃ sampattivipattiṃ dassetvā idāni tesaṃ kammānaṃ ṭhānappabhedaṃ dassento “apalokanakammaṃ katamāni pañca ṭhānāni gacchatī”tiādimāha. Tattha vinicchayo aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Anuttānapadatthameva dassayissāma. “Etarahi sacepi sāmaṇero”tiādīsu buddhādīnaṃ avaṇṇabhāsanampi akappiyādiṃ kappiyādibhāvena dīpanampi diṭṭhivipattiyaṃyeva pavisati, teneva vakkhati “taṃ laddhiṃ vissajjāpetabbo”ti. Bhikkhūnampi eseva [M 2.0290] nayo. Micchādiṭṭhikoti buddhavacanādhippāyaṃ viparītato gaṇhanto, so eva “antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato”ti vutto. Keci pana “sassatucchedānaṃ aññataradiṭṭhiyā samannāgato”ti vadanti, taṃ na yuttaṃ. Sassatucchedagāhassa sāmaṇerānaṃ liṅganāsanāya kāraṇattena heṭṭhā aṭṭhakathāyameva vuttattā idha ca daṇḍakammanāsanāya eva adhippetattā. Kāyasambhogasāmaggīti [V 2.0211] sahaseyyapaṭiggahaṇādi. Soratoti subhe rato, suṭṭhu oratoti vā sorato. Nivātavuttīti nīcavutti.

254. Having thus shown the success and failure of the four formal acts, now, showing the classification of the occasions for those acts, he says: 'To which five occasions does the act of announcement apply?' and so on. Therein, the analysis should be understood in accordance with the method stated in the commentary. We will explain only the meaning of terms that are not plain. In passages such as, 'Now, if a novice...,' both speaking in dispraise of the Buddha and others and presenting what is improper as proper fall under defective view; hence it will be said: 'He should be made to relinquish that tenet.' This is the same method for bhikkhus. 'One with wrong view' is one who grasps the intention of the Buddha's word in a contrary way; he is the one spoken of as 'endowed with a view that grasps at extremes.' Some, however, say he is 'endowed with one of the views of eternalism or annihilationism,' but this is not correct. For it has been stated below in the commentary that grasping eternalism or annihilationism is a reason for a novice's expulsion, whereas here only removal by a penalty-act is intended. 'Communion by way of the body' means sharing a bed, accepting requisites, and so on. 'Gentle' (sorata) means one who delights in the good (subhe rato), or one who is very restrained (suṭṭhu orato). 'Humble in conduct' (nivātavutti) means of humble behavior (nīcavutti).

Tassāpi dātabboti vijjamānaṃ mukharādibhāvaṃ nissāya appaṭipucchitvāpi paṭiññaṃ aggahetvāpi āpattiṃ anāropetvāpi desitāyapi āpattiyā khuṃsanādito anoramantassa dātabbova. Oramantassa pana khamāpentassa na dātabbo. Brahmadaṇḍassa dānanti kharadaṇḍassa ukkaṭṭhadaṇḍassa dānaṃ. Tajjanīyādikamme hi kate ovādānusāsanippadānapaṭikkhepo natthi, dinnabrahmadaṇḍe pana tasmiṃ saddhiṃ tajjanīyakammādikatehi paṭikkhittampi kātuṃ na vaṭṭati “neva vattabbo”tiādinā ālāpasallāpamattassapi na-kārena paṭikkhitattā. Tañhi disvā bhikkhū gīvaṃ parivattetvā olokanamattampi na karonti, evaṃ vivajjetabbaṃ nimmadanakaraṇatthameva tassa daṇḍassa anuññātattā. Teneva channattheropi ukkhepanīyādikammakatopi abhāyitvā brahmadaṇḍe dinne “saṅghenāhaṃ sabbathā vivajjito”ti mucchito papati. Yo pana brahmadaṇḍakatena saddhiṃ ñatvā saṃsaṭṭho avivajjetvā viharati, tassa dukkaṭamevāti gahetabbaṃ. Aññathā brahmadaṇḍavidhānassa niratthakatāpasaṅgato. Tenāti brahmadaṇḍakatena. Yathā tajjanīyādikammakatehi, evameva tato adhikampi saṅghaṃ ārādhentena sammā vattitabbaṃ, tañca “sorato [M 2.0291] nivātavuttī”tiādinā sarūpato dassitameva. Tenāha “sammā vattitvā khamāpentassa brahmadaṇḍo paṭippassambhetabbo”ti. Paṭisaṅkhāti paṭisaṅkhāya, ñāṇena upaparikkhitvā.

It should be given to one who, on account of his existing talkativeness and so on, does not desist from censure and the like regarding a confessed offense; it should be given even without having questioned him, accepted his admission, or charged him with the offense. But it should not be given to one who desists and asks for forgiveness. The giving of the 'higher penalty' (brahmadaṇḍa) is the giving of a harsh penalty, a severe penalty. For when formal acts such as censuring have been carried out, there is no prohibition on giving admonition and instruction. But when the higher penalty has been imposed on someone, it is not proper to have any dealings with him, because even mere talk and conversation is prohibited by the negative particle in such phrases as 'he is not to be spoken to.' Indeed, on seeing him, the bhikkhus turn their necks away and do not so much as glance at him. He is to be avoided in this way because that penalty was permitted for the very purpose of crushing his pride. For this reason, even the Elder Channa, who was unafraid even when subjected to formal acts like suspension, fell down in a faint when the higher penalty was imposed, thinking, 'I have been utterly shunned by the Saṅgha.' But it should be understood that whoever knowingly associates with one on whom the higher penalty has been imposed, dwelling with him without avoiding him, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Otherwise, the ordinance of the higher penalty would become meaningless. 'By this' means by one on whom the higher penalty has been imposed. Just as with those on whom formal acts like censuring have been imposed, so too and even more so must one who is seeking to placate the Saṅgha behave properly; and this has been shown in essence by the words 'gentle, humble in conduct,' etc. Hence it is said: 'For one who has behaved properly and asks for forgiveness, the higher penalty should be rescinded.' Paṭisaṅkhā means having reflected, having investigated with wisdom.

Yaṃ taṃ bhagavatā avandiyakammaṃ anuññātanti sambandho. “Tassa bhikkhuno daṇḍakammaṃ kātu”nti sāmaññato anuññātappakāraṃ dassetvā puna visesato anuññātappakāraṃ dassetuṃ “atha kho”tiādi pāḷiuddhaṭāti veditabbaṃ. Imassa apalokanakammassa ṭhānaṃ hotīti apalokanakammasāmaññassa pavattiṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Visesabyatirekena avijjamānampi tadaññattha appavattiṃ dassetuṃ visesanissitaṃ viya voharīyati. “Kammaññeva lakkhaṇa”nti iminā osāraṇādivasena gahitāvasesānaṃ sabbesaṃ apalokanakammasāmaññalakkhaṇavasena gahitattā “kammaññeva lakkhaṇamassāti kammalakkhaṇa”nti nibbacanaṃ dasseti, idañca vuttāvasesānaṃ kammānaṃ niṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ saṅkhārakkhandhadhammāyatanādīni viya vuttāvasesakhandhāyatanānanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Teneva vakkhati “ayaṃ panettha pāḷimuttakopi kammalakkhaṇavinicchayo”tiādi. Yathā cettha, evaṃ [V 2.0212] upari ñattikammādīsupi kammalakkhaṇaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. parivāra 3.495-496) pana “kammameva lakkhaṇanti kammalakkhaṇaṃ. Osāraṇanissāraṇabhaṇḍukammādayo viya kammañca hutvā aññañca nāmaṃ na labhati, kammameva hutvā upalakkhīyatīti kammalakkhaṇanti vuccatī”ti vuttaṃ. Vajirabuddhiṭīkāyaṃ (vajira. ṭī. parivāra 495-496) pana “imassa apalokanakammassa ṭhānaṃ hotīti evampi apalokanakammaṃ pavattatīti attho. Kammaññeva lakkhaṇanti kammalakkhaṇaṃ. Osāraṇanissāraṇabhaṇḍukammādayo viya kammañca hutvā aññañca nāmaṃ na labhati, kammameva hutvā upalakkhīyatīti [M 2.0292] kammalakkhaṇaṃ upanissayo viya. Hetupaccayādilakkhaṇavimutto hi sabbo paccayaviseso tattha saṅgayhatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tassa karaṇanti avandiyakammassa karaṇavidhānaṃ. Na vanditabboti, iminā vandantiyā dukkaṭanti dassetīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saṅghena kataṃ katikaṃ ñatvā maddanaṃ viya hi saṅghasammutiṃ anādarena atikkamantassa āpatti eva hoti.

The connection is to what the Blessed One permitted as an act not deserving of reverence. To show the general type of authorized act by stating, “A disciplinary act is to be performed against that bhikkhu,” and then to show the specific type of authorized act, the Pāḷi passage beginning with atha kho is cited; so it should be understood. “This is the occasion for an act of seeking consent” means it is the occasion for the occurrence of the general act of seeking consent. Even though it does not exist apart from the specific, it is spoken of as if dependent on the specific to indicate its non-occurrence elsewhere. By the phrase “the act itself is the characteristic,” it explains the derivation “the act itself is its characteristic, hence it is called ‘act-characteristic,’” since the remainder of what is taken—by way of reinstatement, etc.—is understood as being included in the characteristic of the general act of seeking consent. And this should be seen as the concluding place of the remaining actions mentioned, just as the aggregate of formations, the base of phenomena, etc., are for the remaining aggregates and bases. Thus, it will be said: “Here, this is also a determination of the act-characteristic, which is outside the Pāḷi text.” As it is here, so too above in the case of acts preceded by a motion, etc., the act-characteristic is to be understood as stated. However, in the Sāratthadīpanī it is said: “‘The act itself is the characteristic’ means act-characteristic. Like the acts of reinstatement, expulsion, and making someone a scoundrel, etc., it is an act but does not obtain any other name; it is called ‘act-characteristic’ because it is recognized only as an act.” In the Vajirabuddhiṭīkā it is said: “‘This has the occasion for an act of seeking consent’—this means that the act of seeking consent occurs in this way. ‘The act itself is the characteristic’ means act-characteristic. Like the acts of reinstatement, expulsion, and making someone a scoundrel, etc., it is an act but does not obtain any other name; the act-characteristic is like a supporting condition because it is recognized only as an act. For every specific condition, freed from the characteristics of the root condition, etc., is included here.” “The performance of it” refers to the procedure for performing the act not deserving of reverence. “One should not pay respects”: by this, it should be understood that it shows that for one who pays respects there is an offense of wrong conduct. For just as one might trample on an agreement known to have been made by the Saṅgha, so for one who disrespectfully transgresses the Saṅgha’s consensus, there is indeed an offense.

255. Bhikkhusaṅghassapi panetaṃ labbhatiyevāti avandiyakammassa upalakkhaṇamattena gahitattā bhikkhusaṅghassapi kammalakkhaṇaṃ labbhati eva. Salākadānaṭṭhānaṃ salākaggaṃ nāma, yāgubhattānaṃ bhājanaṭṭhānāni yāgaggabhattaggāni nāma. Etesupi hi ṭhānesu sabbo saṅgho uposathe viya sannipatito, kammañca vaggakammaṃ na hoti, “mayametaṃ na jānimhā”ti pacchā khīyantāpi na honti, khaṇḍasīmāya pana kate khīyanti. Saṅghikapaccayañhi acchinnacīvarādīnaṃ dātuṃ apalokentehi upacārasīmaṭṭhānaṃ sabbesaṃ anumatiṃ gahetvāva kātabbaṃ. Yo pana visabhāgapuggalo dhammikaṃ apalokanaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ upāyena bahiupacārasīmagataṃ vā katvā khaṇḍasīmaṃ vā pavisitvā kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Yaṃ sandhāya “apalokanakammaṃ karotī”ti sāmaññato dasseti, taṃ apalokanakammaṃ sarūpato dassetuṃ āha “acchinnacīvaraṃ”iccādi. Yadi apaloketvāva cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, kiṃ pana appamattakavissajjakasammutiyāti āha “appamattakavissajjakena panā”tiādi. Nāḷi vā upaḍḍhanāḷi vāti divase divase apaloketvā dātabbassa pamāṇadassanaṃ. Tena yāpanamattameva apaloketabbaṃ, na adhikanti dasseti. Ekadivasaṃyeva vātiādi dasavīsatidivasānaṃ ekasmiṃ divaseyeva dātabbaparicchedadassanaṃ. Tena “yāvajīva”nti vā “yāvarogā [M 2.0293] vuṭṭhahatī”ti vā evaṃ apaloketuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Iṇapalibodhanti iṇavatthuṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Tañca iṇāyikehi palibuddhassa lajjīpesalassa sāsanupakārakassa pamāṇayuttameva kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ niyametvā [V 2.0213] bhikkhūhi apaloketvā dātabbaṃ, na pana sahassaṃ vā satasahassaṃ vā mahāiṇaṃ. Tādisañhi bhikkhācariyavattena sabbehi bhikkhūhi tādisassa bhikkhuno pariyesitvā dātabbaṃ.

255. And this is indeed obtainable for the Saṅgha of bhikkhus; since it is taken merely as a designation of the act not deserving of reverence, the characteristic of a formal act is indeed obtained for the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. The place for giving out tickets is called the ticket-hall; the places for distributing bowls of rice gruel and meals are called the gruel-hall and the meal-hall. For in these places the entire Saṅgha assembles as on an Uposatha day, the act is not a factional one, and they are not vexed afterwards, saying, “We did not know this.” But when a partial boundary has been established, they are vexed. For when giving Saṅgha property such as uncut robes, etc., those seeking consent must do so after getting the approval of all who are within the monastery precincts. But if an unsuitable person obstructs a lawful seeking of consent, it is allowable to proceed after having him go outside the monastery precincts or after entering a partial boundary. To show in its own nature the act of seeking consent, which he indicates generally when saying, “he performs an act of seeking consent,” he says, “uncut robe,” etc. If a robe is to be given only after seeking consent, what then of the appointment of a distributor of trifles? He says, “But by a distributor of trifles,” etc. “A nāḷi or half a nāḷi” is a demonstration of the amount to be given daily after seeking consent. By this he shows that consent should be sought only for what is sufficient for sustenance, not for more. “Or on a single day,” etc., is a demonstration of the limit to be given on one day out of ten or twenty days. By this he shows that it is not allowable to seek consent saying, “for as long as I live,” or “until he recovers from the illness.” “The encumbrance of debt”: the connection is that it is allowable to give an item for a debt. And for one who is encumbered by creditors—a modest, amiable bhikkhu who is a benefactor to the Teaching—an appropriate amount of allowable goods should be determined and given by the bhikkhus after seeking consent, not a great debt of a thousand or a hundred thousand. For such a one, all the bhikkhus should seek out and give to such a bhikkhu in accordance with the duty of an alms-wanderer.

“Chattaṃ vā vedikaṃ vāti ettha vedikāti cetiyassa upari caturassacayo vuccati. Chattanti tato uddhaṃ valayāni dassetvā kato aggacayo vuccatī”ti sāratthadīpaniyaṃ (sārattha. ṭī. parivāra 3.495-496) vuttaṃ. Cetiyassa upanikkhepatoti cetiyassa paṭijagganatthāya vaḍḍhiyā payojetvā kappiyakārakehi ṭhapitavatthuto. Saṅghikenapīti na kevalañca tatruppādato paccayadāyakehi catupaccayatthāya saṅghassa dinnavatthunāpīti attho. Saṅghabhattaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti mahādānaṃ dadantehipi kariyamānaṃ saṅghabhattaṃ viya kāretuṃ na vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. “Yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjituṃ ruccatī”ti vuttattā attano attano paribhogapahonakaṃ appaṃ vā bahuṃ vā gahetabbaṃ, adhikaṃ pana gahetuṃ na labhati.

“An umbrella or a railing”: here, “railing” refers to the square structure on top of a shrine. “Umbrella” refers to the pinnacle made above that, showing rings. This is stated in the Sāratthadīpanī. “From what is deposited for the shrine” means from an item placed by suitable stewards, having been invested at interest for the purpose of maintaining the shrine. “Even with what belongs to the Saṅgha”: the meaning is not only from what is produced there, but also with an item given to the Saṅgha for the four requisites by donors. “It is not allowable to make a Saṅgha meal”: the intention is that it is not allowable to have a meal prepared like a Saṅgha meal that is being made even by those giving a great donation. Because it is said, “It is approved to use as one pleases,” one may take a small or large amount sufficient for one’s own use, but one is not allowed to take more.

Uposathadivaseti nidassanamattaṃ, yasmiṃ kismiñci divasepi kataṃ sukatameva hoti. Karontena “yaṃ imasmiṃ vihāre antosīmāya saṅghasantakaṃ…pe… yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjituṃ mayhaṃ ruccatī”ti evaṃ katikā kātabbā. Tathā dvīhi tīhipi “āyasmantānaṃ ruccatī”ti vacanameva hettha viseso. Tesampīti rukkhānaṃ. Sā eva katikāti visuṃ katikā na kātabbāti attho.

“On the Uposatha day” is merely a specification; on whatever day it is done, it is indeed well done. The one performing it should make an agreement thus: “Whatever in this monastery within the boundary belongs to the Saṅgha… it is approved for me to use as I please.” Similarly, for two or three bhikkhus, the only difference here is the statement, “Is it approved by the venerable sirs?” “For them also” means for the trees. “That same agreement”: the meaning is that a separate agreement need not be made.

Tesanti [M 2.0294] rukkhānaṃ, saṅgho sāmīti sambandho. Purimavihāreti purime yathāsukhaṃ paribhogatthāya katakatike vihāre. Pariveṇāni katvā jaggantīti yattha arakkhiyamāne phalāphalāni rukkhā ca vinassanti, tādisaṃ ṭhānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, tattha saṅghassa katikā na pavattatīti adhippāyo. Yehi pana rukkhabījāni ropetvā ādito paṭṭhāya paṭijaggitā, tepi dasamabhāgaṃ datvā ropakeheva paribhuñjitabbāni. Tehīti jaggitehi.

“Of them,” meaning of the trees, the Saṅgha is the owner—this is the connection. “In a previous monastery” means in a previous monastery where an agreement was made for the purpose of using things as one pleases. “Having made enclosures, they guard”: this is said in reference to a place where, if it were not guarded, fruits of various kinds and trees would be destroyed. The intention is that the Saṅgha’s agreement does not apply there. But as for those by whom tree seeds were planted and tended from the beginning, the fruits may be enjoyed by the planters themselves after they have given a tenth part. “By them” means by those who tended them.

Tatthāti tasmiṃ vihāre. Mūletiādikāle, pubbeti attho. Dīghā katikāti aparicchinnakālā yathāsukhaṃ paribhogatthāya katikā. Nikkukkuccenāti “abhājitamida”nti kukkuccaṃ [V 2.0214] akatvāti attho. Khīyanamattameva tanti tena khīyanena bahuṃ khādantānaṃ doso natthi attano paribhogappamāṇasseva gahitattā, khīyantepi attano pahonakaṃ gahetvā khāditabbanti adhippāyo.

“Therein” means in that monastery. “At the root” means at the original time; the meaning is “previously.” “A long agreement” means an agreement for an unlimited time for use as one pleases. “Without scruples” means without having the scruple, “This is undivided”; that is the meaning. “It is only a matter of vexation”: regarding that vexation, there is no fault for those who eat much, because only the amount for one’s own use has been taken. The intention is that even if others are vexed, one has taken and eaten what is sufficient for oneself.

Gaṇhathāti na vattabbāti tathā vutte teneva bhikkhunā dinnaṃ viya maññeyyuṃ. Taṃ nissāya micchājīvasambhavo hotīti vuttaṃ. Tenāha “anuvicaritvā”tiādi. Upaḍḍhabhāgoti ekassa bhikkhuno paṭivīsato upaḍḍhabhāgo, dentena ca “ettakaṃ dātuṃ saṅgho anuññāsī”ti evaṃ attānaṃ parimocetvā yathā te saṅghe eva pasīdanti, evaṃ vatvā dātabbaṃ. Apaccāsīsantenāti gilānagamikissarādīnaṃ anuññātapuggalānampi attano santakaṃ dentena apaccāsīsanteneva dātabbaṃ. Ananuññātapuggalānaṃ pana apaccāsīsantenapi dātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti. Saṅghikameva yathākatikāya dāpetabbaṃ. Attano santakampi paccayadāyakādayo sayameva vissāsena gaṇhanti, na vāretabbā, “laddhakappiya”nti tuṇhī bhavitabbaṃ. Pubbe vuttamevāti “kuddho hi so rukkhepi chindeyyā”tiādinā tuṇhībhāve kāraṇaṃ pubbe vuttameva, tehi kataanatthābhāvepi [M 2.0295] kāruññena tuṇhī bhavituṃ vaṭṭati, “gaṇhathā”tiādi pana vattuṃ na vaṭṭati.

“‘Take it’ should not be said”: if it is said so, they might think it was given by that very bhikkhu. It is said that wrong livelihood arises in dependence on that. Therefore he said, “Having investigated,” etc. “Half a share” means half of one bhikkhu’s portion. And the one giving should give it after clearing himself by saying, “The Saṅgha has permitted this much to be given,” speaking in such a way that they gain confidence in the Saṅgha. “By one not expecting anything in return”: when giving one’s own property even to permitted persons such as the sick, travelers, and those in authority, one must give without expecting anything in return. But it is not allowable to give to unpermitted persons, even without expecting anything in return. What belongs to the Saṅgha should be caused to be given according to the agreement. Donors of requisites and others may take even one’s own property with confidence; they should not be stopped. One should remain silent, thinking, “What has been received is allowable.” “It has been said before”: the reason for being silent has been stated before with the words, “For being angry, he might even cut down the trees,” etc. Even if no harm is done by them, it is allowable to be silent out of compassion, but it is not allowable to say, “Take it,” etc.

Garubhaṇḍattā…pe… na dātabbanti jīvarukkhānaṃ ārāmaṭṭhāniyattā dārūnañca gehasambhārānupagatattā “sabbaṃ tvameva gaṇhāti dātuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Akatāvāsaṃ vā katvāti pubbe avijjamānaṃ senāsanaṃ katvā. Jaggitakāleti phalavāre sampatte. Jagganakāleti jaggituṃ āraddhakāle.

“Because they are heavy articles … and so on … they should not be given”: this is because living trees are permanent fixtures of the monastery and because the timber is connected with household furnishings. It was said: “It is not proper to give, saying, ‘You take it all.’” “Or having made what was not made” means having made a dwelling that did not previously exist. “At the time of watching over” means when the time for fruit-bearing has arrived. “At the time of protecting” means at the time when one has begun to protect.

256. Ñattikammaṭṭhānabhedeti ñattikammassa ṭhānabhede.

256. “In the division of the basis for a formal act by motion”: this means in the division of the basis for the formal act by motion.

Iti vinayasaṅgahasaṃvaṇṇanābhūte vinayālaṅkāre

Thus, in the Vinayālaṅkāra, the commentary on the Vinayasaṅgaha,

Kammākammavinicchayakathālaṅkāro nāma

named the Ornament of the Discussion on the Determination of Valid and Invalid Acts,

Tettiṃsatimo paricchedo.

the Thirty-third Chapter.

34. Pakiṇṇakavinicchayakathā

34. The Discussion on Miscellaneous Determinations

Evaṃ [V 2.0215] kammākammavinicchayakathaṃ kathetvā idāni pakiṇṇakavinicchayakathaṃ kathetuṃ “idāni pakiṇṇakakathā veditabbā”tiādimāha. Tattha pakārena kiṇṇāti pakiṇṇā, divāseyyāti kathā viya visuṃ visuṃ appavattitvā ekasmiṃyeva paricchede karaṇavasena pavattā gaṇabhojanakathādayo. Pakiṇṇakā sakatthe ka-paccayavasena.

Having thus explained the discussion on the determination of valid and invalid acts, now, in order to explain the discussion on miscellaneous determinations, he states the passage beginning: “Now, the miscellaneous discussion is to be known.” Therein, “miscellaneous” (pakiṇṇā) means “strewn about in various ways” (pakārena kiṇṇā). Like the discussion on daytime sleeping, they do not proceed separately one by one, but discussions such as the one on group meals proceed in a single chapter for some reason. The word “pakiṇṇakā” is formed by adding the suffix “-ka” in its own sense.

Tatrāyaṃ pakiṇṇakamātikā –

Herein is the miscellaneous matrix:

Gaṇabhojanakathā ca, paramparā ca bhojanā;

Anāpucchā paṃsukūlaṃ, tato acchinnacīvaraṃ.

The discussion on group meals, and consecutive meals; taking without asking, rag-robes, then the unforfeited robe.

Paṭibhānacittaṃ vippa-katabhojanameva ca;

Uddisantuddisāpentā, tivassantarikā tathā.

An inspired thought, and food that has been set aside; those who designate and cause to designate, and likewise those with a three-year interval.

Dīghāsanaṃ [M 2.0296] gilānupa-ṭṭhānaṃ maraṇavaṇṇakaṃ;

Attapātanamappacca-vekkhitvā nisinnaṃ tathā.

A long seat, attending on the sick, praise of death; suicide, and likewise sitting down without having reflected.

Davāya silāvijjhanaṃ, dāyāḷimpanakaṃ tathā;

Micchādiṭṭhikulābhataṃ, gopakadānameva ca.

Piercing a rock for sport, and likewise marking a gift; what is brought from a family with wrong view, and a gift from a cowherd.

Dhammikāyācanā ceva, uccārādīna chaḍḍanaṃ;

Nhāne rukkhaghaṃsanāni, valikādīna dhāraṇaṃ.

A righteous request, and disposal of excrement and so on; rubbing against trees while bathing, and wearing ornaments and so on.

Dīghakesā ādāsādi, naccādyaṅgacchedādi ca;

Patto sabbapaṃsukūlaṃ, parissavana naggiyaṃ.

Long hair, mirrors, etc.; dancing, cutting off limbs, etc.; a bowl, all rag-robes, a water-strainer, nakedness.

Gandhapupphaṃ [V 2.0216] āsittakaṃ, maḷorikekabhājanaṃ;

Celapati pādaghaṃsī, bījanī chattameva ca.

Perfumes and flowers, sprinkling, a single curd-vessel; a strip of cloth, a foot-rubber, a fan, and an umbrella.

Nakhālomā kāyabandhā, nivāsanapārupanā;

Kāja dantakaṭṭhañceva, rukkhārohanakampi ca.

Nails and body-hair, body-bindings, under-robes and upper-robes; a carrying pole and a tooth-stick, and also climbing a tree.

Chandāropā lokāyatā, khipitaṃ lasuṇaṃ tathā;

Na akkamitabbādīni, avandiyā ca vandiyā.

Generating consent, worldly lore, and likewise throwing away garlic; things not to be trodden on, etc., those not to be venerated and those to be venerated.

Vandanākārakathā ca, āsandādikathāpi ca;

Uccāsanamahāsanaṃ, pāsādaparibhogakaṃ.

Discussion on the way of paying homage, and also discussion on chairs, etc.; high seats and large seats, the use of a storied building.

Upāhanaṃ yānañceva, cīvaraṃ chinnacīvaraṃ;

Akappiyacīvarañca, cīvarassa vicāraṇā.

Footwear and vehicles, a robe, a cut robe; an unsuitable robe, and the investigation of a robe.

Daṇḍakathinakañceva, gahapaticīvaraṃ tathā;

Chacīvaraṃ rajanādi, atirekañca cīvaraṃ.

A staff and the kathina, likewise a householder's robe; six robes, dyeing, etc., and an extra robe.

Aṭṭhavaraṃ nisīdanaṃ, adhammakammameva ca;

Okāso saddhādeyyo ca, santaruttarakopi ca.

Eight boons, a sitting cloth, and an unlawful formal act; making an opportunity, a gift of faith, and an inner and outer garment.

Cīvaranikkhepo ceva, satthavatthikammaṃ tathā;

Nahāpito dasabhāgo, pātheyyaṃ padesopi ca.

Putting down a robe, and likewise work on a needle-case; a barber, a tenth share, provisions for a journey, and a region.

Saṃsaṭṭhaṃ pañcabhesajjaṃ, dutiyaṃ vasā mūlakaṃ;

Piṭṭhaṃ kasāva paṇṇañca, phalañca jatu loṇakaṃ.

Being mixed with, the five medicines; secondly, fat and roots; flour, an astringent decoction, and leaves, fruit, lac, and salt.

Cuṇṇaṃ [M 2.0297][V 2.0217] amanussābādhaṃ, añjanaṃ natthumeva ca;

Dhūmanettaṃ telapākaṃ, sedaṃ lohitamocanaṃ.

Powder, affliction by non-humans, eye-ointment and nose-treatment; an inhalation tube, preparation of oil, sweating, blood-letting.

Pādabbhañjaṃ gaṇḍābādho, visañca gharadinnako;

Duṭṭhagahaṇiko paṇḍu-rogo chavidosopi ca.

Anointing the feet, the disease of boils, and poison given in a house; seizure by a malignant being, jaundice, and also skin disease.

Abhisannadosakāyo, loṇasuvīrako tathā;

Antovutthādikathā ca, uggahitapaṭiggaho.

A body with a corrupted humor, and likewise salt-and-sour-gruel; discussion on what is stored inside, etc., and accepting what has been taken up.

Tato nihatakathā ca, purebhattapaṭiggaho;

Vanaṭṭhaṃ pokkharaṭṭhañca, tathā akatakappataṃ.

Then, discussion on what is put down, accepting before the meal; what is in the forest and what is in a lotus pond, likewise unpreparedness.

Yāgukathā guḷakathā, mahāpadesameva ca;

Ānisaṃsakathā ceti, pakiṇṇakamhi āgatā.

Discussion on rice-gruel, discussion on molasses, and the great authorities; discussion on benefits—thus they come in the miscellaneous section.

Gaṇabhojanakathā

The Discussion on Group Meals

1. Tattha gaṇitabbo saṅkhyātabboti gaṇo, yo koci samūho, idha pana catuvaggādigaṇo adhippeto. Bhuñjate bhojanaṃ, byavaharaṇabhāvasaṅkhātā bhojanakiriyā, gaṇassa bhojanaṃ gaṇabhojanaṃ, tasmiṃ. Gaṇabhojane pācittiyaṃ hotīti ettha janakahetumhi bhummavacanaṃ. Aññatra samayāti gilānādisattavidhaṃ samayaṃ ṭhapetvā. Imassa sikkhāpadassa viññattiṃ katvā bhuñjanavatthusmiṃ paññattattā viññattito gaṇabhojanaṃ vatthuvaseneva pākaṭanti taṃ avatvā “gaṇabhojanaṃ nāma yattha…pe… nimantitā bhuñjantī”ti nimantanavasenevassa padabhājane gaṇabhojanaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñci pana sikkhāpadaṃ vatthuanurūpampi siyāti “padabhājane vuttanayeneva gaṇabhojanaṃ hotī”ti kesañci āsaṅkā bhaveyyāti tannivattanatthaṃ “gaṇabhojanaṃ dvīhi ākārehi pasavatī”ti vuttaṃ. Ekato gaṇhantīti ettha aññamaññassa dvādasahatthaṃ amuñcitvā ṭhitā ekato gaṇhanti nāmāti gahetabbaṃ. “Amhākaṃ catunnampi [M 2.0298] bhattaṃ dehī’ti vā viññāpeyyu”nti vacanato, heṭṭhā “tvaṃ ekassa bhikkhuno bhattaṃ dehi, tvaṃ dvinnanti evaṃ viññāpetvā”ti [V 2.0218] vacanato ca attano atthāya aññena viññattampi sādiyantassa gaṇabhojanaṃ hotiyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ viññattito pasavatīti ettha viññattiyā sati gaṇantassa ekato hutvā gahaṇe iminā sikkhāpadena āpatti, visuṃ gahaṇe paṇītabhojanasūpodanaviññattīhi āpatti veditabbā.

1. Therein, a “group” (gaṇa) is what is to be counted or reckoned; any collection of people. But here a group starting from a group of four is intended. They eat “food” (bhojana); the act of eating is the activity of consuming. Eating by a group is a “group meal” (gaṇabhojana). In the phrase “in a group meal there is an offense of expiation,” the locative case here has the sense of a generating cause. “Except on an occasion” means excluding the seven kinds of occasions, such as illness. Since this training rule was laid down in the case of eating after having made a request, a group meal arising from a request is evident from the circumstance itself. Without stating this, in the word-analysis for this rule, a group meal is spoken of only in terms of invitation, as in: “A group meal is when … and so on … those who have been invited eat.” However, since some training rule might also be in accordance with the circumstance, in order to dispel the doubt some might have that “a group meal occurs only in the way stated in the word-analysis,” it was said: “A group meal arises in two ways.” Here, regarding “they receive together,” it should be understood that those who stand without being separated from one another by twelve cubits are said to “receive together.” Based on the text, “Or they might request, saying: ‘Give food to the four of us,’” and from the earlier text, “having requested thus: ‘You give food to one bhikkhu, you to two,’” it should be seen that it is indeed a group meal for one who consents even when a request is made by another for one's own benefit. “Thus it arises from a request”: here, when there is a request, for one who receives as a group by being together, there is an offense by this training rule. If they receive separately, an offense should be understood by the rules on requesting refined food, curry, or rice.

Pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ nāmaṃ gahetvāti ettha “bhojanaṃ gaṇhathāti vuttepi gaṇabhojanaṃ hotiyevā”ti vadanti. “Heṭṭhā addhānagamanavatthusmiṃ, nāvābhiruhanavatthusmiñca ‘idheva, bhante, bhuñjathā’ti vutte yasmā kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhiṃsu, tasmā ‘bhuñjathā’ti vuttepi gaṇabhojanaṃ hotiyevā”ti tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. “Pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ nāmaṃ gahetvā nimantetī”ti vuttattā pana “odanaṃ bhuñjathā”ti vā “bhattaṃ bhuñjathā”ti vā bhojananāmaṃ gahetvāva vutte gaṇabhojanaṃ hoti, na aññathā. “Idheva, bhante, bhuñjathā”ti etthāpi “odana”nti vā “bhatta”nti vā vatvāva te evaṃ nimantesunti gahetabbaṃ. Gaṇavasena vā nimantitattā te bhikkhū apakataññutāya kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhiṃsūti ayaṃ amhākaṃ khanti, vīmaṃsitvā yuttataraṃ gahetabbaṃ.
